Structure: Canon describes the Champion Duelists as a group of selected fighters, not a ranked order. No leader, rank system or parent body is named. A Gardes member says the duelists keep an office in Quartier Lyonnais of the Court of Fontaine, across from the Adventurers' Guild headquarters.

Known current members are Clorinde, Savinien and Guillaume Marais. Ismenor is a retired Champion Duelist. Clorinde's own story shows a qualification trial, but the wiki does not describe a general process beyond saying duelists are chosen from among the country's best fighters.

Members: Clorinde is the best known and, per the wiki, the strongest of them: undefeated in formal duels. Savinien, an open-world NPC in Quartier Lyonnais, is a duelist who jokes about an extra fee. Guillaume Marais is named as a current member in the lines of Sir Arthur, the Steambird newspaper-seller. Ismenor, now retired, spends his evenings in the Vasari Passage and talks about the profession wryly.

Historical member: Marfisa, the earliest known Champion Duelist, who lived over 500 years ago. Clorinde has her own character entry for her history, personality and relationships; this entry only covers the office.

Methods: A defendant who does not accept that they should be tried can request a duel to defend their reputation. Ismenor says only a concession or expiry of the duel can end it, and few people can defeat an official duelist. The worst case is the defendant being killed, which per the wiki only happens when they refuse to yield.

Because the duelist fights on behalf of the court, the choice is deliberate: win and walk free, or lose and face the ordinary trial. Vitruvia, a legal adviser who once wished to be a duelist but cannot fight, builds her business around helping clients avoid both duelists and the theatre by exploiting gaps in the law. She treats the duelists as the ultimate risk of a case.

History: **Marfisa.** She came from Fleuve Cendre, where the weak became prey, and made her name with self-taught spearmanship. Emanuel Guillotin, a Marechaussee Hunter, defeated her and pushed her to adopt justice as her rule; she became a Champion Duelist and offered justice to those who sought to evade judgment. According to weapon text, she was later said to have faced Parsifal the Great in a trial by combat during the Siege of Poisson. While trying to hunt down Emanuel for a final duel, she met the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and was dissolved by its leader, who absorbed her mastery of the spear.

**Callas.** Years before the Fontaine Archon Quest, Callas, president of the Spina di Rosula, chose to settle an accusation by duelling Clorinde. He died in the duel. Clorinde recognised that he had let it happen, though his reasons were not understood publicly until years later.

Relations: The duelists work within the justice system alongside the Gardes and the court. Clorinde once served as Furina's bodyguard and stood ready to duel at the trial that exposed Furina. The Spina di Rosula's president Callas died in a duel with Clorinde, which shaped her later bond with his daughter Navia.

The office has older ties to the Marechaussee Hunters: Emanuel Guillotin's defeat of Marfisa turned her toward justice, and Clorinde is the inheritor of the nearly forgotten Hunters. See her entry for details.

Reputation: Citizens treat the duelists as a sobering last resort. Opponents tend to surrender rather than face Clorinde, and journalists follow her. Vitruvia says she would have liked to join them, and Savinien jokes about extra fees.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Champion Duelists remain active in Fontaine. Clorinde is still the strongest and is no longer on a bodyguard post; she now works as a senior Game Master with the Tabletop Troupe and is travelling with Navia in Snezhnaya.

No change to the office's legal role has been shown after the events of Fontaine's Archon Quest.

49.content:
Marfisa was a Champion Duelist over 500 years ago, originally from Fleuve Cendre and a spear fighter. She was beaten by the Marechaussee Hunter Emanuel Guillotin, took up his idea of justice and became a duelist. She was later dissolved by the leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, who took her spear technique.

She has a link to Parsifal the Great through the Lumidouce Bell, which Parsifal gave her as an invitation to a surface performance. In weapon text she faces Parsifal in a trial by combat; the wiki says Parsifal may be Josephine using the name.

50.comment: Champion Duelist: Callas and Clorinde's duel
50.content: Callas, founder and president of the Spina di Rosula and Navia's father, was accused of murder and chose to defend his honour in a duel with Clorinde. He died in it. Clorinde saw that he had let her win, but his reasons only became public years later.

51.content:
Chasm Exploration Team (also: The Chasm Exploration Team, Chasm exploration crew, Chasm Delvers): The Chasm Exploration Team is a small crew hired by Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs to look into the strange happenings in the Chasm, the mining region that was sealed off after a mysterious crystal appeared. They are the heart of the Chasm Delvers world-quest series, in which the Traveler helps them break the seal, set up camp in the Underground Mines and trace the dark mud to its source. Afterwards the team became an official part of Huishan Hall.

It is a practical, mixed crew rather than a military unit: an adventurer-cartographer, a foreign ecologist, a safety technician, a bard and a reformed Treasure Hoarder, all supplied by a bureaucrat who would rather be somewhere else.

Structure: The team has no named commander. Muning, a specialist of the Ministry of Civil Affairs sent to the Chasm, handles its supplies and paperwork. The members are Zhiqiong (Adventurers' Guild, an adventurer chosen for her mapping talent), Khedive (an ecologist from the Sumeru Akademiya's Amurta), Jinwu (the Chasm's safety technician), Taliesin (a bard from Mondstadt) and Clitopho (a former Treasure Hoarder and alchemy student from Mondstadt). The team runs two camps, one near the Chasm's eastern surface entrance and, after the seal is broken, camps inside the Underground Mines.

Khedive's presence comes from a collaboration agreement with the Liyue Qixing: he funds the team and studies the Chasm's ecological changes. Jinwu runs a simple crafting bench that upgrades the Lumenstone Adjuvant, the light source used against the darkness underground. Clitopho joined as the demolitions expert after the Traveler and Zhiqiong rescued him from other Treasure Hoarders, a gap that Jinwu says was meant to be filled by Klee with Kaeya as her partner before Klee was grounded.

Goals: The team's job is to learn why the Chasm turned dangerous and to map and make safe the sealed mines. Individual members want different things: Zhiqiong wants to be remembered for a discovery, and Khedive wants to understand the ecological change.

Methods: Expeditions advance in stages. The Traveler first shatters the Bedrock Keys of the Seven-Star Seal that the Liyue Qixing placed over the Chasm. The team then establishes a camp underground, lights the mines with Lumenstone Adjuvant, maps the tunnels and clears obstructions, including a rockfall that is blown open with a giant cannon loaded with specially prepared fuses.

History: The team first appears in version 2.6 in The Chasm Delvers. The Traveler accepts an Adventurers' Guild commission and meets Muning, who is worried about the sealed Chasm. After the Seven-Star Seal is broken the team moves into the Underground Mines, where it meets miners, deals with Treasure Hoarders and finds the "dark mud" that spreads Abyssal corruption.

Deeper down, the Traveler finds an ancient ruin tied to the cataclysm 500 years ago and a corrupted Skyfrost Nail, a meteorite-like object that fell from Celestia and was tainted by the Abyss Order. Purifying it makes the black ooze recede and the earthquakes stop. Zhiqiong, still hungry for answers, chooses to continue alone into the Abyss-touched depths, and Muning makes the rest of the group an official part of Huishan Hall.

Relations: - **Ministry of Civil Affairs**: hired the team; Muning is its representative.
- **Liyue Qixing**: sealed the Chasm and, via Khedive, funds the research.
- **Huishan Hall**: the group became an official part of it.
- **Treasure Hoarders**: a recurring threat in the mines; Clitopho is a former member.

Status as of 7.1: After The Chasm Delvers the team remains at its camps as an official arm of Huishan Hall. Zhiqiong is no longer with the group. No later developments for the team were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

52.content: Zhiqiong is an Adventurers' Guild member chosen for the Chasm Exploration Team for her cartography. She comes from Mingyun Village, whose mines have dried up, and she admires great adventurers such as Stanley, Alice and the Traveler. She resents authorities who do little fieldwork of their own, and her wish to leave a mark makes her reckless around dangerous Abyssal forces. At the end of The Chasm Delvers she disappears into the mines' depths. See her own entry for more.

53.content:
Children of Echoes (also: Nanatzcayan, Nanatzcayan tribe, Children of Echoes tribe): The Children of Echoes, or Nanatzcayan, are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live in the canyons of Tequemecan Valley in eastern Natlan, where the ring of hammers and the tapping of gem hunters echo off the cliffs. They are miners, excavators, smiths and gem appraisers who work alongside drill-horned Tepetlisaurs, and they are known for their love of dance and rhythmic music. Their chief is Pacal. Kachina and Xilonen are the best-known members.

Stone is one of their symbols. They are Natlan's only source of obsidian, a material used in important rites, and their Name Engravers forge the obsidian stones that carry Natlan's Ancient Names.

Structure: Like Natlan's other tribes, the Children of Echoes govern themselves. A chief, normally chosen by the previous chief, oversees the tribe's customs and may change them. Even the Pyro Archon does not overrule a chief's decision as long as the tribe agrees. The tribe works in 19 mining teams: 12 handle the tribe's own work and 7 can be hired for mining or excavation elsewhere. Large ore deals and the hire of mining teams are negotiated directly with the chief. Guards such as Avilix and Cauich watch the settlement. The tribe's Wayob, its ancestral spirits in the Night Kingdom, choose who receives the tribe's Ancient Names.

The tribe keeps its business informal. Its bulletin board admits that its people dislike paperwork and the fine print of commercial terms, and trust partners not to cheat them. Disputes that cannot be settled go to Chasca's mediation table. The chief issues decrees through the tribal bulletin board next to Stage Tepetl.

Leadership: Chief Pacal is a big, warm-hearted man who prefers looking after and supporting his people to managing the details of their lives. As a young man he hoped to be chosen by the Wayob, but he never received an Ancient Name. He took up eating to cope with stress, and once ate 71 servings of Glittering Gemstones in a contest. He made his peace with it, and he lives by the tribe's mantra: no one fights alone.

Pacal has looked out for Kachina since she received her Ancient Name. Kachina calls him "Uncle Pacal" and says he defends her whenever others in the tribe run her down. His Tepetlisaur companion is Uchu. Manqu warns that, Ancient Name or not, Pacal is not to be taken lightly.

Members: - **Kachina**: a young warrior who bears the Ancient Name Uthabiti ("toughness and tenacity"). She is a gifted dancer and a tireless digger, and her Tepetlisaur companion is Ayo. She was the Traveler's first guide in Natlan.
- **Xilonen**: a renowned smith and the tribe's Name Engraver, bearer of the Ancient Name Baraka. Her parents and most of her relatives were Name Engravers too. Most of her work is tools, weapons and machines for the tribe.
- **Pacal**: chief.

Other residents include Cheven, owner of Muhuru's Gemporium, and her apprentice Imix; Apoxpalon of the Macuahuitl Workshop; Titu, an old storyteller who tends the Shadow Pins; Pochtli, a regular at Stage Tepetl who rarely hands out compliments; and Itzna, a champion of the daily Drillbit Dance. Tepal, who designed the Phlogiston Wings, was raised in the tribe and died during an experiment. Batz died in the Abyss's invasion. Siyah, of the Saurian Relics Association, says he was given its stand at the Stadium's Chuwen Fair because the Children of Echoes "have a knack for business".

Goals: The tribe wants to keep its people, its Tepetlisaurs and its mountains safe, and to pass on its craft. Its members still dream of the glory of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and they see their work as a "blessing" made by mortal hands rather than granted by gods or masters. The bulletin board's welcome promises visitors sincerity "as solid and steady as the stones and as hot as the fires of the forge".

Methods: **Mining and gems.** The tribe digs deep into the mountains for ore, solid phlogiston and gems, so deep that one guard jokes it can be hard to get enough sunlight. Members decorate their tools, weapons and accessories with gems, and some people read the gems as a sign of skill or status. Most members love tunnelling, and finding a vein of ore gives them a warmth that everyone in the tribe understands.

**Tepetlisaurs.** Tepetlisaurs can drill through rock and solid phlogiston. They have lived beside the tribe since before anyone's great-great-grandfather, and their nests are never far from human homes. The tribe treats them as equals rather than livestock or pets, and most bonds form freely: a Tepetlisaur simply starts following a person home. Legend says the ancestor of all Tepetlisaurs was a drake as large as a mountain, and that the huge drill-shaped objects in the cliffs above the settlement are the remains of its horn.

**Craft and machines.** The tribe's smiths use phlogiston engravings to make many of Natlan's phlogiston-powered machines. Xilonen built Kachina's bouncing drill, the Turbo Twirly, as well as Chasca's oversized gun, Mavuika's phlogiston-powered motorcycle and sunglasses, and her own phlogiston-propelled roller skates. Forging Ancient Names is the tribe's most solemn craft, and Xilonen insists it is above all a matter of technique and study.

**Dance.** Other tribes joke that dancing runs in the Children's blood. The tribe holds dance-offs at Stage Tepetl, and the daily Drillbit Dance Dance-Off has reached its 127,751st round.

History: **The founding.** In the age of myth, before Och-Kan's reign some 2,000 years ago, the twins Ixquieh and Ahpub, orphaned under a Dragonlord, reunited with help from the Collective of Plenty and "the clans of the mines". They became two of Xbalanque's Six Heroes. Ixquieh, first bearer of Baraka and called the "Hero of the Forged Flame", is honoured as the tribe's founder and first chief. When Och-Kan ordered that fleeing dragons be hunted, she refused to hand over the "beasts hidden in the mountains", the Tepetlisaurs. Ahpub, by then chief of the Collective of Plenty, came for them, and the twins' quarrel ended in Ixquieh's death. Accounts of how she died differ.

**Against Och-Kan.** Sakkuk's father was executed for protecting the tribe's saurians. Sakkuk became the first hero to join the Scarlet-Eyed Youth against Och-Kan, was the last of her companions left alive, and later served as chief. She also bore the Ancient Name Baraka.

**The cataclysm.** Five hundred years ago, Chief Sundjatta and his saurian companion Muhuru joined Tenoch's heroes against the Abyss. He died in the final battle. At home, Elder Traore led the tribe against an Abyssal tide that reached the mountains, and the tribe trapped the Abyss deep underground beneath the Shadow Pins in the Sulfurous Veins.

**The present.** In 5.0 Kachina brought the Traveler to the tribe. She later failed to return from the Night Kingdom after her team's victory, until a rescue brought her back. When the Abyss invaded Natlan in 5.1, Pacal, Kachina and Xilonen oversaw the tribe's evacuation to the Stadium, with Pacal among the last to leave, covering the rear. After the war ended in victory (5.3), the tribe announced a celebration at Stage Tepetl for the victory and the fallen.

Relations: - **Pyro Archon**: Mavuika visited the tribe several times after the war to ask about its losses and support rebuilding. Xilonen has made things for her, including a pair of sunglasses.
- **Other tribes**: Pacal recommends the People of the Springs and the Flower-Feather Clan to visitors. Chasca mediates disputes over trade. Xilonen forges for the Collective of Plenty, and Ifa of the Flower-Feather Clan treats the tribe's Tepetlisaurs.
- **Outsiders**: the tribe likes making friends with outsiders and believes the two sides can learn from each other. Pacal once found the Adventurers' Guild a mixed bag, but he welcomed the Traveler warmly once he knew who they were.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe lives on in Tequemecan Valley under Chief Pacal, rebuilding after the Abyss's invasion. Pacal stresses that the victory was real but temporary, and that the tribe must stay vigilant.

Kachina and Xilonen remain its best-known members. After the Night Kingdom was purified, Natlanese people could leave their country more freely. No new Children of Echoes story was found for 6.0-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

54.comment: Children of Echoes: "Children of Echoes" settlement
54.content: The tribe's home lies inside a gorge in Tequemecan Valley, beneath an enormous drill embedded in the cliffs. Stage Tepetl, the dance stage, stands beside the bulletin board. Muhuru's Gemporium sells gem accessories just over the bridge, and steps lead up to the chief for large ore deals. The Macuahuitl Workshop makes heavy-duty tools and weapons, and Xilonen's workshop is nearby. Duels are held on grounds in the mountain behind the stage, because, as Pacal says, the stage is no place for tunnelling. Tepetlisaurs nest close to the houses. An official map description says that, long ago, a sage of Phlogiston Engraving painted murals across the valley's cliffs, and that this is the origin of Natlan's graffiti.

55.comment: Children of Echoes: Ancient Names of the Children of Echoes
55.content: **Baraka** ("blessings") was first borne by the founder Ixquieh; later bearers include Sakkuk, Sundjatta and now Xilonen. **Uthabiti** ("toughness and tenacity") belongs to Kachina, who long doubted she deserved it. Ancient Names are given by the tribe's Wayob and forged into obsidian by Name Engravers. Xilonen, the current Name Engraver, studied under the respected engraver Teyiz, who taught that "stories and equations are, in essence, one and the same". Tlazolli, another forger, bore **Undugu**.

56.content: The Shadow Pins are great stone pillars in the Sulfurous Veins, one Greater Pin and three Lesser Pins. Children of Echoes legend says they pin down a "shadow": the Abyss that Elder Traore and his warriors sealed underground 500 years ago at the cost of their lives. The storyteller Titu looks after them. Even miners know not to touch the phlogiston around them. In 5.0 the Pins began to float and the Greater Pin fell. With the Traveler's help, Titu discovered the true story beneath them.

57.comment: Children of Echoes: Tepetlisaurs and the tribe
57.content: Tepetlisaurs are the tribe's saurian partners. Each tribe bonds best with one kind of saurian, and the Children's is this burrowing kind with its drill-horn, which helps them mine and find the best ore. Companions known by name include Kachina's Ayo, who shows affection by headbutting, and Pacal's Uchu, whom Pacal is always telling to eat less. In Och-Kan's age, the tribe protected its Tepetlisaurs from his dragon hunts, and the father of the hero Sakkuk was executed for it.

58.content: The Drillbit Dance Dance-Off is the tribe's daily dance contest at Stage Tepetl. By the Traveler's time it had passed its 127,751st round, which the wiki works out as roughly 350 years of daily contests. Itzna has won it 200 times, and veterans Zacatula and Tlaco have taken part on 1,200 and 1,700 days. Kachina's dancing is famous in the tribe. In Searing (5.8), Ineffa amazed onlookers by performing "the robot" on the stage.

59.content:
Church of Favonius (also: Favonius Church, Mondstadt Church, the Church of Favonius, Church of the Anemo Archon): The Church of Favonius is Mondstadt's church of the Anemo Archon Barbatos, the nation's patron of freedom. Its clergy pray, run morning prayers and choir, help the sick and answer letters from believers at the Favonius Cathedral in Mondstadt City. The Knights of Favonius manage it, and the two institutions work side by side. Its Seneschal is Seamus Pegg, Cardinal of Daybreak.

The Church is a community of devoted adherents more than a ruling body. Government belongs to the Knights, and the Archon himself does not rule. The Church supplies ritual, charity and a place to bring troubles. Its best-known members are the Deaconess Barbara, the Deacon Dahlia and the unorthodox Sister Rosaria.

Structure: At the top is the Seneschal, Seamus Pegg, who also carries the title Cardinal of Daybreak. Cardinal Calvin ran the Church's affairs during Seamus' absence. Below them are deacons and a deaconess (Dahlia, Barbara), a Mother (Maria), and a body of nuns and sisters. Dahlia also leads the choir as cantor and holds the unique post of Herald of Barbatos. The clergy take turns at routine tasks, such as writing replies to letters from the congregation, and attend compulsory classes, hymn practice and morning prayers.

Some posts are tied to one person. The wiki lists Barbara's title as Shining Idol, Rosaria's as A Nonconforming Sister and Vind's as Storm Watcher. Named nuns and sisters include Annette, Edna, Gotelinde, Grace, Hannelore, Jilliana, Philomena, Victoria and Ophila. Maria is called Mother in Rosaria's story. The Church holds sacred objects in the Cathedral, and the Deaconess is the one who safeguards them. Borrowing the Holy Lyre der Himmel needs written permission from three people: the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative.

Leadership: Seamus Pegg is Seneschal and the senior figure. He is a former famous adventurer born in Nod-Krai who settled in Mondstadt and joined the Church. He is the father of Jean (the Knights' Acting Grand Master) and Barbara (the Deaconess), though he and Jean's mother Frederica Gunnhildr are no longer together. He joined Varka's expedition and handled its paperwork, then came home to Mondstadt and the Cathedral once the Nod-Krai conflict wound down. He greets visitors with a blessing from the Anemo Archon and says he means to shoulder more of the Church's work.

Cardinal Calvin took over Seamus' responsibilities while he was gone. Barbara says he is so busy that he almost never leaves his room, and that she last saw him in person when the Holy Lyre was stolen and he was distraught. Calvin has no voice lines of his own and is known only through others.

Members: Notable members are Seamus Pegg (Seneschal), Cardinal Calvin, Dahlia (Deacon and Herald of Barbatos), Barbara (Deaconess and idol), Mother Maria and Sister Rosaria (who works alone).

- **Barbara**: cheerful, hardworking and loved by the whole city. She became a healer on her father's advice and sings to lift spirits. She admires her sister Jean and is unaware, according to the wiki, that she has met Barbatos.
- **Dahlia**: a young deacon with a love of "drama" and of meddling in other people's troubles. He is not especially devout. He knows Venti is Barbatos and relays news and feedback between the Archon and the people.
- **Rosaria**: the Church's least devout sister, who skips services and dodges overtime. Her real work is investigating suspected threats to Mondstadt, and she is trusted to do it.
- **Victoria**: a nun who looks after Barbara and worries when she goes missing. She asked Dahlia to write a letter for Rosaria's birthday.

Other nuns seen in or around the Cathedral include Jilliana, Grace and Victoria, and the NPCs Lily and Rudolf in daytime, whose roles the wiki does not state. Ophila is a sister who scolds Rosaria for skipping hymn practice in her character story, and the same scene, addressed partly to Mother Maria, ends with Rosaria being asked whether she intends to do any work at all at the Church ("No. I've already found other work.").

Goals: The Church worships the Anemo Archon and tries to keep Mondstadt's faith in freedom alive. It offers spiritual guidance, prayer and charity. Part of its role is practical: looking after the sick, answering the congregation's letters and giving people somewhere to bring their worries. It also cares for the sacred objects that belong to Barbatos.

Methods: Daily life centres on morning prayer, hymn practice and choir, led by Dahlia. Clergy take turns answering letters, and sisters like Barbara use healing and song. Dahlia's approach is unusual: he has been known to settle quarrels by taking the parties to a tavern for a drinking contest, which Jean thinks may not be fair or just. Seekers can bring problems to him because many believe Barbatos listens to him.

Rosaria's methods are quieter and harsher. After sunset she follows, questions and, if she must, kills people judged to be threats, and she does so as a sister of the Church. Her character stories say she learned this skill from her former bandit family, and that she accepts her work being done in secret. The Church also lends its authority at formal events, as when Deacon Dahlia sat as assessor at Albedo's trial in 5.6.

History: **Old Mondstadt and the aristocrats.** Over the centuries the Church followed Mondstadt's rulers. Under the Lawrence-led aristocracy, wiki history based on in-world books says the Church was used to justify the nobles' actions and keep commoners from the truth, and that it split, with higher-ranked clergy backing the nobility.

**Vennessa's restoration.** About 1,000 years ago, after the rebellion, Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius and restored the Church of Favonius, in the stated aim of keeping tyrants from taking power again. Believers mobilised by a "Nameless Shepherd" are said to have joined the rebellion.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: manage the Church and work with it. Jean is Seamus' daughter. Adorno was buried at the Favonius Cathedral after dying in 6.6. Albedo's 5.6 trial involved both bodies.
- **Barbatos**: the Church's god. Venti is Barbatos, and Dahlia is the Herald who knows it.
- **Hexenzirkel**: Alice, an elder of the Hexenzirkel, coached Barbara on becoming an idol, a link that has no direct connection to Church doctrine.

- **Rosaria and Varka**: Varka brought Rosaria to Mondstadt after the Knights wiped out her bandit crew and told her to be cleansed by the Archon's light at the Cathedral. She stayed in the clergy but kept to her own path.
- **Fatui**: a Fatui diplomat is seen at the Cathedral, and a Fatui agent stole the Holy Lyre during the Prologue.

Reputation: Mondstadters love Barbara, so the Cathedral draws visitors who hope to see her. Many believe Dahlia has the Archon's favour. Rosaria is thought of as a lazy, chain-smoking sister, while few know of her secret work. The map description of the Cathedral muses on whether a city taught freedom by its Archon should spend so much wealth on such a grand building.

Barbara says that even inside the church people come hoping to greet her, and in her hangout she hides from an admirer while gathering herbs at Wolvendom. Jean and others admire Barbara's effort. The Church's reputation for gentleness fits Barbara, but Rosaria and Dahlia show that the clergy is not as uniform as its image.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Seamus Pegg is back in Mondstadt as Seneschal. The Church is peaceful and no Church-centred story content was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

Dahlia is active as Deacon and Herald. Barbara, Rosaria and the sisters continue their duties. Seamus has returned from the expedition and is working to share the load.

60.content: The Favonius Cathedral, also called the Mondstadt Cathedral, stands in Mondstadt City and is run by the Church of Favonius. Clergy work and pray here, and its grand architecture resembles real-world Gothic cathedrals. A basement at the back holds the Holy Lyre der Himmel under guard. The Cathedral is a place of prayer, choir practice and counsel. The Traveler can meet nuns such as Jilliana, Grace and Victoria there, and Seamus Pegg in the later story.

61.comment: Church of Favonius: Holy Lyre der Himmel
61.content: The Holy Lyre der Himmel is the lyre the Anemo Archon Barbatos once played. Its frame is rosewood, carved with a pattern of flowing wind, according to Venti. It is used in the Ludi Harpastum festival, and any other use requires signed documents from the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative. The Church keeps it in the Cathedral basement. In the Prologue the Traveler and Venti obtained it, lost it to a Fatui agent, and later returned it to Barbara in damaged condition, which Venti hid with an Anemo illusion.

62.comment: Church of Favonius: Seamus Pegg, Seneschal
62.content: Seamus is the Church's Seneschal. He was an adventurer from Nod-Krai who met the wandering Varka abroad, persuaded him to return home and then settled in Mondstadt himself. He married Frederica Gunnhildr and had two daughters, Jean and Barbara. The marriage ended, and Barbara stayed with him. He dryly scolds Varka for his antics and handles most administrative work on his own. He saw Eroch's plot unfold, and he regretted the diplomatic cost to Mondstadt when Dottore took credit for killing Ursa. Seamus went on Varka's expedition, returned after the Nod-Krai conflict and now helps shoulder the Church's work.

63.comment: Church of Favonius: Dahlia, Herald of Barbatos
63.content: Dahlia is a deacon of the Church and choir cantor who holds the post of Herald of Barbatos. He knows Venti is the Anemo Archon, passes news to him and brings his feedback to the people. He was a nosy helper before joining the clergy, and he is not especially religious. Venti helped create the Herald role so that he could contribute without being tied to dull routine. Dahlia is a quick learner who memorised hymns overnight when challenged. He took part in the Knights' plan around Albedo's trial in 5.6.

64.content: Barbara is the Deaconess and a beloved idol. She joined the Church young, and her father Seamus served in it too. She has a Hydro Vision that appeared after she sang a lullaby to a feverish boy. Her father counselled her to become a healer. She safeguards religious artifacts and worships Barbatos, but the wiki states she is unaware she has met him. She sometimes hides from crowds to recover alone, and her story with Victoria shows how the nuns look after her.

65.comment: Church of Favonius: Rosaria, the Nonconforming Sister
65.content: Rosaria is a sister in name, famous for skipping classes, hymn practice and morning prayers. Raised by bandits and offered a second chance by Varka, she entered the Church and secretly works as its investigator of threats. She is unpredictable and disappears for days. Barbara keeps trying to bring her back to duties, and Dahlia once covered her letter-writing shift. She refuses overtime. The Church has never imposed serious consequences for her behaviour, and Rosaria has said she has found "other work".

66.comment: Church of Favonius: Vennessa and the Church
66.content: Wiki history based on in-world books says the Church was bent to support the Lawrence aristocracy, and its higher clergy took the nobles' side in a schism. Adherents, mobilised by a figure called the Nameless Shepherd, joined Vennessa's rebellion. After victory, Vennessa founded the Knights and restored the Church, so that tyrants could not seize Mondstadt again. These accounts come from medium-confidence sources and some details remain inferred.

67.comment: Church of Favonius: Morning prayers and the Weinlesefest
67.content: Dahlia leads morning prayers, which the congregation uses to ask Barbatos for guidance. The clergy take turns answering letters. Rosaria, whose turn came up during a long absence, left a pile that Dahlia dealt with in her place. During the Weinlesefest event, Rosaria said she hid to avoid extra work and the sung poetry event, watching for Dahlia or Victoria. The Weinlesefest remark comes from a limited-time event.

68.content:
Collective of Plenty (also: Teteocan, Teteocan tribe, the Collective of Plenty): The Collective of Plenty, also called the Teteocan, is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its people farm the rich volcanic soil beside the Great Volcano of Tollan in Atocpan and live alongside Tatankasaurs, their bonded saurians. The tribe is known across Natlan for two things: the best fruit and vegetables in the nation, and a culture built around physical strength, from bodybuilding contests to wrestling. Its chief is Acatl, a cheerful masked wrestler.

Notable members include Iansan, head coach of the tribe's fitness club and bearer of the Ancient Name Uwezo ("Power"), and her star pupil Varesa, an orchard manager and Patrol Team warrior whom local children call the "Masked Hero". Of all the tribes, they live the farthest from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

Culture: Fitness is close to sacred here: Iansan's stories say it is second in importance only to the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Most adults have huge, heavily muscled frames. Young people show off their muscles to each other as a friendly greeting, and a fitness coach is only taken seriously if they are very strong. Wrestling Tatankasaurs is a long-standing tradition, and beating one is a great honour. Some warriors even seek out wild Halberd-Crest Birds to find out "whose head is harder".

Many wrestlers wear masks. When two masked fighters duel, the loser takes off their mask and the winner keeps theirs, keeping an air of mystery that invites others to challenge them. Acatl says he has never once been unmasked by human or saurian. When young tribespeople ask how they would know he is not an imposter, he tells them to face him in the ring, because "muscles... never lie".

The tribe values courage, perseverance and refusing to back down over formality, and treats guests generously. Acatl's own motto is "If it's something you believe in, just do it!" He welcomes returning friends with a hearty tribal meal. Varesa says that in the tribe, a person's birthday is celebrated with a bonfire feast among friends. Tired tribespeople drink a special fruit juice, Fruits Aplenty, to recover. Honours are physical too: Kitera, a warrior of the tribe, won an honorary belt so heavy that two people struggled to lift it, so he had a lighter copy made to wear while training.

Places: The tribe's settlement, also named "Collective of Plenty", lies on fertile plains below the Great Volcano of Tollan. Volcanic ash has made the land rich, and its golden harvests are the tribe's pride. At its centre is the Grand Wrestling Grounds, also called the Resonating Arena: a raised arena decorated with huge bull horns, where the tribe's athletic competitions are held. Varesa's family orchard stands just outside the settlement and is guarded by her Tatankasaur Vanana.

The settlement also has a training ground with a fitness coach and trainees, machines for making Fruits Aplenty and puffed grainfruit bars, and bulletin boards. Runes are supposed to keep saurians from other places out of the tribe's grounds. The volcano sometimes throws boulders called Pulverite into the area. Locals simply smash them, with their shoulders, feet or heads, or with a charging Tatankasaurus. Tonaca, at the Grand Wrestling Grounds, handles the tribe's relations with visitors who help out.

Structure: The chief leads the tribe, with the elders also taking part in major decisions such as war planning. The fitness club is one of the tribe's central institutions. Meztcala founded it, and its head coach is a figure of real authority: Acatl was both chief and head coach before Iansan took over the club. The Patrol Team defends the tribe against monsters and the Abyss; Varesa is a core member, and Iansan led its counterattacks in the three-pronged Abyss assault. Like every tribe, the Collective has a Wayob, which chooses bearers of Ancient Names. For the Collective of Plenty, the name "Power" (Uwezo) carries special weight, standing for unrivalled honour and responsibility.

The tribe's Tatankasaurs have a chief of their own. In Iansan's time this was Emela, an orphaned Tatankasaurus raised by the tribe who grew larger than any other Tatankasaurus there. She was killed fighting in the war against the Abyss invasion. In Ahpub's era, when the tribe's chief vanished, Och-Kan's emissaries tried to persuade the tribe to hand authority to the Grand Alliance until it chose a new chief.

Leadership: Chief Acatl is a tall, powerfully built man who always wears a horned wrestling mask. He is warm, relaxed about formalities and attentive to the tribe's young people, and he has long kept a concerned eye on Varesa.

Acatl coached the fitness club when the young Iansan, newly chosen by the Ancient Name "Power", asked to train. When she was badly hurt trying to lift a barbell, he was criticised for not stopping her. He still visited her and told her that fitness is "a question of choice", not of credentials. He also kept a watchful eye on the young Varesa, and agreed with the warriors to admit her to wrestling training. During the war he led the tribe's defence and repelled the Abyss.

Members: - **Iansan**: head coach, nutritionist and founder of the Pilgrimage Victors Academy. She holds an all-time record for Pilgrimage victories and bears the Ancient Name Uwezo.
- **Varesa**: orchard manager, Patrol Team warrior and famous competitive eater. Her fruit is sold to every tribe.
- **Acatl**: the chief.
- **Bennett** is the son of Macani, a member of the tribe (see the entry on Macani).
- Residents of the settlement include the chef Atolli, the reputation advisor Tonaca, the fitness coach Tecoma, the wrestling referee Macacoz, the blacksmith Xona and the self-styled "strongest in the Collective of Plenty" trainer Ma'chah. The merchant Cintli sells the tribe's produce at the Stadium.

Goals: The tribe's aims are simple: feed Natlan, grow strong, and protect its homeland and its neighbours. Its teaching, passed down from Meztcala, is that strength is something anyone can choose to build. Iansan has pushed this outward, offering training to people from any tribe.

Methods: The tribe's economy rests on farming, and it grows enough to sell a good share of its produce to the other tribes. Varesa's produce even reaches buyers abroad, including Escoffier and Dori. Tonaca says that the tribe, as Natlan's most agriculturally developed, puts resource coordination and management first. In war, the tribe relies on its Patrol Team and on warriors toughened by constant training. When the Abyss struck in force, the elders spread the defence out in layers, kept the front lines far from civilians, and sent elite strike teams to take out the enemy's leaders.

History: **Founding era.** The tribes date back at least to the age of Xbalanque and Och-Kan's Grand Alliance; Och-Kan's rule is placed about 2,000 years ago. The tribe's founding is linked to Ahpub, first bearer of the Ancient Name Uwezo and one of the original heroes. He and his twin sister Ixquieh followed Xbalanque and joined Och-Kan's Grand Alliance. Ahpub became chief of the Collective of Plenty, and Ixquieh chief of the Children of Echoes. Ahpub hated dragons. When Och-Kan ordered the pursuit of the fleeing dragons, Ahpub was the only hero who obeyed, and he led the tribe's warriors to his sister's mountains. Their argument ended with Ixquieh dead by his blade and Ahpub gone into the fire. Accounts of their deaths differ.

**Settling the volcano.** Under Chief Meztcala, during a dangerous eruption cycle, the tribe finally secured its home at the volcano's foot by teaching every member to fight monsters and magma. That was the origin of the fitness club.

**Five hundred years ago.** Wanjiru, a "great runner" of the tribe and bearer of Uwezo, was one of the six heroes who fought the Abyss beside Mavuika. She was Mavuika's friend and regular wrestling partner, and she won their last match before Mavuika became Archon. Wanjiru died in the final battle. Fietena, a masked wrestler born in the tribe who had grown up listening to Wanjiru's stories, helped defend Natlan through the hard decade that followed.

**Modern era.** When Varesa was five, the Abyss raided the tribe and ruined her family's orchard. Later, during an eruption cycle, the Abyss launched a three-pronged assault meant to isolate and wipe out the tribe's warriors. With only a few Scions of the Canopy couriers to help, the elders' layered defence and repeated counterattacks under Iansan won through. Varesa won her Vision in that battle.

Relations: - **Other tribes**: the Collective of Plenty feeds them. Varesa's cart reaches from the Children of Echoes to the Flower-Feather Clan, and Iansan's academy welcomes other tribes' trainees. Fietena's marriage into the Flower-Feather Clan strengthened ties between the two tribes.
- **Children of Echoes**: linked through the twin founders Ahpub and Ixquieh, whose adventures inspired traditions in both tribes. Varesa learned mask-making from their smiths.
- **Scions of the Canopy**: their couriers were the only reinforcements in the three-pronged Abyss assault.
- **Masters of the Night-Wind**: Citlali helped Iansan bind a young Tatankasaurus spirit, Alaye, into its skull.
- **Pyro Archon**: Mavuika is admired here; Wanjiru was her friend and wrestling rival.
- **Abyss**: the tribe's chief enemy, repelled many times.

Reputation: To other Natlanese, the Collective of Plenty means "universal fitness" and sweet fruit and fresh vegetables. Not everyone agrees: Suriqui, a dissenter within the tribe, calls its muscle-worshippers a "bunch of meatheads" and insists the heroes of old carried a protective layer of fat. In children's stories, the tribe's "Masked Hero" (Varesa) shows up, wreathed in lightning, wherever monsters run amok.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is thriving under Chief Acatl. It survived the Abyss war, rebuilt, and fought off the Abyss Order's 5.7 attack.

Iansan's academy now stands near the Stadium and takes trainees from every tribe. Varesa is training to fight without her mask. The green mushrooms are being kept in check under Sumeru's watch. Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya content (6.0-7.1) only touches the tribe in passing, with a member found in Nasha Town.

69.comment: Collective of Plenty: Iansan and the fitness club
69.content: Iansan's family carries the "Blood of Egungun": none of them ever grow taller than a child. The tribe took the family in and always protected them, keeping them off the front lines as medics and cooks. When the Ancient Name "Power" chose Iansan, many tribespeople doubted her. She asked Acatl, then chief and head coach, to train her, injured herself badly on her first lift, and came back anyway. Her mother suggested building on what the family was good at, treating injuries and cooking. Iansan then created a training method of steady routines, controlled calories and precise nutrition, which introduced the science of nutrition to Natlan. She later beat the Tatankasaurs' chief, succeeded Acatl as head coach and set a Pilgrimage victory record. When other tribes began calling her bloodline a gift that explained her wins, she moved the club close to the Stadium as the Pilgrimage Victors Academy. Her flyers promise that toil, not birth, gives strength.

70.comment: Collective of Plenty: Varesa's orchard and the Masked Hero
70.content: Varesa's family orchard, just outside the settlement, sends fresh produce to every tribe. Varesa took it over after years of training and runs it with her Tatankasaur Vanana. Children's stories tell of a lightning-wreathed "Masked Hero" whose rescues happen to follow the orchard's trade routes. Varesa's mask is based on one worn by the tribe's heroine Fietena, and grateful villagers draw a little mask on their thank-you letters to her. She has entered the Pilgrimage five times and never got past the team stage, because she cannot bring herself to fight her fellow Natlanese seriously. Against the Abyss, though, she has never lost while defending the tribe.

71.comment: Collective of Plenty: The three-pronged Abyss assault
71.content: In Varesa's second month on the Patrol Team, the Abyss attacked the Collective of Plenty from three sides during one of the volcano's eruption cycles. Only a handful of Scions of the Canopy couriers arrived to help. The elders spread the defences out in layers, kept the front lines away from civilians, and posted the couriers on high ground to track the enemy's leaders. Elite warriors then struck those leaders from behind. Each counterattack lost more fighters. In the last, after Iansan cleared the way, Varesa came back carrying a wounded older warrior and dragging a mitachurl, put on her tattered mask and destroyed the enemy leader. Iansan dug her out of the battlefield asleep, with a new Electro Vision in her hand. She slept for half a month and remembers nothing of the fight.

72.comment: Collective of Plenty: Ahpub and the Grand Alliance
72.content: Ahpub, the first bearer of Uwezo, fought with blowdarts and had a fiery temper. He and his twin Ixquieh lost their parents to a dragon lord's cruelty and were reunited with the help of the Collective of Plenty and the mine clans. They swore to end suffering, followed Xbalanque and joined Och-Kan's Grand Alliance, and Ahpub became the Collective's chief. When Och-Kan ordered the fleeing dragons pursued, Ahpub alone obeyed. He marched the tribe's warriors to his sister's mountains and demanded she hand over the saurians she sheltered. Their private argument ended when his blade, meant only to intimidate her, struck her throat. He carried her into the fire and was never seen again. Afterwards Och-Kan quietly tried to take both leaderless tribes under the Alliance's authority.

73.comment: Collective of Plenty: Wanjiru and Fietena
73.content: Wanjiru, the tribe's Uwezo bearer 500 years ago, was called "the great runner". With her Tatankasaurus Kayeke she joined the six heroes who fought the Abyss alongside Mavuika. She was Mavuika's close friend and wrestling rival, and she died in the heroes' final battle. Fietena, who had followed Wanjiru as a girl, was a masked wrestler of the tribe who never received an Ancient Name. She defended Natlan through the decade after Mavuika entered the Sacred Flame, married into the Flower-Feather Clan, and passed the torch to Taika once Abyssal wounds had worn down her body. Stories say she could send lightning back into the sky. She is now a comic-book favourite who wore five different masks, and Varesa's mask is modelled on one of them.

74.content:
Communications Office (also: Heji Hall, Héjì-tīng, Liyue Communications Office): The Communications Office is one of the Eight Trades, the commercial sectors under the jurisdiction of the Liyue Qixing. It is the Hall in charge of transportation: moving goods and shipments around Liyue and arranging overseas shipping.

Its staff are officials rather than merchants. The Office also takes on related public works, so it is as much a transport authority as a trade body. Its base is Hezhe Post.

Structure: The Office is a Hall of the Eight Trades and answers to the Liyue Qixing like the other Halls. It is large because its duties cover more than shipping. No head is named in the sources checked, and no ranks are described. The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is listed on the wiki as a sub-faction.

Known associates are Master Qin "Thunder Hand", a bodyguard, and friends of Yanfei, who are named as members on the Eight Trades page. Treat any further individual as unknown.

Goals: By its staff's own account, the Office exists to keep goods moving. In the words of a member, good roads, bridges, waterways and docks are critical to getting goods to every part of Liyue.

Methods: The Office handles shipments and transport within Liyue and overseas shipping logistics, and oversees some construction and road management. An NPC mentions that it plans to build several small lifts, which should improve local access.

In a scene, expect paperwork, route planning and requests to repair or extend a road or dock, more than market haggling. Outsiders hear of it as the Liyue agency that specialises in overseas shipping.

History: It first appears in version 1.5 content. Canon gives no founding date or earlier history.

Relations: - **Eight Trades and the Liyue Qixing**: the Office is one of four Halls named in canon, and the Qixing hold jurisdiction.
- **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: a listed sub-faction.

- **Yanfei**: her troubles, as told in her voice-overs, involve friends who are members of the Office.
- **Overseas contacts**: foreign visitors know it as the place to arrange shipping from Liyue.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. No new story involving the Office was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

75.content: The wiki lists Hezhe Post as the Communications Office's base. See the location entry for the place itself.

76.content:
Conch Gang (also: the Conch Gang, Conch Gang kids): The Conch Gang is an informal band of stray children in Nasha Town, in Nod-Krai. Katya, the retired adventurer who runs the restaurant Speranza, feeds, houses and employs them while letting them live freely. The gang makes its own decisions by vote, and Speranza is its home base.

It is not an official guild or criminal outfit. Maite describes it as a mutual aid and coordination group for like-minded people of similar age. Its name comes from a local folk tale about children who ruled Nasha Town and called each other together by blowing a conch shell.

Structure: There is no named leader. A new member can join only if every existing member agrees. The Traveler remarks that the gang has many members and some pretty good benefits: food, shelter and work at Speranza. Members have great freedom to follow their own interests, from studying jellies to travelling abroad. The gang usually takes only children and sends members away at a certain age, though there is a precedent for admitting someone older.

Katya is the adult guardian but not a member. Helka calls her "not one of us" and a trustworthy person to turn to. Members treat each other as a chosen family: Helka calls her friends more like family, even though they are not related by blood. Havu, a local child outside the gang, claims not to care about them and admits they once fought, yet her idle line suggests she might think about joining if they begged.

Members: Current members named on the wiki:
- Jurva: the super chef at Speranza. She hopes everyone can live the lives they want.
- Maisie: a timid girl who works at Speranza as a host and does simple chores. Helka says her constitution is too frail for travel, and she keeps in touch with Helka through pictures and postcards.
- Mikko: a Speranza host who worries Katya is angry after he dropped and broke some things.
- Helka: a member who left Nod-Krai to catalogue monsters of other nations.
- Maite: a self-styled master thief, met at the Crab Tsar's Palace after The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar.
- Auni: a small girl who holds funerals for animals, met in Friends of Moleyvalley.
- Semyon: a member who went to Maroon Basin to research Tassel Jellies.

Former members: Aino and Linnea (both playable characters) and Tapani.

Maite dubs the Traveler an official friend of the gang, but tells them they are too old to join. Auni tells the Traveler and Paimon to call her "Big Sis", says Jurva gave her pocket money, and insists that anyone who gets help should repay it and say thanks. Tapani, met at The Flagship tavern, says Katya raised him but that he does not hide it or shout it from the rooftops, and he recommends Speranza.

Goals: The group has no stated mission. Their shared aim is to look after one another and live as they like. Jurva says Katya taught her that it is better to have impossible dreams than none, and that the younger kids living as they do now means her own dream has come halfway true.

History: Canon gives no founding date. The story of children conquering Nasha Town is folklore. In the present, Katya, a former Treasure Hoarders adventurer who retired because of injuries, took in children left to fend for themselves on the streets. She says she could not stand seeing them without shelter and warm food. The kids work for their keep.

Helka and Maisie are first mentioned in the On the Trail of Behemoths event, which is where the Conch Gang first appears.

Relations: Katya is their protector and employer, and Speranza is their base. The Traveler is a friend of the gang but not a member. Derwent taught some of them to read.

Maite says Katya warned against making contact with the Frostmoon Scions, and that she herself was nearly caught by them once.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Conch Gang is active around Speranza in Nasha Town. Helka remains abroad on her monster-cataloguing journey, and Maisie stays in town. The sources checked show no appearance by the gang in Version 7.0 or 7.1 content.

77.comment: Conch Gang: Joining the Conch Gang
77.content: Joining takes a unanimous yes from every current member. Havu says it is somewhat difficult. The gang usually accepts only children and sends members away at a certain age, though there is a precedent for older newcomers. Maite told the Traveler they are too old, and Helka said age might complicate things but did not rule it out.

78.comment: Conch Gang: The Conch Shell Tale
78.content: Jurva says a story goes that children once built Nasha Town and called each other together by blowing into a conch shell, voting on every decision. She says nobody really believes it and wonders who made it up. The Traveler's voice-over line adds that the town developed into the bustling settlement it is today, and the gang no longer dominates it.

79.comment: Conch Gang: Helka and the Monster Handbook
79.content: Helka appears in the On the Trail of Behemoths event. She is a Conch Gang member who knows every monster in Nod-Krai and left to learn about monsters elsewhere. Her task is an illustrated handbook of 100 monster varieties, and she posted a commission with the Adventurers' Guild for help. She says Katya told her a good enough book might get her published. She sends copies and pictures to Maisie, who loves monster stories.

80.content: Speranza is the main restaurant in Nod-Krai, in Nasha Town on Lempo Isle, run by Katya. Staff include the chef Jurva and the hosts Maisie and Mikko. A fortune wheel stands outside, and a dog named Pavlov is nearby. The Conch Gang treats it as its home base. It sells food and ingredients, and completing the quest Rest Beyond Reach gives a permanent discount.

81.content:
Confrerie of Cabriere (also: Confrérie de Cabrière, Cabriere Confrerie): The Confrerie of Cabriere was a merchants' guild in Fontaine, founded and led by Marcel. Publicly it was one of the richest and most powerful trading guilds in the nation and a friendly sister body to the Spina di Rosula. In truth it was a front for Marcel's underground trade in Sinthe, which paid for his experiments. It was dissolved after Marcel was exposed in the 4.0 Archon Quest.

Callas and the Spina di Rosula helped it grow when it was only reselling everyday goods. Its Sinthe business was wiped out with the guild, though a successor "Imitation Sinthe" trade later appeared.

Structure: Marcel led and founded the guild. The wiki names two other people tied to it: Calcagni, a staff member (found as an open-world NPC in the Court of Fontaine, listed as formerly of the Confrerie), and Truand, an enforcer who collected debts. Its shops were built to a single design with a plain, approachable look, so that customers of every budget would feel welcome. The same buildings carried anti-theft features: walls that would warp if hammered repeatedly and a claimed 100-year rustproof finish.

The guild owned a countryside estate that once hosted a large banquet. Marcel also kept a large number of privately owned Gardemeks, which the wiki says his wealth made possible.

Goals: In public, trade and commerce. In reality, to bankroll Marcel's experiments with Primordial Seawater. Marcel's deeper aim was personal, not commercial, and belongs to his own story.

Methods: Marcel sold Sinthe, a drug made from diluted Primordial Seawater that causes euphoria and pleasant hallucinations. It is highly addictive, can cause lasting problems with focus and emotional control, and brings withdrawal symptoms of fatigue, anxiety and paranoia. Many families were ruined by it. By the time of his arrest he had even made a fruit-flavoured version. Marcel protected the operation by removing threats. He framed Callas for murder after she banned Sinthe in Poisson and found its production base.

The Confrerie's front business gave the trade a legitimate face and a reason to move goods and money. Truand's debt collecting was part of how it applied pressure.

History: At first the Confrerie only resold daily goods, with support from Callas and the Spina di Rosula, and grew into one of the richest guilds in Fontaine. Marcel later began the Sinthe trade. When Callas, the head of the Spina di Rosula, banned Sinthe in Poisson and tracked down the production base, Marcel framed her for murder, which led to her death in a duel against Champion Duelist Clorinde. In the Chapter IV act As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, the Traveler and Navia exposed Marcel as the culprit behind the serial disappearances, and he died in the final quest of that act. Authorities then stopped Sinthe production and began confiscating what remained on the market.

Relations: - **Spina di Rosula**: the Confrerie was regarded as its sister organisation. Callas led the Spina and supported the Confrerie early on, and her daughter is Navia.
- **Marcel**: founder and leader, whose double life the guild hid.
- **Navia and the Traveler**: exposed the scheme.
- **Clorinde**: the Champion Duelist who fought Callas in the duel Marcel arranged.

Reputation: Before the exposure the Confrerie was known as one of the richest and most powerful merchant guilds in Fontaine, and as an honest sister to the Spina di Rosula. Afterwards its name is linked with the Sinthe scandal.

Secrets: Its Sinthe business and Marcel's identity were hidden until the Chapter IV investigation. Marcel was really Vacher, an adventurer from Snezhnaya who took on a new identity.

Status as of 7.1: Disbanded. The Confrerie ended when Marcel was exposed in 4.0.

As of 7.1 no revival of the Confrerie was found. Canon only mentions it in the past tense, although Imitation Sinthe smuggling (4.5) shows the drug's market outlasted it.

82.content: Sinthe is a drink made from Primordial Seawater diluted with ordinary water. It gives short-term euphoria and pleasant hallucinations, then erodes concentration and emotional control, and stopping brings fatigue, anxiety and paranoia. It is highly addictive and wrecked many families. Marcel made and sold it to fund his experiments, and the Confrerie of Cabriere was its commercial front. Production ended after his arrest. Later, "Imitation Sinthe" appeared to mimic its effects, made from ingredients that have many ordinary uses, and the Traveler helped the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol expose a smuggling ring in the 4.5 event Checks and Cats.

83.comment: Confrerie of Cabriere: Truand and Calcagni
83.content: Truand is a quest-only Fontainian enforcer for the Confrerie who is shown collecting debts, including from a woman named Estelle. The wiki says these debts were later tied to the Gardemek force used against Navia. Calcagni is an open-world NPC in the Court of Fontaine's Vasari Passage, labelled as a former member of the Confrerie's staff; canon says nothing more about the role.

key: Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty
84.content:
Corps of Thirty (also: the Corps of Thirty, Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty): The Corps of Thirty is the mercenary brigade that guards Sumeru City. It is not an official army. It is a permanently hired brigade of Eremites, kept on retainer by the Sumeru Akademiya, and its members wear teal-green scarves instead of the crimson ones of other Eremites. Its base is the Citadel of Regzar, and its commander is the Parchamdar, Rukh Shah.

Its name remembers its origin: thirty mercenaries hired by the Akademiya's sages. It has since grown far larger, but the name stayed. The Corps defends the city, polices it, and handles the everyday problems of residents.

Structure: A Parchamdar commands the Corps (the word means roughly "standard-bearer"). A Consultant serves beside the Parchamdar as a second, administrative leader.

The wiki calls the Corps the oldest of the Eremite brigades (Rukh Shah himself says only "among the oldest"). The wiki, citing the quest "The Trail of the God of Wisdom", says it manages and coordinates the affairs of the other mercenary brigades, though what is visible in play is mostly its work in Sumeru City. The Akademiya employs a liaison, Effendi, to coordinate between the scholars and the Corps. Staff at the Citadel of Regzar include a logistics officer (Yunus, nicknamed "Bigfish"), a messenger called the "Swallow" (Sekkura) and a member nicknamed "Goat" (Udad). Rank-and-file mercenaries are posted around Treasures Street and the Puspa Cafe.

Management of manpower, training and supplies is relaxed. Sido, who spoke for the Corps at the 4.7 wargame event, said that the Corps relies on individual blacksmiths rather than a standard supply system, and that skill levels vary greatly among its members. A Su Ding briefing in the same event relays the Corps representative's claim that it is lightly armed on purpose, so that it can fight in environments from desert to rainforest on small supplies, which leaves it at a disadvantage against heavily armoured foes.

Leadership: Rukh Shah is the Parchamdar. He is the youngest person ever to hold the post. The Consultant, Asfand, is a retired veteran who still advises him.

Rukh Shah greets visitors by explaining his role and offering the Corps' help in town, then warns them to be careful of other Eremites outside the city, even in Port Ormos. According to the Swallow Sekkura, he is supposedly from the rainforest, not the desert, which is very rare among Eremites, and he gets along both with desert people and with Akademiya researchers. She also repeats a rumor that he was once a researcher himself; Effendi, the Akademiya's liaison, says the Parchamdar used to be a researcher. Asfand says he retired but was asked by Rukh Shah to advise because he has served in both the Corps and other groups, and he offers to settle unexpected conflicts.

Asfand's idle thoughts say he wishes Dehya would join the Corps, because it needs more people like her. Rukh Shah's idle thoughts say only that the workload is increasing again.

Members: Dehya, the "Flame-Mane", was once a member and is respected by the Corps. Other named members include Sido, the Swallow Sekkura, the logistics officer Yunus, Udad, the mercenaries Hakan and Farid, and Izem, a veteran now retired to the Puspa Cafe.

Asfand calls Dehya a reliable partner and one of the best in the Corps, adds that she speaks frankly, and says she handled her recent commission well (she met the young lady of the Homayani family, Dunyarzad, and made friends). Sido says that everyone in the Corps greatly respects her. She looked out for many of its members, and many followed her into battle. The wiki lists her Corps affiliation as "formerly". Sekkura longs to visit Aaru Village again and says she has not seen Candace for ages.

Sido appears only in limited-time events. In Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2), he led a Corps operation after the Beast Tamers Tournament: Cyno's letter says Sido confirmed all the locations where the remaining criminals were likely to appear and that the Corps could capture them with a limited number of people. In the 4.7 wargame event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation he represented the Corps in a delegation of regional armed services.

Goals: The Corps' job is to keep Sumeru City safe: defend it, guard it against criminals, and deal with disorders that the Akademiya or ordinary residents report. Most tasks are assigned by the Akademiya, plus requests from civilians. The Corps does not make policy.

Methods: Corps members patrol the city, take on residents' commissions and keep watch over crowds during festivals. During the Akademiya's Parade of Providence event, Rukh Shah said he had increased patrols because the influx of tourists gave schemers cover, and during the Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses event he asked people to report anything unusual to the nearest Corps member. Sekkura says that dusk birds now carry many messages, which lightened her errands but added the care of the birds.

In the world quest Corps of Thirty Recruitment, Effendi explains that the Corps is overburdened by residents' small requests on top of defending the whole city. He recruits the Traveler as an assistant for those commissions, with fair pay for each job, and says that doing them well will raise the Traveler's standing with residents. That quest unlocks the Sumeru reputation menu.

Relations: The Corps works for the Akademiya, has an uneasy relationship with other Eremites, and shares Sumeru City's security with the matra.

Other Eremites are sometimes hostile toward it. In the 3.1 Archon Quest The Gaze From a Certain God, an Eremite leader named Tashfin says his brigade is nothing like "those government lapdogs who don't even get scraps", meaning the Corps. The Eremites page mentions a swindler, Kasim, who uses the Eremite name for personal gain and is known as a fraud by the Corps. Alhaitham notes the Corps' poor relationship with the Ayn Al-Ahmar, devout followers of King Deshret who loudly denounce Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. In the repeatable Reputation Request Eremite Mayhem, residents ask the Corps to deal with Eremites dumping refuse on Devantaka Mountain, troubling the road to Caravan Ribat and skulking on the outskirts of Sumeru City.

Besides the matra, who deal with scholars and Akademiya affairs, the Corps is the city's armed force. It is not a branch of the Akademiya or of the matra, and its pay depends on the Akademiya. Sido told the 4.7 wargame audience that the Akademiya pays straightforwardly but is unlikely to set up a dedicated department to supply the Corps.

Reputation: Residents treat the Corps as the people to turn to in town. Rukh Shah tells the Traveler to feel free to seek the Corps' help there. Outside the city, some independent Eremites regard its members as the Akademiya's servants.

History: The Corps began as a band of thirty hired by the sages of the Akademiya and is the oldest of the Eremite brigades. It grew well beyond thirty, but the name remained in memory of the founders (Paimon notes during Gourmet Supremos: Within Our Duties that the Corps has more than thirty people, and the staff there agree). The 3.1 Archon Quest depicts attackers wearing Corps of Thirty uniforms in a cinematic at Pardis Dhyai; canon does not explain this.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Corps of Thirty is still the working force of Sumeru City, based at the Citadel of Regzar under Rukh Shah.

Dehya is still regarded as a friend of the Corps, and Asfand still hopes that she will join it.

85.content: Rukh Shah is the Parchamdar of the Corps of Thirty and the youngest person to hold that post. Sekkura says he is supposedly from the rainforest rather than the desert, which is unusual among Eremites, and that he may once have been a researcher. He explains his role plainly, takes the Corps' workload seriously and warns visitors to be careful about other Eremites outside the city.

86.content: Asfand is the Consultant of the Corps of Thirty, a retired veteran who advises at the Citadel of Regzar at Rukh Shah's request. He has served in the Corps and in other groups. He calls Dehya a reliable partner and one of the best in the Corps, and hopes she will join it. He duels visitors in the Genius Invokation TCG.

87.comment: Corps of Thirty: Citadel of Regzar
87.content: The Citadel of Regzar is the Corps of Thirty's headquarters and barracks, in the middle of Sumeru City near Treasures Street. It is where Corps members coordinate and meet the Akademiya's liaison Effendi. "Regzar" is a Persian word for "desert". NPCs posted there include Rukh Shah, Asfand, Effendi, the Swallow Sekkura, Udad and the logistics officer Yunus.

88.comment: Corps of Thirty: Sido of the Corps of Thirty
88.content: Sido is a Corps of Thirty mercenary who appears only in limited-time events: Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2), where he led the Corps side of the investigation after the Beast Tamers Tournament, and Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation (4.7), where he represented the Corps in a wargame with delegates of the Knights of Favonius, Millelith, Shogunate Samurai and Maison Gardiennage. In the wargame he praised Dehya, described the Corps as one of many Eremite organisations with relaxed management, and said he envied the Millelith's standard training and equipment supply.

89.content: Qanafiya is a quest-only Corps of Thirty member in the 6.6 Archon Quest Darkness Looming. He helps with the evacuation of Caravan Ribat and offers Nefer a ride, and Cyno and Nefer single him out as the suspected traitor. Cyno catches him with an untraceable gold coin and obtains the location of his contact. The Wanderer later suspects the Fatui had written the mole off from the start.

90.content: Tashfin leads an Eremite brigade hired by a mysterious client called "The Outcast" to attack the Traveler at the entrance to Gandharva Ville in the 3.1 Archon Quest The Gaze From a Certain God. When Paimon asks whether they are from the Corps of Thirty, he rejects the comparison and sneers at the Corps as government lapdogs. This shows how some independent Eremites see the Corps.

91.comment: Corps of Thirty: Corps of Thirty Recruitment
91.content: Effendi, a researcher sent by the Akademiya as liaison to the Corps of Thirty, asks the Traveler to take a job as an assistant. The work is completing small commissions from Sumeru City residents so the Corps can focus on defending the city. In return the Traveler is paid per task and builds a reputation among residents.

92.content:
Courier's Longhouse (also: Couriers' Longhouse, Courier's Longhouse (Faction), Natlan couriers): The Courier's Longhouse is the courier agency of the Scions of the Canopy, the Natlan tribe of Coatepec Mountain. Its couriers carry letters and parcels. It accepts ordinary deliveries only, not anything extremely valuable, fragile or dangerous. It is run from a base in the Scions' settlement.

The bulletin board calls the couriers highly skilled professionals whose deliveries almost always arrive, though the Longhouse will not guarantee against accidents along the way.

Structure: The base is the Courier's Longhouse inside the Scions of the Canopy settlement, with a bulletin board beside it. Michica is its manager and is the person customers see to hire a courier. Commissions are taken per delivery, not for fixed periods. Couriers pay management fees, which the Longhouse says go toward standard-issue gear. Michica's gear assessment report goes to Chief Wayna, and the board invites couriers to send feedback to Miss Amauta. Couriers are ranked each month by completed deliveries.

A courier's work is not limited to the settlement. Sorimana, a courier in Tequemecan Valley, leaves regular supply drops of food and other goods at places where couriers tend to stop off. Some are for humans and some are made for their saurian companions. The monthly top ten receive a cash prize, and a chew stick made by Aclla.

Members: Michica is the manager. The bulletin board names Zeila, who topped one monthly ranking with 110 long-distance deliveries in twenty days, and Adama, a star courier who fell to fifth while preparing for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Tundama, Sausa and Sibu are named in that order for the next places, and the top ten includes others. Sorimana is a courier who handles supply drops.

Michica describes some of the younger couriers as careless, thrill-seeking youngsters. In the daily commission "Hey, Your Letter!", the Traveler is asked to recover parcels lost by couriers who ignored instructions and slid down slopes as if on holiday.

Methods: Customers sometimes demand the impossible, such as falcon-speed delivery across a distance greater than the deserts of Sumeru with no damage to the packaging, and the Longhouse says plainly it cannot promise that. It warns couriers delivering to the Flower-Feather Clan to drop off their parcels before accepting any gliding race with clan members. The clan is better at gliding, and a race could damage the contents.

Michica inspects parcels and has confiscated a great deal of contraband, including explosive paint. The usual hazards of the job are broken contents and misdelivered parcels, for example an address written in ink that changes with the outside temperature.

Goals: The Longhouse aims to deliver ordinary items reliably, to maintain the couriers' reputation, and to improve its protective gear, whose usage rate it admits is low.

Relations: It is part of the Scions of the Canopy under Chief Wayna. Its couriers deal with the Flower-Feather Clan, whose gliding skill the board warns couriers about. The board says Kinich, a Scion, is the only one capable of the most extreme deliveries, but he is not a courier.

The board shows couriers taking part in the preparations for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, since the Pilgrimage is the reason Adama's ranking slipped.

Reputation: Publicly the Longhouse presents its couriers as skilled and reliable. Michica is more candid, complaining about contraband and careless couriers, and says the carelessness damages the Scions' reputation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Longhouse is still operating at the Scions of the Canopy under its manager Michica.

After the Natlan war (the Archon Quest No One Fights Alone), Michica says the Longhouse is short-staffed. Many couriers carrying battle reports collapsed from exhaustion and others are still running between camps. Intelligence about the Abyss and reconstruction takes priority, so other parcels may be delayed. No later developments were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

93.content: Michica is the manager of the Courier's Longhouse and an open-world NPC at the Scions of the Canopy. Michica sounds worn down: after joking that the confiscated contraband could stock a shop, Michica insists that it was only an analogy and not a plan to change jobs. After the war in Natlan, Michica reports that couriers are exhausted and stretched thin. Pronouns and age are not stated in the sources checked, and Michica asks the Traveler for help in the daily commission "Hey, Your Letter!" because the Longhouse has too few hands to look for lost parcels.

94.comment: Courier's Longhouse: Couriers' Longhouse Bulletin Board
94.content: The board carries cycling notices from the Longhouse. They include the monthly courier rankings, a warning about racing the Flower-Feather Clan, instructions on hiring a courier, and a request for feedback on standard-issue gear. The gear notice asks couriers to report which parts of the protective gear break, where screws fall out, and which materials suffer from moisture and Gaseous Phlogiston. It admits the gear is not used much at present. The board also says the Longhouse takes commissions per delivery only and cannot guarantee against accidents.

95.content:
Court of Khaenri'ah (also: Court of Khaenriah, Khaenri'ahn Court, Khaenri'ah's court, Royal Court of Khaenri'ah): The Court of Khaenri'ah was the household of King Irmin, the last Vinster King, made up of his advisers, subordinates and others who served him in the underground kingdom. Its best-known member is the seer Vedrfolnir, called "The Visionary". It is chiefly remembered for the ceremony in which the Traveler's Sibling was named heir.

Canon says little about the court as an institution. It is a stub on the wiki, and nearly everything known comes from Dainsleif's memories and from item text about the last years of the Eclipse Dynasty.

Structure: No ranks, offices or numbers are given. The court sat around a king who ruled with a circle of trusted figures, a Knight Marshal, royal guards and the Universitas Magistrorum, but canon does not say which of these counted as the court itself.

Dainsleif was a young knight keeping order in the plaza before the palace gate on the day the heir was announced. He was promoted afterwards and given the title "Twilight Sword"; his talent text in A Space and Time Without You calls him the Khaenri'ahn court guard captain.

Leadership: King Irmin was the only ruler. The glider lore calls him "the great king", and the court acted as his voice. After he was gone, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself Regent, according to a damaged bulletin in the ruins at Gavireh Lajavard.

Members: Vedrfolnir, the seer, is the only member the wiki lists. Rerir described him as "The Visionary", renowned throughout the court for a wisdom beyond ordinary men. He was Dainsleif's elder brother, and Surtalogi said his prophecies were never wrong.

Others in the king's circle are covered in their own entries. Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir were among the king's most trusted council. Rerir served Irmin as a secret agent, Pierro tried in vain to win the king's favour, and Anfortas was Knight Marshal. Whether each should count as a member of the court is not settled in canon.

Goals: Publicly, the court presented itself as a source of power that would bring Khaenri'ah a bright future. Dainsleif says it was loudly proclaimed that, with the new heir, all pain and suffering would be washed away. He now reads that rhetoric as covering the king's lust for power.

Methods: The court's main recorded act is public ceremony and persuasion. The announcement of the heir was a great celebration at the palace, with flowers both real and fake strewn about, and the title "Savior" was coined for the heir by those who believed the rhetoric. Behind the scenes the king used harsher means. When Vedrfolnir warned him that the kingdom would fall if he kept to his path, he had the seer's eyes gouged out and had him imprisoned.

History: Late in the Eclipse Dynasty the king named the Traveler's Sibling heir and Prince or Princess of Khaenri'ah. The king and court announced the heir as a bringer of prosperity, and many took up the idea of a "Savior". Soon after, Irmin led the heir into the kingdom's deepest depths and used them as a vessel for limitless Abyssal power. Vedrfolnir, imprisoned for his warning, was freed when Dainsleif and four allies stormed the palace by night. The court did not outlive the fall of the kingdom.

The loss of his sight also cost the seer his gift of foresight. Wishing to see the future again, Vedrfolnir yielded to the Abyss and shared its power with four of the others (Surtalogi, Rhinedottir, Hroptatyr and Rerir), and they became known as the Five Sinners.
