Long afterwards a voice and presence of Vedrfolnir is seen again in fragments of memory, including one in which he observes the Traveler and Varka in Nod-Krai (6.4).

Relations: - **Eclipse Dynasty**: the court served its last king.
- **Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah**: Vedrfolnir, Hroptatyr and Rerir were tied to the king's circle, and the group came together in a raid against the palace.
- **Dainsleif**: a young knight at the heir's announcement, later the court guard captain, who turned against the king.

- **Universitas Magistrorum**: the king ordered it to research the Abyss.
- **Traveler's Sibling**: the court's chosen heir, on whom its promises rested.

Status as of 7.1: The court no longer exists. It ended with the cataclysm about 500 years ago.

As of 7.1 no court or royal household has been revived. Former associates persist as individuals: Dainsleif the Bough Keeper; Vedrfolnir, one of the Five Sinners, whose consciousness survives in an Abyssal crystal; Rerir, another Sinner, sealed beyond a gate into the moon's reflection in the 6.x Nod-Krai story; and Pierro as the Fatui's Jester. The wiki still marks the entry a stub.

96.comment: Court of Khaenri'ah: Proclamation of the heir
96.content: When King Irmin named the Traveler's Sibling heir, he and the court proclaimed that the heir would bring a bright future. Dainsleif, then an ordinary young knight keeping order in the plaza, remembers the celebration. The glider lore sets the scene: the heir gazed out at the crowd and realised only then how many people lived underground. The word "Savior" came from those who believed the rhetoric. Dainsleif calls the whole thing a cruel irony in hindsight.

97.comment: Court of Khaenri'ah: Vedrfolnir the Visionary
97.content: Vedrfolnir was the court's seer, famed for prophecies that were never wrong, and Dainsleif's elder brother. He warned King Irmin that Khaenri'ah would fall if the king continued down his path. The king had his eyes gouged out and cast him into a cell, which also took away his sight of the future. Dainsleif's raid freed him, and he later became one of the Five Sinners. See his own entry for his later life.

98.comment: Court of Khaenri'ah: Regency of Anfortas
98.content: A notice in the ruins of Gavireh Lajavard says that, in view of the king's indisposed state and unknown threats, Knight Marshal Anfortas proclaimed he would temporarily take the post of Regent and lead the Regnum Concilium Ultimum until the kingdom returned to normal. The notice is badly worn and its last lines are lost. Kaeya's childhood lessons on Alberich Clan history said that the Alberichs, who lacked royal blood, stepped in as regents when the strength of the one-eyed king Irmin failed; the wiki infers from this that Anfortas was an Alberich, which canon does not state. Canon does not say what became of the rest of the court.

99.content:
Crimson Moon Dynasty (also: Red Moon Dynasty, Crimson Moon descendants, Crimson Moon bloodline): The Crimson Moon Dynasty is the earlier of the two known ruling dynasties of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom that fell in the cataclysm. It takes its name from the crimson moon that once shone over the realm. The dynasty is long gone, but some descendants survive and carry its Balemoon Bloodfire, most notably Arlecchino.

Almost everything known about its age comes from the legend of Perinheri, which cannot be verified. In Khaenri'ah's last years the later Eclipse Dynasty hunted its remaining descendants.

Structure: Canon names no ruler, court or lineage list for this dynasty. The legend of Perinheri shows a single 'great ruler' who answers the counsel of sages and lets them found an orphanage for children who may have come from beyond the world. In that era alchemy and the Beastmaster Knights were at the height of their influence. The legend also mentions the 'Darksprites', the first black-wolf warbeasts, created through alchemy.

Not all descendants stayed close to the main line. Tholindis belonged to a sub-branch whose family was only distantly related and had cut ties long before. Canon notes that a Crimson Moon descendant does not always show any sign of it. Tholindis had ordinary purple eyes and Frithr's eyes show no sign of the bloodline either.

Members: No member of the dynasty's ruling house is named. Known descendants are Arlecchino and, in Khaenri'ah's last years, Tholindis, Frithr and Orlog.

- **Arlecchino**: the best-known living descendant, the Knave, a Fatui Harbinger and head of the House of the Hearth. She did not know of her heritage until she met Pierro. The Balemoon Bloodfire runs in her blood, and she uses it carefully.
- **Tholindis**: from a distant sub-branch, a Moon Marrow researcher at the Universitas Magistrorum, engaged to Rerir without knowing his secret mission.
- **Frithr** and **Orlog**: other descendants hunted in the last years of Khaenri'ah. Orlog was arrested and probably killed; Frithr was spared by Rerir.

- **Rerir**: not a descendant but an agent of the Eclipse Dynasty (the Rächer of Solnari), ordered to kill the remaining Crimson Moon line.

Goals: As a dynasty it has no known goals now. The Perinheri legend says the founding of its orphanage aimed to catch a child from beyond the world who could transcend the gods. Surviving descendants are mainly concerned with staying alive and, in the Khaenri'ah period, hiding their ancestry to avoid persecution.

Methods: The dynasty's era is remembered for alchemy and warbeasts. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo's archaeological records say these were at their peak then. The Universitas Magistrorum later ran a Moon Marrow Lab, studying the energy left by the crimson moon's remains, as a possible new energy source for Khaenri'ah.

History: **The age of the crimson moon.** In the legend, the underground kingdom was lit by a crimson moon rather than the later dark sun. Sages persuaded the ruler to establish an orphanage for children said to come from beyond the sea of stars. Perinheri, an outlander, was raised there.

**The change of dynasty.** The legend says the crimson moon set and the dark sun descended, replacing one dynasty with the other. The way this happened is not told. The Crimson Moon era ended before the events of Perinheri (II), set during the Archon War.

**Purge.** Long after the dynasty fell, the last ruler of the Eclipse Dynasty, King Irmin, wanted the secrets the Crimson Moon had left and sent his agent Rerir, the Rächer of Solnari, to find and kill its few remaining followers. Irmin's purge deepened as his madness grew. Tholindis kept her own ancestry secret and quietly helped other descendants to escape. She entrusted Frithr with a piece of the Crimson Moon so the bloodline would not fade out. Rerir, losing faith in the king, spared Frithr and told her to keep hidden.

Relations: - **Eclipse Dynasty**: the dynasty that followed it and later hunted its descendants. Dainsleif's official introduction alludes to both dynasties with the line that the eclipse is swallowed by the crimson moon; the original phrasing implies revenge.
- **House of the Hearth and Fatui**: Pierro implies that the original orphanage is the House of the Hearth, whose later link to the Fatui he may be responsible for.
- **Universitas Magistrorum**: housed the Moon Marrow research and employed Tholindis.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dynasty is long extinct as a ruling house. Its descendants include Arlecchino.

In A Rekviem for the Underworld (7.1), Pierro starts a project with Arlecchino, using her status as a Crimson Moon descendant and the Crimson Moon's authority over death, to create new Delusions to oppose Ronova. The test at the Snezhnayan facility was only mildly successful. In return for her help, Arlecchino has the House of the Hearth stop working for the Fatui and end its training of children as spies.

100.content: Perinheri is a two-volume in-world book, also called Hleobranto Innamorato, sold in Fontaine. It claims to retell an old Khaenri'ahn legend that nobody can confirm and was written over generations. Its first volume sets the story in the Crimson Moon era and describes the orphanage for children from beyond the world. Its second volume has the knights Perinheri and Hleobrant, and Angelica, a woman who claims to be a noble princess from a defeated land. The volume names the four mightiest figures in the kingdom: Njord, Alf of the Universitas Magistrorum, Alberich, and Perinheri.

101.content: The Balemoon Bloodfire is the ancient flame in the blood of Crimson Moon descendants. In Arlecchino it is both a curse and a source of strength. It uses Abyssal energy and slowly corrupts the user. She learned that if the corruption reaches the heart, the user becomes a different person, and she uses it with great caution.

102.content:
Curatorium of Secrets (also: the Curatorium of Secrets, the Curatorium): The Curatorium of Secrets is an intelligence and commission agency in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, owned and run by Nefer. It takes commissions from the public, such as finding lost cats, tracking down people or things, and righting wrongs. It is also the public face of the underground Northern Intelligence Network. It follows a policy of strict neutrality toward every faction in Nod-Krai, and its only official employee is Jahoda.

To townspeople it is a busy, efficient, fairly cheap commission shop with a black cat on the counter. Beneath that is a broker of secrets with contacts in nearly every nation. Neutrality is the principle it sells.

Structure: Nefer is the owner and decides everything. Jahoda is the only official employee. Ashru, Nefer's cat, sits at the reception counter.

The building stands at the heart of Nasha Town and has at least two floors. The upper floor holds a reception area and Nefer's office, and visitors can walk in.

Nefer is also a member of the Voynich Guild. A secret room on the same floor holds her private records. In the Northern Intelligence Network, the Curatorium is the main point of sale; the Network's other people are informants and clients, not Curatorium staff. The Network is made up of volunteers. Many of them gave up their old posts, reputations or even names to join. It is loosely organised, with no formal rules, and runs as an exchange where well-connected people sell what they know. The Curatorium sits at its centre. Network members include Diluc, whom Nefer codenamed "Owl", and informants such as Sarin of the Adventurers' Guild, Iratxa, Lestocq, Sieciech, Cairuo and Tarno. (This roster is taken from the wiki's Northern Intelligence Network page.) The Curatorium's own staff are Jahoda and Ashru.

Leadership: Nefer, who came to Nod-Krai from Sumeru, owns the Curatorium and also heads the Northern Intelligence Network. She is calm, mercenary, and several moves ahead of whoever is in front of her.

Nefer treats information and favours as currency and nothing as free. In Hidden in the Shadows she tells Jahoda never to accept favours, since they are the hardest debts to repay.

In Character Story 3, Nefer deliberately removes the "leaders" who had carved Nod-Krai into private territories, and she then lets their followers fight among themselves. She takes care to keep innocent people out of it, because she expects to serve them as clients later. Character Story 4 describes her calmly brewing tea for visitors as if she had never destroyed a gang or ruined a boss, and calls her the unseen hand keeping Nod-Krai's waters "just the right degree of murky". In the same story she tells a young man who drew a blade on her that Nod-Krai's powerful figures are weighed down by their names and fortunes, and then offers him a commission.

Members: - Nefer: owner, head of the Network.
- Jahoda: the only official employee, a former Seahook Gang member whose life Nefer saved.
- Ashru: Nefer's black cat, the receptionist.

Jahoda handles most field commissions, from searching for lost cats to chasing down clients who cheat. Ashru descends from cats once kept by Thoth, the Ibis King.

According to the wiki, citing Nefer's voice-over, Nefer paid in full for Jahoda's robotic arm. While imprisoned in Aaru, the Ibis King once spoke to Nefer through Ashru. The Curatorium's lines of trust run through Nefer: the Adventurers' Guild's Nod-Krai head Sarin has an understanding with her, and the two collaborate. Dori, a merchant and a fellow Sumeru native, is shown dropping in to chat. Nefer is credited with saving her when she arrived in Nod-Krai in a dire state.

Goals: The Curatorium sells information and handles commissions at a profit. Through Nefer it also aims to keep Nod-Krai stable and no single faction dominant.

Nefer says she joined the League only for appearances, until the venture becomes worth her while. Behind the profit motive, the stories show Nefer protecting people she values: she paid for Jahoda's arm, is credited with saving Dori, and risked her sight to help seal Rerir. The Curatorium's neutrality reads as a business principle that she will bend quietly for such people.

Methods: The Curatorium does public commissions at reasonable prices, lower when Jahoda is on duty, and brokers intelligence through the Network, where informants sell facts and clients pay for them.

Nefer reads people closely and often arranges things in advance, so visitors find she already knows why they came. Nefer's tools include a chess-like ritual board given to her by Thoth. With it, and with objects tied to a person or place, she can view their past, a technique she uses on Rerir's memories and on Luonnotar's. The ritual carries danger, as Rerir imprisoned her inside her own memory. The Curatorium also uses ordinary trade methods: letters, tips from informants and favours called in, as when Nefer calmed Nasha Town after Rerir's attack.

History: Nefer came to Nod-Krai after leaving Sumeru. She eliminated the leaders who had divided the region, then opened the Curatorium and hired Jahoda. At some point she also came to head the Northern Intelligence Network. The doors were nearly always shut until the Curatorium announced that it would take commissions from anyone.

The first ordinary client was a crying little girl whose parents had not come home, and Jahoda rescued them. Before that, Nasha Town told rumours about the mysterious owner.
**Frostmoon Scions' relic (6.0).** When the Frostmoon Scions' sacred relic, the Moon Marrow, was stolen, Lauma tried several times to commission Nefer. Nefer repeatedly declined, citing neutrality. After hearing the Traveler's account, Nefer argued that the Fatui may have taken the relic, rather than the Traveler's sibling. Still citing neutrality, she turned down an open request to help infiltrate the Fatui's facility. She then agreed to a final condition from Lauma: to persuade whoever walked through the door next to help. That was Jahoda, whom Nefer politely asked to go and then fired on the spot, so that Jahoda would be earning on her own account. The Curatorium would take her back once the job was done.
**Secret Base (6.1).** In Hidden in the Shadows, Varka arranged a meeting at the Knights of Favonius's covert Nod-Krai base, a contact hub for the Network, and asked Nefer to help unite the factions of Nod-Krai against Rerir. She first declined, until Jahoda offered her own wages and Lauma offered a formal commission. She then agreed to follow up leads, and borrowed the fragment that Rerir had been after from Flins.

Relations: **Voynich Guild:** works closely with it; Nefer is a member. **Adventurers' Guild:** cooperates through an understanding with Sarin. **Knights of Favonius:** Varka is a Network client. **Frostmoon Scions:** Nefer and Lauma know each other well and spar constantly. **Fatui:** the Curatorium has refused to help either side infiltrate the other.

**Liyue:** the Network has no foothold in Liyue because Yelan and her colleagues prevented it, though Yelan buys intelligence from the Curatorium's side and Nefer bears no grudge. **Marechaussee Phantom and Spina di Rosula:** the wiki lists both as allies of the Network. In coded talk, Nefer asked Lestocq of the Marechaussee Phantom about remaining Seahook Gang members who had made their way to Fontaine. **League:** Nefer is the Curatorium's representative in the League, and has said her participation is for appearances until the venture proves worth her while.

Reputation: Residents of Nasha Town know it as an efficient, comparatively cheap commission shop. Children remember Nefer as the kind lady with candy and slightly scary stories.

Adults told lurid urban legends about the owner, such as an army of grotesque minions inside, and some avoided the place. People who deal with Nefer on serious business speak of her very differently. Lauma calls the Curatorium's professional standards beyond question after watching how Nefer handled Jahoda's commission.

Secrets: The Curatorium's polite exterior hides the Northern Intelligence Network, an underground exchange for intelligence. Nefer's earlier career in Nod-Krai included the planned killing of its criminal leaders, according to her Character Story 3. At the Curatorium's heart is a hidden back room where Nefer keeps private papers and a store of the agency's money. Letters from clients and the finance chest are only meant for Curatorium members to open.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Curatorium is open and operating in Nasha Town. Nefer is back at its head, her sight having returned, and Jahoda still handles most of its commissions.

The agency has joined the Nod-Krai League as a representative body. Nefer has said she will stay a member only while it remains worthwhile. Since Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (6.6) the reception board lists Nefer herself at the counter again. Versions 7.0 and 7.1 add no new Curatorium story in the sources checked; in the 7.1 Anecdote Jahoda: A Thief's End, Jahoda is in Snezhnograd and says she has another errand to run for her boss before heading back to Nod-Krai.

103.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Northern Intelligence Network
103.content:
The Northern Intelligence Network is an underground exchange of information, headquartered in Nod-Krai with contacts in every nation except Liyue. Its members are volunteers, many of whom gave up their old lives to join. It is loosely organised and has no firm rules. People trade what they know for payment. Nefer is its current head, and the Curatorium of Secrets is its main point of sale. Varka calls it the black market of intel and says the Knights of Favonius rely on it for local information.

The Network's roster, as listed on the wiki, includes Diluc as a contact with the codename "Owl", Jahoda and Ashru as employees, a spread of informants, and clients such as Yelan and Varka. Its Liyue operation failed because Yelan's side blocked it. Nefer's Character Story "Moon Wheel" hints at an older representative who wanted a successor, but does not say how she took over.

104.content: The Curatorium of Secrets says it has always followed a policy of strict neutrality and takes no side in Nod-Krai's factions. Nefer cites it to refuse commissions that would make her an enemy of the Fatui or the Frostmoon Scions. She has refused a Harbinger's request to help infiltrate the Scions' territory and refused Lauma's request to help infiltrate the Fatui facility. She still works around it. When Lauma asked her to persuade whoever walked in next to help, she was willing, as long as she was not personally involved. She treats the rule as a business principle, not a moral one.

105.content: In Reunion Beneath the Moonlight, Nefer politely asks a startled Jahoda to help the Traveler, Paimon and Lauma infiltrate the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. When Jahoda agrees, Nefer fires her on the spot, effective immediately, and says the Curatorium will take her back after the job. This keeps the Curatorium neutral on paper, since Jahoda is a private contractor, and Jahoda earns more without Nefer's cut. Lauma later praises the Curatorium's professionalism.

106.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: The Secret Base
106.content: The Secret Base is an underground meeting place used by the Knights of Favonius and other clients of the Northern Intelligence Network. It is hidden and secure. In Hidden in the Shadows, Varka leads Lauma, Flins, Aino, Ineffa, Jahoda and the Traveler there to hide from the Wild Hunt. Nefer arrives in response to a letter from a "humble knight of Favonius". She turns out to be the Network's head, and Varka asks her to help unite Nod-Krai against Rerir. The interior is only accessible during certain quests.

107.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Chessbox and memory-delving
107.content: Nefer owns a ritual chess-like board from Thoth, which she calls her chessbox. She uses it to view memories tied to objects and places. In the Rerir arc she used it, plus a protective charm from Dori, to look into Rerir's past, and was drawn into a counter-attack in which Rerir trapped her inside her own memory. She sealed him inside the box. During the final fight, she risked her sight to hold him back. In 6.3 she used the box again on the Traveler's belongings to locate where Dottore had them, and later to view the memory of Luonnotar.

108.content: Ashru is Nefer's black cat and the Curatorium's receptionist. He descends from the cats Thoth once kept. While imprisoned in Aaru, Thoth took over Ashru's body to speak to Nefer, then left it before she could exploit it. Nefer has kept Ashru close in case Thoth ever speaks through him again. In daily life he is a lazy cat who eats well; Nefer keeps his bowl filled and Jahoda pets him. Ashru's dialogue hints that Lauma or Columbina might be able to understand him.

109.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Opening to the public
109.content: According to Nefer's fifth Character Story, the Curatorium used to be a place the town feared, and the news that it would take commissions from anyone alarmed parents. The first ordinary client was a tearful little girl whose parents had not come home. Jahoda rescued the couple from bandits, and Nefer asked only for a hairpin as payment. Word spread, and the Curatorium came to resemble a river winding through town: visible at the surface, deeper currents hidden. The story adds that only one person can uncover its true secrets.

110.comment: Curatorium of Secrets: Nod-Krai Trade Expo commission
110.content: During the event Where Waves Meet the Reef (6.5, April to May 2026), Nefer asks the Traveler to help Jahoda manage VIPs at the Voynich Guild's annual expo. Among them are Beidou, captain of a large fleet, and Navia, who leads an underworld organisation, and Jahoda separates their booths. The expo's rule against violence stops visiting Liyue and Fontaine authorities from arresting an arms syndicate inside it, so Nefer lets Yelan and Chevreuse handle the arrests outside. A man called Ashvapati, who joined the Voynich Guild with a hidden agenda, lies about everything except his desert origins. Nefer later suggests that he return to the desert to build a peaceful life there.

111.content:
Daydream Club (also: Daydream Club of Petrichor, the Daydream Club): The Daydream Club is a small group of inventors and researchers from Fontaine, centred on the town of Petrichor. Its members are united by their 'daydreams', ambitious ideas that other people call unrealistic. Known members include Garcia (Numbering Machine), Xavier (Film Kamera), Felix Yogue (a perpetual-energy machine), the brothers Mecantre and Babisse (a giant cannon), Grispan (phlogiston and thermal hypnosis) and Este. Their 'President' is a cat, Lady Grobel.

The club is informal and good-humoured: a group that values curiosity and, by the account of a recording in Daydreams Beyond Space and Time, began with the idea of providing research for free. Felix Yogue says the name was chosen on purpose: since outsiders call the members' dreams unrealistic, they decided to call the club 'daydream'.

Structure: There is no formal hierarchy in the sources. The club's 'President', or 'Director', is Lady Grobel, a cat whom Grispan treats as his leader and whose meows he translates for others. Members each pursue a separate project and trade ideas and equipment; Mecantre plans to borrow Garcia's Numbering Machine to calculate a bridge, for instance. The club has a base in Petrichor stocked with unusual equipment, including divesuits that Grispan bought to study underwater hypnosis.

Some members travel widely while others stay in Petrichor. Xavier went to Inazuma, Garcia and his assistant Lutong to Liyue and Sumeru, and Grispan to Natlan; Grispan's letters to Petrichor show they keep in touch by post. Wiki infoboxes call Mecantre 'Chief Designer' and Babisse 'Chief of Construction' of the Teyvat Grand Cannon, titles for that one project.

Members: - **Garcia**: builds the Numbering Machine, a calculating device. Absent-minded and fond of formal language, he travels with his assistant Lutong.
- **Xavier**: inventor of the Film Kamera and a filmmaker. He helped maintain the Mikage Furnace in Inazuma and later founded Musketeer Pictures in Fontaine.
- **Felix Yogue**: wants to build an energy source that runs forever using only mechanical parts. He appears in the Evermotion Mechanical Painting event (limited).
- **Mecantre and Babisse**: brothers designing a super-sized cannon meant to carry people up to touch the stars.
- **Grispan**: researches phlogiston and 'thermal hypnosis'.
- **Este**: a Petrichor resident, a descendant of the Remurian golem Este, who takes up Grispan's hypnosis notes.
- **Lady Grobel**: the cat President.

People close to the club but not members include Lutong (Garcia's assistant), Kaia (who accompanies Garcia), and Grundeland, a self-styled 'Good Merchant' who tried to get hold of the club's research for profit.

Goals: Members chase ideas for their own sake. According to a recording heard in Daydreams Beyond Space and Time, the club's original purpose is to provide research for free so that it belongs to everyone, and Garcia insists its research will not be used to make Mora. Mecantre explains why daydreaming matters: it is the reef on which a researcher's torrent of ideas breaks into inspiration, and without it research becomes a stagnant pool.

Methods: Members work by imaginative leaps and practical engineering: calculating machines, cameras, a cannon, phlogiston-powered hypnosis. When Grundeland pressured them, Mecantre and Babisse planted phonographs around Petrichor to record what he said.

Grispan's thermal hypnosis is a steam-heated box big enough to seat a person with only the head outside, meant to make hypnosis work faster and better. The Traveler points out that it would knock the person out, and Grispan answers that they define 'knocking out' differently. Garcia's method for the Numbering Machine is to turn cooking into a formula, which he tested on Radish Veggie Soup in Garcia's Paean (2.7).

History: **Garcia's Paean (2.7).** At Wangshu Inn in Liyue, Garcia and Lutong ask the Traveler to taste-test soup made from a formula, and say they are heading for Sumeru to improve the Numbering Machine.

**Evermotion Mechanical Painting (2.8).** In this event (12 to 22 August 2022), Felix Yogue introduced the club to the Traveler in Mondstadt and invited them to visit Petrichor.

**Petrichor mass dream (4.6).** In Canticles of Harmony, the Prelude 'Petrichorror Dream', Petrichor's residents, including Mecantre, Babisse and Grundeland, were caught up in the Symphony of Remuria under Phobos. They spoke as Remurian scientists and praised the God King. Este, descended from a Remurian, was unaffected.

**Daydreams Beyond Space and Time (4.6).** Garcia, with Kaia and Lutong, hurries home to Petrichor out of fear for his friends and finds them dazed and Grundeland remorseful. The Traveler explains Remuria and Phobos, and the group dives to the ruins using the club's divesuits. Mecantre and Babisse find the statues whose 'shadows' they were in the dream: a researcher of high-altitude aqueducts and one of aquabuses. They conclude the statues lacked the ability to daydream. Grundeland, in tears, finds the statue of the director of the Remurian Academy of Sciences. Back in Petrichor, Mecantre and Babisse vow to carry the statues' ideas forward as their own work, and Lutong plans to hand Grundeland to Officer Menthe.

Relations: The club is on good terms with Petrichor's people. When Garcia fears for his friends, Lutong suggests trusting Mr. Bossuet and hoping the Fontaine Research Institute will see them through; Officer Menthe is the authority who is to receive Grundeland. Grundeland is an antagonist who turns penitent. Outside Fontaine, members have been helped by the Traveler and Paimon in Inazuma, Liyue and Natlan.

Mecantre and Babisse argue for giving Grundeland a chance to reform, while Garcia stays wary.

Reputation: Felix Yogue admits outsiders call the members' plans unrealistic, and the members embrace the label. Lutong calls them brilliant people. The Traveler is warmly welcomed by them.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1 though scattered. The club's Petrichor members survived the mass dream and returned to their projects, and Grispan remains in Natlan.

The Teyvat Grand Cannon, the Numbering Machine and thermal hypnosis are described as ongoing, not finished. No source after 5.0 adds a new club appearance.

112.content: Garcia is a quest NPC from Fontaine who is building the Numbering Machine, a device for calculation. He is formal, distracted and fond of long phrases, and he is short of Mora. In Garcia's Paean (2.7) he and Lutong cooked Radish Veggie Soup at Wangshu Inn to find a recipe formula and left for Sumeru's Akademiya. In Daydreams Beyond Space and Time (4.6) he rushes home to Petrichor with Kaia and Lutong, fears his friends were exploited and leads the dive to Remuria with the Traveler. He asks the Traveler whether the machine possesses 'thought'; the question is left open.

113.content: Grispan is a florid, anxious Fontainian researcher who is working on thermal hypnosis in Natlan. Lady Grobel is the club's cat President and speaks only in meows, which he translates; she dislikes unexpected trouble. If the Traveler has finished Daydreams Beyond Space and Time, they can fill him in on events in Petrichor. He is uncomfortable around Natlan's exuberant residents and wants to return home once his research is done.

114.content: Brothers and club members in Petrichor. Felix Yogue says they are building a cannon big enough to take people to the stars and are still looking for the right fuel. During the mass dream they were under the Remurian Symphony and spoke of an aqueduct and a fast aquabus. Afterwards they use the dreaming researchers' ideas as seeds for a large bridge and a speedy boat. They hold that research needs a 'daydream' as its spark, and after the quest each says the cannonball must be 'super-sized'.

115.comment: Daydream Club: Daydreams Beyond Space and Time
115.content: A Fontaine World Quest that follows the Petrichor mass dream. Garcia and company return to Petrichor, learn of Phobos and Remuria from the Traveler, and dive to the ruins. Mecantre and Babisse find the statues of two researchers they dreamed as, and Grundeland finds the director of the Remurian Academy of Sciences. The club members conclude those researchers lacked the ability to daydream. The achievement 'In Those Ruins of Dreams...' is granted at the end.

116.comment: Daydream Club: Evermotion Mechanical Painting event
116.content: A 2.8 event (12 to 22 August 2022) in which Felix Yogue, a Fontainian in Mondstadt, asked the Traveler to rebuild a mechanical painting. He described the club's members to the Traveler and invited visitors to Petrichor. Felix says he wants an everlasting energy source made of purely mechanical parts.

117.content:
Druzhna (also: Druzhina, the Druzhna, Druzhna Guards, Winter Pact Corps): The Druzhna is Snezhnaya's personal guard of the Tsaritsa. It answers only to her, and most of its members are Vila, winged fae of the Snowland Fae. Besides protecting her, it is responsible for containing Shadow Realm breaches. Its headquarters is Druzhna HQ in the Everfrozen Earth area, and its Commander-in-chief is Vesna Strivozha.

The word is Russian: a druzhina was a warrior band that served a medieval prince. In Snezhnaya the name belongs to a force older than the Tsaritsa's own reign, founded by the Belyi Tsar. It is separate from the Fatui, which is the army and government apparatus she built, and the two are described as allies.

Leadership: Vesna Strivozha, a Vila of House Strivozha, is Commander-in-chief. Her profile calls her the Tsaritsa's "keen blade", and she and the head housemaid Danica are both called the Tsaritsa's right hands and are often at her side.

Vesna joined as a young recruit, known at first as "that little lass from House Strivozha". Her profile says that by the time she took command, "Vesna" shone so brightly that people forgot the surname. She was trained in her youth by Capitano. In her character story "Druzhna Recruit's Badge", an audience with the Tsaritsa ended with Vesna receiving a Druzhna recruit's badge and Capitano, not Pulcinella, as her mentor. Capitano told her to become a disciple he could be proud of and said he would wait for the day she stood at the pinnacle of the Druzhna. Following a story of her mother's, she left that badge high on the roof of the family estate, and dug it out again after the banquet celebrating her appointment as commander-in-chief.

The first Commander was Grand Duke Filipov Vseslavyevich, the shapeshifter and the Belyi Tsar's closest comrade, who vanished during the Cataclysm.

Other named members are Yarovaya, a Podporuchik who runs the Shadow Realm work at Druzhna HQ, and Akvilina, who introduces herself as a Privy Councillor (3rd Class) and Officer of the Druzhna Guards. Both are Vila.

Structure: The Druzhna is a single armed force with a Commander-in-chief at its head and, in canon, no other formal structure shown. Ranks glimpsed include Commander-in-chief, officer of the guards and Podporuchik, a junior officer rank. Its base is Druzhna HQ, a subarea of Everfrozen Earth in Snezhnaya. It sits under Zapolyarny Palace, the Tsaritsa's seat, and takes its orders from her alone.

Recruits are drawn mainly from the Vila. During the recruitment drive that began in 7.0 the Druzhna also took on volunteers from the public for the dangerous Shadow Realm work. Yarovaya admits that ordinarily the Druzhna itself should be completing such missions, and an applicant says the entry standards this time are much stricter than usual.

Members: Members are overwhelmingly Vila: winged fae with pointed, green-tipped ears and insect-like wings. Their wings let them fly briefly, which suits scouting and long-range raids. Vesna is the only playable member. Named non-playable members are Yarovaya and Akvilina at Snezhnograd. Soldiers of the Druzhna also appear in Vesna's stories.

Akvilina speaks of herself as a blade "ever prepared to strike and fall" in the Tsaritsa's service, and her lines on the Veche and on rogue Vila show the force's fierce loyalty.

Goals: Protect the Tsaritsa and keep peace across the lands she surveys. Yarovaya states the duty plainly: the Druzhna exists so that "all lands the Tsaritsa surveys are at peace". Its other standing task is dealing with Shadow Realms, which it treats as the opposite of that peace.

Methods: For Shadow Realms, the Royal Energy Commission detects breaches and reports them, and the Druzhna acts on each report. According to Yarovaya, it organises search groups; if the group finds the Realm's energy core, it neutralises it, and if not, it seals the Realm off. Most Shadow Realms vanish by themselves over time, so the main danger is people entering one by mistake.

From 7.0 the Druzhna has run the Special Recruitment Project, which Vesna says the Tsaritsa herself arranged, with weekly training missions in which volunteers helped clear Shadow Realms for rewards. The map text describes Yarovaya as a high-ranking officer who verifies sightings, processes intelligence from the Commission, sets up containment and then goes in to clear the Realm.

History: **Origins.** The Belyi Tsar founded the Druzhna and led it as his personal guard. Its ranks were drawn from the Vila, who were among the first fae to follow him when he united the Snowland Fae. The Vila had earlier been vassals of King Miscislav of the Volkodlak, paying him tribute. After their first Grand Duchess, Vaselisa Strivozha, was beaten by the Tsar, they switched sides. Grand Duke Filipov Vseslavyevich was its first Commander.

**Under the Tsaritsa.** After the Belyi Tsar died in the Cataclysm and Anastasya became Cryo Archon, some Vila rebelled over her policy toward the fae nobility. These revolts were put down, which split the Vila. A history book says that when she moved against the fae princes early in her reign, she did not call up the Druzhna but built the Fatui instead. She later took the Druzhna as her own personal guard, as the loading-screen text says it is today.

**Shadow Realms and recent years.** The Druzhna handles the Shadow Realm breaches reported by the Energy Commission. In Chapter VII (7.0 to 7.1), the Commander Vesna was beside the Tsaritsa when she dealt with a storm-causing monster in the east, and was shown greeting the crowd at the Armory Palace after Ronova had left it. Shortly afterwards the Druzhna's Special Recruitment Project signed up the Traveler, Vesna noticed the name on the roster, and she later met the Traveler in person. Her own part in that story, including her power of Life, belongs to her character entry.

Relations: - **The Tsaritsa**: sole master. Loading-screen text says the Druzhna answers only to her.
- **Fatui**: described as allies. The Tsaritsa created the Fatui rather than using the Druzhna to subdue the fae princes, so the two forces have different roots.
- **Vila**: the people from whom the Druzhna is mostly drawn. Vila Druzhna such as Akvilina treat rogue Vila bandits as traitors who shame their people.

- **Royal Energy Commission**: reports Shadow Realms to the Druzhna and is described as more mobile, since its staff travel to maintain Kresnik's Torches. Yarovaya finds it odd that the Commission sometimes seems to know more about the Realms than it says.
- **House Strivozha**: the Vila house that Vesna comes from. According to the wiki, the house submitted to the Belyi Tsar in the era of the unification.
- **Snezhnograd Veche**: Akvilina says the Veche is corrupt and that she would uncover whether its members are truly loyal to the Tsaritsa. This is her opinion, not official Druzhna policy.
- **Rokot**: in the world quest A Special Selection, the Traveler can treat the recruitment drive as a job for the Rokot, the civil group; the Druzhna side never mentions the Rokot.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Druzhna is active under Commander Vesna. It is short on hands for Shadow Realm work and is running the Special Recruitment Project to bring in volunteers.

Vesna and Danica returned to Snezhnograd with the Tsaritsa after dealing with the eastern monster. No change to the Druzhna's structure or command has been shown in 7.0 to 7.1. Nothing after 7.1 is covered.

118.content: Vesna is the Druzhna's Commander-in-chief and its only playable face. She is a Vila of House Strivozha, trained by Capitano, who holds a fragment of the Ruler of Life's authority. Her profile calls the Druzhna the blade the Tsaritsa wields and Vesna its keenest edge. For her personality, voice and personal history, see her own entry; this entry covers only her role in the force.

119.content: Druzhna HQ is the force's base in the Everfrozen Earth area of Snezhnograd. Named NPCs on the wiki map include Malinina, Musina, Rozhdestvensky, Shakhovskaya and Yarovaya, the last the "Druzhna" Podporuchik who runs the Shadow Realm cleanup. In the world quest A Special Selection (7.0) the Traveler finds applicants lining up to be tested there.

120.content: After the world quest A Special Selection, Yarovaya offers weekly training missions in which the Traveler enters set Shadow Realms and clears them. The project is a manpower measure: the force is stretched, so it takes volunteers who pass strict shooting tests. This is a gameplay system as well as a story beat, and in the story the Traveler joins as a recruit. The map description says the work might even earn the favour of the one on Zapolyarny Palace's throne.

121.content: Filipov was a Snowland Fae Grand Duke, called the progenitor of the shapeshifters, and the Belyi Tsar's Synaimos, a fae word for a comrade-in-arms. General History of Snezhnaya tells how he challenged the young Monomakh and lost, changing shape again and again, then swore to him. He became the first Commander of the Druzhna. According to the book he lost three times in his long life: to Monomakh, to his wife Nepla Korolevitsna, and to the Abyss during the Cataclysm.

122.comment: Druzhna: Vila and the Belyi Tsar
122.content: The Vila were vassals of Miscislav, king of the Volkodlak, until the Belyi Tsar's campaign. Their first Grand Duchess, Vaselisa Strivozha, was defeated by the Tsar in single combat, and the Vila submitted willingly to the Pale Star Court. He granted them amnesty and let them live with humans, which Druzhna Vila such as Akvilina remember with gratitude. After he died, some Vila nobles' descendants staged small rebellions against the Tsaritsa. A raider called the Burner of Cities rode the railway in one of them. The revolts were crushed but split the Vila people. The Druzhna's Vila see the rebel remnants as a lasting disgrace.

123.content:
Eclipse Dynasty (also: Black Sun Dynasty, Dark Sun Dynasty, Blacksun Dynasty, the dark sun): The Eclipse Dynasty was the second and last known ruling dynasty of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom destroyed in the cataclysm 500 years ago. A dark sun stood as its emblem, replacing the earlier crimson moon. Its final ruler was the one-eyed King Irmin, and it fell with the kingdom.

Its era leaned on mechanical engineering and knowledge said to come from beyond the sky, and later turned to the Abyss. Khaenri'ah's survivors, such as the Alberich Clan, and figures such as Dainsleif, trace their roots to its court.

Structure: The Eclipse Dynasty is known mainly from fragments. A king ruled, with a military of knights, a scholarly body (the Universitas Magistrorum), and by the end a Royal Guard called the Black Serpent Knights. The Alberich Clan produced leaders of the kingdom's knights, and the Knight Marshal could advise the king directly.

The knights' roles shifted from the earlier dynasty. The Beastmaster Knights and alchemy, mainstays of the Crimson Moon era, were pushed aside for mechanical engineering. By the cataclysm the Schwanenritter used earlier-model Ruin Golems, and the Black Serpent Knights included Dainsleif, called the Twilight Sword, and Halfdan.

Members: King Irmin, the last ruler; Dainsleif of the Royal Guard; and the Traveler's sibling, adopted into the royal house.

- **Irmin**: the one-eyed Vinster King, last of the dynasty.
- **Dainsleif**: Twilight Sword and a captain of the Black Serpent Knights, who later became the immortal wanderer of Teyvat.
- **The Traveler's sibling**: arrived 500 years ago, was adopted as royalty and was believed able to command the Abyss.
- **Rerir**: an intelligence officer and secret agent called the Rächer of Solnari, later one of the Five Sinners.
- **Anfortas and Chlothar**: Alberich nobles, with Anfortas serving as regent at the end.

- **Halfdan**: another Black Serpent Knight, later a Shadowy Husk.
- **Pierro**: says he once served the final dynasty, before the Fatui.

Goals: Little is said of official aims. The dynasty valued mechanical engineering and secrets from beyond the skies, which drew resistance from people who held that human will mattered more than such techniques. Late in its reign Irmin redirected the Universitas Magistrorum's resources toward researching the Abyss.

Methods: The dynasty's rule leaned on technical progress. Mechanical Wardens, now known as Ruin Golems, guarded the kingdom, and forbidden knowledge was used. Irmin also deployed secret agents, notably Rerir, to purge descendants of the earlier dynasty. The Traveler's sibling was set to absorb the Abyss's world-shattering power, which was later split among the Five Sinners.

History: **Rise.** The legend says the crimson moon set and the dark sun descended, replacing the Crimson Moon Dynasty, though the dates and manner are not known. The Perinheri book already shows the Universitas Magistrorum and an Alberich as established names in this time.

**Final reign.** The last king, Irmin, ruled when the cataclysm struck 500 years ago. The Traveler's sibling arrived and was adopted as royalty. Gods cursed the kingdom's people, the Abyss spread, and Khaenri'ah fell.

Before the fall, Irmin grew more erratic. His resources shifted toward the Abyss, and he ordered the purge of the earlier dynasty's remaining descendants. Dainsleif led an assault on the palace to free Vedrfolnir, releasing Abyssal energy that spawned monsters across the kingdom. With Irmin indisposed, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself regent. The Schwanenritter led survivors to the surface, using Ruin Golems to hold off the beasts.

Relations: - **Crimson Moon Dynasty**: its predecessor; the Eclipse Dynasty hunted its remaining descendants, partly for its secrets.
- **Alberich Clan**: provided the regents and knights; the clan says it had no royal blood.
- **Abyss Order**: founded by Chlothar, formerly of the dynasty's nobility.
- **Universitas Magistrorum**: the scholarly body, later redirected to Abyss research.

Status as of 7.1: The dynasty ended with Khaenri'ah's fall and no ruling house survives.

As of 7.1 nothing new about the dynasty itself was found in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content checked beyond Pierro's remarks and memories. Its surviving figures remain active.

124.content: Irmin was the last king of Khaenri'ah, called the Vinster King and described as one-eyed. When the cataclysm began he was 'indisposed' and unable to deal with the dark beasts, so Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself regent. Earlier he redirected the Universitas Magistrorum toward Abyss research and ordered the purge of Crimson Moon descendants. The Traveler's sibling absorbed the Abyssal power he demanded.

125.content: The Black Serpent Knights were Khaenri'ah's royal guard at the time of the cataclysm. Dainsleif, the Twilight Sword, was among their captains, and Halfdan another member. Apart from Dainsleif, the others have become Shadowy Husks by the time the Traveler meets them in The Chasm's Underground Mines.

126.content: In the legend of Perinheri, the crimson moon set and the dark sun descended into a darker dusk. Alchemy and Beastmaster Knights were a mainstay under the crimson moon, but the Eclipse era's interest in mechanical engineering sidelined them. In the book's second volume, Angelica names the four mightiest figures of the kingdom: Njord, Alf of the Universitas Magistrorum, Alberich, and Perinheri.

127.content:
Eight Trades (also: Bāmén, Eight Gates): The Eight Trades are eight commerce sectors that run Liyue's major industries, under the jurisdiction of the Liyue Qixing. Their divisions are called Halls or Offices. Canon names four: the Communications Office (transport), Huishan Hall (mining), Shenglu Hall (glazed ceramics) and Yinyuan Hall (salt).

When Rex Lapis relinquished his post, his duties fell to the Qixing and the Eight Trades. The Chinese and Japanese names mean "Eight Gates". The English "Hall" translates the Chinese word for a government office.

Structure: The Qixing hold authority over the sectors. Each Trade is a Hall or Office with its own representatives and members. The wiki lists only four of the eight, and no shared leader or headquarters is described. The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is a sub-organisation of the Communications Office.

Known sectors, members and tasks:
- **Communications Office** (Hezhe Post): transportation, shipments around Liyue and overseas logistics, plus related construction and road management. Master Qin "Thunder Hand" acts as a bodyguard, and Yanfei's friends are tied to it.
- **Huishan Hall**: mining and matters involving the Chasm. Uncle Dai is its foreman, and Zhiqiong was offered a place there as consultant and guide.
- **Shenglu Hall**: glazed ceramics. Miss Ruoyu is the representative, Wanyu heads human culture and civilisation research, and Muning is its specialist.
- **Yinyuan Hall**: salt. Wanyan is the only known member.

Members: Members named in canon come from four Halls: Fangju, Master Qin and others at the Communications Office; Uncle Dai at Huishan Hall; Miss Ruoyu, Wanyu and Muning at Shenglu Hall; and Wanyan at Yinyuan Hall.

After the events of the limited-time event The Chasm Delvers, the Chasm Exploration Team became an official part of Huishan Hall.

Goals: The Eight Trades keep Liyue's industries and shipping running. Their activities include reopening Chasm mining, researching rare Archaic Stones, and handling transport routes and docks. Under the Qixing they also help carry on the administrative duties that once fell to Rex Lapis.

Methods: They work through official notices (such as bulletin boards at Feiyun Slope and Mingyun Village), commissions from the Ministry of Civil Affairs and trade specialists. Fangju of the Communications Office says its large staff is needed because transport depends on good roads, bridges, waterways and docks. A staff member mentions that the office plans to build small lifts.

Huishan Hall has forbidden people working in the Chasm from eating plants and mushrooms that grow in the underground mines, because they may harm the body.

History: Shenglu Hall's members are mostly descendants of the indigenous tribes who lived near the Chasm. After Morax arrived, these tribes made blood-pacts with the Yaksha, became his allies and fought against Azhdaha and the monsters of the cataclysm. Most later moved to Liyue Harbor and formed Shenglu Hall, which specialises in glazed ceramics passed down through generations. The Chasm's closure worried the Hall, which relied on materials from there.

Relations: - **Liyue Qixing**: they supervise all eight Trades.
- **Ministry of Civil Affairs**: it works with the Halls, for example by commissioning a Shenglu Hall specialist to oversee the Chasm.
- **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: a guard company that works under the Communications Office.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Eight Trades remain Liyue's commercial administration under the Qixing. No new developments were found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

128.content: The Communications Office is the Trade that handles transport in Liyue: shipments, roads, bridges, waterways and docks, and overseas shipping logistics. Its staff is large. Fangju explains its role, and another worker mentions plans for small lifts. The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency, whose guards escort goods, is one of its sub-organisations. Gaming's profile says the Agency has many skilled guards but only Gaming can both keep clients happy and beat bandits. The Communications Office first appears in 1.5.

129.content: Huishan Hall oversees mining and matters involving the Chasm. Its foreman is Uncle Dai. Its higher-ups are studying rare Archaic Stones from the Chasm, which Muning of the Ministry of Civil Affairs was sent to fetch. The Chasm's changes lowered the quality of the stones that remain.

130.content: Shenglu Hall governs the glazed ceramics trade. Miss Ruoyu is the industry representative. Her notice on the Feiyun Slope bulletin board says she is investigating the possibility of restarting Chasm mining. Wanyu is head of human culture and civilisation research.

131.content: Yinyuan Hall governs the salt industry and worships Havria, the long-dead God of Salt. Wanyan, an archaeologist, is the member seen in canon. Its account of Havria's death differs from other accounts, as the uncertainties note.

132.content:
Eleven Fatui Harbingers (also: Fatui Harbingers, Eleven Harbingers, Harbingers of the Fatui, the Eleven Fatui Harbingers): The Eleven Fatui Harbingers are the executive heads of Snezhnaya's Fatui. The Tsaritsa gives them god-like authority and Delusions, and each leads a division. The Director, Pierro ("The Jester"), leads them. In the early Archon Quest chapters they were sent abroad to collect the Archons' Gnoses.

Seat numbers reflect combat power, and empty seats are not filled by moving everyone up.

Structure: - **The Tsaritsa** appoints every Harbinger. She does it in person at a ceremony in Zapolyarny Palace, or through the Director.
- **The Director** (Pierro) assigns missions and calls meetings. He also chairs votes on decisions that carry national-level risk. Such a decision needs the in-person, unanimous approval of every active Harbinger. Incapacitated members are not counted.
- **Divisions**: each Harbinger commands at least one company or division, and abroad also takes charge of the ordinary Fatui in that nation.

Harbingers are said to be chosen from the eleven most powerful members of the Fatui, and the most recent holders of the top three seats had power that could rival gods. A codename can pass from one holder to the next; there have been two Knaves. Tartaglia once had to give new recruits in Liyue their welcome speech because he was the only Harbinger there.

Harbingers have wide autonomy and may act on their own judgement even against central policy. Pierro said that during the Gnosis hunt the Harbingers did not fully represent Snezhnaya's official stance. That freedom has limits. The Tsaritsa forbids Harbingers from fighting one another, though she can lift the ban, and Fatui Internal Affairs (the Okhranka) can review a Harbinger's conduct. The wiki says that, on Capitano's orders, a Harbinger whose soldier dies must look after that soldier's family. Wanderer's character stories mention a "wild, frenzied banquet" of the Harbingers, which seems to play a part in deciding rank. Nobody has explained what it actually is.

Leadership: Pierro (Eftirvit), a former Khaenri'ahn royal mage, is the Director and was the first Harbinger.

The Tsaritsa founded the Fatui under Pierro's leadership, and he fights with an Electro Delusion.

Pierro personally recruited Signora, Dottore and Scaramouche. When Tartaglia was made a Harbinger, Pierro pinned the Delusion on him. More than a decade ago he announced the Tsaritsa's pardon of Peruere, who had killed the previous Knave, and her appointment as the new Knave, Arlecchino. Shortly before the Traveler's journey began, he gathered the Harbingers to explain the Tsaritsa's plan to collect all the Gnoses. He gave Pantalone the financial arrangements and Sandrone the technical needs.

Members: Roster as of 7.1: 1 Capitano (incapacitated, seat kept), 2 Dottore (dead), 3 Columbina (resigned), 4 Arlecchino, 5 Pulcinella, 6 Scaramouche (resigned, erased), 7 Sandrone, 8 Signora (dead), 9 Pantalone, 10 unknown, 11 Tartaglia (Childe). Seats without a note are active, as is the Director, Pierro.

Titles: Capitano is "The Captain", Dottore "The Doctor", Columbina "The Damselette", Arlecchino "The Knave", Pulcinella "The Rooster", Scaramouche "The Balladeer", Sandrone "Marionette", Signora "The Fair Lady", Pantalone "Regrator" and Tartaglia "Childe".

Personal names of the members are:
- Pierro: Eftirvit
- Capitano: Thrain
- Dottore: Zandik
- Columbina: Kuutar by birth; she now calls herself Columbina Hyposelenia
- Arlecchino: Peruere
- Pulcinella: Mirko Radovidovich Veleshek
- Scaramouche: Kunikuzushi, a name he coined himself; he is now the nameless Wanderer
- Sandrone: Marionette Guillotin
- Signora: Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter
- Pantalone: Feofan Sergeyevich Veksel
- Tartaglia: Ajax

Crucabena was a previous Knave. Peruere killed her, so she is a former, dead member.

Their portfolios differ widely:
- **Capitano** directly commanded the Fatui armed forces and was their councillor in the Snezhnograd Veche.
- **Pulcinella** is Mayor of Snezhnograd and Glupov, Speaker of the Veche and its "linchpin". Sandrone says he represents politics itself.
- **Pantalone** runs the Northland Bank, speaks for finance in the Veche and is the richest Harbinger.
- **Sandrone** handles the Harbingers' technical needs and leads the Adventurers' Guild. She speaks in the Veche for her engineers and researchers.
- **Arlecchino** is "Father" of the House of the Hearth.
- **Tartaglia** inherited most of Capitano's troops and his Veche seat as the voice of the Fatui soldiers.

Goals: The Harbingers serve the Tsaritsa's plan, and Pierro explains that plan's purpose as confronting the Heavenly Principles. In practice this meant gathering the Archons' Gnoses, and later, in Snezhnaya, Project Mistilteinn, along with the energy-rationing Project Stuzha that feeds it. Individual Harbingers also pursue goals of their own. Some align with the Tsaritsa's will and some do not, as Dottore's fate shows.

Methods: Each Harbinger works in their own way. Signora used coercion and diplomacy. Tartaglia started a crisis in Liyue as a decoy. Dottore ran human experiments. Pantalone works through loans, and Pulcinella through politics and carefully worded letters. Arlecchino uses intelligence work and negotiation. Their status gives them weight: Tartaglia could not simply be handed over to the Liyue Qixing after Osial, so the Northland Bank paid heavy reparations instead. Many rank-and-file Fatui respect their Harbingers, and some act without orders to advance them or avenge them. After Signora's death, some of her subordinates stayed behind in Inazuma, apparently to settle the score.

History: **Origins.** After the cataclysm 500 years ago, the Khaenri'ahn Eftirvit joined the Tsaritsa's cause. In the third year of her reign she founded the Fatui under his leadership, and he became Pierro, the first Harbinger. Over the following centuries he brought in Signora (the Crimson Witch of Flames, whose fire he suppressed with a Cryo Delusion), Dottore (an expelled Sumeru scholar he found 400 to 450 years ago) and Scaramouche (the Raiden Shogun's discarded puppet, after the Tatarasuna affair). Arlecchino rose to the Fourth seat over a decade ago by killing Crucabena, and Tartaglia was conscripted as a youth and became the Eleventh.

**The Gnosis hunt (1.0-4.x).**
- Signora took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti.
- Signora also obtained the Geo Gnosis through Zhongli's contract with the Tsaritsa, while Tartaglia's summoning of Osial served as a decoy.
- Scaramouche secured the Electro Gnosis in Inazuma. Signora lost a duel before the throne to the Traveler, and the Raiden Shogun executed her (2.1).
- Dottore made Scaramouche into an artificial god in Sumeru and took the Electro and Dendro Gnoses back to Snezhnaya (3.x).
- Scaramouche erased himself from Irminsul, which left the Sixth seat remembered as empty for centuries (3.3).
- Neuvillette gave Arlecchino the Hydro Gnosis as a diplomatic gift (4.2).
- In Natlan (5.x), Capitano fought Mavuika and refused to take the Pyro Gnosis from her while she was weakened. He later took Mavuika's place as the death Ronova demanded and merged with the Lord of the Night (5.3). The Tsaritsa kept his rank as it was.

Relations: - **The Tsaritsa**: the Harbingers' source of authority and their only superior. She appoints them, forbids them to fight one another and decides their fate. She kept Capitano's rank, and she later revoked the order against Columbina.
- **Among themselves**: they trade barbs openly. Arlecchino and Sandrone despised Dottore. Columbina says Pantalone and Pulcinella despise each other even though they get along in public. Sandrone says Capitano left his troops to Tartaglia because he expected Pulcinella and Pantalone to "swoop in on his army like vultures" and divide it between them. Capitano privately respected Tartaglia and sometimes brought him to Sandrone's tea parties. Sandrone, Arlecchino, Columbina and Signora were tea-party companions.
- **The Archons**: mostly adversarial during the Gnosis hunt. The exception was contracts and gifts, such as Zhongli's and Neuvillette's.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 six are active: Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia. Capitano's body lies dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire in Natlan.

In 7.1 the active Harbingers voted unanimously to open Hroptatyr's notebook. Pierro, the Director, used the resulting "Eye of the Fatui" Delusion to mortally wound Ronova, at heavy cost to himself. Arlecchino's deal means the House of the Hearth is to leave Fatui service, but this has not yet been shown taking effect. Project Stuzha is on hold. No new Harbinger has been appointed to any empty seat.

133.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Harbinger seats and codenames
133.content: Each Harbinger is appointed by the Tsaritsa and given a new codename and title, plus a seat number that reflects combat power. Wanderer's stories say the young Scaramouche was boosted until he matched the lower-ranked Harbingers, and that he later earned the sixth seat. Codenames can be inherited: Peruere took "The Knave" from Crucabena. Seats do not move up when a higher one empties, and they can stay empty indefinitely. As of 7.1 the 2nd and 8th belong to the dead, the 3rd and 6th to resigned members, and the 10th has never been identified. Capitano's 1st seat has been kept for him.

134.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Unanimous vote of the Harbingers
134.content:
In the Fatui, any decision carrying a national-level risk must be voted on in person by every active Harbinger and must pass unanimously. The Director chairs the vote. Pierro had Hroptatyr's notebook sealed by this rule centuries ago. In Etched in Time (7.1) he called the Harbingers to the Armory Palace archives. The votes went like this:
- Pulcinella said the old fear of making Snezhnaya a "second Khaenri'ah" no longer applied, since they were already at odds with the Ruler of Death.
- Tartaglia was in favour because the Traveler could deal with Abyssal corruption.
- Arlecchino would not leave "a valuable card" unplayed.
- Pantalone called the risk acceptable.
- Sandrone, repelled by the comparison with Dottore, agreed out of curiosity.

Pierro, who had raised the motion, did not need to vote, and it passed. Capitano was not required because he is incapacitated.

135.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Prohibition on Harbinger infighting
135.content: The Tsaritsa forbids Harbingers from fighting each other. They may insult one another, but they may not draw steel. During the Nod-Krai crisis Arlecchino said that if the ban was not lifted, she would fight Dottore as Peruere rather than as the Knave. The Tsaritsa then had Fatui Internal Affairs review Dottore's case, granted the Harbingers unilateral powers and allowed Arlecchino and Sandrone to eliminate him if needed. Columbina destroyed him. Afterwards the Tsaritsa revoked the Palestar Edict, the order to bring Columbina back.

136.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: Capitano's letter and Councilor Tartaglia
136.content: Before leaving for Natlan, Capitano gave Pierro a detailed letter arranging the future of his subordinates. All his key people went to Tartaglia, along with his place in the Snezhnograd Veche as the voice of the Fatui soldiers. Sandrone explains that Capitano thought Tartaglia was immature but showed great potential and an unusual purity. He also wanted to keep Pulcinella and Pantalone from dividing his army and becoming unstoppable. By 7.0 Tartaglia, who had always assumed Capitano looked down on him, is buried in Veche paperwork.

137.content: The 2022 teaser A Winter Night's Lazzo shows the surviving Harbingers, without Scaramouche, gathered around Signora's coffin after her death in Inazuma. Capitano called her methods dishonourable but her loss a great pity, then pressed Dottore about Scaramouche and the Electro Gnosis. Pulcinella's half-day of mourning drew criticism from Pantalone and Arlecchino. Pierro silenced the squabbling and called her Rosalyne. Her tomb is the ice-bound Sanctuary of Grief in Snezhnaya, which became accessible in 7.0.

138.comment: Eleven Fatui Harbingers: The Tenth seat and the previous Knave
138.content: No Tenth Harbinger has been named in canon through 7.1, and nothing about the holder is known. The wiki notes that every active Harbinger attended the 7.1 vote and no Tenth appeared, so the seat is either empty or held by Pierro. A previous Knave, Crucabena, ran the House of the Hearth. Peruere killed her more than a decade ago, and the Tsaritsa pardoned Peruere and made her the new Knave, Arlecchino. Capitano, Scaramouche and Signora were present when Pierro announced the decision.

139.content:
The Eremites (also: Eremites, Eremite, Eremite mercenaries, Eremite brigades): The Eremites are the desert mercenaries of Sumeru. They come from the Great Red Sand, whose ancient civilisations have collapsed, and they hire out their blades across Teyvat. Outsiders use "Eremites" as a blanket name for many separate brigades and tribes. Some are honourable, some are criminal, and some ignore the others entirely. They are the only authorised mercenary organisation in Sumeru, and many foreigners judge them as unscrupulous soldiers of fortune. The best-known members are Dehya of the Blazing Beasts and the Corps of Thirty who guard Sumeru City.

The Eremites hold a claim to part of the legacy of the desert's lost civilisations, which the official Sumeru teaser calls a "deterrent of last resort in a crisis". They have an open partnership with the Adventurers' Guild.

Structure: There is no overall chain of command. The Eremites are split into brigades and tribes, each with its own beliefs and code of conduct, and the groups overlap or conflict. Anyone can join the mercenary brigades. Traditionally only people from the desert may, but Rukh Shah is an exception. Some people simply borrow the name for their own benefit. Consultants and advisors help the groups talk to each other.

Major groups named in canon:
- **Corps of Thirty**: the Akademiya's permanently hired brigade in Sumeru City, based in the Citadel of Regzar, with teal-green scarves instead of the usual red.
- **Blazing Beasts**: the brigade of Dehya.
- **Deshret's Relics**: a large faction that held its members by recording their sins, with subgroups **Ayn Al-Ahmar** (Port Ormos) and **Dakan Al-Ahmar** (led by Kusayla).
- **Rahman's faction**, near the Valley of Dahri.
- **Caracal Battalion**, active in Port Ormos.
- **Thutmose**, whose secret base is on Lamb-Devourer Rock.
- **Farrokhzadan**, a sellsword clan led by Siman Farrokhzad.
- **Aybak's group** at Caravan Ribat.
- Tribes: **Tanit**, **Shimti** and **Uzza** (matriarchal and devoted to the Goddess of Flowers), **Afiyah** (nomads of the Desert of Hadramaveth), and **Iab** and **Unut** (descendants of the Thamudians).
- Others: unaffiliated brigades and tribes that take private commissions as bodyguards, with no clear structure.

Members: Dehya is the best-known: a legend among Eremites, former Corps of Thirty and now Blazing Beasts. Rukh Shah, the Corps of Thirty's Parchamdar, is the youngest ever to hold the post. Aybak leads a group at Caravan Ribat that is under contract with the Akademiya to guard the town and maintain the Wall of Samiel. His group calls each other brother and sister. Rahman leads his own faction. Dehya's adoptive father Kusayla led Dakan Al-Ahmar. Mizri led Ayn Al-Ahmar in Port Ormos.

Further named figures:
- Babel, Tanit matriarch (see her entry).
- Siman Farrokhzad, sage of the Akademiya and head of the Farrokhzadan.
- Lunja, who leads one Farrokhzadan group.
- Asfand, Corps of Thirty Consultant.
- Mishal, last leader of Deshret's Relics.
- Sinuhe, last chief of the Shimti, and Nefer, his adopted daughter.
- Arif, last known chief of the Iab, and Nizar, last chief of the Unut.
- Tariq and Tumart, Ayn Al-Ahmar members at Port Ormos.
- Jebrael and Samail, once called the twin blades of Thutmose.
- Kasim, a fraud who uses the name for his own benefit and is known as one by the Corps of Thirty.
- Younan, who travels to Inazuma to facilitate trade from Sumeru, and Irus, whose crew was hired by Jakob in Fontaine.

Abilities and limits: Eremite fighting is tied to their ancestry. The Sword-Dancers' skills are said to date from Deshret's civilisation and are now an art as well as a combat style. Eremite dance traditions descend from their ancestors' worship rituals. Elemental power among them is not innate but borrowed from Spirits of Omen, ancient desert spirits that dwell in their weapons and awaken in times of peril.

High-ranking Eremites can summon Spirits of Omen: Stone Drakes for Geo, Wind Gledes for Anemo, Dendro Spirit-Serpents for Dendro and Pyro Scorpions for Pyro. Equipment varies, including axes, halberds, crossbows, katars, curved swords, lances, bows and catalysts.
Tiers in the game: the weakest are physical fighters, mid-level Eremites channel one element (Electro axes, Cryo twin blades, Hydro katars), and high-level Eremites wield Geo, Anemo, Dendro or Pyro with spirit support. The Loremaster's text also says that the oral history of the ancient civilisations is slowly fading or being distorted, though those who remember keep it alive. The Eremites' history survives mainly in their performance culture and combat.

Goals: Most Eremites seek coin. They take commissions as guards, escorts, caravan protectors and fighters. Some groups follow causes: devout followers of King Deshret seek his resurrection or oppose the Akademiya's version of history, and some brigades act for their own survival. Dehya hopes to bring hope to the desert she considers home.

Methods: Contract work: guarding caravans and settlements, hunting monsters, escorting scholars and delivering goods. Many play the Genius Invokation TCG across Sumeru. Criminal factions blackmail, raid and extort. Deshret's Relics collected "records" of members' shameful deeds to bind them, the Tanit raised captured children as devoted "Falcons", and Dakan Al-Ahmar raided caravans for supplies during its revenge campaign.

Alliances can be pragmatic or religious. Thutmose sought knowledge and partners from Sumeru researchers to the Fatui. The Farrokhzadan carried out a commission for Dottore and later tried to capture Aranara for him. Rahman's faction held Village Keepers hostage to cross the forest. Corps members follow the Akademiya's assignments and civilians' requests.

History: The Eremites descend from the lost civilisations of the Great Red Sand, particularly the realm of King Deshret. Their stories pass down mainly by word of mouth. Their age is unknown, and the best-documented events come from the 3.x content.

**Sumeru Archon Quest (Chapter III).** Rahman's faction intercepted men of the Akademiya who had kidnapped the Village Keepers of Aaru Village and took everyone hostage. They believed rumours that King Deshret would return. After the Traveler's party showed them what the previous Dendro Archon had done, Rahman's group abandoned their prejudice and helped free Lesser Lord Kusanali.

**Deshret's Relics.** Dehya's father Kusayla burned the faction's records room with himself inside, freeing members from blackmail. After his death Dakan Al-Ahmar attacked the Relics. In Sincerity's Facade, the Traveler, Dehya and Dakan Al-Ahmar dismantled the Relics and their leader Mishal. The Corps of Thirty took the survivors.

**Port Ormos.** Ayn Al-Ahmar and the Caracal Battalion competed for a Divine Knowledge Capsule that was rumoured to hold King Deshret's power. Ayn Al-Ahmar won it at auction, but Mizri went mad when he used it. Alhaitham and the Traveler defeated him, and Alhaitham secretly took the capsule.

**The Tanit.** In the Dune-Entombed Fecundity quests, the Tanit tribe, under Matriarch Babel, were destroyed by the Traveler and Jeht after Babel's attempts to remove them failed.

**The Shimti, Iab and Unut.** About 20 years ago, a sandstorm blocked the Shimti's well, and Sinuhe drew water from the Iab's well without permission. The Iab destroyed the Shimti save for his adopted daughter Nefer, who later set the Iab and Unut against each other, so that both lost their warriors in the fighting.

**Later appearances (6.5-6.6).** In the limited-time 6.5 event Where Waves Meet the Reef, the former scholar Ashvapati recounts how the Eremite tribe of Khaemwaset, which had taken him in, was razed by enemies armed with technology that the Eremite Sennedjem had sold them; Ashvapati saved three children, Ati, Raya and Neb. In the 6.6 Archon Quest act As All Falls to Emptiness, Dehya meets the Traveler and Nefer in Sumeru and introduces herself as an Eremite mercenary whose work keeps her in the desert.

Relations: **Akademiya.** The Corps of Thirty serves the Akademiya as hired peacekeepers, and the Akademiya's liaison officer is Effendi. The Akademiya's wider reputation among Eremites is poor, especially among devoted followers of Deshret. Aybak's group is also contracted to the Akademiya. After the reforms that followed the Archon Quest, Rahman's faction now works with Setaria to promote education among desert peoples. The Matra are the Akademiya's disciplinary officers, and their General Mahamatra Cyno hails from the desert.
**Adventurers' Guild.** An open partnership.
**Rival Eremites.** The Corps of Thirty has a tenuous relationship with other groups, and Rukh Shah warns visitors to be careful of Eremites outside the city.

**Fatui.** Thutmose and the Farrokhzadan cooperated with the Fatui, and the Doctor commissioned the Farrokhzadan.

Reputation: Outsiders see them as mercenaries who will do anything for coin. The scholar Nazafarin calls them true soldiers of fortune who will do anything for money. Impostors who use the name and do poor work for unwary foreign clients also drag down the reputation of the whole group. Dehya is considered a legend among them.

Status as of 7.1: Active in Sumeru as of 7.1, with the Corps of Thirty guarding the capital and brigades taking contracts across the desert.

Rahman's faction now supports the reformed Akademiya. Deshret's Relics and the Tanit are gone, and Dakan Al-Ahmar surrendered after avenging Kusayla. In 6.6, during the crisis that sealed Sumeru, Dehya was still working in the desert as an Eremite mercenary. No Eremite story in the Snezhnaya content (7.0-7.1) was found.

140.content: The Akademiya's permanently hired Eremite brigade in Sumeru City. It started as thirty founders hired by the sages and is said to be among the oldest Eremite groups. It now has more than thirty members, but keeps the name in memory of the founders. Its members wear teal-green scarves with a petal-like emblem like the Akademiya's, and its barracks are in the Citadel of Regzar. The Parchamdar, Rukh Shah, commands it, and Asfand serves as its Consultant. It keeps the peace in the capital and manages and coordinates the other mercenary brigades. Dehya is a notable former member.

141.content:
The brigade of Dehya, who joined at a young age after her last argument with her adoptive father Kusayla. Kusayla had quietly arranged her place there to protect her from Deshret's Relics. During the Whirling Waltz event, the Traveler and Paimon became the Blazing Beasts' official partners.

The Whirling Waltz material is limited-time event content and Paimon's remark is the only source for the partnership claim here.

142.comment: The Eremites: Deshret's Relics and Ayn Al-Ahmar
142.content: Deshret's Relics was a large Eremite faction that held its members by blackmail, having them leave behind "records" of their sins as proof of loyalty. Subgroups were **Ayn Al-Ahmar** and **Dakan Al-Ahmar**. The names refer to King Deshret's alleged true name, Al-Ahmar. Kusayla, leader of Dakan Al-Ahmar, died burning the records, and his followers took revenge on the Relics and on innocent travellers. The Relics' last leader Mishal was taken down by Dakan Al-Ahmar, Dehya and the Traveler. Ayn Al-Ahmar survived in Port Ormos under Mizri, devout in their worship of Deshret and disdainful of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.

143.content: An Eremite faction near the Valley of Dahri led by Rahman, a longtime friend of Dehya. Maqrin and Tanina are other members. They believed the Akademiya's rumours that King Deshret would return, resented the forest and its Archon, and held the Village Keepers of Aaru Village as hostages. After learning the truth about Rukkhadevata, they helped the Traveler's party against the sages and, afterwards, work with Setaria to promote education among desert peoples.

144.comment: The Eremites: Tanit and the matriarchal tribes
144.content: The Tanit were a nomadic, matrilineal tribe in the Desert of Hadramaveth who venerated the Goddess of Flowers. They were led by a Matriarch and Nine Elders, traded in crocodile products, spices and essential oils, hunted wenut, and raised captured children as devoted "Falcons". They were eventually annihilated by the Traveler and Jeht after Matriarch Babel's schemes failed. The Shimti and Uzza were also matriarchal tribes. The Shimti, known for their beautiful women, were massacred by the Iab about 20 years ago after their chief Sinuhe took water from the Iab's well; only his adopted daughter Nefer survived. The Thamudian-descended Iab and Unut were later wiped out or scattered in the conflict set off by Nefer's revenge.

145.content: An Eremite clan likely descended from a man named Agha Farrokh, now led by his daughter Siman Farrokhzad, an Akademiya sage connected with Amurta and the Bimarstan. On her orders the clan dealt with the Fatui, completing a commission to kill a Fatui traitor for Dottore and then trying to capture Aranara for him. Lunja leads one of its groups.

146.content: Ancient desert spirits, or fragments of them, that can manipulate the elements and dwell in Eremite weapons. They awaken in times of peril and are summoned by high-ranking Eremites: Stone Drakes by Stone Enchanters, Wind Gledes by Galehunters, Dendro Spirit-Serpents by Floral Ring-Dancers and Pyro Scorpions by Scorching Loremasters. The lore suggests an awakened spirit is satisfied only once blood has been spilled.

147.content: The **Caracal Battalion** competes in Port Ormos for the Divine Knowledge Capsule; Ayn Al-Ahmar's Tariq and Tumart call them money-grubbing opportunists. **Thutmose** is a Deshret-devoted group seeking the secret of Al-Ahmar from researchers and the Fatui, from a base on Lamb-Devourer Rock. **Aybak's group** guards Caravan Ribat and the Wall of Samiel for the Akademiya.

148.content:
Fatui (also: Fatuus, the Fatui, Fatui of Snezhnaya): The Fatui (one member is a Fatuus; the name is Latin for "fools") are Snezhnaya's government, diplomatic corps and military in one body. They answer to the Tsaritsa, the Cryo Archon, who founded them 500 years ago with Pierro as their first member and Director. Under him the Eleven Fatui Harbingers each run a division. The Fatui are headquartered in Glupov, a fortress city inside Snezhnograd, and their emblem is the Palestar Banner. Abroad they present themselves as envoys of the Tsaritsa's goodwill, but most nations distrust them: in the Traveler's journey they took Gnoses from one Archon after another, using deceit, extortion, bribery and human experimentation along the way.

At home the Fatui are simply the state. In-game guide text says they handle all aspects of governance and military affairs.
