Their members include soldiers, bureaucrats, politicians, bankers and spies, and most rank-and-file Fatui know nothing of the Tsaritsa's true plan but are loyal to her and to Snezhnaya.

Structure: The Tsaritsa sits at the top. Below her, Director Pierro relays her appointments, assigns missions and convenes the Harbingers. Each Harbinger leads a division with personal subordinates, and below them are numbered companies and squads.

Known parts of the organisation include:
- **Debt Collection**: mostly Pyro Agents. It recovers debts owed to the Northland Bank, using as much force as it takes.
- **The House of the Hearth**: the intelligence arm, an orphanage that raises children as agents under Arlecchino, "Father".
- **The Northland Bank**: the state bank, presided over by Pantalone, which also funds and houses Fatui operations abroad.
- **The Armory Palace**: the royal weapons-development institution in Glupov, managed by Sandrone.
- **Fatui Internal Affairs**: also called the Okhranka. It investigates misconduct among the Fatui and reports to the Tsaritsa.

Members receive pay, supplies and powerful weapons. In return they choose neither where they are sent nor whom they serve under. Annual leave grows with rank: a sergeant named Wislawa started with about ten days and said she could reach twenty-five through promotions.

Leadership: **The Tsaritsa (Anastasya)** rules Snezhnaya directly, and the Fatui exist to carry out her will. **Pierro, "The Jester"**, is the Director of the Fatui, the first Harbinger and the Harbingers' leader. Each Harbinger takes a codename from Italian commedia dell'arte, a title and a rank number based on combat power.

Status of the seats as of 7.1:
- Director: Pierro, active.
- 1st: Capitano, incapacitated. His life force is merged with the Lord of the Night in Natlan, but the Tsaritsa kept his rank.
- 2nd: Dottore, dead.
- 3rd: Columbina, resigned.
- 4th: Arlecchino, active.
- 5th: Pulcinella, active.
- 6th: Scaramouche, resigned and erased from Irminsul. He now lives as the Wanderer.
- 7th: Sandrone, active.
- 8th: Signora, dead.
- 9th: Pantalone, active.
- 10th: never revealed.
- 11th: Tartaglia (Childe), active.

Ranks are not shuffled upward when a higher seat empties, and seats can stay vacant indefinitely. Harbingers receive their appointments from the Tsaritsa, either in person at Zapolyarny Palace or through Pierro (it was Pierro who pinned Tartaglia's Delusion on him). Names can be inherited: Arlecchino took the codename of the previous Knave, Crucabena, after killing her. Prospective Harbingers may be invited by the Director to a "wild" and "frenzied banquet" that seems to decide their place. Whether that banquet is literal is unknown. Harbingers have wide autonomy and may act against central policy, but the Tsaritsa forbids them to fight one another unless she lifts the ban.

Members: The Fatui come from many backgrounds. Some are House of the Hearth orphans, some volunteer, and some are drafted, as Tartaglia was. Many are ordinary workers. Some are homesick on foreign postings, others grow fond of them, and they play wargames, buy souvenirs and grumble about their superiors. Playable characters tied to the Fatui include Tartaglia, Arlecchino, Sandrone, Lyney, Lynette, Freminet and Odette, and the Wanderer and Columbina are former Harbingers.

Goals: The Fatui serve the Tsaritsa's aim of a "perfect world", which means overthrowing the Heavenly Principles. In the Traveler's journey, that meant collecting the Gnoses: Harbingers were sent to each of the other six nations to obtain them, and by 7.1 the Tsaritsa held every Gnosis except the Pyro Gnosis, which was lost when Irminsul burned. They also develop Delusions and weapons, gain influence in other nations, and strengthen Snezhnaya against Celestia.

Pierro revealed in 7.0 that Project Stuzha, the energy-rationing policy that saved power for the Armory Palace, was really a lead-up to Project Mistilteinn, a weapon for facing the Heavenly Principles that relies on Stellar Linchpins. The Tsaritsa believes all seven Gnoses are needed to unlock a seal left by the Third Descender. By the end of 7.1 she held six. The Pyro Gnosis burned with Irminsul, and she expects it to be ejected from the Ley Lines eventually. Individual Harbingers add their own aims, for example Pantalone's wish to end the gods' control over Mora.

Methods: Abroad, the Fatui's usual pattern is to provoke or exploit a crisis and then offer "help" that leaves the local authorities in their debt. They bribe or collude with local elites, lend money through the Northland Bank and collect it ruthlessly, plant sleeper agents raised in the House of the Hearth, and use deniable operatives. Delusions (Vision-like devices that work for anyone and can be stronger than Visions, but drain or even kill their users) give their elite troops elemental power.

Ordinary troops differ by region. Skirmishers in elemental armour are the common line infantry abroad, while Oprichniki and Landcruiser war machines serve in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. Elite Delusion users (Agents, Cicin Mages, Mirror Maidens, Operatives) work alone or in small teams. Harbingers' personal styles shape their subordinates: some Fatui act without orders to advance their Harbinger's goals or to avenge a fallen one. Divisions sometimes work against each other. In Sumeru, another Fatui division had the troublesome Elchingen assassinated. By Capitano's policy, a commanding Harbinger is responsible for the families of Fatui who fall in service.

History: **Founding.** After the Belyi Tsar died in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Anastasya became Snezhnaya's Archon. In the second year of her reign the humans of Port Belovodye rebelled against their Fae rulers. In the third year she founded the Fatui with Pierro as first member and leader, choosing them over the Druzhna, and sent them against the port's independent government. On that campaign the Fatui occupied the lands of several Fae clans, whose princes were charged with negligence and condoning rebellion; envoys then talked the port into surrendering its instigators. The next year she ordered the Fatui to build Glupov, "the city of fools", near Snezhnograd, and she replaced the Fae aristocracy with the Snezhnograd Veche.

**The Gnosis campaign.** Shortly before the Traveler's journey began, Pierro briefed the Harbingers on the Tsaritsa's plan to collect the Gnoses. Pantalone was given the finances and Sandrone the technical needs. Signora took the Anemo Gnosis in Mondstadt and the Geo Gnosis in Liyue. Scaramouche took the Electro Gnosis in Inazuma. Dottore secured the Electro and Dendro Gnoses in Sumeru, and Neuvillette gave Arlecchino the Hydro Gnosis in Fontaine as a "diplomatic gift". In Natlan, Capitano declined to take the Pyro Gnosis.

**Nod-Krai (6.x).** After Columbina resigned and fled, the Tsaritsa issued the Palestar Edict and sent Harbingers to Nod-Krai. Dottore turned rogue, Internal Affairs ruled against him, and Arlecchino and Sandrone, with the Traveler and others, brought him down. Sandrone sacrificed herself and was later rebooted in Fontaine. Dottore then died for good when Nahida burned Irminsul, after Pantalone had secretly helped his soul's attack on Sumeru.

Relations: - **Other nations**: Snezhnaya keeps official relations with every nation, but its Fatui are distrusted nearly everywhere. Inazuma expelled them as a friendly party after Signora's plot, and the Liyue Qixing watch them closely.
- **The Traveler**: long a thorn in the Fatui's side, by 7.1 the Traveler is a trusted outsider. The Tsaritsa made them a "Consultant to the Tsaritsa".

- **Knights of Favonius**: relations are tense. Dottore used Inspector Eroch, and Fatui diplomats tried to exploit the Stormterror crisis.
- **The Rokot**: a non-violent Snezhnayan civic group opposed to Project Stuzha. The Fatui consider it an enemy but tolerate it.
- **Snezhnograd Veche**: Snezhnaya's legislature, chaired by Pulcinella as Speaker. Harbingers may sit in it, and the Fatui can usually get their policies passed. Tartaglia now sits there as the voice of the Fatui armed forces.
- **The Druzhna**: the Tsaritsa's personal guard, mostly Vila. It is separate from the Fatui. In 7.1 the Tsaritsa lent its Third Company to Tartaglia to help review officials accused of corruption.
- **Northern Intelligence Network**: the network Diluc belongs to tracks the Fatui and once foiled a Harbinger attempt on Diluc's life.
- **Celestia and the Shades**: since 7.0 the Fatui have been in open conflict with Ronova, the Ruler of Death.

Reputation: Abroad, "Fatui" is close to a curse word. People expect masked soldiers, crooked loans and plots behind diplomatic smiles. At home the picture is more mixed. The Fatui are the state, and Harbingers are wealthy, powerful public figures whose interests can start fashions (Tartaglia's taste in fishing gear made one item a sought-after craze). But Project Stuzha's rationing made many citizens resentful.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fatui remain in power in Snezhnaya. Pierro mortally wounded Ronova with the new Eye of the Fatui but was left badly depleted. Ronova's curse is lifted, and Project Mistilteinn can resume.

Six Harbingers are active: Pierro, Arlecchino, Pulcinella, Sandrone, Pantalone and Tartaglia. Capitano's seat is kept, and the seats of Dottore, Columbina, Scaramouche and Signora are empty. Arlecchino's agreed price for helping build the new Delusion is that the House of the Hearth will become independent of Fatui affairs and that no more children will be trained as spies. This has been agreed but not yet shown in practice. Tartaglia commands most of Capitano's former troops, and corruption lists from Pulcinella and the House of the Hearth are being reviewed with the Druzhna's help.

149.content:
- **Skirmishers**: the common soldiers abroad, wearing mechanical suits that give their weapons and armour elemental power and shields. Variants include Cryogunner and Hydrogunner Legionnaires, Pyroslinger and Geochanter Bracers, and Electrohammer and Anemoboxer Vanguards. Their handbook entry says they advance into foreign lands to scout and lay groundwork without asking whether they will live, and that they rely on teamwork because each is weaker alone.
- **Cicin Mages**: Delusion-wielding mages (Cryo or Electro) who command swarms of small elemental Cicins and enjoy toying with their prey.
- **Agents**: elite Pyro or Electro operatives who blink in and out of sight and fight with blades. Pyro Agents staff Debt Collection.
- **Mirror Maidens**: elite Hydro users who fight through conjured mirrors.
- **Operatives**: covert Wind and Frost agents, seen in Fontaine.
- **Landcruisers**: war machines built by the Armory Palace with the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau.

150.content: Unlike Skirmishers, Oprichniki are formally recruited, rigorously trained volunteers, sent either to the Fatui's most important strongholds or to the deadliest front lines. They serve in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya with kuuvahki-powered gear. Line Troopers, Vanguards, Grenadiers, Support Troopers, Medics and Bombardiers make up the ranks. Officers such as Fireblade Shock Troopers, Hailstorm Cannoneers and Thunderblitz Gvardiya fight with pure elemental power and mostly come from the Royal Military Academy. Oprichniki guard the Northland Bank's vaults in Snezhnograd with radios and access cards.

151.content: The Northland Bank lends generously and expects repayment in full and on time. When someone defaults, the Fatui's Debt Collection division, made up mostly of Pyro Agents, is usually sent and uses as much force as it takes. The bank sometimes chooses other options: in Nasha Town it turned the debtor Zhuoxin into an informant for ten years instead. Snezhnaya's deep cultural regard for loyalty and promises underlies the bank's claim to be "no ordinary bank".

152.content: The Fatui began as the Tsaritsa's instrument for securing her throne. In the second year of her reign, the humans of Port Belovodye rebelled against the Snowland Fae ruling class. The next year she founded the Fatui with Pierro as first member and leader, rather than mustering the Druzhna as Emperor Monomakh had done, and sent them against the port's independent government. The Fatui occupied the lands of the Drevogorye, Volkhovan and Cirnareka Fae clans, whose princes were charged with negligence and condoning rebellion and stripped of their titles. Grand Duke Drevogorye accused the Tsaritsa of treason, fought the Fatui and was killed. Her envoys then persuaded Port Belovodye to hand over the rebellion's instigators in return for amnesty for everyone else. The following year (the fourth year of the 799th Cycle) she ordered the Fatui to build the fortress of Glupov near Snezhnograd, and in the sixth year she set up the Snezhnograd Veche.

153.content: In Mondstadt the Fatui stirred up or exploited trouble to embarrass the Knights of Favonius. They lured Ursa the Drake into the attack that killed Crepus Ragnvindr, who died after using a Delusion, and Varka blames Dottore personally. After Stormterror's attack, a Fatui diplomat pressed Jean to let them kill Dvalin. Agents stole the Holy Lyre der Himmel, which was soon recovered. Signora then took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti by force. Some Fatui colluded with Schubert Lawrence to restore the Lawrence Clan, a plot the Knights foiled. They also eyed the heart of the dead dragon Durin on Dragonspine, and they compete with Diluc for a stolen vial of the Anemo Archon's breath. A diplomatic delegation lives in the Goth Grand Hotel, which Pantalone rented in its entirety, though they are apparently under lockdown.

154.content: The Fatui once had an embassy and a kind of diplomatic immunity in Liyue Harbor, and they invested through the Northland Bank. Tartaglia summoned Osial to draw out Rex Lapis, and Fatui soldiers fought the Millelith on the Jade Chamber. Behind that, Signora's real business was a contract under which Zhongli handed over the Geo Gnosis. Afterwards the remaining Fatui were viewed with suspicion and the Northland Bank paid heavy reparations. Later the Fatui backed Zhiyi's attempt to assassinate and replace Uncle Tian on the Qixing. Yelan foiled it, though Pantalone limited the damage. In a smaller affair, the Fatuus Javert ordered Cor Lapis through Gentry Maocai, whose bullying of merchants the Traveler and Xingqiu turned against him.

155.comment: Fatui: Ninth Company in the Chasm
155.content: Under an agreement Signora negotiated with the Qixing, the Fatui's Ninth Company, 64 soldiers sent by Pulcinella, entered the Chasm's underground mines to cleanse a strange sludge with an experimental device. The device exploded. About half the company, including its captain, died or went missing, and Staff Sergeant Anton took command as brevet captain. After Tartaglia's actions in Liyue Harbor the agreement was voided: the company's supplies were cut off, and the Millelith declared its members criminals while they were still trapped underground. When the Traveler found Anton he had only three men left, and they decided to retreat. Katarina, raised in the House of the Hearth, stayed behind to search for her lost brother.

156.content: The Fatui masterminded the Vision Hunt Decree and kept Inazuma's civil war going, probably by Pierro's design. Signora had the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions feed the Raiden Shogun false information and supply materials for a Delusion Factory that used Orobashi's Crystal Marrow. Life-draining mass-produced Delusions went to the Watatsumi Army, and the infiltrator Nathan got the wards on Yashiori Island destroyed, releasing the Tatarigami. Centuries earlier, Dottore's sabotage of the Mikage Furnace caused the Tatarasuna Incident. Scaramouche ran the factory and took the Electro Gnosis. After the Traveler beat Signora in a duel before the throne, the Shogun executed her and expelled the Fatui as a friendly party. Signora loyalists and a breakaway House of the Hearth cell under Efim Snezhevich, still following the dead Crucabena's directives, tried to reignite the war. Lyudochka Snezhevna's defection helped stop it.

157.content: Most Fatui work in Sumeru served Dottore. With corrupt Akademiya sages he turned Scaramouche into the artificial god Shouki no Kami. After that failed, he obtained the Electro Gnosis from Nahida by deleting his other Segments, and the Dendro Gnosis in an exchange of knowledge. His teams hunted Aranara and studied the Withering, and a desert expedition under Professor Fronkonsteen, betrayed by the Tanit matriarch Babel, was finally wiped out when its captive Jeht broke free. Viktor helped Vsevolod open a Northland Bank branch in Sumeru City. After Nod-Krai, Pantalone, disguised as one of Dottore's men, led Fatui to Gurabad and Sumeru City to support Dottore's takeover of Irminsul. Nahida burned the tree with the Pyro Gnosis, and Pulcinella wrote to apologise for Dottore's "unsanctioned" actions and promised relief supplies.

158.content: Arlecchino's House of the Hearth worked in Fontaine, officially to prevent the prophecy that the people would dissolve into the Primordial Sea, and investigated the Hydro Archon. Tartaglia, sent to help the local Northland Bank branch, was wrongly convicted and sent to the Fortress of Meropide, where Arlecchino's agents also tried to infiltrate. After the prophecy passed, Neuvillette gave Arlecchino the Hydro Gnosis as a "diplomatic gift". She later agreed with him that House members who wanted to leave could have their memories of it erased and live normal lives in Fontaine, and she withdrew most of her forces. Smaller affairs include Henri being tricked into stealing water-monitor cores, and a 34th Squad that only pretended to work.

159.content: Capitano came to Natlan for the Pyro Gnosis and duelled Mavuika. Learning that she had spent her power fighting him, he would not exploit her weakness and asked the Tsaritsa to release him from the task, which she accepted. His men's attempt to rework Natlan's Ley Lines through the Source Mechanism instead woke the Lord of the Night. Capitano then backed Mavuika's plan, and the Fatui fought beside the Natlanese against the Abyss, taking immense casualties. He finally merged his life force with the Lord of the Night to pay Ronova's price in Mavuika's place. Other Fatui in Natlan experimented on captured Saurians, and Sandrone's artificial Fatuus Velimiru hunted a Sovereign Lord's core with Ineffa as an unwilling key.

160.content: Edicts are the Tsaritsa's highest form of decree. After Columbina, the Third Harbinger, gave up much of her power to fulfil a promise to the Tsaritsa, then resigned and fled to Nod-Krai, the Tsaritsa issued the Palestar Edict, ordering the Fatui to find her at all costs. Harbingers were sent to Nod-Krai, and Dottore, Sandrone and Arlecchino stayed to oversee operations, including Sandrone's construction of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau over ancient moon ruins. After Dottore's defeat and Columbina's restoration, the Tsaritsa revoked the Edict.

161.comment: Fatui: Fatui Internal Affairs ruling on Dottore
161.content: Fatui Internal Affairs, also called the Okhranka ("security"), investigates misconduct inside the Fatui and reports to the Tsaritsa. Little else is known about it. When Dottore ignored a recall order and pursued the power of the Three Moons in Nod-Krai, the Tsaritsa had it investigate him. It concluded that he had acted against her will, and she lifted the ban on Harbingers fighting him, giving Arlecchino and Sandrone authority to eliminate him. In 7.1 the Tsaritsa promised that a suspect in the theft of Seals of Life would be sent to the internal division.

162.content: The Eye of the Fatui is the improved Delusion Pierro built for the fight with Ronova. Arlecchino explained that a Delusion's drain on its user falls under the authority of Death. The authorities of Life, Death, Time and Space once belonged to the moons, with the Iridescent Moon holding the greatest share of Death; after the moons fell the Heavenly Principles gave them to the Four Shades, but the broken Crimson Moon merged with the Abyss, so Death's authority survives in the Crimson Moon's bloodline. Arlecchino, a descendant of the Crimson Moon Dynasty, agreed to serve as the base, on condition that the House of the Hearth leave Fatui affairs and that no more children be trained as spies. During a full-power test the Abyssal influence surged out of control, and only the Traveler's quick purification kept it from corroding her. The decisive knowledge came from Hroptatyr's unsealed notebook. At Rankova Zorya, after Celestia had already reclaimed Ronova's authority, Pierro awakened the Eye against her. It poured out Abyssal energy, dealt her what Pierro judged fatal and irreversible damage, and left him badly depleted. Dainsleif remarked: "To wield the immense power that he did, one always has to pay an irrecoverable price."

163.content:
Fatui Internal Affairs (also: Okhranka, Fatui Internal Division, the Okhranka): Fatui Internal Affairs, also known as the Okhranka (Russian for "security"), is a special group within the Fatui that investigates misconduct among Fatui ranks. It answers to the Tsaritsa. Little else about it is known: canon names no members, leader or base.

It is not a combat division or a public face of the Fatui. It appears in canon only as the body that gets handed a case when the Tsaritsa wants a Fatui member's loyalty or conduct judged.

Structure: Canon gives no structure for the division: no ranks, no named staff, no headquarters. All that is established is that it is a special group of Fatui and that it reports to the Tsaritsa, not to a Harbinger. It should be treated as an unseen office. Scenes may refer to its existence, but should not show it with invented officers or an invented building.

Because it reports to the Tsaritsa, its findings carry her authority, as the Dottore case shows: the Harbingers acted on the outcome. How it gathers evidence, who sits in judgement and whether it has its own detention is never described.

Leadership: The only authority above the division that canon names is the Tsaritsa (Anastasya). The Harbinger Tartaglia, who describes the division to Arlecchino, is a messenger of the Tsaritsa's orders and is not shown to belong to it. No head of Internal Affairs is named through 7.1.

Goals: Its job, as canon states it, is to look into misconduct inside the Fatui and to deliver a formal verdict when the Tsaritsa asks, for example on whether a member has turned traitor and whether he is a threat to Snezhnaya.

Methods: Nothing is shown of its investigative methods. What canon does show is its role in the process: the Tsaritsa authorises it to review a case, it reaches a formal verdict, and the Tsaritsa then acts on that verdict. In the Seals of Life matter it is the destination for a suspect, who is to be handed over to it, which suggests it also takes custody of those it examines. That last point is an inference from the wording, not something shown on screen.

History: Its earliest appearance in canon is in Version 6.3 (Song of the Welkin Moon, Act VII), during the crisis in Nod-Krai. Dottore, the Harbinger called the Doctor, was recalled to Snezhnaya on the grounds that he was redundant, but did not leave. He stayed to attack Columbina and seize the power of the Three Moons. When the Tsaritsa learned of this, she authorised Fatui Internal Affairs to review his case and reach a formal verdict on whether he had turned traitor and whether he threatened Snezhnaya. Tartaglia relayed this to Arlecchino while he was sent to receive the refugees from Nod-Krai.

The wiki's account of the Tsaritsa summarises the result: the division found that Dottore had acted against her will. On that basis the Tsaritsa issued a decree, which Tartaglia read to Arlecchino, giving the Harbingers unilateral executive powers while the exceptional circumstances lasted and permitting Arlecchino and Sandrone to eliminate Dottore should he pose a threat. She also decided not to attack the evacuated Nod-Krai because unretrieved research material remained there. The Palestar Edict was lifted afterwards.

Version 7.1 (Chapter VII Act III) gives its second mention. After the Traveler learned from Avaz, a Northland Bank employee, that Pantalone might be behind the missing Seals of Life, the Traveler reported it to the Tsaritsa. She said the culprit should be handed to Fatui Internal Affairs, and that Pantalone himself was too proud to be involved.

Relations: Its relationship to the Fatui is that of an internal watchdog. It answers to the Tsaritsa, and its verdict on Dottore bound the Harbingers Arlecchino and Sandrone. Its dealings with Pantalone, the Northland Bank and the other Harbingers are not described.

The Harbingers lead their own divisions and are not shown to command Internal Affairs. In the Dottore case they waited for its verdict before acting. Characters who are shown to know of it include Tartaglia and Arlecchino, who discuss it in Nod-Krai, and the Tsaritsa herself.

Reputation: Canon gives no public reputation. It is spoken of matter-of-factly by senior Fatui, as a known part of the organisation.

Secrets: Nothing about its personnel or operations is established. The roleplay-safe approach is to leave its members unnamed and its methods vague, and to let it appear through the effects of its verdicts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is still the Tsaritsa's tool for judging Fatui misconduct. It has not appeared directly in any scene.

Its most recent mention is in Version 7.1, when the Tsaritsa said the suspect in the Seals of Life theft should be handed to it. Its future is not shown.

164.content: Fatui Internal Affairs, known as the Okhranka, investigates misconduct inside the Fatui and reports to the Tsaritsa. Little more is known. In 6.3 the Tsaritsa had it review Dottore's case after he ignored his recall in Nod-Krai; by the wiki's account it found he had acted against her will, which freed Arlecchino and Sandrone to eliminate him if he became a threat. In 7.1 she said a suspect in the Seals of Life theft should be sent to it.

165.content:
Feiyun Commerce Guild (also: Feiyun Guild, Fēiyún Shānghuì, Flying Cloud Commerce Guild): The Feiyun Commerce Guild is a powerful trading guild in Liyue, run as a family business. It deals in silk, tea and printed books. Its best-known member is Xingqiu, the second son of the Guild Manager, a studious young man with a mischievous streak.

The Guild apparently originated at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale and still keeps the family's old home there. Merchants in Liyue Harbor know the family well, and its reputation depends on its children behaving as befits it.

Structure: The Guild's leadership is the family: a retired great-grandfather who founded it, a grandfather who is patriarch, a father who manages it, and an elder son who is heir. Xingqiu is the second son.

The family estate is a multigenerational household, with servants. The wiki lists Xu, Sheng and Hongxing as servants, Qiuwei as a retailer, Lixin as a messenger at Yilong Wharf, and An Su as a butler. The family members are not named in canon. Xingqiu's older brother is learning to run the business, and Xingqiu is expected to support him once he takes over, though Xingqiu is not required to shoulder the Guild's affairs.

Leadership: Xingqiu's father holds the post of Guild Manager. His grandfather is the patriarch, and a great-grandfather, styled "His Lordship", founded the Guild and is now retired. Xingqiu's brother handles business tasks such as arranging transport through the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency. He and the father also host influential figures. Xingqiu once concluded from the way they treated Zhongli that Zhongli must be a high-profile person.

Goals: The Guild's goals are commercial: moving goods, selling them and keeping the family's reputation. It also wants its heirs to act the part. Xingqiu's brother tells him that if he cannot tidy a room he cannot tidy the world, because both brothers are responsible for the Guild's name.

Methods: The Guild trades silk, prints books and sells tea, and it has a warehouse in the Lisha region, left of Mt. Tianheng on the map. It hires the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency to move and protect goods. A shop in Sumeru's Port Ormos sells jewellery and silk, and the materials used to make them.

Xingqiu sometimes uses the Guild's influence to solve problems that violence cannot, in the manner of the disguised-king heroes in his novels. In a story quest, he averted a disaster and earned the Guild a sizable sum while doing so.

History: The Guild apparently originates at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale. The old family home there remains part of its property. The wiki links this to the Liyue Celebrates and Eight Adepts Face a Hidden Calamity quest, which establishes the family's multigenerational estate.

Relations: - **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: a guard company commissioned to move and protect the Guild's goods. It belongs to the Communications Office.
- **Guhua Clan**: Xingqiu studies its sword arts with his father's approval.
- **Ningguang, Yelan and Ganyu**: the family hosts or meets them. Yelan says she often has dealings with the family and expects Xingqiu will one day be "outsmarting everyone around him".

Xingqiu's older brother never discusses business with him directly and lets him pursue his interests. Xingqiu says he now sympathises with his brother, who has gone prematurely grey from stress. This is stated in a 2026 birthday mail from 7.1.

Reputation: Every merchant in Liyue Harbor knows of Xingqiu and the Guild. People see Xingqiu as kind, polite and promising, and parents hold him up as a model for their own children. Xingqiu says people see him only as the Guild's second son.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guild is active, with Xingqiu still balancing its affairs against his wandering adventures. The wiki records no changes to it in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

166.content: Xingqiu's family are unnamed in canon. His father is the Guild Manager, strict about behaviour befitting the Guild's name. His elder brother is the heir and lectures Xingqiu about messy rooms, bad calligraphy, skipped banquets and skipped meals, yet is gentler than the father. He once told the servants not to disturb Xingqiu's room, having mistaken the martial-arts novels under the bed for something more adult. Xingqiu in turn has developed an elaborate method for evading both, recounted in birthday mails.

167.comment: Feiyun Commerce Guild: Feiyun warehouse and shops
167.content: The Guild keeps a warehouse in the Lisha region, to the left of Mt. Tianheng on the map. It appears in Xingqiu's story quest Bookworm Swordsman (Fabulae Textile Chapter, Act I). There is also a Feiyun storefront in Port Ormos in Sumeru, selling jewellery and silk and their raw materials.

168.content:
Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah (also: Five Sinners, the Five Sinners, Five Sinners of Khaenriah, Sinners of Khaenri'ah, Five Great Sinners): The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah are five people who were once among Khaenri'ah's most admired, each the best in their field: "The Wise" Hroptatyr, "The Visionary" Vedrfolnir, "Gold" Rhinedottir, "The Foul" Surtalogi and the "Rächer of Solnari" Rerir. About 500 years ago, on the night they joined Dainsleif to storm the royal palace, they could not resist the call of the Abyss. They divided among themselves a world-shattering Abyssal power and became transcendent beings. When the cataclysm came, none of them defended their nation. Dainsleif, who fought beside them that night, has sworn he will never forgive them.

They were never a formal order. "Five Sinners" is what others call them, and the name stuck to all five. The power they took was the Abyssal power that King Irmin had the Traveler's sibling absorb. Dainsleif first named all five to the Traveler in Sumeru (4.7).

Members: - **Hroptatyr, "The Wise"**: President of the Universitas Magistrorum and Chief Royal Mage. He wanted limitless knowledge.
- **Vedrfolnir, "The Visionary"**: a prophet and Dainsleif's older brother. He wanted to see the future again.
- **Rhinedottir, "Gold"**: an alchemist of the Art of Khemia who wanted to create life. She later created Albedo.
- **Surtalogi, "The Foul"**: a knight who wanted supreme strength. He later became Skirk's master.
- **Rerir, "Rächer of Solnari"**: an ordinary intelligence officer. Dainsleif could not understand his fall until Nefer read his past in 6.1.

Dainsleif summed up their motives in 6.1: each was driven by a personal desire, and the Abyss tempted each of them through that desire. Rerir's was Tholindis: after watching his fiancée flee through a moon gate, he broke down and took the power hoping to follow her.

Before the fall, Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir were the two councillors King Irmin trusted most. Rhinedottir said Hroptatyr was by far the most favoured of the "Four Pillars of Khaenri'ah". Surtalogi was born in prison to parents condemned to death. He and Dainsleif trained under the knight Haden, and he lost limbs as punishment for following the code of knighthood. Rerir had handled Surtalogi's case file during his sentencing. In secret, Irmin had Rerir hunting down the last descendants of the Crimson Moon Dynasty.

Structure: The five had no hierarchy, no leader and no shared goal. They came together only once, as allies Dainsleif called on for one night. Afterwards they scattered, and none of them has been shown acting with another since.

Ties between individuals did survive, though. Vedrfolnir prophesied that Surtalogi would find a disciple out in the universe and bring her to Teyvat. Surtalogi trusted his prophecies and later took Skirk as that disciple. Skirk learned the names of Rhinedottir and Vedrfolnir from Surtalogi, and in 4.2 she said her master and Rhinedottir were both "pursuing some form of perfection". Hroptatyr said Vedrfolnir once told him a parable about two blond heirs to the crown.

Goals: They shared no goal. What they had in common was that each wanted something beyond human limits: foresight (Vedrfolnir), infinite knowledge (Hroptatyr), the creation of life (Rhinedottir), supreme strength (Surtalogi) and Tholindis (Rerir). Afterwards each went after that desire alone:
- Hroptatyr resolved to leave Teyvat and merge with the Abyss to gain infinite knowledge.
- Surtalogi crossed the sea of stars looking for an opponent who could beat him.
- Rhinedottir went on making life through alchemy.
- Rerir tried to follow Tholindis into the moon gate.

History: Late in the Eclipse Dynasty, Vedrfolnir warned King Irmin at court that Khaenri'ah would fall if he kept to his path. Irmin had him blinded in both eyes and thrown into the dungeons. Furious, Dainsleif secretly called together Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir, and that same night they stormed the palace. Dainsleif and Surtalogi fought the guards, Hroptatyr and Rhinedottir disabled the palace's security measures, and Rerir went to free Vedrfolnir. The rescue succeeded. Then the Abyss tempted the five, and each betrayed Dainsleif by taking a share of the Abyssal power held by the Traveler's sibling. Even Vedrfolnir, the brother Dainsleif had come to save, took his share.

**The cataclysm and after.** None of the five defended Khaenri'ah when the cataclysm came. Their fates afterwards went in different directions:
- **Rhinedottir**: her creations attacked the seven nations, among them the dragon Durin, the beast Elynas, the Rifthounds and the Bakunawa. She later made Albedo and then devoured the Heart of Naberius, taking on the role of Ruler of Life (revealed in 5.6).
- **Surtalogi**: told Teyvat he had lost interest in it and left for the stars.
- **Hroptatyr**: handed his notebook to Eftirvit (Pierro) in the ruins and departed for the sea of stars.
- **Vedrfolnir**: his consciousness was later seen as a chained crystal in the Unknown Sanctuary, empowering Chlothar.
- **Rerir**: entered the moon gate and was torn into fragments that became the Wild Hunt of Nod-Krai.

**Revelation order.** Gold was mentioned in Mondstadt book lore long before the group was named. Vedrfolnir's voice was heard in 3.5. Surtalogi was named as Skirk's master in 4.2. The group was named in 4.7, and the full story of the raid was told in 6.1.

Relations: - **Dainsleif**: their former ally and the organiser of the raid. He calls them traitors to himself and to their nation and has vowed vengeance. He still remembers Rerir as a friend.
- **King Irmin**: their sovereign. Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr were his most trusted servants until Vedrfolnir was blinded.
- **The Traveler's sibling**: the vessel of the Abyssal power the five divided.

- **Pierro (Eftirvit)**: Hroptatyr's old colleague and rival. He blames Hroptatyr for the nation's ruin, and in 7.1 he still said Hroptatyr had betrayed Khaenri'ah and the world.
- **Capitano**: told Ronova in 5.3 that most Khaenri'ahns knew nothing of the Five Sinners' exploitation of Abyssal power, yet all were cursed.
- **Skirk**: Surtalogi's disciple, brought to Teyvat in line with Vedrfolnir's prophecy.
- **Albedo and Durin**: two of Rhinedottir's creations, now in Mondstadt.
- **Abyss Order**: Chlothar turned to worshipping Vedrfolnir after the Sinner empowered him, and Paimon concludes Vedrfolnir inspired the Order's founding.
- **Hexenzirkel**: Rhinedottir is one of its witches (codename "R").

Reputation: Among Khaenri'ahns the five are hated for forsaking their nation in its hour of need. Dainsleif says he will never forget their names, and Pierro, speaking as Eftirvit inside Hroptatyr's memory in 7.1, told him he is "the scum of the earth". Elsewhere they are known mostly through their legacies: Gold's monsters, the Abyss Order and the Wild Hunt. Their power is spoken of with dread. Whole civilisations among the stars have failed to defeat Surtalogi, and Rhinedottir now holds a seat among the Four Shades.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they act separately. Rhinedottir is the Ruler of Life, Surtalogi roams the stars, Rerir is trapped in the moon's reflection, and Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir are unaccounted for.

- **Rhinedottir**: appeared in person in Snezhnograd in 7.1. She reclaimed the life authority stolen from Naberius and met the Tsaritsa.
- **Surtalogi**: last seen still seeking a worthy opponent, waiting for Skirk to surpass him.
- **Rerir**: sealed beyond the moon gate since 6.1. When Columbina met him there in 6.3 he was remorseful.
- **Hroptatyr**: in 7.1 only a memory of his younger self was met, preserved in his notebook's prism.
- **Vedrfolnir**: no confirmed whereabouts.

169.comment: Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah: The night of the palace raid
169.content: After King Irmin blinded and imprisoned Vedrfolnir for warning that Khaenri'ah would fall, Dainsleif gathered Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir and stormed the palace that same night. Each had a task. Dainsleif and Surtalogi fought the guards, Hroptatyr and Rhinedottir disabled the security measures, and Rerir freed Vedrfolnir. The rescue worked, but the five then gave in to the Abyss and divided among themselves the power Irmin had placed in the Traveler's sibling. Dainsleif was left alone and betrayed. The Wings of Fate's Course Intertwined glider lore calls the raid's "righteous deed" of saving the nation "but a deed done in passing".

key: one sixth of the Abyssal power
170.comment: Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah: The Sinners' share of Abyssal power
170.content: Dainsleif calls what the five took "a power that could destroy the world", which turned each of them into a transcendent being. The power came from the Traveler's sibling, whom Irmin had used as a vessel to absorb the Abyss. In her Character Story 5, Skirk recalls Surtalogi mentioning that the group divided enough Abyssal power to overturn a world, "or at least a sixth of it", and asks how he alone is now many times stronger than that. Canon does not say who holds the remaining sixth.

171.comment: Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah: Dainsleif's vow against the Sinners
171.content: In Sumeru (4.7), Dainsleif told the Traveler that the Sinner who had empowered Chlothar was his older brother Vedrfolnir. He then named all five. They had been the hope of their nation, he said, and the six of them together should have stopped the Vinster King. Because none of them defended Khaenri'ah, they will never have his forgiveness, and he vowed vengeance. He contrasted them with the Traveler's sibling, saying the twins could still be reconciled. By 6.1 he was willing to go further: he hired Nefer to uncover Rerir's past and held open the gate that sealed his old friend away.

172.content:
Flower-Feather Clan (also: Tlalocan, the Flower-Feather tribe, Flower-Feather Clan settlement): The Flower-Feather Clan, whose older name is Tlalocan, is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its people live alongside the Qucusaurs, the proudest of the flying Saurians, and its elite flying squad patrols the skies on Qucusaur-back. The settlement sits among the cliffs of Quahuacan Cliff in northern Natlan, overlooking the ruins of Ochkanatlan. The current chief is Mutota. Its most famous member is Chasca, the Peacemaker who bears the Ancient Name Vuka.

Some clan members, like the Qucusaurs, have mastered riding Natlan's hot currents of gaseous Phlogiston without being burned. Joining the flying squad means passing a famously hard trial, and those who give up are called the "Wingless". The tribe was founded thousands of years ago by Lianca, a girl raised by dragons, as a refuge for people who had nowhere else to go.

Structure: A chief leads the tribe, advised by elders. Its pride and best-known institution is the Qucusaur Riders, the flying squad, which has both active and reserve members. Any applicant must be a capable warrior and must also win a Qucusaur's trust; the flying trials are held at a trial arena in the valley below the settlement. People who repeatedly fail, or who stop trying, are called the "Wingless". Many keep retaking the trials, some leave to work for other tribes, and some find other work in the clan. Clan members summon their Saurian companions by whistling or blowing a horn.

The clan also has Peacemakers, mediators who settle disputes between people, between tribes, between humans and Saurians, and even between Saurians. Chasca is the most famous, and by her own account she named the role after a lesson about communication being humanity's strongest weapon. Other roles seen in the settlement include a tribal doctor (Chuychu, who specialised in Abyssal corruption), a Saurian veterinarian (Ifa), a trial-arena administrator, hot-air-balloon operators and a reputation advisor, Abundi, who handles the clan's dealings with outsiders.

Leadership: Chief Mutota is a scarred, grey-haired veteran who values patience and caution above bravado. He likes to remind people that scars are a badge of honour but also a record of mistakes.

Mutota led the defence during the Abyss invasion and then the rebuilding. He accepted Iansan's help and asked the Traveler and Chasca to look into trouble inside the tribe. He gets on with ordinary members as well: Pixica calls him "Boss", and he coaches Wingless applicants himself. When the elder Allpa tried to depose him, he escaped capture only because he was out coaching, and he quickly rallied the tribe against her.

Members: - **Chasca**: Peacemaker and flying-squad warrior, bearer of the Ancient Name Vuka. She was raised by the Qucusaur Chimpu and adopted by Cusco's family.
- **Ifa**: a renowned Saurian veterinarian, known as the "Tlalocan Vet".
- **Mutota**: the chief.
- **Allpa**: a former elder and Flying Captain who found the infant Chasca. She is now imprisoned for her coup.
- **Cusco**: Chasca's adoptive father and Chuychu's father. He also checks injured Saurians.

- **Chuychu**: Cusco's daughter, Chasca's younger sister and the clan's doctor for Abyssal corruption. She died in the Abyss invasion.
- **Pixica**: a Wingless warrior who chose to stay and now runs the hot-air balloons.
- **Coyllur and Zhunan**: Wingless applicants. Mutota coached them during the Phlogiston Wings crisis.
- **Coya**: a Qucusaur, Chimpu's daughter and Chasca's "sister". She is listed with the clan because of her bond with Chasca.

Goals: The clan's ideals go back to Lianca: a place where the weak can live freely and without fear, where no one has to kneel to anyone. In practice its people guard their own territory from the air, keep watch over the ruins of Ochkanatlan, and protect the bond between riders and Qucusaurs that the clan is built on. Chasca says that clan pride, and especially the riders' pride, sometimes "borders on arrogance".

Methods: Riders fly Qucusaurs on patrol and in battle. Qucusaurs and some clan members can use the high-temperature currents of gaseous Phlogiston without being burned. Some members, such as the trainee Kallfu, ride the currents without any equipment. Riders are expected to train relentlessly: a Qucusaur that is not fully under control can kill both itself and its rider. To other tribes, a lone Flower-Feather member who starts whistling is a sign that something nearby is wrong.

Since the fall of Ochkanatlan the clan has kept watch over the ruins, and at some point it set up a blockade to stop travellers from entering. Its weapons include firearms: Xilonen built Chasca's oversized gun, and Xilonen called it the strongest weapon she had ever made "for your tribe". The tribe's own Peacemakers prefer to settle conflicts with words first.

History: **Founding.** Thousands of years ago, the abandoned girl Lianca was raised by the Eighth Sovereign Lord, a dragon who taught her to "kneel to no one". She left on her own journey, came to see how rare freedom was, and gathered other orphans. Then came warriors who would not live under other tribes' rules, and finally banished dragons, and she took in friend and foe alike. Lianca travelled with Xbalanque and later joined Och-Kan's Grand Alliance. As Och-Kan became obsessed, she refused his orders to send more labourers. Her own son, who was also her chosen successor, secretly turned Och-Kan against her, and she died fighting his forces. By legend she shot her treacherous son with her first arrow, and with her last pinned her own body to her bow rather than fall.

**Liberation from Och-Kan.** Under Och-Kan, people sympathetic to Saurians were persecuted. A tribal elder of Tlalocan banished a scarlet-eyed youth to save him from capture. The youth later gathered heroes against Och-Kan and burned the "ineffable city", freeing the Flower-Feather Clan, and he became the second Pyro Archon about 2,000 years ago. He asked that his name be erased so that others would take up his mantle. Since then the clan has lived on the cliffs, looking down on the ruins of Ochkanatlan.

**The Abyss invasion (5.1).** When the Abyss attacked all of Natlan, the Flower-Feather Clan was hit hardest. Chuychu died of Abyssal corruption, and in that moment Chasca was acknowledged by her Ancient Name and became the sixth hero.

Relations: - **Qucusaurs**: the clan's partners and the core of its identity. Riders must earn their trust. Allpa's betrayal, which treated Qucusaurs as a resource, horrified the tribe.
- **Other tribes**: the clan is one of six. Iansan of the Collective of Plenty came to help rebuild, and Xilonen of the Children of Echoes makes the clan's weapons. Allpa's son Tepal was raised among the Children of Echoes.
- **The Pyro Archon**: Mavuika visited Cusco's family to give her condolences after Chuychu's death and later worked with the clan's elders on the Nod-Krai harbor. The clan counts the second Pyro Archon among its own.
- **Ochkanatlan**: an old wound. The clan once served in Och-Kan's Grand Alliance and was later liberated from it. Mutota was disgusted to learn that the Phlogiston Wings were based on Ochkanatlan technology.

Reputation: Natlan knows the clan for its flying squad and its proud riders. Furnishing text says that nearly every member dreams of joining the flying squad and setting off on a "crusade to conquer the sky". Other tribes treat the clan's warning whistles seriously. Chasca won the clan new respect when she competed for it in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, though people in the clan once called her a "little vulture" before she became a respected Peacemaker.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan has recovered from the Abyss invasion under Chief Mutota, and its flying trials have resumed. Allpa and her accomplices are in custody.

Since 5.8 the clan has run a simple harbor at Quahuacan Cliff for people coming from Nod-Krai. No clan story developments were found in the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quests. In a 6.7 limited-time event, Chasca agreed to plan a training exchange with Fontaine's Special Patrol, but whether it has started is not shown.

173.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: Qucusaur Riders and the flying trials
173.content: The Qucusaur Riders are the Flower-Feather Clan's elite flying squad. Applicants must prove themselves as warriors and then win a Qucusaur's approval in the flying trials, held at an arena in the valley below the settlement. Losing a Qucusaur's trust is the most common reason for failure, and the clan treats it seriously because an uncontrolled flight can kill both rider and Saurian. Chasca, who was raised by Qucusaurs, says even she had to earn their approval. Applicants call Qucusaurs by whistle or horn, and a weak, unsure whistle will not bring one. After the Abyss invasion the trials were held again. The arrival of Phlogiston Wings led Chasca to argue that wing users should be judged by different standards.

174.content: "Wingless" is the clan's name for people who fail the flying trials repeatedly or give up on them. They must give up their Saurian companion for their own safety, and life in the tribe can be hard for them. Some keep trying. Allpa eventually passed. Others, like Pixica, who runs the hot-air balloons, make peace with it and find other ways to reach the sky. Chasca says that only the best warriors attempt the trials at all, and that the clan quietly watches over the Wingless until their fighting spirit returns, as Qucusaurs watch their unfledged young. Allpa used the Wingless' longing to fly to win support for her Phlogiston Wings.

175.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: Peacemakers of the Tlalocan
175.content: The Peacemakers are the Flower-Feather Clan's mediators. As a child, Chasca was so prone to fighting that Allpa taught her from a woven scroll titled "Peacemaker - the Art of Communication", which taught that language is humanity's greatest weapon. Chasca later adopted the name for herself and her role. Peacemakers step into disputes between people, tribes, humans and Saurians, or Saurians among themselves, and settle them with words first and force only when words fail. In one story a pair of feuding chiefs signed a very formal joint statement thanking the Peacemaker for their "reconciliation".

key: First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan
176.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: Lianca, founder of the Flower-Feather Clan
176.content: Lianca, the clan's founder and first bearer of the Ancient Name Vuka, was an abandoned infant raised by the Eighth Sovereign Lord (Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak), who gave her the bow Chain Breaker. She built the tribe from orphans, rule-breaking warriors and banished dragons, accepting anyone. She journeyed with Xbalanque and joined the Grand Alliance, then defied Och-Kan. She also saw through a scheme by the Eleventh Lord, imprisoned its vengeful half in the Temple of Cascading Colors, and sent its benevolent half, later rebuilt as Ineffa, away from Natlan. Her son, also her chosen successor, betrayed her to Och-Kan, and she died in battle refusing to kneel. Afterwards, a former clansman tried to seize the tribe's banner by marrying her second daughter, who lured him into the warehouse where it was kept and set it on fire, killing them both.

177.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: The Scarlet-Eyed Youth of Tlalocan
177.content: The second Pyro Archon, about 2,000 years ago, was a young man of Tlalocan with red eyes. Under Och-Kan, people who sympathised with Saurians were persecuted, so the tribe's elder banished him to save him from capture. After trials in which he faced his own death, he gathered heroes such as Sakkuk against Och-Kan, burned the ineffable city and freed the Flower-Feather Clan. He then asked Sakkuk to erase his name from history, so that others would be inspired to take up his mantle. His real name is unknown.

178.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: Allpa's coup and the Phlogiston Wings
178.content: After the Abyss invasion, merchants brought Phlogiston Wings to the clan. These Phlogiston jetpacks, steered with a handheld trackball, let the Wingless fly without a Saurian. A Qucusaur kept attacking the merchants. It was Coya, whose hatchling Chime had been stolen by hunters supplying the wings' maker, supposedly the failed applicant Tepal. Chasca, the Traveler and Coya traced the operation to a flying workshop above the trial grounds, powered by an Ochkanatlan relic, where Qucusaurs were being drained of the Phlogiston their glands produce. Tepal had long been dead, and the mastermind was his mother, Elder Allpa. She blamed Qucusaurs for his death, saw them as beasts that cared only for themselves, and believed the tribe's safety could not be entrusted to wild Saurians. She threatened the caged Chime to force the group to surrender and sent followers to seize Mutota, but Mutota was away coaching, and her coup collapsed. Coya shielded Chasca from the exploding relic, the two "sisters" made peace, and part of the dismantled workshop became the jail for Allpa and her followers.

179.comment: Flower-Feather Clan: The Flower-Feather Clan in the Abyss invasion
179.content: During the nationwide Abyss invasion (5.1), Abyssal "tumours" fell across Natlan, and the Flower-Feather Clan suffered the worst losses. Chuychu, Chasca's sister and the clan's doctor for Abyssal corruption, was overwhelmed on the way to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. She died after thanking Chasca for being her sister, and at that moment Chasca was acknowledged by the Ancient Name Vuka. Chuychu's name is among the dead in the Record Penned by All. Afterwards, Mutota still caught himself calling for her help. In the aftermath, missing warriors were found in the wilds suffering lasting Abyssal terrors, and Iansan and the Traveler helped treat them.

key: Where Feathers Are Intertwined Like Flowers
180.content: The tribe's home sits on Quahuacan Cliff in northern Natlan, looking down on the ruins of Ochkanatlan. It is a settlement of floating platforms, hot-air balloons, Saurian stables and training grounds, with the flight-trial arena down in the valley. Residents include Chief Mutota, Saurian riders, guards, the trial-arena administrator Inkanak, the balloon operators Pixica and Zyanya, and the reputation advisor Abundi. A message board carries the vet Ifa's notes reminding people to bring their Saurians for regular check-ups. From 5.8 a simple harbor below the cliff receives people coming from Nod-Krai.

key: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
181.content:
Fontaine Research Institute (also: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering): The Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, usually just "the Institute", is Fontaine's centre for the study of machines and energy. It was founded by the genius inventor Alain Guillotin, whose clockwork mechanisms and kinetic cores are still built in Fontaine's factories. Unlike Sumeru's Akademiya, it has no governing or teaching role. Its central laboratory was wrecked by an explosion during Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment, and the rebuilt Institute is better known for muddle and money trouble than for brilliance.

Many of Fontaine's mechanical inventions come from the Institute, though some projects have embarrassed it, such as the "Mekafish" water cleaners that began killing fish.

Structure: The Institute is a working organisation of researchers, engineers, technicians, assistants and clerks. Known departments include Advanced Artificed Technology Research and Development and the Department of Statistics and Mathematics; a Natural Ecological Environment Monitoring Department was dissolved after the accident. Notices mention executive, materials, logistics, finance investigation and disciplinary offices. Titles seen include Senior Technician, Senior Researcher, Researcher, Engineer, Research Assistant and Department Director.

Internal notices show a bureaucracy that argues about paper use and bans gambling with paper chips. Researchers compete for backing, and Augustus Lovelace, an Institute researcher met in Sumeru, expects Raimondo to "reorganise", meaning end, his project.

Leadership: Raimondo is the Senior Technician appointed to lead the Institute, and Choiseul is its administrative officer. Both took over the rebuilding after the explosion. Founding Director Alain Guillotin is long dead.

Edwin Eastinghouse, the Senior Technician who led the Arkhium project, was first presumed dead, then dismissed for long unauthorised absence, and finally fired after being found alive. Choiseul says the Institute is better ordered without Edwin's influence. Augustus Lovelace claims that research spirit has been in freefall since Raimondo and Choiseul took over, and says the Institute used to be a paradise for researchers. Rogier Cotes is named as a deceased Third Director.

Members: Named staff include the engineer Anatole, who talks about the Institute to the Traveler in Liyue; Desnos, who handles recruitment at the temporary office; the researchers Xavier and Refait; and Maurice Juglar of Statistics and Mathematics. Delaroche, a former clerk now partly in charge of the Fishing Association, appears to remain formally a member. Former members include Edwin Eastinghouse and Nacker (both fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide), Jurieu (a former assistant of Edwin who helped design the airship The Wingalet), and deceased members such as Bravais, Teilhard, Mosso Lombroso and Pierre Lefevere.

The Traveler is an Honorary Senior Researcher and Paimon is Assistant to the Honorary Senior Researcher, titles given after the Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles (4.1). Salsa, a young Fontainian whose parents are on the staff list, says the Institute has financial problems and is considering "Ruins Tours" for outsiders.

Goals: The Institute researches machines and energy for Fontaine's benefit. Its most ambitious project sought a way to survive the prophesied flood: researchers believed that harnessing Arkhium to defy gravity was the key, and planned to lift Fontaine into a "city in the sky". Since the disaster, leadership aims to stay solvent, restore order and keep the Arkhium ruins from exploding again.

Edwin's own aim remained Arkhium research whatever the cost, and he treats lost researchers as replaceable. Raimondo told him to stay away from research and Arkhium.

Methods: Researchers prototype machines, kinetic cores and automatons and track hazards with Survey Anchors. The Arkhium project used an Experimental Field Generator, a huge device that creates a gravity-reduction field, powered by an Arkhium Kinetic Core with a suppression device. Edwin's Prototype Cal. Breguet clockwork meka belonged to this work. Unlike the Akademiya, the Institute does not administer or educate the people of Fontaine.

Alain's technology underlies the Clockwork Meka. He developed controlled Pneumousia Annihilation reactions, artificial Pneumousia Blocks and the kinetic core, and the Arkhe system that makes meka pneuma- or ousia-aligned. An attack of the opposite alignment disrupts a mek.

History: Alain Guillotin, who had been a member of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, a researcher at the Institute of Natural Philosophy and a Marechaussee Phantom hunter, founded the Institute. His inventions made it famous, and late in life he retired to his workshop, where he created Sandrone and Pulonia.

The Institute's crisis came when Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment in the Central Laboratory overloaded. The explosion levelled most of the old Institute and sent blocks of anti-gravity water and remnants of the old ruins into the sky. The Callas Line aquabus route was shut down, and the Institute rebuilt at a new site near the ruins. Edwin was presumed dead.

**Chronicles (4.1).** Desnos recruits the Traveler at a temporary office to investigate the ruins, which hold out-of-control meka and residual Arkhium. The Traveler learns the details of the first explosion and of the Institute's efforts to downplay the danger. A second accidental explosion follows when Nacker, a researcher who worked with Edwin, tampers with an Arkhium chunk and damages the cooling mechanism, which also reactivates the old field generator. The Traveler and Raimondo shut it down and place inhibitors to stabilise the ruins for the time being. Raimondo and Choiseul reward the Traveler with the honorary title.

Nacker then disappears, and the Traveler helps track him down. He has taken up with Concini, one of the financial backers (with Loillier) who had first funded Edwin, and Edwin turns out to be alive too: he had been inspecting other departments during the explosion and had set up a new laboratory in the Morte Region. Both are brought back to the Institute, dismissed, and handed to the Maison Gardiennage, who take them to the Fortress of Meropide.

Relations: Fontaine regards the Institute with mixed feelings: useful machines, poor accountability. Elphane finds its technicians' long-winded talk "ghastly", and Linorea holds a grudge over the Mekafish. It is separate from Sumeru's Akademiya. The Maison Gardiennage removed Edwin and Nacker to the Fortress of Meropide.

Alain's creation Sandrone later became a Fatui Harbinger, and the Institute's link to the larger story runs through her (see status). Raimondo and Choiseul are on good terms with the Traveler and Paimon.

Reputation: Fontainians see the Institute as a source of both useful machines and disasters. Complaints include long-winded technicians, the Mekafish failure, the explosion and money worries. Engineer Anatole admits the incident "put the Institute on the map".

Secrets: The danger around the ruins was bigger than the public was told: activated Arkhium can resonate and set off chain explosions, and the first explosion left shattered crystals that could be re-activated. Edwin's survival was unknown to the Institute at first; officially he was still an employee until dismissed for absence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Institute works from the New Fontaine Research Institute, still active but troubled. After Sandrone's death in Nod-Krai, her core was delivered to the Institute, and she has since reawakened in Fontaine.

The Institute is rebuilding under Raimondo and Choiseul, with financial problems, and Edwin and Nacker are in the Fortress of Meropide.

Honouring a long-standing request that she called Sandrone's will, Arlecchino delivered Sandrone's and Pulonia's cores to the Institute after Sandrone's death in Nod-Krai (True Moon, 6.3). Sandrone woke on a workbench in a Fontainian-style room with Institute books around her; the manifestation of a Stellar Linchpin let Alain's built-in "Gift", a second chance, trigger, while Pulonia was beyond repair (Should We Meet Again, 6.7). Canon does not say what Institute staff knew of this.

182.content: Alain Guillotin was the Institute's Founding Director, a prodigy raised at the Narzissenkreuz Institute who later researched at the Institute of Natural Philosophy and served in the Marechaussee Phantom with his sister Mary-Ann. He invented the Arkhe system and the Clockwork Meka. Legend says he retired to his workshop and published nothing. He created Sandrone and Pulonia before his death. His own entry holds the detail.

183.comment: Fontaine Research Institute: Edwin Eastinghouse and the Explosion
183.content: Edwin Eastinghouse was a Senior Technician and acknowledged genius who led the Arkhium project, building the Prototype Cal. Breguet meka and the Experimental Field Generator to lift Fontaine above the flood. He is dismissive of colleagues, treats lost researchers as replaceable and blames others for the explosion, saying he was inspecting other departments. After being found alive he was fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide, where he still wants to research Arkhium.

184.content: Arkhium is a yellow, green and blue crystal and a potent energy source. Inert, it is stable; activated, it emits powerful pulses and can trigger chain-explosive resonance in nearby crystals. An inhibitor can make activated Arkhium inert. Exposure makes most people ill, but the Traveler and Paimon resist it. It occurs naturally in parts of Fontaine such as the Geode Mine Shaft beneath the Fortress of Meropide.

185.comment: Fontaine Research Institute: Sandrone at the Institute
185.content: After Sandrone was killed by Dottore in Nod-Krai (True Moon, 6.3), Arlecchino honoured a request Sandrone had made long before, which she called her will, and delivered her core and Pulonia's to the Fontaine Research Institute. Sandrone later reawakened in Fontaine: a Stellar Linchpin manifested and let Alain's built-in "Gift" trigger, after which she repaired her body and imported the numerological array and some of Pulonia's surviving algorithms into herself. Pulonia was beyond repair (Should We Meet Again, 6.7). She then rented The Wingalet during the Fontinalia Film Festival to search for Alain's old home. Earlier, Alain had asked her to take Pulonia to the Institute for maintenance, but she kept it.

186.content:
Forest Rangers (also: the Forest Rangers, Forest Watchers, Vanara): The Forest Rangers are Sumeru's civil servants of the rainforest. They help travelers who are lost or in trouble, patrol the woods, watch the animals, and fight the spread of the Withering. Their main outpost is Gandharva Ville, "The City Above the Forest", in Avidya Forest. Higher-ranking members are called Forest Watchers and wear lighter green clothes. Tighnari is the Chief Officer, and Collei is an official ranger.

The Rangers are a public service, not a military unit. Shirin, their doctor, calls bows a common choice for hunting and for defence against monsters.

Structure: Two grades are seen: ordinary Forest Rangers and the higher-ranking Forest Watchers. Specialist roles include a doctor, a logistics chef and a search-and-rescue dog trainer.

The wiki lists Tighnari (Chief Officer), Amir, Ashpazi, Rana and Shirin as Forest Watchers, and Iraj, Izad, Kamran, Nasrin and Collei as ordinary rangers. Gandharva Ville's NPC list calls Shirin a ranger, so her rank is not fully consistent.

Newcomers train as Trainee Forest Rangers. Collei held that rank when she first appeared, and Amir mentions "a Trainee Forest Ranger" stationed with them. Tighnari occasionally gives training courses to the Rangers, and he jokes that the Akademiya could regard this as illegal "dissemination of information" while daring them to act on it.

Leadership: Tighnari is the Chief Officer of the Forest Rangers. He is an Avidya Forest Watcher and a botanist who graduated from Amurta.

His character stories say that he first arrived at Gandharva Ville as an ordinary member, fresh from Amurta and parted from the Akademiya. After he arrived the Rangers began to rely on him as a knowledgeable and active researcher, and he eventually got everyone to go back to calling him "Forest Watcher", "Master" or "Mr. Tighnari". He is stern and often lectures travelers on survival and the forest, which is why his Wilderness Survival Skills Lecture is well known.

Tighnari raised funds for the Rangers by arranging with city flower sellers to collect their unsold flowers for free, in return for a receipt that buyers could exchange for a dried-flower decoration made by the Rangers. Part of the Mora went to the shop owner as a handling fee and the rest to forest upkeep. His character stories describe this as practical, and Collei in particular quickly agreed with it.

Members: **Tighnari**: Forest Watcher and Chief Officer; mentor of Collei. **Collei**: a trainee when first seen, an official ranger since 6.6. **Rana**: Forest Watcher from Vimara Village. **Amir**: trains the search and rescue dogs. **Ashpazi**: logistics supervisor and "Master Chef". **Shirin**: the Rangers' doctor. **Izad**: liaison to Pardis Dhyai. **Sag**: forest-patrol hound, captain of the dog team.

Iraj, Kamran and Nasrin are rangers posted at Gandharva Ville. Kamran is blunt about Collei's illness. He says that without the forest's alleviating effect on Eleazar, "someone with Eleazar" would never have been allowed to join, and he is surprised to see her cured. Amir hopes that more kind people will join the Rangers. Izad says the Rangers pick suitable planting areas and distribute seeds to villagers nearby so the rainforest can be a little greener.

Goals: Protect the rainforest and the people who pass through it.

Concretely the Rangers help travelers in need, suppress Withering Zones, monitor beast populations and preserve the ecosystem of Sumeru's rainforests. They also send regular reports on the state of Avidya Forest to the researchers at Pardis Dhyai, who supply ecological help such as seeds and nutrients in return. Tighnari lists his troubles as pollution in the forest, adventurers who cause problems and rescue dogs that play with his tail, and says he has no larger worries.

Methods: Rangers patrol on foot, record anomalies in patrol logs, give travelers practical advice, and use trained dogs to search for missing people. Rana tells the Traveler during Into the Woods that when a missing person is found they should be given something easy to digest. They keep the outpost supplied: Ashpazi hunts and cooks as part of his logistics duties, and the Rangers' food at the outpost is a subject Tighnari takes an interest in (he asked for a recipe to put on the Rangers' menu).

When the Withering struck, rangers faced it directly. In the Aranyaka World Quest series (3.0), Rana protects a trapped child, Iotham, in a Withering Zone and falls severely ill from the exposure. The Aranara guard her until the Traveler obtains Bija to purge the corruption. When she recovers, a Dendro Vision appears at her waist, and she leaves to travel with the Aranara Arana. Furnishing descriptions add that a ranger's provisions backpack holds tools, rations, specimen containers and a tent, but is so heavy that rangers seldom carry it, and that their break rooms are designed for quick departures and sample analysis.

History: Little is known about the Rangers' origins. According to Rana in Into the Woods, the earliest rangers were the royal guards of Viaghara, the forest king, and walked forests where there were real tigers. Separate lore about Viaghara describes his squire Cinnamon, who taught other forest children to follow the rules of nature and began a line of forest guardians, but the wiki does not say that this is the same organisation.

Relations: The Rangers work with Pardis Dhyai's Amurta researchers on conservation. Tighnari's Amurta training links the Rangers to the Akademiya's scholars. They also treat the Aranara kindly: Rana befriended Arana as a child, and the quest series reveals their friendship. The Eremites around Gandharva Ville include a few mercenaries, and a group of Eremites under Tashfin attacked the Traveler there in 3.1, but they were mercenaries hired by an anonymous client, whom Paimon connects with the Doctor, and not part of the Rangers. Kamran says the Bimarstan advises Collei to rest despite her work.

Gandharva Ville also hosts traveling merchants, researchers and adventurers who stop at the Rangers' outpost, along with a few Eremite mercenaries.

Reputation: Travelers are told to flag down a Forest Ranger if anything happens. The Rangers are known for patient, practical help, and for Tighnari's lectures. Merchants bow to the diminutive Forest Watcher Tighnari, which amuses the rangers, according to his character stories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Forest Rangers still patrol Avidya Forest from Gandharva Ville. Collei is an official ranger, and Tighnari remains their Chief Officer.

In the 6.6 Archon Quest Your Past Is Like a Garden, Naphis tells Collei she has finally become a full-fledged ranger, and Cyrus congratulates her on no longer being a trainee. Collei wrote to Sucrose that she is now an official Forest Ranger. Cyno introduced her to the party as the "official" ranger.

187.content: Tighnari is the Chief Officer of the Forest Rangers and a Forest Watcher at Gandharva Ville. His own entry carries his biography. In the context of the Rangers: he arrived as an Amurta graduate who had left the Akademiya, became the one the others looked to, runs training courses and raised funds through a dried-flower scheme with city flower sellers.

188.comment: Forest Rangers: Collei and the Rangers
188.content: Collei was a Trainee Forest Ranger when she first appeared, and said that her years in the wilderness made the work a natural fit for her. In the 6.6 Archon Quest Your Past Is Like a Garden she is promoted to an official ranger, with Naphis and Cyrus congratulating her. Kamran remarks that she was allowed to join only because the forest eased her Eleazar.

189.content: Gandharva Ville is the Rangers' main outpost in Avidya Forest, called "The City Above the Forest". Travelers, merchants and adventurers often stop there. Rangers, a few Vanara, researchers, Eremite mercenaries and traveling merchants share the village. Official map text says the remnants of the "kingdom of lost dreams" lie atop the tree. The location's own entry carries geography.

190.content: Rana is a Forest Watcher from Vimara Village. In the Aranyaka World Quest series she guides the Traveler and Paimon through the forest, nearly dies of exposure while saving a child from a Withering Zone, and is healed with Bija. As a child she was befriended by the Aranara Arana, whom she had forgotten. At the end a Dendro Vision appears at her waist and she leaves with Arana. She is the first NPC to display a Vision on her character model.

191.comment: Forest Rangers: Amir and the search dogs
191.content: Amir is the Forest Watcher who trains the Rangers' search and rescue dogs. Sag, a forest-patrol hound he considers his best student, is captain of the dog team. Travelers who cannot find a ranger can ask Sag for help.

192.content: Suppressing Withering Zones is one of the Rangers' core duties. They log pollution in the forest, and Rana mentions them in connection with monsters and unusually aggressive wildlife. Exposure to the Withering can make a person severely ill, as happened to Rana. Cure and cause belong to the lore of the Withering, not to this entry.

193.content: Pardis Dhyai is the Amurta research station near Avidya Forest. The Rangers send it regular reports on the forest, and its researchers send seeds, nutrients and other ecological help. Izad is the Ranger who handles this liaison, and he says the Rangers choose planting areas and distribute seeds to nearby villagers.

194.content:
Four Winds (also: the Four Winds, Four Wind Guardians, Wolf of the North, Lion of the South, Dragon of the East, Falcon of the West, Lionfang Knight, Dandelion Knight): The Four Winds are four guardians of Mondstadt: the Wolf of the North, the Lion of the South, the Dragon of the East and the Falcon of the West. The Anemo Archon Barbatos entrusted them with the city's safety before he vanished a thousand years ago. Mondstadt once worshipped them and built temples to them. Today the worship has faded, and the titles live on mainly through the Knights of Favonius, the wolf spirit Boreas and the dragon Dvalin.

They are a tradition rather than an organisation. There is no headquarters or roster, and who bears each title is a matter of old ballads, weapon lore and a few quest lines that do not always agree.

Structure: Each wind holds one compass direction and a symbol on a side of Mondstadt City. Per the wiki's trivia: the Lion above the main gate (south), the Wolf on the stairs up to the cathedral (north), the Dragon over the side entrance (east) and the Falcon on both sides of the Knights' headquarters entrance (west). The order's name, Favonius, is the Roman name for the west wind. Each wind had a temple, though only the Wolf, Lion and Falcon temples exist as ruins the Traveler can visit.

Three of the four are tied to ranks or beings, not to a single bloodline. The Wolf is Boreas the wolf king and, by some accounts, the Knight of Boreas whom he recognises. The Lion is passed down through the Grand Masters of the Knights as the Dandelion (Lionfang) Knight. The Dragon is Dvalin. The Falcon is the vaguest and is most often read as Vennessa.

Members: - **Wolf of the North:** Boreas (Andrius), the great wolf king whose spirit dwells in Wolvendom, and the human Knight of Boreas he recognises. Known Knights of Boreas are a nameless wandering knight, Ravenwood, Rostam and now Varka, the Grand Master. Roland was named a candidate but never granted the title.
- **Lion of the South:** the Dandelion (Lionfang) Knight. Past holders include Vennessa, Arundolyn and Valentine; Jean holds it as of 7.1.
- **Dragon of the East:** Dvalin, the Wind Dragon, called Stormterror when Mondstadt feared him.
- **Falcon of the West:** most commonly Vennessa, said to have taken the title after her ascension, or symbolically the whole Knights of Favonius. This is disputed.

The lists of current and former holders come from a HoYoLAB anecdote about Varka that the wiki cites, not from in-game text. Treat names beyond the in-game weapon and book lore as sourced to that anecdote.

Goals: Barbatos charged the Winds with guarding Mondstadt and its people. In the ballads, the Wind Dragon is the one shown acting on that charge, fighting the corrupted dragon Durin at the height of the cataclysm as the city's last defender.

History: The wiki dates the formal establishment of the Four Winds to after Vennessa's rebellion against the aristocracy about 1,000 years ago, when Barbatos entrusted Mondstadt's safety to them before he disappeared. The Dragon Tome adds that Dvalin predated the others: the ballads say Barbatos befriended him and taught him to speak, so he is regarded as one of the oldest guardians and the longest worshipped. For roughly five hundred years people worshipped the Winds and built temples to them.

During the cataclysm five hundred years ago, Dvalin was badly wounded fighting Durin and slept for centuries. Afterward worship declined, the temples were abandoned and most people forgot the Winds. When Dvalin woke he believed Mondstadt had abandoned him, turned on the city and was called Stormterror, until the Traveler, Venti and their allies freed him from the Abyss Order's manipulation during the Prologue.

The Dragon Tome records a belief that Dvalin would wake whenever Mondstadt faced a new threat. By its account, the people's prayers woke Barbatos, who called Dvalin to defend the city. The book's one-hundred-year figure is a beta leftover; canon places the cataclysm five hundred years ago.

In the Prologue, the Traveler visits the temples of the Falcon, Wolf and Lion in the quests Winds of the Past, Crash Course and Sparks Amongst the Pages, where they appear as ruins.
