In Fallen Tears, Diluc says the Fatui have been hunting traces of Barbatos' power, and a vial of the Anemo God's breath was stolen from an East Temple of the Four Winds. That detail implies a Temple of the Dragon existed about six months before the game began.

Relations: Barbatos is the one who set them in place, and Venti, who is Barbatos, still treats the Winds as his own. Dvalin is the Wind with the best-attested personal friendship with him. The Knights of Favonius inherited the Lion and Wolf titles through their Grand Master and the Knight of Boreas, so the order is the Winds' most active human heir. Dahlia, Barbatos' herald, serves the same god.

The Winds are bound to the Knights through objects as well as titles. Favonius Sword and Favonius Greatsword lore ties the Lion and Wolf tradition to Rostam and Arundolyn, and Wolf's Gravestone and Wolf-Fang preserve the story of the first Knight of Boreas and his wolf. Aquila Favonia lore carries the belief that Vennessa became the Falcon.

Reputation: Mondstadt remembers the Winds only dimly. Most people treat them as folklore. Dandelion seeds on the wind are said in the Temple of the Lion's text to be the Lion's blessing. After the Stormterror crisis the people of Mondstadt resumed their belief in Dvalin, and the Winds' symbols still mark the city. The ballad collections that tell their stories were compiled by scholars from bard songs, and the book itself warns that bards embellish history.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Four Winds are a fading tradition. Dvalin is again regarded as a guardian of Mondstadt; Boreas's spirit is in Wolvendom; Jean is Acting Grand Master and holds the Lion title; Varka is Grand Master and the Knight of Boreas. The Falcon is disputed.

No change to the Winds as a concept was found in the 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0 to 7.1 Snezhnaya material checked. The wiki's holder list rests on a HoYoLAB anecdote about Varka.

195.comment: Four Winds: Wolf of the North
195.content:
The Wolf of the North is both Boreas, the wolf king also called Andrius who now rests as a spirit in Wolvendom, and the Knight of Boreas, a human recognised by him. The Temple of the Wolf near the Thousand Winds Temple in Starfell Valley was originally a training ground and is now a monster-infested ruin. Known Knights of Boreas: the nameless wandering knight (original wielder of Wolf's Gravestone), Ravenwood, Rostam and Varka. Roland was a candidate who never received the title.

Accounts differ on how the Wolf title relates to the Knights' Wolf and Lion tradition. Favonius Sword lore says leaders get one of the two, but whether the Wolf of the Winds is always the Knight of Boreas is unclear. At some point Boreas and his wolves moved west and settled in Wolvendom.

196.comment: Four Winds: Lion of the South
196.content: The Lion is handed down among the Grand Masters and Acting Grand Masters of the Knights of Favonius as the Dandelion or Lionfang Knight. The Temple of the Lion lies in Falcon Coast in Galesong Hill; dandelions riding the wind are said to be the Lion's blessing. Vennessa, Arundolyn, Valentine and now Jean are listed holders. The Lion symbol is above Mondstadt City's main gate.

key: East Temple of the Four Winds
197.comment: Four Winds: Dragon of the East
197.content: Dvalin is one of Barbatos' oldest friends among the Winds and has been worshipped the longest. Ballads say Barbatos won the people's trust for him and taught him human speech. Wounded by Durin in the cataclysm, he slept for centuries, woke to a city that feared him and was called Stormterror, and in A Long Shot said he was no longer part of the Four Winds. After the Prologue Mondstadt resumed believing in him. His temple does not exist as a visitable site.

198.comment: Four Winds: Falcon of the West
198.content: The most uncertain of the Winds. Common belief says Vennessa became the Falcon on ascending to Celestia, and the wiki reads Dainsleif's cryptic line the same way. Breeze Amidst the Forest suggests instead that the whole Knights of Favonius is the Falcon, which the book calls debatable. The Temple of the Falcon is at Windrise in Galesong Hill, between Mondstadt City and the oak where Vennessa is said to have ascended. The Falcon symbol flanks the entrance to the Knights' headquarters. The English name uses falcon, but the emblem looks like an eagle, which may be a translation quirk.

199.comment: Four Winds: Breeze Amidst the Forest
199.content: A two-volume ballad collection assembled by scholars from bard songs, with a supplement, The Dragon Tome, quoting a cultural survey by Jacob Musk. It is the main in-world source for the Four Winds as a tradition and for Dvalin's friendship with Barbatos. The collection itself warns that bards embellish history, so its details are of low reliability.

200.content:
Frostmoon Scions (also: Moonchildren, Frostmoon Scion, Scions of the Frost Moon): The Frostmoon Scions, also called the Moonchildren, are an indigenous people of Nod-Krai descended from the fallen golden realm of Hyperborea. Their home is the Frostmoon Enclave on Hiisi Island. For centuries they have worshipped the Goddess of the Frost Moon, and in particular the Moon Maiden Kuutar, who was later revealed to be the former Fatui Harbinger Columbina. They are led by the Moonchanter Lauma. They are known for antlered crowns, silver blood, a gift for speaking with animals, vegetarian food, charity and deep suspicion of outsiders who threaten them.

To most of modern Nod-Krai they seem ancient and set in their ways. They believe the wintry woods shelter them and that the full moon's light can cure every ill, and for generations they prayed to a goddess who never answered.

Leadership: Lauma, the Moonchanter, is the spiritual leader, healer and voice of the Scions. She was chosen for the role at birth because she was born with an antler crown, silver blood and an extraordinary sensitivity to moonlight. Her people bring her every question, and senior members salute her as she passes.

The title of Moonchanter dates from about 500 years ago, when Aila became the first to hold it. Before that the Scions were led by Archpriests or Archpriestesses who ran Hyperborea's ancient rites. Lovia was the last of them, and her name has been struck from the record.

Lauma was born to an ordinary Scion couple, and the faithful hailed her as proof that the Moon Goddess had not abandoned them. She kept two truths from her people to protect them: that the moon in Teyvat's sky is false, and that their goddess Kuutar had become the Harbinger Columbina and was hiding on their island. In 6.0 she decided this had been a mistake and told them. Among the elders is the priestess Sarakka, whom Lauma calls Grandma Sarakka. It was Sarakka who said Lauma's Moon Wheel fell out of her swaddling clothes.

Structure: The Moonchanter leads. Below her, in descending order, are:
- **Priestesses**, who carry more responsibilities.
- **Acolytes**, who must first pass an exam on hymns and blessings.
- **Adherents**, the ordinary followers.

Men of the tribe cannot become acolytes or priestesses. One Scion grumbled about this while hauling heavy festival decorations.

Some knowledge is restricted by rank. Only those of priestess rank or higher are supposed to know Lovia's name. The Enclave holds a library, where hymns are copied and records kept; Lauma once searched its entire records for the origin of her Moon Wheel without finding an answer.

Members: The Scions named in the 6.x story include Lauma (Moonchanter), the priestesses Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar, the acolytes Verna, Zirnytsia and Eveliina, adherents such as Reetta, Lyylikki and Krodo, and other members such as Kapy. Kapy's daughter Kaarina suffers from a sensitivity to kuuvahki that flares up as illness; Lauma treats it with her own silver blood and urges Kapy to accept help from Nasha Town's doctors. Former members include Vilemina, Lauma's childhood friend, who defected to the Fatui in 6.0, and Columbina herself.

Goals: For generations the Scions' goal was faith itself: to honour the Moon Goddess, keep the old blessings alive and wait for a prophecy that the goddess would return. Under Lauma, especially since 6.0, the aim has shifted. In her words they are learning to thrive on their own, without relying on the Moon Goddess, and to make their home a better place to live. Lauma still defends their people: when the Fatui delivered their ultimatum she answered that the Scions would never hand anything over, and that with intruders' blood they would "draw an inviolable line in the snow".

Methods: Aila's reform turned the Scions toward benevolence and faith, and they avoid conflict with outsiders where they can. They hand out food in Nasha Town, even to Fatui soldiers who sneer at them. Lauma warned such soldiers that kindness is "the first lantern" left for those who stumble in ignorance, but those who still refuse the moonlit path will be shown its shadow by frosted blades. They eat no meat and live on spring water, fruit and vegetables.

- **Prayer and hymns.** Prayers, blessings and Runo hymns, some of them preserved in the book "Hymns of the Far North", are the centre of daily life.
- **Kuuvahki.** Kuuvahki is the moonlight's blessing. Using it for personal gain, including in kuuvahki devices, has traditionally been considered blasphemy.
- **The Moon Marrow.** The Scions guarded a Moon Marrow in a sealed chamber below the statue of Kuutar on Hiisi Island. Moonchanters use it to see the "true" past, and normally it could only be taken out when the moon is closest to Teyvat.
- **Animals.** Through Lauma, ibises, moles and finches carry messages and act as lookouts.
- **Life and death.** Scion teaching holds that death is not the end. Life is in constant flux, the dead return to nature, and loved ones will meet again.
- **Ceremonies.** They have their own rites, such as a formal engagement ceremony with a master of ceremonies, a member of the bride's family and an ecclesiast.

History: **Hyperborea.** The Scions' ancestors lived in Hyperborea. The apostle Anacharsis taught them to build Mekhaneikos constructs and to predict and use the lunar tides for magic, founded on the Runo hymns. Their old rites honoured the Frost Moon and many other powers. When the Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, the Frost Moon goddess Canon, whom they call Huurrekuutar, guided the survivors to Hiisi Island and then died. The exiles kept practising their rites even though no one answered their prayers. A prophecy grew up that the Moon Goddess would return through a Sacred Heir born among them.

**Lovia and Aila (about 500 years ago).** Kuuvahki was fading, and Archpriestess Lovia grew desperate for the Sacred Heir. She conspired with Rotwang and had people killed. Aila turned against her, killed her, and became the first Moonchanter. Aila abolished the Archpriestess office and the Hyperborean rites, rewrote many hymns, and refocused the faith on the moonlight. Together with Solovei she fought an Abyssal calamity at the Pillar of Embla, and she gave him the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, which became the basis of the Lightkeepers.

**Kuutar.** Aila foresaw and witnessed the birth of a new moon goddess in the Sanctum of the Oathbearer 400-500 years ago, and offered her the first drop of silver blood with the sword Moonweaver's Dawn. The Scions worshipped her as the Moon Maiden Kuutar, successor of the Frost Moon, and carved Statues of the New Moon in her likeness across Nod-Krai. They cared more about having their prayers granted than about her as a person. About 350-400 years ago she left them and joined the Fatui as the Harbinger Columbina.

Relations: - **Columbina (Kuutar)**: the goddess they once burdened with demands. After True Moon she accepted Lauma's suggestion to live among the Scions. She gave Lauma the Eternal Moon Marrow.
- **Fatui**: bitter enemies through 6.0-6.3. They defaced the Scions' statues, threatened to cleanse Hiisi Island, recruited Vilemina and hunted Columbina. Lauma still reminds her people that not every Snezhnayan is a Fatuus.
- **Lightkeepers**: allies through history. Aila helped Solovei found them and gave them the Arrow of Terpikeraunas.
- **Curatorium of Secrets**: Lauma and Nefer trade favours, medicine and Hyperborean records.
- **Nasha Town**: the Scions hand out food there. Some, like Kapy, distrust its Snezhnayan doctors.
- **League**: in 6.3 the Scions joined Nod-Krai's new League, alongside the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium, the Lightkeepers and others.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Scions still live in the Frostmoon Enclave under Lauma. Columbina lives among them as herself, not as a goddess to be petitioned. Older Scions still bow and keep their distance from her, but the children are curious.

After the 6.0 revelation some members left. Those who stayed have joined the League and are trying to stand on their own. Lauma holds the Eternal Moon Marrow. In a 6.3 world quest the Scions refurbished a statue of Columbina, adding wings, and Lauma invited her to a feast. No new Frostmoon Scions story was found in the 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quests. In 7.0 Columbina appears only to see the Traveler off from Nod-Krai.

201.comment: Frostmoon Scions: Sacred bloodline and antler crowns
201.content: The Scions treat their Hyperborean bloodline as sacred. Its marks are silver blood, sensitivity to kuuvahki, antler crowns (said to be the Frost Moon's last gift to the Hyperboreans) and an ability to communicate with all living things. Antlers grow under moonlight. Lauma's sensitivity is said to occur only once a century, and her silver blood can be mixed into medicine. The Sacred Heir Project was an old plan to keep the bloodline pure so that a prophesied heir would revive Hyperborea. After the fall, the Hyperborean genetic methods were lost, so it relied on controlled family lines. It was meant to be wound down by the seventh generation to avoid inbreeding, but later priestesses only intensified it.

202.comment: Frostmoon Scions: Lovia, the last Archpriestess
202.content: About 500 years ago, Archpriestess Lovia was desperate for the Sacred Heir as kuuvahki faded. A maiden of exceptionally pure blood, who had been chosen to bear the heir, eloped with a Snezhnayan officer and gave birth to Avrelian. Lovia asked Rotwang to bring her back. The officer was killed, and the woman took her own life. Lovia then raised the twins Alia and Aila in isolation. To raise their purity, she had them kill other Scions and drink their blood. She also sought the Sampo Mill through Rotwang, and urged Aila to kill Solovei. Instead Aila killed Lovia, reportedly discovering that Lovia herself had no silver blood. Lovia was then struck from the record.

203.comment: Frostmoon Scions: Aila, the first Moonchanter
203.content: Aila became the first Moonchanter after killing Lovia. She abolished the Hyperborean rites and the Archpriestess office, rewrote hymns, and turned the faith toward the moonlight and toward kindness. With Solovei she ended an Abyssal calamity at the Pillar of Embla, and the two of them later sealed away the returned Rotwang. She gave the Lightkeepers the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. She witnessed Kuutar's birth, offered her the first drop of silver blood with Moonweaver's Dawn, and carved the Idol of the New Moon. She sealed the Court of the First Edict, with evidence of Lovia's crimes inside, for the Traveler to open 500 years later. When Solovei died, she declined to see the Reed Miller Brahe, who came to tell her the news.

204.comment: Frostmoon Scions: Kuutar, the Moon Maiden
204.content: Kuutar is the Scions' name for the moon goddess born on Hiisi Island 400-500 years ago, whom they hailed as the successor of the Frost Moon. They carved Statues of the New Moon in her likeness across Nod-Krai. Their constant, demanding prayers drove her away. She joined the Fatui as Columbina, the Damselette, and centuries later returned to hide on Hiisi Island. She has said that while she lived among the Scions, people went solemn and stiff whenever she appeared. Since 6.3 she has lived among them by choice. On one visit to the Enclave with the Traveler, she noticed that the Scions' greeting had changed to "May the moonlight connect us" and was glad that they had changed.

205.content: Vilemina grew up with Lauma and came to resent what she saw as empty, inherited prayers. She joined the Fatui, followed the Traveler into the sealed chamber and stole the Moon Marrow for Marionette (Sandrone). When Lauma confronted her and admitted that the sky's moon was false, Vilemina asked what happens to those who betray the Scions. Lauma recited the punishment: their antlers are cut off with silver blades and they are cast into "the long night of unknowing". Vilemina cut off her own horns as a last act of respect, then told them where the Marrow had gone.

206.content: Moonchanter is the title of the Frostmoon Scions' leader, created by Aila about 500 years ago to replace the Archpriest office. It is held now by Lauma, who was chosen at birth. The Moonchanter leads prayer and the community, heals, keeps the Moon Marrow and reads the true past with it. When the bloodline was stronger, one Moonchanter even sheltered the Moon Marrow inside her own body, though she could endure it for only two days. Lauma believed she could last five at most.

207.content:
Fruity Order (also: the Fruity Order, Order of the Fruit, Five Great Operatives): The Fruity Order is a Treasure Hoarder group that operates in Fontaine and Nod-Krai. It is run by an unnamed boss, with Five Great Operatives who carry fruit and plant codenames, and several dozen other members. Betrayal is punishable by death. Its members claim the order exists to keep order and balance in the world. They are more eccentric than most Treasure Hoarders.

Only three of the Five Great Operatives remain: "Guileless Wolfhook", "Ruthless Calla Lily" and "Trendy Zaytun Peach". "Tricky Bulle Fruit" and "Intrepid Valberry" have left.

Structure: At the top is the boss, unnamed. Beneath the boss are the Five Great Operatives: Zaytun Peach, Bulle Fruit, Wolfhook, Valberry and Calla Lily, each with a title (Trendy, Tricky, Guileless, Intrepid, Ruthless). Below them are several dozen ordinary members. The order belongs to the wider Treasure Hoarders.

The same five codenames appear in the Godfather's original order, in the Nod-Krai lore, but canon does not say if the modern order is that group's descendant.

Members: - **"Guileless Wolfhook"**, **"Ruthless Calla Lily"** and **"Trendy Zaytun Peach"**: the remaining operatives. Peach loves trendy slang, mocks outdated ideas ("Ley Lines are outdated") and hands out new names to people, such as calling Paimon the "Trendy Flyer". Wolfhook is polite and friendly while accepting majority votes against his own side, saying "This is how the world works". Calla Lily fights the Traveler in Villains and is the one who speaks for the order in the 6.5 event.
- **"Tricky Bulle Fruit"**: left the order after the Villains quest. He keeps a younger sister, Blanche, and is later found in the Fortress of Meropide.
- **"Intrepid Valberry"**: expelled or left earlier, then joined a different group.
- **Lakkaberry**: a fan who is not a member (see below).

Lakkaberry applied for a booth at the Nod-Krai Trade Expo under the Fruity Order's name, learned of it through the "New Tide Anthology" and tales of Valberry heard in the Fortress of Meropide, and has no real standing in the order.

Goals: The order says it exists to keep order and balance. In practice the quests show the members pursuing valuable potion formulas and pursuing those they see as traitors.

Methods: Theft, threats and intimidation. Members use slang and rank titles, settled one dispute in Villains by a vote, and treat betrayal as a capital offence. They hunted Bulle Fruit as a traitor over a potion formula, as seen in Villains. They have won the Treasure Hoarder booth at the Nod-Krai Trade Expo several years running, and in the latest expo they removed rival groups before they could cause trouble for a lookalike.

A weapon-lore story claims the original order's creed is that theft alone can balance an unjust world, and that its leader recruited three rival thieves into it by having them swallow fruits.

History: In Villains (4.1) the Traveler and Paimon meet Blanche, who is being threatened by Zaytun Peach and Wolfhook over her brother, Bulle Fruit, whom they call a traitor for keeping the "Pure Water" potion formula to himself. The Traveler helps Blanche and Bulle Fruit, and repels Calla Lily, who has come for him. By the end Bulle Fruit has left the order and later appears in the Fortress of Meropide. The Red and the Black (4.2) then shows Valberry's diary, which says he left the order and joined another group, the Elegant Tableware Confrerie, whose boss later fired him. In the follow-up Questions and Answers, Valberry is an NPC. In the Nod-Krai content, the Problem-Sorting Robot quest has the order steal "Curve"'s core from the Fatui and hide it in an Aino prospector robot, leading to Curve's rebuilding as Chard Lombro. The wiki infers that Wolfhook, Calla Lily and Zaytun Peach did this.

Relations: - **Treasure Hoarders**: it belongs to this wider group of thieves, but behaves as a distinct organisation with its own codenames and rules.
- **Fatui**: the order took Curve's core from them, according to the wiki's reading of the Problem-Sorting Robot quest.
- **Voynich Guild and the Nod-Krai Trade Expo**: the Guild's rules forbid trouble at the expo, and Calla Lily says so in her dealings with the organisers.
- **Traveler**: met Wolfhook, Zaytun Peach, Bulle Fruit and Calla Lily in Villains.

Reputation: Calla Lily says the order has proven untouchable so far, and a fan such as Lakkaberry wants to join it. The Curatorium of Secrets suspects the group may be outsiders to the area.

Secrets: The identity of the boss is not known. Calla Lily's pursuit of Bulle Fruit is explained by Valberry's diary as an order from "higher-ups".

Status as of 7.1: Active but diminished: three of five operatives remain, and the boss is unnamed.

As of the 6.5 event Calla Lily was still acting on the order's behalf in Nod-Krai. No Fruity Order content was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

208.content: The Five Great Operatives of the Fruity Order are known by a title and a fruit or plant name. Guileless Wolfhook is the soft-spoken one who supports majority votes. Ruthless Calla Lily fights in Villains and later speaks for the order at the expo. Trendy Zaytun Peach is the slang-loving one. Tricky Bulle Fruit held the "Pure Water" formula, left the order and is later found in Meropide. Intrepid Valberry was removed from the order and later worked for a different group.

209.comment: Fruity Order: Godfather of Nod-Krai and the original order
209.content: Weapon lore for the Blackmarrow Lantern and the Prospector's Shovel describes Soini, a poor farmer after the cataclysm who found buried treasure and became the feared Godfather of Nod-Krai's black market. Three rival thieves, a fae, a young woman and a hunter, failed to beat his vault. He had each swallow a fruit (Bulle Fruit, Wolfhook and Valberry) to join his creed that theft alone could rebalance a corrupt world. His butler then turned on him, seized the master thief's relic, left the Calla Lily fruit behind as an antidote and spared his life because he had spread the thieves' ideals. The wiki also lists Nashchokin, Schanzkowska and Dmitri Dubrovich Sukhotin as the first holders of the Bulle Fruit, Wolfhook and Valberry codenames.

210.content: Lakkaberry is an enthusiast in the 6.5 event Where Waves Meet the Reef who admires the Fruity Order and applied for an expo booth in its name. He is not a member. The order's real operative Calla Lily appears, tells him to meet her at the Nasha Town harbour after the expo. She says the order itself dealt with the rival Treasure Hoarders angered by his stunt.

211.content:
Garde (also: Gardes, Fontaine Gardes, Garde officers, Captain of the Gardes): The Gardes are the uniformed security officers of Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage, the nation's law enforcement service. They patrol the Court of Fontaine, handle everyday public order, and share the patrol work with Gardemek meka. Their captain is Grosrochard. They are the standard-issue face of the law, as opposed to the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol or the Marechaussee Phantom.

Gardes are ordinary civil servants. The open world shows them chatting in cafes, grumbling about assignments and retiring to a quiet life. In other Fontaine entries they are mostly background: someone who arrests, escorts or guards on behalf of the Maison Gardiennage.

Structure: The Gardes are one department of the Maison Gardiennage, listed with the Gardemeks, the Guard Poodle, the Marechaussee Phantom and the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. A Captain heads them, currently Grosrochard. The Gardes and their Gardemeks make up the service's main force. The Special Patrol and the Marechaussee Phantom are its two special branches. The Special Patrol, led by Chevreuse, handles violent criminals whom ordinary Gardes would struggle with. The Phantom does investigation and answers directly to the Chief Justice.

The Maison, and with it the Gardes, is based in the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine. Officers can move between departments: Thurel began as a Garde, joined the Special Patrol because of skill with a gun, switched departments several times, and was briefly posted as a guard at the Fortress of Meropide. Riqueti, also a former Special Patrol member, is now with Maison Gestion, a separate service.

Leadership: Grosrochard is the Captain of the Gardes. He is only ever mentioned: in Chevreuse's introduction he is the superior who wrote to her for the ninth time, asking her to be pickier about who joins the Special Patrol.

After the Traveler's part in the Roses and Muskets event, Grosrochard and Chevreuse both took to calling the Traveler "Proto-Boss". Turenna presents their joint assessment as the highest acknowledgment of both the Special Patrol and the Gardes. Garde Edler repeats the nickname and can quote his advice from memory.

Edler quotes Grosrochard's advice about blending in with criminals by learning to "swear like a sailor", and says she has never heard him swear. She also quotes him comparing good fighters to wolves, whose teeth are sharp but who also know exactly where to bite. These are the only glimpses of his manner: a mentor figure who is respected and never seen.

Members: Named Gardes are few and come mostly from open-world conversations.
- Santallier: a patrolling Garde at the Quartier Lyonnais, who says he asked his superiors not to patrol that block, since the safest area in town sits across from the Champion Duelists' office, and was told that only he could take the task.
- Nolette: a retired Garde near the Vasari Passage, still proud of being a former officer of the Palais Mermonia, and regretful about failing to catch a pickpocket.
- Thurel: a retired Garde near the Fountain of Lucine, who later served in the Special Patrol and briefly at the Fortress of Meropide, and says their memory is fading.

- Edler: an energetic Garde who appears in limited-time events. She told Wislawa she was a "kind-hearted merchant", has tinkered with the Maison's standard-issue wargame, and once mistook Wislawa for a kidnapper in Fontaine before meeting her again in Nod-Krai.
- Vaughn: a Garde who was secretly an accomplice of Marcel in the Archon Quest. He is the only known corrupt Garde.

Goals: Keep Fontaine's streets safe: patrol the Court of Fontaine, respond when citizens call for help, guard places and prisoners on behalf of the Maison Gardiennage, and hand serious investigation to the Phantom and violent cases to the Special Patrol. Gardemeks share this work, and Fontainians treat them as reliable helpers.

Methods: Gardes patrol on foot and with Gardemeks, which are pre-programmed to complete the tasks assigned to them. A Garde works with them rather than controlling them. Each Gardemek has a serial number for accountability, and a shout for help is said to bring a nearby Gardemek at once. The Maison keeps records of civil cases and transports and punishes hostages, and Gardes carry out such duties. For training it uses a standard-issue wargame.

The Special Patrol distrusts the mechanised approach. Chevreuse's Character Story 2 says Gardemeks' rigid movements and large size block musket shots, and criminals could turn them against their allies, which is why the Patrol is the least mechanised section. The Maison also passes its information on dangerous monsters, meka and bandits to the Steambird's Editor-in-Chief, who publishes it with bounties.

History: The founder and founding date of the Maison Gardiennage, and so of the Gardes, are unknown. The Gardes appear in the archive from Version 4.0. In the Archon Quest "Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights", during Lyney's trial, the Garde Vaughn claimed that the Gardes had found Primordial Sea water in Lyney's belongings, to protect his superior's identity. When Neuvillette saw through the deception, he ordered Vaughn to confess and seek the Gardes' protection, but Vaughn dissolved into water before he could name his boss.

Relations: The Gardes belong to the Maison Gardiennage. The Special Patrol and the Marechaussee Phantom sit alongside them in the same service. The Steambird newspaper uses the Maison's intelligence for its bounties.

Reputation: Fontaine's citizens regard the public security as "top-notch", as an Aquabus passenger puts it, and treat Gardemeks as dependable helpers. Individual Gardes are shown as dutiful but human: tired, nostalgic or complaining about assignments.

Secrets: Vaughn, a Garde, secretly served Marcel's organisation and planted Primordial Sea water as false evidence against Lyney. That is the only established case of infiltration of the Gardes.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. The Gardes keep Fontaine's public order under Captain Grosrochard.

Nothing in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 stories changes the Gardes' standing. Their latest appearances are limited-time events.

212.content: Edler is a Maison Gardiennage agent who appears only in limited-time events, among them Tracing Vanishing Trails (5.8) and the Moonlit Patrol Exercise (6.3), where she is in Nod-Krai with an improved version of the Maison's standard-issue wargame. She respects Captain Grosrochard, calls the Traveler "Proto-Boss", and once mistook Wislawa for a kidnapper in Fontaine, afterwards telling her she was a kind-hearted merchant.

213.content: Grosrochard is the Captain of the Gardes. Canon mentions him in Chevreuse's introduction, where he wrote to her for the ninth time to ask her to be more selective with Special Patrol recruits. He appears nowhere in person.

214.content: Vaughn was a Garde and secret accomplice of Marcel. During Lyney's trial he claimed the Gardes had found Primordial Sea water among Lyney's belongings, having planted it himself. After Neuvillette exposed him, he began to confess but was dissolved into water before naming his employer.

215.content:
Golden Troupe (also: Golden Troupe of Remuria, the Golden Troupe): The Golden Troupe was an order founded by Boethius, a Harmost of Remuria, from the survivors of the empire after its first fall. Its aim was to save Remuria and the Symphony (Phobos) so that music could unite the world in peace. It gathered in the Faded Castle, built music devices, studied spirit and fate, and used golems and sacrifice. It is long gone, but its remains lie under Petrichor in Fontaine.

Because its work is known only from ruins, items and later scholars' notes, the troupe is a historical faction: it is met through relics, not living members.

Leadership: Boethius, once one of Fontaine's greatest musicians and a Harmost of the God King Remus, gathered the remnants of Remuria into the troupe. The sources name no other officers.

Boethius had been devoted to Remus's vision to the point of fanaticism. His devotion continued after Remus himself changed his mind, and the wiki states that he was ultimately corrupted by the Symphony. His own entry carries his life story.

Goals: The troupe wanted to save Phobos, the Symphony of Remuria, so that its power could unite the whole world and bring peace through music and the "Grand Symphony". Item text says Remuria's remnants never gave up their wish to rescue their waning civilisation and surpass fate.

An artifact text in the set voices the troupe's bitterness: musicians who had lost their score mourned the empire, scorned the "savages" who inherited its lands, and promised that when the great symphony played again the loyal would be rewarded and humanity sorted into masters and the rest.

Methods: Members met in the Faded Castle to study the spirit and fate, and built musical devices in imitation of Remuria's golden-age constructs, including autoharmonic music boxes that read scores. The troupe saw fate as a fixed script. By collecting and copying "cruel dramas" they produced what outsiders called magic. Its music was also used to record things, including magic, and conches carried information.

To survive the Prophecy of Fontaine, the troupe studied ways to preserve lives and bodies: moving a consciousness into a stone golem filled with golden ichor and making seals such as the "Seal of the Chymical Marriage". Este, a Remurian, is said to have survived the ages as a golem. Item text states the troupe used melodies to entice children to give their souls to sleeping golems, and the wiki calls this child sacrifice.

History: After Remuria's first fall, Boethius gathered its remnants and founded the troupe. The troupe worked in the Faded Castle and left its remnants, golems and records in the Petrichor area and the waters of the Nostoi Region and Sea of Bygone Eras.

Relations: - **Remuria and Remus**: the troupe was the afterlife of Remuria's court, led by one of its Harmosts.
- **Marechaussee Hunters**: founded to oppose it.
- **Narzissenkreuz Ordo**: inherited and adapted its methods.
- **Petrichor's Consilium Sapientum**: concealed its secrets.

Status as of 7.1: The troupe no longer exists. Its remains are in Petrichor and the Faded Castle, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found that changes this.

Players meet it through the Faded Castle exploration in the Petrichor quests, the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box, and the Golden Troupe artifact set.

216.content: A musician from a conquered island tribe, Boethius rose to be one of Remus's four Harmosts and a close friend of Cassiodor. He enforced Remus's orders against barbarians and Lochfolk, and when Remus relented he rallied Remuria's last armies, took the golden ichor and sealed the dragon Scylla. He was swept away with Remuria by the Symphony's tsunami, and the troupe was his attempt to continue Remuria's cause afterward. His full entry holds the details.

217.comment: Golden Troupe: Praetorian golems and the Seal of the Chymical Marriage
217.content: The troupe's preservation techniques put a consciousness inside stone golems with golden ichor. Item texts describe silent, hungry golems that wait in the theatre of the Faded Castle for innocent souls. The troupe's sealing methods included the "Seal of the Chymical Marriage".

218.content:
Graffiti Alliance (also: the Alliance of graffiti artists, Natlan graffiti artists): The Graffiti Alliance is a group in Natlan that promotes the art and history of graffiti. Anyone can join, whatever their experience or style, and the Alliance gives new members free supplies and lessons. It is hundreds of years old and now has hundreds of members.

Members paint all over Natlan. The Alliance's headquarters is a plain-looking house at the Masters of the Night-Wind, but its members' works are not kept there. They are painted on cliffs, walls and houses across the region.

Structure: The Alliance is loose. There is no test or ceremony to join and no required meetings or duties. A new member is simply noted down by "Mural Maniac", the Guru-in-Chief, who manages the headquarters. Members are mostly out painting, and visit only to pay fees or ask for technical help. Dues are one thousand Mora per person each year, and members are expected to spread the word about the Alliance.

The Alliance has a gallery (Yolo's setting) with members' paintings on the walls, and it was planning a training area at its headquarters. Dopey Dazzler describes the group's "lofty ambition" of matching the Adventurers' Guild, which is why a headquarters mattered.

Leadership: "Mural Maniac" is the Guru-in-Chief and runs the headquarters. "Dopey Dazzler" is a mainstay who promotes a philosophy of avant-garde art. Neither has a stated real name; Dopey Dazzler says titles matter more than real names to graffiti artists.

Members: Known members are "Mural Maniac" (Guru-in-Chief), "Dopey Dazzler" and Yolo. Mural Maniac says anyone in Natlan holding a spray can and a paint bucket is probably a member. Yolo is also affiliated with the Collective of Plenty.

Dopey Dazzler was once badly injured painting a cliffside when a safety line snapped, and was laid up for three months with bandages around her head; she envies the Scions of the Canopy's skill at working at height. Mural Maniac took some commissions drawing comics and is also a registered member of the Adventurers' Guild, which makes survey trips abroad easier.

Goals: The Alliance teaches and spreads graffiti across Natlan. Some members, such as Dopey Dazzler, want to advance graffiti as a whole through "avant-garde" thinking, first in Natlan and then in the rest of the world.

Methods: The Alliance funds supplies and free lessons from yearly dues. Dopey Dazzler's advice is to study Natlan's landscape and customs to find the shape and colour of emotions, and her notebook says bold lines and vivid, bright colours are the key to eye-catching graffiti. Members mix pigments from local minerals, petals and saurian scales, according to Yolo.

Dopey Dazzler says graffiti grew out of imitations of Phlogiston Engravings, the tribal symbols cut by inscribers, which ordinary people painted as marks of courage and honour. Over time the designs became more free-spirited. Her notebook adds that Natlan is not strict about technique, unlike the formal art schools of Liyue and Fontaine: anyone can paint on any flat surface as long as they cause no trouble for others.

History: The Alliance was established a few centuries ago, possibly by someone from the Masters of the Night-Wind. Outsiders told the Alliance that art elsewhere prized heritage, and a master then introduced the dues system. The fees have not changed for hundreds of years.

The Alliance's growth is recent. In Traces of Artistry (5.0) Dopey Dazzler says the group has just over ten people and is gathering funds for a headquarters. By Mural Maniac's dialogue the headquarters is built and there are a couple of hundred members, which Mural Maniac says has caused an expense problem because the dues no longer cover costs.

Relations: The Alliance's headquarters sits at the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its members admire the Scions of the Canopy's skill at heights. Dopey Dazzler treats the Adventurers' Guild as a model.

In Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey (6.2, a limited-time event), Mural Maniac says the Alliance is recruiting talented artists from across the world. In that event the Guru-in-Chief collaborated with the Knight of Favonius Mika on the "Saury-Saury Scout" after Mika rescued Mural Maniac from the cold on Dragonspine.

Reputation: The Alliance thinks of itself as a long-standing craft community and its members as the makers of Natlan's most visible art. The dues and free lessons are credited with spreading graffiti's popularity. Mural Maniac says people should only paint in areas the administrators permit and never damage local scenery.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Alliance is active, with a headquarters and a couple of hundred members, and has money worries.

Following the end of the Natlan crisis, Mural Maniac says the Alliance has been expanding and recruiting artists from all over the world (limited-time event dialogue in 6.2). No later developments were found for 6.3-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

219.content: "Mural Maniac" is the Graffiti Alliance's Guru-in-Chief and an open-world NPC at the Masters of the Night-Wind. Mural Maniac welcomes visitors, admits anyone interested in graffiti on the spot, and worries about money because membership grew faster than the yearly dues can support. Mural Maniac considers taking portrait commissions to raise funds. In the limited-time event Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey, Mural Maniac appears in Mondstadt to scout locations for graffiti, and credits Mika with saving them on Dragonspine. Pronouns and age are not stated in the sources checked.

220.content:
"Dopey Dazzler" is a graffiti artist and Graffiti Alliance mainstay who hosts the Traces of Artistry event in Natlan (5.0). She invites the Traveler and Paimon to travel to find inspiration, and preaches avant-garde art. She says the nickname came from a friend who praised her colour combinations while others laughed that she gets dopey blending paint, and that her real name is less important than her title.

Her notebook, left for a future graffiti genius, says graffiti is the simplest emotions made visible and that Natlan has no strict teachers. She gave the Traveler a Graffiti Kamera for collecting source material during the event. This material comes from a limited-time event.

221.content: Yolo is a member of the Graffiti Alliance and the Collective of Plenty who paints at the Alliance's gallery. Yolo says every piece of graffiti has a soul, and that long ago a group of mystics could infuse paint with the power of the Wayob to protect Natlan from calamities. Today the "soul" comes from pigments made of different minerals, petals and saurian scales.

222.content: Traces of Artistry was the 5.0 flagship event (2024-08-28 to 2024-09-16) in which "Dopey Dazzler" invited the Traveler to tour Natlan in search of inspiration, with stops at the Children of Echoes, the Scions of the Canopy and the People of the Springs. It introduced the Graffiti Alliance in game. The event is limited-time canon.

223.content:
Grand Alliance (also: the Grand Alliance, seven-tribe alliance): The Grand Alliance was the coalition of Natlan's seven tribes, created to build the new nation of Ochkanatlan under Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord. It began as an agreement between autonomous groups, but Och-Kan, growing obsessive, gathered the tribes' authority into his own hands. The Alliance ended in a civil war: by the wiki's reading, six tribes rose with the Scarlet-Eyed Youth and the seventh stood with Och-Kan. It is a historical organisation, long gone by the present day.

It is known mostly through relics: Och-Kan's notes in the ruins of Ochkanatlan, and the texts on weapons belonging to its officers and rebels.

Structure: Seven tribes joined as autonomous groups. Their leaders handed over authority, and Och-Kan acted as the Alliance's single ruler. Known offices include the Ordnance Officer (held by Yupanqui) and the Recording Officer (Amoxcihuatl). The tribes also supplied labour: Och-Kan's notes describe requisitioning one laborer from every ten households for waterworks under his city.

A weapon text describes the Ordnance Officer post as idle, or perhaps it always was. Yupanqui took it while dispirited, expecting to wait out his days. The Alliance's other offices are not described in the sources checked.

Leadership: Och-Kan led the Alliance as the Sacred Lord, also called the Holy Sovereign. He took the reins after Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, entered the Sacred Flame. He held that Xbalanque alone deserved the title of god and that no other ruler should arise. Details of his rule and fall belong to his own entry.

Tribal leaders mattered before the Alliance consolidated. Ixquieh and Ahpub, twin chiefs of the Nanatzcayan and Teteocan, died, and Och-Kan then persuaded their tribes to hand authority over "temporarily". Sakkuk was later appointed the Nanatzcayan's agent. Uenuku and the Oceanids who followed him left the Alliance around the time Ixquieh died. The First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan, Lianca, doubted Och-Kan and later rebelled.

Members: Known members and figures tied to the Alliance:
- Yupanqui: Ordnance Officer, who later joined the Scarlet-Eyed Youth against Och-Kan.
- Amoxcihuatl: Recording Officer.
- Ixquieh and Ahpub: twin chiefs of the Nanatzcayan and Teteocan.
- Lianca: First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan.
- Uenuku: left the Alliance with his Oceanid followers.

Tribes known by name in connection with it are the Nanatzcayan (Children of Echoes), the Teteocan (Collective of Plenty), the Flower-Feather Clan and the seventh tribe, whose people are later called Muratans. Canon does not name all seven in one place.

Goals: The Alliance was created to build Ochkanatlan, a new nation for the human tribes. Under Och-Kan the aim hardened into making humanity safe from "all that is beyond human comprehension", dragons and the Night Kingdom alike.

Methods: Och-Kan used labour levies, treated objections as betrayals of the alliance, banned live sacrifice and worship of the Night Kingdom, and used the Turnfire against opponents. His notes show him reasoning that divided rulership led to endless strife and that any chance of revolt must be eliminated. He also kept the ancient dragon Ixlel imprisoned in a statue so that her power could run his city.

History: After Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, the seven tribes formed the Alliance and placed authority in Och-Kan's hands. The tribes' consent frayed as the Sacred Lord grew more suspicious. The Alliance ended in a civil war in which the Scarlet-Eyed Youth gathered heroes against Och-Kan and his city fell. (That the seventh tribe sided with Och-Kan is the wiki's reading, not a direct statement.)

**Strains inside.** Och-Kan's notes record that only the Flower-Feather Clan's First Speaker refused to recruit laborers, and that he saw her storming out as an abuse of power and disregard for the oaths of alliance. Uenuku and the Oceanids had already left. The First Speaker later rebelled and died in battle against Och-Kan's forces.

**The split.** The wiki reads The Frozen, Rekindling Land and The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc as placing the seventh tribe on Och-Kan's side and the other six on the Youth's. Enjou tells it as a kingdom torn apart by civil war, with the wicked king slain and his people exiled. The wiki's Muratans page says the seventh tribe split in two: the Muratans, who became wanderers, and the Tenochtzitoc, who settled apart on islands to the north-west of Natlan.

Relations: - **Ochkanatlan**: the city the Alliance built, and its seat.
- **The Scarlet-Eyed Youth**: led the revolt of the six tribes.
- **Muratans**: by the wiki's account, the wandering branch of the seventh tribe, who later settled in Mondstadt; Vennessa is their representative in history.
- **Dragons and Saurians**: persecuted during Och-Kan's rule. The Youth was among those sympathetic to the Saurians.

Status as of 7.1: The Grand Alliance has been defunct since the civil war. As of 7.1 it appears only as ancient history.

224.content: The Holy Sovereign's Notes are Och-Kan's fragmentary writings in the Old Core of Chu'ulel and elsewhere in Ochkanatlan. They record his requisition of laborers from the tribes, the First Speaker's refusal, his fear that surviving dragons might regain their power, and his decision that there must be one ruler, one sovereign, one god. A later note shows that he saw himself as loyal to the Alliance to the end.

225.comment: Grand Alliance: Alliance officers and rebels
225.content: Yupanqui was the Alliance's Ordnance Officer and, by a weapon text, accepted the empty post out of loyalty to his last surviving friend. The Scarlet-Eyed Youth later convinced him to fight Och-Kan. Amoxcihuatl served as Recording Officer. Lianca, First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan, doubted Och-Kan, refused his labor quotas and died rebelling against him.

226.content:
Grand Narukami Shrine (also: Narukami Ooyashiro, the Grand Shrine): The Grand Narukami Shrine is Inazuma's chief religious organisation. It worships the Electro Archon and leads the faith of the Narukami people from the largest shrine in the nation, on the summit of Mt. Yougou on Narukami Island, beside the ever-blooming Sacred Sakura. Its head is the Guuji, Yae Miko, a kitsune who is also the Shogun's friend and the owner of Yae Publishing House. Its shrine maidens wear white and red.

The shrine's everyday work is receiving worshippers, handing out fortune slips and omamori, performing rituals and ceremonies, and protecting the Sacred Sakura and its offshoots, the Thunder Sakura. Use of military force is forbidden on its grounds, because it would dishonour the Shogun, so the shrine stands outside the Shogunate's armed jurisdiction while still serving the Electro Archon.

Places: The shrine sits at the peak of Mt. Yougou. Pilgrims climb the long stairway and pass through many red torii gates; visitors favoured by Electro can ride Thunder Spheres up instead. The huge Sacred Sakura grows in the shrine grounds and is said to symbolise the eternity of Narukami. Its five-petal blossom appears on the shrine's buildings and on Yae Miko's clothing. Fortune slips are drawn from a box at the shrine maidens' stall, and a bad slip can be tied to a hanger in the hope of changing one's luck. Wishes can also be written on prayer plaques and hung on a prayer rack.

Leadership: Guuji Yae Miko leads the shrine. Worshippers and maidens call her "Lady Guuji" or "Lady Yae". She is solemn and mysterious in her ceremonial role and far more relaxed as head of her publishing house.

Miko says she never wanted to manage the shrine. The Kitsune Saiguu, her elder in the Hakushin line, persuaded her (partly by promising all the fried tofu she could eat) and then left on a "long trip" from which she never returned. The Guuji must attend every ceremony in full dress, which Miko finds the most tiresome part of the job.

Earlier leaders were kitsune and their companions. Hakushin, matriarch of the Hakushin Clan, managed the shrine with her six apprentices. About 500 years ago it was led by the Kitsune Saiguu together with Reizenbou, the Great Tengu and chieftain of the Yougou Tengu, who became the Saiguu's bodyguard. After the Saiguu was lost in the cataclysm, the human shrine maiden Asase Hibiki is said by the wiki (without a cited source) to have taken over, before she returned to Asase Shrine on Seirai Island.

Structure: Below the Guuji serve the shrine maidens. The Kuki Clan has supplied them for generations, and other old families such as the Inagi serve too. Newcomers start with simple tasks such as cleaning. Specific duties include greeting worshippers and handing out fortune slips, looking after particular people (Kano Nana is responsible for finding the Shuumatsuban ninja Sayu when she slips away), and being sent out on errands such as investigations. Toda acts as liaison between the shrine and the Yashiro Commission, handling fund-raising and manpower.

Miko describes a ladder of ranks. A trainee becomes a Chokkai after completing the required studies and learning to chant correctly for ceremonies, which she calls the hardest step for kitsune. A Guuji's Assistant, or Seikai, must endure strict restrictions. The honorary rank of Joukai has only ever been held by the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine. According to the wiki, most shrine maidens in Inazuma (outside Watatsumi Island) train at the Grand Narukami Shrine and stay affiliated with it, and their care of smaller shrines keeps them aligned with it.

Members: - **Yae Miko**: Guuji and head of the shrine.
- **Miyuki**: a Kuki Clan shrine maiden, Kuki Shinobu's older sister. She is fiercely eager for Lady Yae's approval and a little jealous of Kano Nana.
- **Kano Nana**: shrine maiden, novel enthusiast and Miko's favourite at the shrine. She is Shikanoin Heizou's older distant cousin and is forever chasing Sayu.
- **Inagi Hotomi**: shrine maiden who greets worshippers coming for fortune slips. She descends from Inagi Misato, a shrine maiden who was the Kitsune Saiguu's friend 500 years ago.
- **Maki**: shrine maiden at the fortune-slip stall who explains the Sacred Sakura to visitors.
- **Enyashi Yukari**: a nervous newcomer who keeps the prayer-plaque area tidy.
- **Toda**: the Yashiro Commission liaison, usually found at the Kamisato Estate.
- **Gendou Ringo**: the curt maiden who hands out fortune slips. See the entry below for who she really is.

Kuki Shinobu is a former trainee shrine maiden. Her parents sent her to the shrine as a child after Miyuki. She came to doubt the shrine's unexplained rules, received a Vision when she left, and is determined never to be dragged back to being a shrine maiden. She wears a mask so that people she knows will not recognise her while she works with the Arataki Gang. Miyuki first meant to talk her out of leaving but, seeing the Vision, helped persuade their parents to let her go.

Goals: The shrine exists to serve and honour the Electro Archon, guide the people's worship, and keep the Sacred Sakura healthy, which in turn protects Inazuma from accumulated filth. Its maidens describe everything there as being done according to the Archon's will. Under Miko, the shrine also quietly works to protect Ei's path to Eternity and Inazuma's stability, sometimes in ways the Shogunate itself does not see.

Methods: The shrine's tools are ceremony, purification and prestige rather than force. Maidens perform exorcisms on request; the disciples of the swordmaster Domon hired them, for example, when he seemed possessed after losing his Vision. They also run the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual, sell omamori and fortune slips, and host festivals and ceremonies such as the Goshintou Ceremony, at which master smiths offer swords to the shrine. The ban on armed force at the shrine makes it a refuge: Miko sheltered the wanted Traveler there and faced down Kujou Sara by reminding her of that rule.

History: **Origins.** The shrine is very old. Hakushin, the kitsune matriarch, served there with her apprentices, and the wiki reads New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune as placing it before the Archon War. Over centuries the Hakushin kitsune were its keepers. Miko says the Sacred Sakura owes its foxlike shape to centuries of their care.

**The cataclysm era.** About 500 years ago the Kitsune Saiguu, worshipped as a kitsune goddess, led the shrine with the Great Tengu Reizenbou. The young Yae Miko had arrived shortly before the cataclysm. A circle of mortals gathered around the mountain: the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki, Inagi Misato, and the "Yougou Three" (Hibiki, Kamuna Harunosuke and Mikoshi Nagamasa), who trained under the Yougou Tengu. When Makoto and Ei went to Khaenri'ah, the Saiguu stayed to defend Inazuma and was consumed by the darkness. Reizenbou went into self-imposed exile, the Yougou Three parted ways (the wiki says, without a source, that Hibiki ran the shrine for a time before returning to Asase Shrine), and the Hakushin lands at the foot of the mountain were abandoned. Echoes of the Saiguu's memory later formed Hanachirusato, who kept the Cleansing Ritual alive and once persuaded the returning Kamuna to perform it.

**The Sakoku era (2.0-2.1).** While the Vision Hunt Decree and Sakoku Decree were in force, worshippers prayed for the closure to be lifted because of their economic hardship. Miko watched the Traveler from the start of the Inazuma Archon Quest. In Omnipresence Over Mortals, she rescued them from the Balladeer, brought them back to the shrine, trained them against the Shogun, and used the shrine to meet Kujou Sara. There she gave Sara proof that Kujou Takayuki had betrayed the Shogunate, and gave the Traveler an omamori. She later revealed that she had paid the Balladeer the Electro Gnosis, which Ei had entrusted to her, for the Traveler's life. After Ei abolished the Sakoku Decree, worshippers came instead to give thanks and pray for business and safe travels.

Relations: - **Electro Archon**: the shrine worships her. Ei and Miko are old friends, and Ei entrusted Miko with the Electro Gnosis before entering the Plane of Euthymia.
- **Yashiro Commission and Kamisato Clan**: the Commission manages religious and ceremonial affairs, and Kano Nana says shrine maidens must follow its orders. Its ninja Sayu is looked after by a shrine maiden. Miko once saved the Kamisato Clan from dismissal after a scandal over the Raiden Gokaden, leaving them with a debt of loyalty to the Shogun's path.
- **Tenryou Commission and Kujou Clan**: Tenryou once chaired the Fire-Soothing Festival Committee the shrine ran, until Miko took its budget. Kujou Sara visits the shrine, and Miko finds her incessant questions about Ei tiresome.
- **Watatsumi Island**: a separate faith with its own shrine maidens in blue. The Raiden Shogun says Sangonomiya destroyed the local Narukami shrine on the island.

Reputation: Ordinary Inazumans revere the shrine and climb the mountain for blessings and fortune slips, and visitors from abroad are told they too will be blessed if they believe. Its head inspires a different feeling: few people have ever "figured out" Miko, and some, such as Thoma and Gorou, are openly wary of her. In the shrine, Miko's solemn manner at ceremonies awes the junior maidens.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shrine is active and Yae Miko is still Guuji. With the Sakoku Decree gone, worshippers now come to give thanks and pray for business and safe journeys.

No new shrine storyline was found in the 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) updates; Inazuma has no story content in those versions.

227.comment: Grand Narukami Shrine: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual
227.content: The Sacred Sakura and its grafted offshoots, the Thunder Sakura, purify Inazuma by drawing filth into their roots. The roots are all connected, so filth flows toward the central roots beneath Mt. Yougou. It cannot dissipate on its own, so the Grand Narukami Shrine normally performs a Cleansing Ritual. Minor cleansings check the roots and set barriers that protect the roots from people and people from the filth. A major cleansing is due every 60 years. The barriers are broken with wards, the filth condenses into "defilement incarnate" (harmless in peaceful times, dangerous in troubled ones) and is destroyed, and finally the tumour at the central roots is purged. Records say that when the ritual once lapsed, centuries ago, monsters ran rampant and the seas turned black. The most recent major cleansing was done by the Traveler and Hanachirusato after Miko cancelled the shrine's own preparations.

228.content: "Gendou Ringo" is the name of the curt shrine maiden who exchanges bamboo slips for fortune slips at the Grand Narukami Shrine. The name was a cover: the first person using it was a Shuumatsuban agent (later codenamed Momoyo), and in The Very Special Fortune Slip the Fatuus Lyudochka Snezhevna took over the role and became far friendlier to visitors. The other maidens noticed she "seems like a different person", but trust her because Lady Yae let her stay.

229.comment: Grand Narukami Shrine: Shrine maiden ranks
229.content: According to Yae Miko, a trainee shrine maiden earns the title Chokkai once she has finished her studies and can chant correctly at ceremonies. A Guuji's Assistant (Seikai) must keep many strict restrictions; Miko's advice is to snack at night and not get caught. The honorary rank Joukai has only ever been held by the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine.

230.comment: Grand Narukami Shrine: Hakushin kitsune and the shrine
230.content: The Hakushin Clan was a prominent, influential kitsune lineage in Inazuma that managed the shrines around Mt. Yougou. Its matriarch Hakushin ran the Grand Narukami Shrine with six apprentices. The Kitsune Saiguu and Yae Miko both descend from her line. After the Saiguu's death in the cataclysm, the clan's lands at the foot of the mountain were left abandoned, and statues of Earth and Sky Kitsune still wait for her return.

231.content:
Guhua Clan (also: Guhua Brotherhood, Guhua Sect, Guhua School, Sect of Ancient Splendor): The Guhua Clan is a Liyue martial arts school that honours the wandering hero Guhua and teaches sword and spear. It was once famous across Liyue and beyond. Today only a few members remain, and its base, Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng, is falling apart. Xingqiu is its best-known member.

Its belief, as former member Chen the Sharp quotes it, is that the noblest martial virtue is to pursue what benefits other people. It was formerly called the Guhua Brotherhood and later the Guhua Sect.

The clan is a small and often comic presence in Liyue, but it carries real history. Its members are proud and anxious in equal parts: they cling to the old arts while short on money, students and a clear leader. Guhua himself never founded anything. The clan was built afterwards by someone claiming to be his disciple.

Structure: There is no visible hierarchy beyond seniority and epithets. Members use titles such as Cloudpiercing Arrow (Huang the Third), Snowstriding Sword (Wen the Fourth) and Guhua Guru of Feiyun Fame (Xingqiu). Wangshan Hall is the headquarters and training ground. Visitors who ask for the master at the gate are told he is off in the mountains.

Wen the Fourth counts the clan's masters by generation. The 11th Master, Yingmin, known as the Piercing Blade, judged the old techniques too hard for general study and had a set of easier entry-level forms made. Zhangsun Jijing, the Rainbearer, is another named Guhua disciple, now preserved in the Temple of Space.

Leadership: No master is named in the present day. Guhua is honoured as founder and namesake but was never a master and never took a disciple. The actual founder was Boxuan, called Master Baixuan, a man Guhua had once favoured as a boy. After Guhua's death Baixuan founded the brotherhood in his name and called himself Guhua's disciple. Xingqiu is the clan's most celebrated talent: his profile says that when the clan's head read his verse on the Martial Principle, he wept and declared that it was the clan that needed Xingqiu, not the other way round.

Members: Members the Traveler can meet include Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth at Wangshan Hall, Sun Yu and Little Que'er at Huaguang Stone Forest (until Sun Yu leaves), and Xingqiu. Former members include Chen the Sharp, a grilled-fish vendor in Liyue Harbor, and Zhiruo, a waitress.

Huang the Third guards the gate and, hoping to raise Mora for repairs, lures visitors in Yilong Wharf into a paid tour of the hall with inflated claims. Wen the Fourth is a gloomy senior who worries about what happens to the clan's books when the last old members are gone. Wakamatsu is an Inazuman who slipped out during the Sakoku Decree, inspired by a martial tale, to seek training at the clan. The wiki lists him among current members, though his place is informal. After the Traveler opens Wangshan Hall's hidden chamber, he begs Wen the Fourth to take him as a disciple, and Wen tells him to start with the basics.

Chen the Sharp spent ten years training in seclusion with the clan and now uses its bladework to scale and gut the fish he sells. He thinks this is a worthwhile use of the art. Zhiruo left the clan and works at the Third-Round Knockout restaurant; the wiki says she remembers Sun Yu and Xingqiu from her time in the clan. Zhangsun Jijing, the Rainbearer, is a historical disciple who trained in Raincutter.

Goals: The stated aim of the remaining members is to restore the clan's former reputation, or at least to keep Wangshan Hall standing. Sun Yu had sought the adepti's advice on reviving the clan before concluding that this was going nowhere. Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth worry about leaving no successors.

Methods: The clan teaches the Three Guhua Greats: Light Piercer for polearms, Rain Cutter (Raincutter) for swords, and Life Ender for those who master both. Guhua is said to have worked them out at Lingmeng Chamber, now Wangshan Hall. New members start with the fundamentals, such as practising against wooden stakes. In its prime the clan travelled the world, doing justice with sword and spear.

Xingqiu's profile says Guhua weapon arts treat the weapon as an extension of the body. Xingqiu's own insight was that a Vision should be seen as an extension of oneself and the weapon as an extension of the Vision, so both weapon arts are arts of the eye. He wrote a verse on this after four years of study, and it is sealed at Wangshan Hall. The reason given for sealing it is his dreadful handwriting. Xingqiu also found that the clan taught stage tricks (quicklime, smoking sand, paper fish, sword-swallowing, fire-breathing) that he valued as part of a heroic repertoire.

History: Guhua was a peace-keeping martial nomad who trained at Lingmeng Chamber and never meant to start a school. After his death the boy he had once favoured, Boxuan or Master Baixuan, founded the Guhua Brotherhood. In its heyday it had a large following, and its members travelled Teyvat, known for sword and spear. Over the following centuries members deserted, and it went through several name changes, shrinking to the small Guhua Sect and then to today's Clan.

Guhua's notes in the hall's library show a very human man. His training was derailed by falls from the Plumwatcher Piles, he took up fish farming and filled pages with fish recipes. When young Baixuan brought him a mutton and fish dish while he recovered from an injury, he traded his Life Ender technique for the recipe. In the hidden chamber the Traveler finds an engraving attributed to Guhua whose grim tone is unlike his notes, asking what readers will do when they reach a dead end.

Relations: The clan has no formal alliances. Huang the Third drops his tour swindle when the Traveler threatens to report him to the Millelith. Xingqiu's family, the Feiyun Commerce Guild, is wealthy; his father let him learn martial arts from the clan to keep him out of the Wanwen Bookhouse for a day, knowing it was a declining art. The luxury dojo Xingqiu first trained in was not the clan's and had been rented to keep up appearances.

Reputation: In its heyday the clan's name rang like steel through Liyue Harbor. Now it is a faded name that many treat as a joke. Its members know it: Little Que'er calls it an archonforsaken martial arts club.

Secrets: Wangshan Hall's hidden library and secret chamber were unknown to the modern members, who remembered only legends of a treasure. The chamber lies behind a rusted door and elemental-colour book puzzles and holds trials and Guhua's engraved message. Huang the Third gave the Traveler the hall's backup key after the Traveler humoured him. He admitted the Traveler was more honest than other visitors.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guhua Clan is nearly extinct. A few members still keep Wangshan Hall, and no source shows a revival.

Sun Yu has left for Fontaine. Wen the Fourth and Huang the Third remain at the hall, the former with a possible new student in Wakamatsu. The clan's future is unknown.

232.comment: Guhua Clan: The Three Guhua Greats
232.content: The Three Guhua Greats are the clan's three secret arts: Light Piercer (spear), Rain Cutter (sword) and Life Ender (both together). Guhua is said to have worked them out at Lingmeng Chamber. Xingqiu's profile describes them as arts refined over the generations that waited for a worthy successor, and he was the one who grasped the Martial Principle.

233.comment: Guhua Clan: Wangshan Hall and Its Secret Chamber
233.content: Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng, in Chenyu Vale, is the clan's base. It is run down, and Huang the Third gives paid tours to raise money. Beneath the library the Traveler discovers a hidden chamber sealed by scrolls readable only with Elemental Sight, then trial areas and Guhua's inscriptions. Wen the Fourth says the hall was where Guhua was said to have reached enlightenment.

234.comment: Guhua Clan: Sun Yu and Little Que'er
234.content: Sun Yu and Little Que'er are two young Guhua disciples who grew up training together. Sun Yu wanted to revive the clan and sought the adepti's guidance near Huaguang Stone Forest. Que'er is hostile to strangers who approach him and has feelings for Sun Yu that he does not notice; he regards her as a sister. In the 3.3 commission series he gives up the search and decides to travel abroad. Que'er refuses to go and is left heartbroken, mistakenly believing he never cared for her.

235.comment: Guhua Clan: Huang the Third and Wen the Fourth
235.content: Huang the Third, the Cloudpiercing Arrow, is the cheerful swindler at Yilong Wharf who is fond of the hall and ashamed of what he must do to maintain it. Wen the Fourth, the Snowstriding Sword, is the gloomy senior who explains the clan's history. They talk like old comrades and tease each other about who was the better fighter a few years ago.

236.content:
Gunnhildr Clan (also: House Gunnhildr, Gunnhildr Family, the Gunnhildr Clan): The Gunnhildr Clan is Mondstadt's oldest family of knights. Its motto is "For Mondstadt, as always". Its roots go back to the priestess Gunnhildr, who stood with Barbatos against Decarabian, and the clan stayed loyal to the people through the age of the aristocracy. Many Knights of Favonius and Church clergy come from it. Jean is its best-known member today.

The clan was one of the founding houses of the aristocratic age, alongside the Lawrence and Imunlaukr clans, but unlike the Lawrences it never turned tyrant. When Vennessa rebelled, the Gunnhildrs sided with the people and were not exiled.

History: The clan traces itself to Gunnhildr, daughter of a nomadic clan leader who left Decarabian's city. She led her people alongside the wind spirit that became Barbatos and crowned him with laurels after Decarabian fell. In the aristocratic age the clan kept its oath to protect Mondstadt, and it sided with Vennessa's rebellion about 1,000 years ago.

**Decarabian's era.** The Biography of Gunnhildr says the clan's leader had served Decarabian and led his people out of the city rather than live under a despot. In the blizzards beyond the walls, his daughter Gunnhildr prayed, and a wind spirit heard her. The faith of her people let it build a small shelter and gave her the power to protect them. After her father died she became chief and the clan's first priestess. A shrine in the Thousand Winds Temple, where the clan prayed to Istaroth, is attested in weapon lore.

**After Decarabian.** When Barbatos won, the clan settled north in an old fortress. That land later became Dornman Port, and an NPC says the clan founded Mondstadt's first sanctuary of Barbatos there. Later, as the Church became a puppet of the nobility, the Gunnhildrs of the time threw the bishop sent from Mondstadt out of the sanctuary tower and tore it down, and the port has had no church since.

**Vennessa's rebellion.** The clan sided with the people and escaped the exile imposed on the other noble houses. A loading-screen text says Vennessa won the clan over before setting up the resistance's first base at Dornman Port. Afterwards, the wiki says, the clan led a push to abolish hereditary fiefs.

**The cataclysm era.** Dornman Port was a front line when the Knights fought the monsters of the cataclysm 500 years ago, as the Knights' own history records.

Structure: The clan is a family house of knights and clergy, not an organisation with ranks. Its identity is carried by its motto and its tradition of service. No head of the clan is named in canon. A cadet branch, the Dornmannshaven family, uses the motto "Sail Toward Freedom".

Swordsmanship became required of nobles, and the Royal Longsword's text suggests the habit grew out of the Gunnhildr culture of always being ready to protect Mondstadt. The wiki also notes that the oath of the ancient Mondstadters echoes the clan's own saying.

Members: Jean Gunnhildr, Master of the Knights of Favonius, is the clan's heir and public face. Her mother is Frederica Gunnhildr, the Alder Knight. Her younger sister Barbara Pegg was born into the clan but left with their father, Seamus Pegg.

Jean was raised by Frederica, with a strict regime, to succeed her as the clan's heir. Her profile says a Gunnhildr learns to say the motto before saying "Mommy". Frederica is a captain and long-serving front-line commander. Seamus Pegg, a former adventurer, is the Church's Cardinal of Daybreak and Seneschal. The parents' marriage ended; Barbara joined the Church and became a deaconess. Eckhard Gunnhildr is a modern historian of the clan and the author of the Biography of Gunnhildr. Historical bearers of the name are the priestess Gunnhildr and the Knight of the Golden Bough.

Goals: The clan's only stated purpose is its oath to the Anemo Archon: to protect Mondstadt, its land and all its people. The motto sums this up.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius and Church of Favonius**: the clan supplies many knights and clergy, and its members hold senior posts in both. Frederica and Jean are knights; Seamus and Barbara serve the Church.
- **Barbatos**: Gunnhildr crowned the new Anemo Archon, and the clan has served him since.
- **Lawrence Clan**: the Biography contrasts the Gunnhildrs with the scheming Lawrences. Eula, of the disgraced Lawrence line, serves under Jean's command today.
- **Ragnvindr Clan**: the other house known to have escaped exile.
- **Imunlaukr Clan**: the third founding house of the aristocracy, not mentioned in the present day.

Reputation: Gunnhildrs are seen as reliable and old-fashioned in the best sense. Jean is trusted across Mondstadt, and the Alder Knight is a heroine to the young. The weight of the name is also a burden: Jean's profile says the lineage can feel heavy.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan remains in service. Jean is Acting Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

Frederica went north with Varka's expedition as second-in-command, was later sent back to defend Dornman Port, and is now said to be on a secret mission known in detail only to Jean. No clan developments from 6.7 to 7.1 were found.

237.content: The Biography of Gunnhildr is a history of the clan's apical ancestor, compiled by Eckhard Gunnhildr, a modern Mondstadt historian, from fragments of aristocratic-age legend. A copy can be found in Dawn Winery. It tells the priestess Gunnhildr's story and ends by predicting that the clan will keep its duty to the Anemo Archon.

238.content: "For Mondstadt, as always" is the clan's motto. Jean links it to the sense of duty that made her give up childhood play, and her Vision story says she heard it in her mind when she received her Vision. The cadet Dornmannshaven branch has its own motto, "Sail Toward Freedom".

239.comment: Gunnhildr Clan: Dornman Port and the clan
239.content: Dornman Port lies in the lands of the clan's old hereditary fief. Loading-screen text says it was named after the Thorn King, an ancestor of the clan. Mondstadt's first sanctuary of Barbatos stood there. The port has no church because the Gunnhildrs of the late aristocratic age tore down the sanctuary after throwing the bishop out. In 6.x, Frederica was sent back to Dornman Port to help defend it.

key: School of the Theory of Knowledge
240.content:
Haravatat (also: Haravatat Darshan, School of Semiotics, School of the Theory of Knowledge, Darshan of Semiotics): Haravatat is the Sumeru Akademiya's school of semiotics, the study of signs, meaning and language. It covers linguistics, ancient runes and the translation of old texts. Its colour is black, its crest shows a bull, and it is led by Sage Rushd. It is the smallest Darshan by enrolment, but it has produced Alhaitham, the Akademiya's Scribe, and the veteran scholar Faruzan.

Haravatat sees language and writing as the core of the world. The Akademiya receptionist Sitt sums it up as deciphering ancient texts or creating new words. Because its focus includes ancient languages, the Darshan's work overlaps with Vahumana's study of history.

Structure: Haravatat is one of the Six Darshans, with one Great Sage at its head. Its disciplines include linguistics, ancient runes and syntax, as in Gregor's remark that his Haravatat classes spend their time on syntax and structure rather than literature. Members range from students and Driyosh to researchers and mentors. Entrance is by exam: Alhaitham was admitted with top marks in the Haravatat entrance test, and his grandmother also arranged for him to attend classes in other Darshans.

The Darshan studies old scripts, among them the King Deshret script. Since a century ago, its research has shifted from the analysis of ruin machinery with the aid of ancient texts to language itself. The older machinery work became a niche within Haravatat as Kshahrewar grew into the Darshan of technology and overtook it.

Leadership: Rushd is the current Sage. He is the youngest of the sages and succeeded Khajeh after the Akademiya-Fatui plot collapsed.

Khajeh, the previous Sage, was one of the four sages who joined the plan to build an artificial god. In 3.0 he travelled to Gandharva Ville with several subordinates to invite Tighnari into the project, implying that Tighnari's refusal damaged Naphis' reputation. Khajeh was among the sages exiled to the Avidya Forest after the Sabzeruz Festival. Rushd was Khajeh's junior. In 6.6, among the six sages at Caravan Ribat, he warned that Irminsul is vital to all Teyvat and asked for backup plans. He also called the Temple of Silence plan too risky.

Members: Alhaitham is the Akademiya's Scribe, a Haravatat graduate whose brilliance baffles colleagues because he refuses higher office. His father had been a Haravatat mentor, and his mother a Vahumana scholar. Faruzan is a Haravatat professor who returned to the Akademiya after a century trapped in a King Deshret ruin. Her mechanics research became the foundation of mechanical study in Kshahrewar, but she remains Haravatat and has refused Kshahrewar's offers to move. Gregor, a student from Mondstadt, studies syntax here. Yavanani is a Haravatat scholar who debates Vahumana's Khaldun, and Rifaet, also Haravatat, is one of the top candidates for Grand Conservator of the House of Daena.

Others the wiki lists as Haravatat include Amandeep, Azmi, Bahar, Murtada Radkani, Rezakhani, Rowshan, Tafazzoli, Viraf and Ziryab. Hawa of Rtawahist sometimes dabbles in ancient runes, though she may have learned them from her family rather than the Darshan.

Goals: Haravatat tries to understand meaning through signs: translating ancient writing, studying structure and building theories of language. In debates with Vahumana, Haravatat members say Vahumana's habit of seeking universal rules for all events puts the cart before the horse. Faruzan, defending the Darshan, insists that someone has to keep studying niche topics to expand the frontiers of knowledge.

Methods: The Darshan works in libraries and texts rather than the field. Haravatat students are said to spend more time on grammar than on stories, and a posted comment in the Akademiya complains that Haravatat means only research and papers, with no chance to see the outside. A rule that students master twenty languages before graduating is cited by Alhaitham, though it appears to be a former policy kept alive as a joke.
