Three types was the accepted limit, but Aksinya's version briefly held five, as part of a bet. The Eitr (Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment), a Hyperborean creation, could absorb any embryo, though it could not preserve the special traits of each. Koshchei used this line of work to create the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters. After the Cataclysm, working under the name Doctor Moreau in Okurov, he pursued eternal life.

290.comment: Hvergelmir: Alvis and Pavlina at Hvergelmir
290.content: Alvis, a long-lived Domovoy, feared and resented humanity but set aside that feeling for the Tsar's sake and taught Aksinya. He also had Izmaylov spy on the institute. His private notes in the ruins show an obsessive wish to get hold of the Proto-Man's power. Pavlina, a Snegurochka alchemist, met Aksinya as a child at a banquet in her manor and became her friend. She had a laboratory in the Pale Crown Palace and a cat named Lara. After the betrayal she returned to the House of Hesperides, where she later pursued her plan involving Ikhor.

291.content: Alvis placed Izmaylov at the institute to spy, but Aksinya took him as a student, and the kindness she showed him made him a believer. She anchored him during an expedition into Hyperborean ruins and gave him a pen. When she vanished, he suspected foul play, turned against Alvis and took the presidency of the Royal Energy Commission. When Aksinya returned after 500 years, she found him elderly. He confessed his joy at seeing her and returned her pen, and they parted owing each other nothing.

292.content: The Ruined Hvergelmir is a hidden space in the White Birch Snowgrave, beneath the Pale Crown Palace, which the Traveler reaches on an old prototype train. It contains four laboratories belonging to Aksinya, Alvis, Koshchei and Pavlina, notes on alchemy, potion formulae and a locked chamber. In the 7.0 world quest "To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown" the Traveler sees the institute as it was, with Izmaylov, Azazel and Vsevolod unaware of their presence, and finds Pavlina's note about her cat.

293.content:
Imunlaukr Clan (also: the Imunlaukr, Tyrant of Imunlaukr): The Imunlaukr Clan was one of the founding clans of old Mondstadt, alongside the Gunnhildr and Lawrence clans. It descended from Imunlaukr, an outlander warrior, and became known for gifted fighters who fought hard and died young. In the dark age of the old aristocracy it turned tyrannical. Its bloodline is now gone.

The clan is known almost entirely through weapon lore and two remarks from Dornman Port townsfolk. It is not mentioned in present-day Mondstadt, unlike the Gunnhildr and Lawrence clans.

Members: No individual clan member is named apart from the ancestor Imunlaukr, who gave the clan its name, and an unnamed "tyrant of Imunlaukr".

Imunlaukr himself was an outlander who lived in Sal Vindagnyr, the lost city on Dragonspine, and survived its destruction because he had left to seek a way to save it. His own entry covers his story. In Dornman Port, Irmgard, a Dornmannshaven descendant, boasts that her family once outwitted the "tyrant of Imunlaukr" in trade. That is the only reference to a clan leader of the aristocratic era.

Goals: Weapon lore says the clan inherited its founder's outlook: combat was an entertainment for the gods watching from above, not a means of protection, glory or territory. Its warriors fought monsters and outlaws alike, with no thought of whether they would return home, because roaring in the heat of battle counted as duty fulfilled. Such a life had no end and no hope of victory. When Barbatos swept away the snow and Mondstadt took shape, the clan came to feel it had found something worth fighting for.

This is the clan's outlook as the Sacrificial Greatsword's text tells it. The text does not say what happened to that new purpose once the aristocracy turned tyrannical.

Methods: In the early period, when Mondstadt's people worshipped the gods of Anemo and Time together, the clan acted out war tales with prop weapons. They also staged duels between warriors stained black with blood as part of sacrificial ceremonies. The Sacrificial Greatsword was one such prop; the text says it began as a stage weapon and was hardened by the passage of time. A separate text on the Royal Greatsword says gladiatorial combat in Mondstadt began as a religious ceremony alongside prayers to the wind gods, and the wiki infers that the clan's culture inspired it. Later the practice was twisted into a sport for the pleasure of the Lawrence Clan, and the Knights of Favonius outlawed it.

History: The clan came from Imunlaukr, whose descendants settled in what became Mondstadt. By the time Decarabian's rule ended it was known for brave, short-lived warriors. In the aristocratic age it grew tyrannical, and the Gunnhildr Clan broke with it. Today its line has died out.

**Origin.** Imunlaukr returned empty-handed to Sal Vindagnyr and found everyone dead. He decided that Celestia only watched the people below suffer, and went in search of a war-torn land to entertain the gods. He ruined three thriving kingdoms until the survivors hunted him as a sworn enemy. At that point he gave up the life of a warrior for good. His fate after this is not stated, but his descendants formed the clan.

**Decarabian's era and after.** By the time Decarabian's Mondstadt fell, the clan was known for gifted fighters who died young. After Barbatos cleared the snow and made Mondstadt a land of breezes and green pastures, they believed they had found a cause.

**The dark age.** Under the old aristocracy the clan became more and more tyrannical. The Gunnhildr Clan, then settled at Dornman Port, made a total break with it. According to Hannelore, the priest there, the Gunnhildrs of that time seized a bishop sent from Mondstadt, threw him from the high window of the port's sanctuary tower, and tore the sanctuary down. The Church had by then become a puppet of the aristocracy, and the Church of Favonius regards the act as true piety. The sanctuary was never rebuilt, and the place remains roofless. Hannelore's account names the Imunlaukr as the tyrannical clan being cut off.

**Afterwards.** After Vennessa's uprising, the Gunnhildrs pushed to abolish all hereditary noble fiefdoms. Hannelore says the once-mighty Imunlaukr line has since vanished and its accomplices have lost their former prominence.

Relations: - **Gunnhildr Clan**: broke with the Imunlaukr over their tyranny, famously by the bishop incident at Dornman Port. The Gunnhildrs later stayed in Mondstadt as the oldest knightly house.
- **Lawrence Clan**: the third founding clan named alongside the Imunlaukr. The Lawrences are the aristocrats later associated with perverting gladiatorial combat into a sport.
- **Knights of Favonius**: founded after the uprising that ended the aristocracy, and outlawed the gladiatorial combat that the clan's culture seems to have inspired.

- **Dornmannshaven family**: present-day merchants at Dornman Port who recall outwitting a tyrant of Imunlaukr in trade.
- **Sal Vindagnyr**: the clan's founder came from that city. His story is told separately by weapon lore and in the Dragonspine murals, and it ties the clan to the lost city only through his ancestry.

Status as of 7.1: Extinct. The bloodline has vanished, and the clan is no longer mentioned in present-day Mondstadt.

As of 7.1 nothing new has appeared about the clan. Its legacy survives only in old weapons and in remarks from Dornman Port locals.

294.content: Several weapons carry the clan's story. The Sacrificial Greatsword, once a ceremonial prop for war tales that hardened over time, belonged to the clan and tells of its warriors and their sacrificial duels. The Royal Greatsword belonged to nobles who once ruled Mondstadt and records how gladiatorial combat began as a religious rite. Snow-Tombed Starsilver and Disaster and Remorse belong to the story of the founder Imunlaukr rather than the later clan.

295.comment: Imunlaukr Clan: Dornman Port and the break with the Imunlaukr
295.content: At Dornman Port, Hannelore tells that the port was a Gunnhildr fief long before Barbatos ended Decarabian's rule, and that Mondstadt's first sacred sanctuary stood there. When the Church became the aristocracy's puppet, the Gunnhildrs of the age ended their ties with the Imunlaukr by hurling a visiting bishop from the sanctuary tower and demolishing the building. The Church of Favonius sees this as true piety. The sanctuary was never rebuilt.

296.content:
Inazuma Shogunate (also: Inazuma Bakufu, the Shogunate, Shogunate of Inazuma): The Inazuma Shogunate is the government of Inazuma. The Electro Archon heads it as the Raiden Shogun, also called the Almighty Shogun or "Her Excellency", from the castle of Tenshukaku in Inazuma City. Day-to-day rule belongs to the Tri-Commission: the Tenryou Commission (military and security), the Kanjou Commission (finance and borders) and the Yashiro Commission (shrines, festivals and culture), each led by a great clan. The Shogunate also commands the Shogun's Army. Its creed is the Shogun's ideal of Eternity.

Most Inazumans do not know that the throne has changed hands. Makoto, the first Raiden Shogun, died 500 years ago, and her twin Ei rules in her name. For centuries a puppet, the Shogun, governed in Ei's place.

Leadership: At the top is the Raiden Shogun. Under her, Kujou Kamaji is acting head of the Tenryou Commission's Kujou Clan and Kujou Sara is the general commanding its forces. Hiiragi Chisato is acting head of the Kanjou Commission's Hiiragi Clan, and Kamisato Ayato is the Yashiro Commissioner.

The previous Tenryou and Kanjou Commissioners, Kujou Takayuki and Hiiragi Shinsuke, were removed for colluding with the Fatui. As of 7.1 no permanent successors have been named.

Historically, Makoto ruled as the first Shogun, with Ei as her kagemusha (body double). After Makoto's death, Ei took her place and her titles. Around 400 years ago Ei handed rule to the puppet Shogun. The puppet followed fixed directives that could not be altered, while Ei meditated inside the Plane of Euthymia and ignored everyday affairs. After the events of 2.1-2.5, the puppet acts as Ei's kagemusha and Ei herself is far more involved.

Structure: The Tri-Commission (San-bugyou) meets at Tenshukaku to decide government affairs. Proposals apparently pass through a council in which the commissions can veto one another: when the Yashiro Commission proposed repealing the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions blocked it. Each commission is led by a hereditary clan, and lesser clans serve under them. The Takatsukasa, for example, are a branch family of the Kujou.
- **Tenryou Commission** (Kujou Clan): the Shogun's executive arm. It handles military affairs, policing and public security, and it enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and, with the Kanjou, the Sakoku Decree. Its headquarters is inside Tenshukaku.
- **Kanjou Commission** (Hiiragi Clan, based at Ritou): handles national finances, customs, borders, trade and bureaucracy. It vets everyone who enters or leaves.
- **Yashiro Commission** (Kamisato Clan, headquartered at the Kamisato Estate): handles shrines and temples, ceremonies and public festivals, and is considered the commission closest to the Shogun. It also controls the Shuumatsuban, a clandestine ninja corps.

Civil officials such as tax secretaries and a head of the civil office work within Tenshukaku alongside the commissions. The Shogun's Army is divided among the three commissions: the Tenryou supplies the main fighting force, the Kanjou guards the borders, and the Yashiro protects shrines and festivals. Some units serve the Shogun directly. These are the Hatamoto and the Okuzumeshuu, the Shogun's bodyguards, who take orders only from her.

Goals: The Shogunate exists to uphold the Raiden Shogun's rule and her ideal of Eternity: a stable, enduring Inazuma protected from loss. In practice it governs, keeps order, defends the archipelago, which lies close to the Dark Sea and has been drawn into many wars, and manages the nation's faith and festivals. Since Ei's change of heart, Eternity has been redefined to include her people's wishes, and the Shogunate has turned outward again.

Members: Key figures include the Raiden Shogun; Kujou Sara (tengu general, adopted daughter of Takayuki, allowed to keep her Vision during the Vision Hunt); Kujou Masahito (general, in charge of military affairs in Kannazuka); Kujou Kamaji (who ran the Tenryou Commission's government business in Inazuma City and is now proxy clan head); Hiiragi Chisato; Kamisato Ayato and Ayaka; and Thoma, the Kamisato retainer. Shikanoin Heizou works for the Tenryou Commission as a doushin detective. Yae Miko, Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, holds no Tri-Commission office but is one of the Shogun's oldest friends and keeps the Electro Archon's confidence.

Methods: The Shogunate rules by decree, backed by the Shogun's absolute authority and the Shogun's Army. The Army's ranks are modelled on a feudal hierarchy, from ashigaru foot soldiers to doushin patrol officers, yoriki, hatamoto and generals. The Tenryou Commission has issued draft orders requiring each family that receives one to send at least one adult to the army. The Kanjou Commission runs strict entry and exit assessments at Ritou and issues travel permits.

Disputes can be settled by a Duel Before the Throne. Both parties present their case to the Shogun at Tenshukaku, and if she allows it they fight until one cannot continue. The loser dies, either in the fight or by execution with the Musou no Hitotachi.

History: **Founding.** In the Archon War, Ei conquered many youkai races. With their help, humans built a city by the sea, and more than 2,000 years ago she brought all of Inazuma's islands under one rule. Ei believed her twin Makoto was better suited to rule. She gave up her body so that Makoto could ascend, and an in-world novel says Makoto then "set up her Shogunate", rebuilt Ei's body and kept her at her side as kagemusha. Most of the world believed there was only one god, Baal. The Shogunate's forces under Ei crushed Orobashi's invasion of Yashiori Island, and Watatsumi came under the Electro Archon, though its people were allowed to keep worshipping their god.

**Cataclysm.** Five hundred years ago, monsters ravaged Inazuma. Makoto went alone to Khaenri'ah and died there. The Kitsune Saiguu fell defending Inazuma, and Mikoshi Chiyo, tainted by a beast of sin, turned her blade on Ei. Ei took over the throne under her sister's name. Around this time the Kanjou Commissioner Hiiragi Hiroshi built Ritou into a trade port.

**Eternity.** Fearing erosion and loss, Ei built puppets. One rejected prototype later became the Balladeer (Scaramouche). About 400 years ago she activated the Shogun, entered the Plane of Euthymia and gave the Electro Gnosis to Yae Miko.

**Sakoku and the Vision Hunt.** A year before the Traveler arrived, the Fatui won over Tenryou Commissioner Kujou Takayuki and Kanjou Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke with promises of power. The Shogun then imposed the Sakoku Decree, which closed the borders behind storms, and the Vision Hunt Decree, which seized Visions for the Statue of the Omnipresent God. Ei knew the Fatui were involved but did nothing, since she judged ambition a greater threat to Eternity. The decree provoked the Sangonomiya Resistance, and a civil war followed. The Fatui armed both sides with Delusions, made from Crystal Marrow that the Kanjou Commission had stockpiled. By Amidst Stormy Judgment, 99 Visions had been seized.

**The turning point (2.0-2.1).** The Traveler exposed the plot alongside Kujou Sara, defeated Signora in a Duel Before the Throne (the Shogun executed her), and then defeated Ei in the Plane of Euthymia with Yae Miko's help. Ei abolished the Vision Hunt Decree, the Visions were returned, and the two commissioners were arrested. Kujou Sara and Sangonomiya Kokomi then held peace talks, with the Traveler as witness.

Relations: - **Grand Narukami Shrine**: the shrine and the Shogunate jointly hold old ceremonies such as the offering of swords. Its Guuji, Yae Miko, is Ei's confidante and held the Gnosis for centuries.
- **Watatsumi Island**: once an enemy god's land, then a subject island that kept its own faith. It became an open enemy in the civil war. The Shogun has said that, because Watatsumi destroyed its local Narukami shrine and rebelled, Kokomi as Divine Priestess must be held accountable. After the war, peace talks set terms such as fishing rights and taxes, while the question of Watatsumi's forces returning to Tenryou command was left open.
- **Fatui and Snezhnaya**: the Fatui exploited the Shogunate from within. Even so, because of Snezhnaya's diplomatic ties, the Sakoku restrictions did not at first apply to the Fatui or to Snezhnayan merchants.
- **Foreign nations**: the Tri-Commission is often compared to Liyue's Qixing and Eight Trades and to Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Shogunate is stable and open. The decrees are gone, the borders are open, the civil war is over, and Ei takes a more active role in rule with the puppet Shogun as her kagemusha.

The Kujou and Hiiragi clans are led by the acting heads Kamaji and Chisato while the former commissioners await judgement. No new Shogunate story developments were found in 6.0-7.1, whose Archon Quests take place in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya.

297.content: The Tri-Commission is the Shogunate's administrative council of three commissions, each held by a great clan: the Tenryou (Kujou Clan; military, police and security), the Kanjou (Hiiragi Clan; finance, customs and borders, based at Ritou) and the Yashiro (Kamisato Clan; shrines, festivals and culture). They meet at Tenshukaku, and any one of them can veto another's proposal. People compare it to Liyue's Qixing and Eight Trades. After 2.1 the Tenryou and Kanjou heads were removed for colluding with the Fatui, and their clans are now led by acting heads Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato. Kamisato Ayato still holds the Yashiro.

298.comment: Inazuma Shogunate: Ranks of the Shogun's Army
298.content: The Shogun's Army uses feudal ranks. Ashigaru are foot soldiers; those of the Kanjou Commission stop people leaving Ritou without permission. Doushin are patrol and police officers, often seen in Inazuma City. Yoriki are mid-ranking samurai who command troops, including at the Kujou Encampment. Hatamoto are high-ranking samurai serving the Shogun directly, and two guard Tenshukaku. Okuzumeshuu are the Shogun's personal bodyguards and answer only to her. Above them are generals, such as Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito. Rank-and-file armour is eggplant-coloured and bears the Shogunate's crest.

key: Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi
299.comment: Inazuma Shogunate: The first Shogun and her kagemusha
299.content: An Inazuman novel, once a restricted text, tells how the Shogunate began. The Electro Archon was originally twin sisters. Ei ("shadow") was the unmatched warrior, but she thought herself unable to understand mortal hearts. She gave up her body so that her sister Makoto could ascend, and Makoto, the True Shogun, set up the Shogunate. Makoto then rebuilt Ei's body and kept her close as her kagemusha. Ei says the book is fairly accurate up to the war against Orobashi but idealises her afterwards. Makoto died in the cataclysm, and Ei has ruled under her name ever since. In 2.5 the puppet Shogun became Ei's own kagemusha.

300.comment: Inazuma Shogunate: Fatui collusion in the Tri-Commission
300.content: A year before the Traveler arrived, the Fatui offered Tenryou Commissioner Kujou Takayuki support and rewards. Wanting to protect his clan's influence and thinking the Fatui no threat to the Shogun, he pushed the Vision Hunt Decree and sent the Shogun misleading reports about the war. Kanjou Commissioner Hiiragi Shinsuke stockpiled Crystal Marrow for the Fatui's Delusion factories, and he plotted with Signora to keep the Traveler stuck in Ritou. Kujou Sara read the evidence and confronted her adoptive father, who admitted everything. After Ei learned how far the deception went, Shinsuke was imprisoned and Takayuki was placed under house arrest, both to await punishment. Takayuki is said to have "aged" overnight.

301.content: With Takayuki disgraced and in poor health, the Kujou lost control of their vassals and the Tenryou Commissioner's post sat empty. Kamaji, the younger son, had already privately doubted the decrees. He opened talks to pass the post to the Takatsukasa branch family. Its head, Takatsukasa Susumu, held him in a hidden Tenryou base with hired ronin and tried to force a confession blaming the Kujou alone. Ei arrived with the Traveler and declared that the post belonged to whoever would duel her, as the Kujou founder once had. Susumu refused out of fear. Kamaji fought, knowing he would lose, and kept going until he collapsed. Ei said that the puppet would have killed him, but she saw the Kujou sense of honour in him and gave the clan more time. Kamaji became provisional clan head. His elder brother Masahito, who stays with the army in Kannazuka, supported the decision.

302.comment: Inazuma Shogunate: Hiiragi Clan after Shinsuke
302.content: Hiiragi Chisato, who earlier helped the Traveler escape Ritou in exchange for carrying her letter to Kujou Kamaji, became the Kanjou Commission's figurehead after her father's arrest. Some Hiiragi retainers forged a marriage announcement between her and Kamaji, hoping she would marry into the Kujou and lose her place so that they could take the commissionership. Kamisato Ayato and the Traveler exposed the plot. The wedding was postponed indefinitely and the announcement treated as false, and Chisato began taking the commission's affairs seriously.

303.comment: Inazuma Shogunate: End of the Inazuma civil war
303.content: The war between the Shogun's Army and the Sangonomiya Resistance reached a stalemate around Yashiori Island and Kannazuka, and both sides were secretly fed Delusions by the Fatui. After the Vision Hunt Decree was repealed and the war ended, Kujou Sara and Sangonomiya Kokomi held peace talks at Tatarasuna, with the Traveler as witness (New Beginning, Kokomi's story quest). Terms added to the peace treaty included lifting wartime fishing restrictions on Watatsumi vessels in return for taxes under Narukami law. When a Watatsumi soldier's outburst exposed two Tenryou soldiers' dealings with Signora's vengeful Fatui subordinates, Kokomi declined, for now, to return Watatsumi's forces to Tenryou command, and Sara promised an internal investigation. During the war, the official Matsukawa Souzen had warned that it was worsening Inazuma's finances.

304.content:
International Trade Association (also: Bankoku Shoukai, Ritou International Trade Association): The International Trade Association is a group of foreign merchants based in Ritou, the port island of Inazuma. It imports overseas goods such as Silk Flowers and gives practical help and shelter to outlanders who are new to Inazuma. Its president is Kurisu, a merchant from Fontaine. Under the Sakoku Decree, Ritou's Kanjou Commission treated its members harshly.

Merchants in trouble usually go to Kurisu directly, and newcomers are pointed to the Association when the Outlander Affairs Agency has taken them for all they are worth. During the lockdown, the Agency's Kageyama told the Traveler that only Association members were authorised to import and export goods.

Structure: No formal ranks beyond the president are given. Kurisu leads and handles the hard cases, and other members run the day-to-day work. Xixi says she does only the simpler reception work, and Harrison runs a shop of imported goods. The Association has a building in Ritou with a small plaza in front. Its members come from several nations, so it is as much a community as a trade body.

Membership has changed over time. Werner, a Mondstadter who had shipped goods between Liyue and Inazuma, was once a member. Thoma says the Association was very generous to him at first, but he left when the decrees made life hard for everyone.

Leadership: Kurisu is the president. His real name is Christopher and he comes from Fontaine; he took the name Kurisu after arriving in Inazuma. He is courteous and patient, and he tells his members that outlanders must look after each other.

Kurisu is a friend of Thoma, the Kamisato clan's housekeeper and fixer. Xixi says he has lived in Inazuma for a long time and that every outlander in Ritou can count on him. In the 2.0 Archon Quest he openly misses Fontaine, but he deals with a corrupt tax collector through reputation and leverage rather than force. After the Sakoku Decree ended, Thoma says he was working to mediate disagreements within the Association.

Members: - **Kurisu:** president and spokesman, from Fontaine.
- **Harrison:** a shopkeeper from Mondstadt who sells imported goods at International Groceries. His shop was closed for weeks by the tax squeeze.
- **Xixi:** a sleepy receptionist whose home region is Liyue.
- **Werner:** a former member from Mondstadt, central to the Crystal Marrow affair (see entries).

Xixi says the Association used to be a place where foreign traders gathered to mingle and swap business news. After the decree ended she says the number of outlander merchants rose sharply, so she has had little sleep.

Goals: Its aims are practical: keep foreign goods flowing into Inazuma, keep outlander merchants solvent, and give newcomers a place to turn. Mutual help among outlanders is also a stated principle, as Xixi says Kurisu always tells them.

Methods: The Association imports foreign goods for sale in Ritou, advises and shelters newcomers, and negotiates quietly when pressed. In the 2.0 Archon Quest, Kurisu confronted the tax collector Keijirou by pointing out how a scandal would tarnish a samurai's reputation, then bargained for compensation. Thoma sometimes acts as an outside fixer who helps the Association with problems.

Harrison's whispered talk about "stocking up" and "premium products imported from merchants all over the world" plays on the line between import trade and smuggling. The scene treats it as a joke, and he insists these are imported goods only.

History: **The decree years.** After the Sakoku Decree was enacted, Ritou's Kanjou Commission treated foreign merchants harshly. Outlanders faced high taxes and strict rules, and the Association was a place of mutual support.

**The Crystal Marrow tax (Chapter II, Act I).** A new Tax Decree required the Association to pay in Crystal Marrow instead of Mora. A single vendor controlled the supply and kept raising the price. The Traveler traced the vendor, Werner, to Keijirou, a Kanjou Commission tax collector who was embezzling the Marrow and selling it back to the merchants. See the entry for details.

**After the decree.** After the Kanjou Commissioner was arrested and replaced and the Sakoku Decree ended, the Commission began treating the merchants on better terms, which delighted Kurisu. Thoma says the Association is still going strong and is still needed in many situations.

Relations: **Kanjou Commission.** Hostile under the Sakoku Decree, better afterward. Kurisu says the Commission's tax collectors cared only about Mora.

**Thoma.** A good friend of Kurisu who sent the Traveler to help in the Crystal Marrow affair, and later talked down the Kanjou Commission's chief Katsuie.

**Outlander Affairs Agency.** A separate state office that processes foreign entry and residency. Kurisu assumes newcomers will have been fleeced there.

**Fontaine, Mondstadt, Liyue.** These are the home nations of Kurisu, Harrison and Werner, and Xixi's home region. Kurisu's longing for Fontaine is a recurring note.

In Kamisato Ayaka's Story Quest, Ayaka and the Traveler asked Kurisu for silk. He said it had been stolen by vagrants, Ayaka helped him recover it, and he gave them some as thanks.

Reputation: Within Ritou's outlander community the Association is well trusted, and Kurisu is regarded as reliable. To the old Kanjou Commission its members were an easy source of tax revenue. Thoma says many people in Ritou are still grateful to the Traveler for stopping Katsuie's persecution of the merchants.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Association remains in business in Ritou under Kurisu. The Sakoku Decree is over, the former Kanjou Commissioner has been replaced, and the number of outlander merchants has grown.

305.comment: International Trade Association: Crystal Marrow Tax Affair
305.content:
In Confessions of an Outlander (Chapter II, Act I), the Kanjou Commission issued a Tax Decree that required foreign merchants to pay in Crystal Marrow instead of Mora. Almost nobody knew where to find it. One older Liyue merchant remembered once shipping some to Snezhnaya. A single vendor, Werner, soon held the only supply and kept raising the price. Thoma sent the Traveler to help. With a Mondstadt and a Liyue local specialty, the Traveler won Werner's trust and learned he was a small cog. Keijirou, a Kanjou Commission tax collector, was feeding him the Marrow, taking nearly all the profit, and recording every payment in a ledger buried on the beach.

Kurisu read the ledger and used the threat of a ruined reputation to make Keijirou hand over his remaining Marrow as compensation. Harrison, whose shop had been shut for weeks, wanted more. Katsuie, Keijirou's chief, arrived and ordered the merchants seized. Thoma showed Ayaka's fan, the Shirasagi Himegimi's, and mentioned a petition to the shogun, and Katsuie backed down. Werner left before facing Kurisu. The Kanjou Commissioner was removed later in the Archon Quest.

306.content:
Werner is a Mondstadt-born merchant who shipped goods between Liyue and Inazuma until the Sakoku Decree stranded him in Ritou. He joined the Association, left because he felt unable to contribute, sold shells on the beach, and then became the sole Crystal Marrow vendor. He is abrasive at first, but gifts of Mondstadt and Liyue specialties remind him of home, and he admits the truth about Keijirou.

He was too ashamed to face Kurisu directly in that quest. Whether he later made peace with the Association is not stated.

307.content: Kurisu is the Association's president, a Fontainian who adopted an Inazuman name. He is courteous, tired of the Kanjou Commission, and homesick for Fontaine. He is acquainted with Thoma, and a cat named Kaiser is often near him. In the open world he offers a Genius Invokation TCG duel and, after a particular dialogue branch, a Guide to Prosperity.

308.comment: International Trade Association: Irodori Festival at the Association
308.content: During the Irodori Festival event Hues of the Violet Garden, the small plaza in front of the Association was called the Five Kasen Plaza. Kurisu remarked that it looked absolutely amazing. The Association also provided housing for the foreign guests of honour. This happened during a limited-time event.

309.content:
Izmaylov Family (also: the Izmaylovs, Izmaylov gang, Izmaylov (Family), Izmaylov fae gang): The Izmaylov family, or the Izmaylovs, are a Snezhnayan fae gang, the biggest and richest in the High Table. The Domovoy Nikolay Izmaylov, the "Old Sire", founded the gang, and his adopted son Vasiliy, the "Young Sire", inherited it. Vasiliy killed the Old Sire, pushed the gang into brutal debt collection to fund a plan to open the Shadow Realm, and died when the Traveler and the Luchkins stopped him. The gang is now leaderless.

The Izmaylovs are the main villains of the Mean Streets of the Despicable world quests in Snezhnograd. Other gangs see them as having broken the Law that the High Table was founded on.

Structure: The Izmaylovs have a top leader, the Old Sire and later the Young Sire, and a second-in-command known as the Butcher who runs a major stronghold. Below them are guards and heavies, shipping crews and debt collectors. Members called by name include Lindenovich, a debt collector, Lorie, a small Volkodlak who handled cargo shipments, and the shippers Kirov, Meselson and Ishogu. Most members are fae, including Volkodlaks.

Members use "Old Sire" and "Young Sire" as titles. Guards at the strongholds demand a password, and the Train Boneyard password was "Oedipus", Vasiliy's own nickname.

Leadership: Nikolay "Pakhan" Izmaylov, the Old Sire, founded the gang and led it until his death. His adopted son Vasiliy Nikolayevich Izmaylov, nicknamed "Oedipus" and called the Young Sire, inherited the gang. He was the most favoured of the Old Sire's four adopted children. Zmei still calls him "Vasya". After Vasiliy died the gang was left leaderless.

Vasiliy resented that the gangs were treated like "dogs" by the lords above and that his father spent his life serving others. He rejected the surname "Nikolayevich" and the title "Young Sire" and wanted to be called "Lord Vasiliy". The Butcher is his second-in-command.

Members: Known members are Lindenovich (debt collector), Lorie (shipping chief), Kirov, Meselson and Ishogu (shippers) and the Butcher (second-in-command). Guards include a tall guard and a short guard at the Gang-Occupied Cavern near Glupov, a muscular guard (who sends a guard called Kubiyev to check a noise), an Izmaylov guard leader and an Izmaylov deputy. The gang also uses Volkodlak workers; one said that when the Old Sire was alive, they never worked so hard.

Goals: Under the Old Sire, the Izmaylovs followed the ideals of the High Table. Under Vasiliy, the gang's goal changed to opening the Shadow Realm in the Train Boneyard and using the technology and power it offered to win the Izmaylovs a seat in the real council, the Snezhnograd Veche, and respect from the lords above. Vasiliy told the Luchkins that "there will always be a place for Izmaylovs at Snezhnaya's table".

Methods: The Izmaylovs make their money from debt collection, and under Vasiliy they pursued it ruthlessly. They collected from people who could not pay, took a father to a lumberyard for his debts, and threatened the daughter and grandmother left at home, despite the Law's ban on harming families, women and children. They rented train carriages to ship raw materials in secret, moved supplies by rail, guarded abandoned bases with armed patrols, and used force against the Luchkins. Disputes can still be settled by a formal duel, as Lindenovich offered to Vseslav.

Lindenovich quotes the Old Sire's own rule, "debts must be repaid", to defend his debt collection, while Sofya says the Izmaylovs now ignore the founding rules. The gang also digs for ancient machinery and prototypes in the Shadow Realm, such as a prototype Kresnik's Torch in the Kristall cavern of Hunter on the Snowfields, where Izmaylov members argued over treasure shares.

History: The Domovoy Nikolay Izmaylov helped found the High Table after the Burner of Cities' rebellion and later gave each of his four adopted children a gang name. The Izmaylovs went to Vasiliy. For years the Old Sire let the Energy Commission take on Shadow Realm commissions so he could search for his teacher. When he found her, he stopped, and he tried to steer the gang and the Commission away from Shadow Realm matters.

Several months before the Traveler arrived in Snezhnograd, the Old Sire fell ill and died overnight. Gang members suspected Vasiliy and the Butcher, who were the last to see him. After that, discipline slipped across the gangs, punishments for breaking the Law became more frequent, and the Izmaylovs began to collect debts by force.

Relations: - **High Table**: the Izmaylovs are the largest of its gangs. Vasiliy held the Law and the High Table in contempt, which could have brought down the whole alliance if the Druzhna had found out.
- **Luchkins**: rivals turned enemies. The Luchkins oppose the Izmaylovs for breaking the Law, but Zmei, Iryna and Vasiliy grew up as siblings.
- **Energy Commission and Druzhna**: Vasiliy complained that the Izmaylovs got the dirty work these bodies did not want. Zmei says the Old Sire had strings to pull at the Commission, which is how the gangs came to know Shadow Realm secrets.
- **Fatui**: the abandoned Fatui base northwest of Snezhnograd later passed through several hands before the Izmaylovs got it.

- **Remusov**: Lyubov, the head of House Remusov, is another of the Old Sire's adopted children and one of Vasiliy's siblings.

Reputation: Among Snezhnayans, especially in Zolnyy, the Izmaylovs are feared as the biggest gang and hated for harassing debtors' families. Sofya calls them "blood-sucking insects" on the people, and the guards at the strongholds know to expect trouble from the Luchkins. Some members respected the Old Sire, and a short fae in Hunter on the Snowfields says the Izmaylovs get "their fair share, for Old Sire's sake".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Izmaylovs are leaderless. Vasiliy is dead, the Boneyard machine is destroyed, and the High Table is deciding the gang's future.

No further Izmaylov story was found for 7.1.

310.comment: Izmaylov Family: Vasiliy, the Young Sire
310.content: Vasiliy Nikolayevich Izmaylov, the Young Sire, was the Old Sire's adopted son and the favourite of his four adopted children. The wiki gives his appearance in the fight as that of a Fanged Zealot. He believed the fae gangs were treated as dogs, resented his father's service to the Energy Commission, and planned to use the Shadow Realm to raise the Izmaylovs' standing. He killed his father when the Old Sire refused. In the Train Boneyard he fought Zmei, Iryna and the Traveler and died when his device shut down. His last words recalled being lost in the dark as a child and being found by Zmei and another sibling.

311.content: The Butcher is Vasiliy's second-in-command, who ran a major Izmaylov stronghold in an old Fatui base northwest of Snezhnograd. Gureva infiltrated it as a spy and was held there for days, but she says the Butcher could not make her talk. He visited her himself, and she smiled at him, according to gossip among the guards. The Butcher is not shown in person in the quests found, and his fate is not stated.

312.comment: Izmaylov Family: Debt collection in Snezhnograd
312.content: Under Vasiliy the Izmaylovs collected debts early and from people who could not pay. Lindenovich took Marfa's father away to work in a lumberyard for his gambling debts, then demanded payment from the girl and her grandmother, who sell dolls to make ends meet. The Traveler beat him in a duel to give them two days. Sofya says people like Marfa seek out the Luchkins, who can protect them but have little money to pay off their debts. The Luchkins claim that the gang does this to fund the Shadow Realm plan.

313.content: The Train Boneyard is a local nickname for a half-excavated tunnel whose construction was halted after a Shadow Realm disaster collapsed it. Abandoned trains were later dumped there. Zmei, Iryna, Vasiliy and Lyubov played in it as children. Vasiliy chose it as the place to open the Shadow Realm, and used the nearby Izmaylov guards, a password and activation devices to guard it. In the finale, the Shadow Realm opened around Vasiliy's mechanism and the tunnel began to collapse. The Luchkins left by mine cart, and Zmei recalled how Vasiliy once hid in the deepest part of a collapsed tunnel during hide-and-seek.

key: the Kamisato Clan of the Yashiro Commission
314.content:
Kamisato Clan (also: Kamisato family, House Kamisato, the Kamisato Clan of the Yashiro Commission, Kamisato-ke): The Kamisato Clan is one of the three great families of Inazuma under the Raiden Shogun. It leads the Yashiro Commission, the part of the Tri-Commission that oversees shrines, festivals and ceremony. The clan head is Kamisato Ayato, who handles government and politics. His younger sister Kamisato Ayaka, called the Shirasagi Himegimi, is the clan's public face, and Thoma is its chief retainer. The clan also commands the Shuumatsuban, a secret corps of ninja. It lives at the Kamisato Estate in Inazuma City.

Among the people the Kamisato name stands for grace, courtesy and good sense. Behind that image is a family that survived a near-collapse: after elders failed in a matter of national importance and the previous heads died, Ayato rebuilt the clan's standing by cunning, and Ayaka grew into the role of its dignified public figure. The clan holds that it owes its survival to the Raiden Shogun's mercy and must follow her path to eternity. Ayato nevertheless kept the Kamisato out of the Fatui's schemes.

Structure: The head of the clan is also the Yashiro Commissioner. The siblings divide the work. Ayato deals with the Shogunate's courts and officials and holds "absolute control" of the Shuumatsuban. Ayaka watches over the clan's internal and external affairs and carries out most contact with commoners. Thoma, a Mondstadt-born man, serves as chief retainer and housekeeper and is a well-known fixer in the city. The household includes a housekeeper, servants and a doorman. The clan also runs the Komore Teahouse, which only people it approves may enter.

The Kamisato Estate contains the Yashiro Commission's headquarters in its main building, so clan, household and commission share one address. Commission staff from the Shogun's Army are called Yashiro Commission representatives. They are relaxed compared with soldiers under the other two commissions, because their duties are mostly civilian. The Shuumatsuban answers to the clan head directly, and Ayaka and Thoma have some authority over it without a stated rank.

Leadership: Kamisato Ayato leads the clan and the commission. He became clan head young, with the family weakened and rivals circling, and succeeded by tactics rather than force. He is courteous, shrewd and fond of tea, chess and calligraphy, and few people understand what he truly values.

Ayato believes people act from interest: find the leverage and most disputes can be settled. He lets others expect him to help and often attends meetings with a teacup and little more than a smile. He still keeps the clan's sense of duty; his character stories say he accepted that the Kamisato stand because of the Narukami's mercy and must never betray her. His private circle of trust is very small, with Thoma at the centre, according to his own voice-over.

Ayaka is the more visible head. She is known to the people as the Shirasagi Himegimi (the "Princess" or "White Egret Princess"), admired for her beauty and manners. Her kindness reaches far beyond ceremony: she took Thoma in against the wishes of some, and during the Vision Hunt she and Thoma ran the clan's quiet help to the Traveler. Ayaka was once a playful child. When the clan met disaster she took up swordsmanship and poetry to ease her brother's burden. Her Cryo Vision came after long practice.

Members: Kamisato Ayato (clan head and Yashiro Commissioner), Kamisato Ayaka (the clan's public face), and Thoma (chief retainer). Their late parents were the former clan head, who is unnamed, and Kamisato Kayo.

Staff and affiliates include Furuta (housekeeper), Koharu (house servant, also a ninja in training), Nobumori (doorman), and at the Komore Teahouse its owner Taroumaru, Kozue and Nakanishi. Sayu is the best-known Shuumatsuban ninja. Other named ninja include Inu Shoushou, Momoyo and Hisashi. Hirano, Hirotatsu and Madarame Hyakubei act as Yashiro Commission representatives at the estate.
Ayato's Vision is Hydro, Ayaka's Cryo, and Thoma's Pyro. Ayato received his Vision on the night his gravely ill father spoke to him of being the clan's successor. Ayaka's came after a lone strike in the dojo. According to Ayato's voice-over, Thoma was advised by him to leave during the clan's crisis, chose to stay, and has spared Ayato much worry; Ayato counts him among the few he trusts completely.

Goals: Protect the clan and restore its prestige, and in doing so keep Inazuma stable. Ayato is committed to the Shogun's rule in public but works to keep the Kamisato from being entangled in the schemes of others. Ayaka's aim is to carry her brother's burden gracefully while keeping time for the ordinary joys of life. As Yashiro Commission head, the clan also wants festivals, shrines and rites carried out properly, so deities and people are both satisfied.

Methods: Quiet pressure, information and social skill. The Shuumatsuban gather intelligence, shadow suspects, and carry out discreet missions; Ayato says members are usually orphans taken in and raised by the corps, which is how loyalty is secured. Ayaka works through etiquette, festivals, hospitality and personal charm, and Thoma through his wide network of acquaintances. The Komore Teahouse acts as a meeting place and cover for discussions the clan wants private.
In Ayato's story quest (2.6) he shows how the clan operates: he suspects that the rumoured marriage between Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato is a plot, sends the Shuumatsuban to watch the Kanjou Commission's representatives, and then turns the public mood against the schemers by making the bride an asset rather than a burden. He explains that he has done such things "plenty of times". Ayaka's story quest (2.0) shows her approach is more direct: she intervenes personally when a trade association clerk is robbed.

History: **Before the story.** The clan's founding is not given in canon. It served Ei's Shogunate alongside the Raiden Gokaden schools. A generation of Kamisato elders failed the Shogunate in the affair of the Goshintou forging, which hurt the Gokaden. According to Ayato's stories, Guuji Yae Miko spoke for the clan and kept the Shogun from punishing it, and the clan has since stayed loyal. Later the clan head and his wife died and Ayato, a young man, was left to restore its position; several groups sought to take advantage, and he defeated them.

**The Vision Hunt (Chapter II, 2.0).** When the Fatui helped drive the Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees, the Yashiro Commission was the only one of the three that did not collaborate. Ayato refused the Fatui's offer, and, as Ayaka says in the Archon Quest A Flower Blooms in a Prison, every Yashiro proposal to repeal the decree was vetoed by the other two commissions. The Komore Teahouse is where the Traveler learns of the next operations from Ayaka and Thoma. When the Tenryou Commission took Thoma to be the 100th victim of the Vision Hunt ceremony, he escaped with the Traveler, told them to seek the Watatsumi Army, and himself took refuge at the teahouse, safe in Yashiro Commission territory. Later Ayaka, Thoma and Sayu helped obtain Kujou Takayuki's falsified reports and the Fatui letters, which turned Kujou Sara against Takayuki.

Relations: - **Raiden Shogun**: the clan's sworn lord. Ayato describes the clan as standing by her mercy.
- **Kujou Clan and the Tenryou Commission**: fellow commission families, but the Tenryou Commission enforced the decrees the Yashiro Commission opposed. Ayato's voice-over says Kujou Takayuki turned Sara into a formidable weapon he can no longer wield. In Ayato's story quest he visits Kujou Kamaji to give his blessings on a marriage.
- **Hiiragi Clan and the Kanjou Commission**: during the Vision Hunt the Kanjou Commission sided with the decrees. In Ayato's story quest he helps Chisato, the acting head, assert herself over the plotters in her own commission.
- **Grand Narukami Shrine**: Ayato says Guuji Yae has been kind to the clan but never quite took to him personally, and calls him "the Yashiro rascal"; he says their working relationship is nonetheless harmonious. His stories say her intervention once spared the clan from the Shogun's punishment.
- **Kaedehara Clan**: formerly a subordinate branch of the Kamisato. Ayato still feels a duty to help Kazuha.
- **Fatui**: the clan refused them, which left the Yashiro Commission mostly unaffected.
- **Traveler**: Ayaka's friend, and a guest and ally of the household. Ayato's voice-over says that Ayaka has mentioned them on many occasions.

Reputation: Inazumans consider the Yashiro Commission the least controversial of the three. Ayaka is loved by ordinary people, and her popularity exceeds her brother's. Ayato's stories say officials say "should we ask the Yashiro Commissioner?" when a matter proves hard. Political opponents once called him "that greenhorn", and ordinary people "the poor young master of the Kamisato Clan".

Secrets: The Shuumatsuban's existence is little known, and the identities of its members are classified. Ayato tells the Traveler it reports directly to the clan head, and that after his father died command passed to him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan still leads the Yashiro Commission and commands the Shuumatsuban from the Kamisato Estate. Ayato is clan head and Commissioner, Ayaka manages its public life, and Thoma serves as chief retainer. No later story has changed this.

315.content: The Yashiro Commission ("Bugyou of Shrines") is the third arm of the Tri-Commission, the other two being the Tenryou (security and army) and Kanjou (finance and borders). It manages shrines, festivals and cultural events. Although its influence is smaller than the other two, each commission has equal authority to check the others. The Kamisato Clan leads it and its headquarters sits inside the Kamisato Estate. During the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees it was the only commission that avoided entanglement with the Fatui, and its soldiers from the Shogun's Army are comparatively relaxed. When it proposed repealing the Vision Hunt Decree, the other two commissions blocked the proposal.

316.content:
The Shuumatsuban are a secret organisation of ninja under the Yashiro Commission and reporting directly to the head of the Kamisato Clan, now Ayato. They handle intelligence, espionage, discreet work and, as the wiki puts it, assassination. Their duties keep Inazuma safe. Most are orphans raised from childhood by the corps, and their identities are secret to the point that even members killed on secret missions are not publicly honoured. Sayu is its best-known ninja. Their base is described as a ninja village.

Members receive a monthly salary, according to a quest line. A Shuumatsuban slogan quoted in a quest says to send the Shuumatsu to end "traitors and criminals alike". Ayato also uses them for small private errands. Several named agents appear in quests, including Inu Shoushou, Momoyo and Hisashi.

317.content: Komore Teahouse is a teahouse in Inazuma City run by the Kamisato Clan. Only visitors the clan approves may enter. Its owner is Taroumaru, a Shiba Inu that used to be a Shuumatsuban ninja dog, and customers pay by leaving coins in a box. The Traveler used it as a base in Chapter II, and Thoma took refuge here after the Vision Hunt ceremony. Staff include Kozue, Nakanishi and Nobumori. A story says the staff signed a contract with Taroumaru to work there forever.

318.comment: Kamisato Clan: Kamisato Kayo and Tsubaki
318.content: Kamisato Kayo was the mother of Ayato and Ayaka and died when Ayaka was young. As "Tsubaki", a name she used only privately, she imagined an ordinary life: pretty kimonos, foods from other places, and sights she had never seen. In Ayaka's story quest (2.0), Ayaka finds a note naming Tsubaki, learns of the alter-ego, and attends a festival in her place to fulfil both wishes. Ayato's stories recall her talk of cypress offerings and the line that the camellia in the courtyard stays fragrant in the bitterest winter.

319.content: An in-world account from a limited-time event (True Tales of the Violet Garden, Act IV: The Palace, Dyed in Black, 2.6). In Kazuha's great-grandfather's generation, the Kaedehara's Isshin Art was ordered to forge an important Goshintou from an ancient diagram. The forging was sabotaged, swordsmiths fled, and the Kamisato clan head was injured pursuing them and died soon afterwards. Treacherous people used the leaderless clan's weakness to threaten its standing in the Yashiro Commission, and it never fully recovered until Ayato. Ayaka tells this account to Kazuha and keeps the old diagram that the commission preserved. Ayato's own story says the failings of the Kamisato elders hurt the Raiden Gokaden, and that Yae Miko spoke up to spare them.

320.comment: Kamisato Clan: Kamisato Ayato and Ayaka's rise
320.content: After their father died of illness and their mother soon followed, Ayato became clan head and Yashiro Commissioner and Ayaka matured quickly. She is called the Shirasagi Himegimi; nobody knows where the nickname began. The siblings agreed a division of labour: Ayato does politics out of sight, Ayaka maintains the clan's public image and social standing. Ayato once advised Thoma to leave rather than be dragged into the clan's feuds, and Thoma stayed.

321.content:
Kanjou Commission (also: Kanjou-bugyou, Kanjou Bugyou): The Kanjou Commission is the part of Inazuma's government that runs finances, customs and the borders. It is one of the three bodies of the Tri-Commission, serves the Raiden Shogun's Shogunate and is led by the Hiiragi Clan from Ritou, the port where foreigners are processed. During the Sakoku Decree it was feared for its strict rules and for abusing outsiders. After the Fatui plot in Inazuma was exposed, its Commissioner was jailed and his daughter Hiiragi Chisato took over as acting head.

Its Japanese name, Kanjou-bugyou, echoes the Edo-period finance magistrates, and the English "Commission" is just a translation of the same title that the other two bugyou bodies carry.

Structure: The Commission is led by the head of the Hiiragi Clan, who holds the office of Kanjou Commissioner. Below that, the wiki lists three kinds of staff. Civilian officials (Hishida, Matsuura and Yagi) handle administration. A military arm is headed by a Chief (Katsuie) with squad leaders such as Ebina Gonshirou and Sasaki, and by officers such as Chiba, Hiromi, Kenzaburou, Kobayashi, Kousaka, Kubo, Nakano, Shinnojou and Yokoyama. Ordinary guards and collectors are called ashigaru, including the tax-collection ashigaru Keijirou. The Commission's seat is the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou, and its Outlander Affairs Agency, where the officer Chiba and the inspector Yurika work, handles documents for visitors from abroad.

The Commission acts as a veto in the Tri-Commission: In A Flower Blooms in a Prison, Kamisato Ayaka says that whenever the Yashiro Commission proposed repealing the Vision Hunt Decree, it was promptly vetoed by both the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions.

Leadership: The acting head is Hiiragi Chisato, a young woman who runs the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou. Her father, Hiiragi Shinsuke, was Kanjou Commissioner until he was jailed.

Shinsuke is described as the head of the Hiiragi Clan and the Kanjou Commissioner. He met Signora before the Traveler reached Ritou and agreed with her to keep the Traveler stuck there. Chisato overheard, and secretly offered to help the Traveler leave Ritou if they would deliver a private letter to Kujou Kamaji, her sweetheart in the rival Kujou Clan. Her father opposed the relationship. After the plot came apart, Chisato was left as figurehead. In a wedding announcement during the Cypressus Custos Chapter she is styled Proxy Clan Head, which the wiki reads as confirming her acting leadership.

Some of the clan's retainers regarded her as inexperienced and tried to remove her and claim the commissioner's post. They forged a love letter from her to Kamaji so that marriage would absorb her into the Kujou Clan and strip her of influence in the Hiiragi Clan. Kamisato Ayato and the Traveler foiled the plot (see the entry below). The wiki says this made Chisato take a more serious stance in Commission affairs. In the quest she says that, for the first time, she had asserted her authority.

Members: Named staff on the wiki's list include the civilian officials Hishida, Matsuura and Yagi, the military chief Katsuie, squad leaders Ebina Gonshirou and Sasaki, and officers such as Nakano, Chiba, Kobayashi, Kenzaburou, Shinnojou and Yokoyama (Sasaki, Yokoyama and Shinnojou are posted at the Hiiragi Estate). Kageyama, the inspector at the border checkpoint, and Yurika, inspector at the Outlander Affairs Agency, apply the entry rules in person.

Goals: Officially the Commission manages Inazuma's treasury, trade and the control of who enters and leaves, so that Inazuma's wealth and borders stay in order. Since the Fatui plot, it is trying to prove that it can serve the Shogun without the corruption of the previous Commissioner. Its reform under Chisato is a stated change in tone, not a documented new programme.

Methods: The Commission works through paperwork and checkpoints. During the Sakoku Decree it ran approvals for anyone entering or leaving Inazuma: Atsuko says the process was long and wore people down so that she fled by raft, and Bibo called the border impenetrable. Non-Inazumans could not leave Ritou without a Travel Permit. The Outlander Affairs Agency used the stranded visitors as a source of fees. The Traveler was first quoted two million Mora for entry and Thoma negotiated it down to six hundred, and he says such charges were common. Through taxes it also shaped Ritou's merchant economy.

**The Crystal Marrow tax decree.** Kurisu, president of the International Trade Association, tells the Traveler that a new decree demanded taxes be paid in Crystal Marrow instead of Mora. The scarcity pushed the price up. Werner explains that the tax-collection ashigaru, led by Keijirou, overtaxed the merchants, stockpiled the extra Marrow and had it sold back at an inflated price, with the proceeds going to the collectors. The Traveler finds Keijirou's ledger, exposes him in front of the Association and Kurisu secures the stockpile as compensation.

History: **Origins.** The Hiiragi Clan has served the Shogun for at least 500 years. About 500 years ago Hiiragi Hiroshi turned the deserted island of Ritou into a trading hub that impressed the Shogun, and he imported foreign inventions, including a Snezhnayan blast furnace for the hot springs of Tenshukaku and a special kamera built with a mirror given to his clan by the Kitsune Saiguu. She counted him a friend.

**The decrees.** The Fatui conspired with the Tenryou Commissioner, Kujou Takayuki, to manipulate the Shogun into enacting the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree and so create a market for Delusions. Shinsuke was also roped in with promises of power and wealth. He accepted by stockpiling Crystal Marrow for them. During the Sakoku Decree the Kanjou Commission turned Ritou into a bottleneck for outsiders.

Relations: - **Tenryou Commission and the Kujou Clan**: political rivals who check each other's power; a Hiiragi-Kujou marriage would be politically significant. They have a personal link through Chisato and Kamaji.
- **Yashiro Commission and the Kamisato Clan**: the Yashiro Commission was the only one of the three to stay out of the Fatui's scheme. Ayato helped Chisato keep her position in 2.6.
- **International Trade Association**: its members in Ritou dealt with the Commission's taxes and customs and suffered under the Crystal Marrow decree.
- **Fatui**: Signora worked through Shinsuke, and the wiki says Snezhnayan merchants were initially exempt from the Sakoku restrictions because of diplomatic ties.
- **Raiden Shogun**: the Commission serves under her and is subject to her final judgment, which is why Shinsuke's fate is pending.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Hiiragi Chisato acts as head of the Hiiragi Clan and the Commission. Her father remains imprisoned.

The Commission's rules for foreigners are looser than during the Sakoku Decree, which Ei abolished after her duel against the Shogun in Transient Dreams. The wiki does not record a new commissioner. No Inazuman story was released in 5.8 to 7.1, so nothing found changes this picture.

322.comment: Kanjou Commission: Hiiragi Shinsuke and the Fatui plot
322.content: Hiiragi Shinsuke was head of the Hiiragi Clan and Kanjou Commissioner when the Traveler reached Ritou in 2.0. He seems friendly: he receives the Traveler as an honoured guest and invites them in. In truth the Fatui had enlisted him with promises of power and wealth, and he stockpiled Crystal Marrow for them. He met Signora and planned to keep the Traveler indefinitely stuck in Ritou so they would not interfere. His daughter Chisato overheard and helped the Traveler escape. After the plot was unravelled he was imprisoned and awaits the Shogun's punishment.

323.content: Chisato is Shinsuke's daughter and the acting head of the Hiiragi Clan. She lives at the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou. In 2.0 she asked the Traveler to deliver a private letter to Kujou Kamaji in exchange for helping them out of Ritou; the delivery earned the Traveler a Travel Permit from Kamaji. After her father's arrest she became a figurehead and, after the forged marriage plot in 2.6, took a firmer hand. She says that despite her worry, anyone who commits a wrong must answer for it.

324.content:
The Outlander Affairs Agency in Ritou is the Kanjou Commission's office for documents and requests from non-Inazumans. During the Sakoku Decree it charged vast and arbitrary fees to stranded visitors. Yurika, the inspector, asked two million Mora from the Traveler before Thoma negotiated six hundred, and Thoma says this was normal. After the Commission was purged of corruption, the Agency became more lenient and charged only 500 Mora. Without a Travel Permit, outsiders could not leave Ritou, and Kanjou ashigaru would turn the Traveler back at the town's edge until Kamaji granted a permit.

Kageyama, the checkpoint inspector, asks visitors to state their name, purpose and goods. At that time only members of the International Trade Association were allowed to import or export goods, and purely personal reasons for visiting were not accepted.

325.comment: Kanjou Commission: Hiiragi Hiroshi and the founding of Ritou
325.content: Hiiragi Hiroshi was the leader of the Hiiragi Clan and Kanjou Commissioner about 500 years ago, after the cataclysm. He wanted all foreign trade to pass through one port under the Inazuman government and built Ritou on a deserted island. To show what trade could bring he brought in foreign inventions: a Snezhnayan blast furnace that heats the hot springs of Tenshukaku as a gift for the Shogun, and a kamera that records memories and emotions, built with a demon-exorcising mirror given to the clan by the Kitsune Saiguu. The Saiguu counted him a friend and remembered his work in her last moments. When Iwakura Michihiro became the Kujou Clan's sword instructor, Hiroshi trained under him and said he would have recruited him for the Hiiragi if the Kujou had not.

326.comment: Kanjou Commission: The Crystal Marrow tax decree
326.content: In Confessions of an Outlander the International Trade Association's president Kurisu reports that the Kanjou Commission has changed the tax from Mora to Crystal Marrow. The Marrow's price climbed because merchants all searched for it, until taxes threatened to exceed profits. Werner, a merchant, reveals that the tax-collection ashigaru under Keijirou overtax merchants, hoard the extra Marrow and have Werner sell it back at an inflated price. The Traveler follows Keijirou and finds a hidden ledger, then confronts him in front of Kurisu and Harrison. Keijirou claims he only wanted a modest living, but he is made to hand over his stockpile as compensation. The Commission's higher authorities appear only briefly, and the quest does not say whether Shinsuke knew about it.

327.content:
Khaenri'ahn Dynasties (also: Dark Sun Dynasty, Black Sun Dynasty, Blacksun Dynasty, Khaenriahn Dynasties): Khaenri'ah, the subterranean kingdom that fell in the cataclysm 500 years ago, had two known ruling dynasties. The older Crimson Moon Dynasty is known almost only through a legend. The later Eclipse Dynasty was the last, and its final king, the Vinster King Irmin, pursued Abyssal power until the kingdom collapsed. The later house's Chinese name means "Black Sun Dynasty", and the legend that describes the change speaks of a "dark sun" replacing the crimson moon.

The two are linked by blood and by grudge. Descendants of the Crimson Moon line still exist; Arlecchino of the Fatui is one. In the Eclipse era the crown hunted such descendants as potential rivals.

Structure: Canon gives no organisational chart for either house. The Eclipse Dynasty ruled through a king, a council of the kingdom's most respected figures and a royal court, with royal guards (the Black Serpent Knights) and a Universitas Magistrorum for research. Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr were the most trusted members of Irmin's council. A Knight Marshal named Anfortas served under Irmin and took the regency afterwards. The Perinheri legend describes the Crimson Moon era as a realm under a "great ruler" (addressed as "high lord of the nobles"), with sages as advisers and an orphanage whose graduates later became knights; the book's footnotes call alchemy and the Beastmaster Knights the era's mainstays.

The legend names figures from the later part of its story, which takes place after the dark sun had replaced the crimson moon: Njord, who walks with black wolf warbeasts ("Darksprites"); Alf, the greatest warrior of the Universitas Magistrorum; an Alberich, commander of half the knights; and Perinheri himself. The footnotes treat the Darksprites as an early alchemical warbeast, which fits the era's stress on alchemy and Beastmaster Knights. The legend also calls the kingdom's aristocracy obstinately pure-blooded.

Leadership: No Crimson Moon ruler has a name in canon. The Eclipse Dynasty's last ruler was Irmin, the one-eyed Vinster King, who became the kingdom's undoing. See Irmin's own entry for his character; this entry covers the dynasty as an institution. After his fall, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself Regent while "unknown threats" faced the kingdom.

A family-history page Kaeya kept says the Alberich Clan, who lacked royal blood, stepped in as regents when Irmin's strength failed. The wiki infers from this that both Anfortas and Chlothar Alberich (the Abyss Order's founder) belonged to the Alberich Clan; no quest states the link for Anfortas.

Members: Legend: the orphanage founded in the Crimson Moon era produced the knight Perinheri, and the foreign "princess" Angelica later joined it; Perinheri's rival Hleobrant came from the descendants of those who forsook their god. The legend's main events take place after the change of dynasty. Tholindis, a Universitas researcher in the Eclipse era, came from a minor branch distantly related to the main Crimson Moon line. Arlecchino carries the blood too, though she learned of it only after Pierro told her.

Eclipse side: Irmin, Anfortas, the Black Serpent Knights (the "Twilight Sword" Dainsleif and Halfdan among them), Irmin's council (Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr were its most trusted members), and the secret agent Rerir, whose duty included hunting Crimson Moon descendants.

Goals: The Eclipse Dynasty's stated aim in All Is Foretold, through Rerir's work, was to protect itself by removing any possible rival. Irmin's own aims turned toward Abyssal power and the machinery of "secrets from beyond the skies". The Crimson Moon remnants in the same quest, such as Tholindis' ally Orlog, wanted the old dynasty restored. The Perinheri legend adds that a sage of the Crimson Moon era hoped for children from beyond the world, among them beings who could "transcend the gods", and the ruler told him to do as he pleased.

Methods: The legend's Crimson Moon government relied on alchemy and Beastmaster Knights. Its sages founded an orphanage to raise children from outside the world and from the kingdom's own orphans, and many of its graduates became knights. The Eclipse Dynasty put its weight on mechanical engineering and on knowledge from beyond the sky, so alchemy and the beast-masters lost ground. Some Khaenri'ahns distrusted this: a letter to Marshal Anfortas argued that only human will could pry open "the corners of this hollow world", and asked that some of the old machinery be kept.

History: **Crimson Moon era.** Only the legend remains. In it a crimson moon shone over the underground realm, outside things leaked in from beyond the world, and a sage advised the ruler to prepare for a child who could surpass the gods. Later the crimson moon set and a dark sun took its place. That dark sun was the Eclipse Dynasty, and the book's notes place the change of rule probably around the Archon War.

**Eclipse era.** The Eclipse Dynasty ended with the cataclysm 500 years ago. Under Irmin the kingdom pursued Abyssal power. The Traveler's Sibling arrived and was named heir, Vedrfolnir was blinded for warning against Irmin's path, and Dainsleif's raid on the palace on his brother's behalf let the Five Sinners take the Abyssal power Irmin had drawn into the Sibling. The kingdom then fell, and the Heavenly Principles' response left the survivors cursed.

The Eclipse era is told in several sources. A ballad in the Mondstadt book Breeze Amidst the Forest sings of "an atrous sun" that befell its kingdom, and its Chinese text reads as the Eclipse Dynasty falling. A bulletin in the ruins at Gavireh Lajavard says Anfortas took the regency over the "indisposed" king and the council Regnum Concilium Ultimum. A traveller's journal in the same ruins records most people fleeing to the surface with the Schwanenritter while others hid below, and rumours of those who went up turning into monsters.

Relations: - **Court of Khaenri'ah**: the Eclipse Dynasty's royal court under Irmin, covered in its own entry.
- **Arlecchino**: a Crimson Moon descendant whose Balemoon Bloodfire draws on Abyssal energy and slowly corrupts her, so she uses it with great caution.
- **House of the Hearth**: Pierro hints that it began as the old orphanage of the legend, and that its later link to the Fatui could be his doing.

- **Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah**: Eclipse-era figures who split the Abyssal power taken from the Sibling.
- **Universitas Magistrorum**: the research body that Irmin ordered to study the Abyss. It had already existed by the early Eclipse Dynasty, since Perinheri mentions it.
- **Abyss Order**: later founded by Chlothar Alberich, whose clan the legend and the family-history page both tie to the dynasty's upper ranks.

Status as of 7.1: Both dynasties are gone. Their legacy survives in the curse of the Khaenri'ahns, the Abyss Order and in Crimson Moon descendants such as Arlecchino.

As of 7.1 canon has not shown a revival of either house. Khaenri'ah itself is a ruin beneath Teyvat. The 6.x Nod-Krai Archon Quests revisit the Eclipse era through the memories of Five Sinners such as Rerir and Vedrfolnir, but show no restored dynasty.

328.content: The Crimson Moon Dynasty is Khaenri'ah's older ruling house, known chiefly through the legend Perinheri (also titled Hleobranto Innamorato). Under it, alchemy and Beastmaster Knights had their peak, and its sages founded an orphanage for children from other worlds, from which came many of the kingdom's best knights. The dynasty ended when a dark sun replaced the crimson moon. Its descendants carry the Balemoon Bloodfire, as Arlecchino does, a power that draws on Abyssal energy and corrupts its user. She was warned that if the corruption reached her heart she would become a different person.

329.content: The Eclipse Dynasty was Khaenri'ah's last ruling house, ending with King Irmin in the cataclysm 500 years ago. It favoured mechanical engineering and knowledge from beyond the sky over alchemy and the beast-masters, and later Abyssal power. Its royal guards, the Black Serpent Knights, included Dainsleif the Twilight Sword and Halfdan, and its research body was the Universitas Magistrorum. The Traveler's Sibling was adopted into the royal house as the heir. The dynasty's end brought the cataclysm and left the Khaenri'ahns cursed.

330.content: Perinheri is a two-volume legend sold in Fontaine, put together over generations. It tells of an orphan, Perinheri, raised in the orphanage of the Crimson Moon era, and his best friend Hleobrant, who falls for a foreign "princess" named Angelica and starts picking duels to impress her. All three leave the kingdom while Perinheri hunts her, believing that killing her will cure his friend. Hleobrant begins to howl like a beast, and Angelica says it is the price of his ancestors forsaking their god. Perinheri, a drifter, bears no such curse. At sunrise Angelica reveals herself as "freedom, that which has broken free of fate". The book's circumstances may be embellished, but Pierro told Arlecchino its key details are accurate.

331.content: When Irmin could no longer rule, the Knight Marshal Anfortas proclaimed himself Regent. A badly worn bulletin at Gavireh Lajavard says the post was temporary, held while the king was "indisposed" and the kingdom faced "unknown threats", and that Anfortas would lead the Regnum Concilium Ultimum until things returned to normal. The Alberich family history Kaeya kept presents the regency as the Alberich Clan's doing. Whether Anfortas and Chlothar Alberich were kin is the wiki's inference.

332.content:
King Deshret's Priests (also: Desert Priests, Hermanubis Priest, priests of King Deshret, Heirs of the Burning Sun): King Deshret's Priests, also called the Desert Priests, were the priesthood who served the god-king of Sumeru's desert in his ancient kingdom. They wore the same style of head ornament as their head, Hermanubis, the Greatest of Sages and one of the king's Seven Pillars. They guarded the king's knowledge, and when forbidden knowledge ravaged the land they built the temples that held it back. Canon says little about them directly. No priest is shown alive in the present, and most of what is known comes from ruins, relics and one dying priest's recorded memory.

Three threads survive: the priest Kasala's recording (Archon Quest, 3.1), Hermanubis' followers who founded the Temple of Silence, and flavour text about descendants who keep the old ceremonies. The wiki page for the group is a stub, so treat anything beyond these as unknown.

Structure: Canon gives no ranks or headcount. Hermanubis stood over all the other priests, and the priests wore a head ornament like his. The Gilded Dreams circlet, Shadow of the Sand King, is a gold-inlaid headband once used by desert priests in imitation of a legendary ruler's.

Its lore says the priests ruled the oasis cities justly in the king's name and received divine oracles together with him. Murals in the Khemenu Temple and the Unknown Ruins show Deshret, his Seven Pillars, priests and subjects together, and slabs there record the deeds of Thoth, Heryshaf and Sobek. The Seven Pillars were the king's ministers, not strictly priests, and canon does not say how the two groups divided duties. Hermanubis is the only Pillar who rose from human stock (a Tighnarian, in Guiding Notes) to the rank of a god's familiar, and the Temple of Silence calls him "priest over all other priests". The slab records seen in the 6.1 event were left by priests, not by the Pillars, which suggests that record-keeping was a priestly task.

Leadership: Hermanubis was the guide of all the priests. Chosen from among the Tighnarians by King Deshret, he was a renowned sage and warrior known for being sincere, steady and kind.

Even his fellow Pillars respected him. After Deshret's death he led his followers to Tulaytullah. Kasala is the only other named priest; canon does not say he answered to Hermanubis directly. His own biography belongs in his separate entry.

Members: Only two members are named: Hermanubis as head, and Kasala as one of the last priests to serve under the king.

Kasala presided over a temple that later lay buried under the sands, and was entombed there. Other priests appear only anonymously in murals and slab records.

Goals: The priests served the god-king and his ideals of justice and abundance. When forbidden knowledge spread, their task became containment. Kasala's last words ask the children of the desert to drop old grievances and remember the kindness that saved them.

Methods: In the disaster the priests built temples at Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's summons, and she infused them with the divine power of life (Dendro). That tempered the damage. The wiki links these to the structures called the Towers of Betrayal. Kasala spent his life guarding one.

Descendants' lore adds that the old priests were proud of three martial skills, the cudgel, the spear and above all archery. They also kept ceremonies, and few could still read the ancient texts. This comes from in-world flavour text, not from a quest, and it describes people who hold the priests' heritage, not the priesthood as it was.

History: **The disaster.** In his grief over the Goddess of Flowers, Deshret exposed the land to knowledge that, in Kasala's words, did not belong to this world. It spread like a plague: crazed whispers, dark grey scales, a drained land. Rukkhadevata came from the forests and had the priests build her life-infused temples. The embers of the civilization survived in Aaru Village. Kasala says Deshret finally sacrificed himself, because the knowledge would blight the world as long as it existed, and that Rukkhadevata exhausted her strength and took the form of a small child.

**Kasala's end.** Kasala guarded a temple for the rest of his life and left a recorded memory there, found in "Secret of the Scorching Desert" (3.1) by Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya, Candace, Rahman and the Traveler.

**After the king.** According to Guiding Notes, Hermanubis led his people to Tulaytullah and founded the Temple of Silence there to preserve and steward knowledge. The wiki's Temple of Silence page adds that the city's rulers later betrayed the Temple to the king of Gurabad. Hermanubis shattered himself into Ba Fragments to protect his followers, who were shunned and eventually settled near Thamud Oasis about 400 years ago, according to the wiki. The Rite of Duels, said to have been created by Hermanubis, is still carried out by the Temple. In Sage of Sages (4.6) Cyno and Sethos fought one, with Hermanubis as witness.

Relations: - **King Deshret**: the priests' lord. Kasala calls him "my eternal lord" and "the proud king of the desert".
- **Hermanubis**: their head, and the founder of the group's lasting successor, the Temple of Silence.
- **Greater Lord Rukkhadevata**: the Dendro Archon who directed the priests' temple-building. In Kasala's account she and Deshret were allies, not enemies.
- **Eremites**: a number of them believed Rukkhadevata had betrayed the king. Kasala's testimony contradicts that, which shook Rahman.
- **Akademiya**: scholars of the Akademiya hold a hollow body named the Temple of Silence. The real Temple, descended from Hermanubis' followers, works separately but has been rebuilding ties since the Oathkeeper quest.

- **Seven Pillars**: ministers of Deshret. The priests' slabs record Thoth, Heryshaf and Sobek.
- **Scholars and desert folk**: descendants claim the priesthood's legacy. The Eremites call them ascetics.

Reputation: In Sumeru today the priests are a half-remembered part of the desert's past. Within the Temple of Silence, Hermanubis is praised as an immortal and valorous figure. Many Eremites, who grew up on a story that Rukkhadevata destroyed their civilization, had never heard the priests' account. The Akademiya treats Hermanubis as a foundational figure of desert civilization.

Status as of 7.1: The priesthood no longer exists as such. Its heritage continues through the Temple of Silence, now led by Sethos, and through descendants who claim it.
