No new material on the priests was found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1, which are set in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. The most recent mention is the limited-time Ruins Exploration event in 6.1.

333.content: Kasala was one of the last priests to serve King Deshret. After the king's sacrifice he continued to serve by guarding one of the temples built at Rukkhadevata's direction, in what is now called the Mysterious Ruins beneath the Mausoleum of King Deshret. He was entombed there. The party found his inscription and heard his last message in "Secret of the Scorching Desert". In it he warns that knowledge can destroy a civilization, describes the disaster, honours Rukkhadevata and Deshret, and urges the children of the desert to drop old grievances and hold on to the memory of her kindness. His voice narrates the cutscene known as Lost Legacies in the Sand.

334.comment: King Deshret's Priests: Mysterious Ruins and the Towers of Betrayal
334.content: The Mysterious Ruins is a quest-only domain buried beneath the sands near the Mausoleum of King Deshret, discovered in "Secret of the Scorching Desert". It is the tomb and temple of Kasala. The wiki connects it with the Towers of Betrayal, the temples that priests built and Rukkhadevata infused with life power. The name reflects the Eremite belief that she betrayed Deshret, which Kasala's message contradicts. A message left by someone who infiltrated a temple, and who took the priests' warnings to be tricks, shows that outsiders did not understand them either.

335.comment: King Deshret's Priests: Heirs of the Burning Sun
335.content: The weapon Scion of the Blazing Sun carries the lore of people who say they descend from King Deshret's priests. They call themselves the Heirs of the Burning Sun, keep the ceremonies of the old kingdom, and preserve a martial tradition of cudgel, spear and archery. Few can read the ancient texts. The text claims that the Eremites call them ascetics, that some have turned to the rainforest and repay the old favour in silence, and that most vanished into the desert. This is flavour text of unknown reliability and no quest depicts them.

336.comment: King Deshret's Priests: Temple of Silence
336.content: The Temple of Silence is the lasting institution of Hermanubis' followers. It keeps the knowledge of King Deshret's civilization. The Akademiya has an office with the same name that handles unpublished information, but the wiki calls it a vestige of the real Temple, which operates from near Thamud Oasis in the Land of Lower Setekh. After the Oathkeeper quest Sethos was appointed its leader, and Cyno, who holds a Ba Fragment, is its leader in name. See the entries on Cyno, Sethos and Hermanubis for details.

337.content:
Knights of Favonius (also: Ordo Favonius, Favonius Knights, the Knights of Favonius): The Knights of Favonius are Mondstadt's order of knights, founded about 1,000 years ago by Vennessa, with Barbatos' help, so that aristocrats could never rule again. They guard the city and its roads, keep order, make and enforce the law, and help manage the Church of Favonius. In practice they are Mondstadt's government. Their headquarters is in Mondstadt City.

Nobody in the order was knighted by royalty. In Mondstadt, "knight" is a title earned through the duties a person takes on.

Leadership: Grand Master Varka, the Knight of Boreas, is a huge, cheerful, famously strong man who hates paperwork. Jean Gunnhildr, the Master and Dandelion Knight, has governed as Acting Grand Master since Varka left on a long expedition half a year before the Traveler arrived.

Boreas (Andrius) recognised Varka as the north wind's human champion, and Jean calls him "the legend of his generation". Jean was made Dandelion (Lionfang) Knight at fifteen and was promoted from captain to Master during the Eroch affair. Varka has told her that if he does not return, she is to succeed him and train the next Knight of Boreas. Officers the Traveler meets most often:
- Kaeya: Cavalry Captain and Quartermaster
- Albedo: Chief Alchemist and Investigation Captain
- Eula: Reconnaissance Captain
- Hertha: Logistics Captain and Coordinator
- Note and Skeiron: captains of the 2nd and 3rd Companies
- Lohen: Vice Captain of the Ranged Company
- Lisa: Librarian
- Amber: the last Outrider

Structure: A single Grand Master leads the order. The Master is the reserve and becomes Acting Grand Master whenever the Grand Master is away. Below them are ten Captains, each heading a numbered company; the companies can be disbanded and re-formed as needs change. Their specialties include general affairs, reconnaissance, ranged fire, logistics, technical support, cavalry and alchemical investigation. There are also special units such as the Outriders. Becoming a knight takes written and practical exams. Not every member is a knight: Sucrose is an Assistant Alchemist, and Noelle serves as the Knights' maid while she keeps trying to pass.

Some knights carry personal epithets: Eula is the Spindrift Knight, Amber the Crimson Knight and Klee the Spark Knight. Klee belongs to no company because she is so young. By tradition, the titles "Lion" and "Wolf" go only to those with great leadership potential, who are expected to become Grand Master one day. "Lion" comes from Vennessa's Dandelion or Lionfang title, which Jean holds; "Wolf" comes from the Knight of Boreas, which Varka holds. Before Eroch's fall there was also an Inspector, who was trusted with Mondstadt's affairs while the Grand Master was away. Most trials are held by the Knights or by the Church alone, but Albedo's trial in 5.6 required both together.

Goals: The Knights exist to protect Mondstadt and the freedom Vennessa won. That means keeping monsters, bandits and foreign schemes away from the people, upholding order fairly, and making sure no tyrant ever rules again. Under Varka they also strike at distant dangers, such as the Abyss in the north, before those dangers reach home.

Members: Playable members include Jean, Varka, Kaeya, Albedo, Eula, Amber, Lisa, Klee, Noelle, Mika, Lohen and Sucrose (staff, not a knight). The Traveler holds the honorary title of Honorary Knight for resolving the Stormterror crisis. Diluc is a former Cavalry Captain who is now openly critical of the Knights. Razor is not a knight, but Varka named him and taught him the claymore. Mika is a surveyor of the Reconnaissance Company. Varka trained him personally and placed him on the expedition's front line.

Methods: Most of the order's work is everyday service: patrols, escorts, monster bounties, citizens' troubles and record-keeping. Heavier work goes to specialist companies, which scout the wilds, garrison Dornman Port, provide ranged support, carry out alchemical investigation and make cavalry strikes. Knights learn Favonius Bladework, the sword style Rostam developed 500 years ago. Conduct is governed by the Knights of Favonius Handbook, which Jean re-edited. It rests on three virtues, modesty, honesty and self-control, because "freedom cannot exist without the support of duty".

History: **Founding.** About 1,000 years ago the Lawrence-led aristocracy ruled Mondstadt as tyrants. Vennessa, an enslaved Muratan gladiator, led a rebellion with Barbatos, Ragnvindr and others. Afterwards most nobles were exiled, though uncorrupted houses such as the Gunnhildrs stayed. Vennessa founded the Knights as their first Grand Master and Dandelion Knight and restored the Church. A loading-screen tip says she set up the resistance's first base at Dornman Port after winning over the Gunnhildr clan. She later ascended to Celestia at Windrise, where a great oak grew.

**The cataclysm.** Five hundred years ago, Grand Master Arundolyn and the Master Rostam led the Knights against the monsters that poured out after Khaenri'ah fell, and Dornman Port was one of the front lines. Rostam died, and Arundolyn gave up his title and his sword.

**Varka's era.** Varka's campaigns brought Mondstadt an unusual peace. Four years ago, while he was abroad, Inspector Eroch's treachery led to Crepus Ragnvindr's death, and Diluc quit the order. Half a year before the Traveler arrived, Varka took about eighty percent of the Knights' manpower north on an expedition that eventually reached Nod-Krai.

Relations: - **Church of Favonius**: separate from the Knights but managed alongside them. Its Seneschal is Seamus Pegg, father of Jean and Barbara. Cardinal Calvin covered his duties while he was away.
- **Barbatos**: Varka, an old friend of Venti, is among the few who know Venti is the Anemo Archon. Barbatos mediated the Knights' pact with the Hexenzirkel.
- **Boreas (Andrius)**: the Knight of Boreas acts as intermediary between the Wolf of the North and Mondstadt.
- **Diluc**: a former captain who distrusts the Knights but still fights for Mondstadt. He has refused to rejoin.
- **Fatui**: relations are tense. Dottore used Eroch, and Signora's agents operated in Mondstadt.
- **Hexenzirkel**: a pact sealed at the Tripartite Conference promises Mondstadt aid in its time of greatest need.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the expedition has come home and Varka is back. He divides his time with the Favonius Keep in Nod-Krai, so Jean still runs daily affairs as Acting Grand Master.

A small garrison under Anselm holds the Keep, which also serves Nefer's Northern Intelligence Network as a post for watching Abyssal attacks. Seamus Pegg is back as Seneschal of the Church. The 5th Company's captaincy has been vacant since Adorno's death in 6.6, and Lohen remains Vice Captain. No new Knights of Favonius story developments were found for 6.7-7.1; the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

key: Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius
338.comment: Knights of Favonius: Grand Master, Master and the knightly titles
338.content: The Knights have one Grand Master. The Master is the reserve who becomes Acting Grand Master when needed, which is why people call Jean both "Master Jean" and "Acting Grand Master". The Dandelion Knight, also called the Lionfang Knight, carries Vennessa's title. Jean has held it since she was fifteen, and it is linked to the "Lion of the South" among the Four Winds. Earlier holders were Vennessa, Arundolyn (the "Lion of Light") and Valentine. The Knight of Boreas is a human knight recognised by the wolf god Boreas, who acts as intermediary between the god and the people. Known holders are the Wandering Knight, Ravenwood, Rostam and now Varka, whom Boreas judged the rightful bearer of the title in this age. As Varka put it in a letter Mika read aloud, "There are ten captains in the Knights of Favonius but only one Grand Master."

339.comment: Knights of Favonius: Companies of the Knights of Favonius
339.content:
- **1st, General Affairs**: plans the economy, regulations and city management, and prefers to recruit knights injured in front-line service. Its captain is unnamed.
- **2nd**: captained by Note. It is apparently the Garrison, with Wernher as Disciplinary Officer.
- **3rd**: captained by Skeiron. It is apparently the Vanguard, the largest company, responsible for the front lines, discipline and coordination between arms.
- **4th, Reconnaissance**: led by Captain Eula. It patrols the wilds, Dornman Port and its trade route. Mika is its surveyor.
- **5th, Ranged**: once archers, now also musketeers, providing fire support in small squads. Adorno was its captain until he died. Lohen is Vice Captain and the captaincy is vacant.
- **6th, Logistics**: led by Hertha. It runs the baggage train, resources and records, and posts bounties and requests. Its previous captain, Anselm, joined the expedition.
- **7th, Combined Arms**: a re-formed company with both ranged and melee fighters. During a limited-time event Phonia predicted that Frederica Gunnhildr would lead it, and knights now call her "Captain Frederica".
- **8th, Support**: inventions, explosives and the new muskets. It works with the 10th. Nymph is its Field Officer.
- **9th, Cavalry**: led by Kaeya; earlier captains were Diluc and Feroux. Every rider except Kaeya went on the expedition.
- **10th, Investigation**: led by Albedo. It provides alchemical inventions, investigates strange phenomena and runs remote reconnaissance. Sucrose is its assistant alchemist.

340.content: The Outriders are a special scout-archer unit of the Knights. They were founded by Amber's grandfather, a former Liyue mercenary leader who joined the Knights after a Favonius doctor saved his life. He trained every member in his archery and gliding. When he suddenly resigned and vanished four years ago, rumours spread that he had defected, and the Outriders fell apart. Amber, who joined just before he left, is now the only Outrider. She works around Mondstadt City and assists other companies. More recently she has asked Jean for unofficial helpers on patrol, but they are not Outriders.

341.content: Half a year before the Traveler arrived, Grand Master Varka led about eighty percent of the Knights' manpower north, including the elite knights and the cavalry. Seamus Pegg (who handled its paperwork), Frederica Gunnhildr (second-in-command, as stated during a limited-time event) and Mika (front-line surveyor) went with him. Varka had glimpsed a calamity in the north, and he did not know at first that it would lead to Nod-Krai. The expedition also quietly gathered wolf spirits split off from Andrius. Along the way it met Capitano, missed two Weinlesefests, and sent Mika home with a letter. For most of the Mondstadt story, the people at home know only that the Grand Master is far away. As Kaeya put it, if Varka has time to write letters, "it's probably nothing serious".

342.content: The Favonius Keep is the expeditionary force's camp in Nod-Krai's Wavechaser Plain, and its large tent smells of dandelion wine. Anselm, formerly captain of the 6th Company, supervises it and handles the administration Seamus used to do. Knights stationed there include Ekbert, Erminie, Laurent, Leifhelm, Nannina and Winfried. After Dottore's defeat, Varka kept a small garrison there by agreement with Nefer, so the outpost could also serve the Northern Intelligence Network in watching for Abyssal attacks. Varka still returns there periodically.

343.content: Eroch was a knight of Varka's generation who often criticised Varka for falling short of the chivalric code. He rose to Inspector, and Varka trusted him with Mondstadt's affairs, including the seal on Ursa the Drake, whenever the Grand Master went abroad. Envious of Varka's fame, Eroch let Dottore's Segments draw him into treason. Four years ago he woke Ursa. Crepus Ragnvindr died stopping the drake with a Delusion, and Eroch ordered Diluc to keep the truth quiet for the Knights' reputation, so Diluc resigned. Jean reported it. Varka had his inner circle investigate and gave Jean authority to act. Jean fought him in two formal duels, losing the first and winning the second decisively (as a knight recalled during a limited-time event), and Eroch was expelled. When Varka finally cornered him, Eroch killed himself, laughing. Varka's character story calls this his most devastating defeat, and in 6.4 he wrote to Diluc to apologise.

344.comment: Knights of Favonius: Knights of Favonius Handbook
344.content: The Knights of Favonius Handbook is the order's code of conduct. Jean personally edited its fifth edition. It names three virtues of knighthood, modesty, honesty and self-control, and calls them pillars of Mondstadt's freedom, since "freedom cannot exist without the support of duty". It requires knights to help citizens promptly and to greet foreign travellers courteously and without suspicion. Knights must stay ready even during breaks, must not be drunk on duty, and must never help minors drink. It even notes that Noelle has been told to report knights who try to hand their work to her.

345.comment: Knights of Favonius: Becoming a Knight of Favonius
345.content: Becoming a knight requires passing both written and practical examinations. Training can begin in childhood. Guy started at eight, learned the sword at ten and became a squire at sixteen before being knighted. Noelle has failed the selection test seven times and keeps serving as the Knights' maid. The young Varka knocked down every examiner and still got a rejection letter, because Grand Master Valentine wanted him to travel first and find his own reason for being a knight. Varka threw the letter away without reading to the end, where Valentine's postscript asked to meet him. That night he ambushed Valentine to prove a point, and over drinks afterwards he was sent abroad.

346.comment: Knights of Favonius: Knights of the cataclysm
346.content: Five hundred years ago, Grand Master Arundolyn (the Lion of Light, who had no Vision and fought with a greatsword in one hand and a longsword in the other) and his childhood friend Rostam (the Wolf Pup, Master and Knight of Boreas) led the Knights against the monsters of the cataclysm. Rostam developed Favonius Bladework, which knights still practise. He was rumoured to secretly run Kreuzlied's old anti-aristocracy society. He died after 23 years of service, and Arundolyn never fought again. Rostam's student Roland, the White Knight, became the feared Bloodstained Knight and vanished into Khaenri'ah. Varka is the only knight said to have mastered Arundolyn's dual-blade style, and even surpassed it.

347.comment: Knights of Favonius: Tripartite Conference and the Hexenzirkel pact
347.content: Before he left, Varka asked Barbatos to convene a Tripartite Conference of the Knights and Church of Favonius, the Anemo Archon, and the Hexenzirkel. There Varka talked the witches into a pact promising Mondstadt help in its time of need. Alice said she wondered whether Barbatos had been whispering lines into his ear. The witches' trial, which was part of the pact, gave Varka a fight he loved, and a glimpse of Barbeloth's scryglass showed him the coming calamity in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. Albedo invoked the pact during Durin's attack in 5.6. Varka cashed in the favour in 6.3 so that Nicole would help pull down the Frost Moon.

348.content: "Honorary Knight" is the title the Knights of Favonius gave the Traveler for helping resolve the Stormterror crisis. The Traveler is not formally a member. Knights across Teyvat, including the expedition's men in Nod-Krai, greet them by this title, and Varka had heard of the Honorary Knight before inviting them to Nod-Krai.

349.content:
Komaniya Express (also: Komaniya, Komaniya Delivery): Komaniya Express is a well-known delivery company based in Inazuma. It is widely praised for punctual and safe delivery, and it has recently begun expanding its service overseas. Its best-known employee is Kirara, a nekomata and the company's Gold Level Courier.

Business has been good enough that the company has hired more staff. Its couriers carry a logo at the waist, which Kaedehara Kazuha recognised when he met Kirara abroad.

Structure: Canon shows a simple structure: an owner or boss, couriers, a warehouse with an "Undelivered Packages" section, and a customer feedback board where clients can leave star ratings. There is a Gold Level Courier title, created for Kirara. The company has an office in Inazuma City, where customers can bring packages.

The owner is unnamed. When a customer asks for the neko courier, the owner calls Kirara over as though it were an everyday occurrence. The owner once privately offered Kirara higher pay and quieter secretarial work, which she turned down.

Leadership: The owner is not named. They are shown as supportive. Kirara's profile says they never considered letting her go, and they designed the Gold Level Courier title overnight when they heard she had delivered every parcel in the Undelivered Packages section.

Members: Kirara is the one employee canon names: a youkai (a nekomata) who loves her job and human society, and whose reputation has done much for the company.

Kirara is the sole courier handling international deliveries, because she is the quickest of the staff. She sometimes changes back into her original cat form and climbs over walls to keep to a schedule. Her profile says she takes a polite, friendly attitude with clients; customers describe her as safe, punctual and vivacious.

Goals: The company's evident aims are fast, careful delivery, customer satisfaction and growth into other nations. Kirara's own motive, which the company benefits from, is that she treats every delivery as an outing and wants to keep her job.

Methods: Couriers deliver parcels on foot and across rooftops, and ask recipients for a signature. Kirara tracks down the right recipient for stranded packages in her spare time, so the "Undelivered Packages" section of the warehouse ends up empty. Customers can rate service on a feedback board.

Bandits have tried to rob Kirara on the road, according to her Character Story. She sends them to the Tenryou Commission in packages labelled "Meanies". The company has also handled orders such as clothing between Inazuma and Fontaine.

History: **Before Kirara.** The company had a long reputation in Inazuma as the most reliable delivery service; asked which firm is most dependable, people there mention Komaniya Express first.

**Kirara joins.** After Yae Miko, the Lady Kitsune of the Grand Narukami Shrine, saw how much Kirara enjoyed the streets of Inazuma City, she recommended that she seek work at Komaniya Express. Miko's reasoning was that to blend into human society one must work like an ordinary human.

**Overseas expansion (3.7).** The company recently began delivering to other nations. Kirara's first appearances abroad are in Mondstadt, where she spoke with Diona at the Cat's Tail, and in Liyue Harbor, where she delivered to Hu Tao.

**Teyvat's Special Delivery (5.0).** In a fourth-anniversary web event, Kirara said Komaniya Express had set up temporary locations elsewhere, that orders had gone through the roof, and that she worried about delayed packages. She asked the Traveler for help delivering them across Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma.

Relations: **Yae Miko.** Kirara's mentor in human society. Miko says packages addressed to Guuji Yae at the Grand Narukami Shrine must be treated as top priority.

**Tenryou Commission.** One of the addresses Kirara knows best, since she climbed the Tenshukaku roof in her first days in Inazuma City, and it receives the bandits she delivers.

**Chiori.** An old customer in Fontaine, an Inazuman designer who dressed Kirara in her current outfit. Kirara's deliveries to Fontaine are in part deliveries to her.

**Hu Tao.** A customer in Liyue who asked whether the company could deliver living people or those in between. Kirara's tails stood on end.

Reputation: Komaniya Express is the best-regarded courier firm in Inazuma. Typical customer feedback is "safe and punctual", "service assured" and "vivacious and adorable". Kirara's tireless record has raised the firm's renown, and no package is undeliverable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Komaniya Express remains in business, now offering overseas delivery. Kirara handles all international orders.

No 6.x or 7.x story content found in this research changes the company's status.

350.comment: Komaniya Express: Kirara and the Gold Level Courier title
350.content:
When Kirara first arrived she noticed that some packages could not be delivered because of wrong addresses, moved recipients or wrong names. She quietly recorded the details and used her routes and spare time to find each recipient. The warehouse's Undelivered Packages section became empty, the owner at first thought they had been robbed, and the owner created the title Gold Level Courier for her.

Her Character Stories add that she keeps working because she likes it: at the end of a day she climbs somewhere high and listens to the market. Her fear of being fired is that she would have to return to being a wild youkai in the mountains.

351.comment: Komaniya Express: Kirara in Liyue Harbor (Summoners' Summit)
351.content: During the limited-time event Duel! The Summoners' Summit!, in Roll! A Sea of New Acquaintances, the Traveler, Paimon and Kazuha met Kirara in Liyue Harbor. She was lost on her first delivery there. She explained that Komaniya Express had just begun overseas service and that she now effectively travels the world as part of her job. She was looking for the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, where she asked Hu Tao for a signature and a five-star review.

352.content:
Korolevskiy Troupe (also: Korolevskiy Theater Troupe, Royal Troupe): The Korolevskiy Troupe is a performance company in Snezhnaya that specialises in opera, theatre, ballet and musical performance. It performs at the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnograd and is very popular, especially among the Fatui Harbingers and Mitya. Its two star performers are Odette, Prima Ballerina, and Vodyanitsa, Prima Donna. Both also have a hidden life beyond the stage.

The name is Russian for "royal". The troupe's reputation rests on its leading women, whose work critics compare with the older, more classical Snezhnayan stage tradition. A critic in the theater says their performances drop the excess of traditional grand-tragedy opera in favour of restraint and elegance. The official map description of the theatre is about the work behind the illusion: success is measured by whether the audience can be given a moment's escape into something beautiful.

Structure: Canon names no director or manager. The two top roles are Prima Ballerina (Odette) and Prima Donna (Vodyanitsa). Odette's character story shows the two principals also coordinating the programme, preparing costumes and calming nervous newcomers before their first performance. Below them are the chorus and ballet performers, who appear mostly unnamed. The wider theatre has its own stage and front-of-house staff, such as the ticket-seekers' queue, critics and local fans, but individual staff are minor.

Former members show that a career can lead out of the troupe. Dorofeya was a rising star who retired and married a nobleman. Pashkov left to become the safety officer in Svetloledovka. Violetta, Odette's mother, was an acclaimed ballerina at the theater until a fall ended her career.

Members: Odette, the Prima Ballerina, is calm, exacting and nearly expressionless on and off stage. Vodyanitsa, the Prima Donna, is a Water Imp (a Snowland fae) whose singing is said to carry an otherworldly allure; she is lively and outspoken.

Odette Spessiva comes from an old ballet family and was taught by her mother Violetta. Her admirers call her dancing precise and austere, and the press describes it as "perfection, polished to an icy sheen". Vodyanitsa is the last of her kind on the stage: the Water Imps once filled Snezhnaya's streets and stages with song, but by the time of her story most had left, and she stayed on at the Korolevskiy Theater. The two are friends and the troupe's senior figures, and few colleagues can talk freely with Odette outside a performance.

Former members named in the sources are Dorofeya, Pashkov and Violetta (see their entries). Fans and critics fill the theater's lobby. Examples are Taisiya, who admires Odette, and Zamorov, who prefers Vodyanitsa and argues with her about which of them best represents the theater. Pisemsky, a critic, appreciates both performers.

Goals: The troupe's stated purpose is performance: giving audiences a beautiful illusion, with the labour kept behind the curtain. No political aim is attributed to the troupe as an organisation. Its two leading performers have additional commitments outside the theatre (see secrets).

Methods: Its repertoire includes opera, ballet and musical shows. The classic Snezhnayan ballet Spirit Seeker is a family inheritance of the Spessivas, and Violetta carried it before Odette. Performances often run in the evening, and seats are in demand, with the theatre not selling standing tickets, taking extra chairs or allowing a draught through the doors. A related item, the Polestar Ballet Anthology, is a book about ballet in Snezhnaya.

History: Nothing is recorded about the troupe's founding. The only dated material comes from the Chapter VII period. Before the Traveler's visit, Odette and Vodyanitsa had already built their reputations: critics use their names as shorthand for the theater, and the old-style gloom of grand tragedies has given way to their sharper, cleaner shows. Violetta's earlier career is part of the troupe's past, and her injury left Odette to carry the Spessiva name forward.

Odette's father, a soldier, died suddenly, and the family lost his income. Her mother Violetta, whose career had already ended in a fall, taught her ballet, and Odette accepted Signora's offer to join the Fatui against her mother's wishes (per Violetta's page, citing her fourth character story). Vodyanitsa's story says that as the Water Imps left Snezhnograd and the city's songs faded, a thread of song was still heard from the Korolevskiy Theater, where she remained.

Relations: - **Fatui and Harbingers**: the wiki says the troupe is especially popular among Fatui Harbingers. After the Traveler's visit, Tartaglia, Arlecchino and Sandrone can be seen as audience members at the theater. Odette works for the Fatui and, per the wiki, is the favoured candidate to inherit her mentor Signora's Harbinger seat.
- **Mitya**: a notable fan of the troupe.
- **Rokot**: Odette (as Lelek) and Vodyanitsa belong to this anti-Project-Stuzha group, though neither knew the other was a member at first.

- **Critics and fans**: papers publish heated commentary at the end of each season. A critic called Tripolev wrote that Odette dances "like a dagger honed to perfection".
- **Spessiva family**: Odette's mother Violetta was a former ballerina of the theatre, and her story describes the Spessivas as a family whose stage glory had faded.

Reputation: Highly regarded, with devoted fans and a queue that never shortens. The audience praises Odette's austerity and Vodyanitsa's voice. Gossip about Odette's coldness is a running joke: one tale has a nobleman reserving a whole row and waiting two hours with a bouquet only to be told she had left by the side door. Others, including Zamorov and Taisiya, fight over which of the two stars represents the theater best.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the troupe is active at the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnograd. Odette and Vodyanitsa are both playable characters.

The Korolevskiy Theater is an open area in Everfrozen Earth with its own Meeting Point (unlocked via the world quest One Yet to Take a Bow) and a set of NPCs. Odette and Vodyanitsa appear in the theater after the Chapter VII events. Nothing further about the troupe is canon beyond 7.1.

353.content: The Korolevskiy Theater is a subarea of Everfrozen Earth in Snezhnograd where the troupe performs. Its named staff and visitors include Balkonov, Osipova, Pisemsky, Polovikova, Roshchina, Shuvalov, Taisiya, Vzdykhalov, Yadova and Zamorov. The wiki notes that the theater and the troupe may take their name from Nepla Korolevitsna, wife of the fae Filipov, though this is not confirmed.

key: One Yet to Take a Bow
354.comment: Korolevskiy Troupe: One Yet to Take a Bow
354.content: In this world quest, the Traveler hears that eerie music and a dancing shadow haunt the theater at midnight. The ghost turns out to be Odette, who is repairing a swan-shaped music box that her mother gave her as a child, at night in her private lounge because her days are full. She asks for help collecting parts and keeping it secret. Her lounge is almost bare, which suggests she gives everything to dancing. Completing the quest unlocks the theater's Meeting Point.

355.comment: Korolevskiy Troupe: Odette and Vodyanitsa as a pair
355.content: The Prima Ballerina and Prima Donna contrast in manner and stand close in friendship. Odette is quiet and dry. Vodyanitsa teases and drags her to meals. A backstage scene shows Odette giving Vodyanitsa honey candy "for your throat" and Vodyanitsa insisting that she saw Odette smile, which Odette explains away as the expression the role required. Post-quest dialogue also has Odette complain that Vodyanitsa would ambush her backstage if she skipped one of her performances.

356.content: Dorofeya was once a rising star in the troupe, grew up begging in Zolnyy before joining, worked with Violetta, still admires Odette's skill and is married to a nobleman who loves her. Pashkov left to become the new safety officer in Svetloledovka and is known for stubbornness. Violetta Spessiva was an acclaimed ballerina who inherited the classic ballet Spirit Seeker from her family; a fall ended her career and she then focused on teaching her daughter Odette. Her grief over her husband's sudden death is said in Odette's story to have led to her injury.

357.content: Spirit Seeker is a classic Snezhnayan ballet that Violetta inherited from her family. Ballet fans like to compare how Violetta and Odette dance it. A critic in the theater notes that Violetta's style leans towards absolute classical restraint, while Odette's choreography has a sense of martial restraint.

key: School of the Theory of Curiosities
358.content:
Kshahrewar (also: Kshahrewar Darshan, School of Technology, School of the Theory of Curiosities, Darshan of Technology): Kshahrewar is the Sumeru Akademiya's Darshan of technology. It covers mechanisms, architecture and puzzle-solving, and its colour is white with a lion on its crest. Its sage is Firnas. It built much of Sumeru City, but it has been underfunded since the loss of its greatest scholar, Pir Kavikavus. Its best-known graduate is the architect Kaveh, the Light of Kshahrewar.

Kshahrewar's designs shape ordinary life: a cheap single-storey house plan that serves as a template across the city, and loom designs behind Sumeru's textile industry. Most people never notice the theory behind these. The Darshan also studies King Deshret's ancient technology, which it has not yet explained.

Structure: Kshahrewar is one of the Six Darshans, with one Great Sage. According to the receptionist Sitt, it began as a school for studying and building propulsion mechanisms, and its scope grew because making machines draws on many kinds of knowledge. Its disciplines now include architecture, mechanical skills and puzzle-solving. Members are students, researchers and teachers. Many scholars are serious about sculpting as a hobby, Firnas says.

Funding comes from the Akademiya's allocation and from private contracts. Dori, the merchant known as Lord Sangemah Bay, supplies Mora in return for the Darshan's technology and craftsmanship. A Kshahrewar researcher helped Aaru Village build the White Lift into its stepwell. The name "Kshahrewar Lift" was proposed, but because relations between the desert peoples and the Akademiya were prickly, the villagers settled on "White Lift", after the Darshan's colour.

Leadership: Firnas is the current Kshahrewar Sage. He reasons like an engineer, comparing crises to faulty machines. His predecessor was removed after the Akademiya-Fatui plot.

Hosseini, in the 2.7 event A Muddy Bizarre Adventure, mentions "our great tutor Firnas". In 6.6 Firnas is one of the six sages gathered at Caravan Ribat. He judged that the Irminsul anomaly resembled a malfunctioning machine and spoke of stress fractures. At Aaru Village he reported on the Jinn breaching the defences and helped move the villagers north. He later judged the Temple of Silence plan sound with manageable risk.

Members: Kaveh is the Darshan's most celebrated alumnus: a Kshahrewar graduate with honours, the architect of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, and known as the Light of Kshahrewar. His mother Faranak graduated from Kshahrewar and was a famous architect too. Faruzan is a Haravatat professor, but her theories underpin the Darshan's mechanics. She also studied there for a time. Alhaitham's grandmother was a Kshahrewar scholar who raised him. Jazari is a researcher who wants to follow Kavikavus and win the Pir Kavikavus Prize.

Alkami, a Kshahrewar senior of Kaveh's, runs a training centre. Zaha Hadi is a veteran teacher of many students. Others the wiki lists include Anis, Ashvapati, Atashye, Daneshvar, Daya, Dzenana, Fawara, Goli, Judar, Kashif, Marwa, Moseis, Narendra, Naysaburi, Pharez, Piyush, Sasani and Vinayak, but little is known about most of them.

Goals: Kshahrewar wants to design and improve working things: buildings, looms, machinery and ancient mechanisms. Its scholars also want to revive their school's standing. Jazari hopes the rediscovery of Kavikavus' work will do that. The wiki says that, likely because of the accident, the Darshan came to advocate strict control over machines and technology, and a forum poster says those above wanted a stable, peaceful society.

Methods: Kshahrewar proceeds by building and testing. Its people design from low-cost, adaptable templates and tune looms to make cloth faster while preserving its beauty. Over the last century they have used Faruzan's manuscripts to establish the fundamentals of mechanics and have more recently developed their own mechanism theories. Cyno's profile jokes that the General Mahamatra works harder than the "Great Vayuvyastra", a machine made by Kshahrewar. Jazari says his school is concerned only with genuine techniques.

History: **Pir Kavikavus.** A prodigy who joined some time after the cataclysm 500 years ago, Kavikavus became a Herbad before thirty. He was friends with the Aranara Aralohita. He was the last person recorded to enter the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain for systematic research. In an accident his research was lost and he likely died. Since then Kshahrewar has been regarded as in decline, with no raise in funding and no major breakthroughs. The Akademiya's prize for outstanding young scholars bears his name.

**The 3.0 revival.** In Vimana Agama and Until Vana is Healed, the Traveler and Paimon helped Jazari recover one of Kavikavus' papers, hidden behind Aralohita's puzzles. Jazari used it to seal the Golem's Chaos Core, which weakened the Abyss Mages and reduced the Abyss Order's threat to the forest. He called it the first breakthrough of its kind in many years.
**The sages' plot (3.0-3.2).** Kshahrewar's sage backed Azar and Dottore and was removed. After Scaramouche fell, Alhaitham told Kaveh and the Traveler that the Kshahrewar and Haravatat seats needed new sages, and said the first thing he would do as Acting Grand Sage was reject Kshahrewar's funding application. Firnas later took the seat.

Relations: - **Haravatat**: Kshahrewar built its mechanics on Haravatat's old work, notably Faruzan's. Faruzan says Kshahrewar tried to recruit her, with more students and a bigger budget.
- **Dori**: the merchant lends Mora to Kshahrewar and to Kaveh. Dori says they signed a private contract: she has the Mora, they have the technology.
- **Tighnari's view**: he called Kshahrewar and Spantamad researchers quite prejudiced, so he would not trust them with a delicate matter.

- **The Akademiya**: it never raised Kshahrewar's funding after Kavikavus, and it favours strict control over machines. Alhaitham jokes that he would deny its funding request.
- **Alhaitham and Kaveh**: Kaveh is the Darshan's representative in Alhaitham's eyes, and the two former students have a complicated relationship.
- **Aaru Village**: a former Kshahrewar researcher helped build the White Lift.

Reputation: Kshahrewar is respected for its builders but short of money. Students treat Kaveh as a role model and speculate about him at the Palace of Alcazarzaray. Others note that few genius architects of Kshahrewar find happiness, as Zaha Hadi says. Faruzan calls the school's scholars "freeloaders" for using her manuscripts. Alkami's training centre used Kaveh's fame as the Light of Kshahrewar to attract students, a scheme that turned out to be a ruse.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Firnas is the Sage. The Darshan remains underfunded, and no Kshahrewar-specific story was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

Its scholars were involved in the 6.6 Irminsul and Akasha work. The 7.0 and 7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya and do not involve the Darshans.

359.content: Firnas is the Kshahrewar Sage, appointed after the previous sage fell with Azar. Earlier, Hosseini called him a "great tutor" in an event. In 6.6, at Caravan Ribat and the Temple of Silence, he approached the crisis like an engineer: the anomaly looked like a malfunctioning machine, not an outside attack, and he warned of supply problems on a move to the desert. He also remarked on sculpting among Kshahrewar scholars and asked Faruzan whether she had once studied in his Darshan.

360.content: Pir Kavikavus was a Kshahrewar prodigy who joined some time after the cataclysm, reached the rank of Herbad before thirty, and was friends with the Aranara Aralohita. While investigating the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain, an accident destroyed his research and he likely died. Aralohita saved some of his work behind puzzles. In 3.0, Jazari used a recovered paper to seal the Golem's Chaos Core. The prize that honours him goes to a scholar under forty with groundbreaking research.

361.content: Jazari is a Kshahrewar researcher who worries about money and hopes to follow Kavikavus in studying the Ruin Golem. In Vimana Agama he tells the Traveler about Kavikavus and says Kshahrewar is concerned only with genuine techniques. In Until Vana is Healed he uses Kavikavus' rediscovered paper to seal the Chaos Core and hopes this revives Kshahrewar.

362.content: Alkami, a Kshahrewar senior, runs a training centre for those who could not enrol in the Akademiya. In Kaveh's Hangout Event, he offers Kaveh a generous per-session fee to teach there. It turns out that he wants Kaveh's fame as the Light of Kshahrewar to boost enrolment, since he is not a talented architect himself. Kaveh suspects that the Akademiya does not know of such centres, and that, with all the necessary permits, they would not act even if it did.

363.content: During the limited-time event A Parade of Providence (3.6), Kaveh represented Kshahrewar in the Akademiya Extravaganza's Interdarshan Championship. He said King Deshret's technology is still not fully understood and Kshahrewar has many differing opinions about it. The wiki adds that Kaveh bought a machine core excavated from King Deshret's ruins and used it, modified, in an automated case, Mehrak.

key: the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission
364.content:
Kujou Clan (also: Kujou family, House Kujou, the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission, Kujou-ke): The Kujou Clan is one of Inazuma's three great families and the head of the Tenryou Commission, the Raiden Shogun's executive arm for security and the army. It is regarded as the most loyal and powerful of the families supporting the Shogun's rule. During the Vision Hunt Decree the Kujou enforced the Shogun's order to seize Visions, through the general Kujou Sara. Its head, Kujou Takayuki, was then exposed as having worked with the Fatui for his own gain. His younger son Kujou Kamaji now leads the clan as acting head. Its estate stands next to Tenshukaku.

The clan counts three generations of difficulty in this period: Takayuki's disgrace, the Shogun's postponement of its punishment, and the rival Takatsukasa waiting to replace it. Its members are not of one mind. Several of them doubted the decree while carrying it out.

Structure: The clan head is also the Tenryou Commissioner. Under him the family splits duties: Kujou Masahito commands the Shogun's Army at the Kujou Encampment on the Kannazuka front, Kamaji handles the Commission's civil business in Inazuma City, and Kujou Sara leads the Commission's forces as a general. Shogunate samurai, yoriki and doushin serve beneath them, and the Takatsukasa Clan supports the Kujou in running the Commission. Kujou retainers and security staff are called the clan's own guard.

Named Tenryou personnel include Okawara Goemon (chief samurai and head of Kujou Clan security), Toranosuke (a Shogunate officer), Yasutake (quartermaster), and Shikanoin Heizou, a Tenryou "detective" among the doushin. Iwakura Michihiro, founder of the Iwakura Art sword style, once became the clan's sword instructor with the title Douin, according to the wiki's history. Staff directly attached to the family include Ikeda Soushirou (retainer) and Ippei, Kamaji's servant.

Leadership: Kujou Takayuki, the former head, is under house arrest. Kujou Kamaji is acting head and Tenryou Commissioner in his place. Masahito and Sara serve as generals.

Takayuki was proud and rigid, loyal to the family's influence above all else. Kamaji is an earnest, self-doubting official who has questioned the Shogun's policies privately but never found anyone to tell. Masahito is a soldier who thinks the war can no longer be won cleanly. Sara is the Shogun's most devoted general.

Takayuki had two sons, Masahito and Kamaji, and adopted Sara after finding her unconscious with a Vision. He used her as a weapon to raise the clan's standing, as Kamisato Ayato puts it in a voice-over, and lost the ability to control her when she learned the truth. Kamaji's relationship with Sara is warm, and Sara says he is the only one who treated her as a real sister. After Takayuki's collapse Masahito, the eldest, could have taken the headship but gave it to Kamaji, whom he judged fitter, and promised to support him as a warrior. Kamaji is also in love with Hiiragi Chisato of the Hiiragi Clan.

Members: Kujou Takayuki (former head), Kujou Masahito (general), Kujou Kamaji (acting head), and Kujou Sara (adopted daughter, general). Kujou Shigeyori is the clan's founding-era ancestor.

**Kujou Takayuki** was a tall, thin elderly man who held the Tenryou Commissioner's post until his dealings with the Fatui came out in Omnipresence Over Mortals. The Shogun was angry at the extent of his deceit, and he seemed to age overnight, losing his will and his position. **Kujou Masahito** is stationed at the Kujou Encampment, from which he commands the Kannazuka troops. He sent his father a warning about the Tatarigami growing stronger on Yashiori Island, was scolded, and the investigation team Takayuki sent went missing. **Kujou Kamaji** is the younger son, in charge of the Commission's government business in Inazuma City. **Kujou Sara** is a tengu who was adopted as a child; she is Electro, uses a bow, and holds the title Devotee of the Divine. Her entry holds her story.

Goals: Protect the Shogun's rule and keep Inazuma secure. Under Takayuki this meant enforcing the Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees and protecting the clan's influence. After his fall the surviving Kujou have a narrower goal: to keep the Tenryou Commission from passing to the Takatsukasa and to earn back the Shogun's trust. Kamaji said in the duel that he accepted the clan's decline as punishment for doubting without acting.

Methods: The Tenryou Commission uses armed force and police authority: patrols, the Shogun's Army, the police station, and investigations led by officers such as Heizou. Sara trains hard, leads from the front, forbade harming civilians in carrying out the decree, and personally tends the wounded after battle. The wiki records, however, that the Commission suffered a high desertion rate, because soldiers were forced to fight people instead of the monsters they expected.

History: **Founding era.** The clan's origins are unknown. Shigeyori built the Kujou Encampment on the Kannazuka front during the cataclysm. After the cataclysm Ei founded the Tri-Commission, and the Kujou Clan came to head the Tenryou Commission.

**The Vision Hunt (Chapter II, 2.0).** Under pressure from the Fatui and its own clan head, the Tenryou Commission enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. A protester challenged the Shogun before the throne and lost to Sara; his friend Kaedehara Kazuha took the Vision and fled. Sara also took Arataki Itto's Geo Vision, according to her wiki profile. When the Traveler was named a wanted criminal after the ceremony at the Statue of the Omnipresent God, Sara led the Shogun's Army against the Watatsumi resistance. She proposed a ceremonial fight of honour and the Traveler won; the resistance's reinforcements then turned the battle and Sara ordered a retreat. Takayuki's falsified reports and Fatui letters were later found with help from the Kamisato clan and presented to Sara, who confronted her father. The Traveler defeated Signora, but Sara lost to her first. Ei ended the decree.

Relations: - **Raiden Shogun**: the sworn lord. Ei decided to give the clan more time because it showed honour in Kamaji.
- **Takatsukasa Clan**: a long-time supporter and rival. Its members tried to take over the Commission after Takayuki's fall, and the Kujou were nearly forced to sign a confession.
- **Kamisato Clan and the Yashiro Commission**: the other major commission family. In the Archon Quest the Yashiro Commission gathered the evidence that exposed Takayuki. Sara respects Ayaka and has always hoped to call on her.
- **Hiiragi Clan and the Kanjou Commission**: Kamaji's love Chisato leads it as acting head.
- **Fatui**: Takayuki dealt with them and then lost his post. Sara, who was devoted to the Shogun, was among those hurt most by his betrayal.
- **Watatsumi Army**: opponents in the civil war, later a ceasefire. Sara called the resistance's leader Kokomi a worthy opponent in her own words, while Kokomi says Sara's loyalty and sincerity is admirable.

Reputation: The Kujou were considered the most loyal and powerful of the Shogun's families, but the Vision Hunt Decree made the Tenryou Commission hated by many ordinary people. Soldiers admire Sara and Masahito. Kamaji is thought a decent but unremarkable heir; Ei said he "is not a great descendant" but his honour is admirable, according to the wiki.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Kujou Clan still heads the Tenryou Commission under acting head Kamaji. Takayuki remains under house arrest awaiting punishment, and the Shogun has postponed any ruling on the clan. Masahito and Sara continue to lead the Shogun's forces.

365.content: The Tenryou Commission ("Bugyou of the Shogun's Domain") is the Tri-Commission's executive arm, responsible for public security and military affairs. It enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and, with the Kanjou Commission, the Sakoku Decree, and posts notices on Inazuma's bulletin boards. It is led by the Kujou Clan and uses Shogunate samurai, yoriki and doushin. Sara, Masahito and Kamaji serve as its leaders. Its rank structure includes police and detectives such as Heizou, and its headquarters stands in Inazuma City beside Tenshukaku. The Commission has a high desertion rate and was in disarray after Takayuki's removal.

366.content: The Takatsukasa have served the Kujou for generations and support them in heading the Tenryou Commission, but the two clans have long been at odds over its leadership. The head is Takatsukasa Susumu. His younger brother Isamu was the police station head and was murdered; Isamu's daughter is Takatsukasa Chika. After Takayuki's fall, Takatsukasa members tried to oust the Kujou by coercing Kamaji into signing a confession that painted themselves favourably, using a hidden mountain base on Mt. Yougou. Ei ended the matter in To Hear Mortal Hearts, and the clan abandoned the base. In the name, takatsukasa means "master of falconry".

367.content: The Kujou Encampment is a fortress at the front line in Kannazuka, said to have been built by Kujou Shigeyori in a single night in the age of the cataclysm. During the civil war Kujou Masahito commanded the Shogun's troops there. He thought the war was a stalemate that either side could win if it dragged on. After the ceasefire he predicted that any peace would be short-lived.

368.comment: Kujou Clan: Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui
368.content: Takayuki agreed to advance the Vision Hunt Decree so that the Fatui could sell Delusions, in return for power, wanting to keep his clan's influence and believing the Fatui would be no match for the Shogun. He sent the Shogun optimistic, false reports of the war. Yae Miko planned to turn Sara against the Tenryou Commission by proving this. With help from Ayaka, Thoma, Yoimiya and the ninja Sayu, the Traveler obtained his falsified report and the Fatui letters. Sara read them and confronted him; he confirmed it and gave selfish reasons. After this, the Shogun was displeased; he aged overnight and lost his post. He is now under house arrest.

369.comment: Kujou Clan: Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato
369.content: Kamaji is Takayuki's younger son and runs the Commission's civil business in Inazuma City. In Chapter II, Chisato asks the Traveler to take a letter to him; she calls him her love and the two begin writing. In the Cypressus Custos Chapter (2.6), a marriage between them is announced. Kamaji says Chisato proposed first, but she tells the Traveler she never sent a letter. Ayato suspects a plot by the Kanjou Commission's plotters to use the match, and resolves it with the Traveler's help. Chisato asserts her own authority at the end.

370.comment: Kujou Clan: Kujou Sara and the Kujou family
370.content: Sara is a tengu who was found unconscious by the roadside, a Vision in her hand, after being thrown from a cliff while fighting monsters near her mountain home. Takayuki saw her as a child sent by heaven, named her Sara and raised her as a soldier. She is grateful to him but knows he does not look at her as he does Kamaji; Kamaji is the one who treats her as family. She believes the Shogun saved her life by granting the Vision. Soldiers first thought she was a boy when she began to train young, and one punishment from Takayuki taught her to keep a distance from others.

371.content:
Lawrence Clan (also: House Lawrence, the Lawrence family, Lawrence noble family, Glacial Seal): The Lawrence Clan was the foremost noble house of Mondstadt's aristocracy. It began as hardy frontier survivors, grew into arrogant rulers and, about a thousand years ago, was deposed by Vennessa's rebellion and driven out of the city. Its descendants still live in Mondstadt, where the name draws hostility. The best-known member today is Eula, who left the clan's ways behind and serves in the Knights of Favonius.

The clan's emblem is the Glacial Seal, which stands for a cold, composed, unshaken character. Eula now carries it. The Lawrences are counted among Mondstadt's historic great clans with the Gunnhildrs, Imunlaukrs and, later, the Ragnvindrs, but only the Lawrences are remembered as tyrants.

History: **Before Mondstadt.** The clan lived outside Decarabian's city and survived the frozen wilderness as pioneers, which led them to think of themselves as conquerors. **Early aristocracy.** When Barbatos refounded Mondstadt, the clan's leader Venerare had a statue of him raised in the plaza, inscribed with an oath from the leaders of all the clans. In this period the clan's nobles hunted to show their strength and shared the spoils with the people, and royal mages kept the history and taught virtue. **Late aristocracy.** The Lawrences' view of themselves slid from conquerors to overlords to kings. They tore down the statue, the mages abandoned their duties, and the gladiatorial games became bloodsport. A thousand years ago they were effectively rulers of Mondstadt City. Vennessa, an enslaved gladiator, rose against them with Barbatos' help, and the clan was overthrown and forced to leave the city for good.

**Details of the decline.** The late nobles held that only swords were fit for them and that bows and spears were for commoners and gladiators, abandoning the bow heritage of their hunting ancestors. In the manga, Lord Lawrence took Vennessa's refugee tribe in and then enslaved it, and his son Barca was offended by Vennessa at Ludi Harpastum, which led to her forced entry into the arena. Venti's Character Story adds that Barbatos forged a document selling Mondstadt to Morax, so the clan's soldiers, fearing slavery themselves, switched to Vennessa's side. **The traitor in the ranks.** One Lawrence, later called Kreuzlied, turned on his family and joined the Wanderer's Troupe in its failed attack on the city. He was spared severe punishment because of his birth and later founded an underground society that helped Vennessa. Some exiled nobles in later years came to see that the clan had betrayed the people, not the reverse.

Members: Known members: Venerare (early leader), Lord Lawrence and his son Barca (a thousand years ago, manga), Kreuzlied (disowned), and in the present Eula, her uncle Schubert and her cousin Lessig. Eula is the only playable one.

Eula carries the Glacial Seal, yet she has chosen to be a Knight of Favonius and is called a traitor by many Lawrences. Schubert, her uncle, is haughty and certain that Mondstadt has fallen into disorder without nobles. Lessig, her cousin, is a young man who once set off on his own to restore the family's honour.

Goals: The clan's later generations cling to the dream of recovering Mondstadt and its former glory, and they raise children to fit the rule they feel entitled to. Individuals who give up that dream, as Eula has, are rare.

Methods: Historically the clan ruled by force of arms and by the arena. Today it has no power, so it relies on pride, etiquette and discipline and, in one case, secret alliance with outsiders. Schubert plotted with the Fatui to take Mondstadt back, regardless of the harm to ordinary people.

Culture: The clan puts great stress on looking noble in the eyes of commoners. Children are taught by the best tutors available in combat, dance, cooking and etiquette, under a regimen most would call abusive. Art is called the clan's "second soul". In battle a Lawrence must appear refined and unshaken, and being knocked down or frozen is thought shameful.

**Dance.** The Dance of Sacrifice is a noble ritual whose third act, Flickering Candlelight, belongs to the Lawrences. It is a solo passed to the eldest daughter, and bleeding toes were once a point of honour. Because the clan lacked dancers to teach it, it was dropped from the curriculum and is now an artistic pastime. **Food.** Since they refused to trust commoners to cook, they trained to cook for themselves with severe penalties for mistakes. This produced dishes of high quality, such as Eula's modified Stormcrest Pie, now a local favourite as Moon Pie. They also like Gebratenes Fleisch mit Sauerkraut, a very sour dish. **Speech.** Forms of address are strictly graded: "dear friend" is for acquaintances and would estrange someone close, while "good friend" is considered offensive. Commoners who offended a noble were expected to kneel, apologise swiftly and not stare. Teaching these rules to outsiders is forbidden.

Reputation: Ordinary Mondstadters hold the clan in poor regard and some become aggressive at the mere mention of the name. Descendants are treated as a social threat. Before joining the Knights, Eula said, almost every shop refused her money, so she hunted and cooked for herself. When clan members clashed with locals, the Knights arrived to mediate, with little effect.

Not every Lawrence fits the stereotype. The wiki notes that about once a generation someone rises above the family's narcissism and earns respect on their own merits. Eula is the example most Mondstadters know.

Relations: - **Mondstadt Aristocracy**: the Lawrences were its foremost clan.
- **Gunnhildr, Imunlaukr and Ragnvindr Clans**: other great clans. Uncorrupted houses such as the Gunnhildrs stayed after the rebellion, while the Lawrences were driven out.
- **Wanderer's Troupe**: Kreuzlied, a disowned Lawrence, was its last known member. The troupe's attack on the city failed.
- **Knights of Favonius**: the order replaced noble rule. Varka and Jean allowed Eula to join despite the uproar, since her combat skill was too valuable to waste.
- **Fatui**: Schubert called them ruffians but treated them as useful business partners.

When Eula applied to the Knights, Lawrences confronted her outside the headquarters and then denounced her as a traitor. Common folk also objected to her joining. The Knights accepted her anyway.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan has no power and no known home. Eula serves as a Knights of Favonius captain, and many of her family regard her as a traitor.

Schubert was taken into custody after the plot with the Fatui failed. Lessig gave up his wild plans and decided to return to Mondstadt, wanting a city where people do not fear his family. No new Lawrence Clan story was found for 6.0 to 7.1.

372.content: The Glacial Seal is the symbol of the Lawrence Clan. It represents the clan's temper since the early days of Mondstadt: cold and unsullied, undaunted by flame, composed in every circumstance. Its mark appears on weapons and artifacts of the Royal Series and Noblesse Oblige and on Eula's namecard. Eula currently carries it.

373.content: Schubert Lawrence, Eula's uncle, believed present-day Mondstadt had fallen into ruin for lack of noble oversight. In The Spindrift Shall Never Return to the Sea he secretly worked with the Fatui to restore proper rule, indifferent to civilian risk. He is easily flattered, and being praised lowers his guard. The Traveler and Eula foiled the plan, and he was taken into custody. Eula found it disgusting, but also surprising, since she had known the other nobles as people who complained and did nothing.

374.content: Lessig, Eula's cousin, appeared in the limited-time event Secret Summer Paradise. Having heard of a way to restore the clan's honour, he went to Sumeru through Liyue and found that nobody knew or cared about his name. He lost his wallet, lived rough and ended up at the Veluriyam Mirage, where he tried to fix things and made them worse. When the Traveler, Collei and Eula found him he thought Eula had come to drag him home. Instead he said he wanted a Mondstadt where people did not fear him and decided to return, realising Eula had seen the truth before the rest of the clan. Eula offered to help him tell his parents.

375.content: Venerare led the Lawrence Clan when new Mondstadt was founded. She guided the people to build the first statue of Barbatos in the plaza, with an oath inscribed by the leaders of all the clans. Her descendants in the late aristocracy tore the statue down, so the oath was lost and does not appear on the rebuilt statue. A book says she helped Leonard reach Pilos Peak, though how the two were related is unclear.

376.content: Kreuzlied was born a Lawrence and turned against the clan; he was disowned. He joined the Wanderer's Troupe as its last known member, wielding the greatsword The Bell, and after the troupe's failed uprising was spared severe punishment because of his privileged birth. He then founded an underground society against the aristocracy, which later aided Vennessa. His real name and fate are unknown. Weapon lore calls him a traitor and outcast from the ruling Lawrences.

377.content:
Legion of Soulblazers (also: Soulblazers, the Legion of Soulblazers, the Legion): The Legion of Soulblazers is a loose group of friends and pen pals led by Varesa of Natlan. Members come from several nations and began as a comic-book fan club. They are devoted to The Soulblazer Saga, a comic series about Natlan's fight against the Abyss, and treat its hero Fietena as a role model. Varesa says the group's real aim is to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes. It appears only in the limited-time event Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey (6.2).

Before that event the members had never met in person. They kept in touch by writing letters and trading illustrations. The Traveler and Paimon join the Legion during the event and take the group's oath. The Legion has no known base, charter or official standing in any nation; it is a club of friends.

Structure: There is no formal hierarchy beyond a captain. Varesa is the captain. Xilonen is called vice captain during the event, a title she says she ended up with without quite agreeing to it. She is standing in for her pen-pal-turned-student Nepecha and says she is not a member of the fan club herself. Alrani calls Varesa "Captain" and often speaks for the group, and Tang Yigang jokes that her camp duty, logistics, is the easiest job. New members are sworn in with a short ceremony that uses a mask of Fietena as the relic and a shouted oath.

The group works as a pen-pal network first and an in-person team second. Members keep one another informed by letter and swap drawings and props. The one meeting shown on screen is the Dragonspine event, which was arranged around Minnie's suggestion. In that meeting the Legion enters a four-person relay, so it also functions as a sports team with a captain, a vice captain and runners.

Leadership: Varesa is the captain: a cheerful, huge-appetited competitor from the Collective of Plenty who trains with her coach Iansan. She leads by enthusiasm, sets the training plans for the race, and takes personal responsibility for her teammates, saying she feels powerless as their captain when Minnie's parents press her to quit. Xilonen, the vice captain, is the practical one. She keeps the group's training sensible, notices when a teammate is hiding something, and steps in when words are needed.

Varesa's leadership style is built on her hero Fietena: persist, stay cheerful, never give up on a dream. Xilonen uses a quieter style of care. She asks direct questions and offers rest before pushing harder. The two split the work in the event. Varesa is the motivator, and Xilonen mediates with outsiders such as Minnie's parents.

Members: - **Varesa**: captain; from Natlan's Collective of Plenty.
- **Alrani**: a student at the Sumeru Akademiya who is still writing her thesis. She is the group's most formal speaker and runs the oath.
- **Tang Yigang**: from Liyue. Dramatic, easily excited about the Saga, and prone to catching colds on the cold mountain.
- **Minnie**: from Mondstadt. A young artist and prop maker who suggested the Dragonspine meetup. Her parents worry about her health and her plans.
- **Nepecha**: a girl in Natlan's Children of Echoes tribe, not present at the event because she is unfit for extreme sports. Xilonen represents her.
- **Traveler and Paimon**: inducted during the event.

Members are tied together by letters. Varesa, who met Minnie only in writing, hugged and lifted her in greeting when they first met in person, which Xilonen teasingly said was an odd first impression. Xilonen is Nepecha's teacher and, in her words, something like family. Minnie's mask and artwork of Fietena travelled to Natlan through Nepecha and became well known in the Collective of Plenty.

Goals: The Legion exists to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes, in Varesa's words. The members read and discuss comics together, eat together and support one another.

The comic fandom was the original bond. The tenets they recite come straight from the Saga: peace is not won by tears and strong words alone, and fighters should be ready to give everything even when the cause may fail. Their motto asks them to meet pain and defeat without fear and to keep championing love and imagination. In practice the Legion's goals are mostly personal. It backs Minnie's wish to work in comics and gets her to the finish line of the race.

Methods: Members write letters, trade illustrations and share copies of the comics, handing spare volumes to newcomers. In person they discuss the series, eat large meals, rest and train together. They recruit by lending out comics and inviting people in, and they swear in members in a ceremony that uses a Fietena mask as a relic and a shouted oath.

Quoting the series is a core habit. Alrani says she knows every line in the Saga across the whole Soulblazer universe, and Varesa brings Fietena lines into everyday talk (about meals, about courage). The group is also good at taking up a cause together: in the event they plan the race, rally behind Minnie, and give the Traveler a place on the relay at the last moment.

History: **Origins.** The Legion of Soulblazers began when a few comic readers from different nations started writing to one another. Canon does not name a founder or give a date. Its members stayed pen pals for some time and never met face to face.

**The Dragonspine meeting.** At Minnie's suggestion the members agreed to meet in Mondstadt and enter the Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge, a contest organised jointly by the Knights of Favonius and representatives from Springvale. Varesa, Alrani, Tang Yigang and Xilonen came from abroad, and Minnie took part from her home city.

**Joining the Traveler.** In the event's first part, the Traveler and Paimon meet the group at its Natlanese camp, where Alrani and Tang Yigang bombard them with quotes. Xilonen explains that the Legion is basically a comic-book fan club. After reading the volume of the Saga they were lent, the Traveler and Paimon accept Varesa's invitation, wear a Fietena mask and swear the oath.

**Training and the deal.** During training, Minnie reveals she has made a deal with her parents: if her team gets ranked, they must take her wishes seriously. Her parents later confront her in person, and Xilonen settles the argument with a group painting made by Nepecha and her friends back home. Minnie's parents let her race but ask her to sleep at home at night.

**The race.** Tang Yigang falls ill on race day and the Traveler takes his place in a relay. The order is Xilonen, the Traveler, Varesa and Minnie. Minnie stops on the last leg to help an injured Inazuman contestant, so the team finishes late and misses a medal. The organising committee still recognises her effort, and her father agrees to let her travel abroad as long as she is careful.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: the Knights, through Amber and Field Officer Heinz, help organise the contest. The Legion visits the Knights' headquarters and library, where Lisa is friendly toward them.
- **Yae Publishing House**: publishes The Soulblazer Saga. Yae Miko rewards the fandom with free first-edition volumes.
- **Collective of Plenty and Children of Echoes**: Varesa comes from the first and Nepecha lives in the second. Xilonen, who fought for the Children of Echoes, travels with the Legion.
- **Iansan**: Varesa's coach, whose advice on food and pacing she repeats to her teammates.

Status as of 7.1: The Legion is last seen at the end of the 6.2 event, with Minnie free to travel and the group still in touch. It has not been mentioned again in anything checked through 7.1.

Nothing suggests the Legion has been dissolved. Varesa remains its captain and still appears as a playable character, but no later quest or event features the group.

378.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: The Soulblazer Saga
378.content:
The Soulblazer Saga is a long-running comic series, published by Yae Publishing House, that dramatises Natlan's struggle against the Abyss during the Cataclysm. Varesa says it runs to 12 volumes, with other comic series focused on the Pyro Archon, and that its characters are based on real people although it is mostly meant as entertainment, not history. The hero is Fietena, a rookie warrior who grows into a commander and survives a period of disillusionment, with friends such as Wanjiru and Mavuika at her side. In volume 2, as shown in the event, Fietena goes into her first battle with Mavuika and the others, with the Pyro Archon confronting the monsters' leader while the rest deal with the minions. Fietena wears five different masks in the story. Varesa's own combat mask is modelled on one of them, and a different one serves as the oath relic. The wider franchise has merchandise such as badges, notepaper and figures.

Quotations from the Saga are the group's shared language. Volume 6, Shadow of Tenebrium, is the source of the Legion's two tenets. Volume 3 supplies a line about proving doubters wrong. In-world, the real Fietena was a Collective of Plenty warrior and renowned wrestler who married into the Flower-Feather Clan, a point covered under Fietena's own entry.

379.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: Legion oath and tenets
379.content: Members swear a short oath by shouting it aloud, which Varesa says is about believing in something enough to shout it for the world to hear. The wording used in the event vows never to fear pain and defeat and to always champion love and imagination. The two founding tenets are taken from the Saga: that tears and strong words alone will not broker peace, and that the Soulblazer will give their life fighting darkness even if the fight is in vain. The oath is taken while holding a mask of Fietena as a relic. Varesa picks the mask Fietena wore when she returned to the fight after her darkest period.

380.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge
380.content: The Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge is the contest at the heart of Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey. Teams from Natlan, Sumeru, Inazuma, Liyue and Mondstadt compete in a relay over Dragonspine's marked course in cold, snowy weather. The Knights of Favonius, represented by Amber and Heinz, handle registration and security, while a Springvale group referees and supports. The Legion enters a four-person team. Its runners are Xilonen, the Traveler, Varesa and Minnie, after Tang Yigang falls ill. Draff announces the teams. The Legion helps an injured Inazuman runner, loses time and misses a medal.

381.content: Minnie is the Mondstadt member of the Legion. She is an artist and prop maker, Nepecha's long-time pen pal, and the one who proposed the Dragonspine meeting. She is a young member of the group and a local of Mondstadt, where her older brother Patton works at the tavern and her parents want her to choose a safer career. She hopes to work in the comic industry, and she made a deal with her parents that a ranked result in the race would make them take her seriously. She is thoughtful, anxious about letting teammates down, and keen to rest properly when Xilonen insists. During the race she stops to help an injured rival, which costs her team a medal. Her parents allow her to travel afterwards, subject to caution.

382.comment: Legion of Soulblazers: Nepecha and the Legion
382.content: Nepecha is a member of the Legion who stays in Natlan. She is a girl from the Children of Echoes, and Xilonen is her teacher and something like family. She and Minnie are pen pals, and Xilonen says Nepecha praises Minnie as an artist and as a source of life advice. Nepecha wanted to join the Dragonspine event but is not fit for extreme sports, so she asked Xilonen to attend in her place. She had friends from the tribe contribute to a group painting for Minnie, which Xilonen delivers early to help persuade Minnie's parents.

383.content:
Lightkeepers (also: the Lightkeepers, Lightkeeper, Ratniki, Warriors of the Nightingale): The Lightkeepers are Nod-Krai's militia against the Wild Hunt, the Abyssal host that has haunted the borderland since the Cataclysm. Solovei the Torchforger founded them about 500 years ago, and a royal edict from Snezhnaya made Nod-Krai an autonomous region under their protection. They are led by a Starshyna, currently Nikita, from the fortress-city of Piramida. Their fighters are called Ratniki, and every one of them carries an Oath Lantern. Their emblem is a nightingale holding a burning wick in its beak.

They are volunteers, chronically short of people, and proud of it. In their own words they "shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains". Playable members are Flins and Illuga.

Structure: - **Starshyna**: the single leader, based in Piramida.
- **Sergeant Majors** (sometimes addressed as Captains): each is responsible for an area of Nod-Krai and coordinates its squad leaders.
- **Squad Leaders**: command a squad, marked by a special brooch on the left lapel of the uniform.
- **Ratniki** (singular Ratnik): the ordinary fighting members.
Every Ratnik carries an Oath Lantern, which lets other Lightkeepers and the Starshyna detect where they are. Members disabled by injury may be moved to other posts if they want to keep serving. Disobeying direct orders brings real trouble. There are also non-combat staff such as doctors and a blacksmith.

Known squads include the investigation squads "Nightmare Orioles" (now led by Illuga and posted at Kipumaki Cliff), "Wildnight Owls" (suspended after a reckless operation) and "Snowfield Falcons" (patrolling around Piramida). There was also a Special Support Squad, "Sumrak", which waited on the island that is now the Final Night Cemetery for a lighthouse signal to reinforce Piramida. All its members died there at some unknown time.

Leadership: Nikita, a middle-aged veteran the Ratniki fondly call "old man", is the current Starshyna. He took over about a decade ago when his predecessor Sigurd fell fighting the Wild Hunt.

Nikita is meticulous, perceptive and even-handed. He never asks of his people what he would not do himself, and he quietly places each member where they fit. He adopted Illuga after the Wild Hunt destroyed Illuga's village. He knows Flins' true nature and treats him as a trusted confidant. Nikita himself says he lacks Sigurd's strength and that the Lightkeepers "are no longer what they once were", so they must act with extra caution.

The known Starshynas are Solovei the Torchforger (the first), Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov (named in a book), Sigurd and Nikita. Named Sergeant Majors include Marushkin and the late Sousi. Lyubertsi is a former Sergeant Major.

Members: - **Flins**: a courtly Ratnik who lives alone in the lighthouse on the Final Night Cemetery, tending the graves of fallen Lightkeepers. He is secretly one of the Snowland Fae.
- **Illuga**: Nikita's adopted son, the young leader of the Nightmare Orioles, and the Lightkeepers' representative in the new League.
- **Olav**: a calm Ratnik recently promoted to squad leader.

Other named members include the squad leaders Gabieta, Vytautas and the late Asebov and Olsson; the doctors Ivar and Radoslaw; the blacksmith Hertta; the quartermaster Patolichev; Inga, a former squad leader; and Ratniki such as Anleifr, Egle, Rollon, Valdis, Vlaicu, Lushne, Sukhovykh and Malusha. Chicherin is a former member who took in Malusha after he and Sigurd rescued her as a child. The Final Night Cemetery holds many Lightkeeper graves.

Goals: Their stated purpose, in Nikita's words, is to safeguard the freedom and peace of Nod-Krai. In practice this means holding back the Wild Hunt, protecting the merchants and travellers who cross their lands, and keeping alive the "paradise" (Elysium) that Solovei defended before the Tsaritsa's court. Illuga describes Nod-Krai as an Elysium built by human hands and kept alive by generations of Lightkeeper sacrifice. He prefers self-reliance to waiting for any god, even the new Moon Goddess.

Methods: Lightkeepers patrol the land, answer Wild Hunt incursions wherever they appear, and keep watch from lighthouses and camps. They have planted Tideseal Stones across Nod-Krai to stop the Wild Hunt from seeping in. Their oath, sworn by every new member, ends: "We are the Lightkeepers, who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains." Flins names prudence, modesty and loyalty as their three cardinal virtues.

Item lore stresses how little they have: no ancient techniques or grand titles, only "weak flesh clad in silver armor", swords, lamps and an inherited oath. Their one great relic is the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, a giant Hyperborean-era cannon at Piramida that turns light into a projectile to purge Abyssal contamination.
