Aila of the Frostmoon Scions gave it to Solovei. For machinery, they rely on the engineer Aino, who keeps trying to make them learn repairs themselves.

History: When the Cataclysm struck about 500 years ago, Abyssal beasts overran Nod-Krai and the northern court could no longer protect its borderlands. Solovei, a Snezhnayan noble, came south, and with power lent by Aila, priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, drove the darkness back. The survivors raised a lighthouse in the mountains, and Solovei won a royal edict for Nod-Krai's autonomy in return for an oath of vigilance and sacrifice.

Since then the Lightkeepers have been nearly wiped out several times and rebuilt each time. About a decade ago, a great battle against the Wild Hunt killed Starshyna Sigurd and most of the order, and destroyed Illuga's village. Nikita had to rebuild almost from scratch. The disaster convinced many young people of the Lempo Isles that the old tales were true, and they volunteered. Three years before the Traveler came, a Wild Hunt surge at Kipumaki Cliff overwhelmed the Nightmare Orioles. Captain Olsson died covering the retreat of Illuga and the badly wounded Ivar.

**Song of the Welkin Moon (6.0).** Sergeant Major Sousi helped the Traveler recalibrate the Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Cannon at Starsand Shoal against a Wild Hunt incursion. Half a day later he was found dead in the Lightkeepers' Nasha Town office, and a witness had seen Flins enter. The Traveler cleared Flins: Rerir had already killed Sousi, worn his face during the repairs and then taken Flins' form. During Dottore's later attack on Nod-Krai, Illuga led the Lightkeepers in evacuating civilians, emptying Piramida itself.

**Nightingale's Song and the League (6.3).** Nikita sent Illuga to deal with the Abyssal blight at Kipumaki Cliff, which was caused by Rotwang's disciples rather than Rerir. With the Traveler, the Nightmare Orioles recovered Solovei's lost Spiralblade, the Arrow's ammunition. The Arrow of Terpikeraunas then destroyed the Calamity Egg on the Pillar of Embla. The Ratnik Bjorn died in the operation. After Dottore's defeat, Nod-Krai's factions formed a joint League, and Flins persuaded a reluctant Illuga to represent the Lightkeepers.

Relations: - **Frostmoon Scions**: allies since Aila aided Solovei. Flins mentions that some former Scions recently joined the Lightkeepers, apparently after Lauma revealed the truth about the false sky.
- **Knights of Favonius**: allies. Varka's expedition fought the Wild Hunt alongside them, and Illuga has fought beside Varka.
- **Fatui and the Tsaritsa**: Nod-Krai is formally Snezhnayan, but its autonomy rests on the old edict. Flins notes that Lightkeepers do not habitually say "Her Majesty the Tsaritsa".
- **The Wild Hunt**: their enemy since the Cataclysm.

- **Nasha Town factions**: they work with the Voynich Guild and Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets, which smoothed their operations in town. All three, with the Frostmoon Scions, sit in the new League.
- **Field and headquarters**: some field members grumble that headquarters is haughty and slow to act on reports, while expecting tiny squads to handle incursions anywhere.

Reputation: Townsfolk respect the Lightkeepers' sacrifices. Flins was once given a civilian commendation medal that the people organised themselves. The work is thankless, though. Many recruits retire early or quit, and recruitment drops after every brutal battle. Lately, Illuga says, more and more people want to join, including children too young to be accepted, and even Nasha Town's merchants have begun to see why the Lightkeepers fight.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Lightkeepers are active under Starshyna Nikita, still understrength but recruiting again, and part of Nod-Krai's new League.

Illuga is their League representative, and his squad is rebuilding a Lightkeeper outpost at Cliffwatch Camp. The Wild Hunt has been leaderless since Rerir was cast out and the Abyss's imitation of Roland expired in 6.4, but its incursions continue. No new Lightkeepers story was found for 7.0-7.1, whose Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

384.content: Every new Lightkeeper swears an oath in seven lines, which is also carved on Oath Lanterns and on a monument at the Final Night Cemetery. It moves from a vision of the sky swallowed by silence, through a promise that whoever keeps the flame burning need not descend into darkness, to a vow to burn "bones and blood" as fuel and "make life greater than death". It ends: "We are the Lightkeepers, who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains." Oath Lanterns are standard equipment. Through them other Lightkeepers and the Starshyna can find a Ratnik, and lanterns of the fallen are still found across the southern isles.

385.content: Starshyna is the title of the Lightkeepers' leader. Solovei the Torchforger was the first. Later holders include Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov and Sigurd, a famously brave longsword fighter whose warning bell was said to make beasts flinch. Sigurd vanished in the great battle about a decade ago. The present Starshyna is Nikita, who fought beside him and rebuilt the order afterward.

386.content: Piramida is the Lightkeepers' headquarters, a city on top of an ancient castle that was once the palace of Nod-Krai's fae governor, built around a giant golden-age lighthouse. A statue of Solovei the Torchforger watches over it, and the great mead hall at its summit hosts victory banquets where the first pour goes to the dead. The Arrow of Terpikeraunas is housed there.

387.content: The Arrow of Terpikeraunas is a giant Hyperborean-era cannon at Piramida that turns light into a solid projectile to purge Abyssal contamination. The Frostmoon Scions rebuilt it after Hyperborea fell, and Aila gave it to Solovei 500 years ago. His sword, the Spiralblade, was its ammunition but was lost for centuries. In Nightingale's Song (6.3), Illuga and the Traveler recovered it, and the Arrow destroyed the Calamity Egg atop the Pillar of Embla.

388.content: The Nightmare Orioles are an investigation squad. Under Captain Olsson they were the first to meet a Wild Hunt surge at Kipumaki Cliff three years ago, and only Illuga and Ivar survived. Illuga took command and now holds Cliffwatch Camp with Anleifr, Egle, Rollon, Valdis and Vlaicu. Bjorn died in 6.3. The Wildnight Owls were suspended after their leader Inga's recklessness got Lauri hurt, and the Snowfield Falcons replaced them on patrol around Piramida. The Special Support Squad "Sumrak" all died on the island now called the Final Night Cemetery.

389.content: The Lightkeepers placed Tideseal Stones across Nod-Krai to dispel the seeping of the Wild Hunt. Three of them bear a blue Lightkeeper symbol and are linked to the fallen Starshyna Sigurd, whose corrupted spirit was seen fighting the Wild Hunt near them.

390.content: A Ratnik (plural Ratniki) is an ordinary fighting member of the Lightkeepers. The word comes from an old Slavic term for a warrior of a militia or host. Flins calls himself "a humble Ratnik" and says the role, keeping humanity's light burning on nights when monsters roam, suits a nocturnal creature like him perfectly.

391.content:
Liyue Qixing (also: Qixing, Seven Stars of Liyue, the Liyue Qixing): The Liyue Qixing ("Seven Stars of Liyue") are a committee of seven business leaders who govern Liyue. Each is a magnate in their own field, and each holds a title named after a star of the Big Dipper. They meet at Yuehai Pavilion on Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor. For millennia they carried out the policies of Rex Lapis, the Geo Archon, and handled day-to-day government. Since his apparent death, which he staged, they have ruled Liyue without divine guidance. The best-known members are Ningguang, the Tianquan, and Keqing, the Yuheng.

Liyue's people call them "the hands and feet of Rex Lapis". They oversee all of Liyue's major trades, and very little business, inside or outside the nation, escapes their notice.

Structure: The seven members are equal in rank, but they divide the work clearly. Known seats:
- **Tianquan** (Ningguang): keeps Morax's book of ancient laws and its amendments, and handles foreign relations.
- **Yuheng** (Keqing): land, livelihood, construction works and real estate.
- **Tianshu** (Uncle Tian): plans policy and advises from behind the scenes, and traditionally rarely appears in public.
- **Kaiyang**: an unnamed current member.
- **Tianxuan**: mentioned in Ganyu's stories, but the current holder is unnamed.

The remaining seats have never been named in canon. Responsibilities overlap: water quality falls under the Yuheng, yet a Tianquan amended the sanitation act on sabotaging water sources, and every member helps make law. The Millelith (Liyue's security force), the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Eight Trades (the offices running Liyue's major industries) all answer to the Qixing.

Ganyu, the General Secretary of Yuehai Pavilion, is not attached to any one member. She produces the calculations and data behind their decisions and drafts every ordinance they announce. She has been with the Qixing since the first generation, through every change in its membership. Other secretaries such as Huixin work at the pavilion as her junior colleagues. Some members keep personal staff: Ningguang has three trusted secretaries, Baiwen, Baishi and Baixiao, and Keqing's assistants rarely last beyond three months.

Leadership: Ningguang, the Tianquan, is the Qixing's most public face. Keqing, the Yuheng, is known for hard work and for doubting reliance on the gods.

Most members keep a low profile and play it safe. Ningguang is the exception: she lives in the floating Jade Chamber, appears all over Liyue Harbor and is the subject of endless gossip. Keqing works in the field, from the south wharf to the Chasm, and once made a famous speech at the Rite of Descension asking how long Liyue could depend on Rex Lapis. Uncle Tian, the Tianshu, passes as an old, forgetful fisherman at the docks, and only a handful of people outside key posts know who he is. The Kaiyang has not been shown on screen. The Kaiyang proposed a multinational wargame to the Tianquan and, together with her, approved a long-term partnership with the Traveler.

Members: - **Current**: Ningguang (Tianquan), Keqing (Yuheng), Uncle Tian (Tianshu), the unnamed Kaiyang, and the unnamed Tianxuan.
- **Staff**: Ganyu (General Secretary); Huixin, Uncle Tian's daughter (secretary); Baiwen, Baishi and Baixiao (the Tianquan's secretaries).
- **Agents**: Yelan presents herself as an employee of the Ministry of Civil Affairs. She is actually a special intelligence officer who reports directly to Ningguang, though she sees the arrangement as a pact rather than service. After the Liyue Archon Quest she took over Yanshang Teahouse as a front. Every employee of Wangshu Inn, including its boss Verr Goldet and innkeeper Huai'an, is a Qixing agent.
- **Past members**: the weaponsmith Yun Hui, seventh master of the Yun family, joined the Qixing after handing his forge to his daughter. A former Tianxuan ("the then-Tianxuan" in Ganyu's stories) once nearly filed a missing-person report after Ganyu fell asleep in a roadside haystack following a lunch outing and was carted off to Dihua Marsh.

Goals: The Qixing aim to keep Liyue prosperous and orderly. Their tools are law, contracts and commerce. They punish lawbreakers relentlessly, both to uphold Morax's rulings and to keep trade alive. Since the god's departure they have also had to rewrite old divine strictures into laws that suit a human-run Liyue.

Methods: The Qixing govern through law, money and information. Morax's ancient laws, with each Tianquan's amendments, are published with a 279-page commentary, and every citizen gets a copy. Merchants treat any loophole as fair game until the Qixing patch it, which is why Ningguang is privately called the "Tailor of Liyue".

Their intelligence reaches far. Ningguang learns the city's secrets from street children (in return for treats) and checks them against other sources. Her confidants pin the summaries to the intel wall of the Jade Chamber. Yelan handles foreign agents. Wangshu Inn gathers news of travellers entering Liyue. The Millelith make arrests, and Keqing once worked for two months as a labourer to refine a plan for workers' treatment, using the time to gather evidence to report a powerful man known for his abuses. The Qixing also preside over state ceremonies. Each year one member asked Rex Lapis for his prediction at the Rite of Descension, and they organise cultural events such as the Moonchase Festival's Masterful Chefs contest.

History: **Founding.** When the Archon War ended, Liyue turned to commerce and craft, and those who prospered most formed the Qixing. Ganyu, who had fought for Morax, stayed on as their first secretary.

**End of divine rule (1.0).** Rex Lapis was apparently killed during the Rite of Descension, and the Qixing sent the Millelith after the culprit. Childe remarked that the Qixing had always been suspicious of the Fatui. The Qixing then received word in secret that the god was not really dead. They declared that he had died failing a divine trial, dropped the hunt for the killer and moved to fill the power vacuum, which brought them into open confrontation with the adepti. When the Fatui released the ancient god Osial, the Qixing, the adepti, the Millelith and the Traveler fought him together, and Ningguang dropped her Jade Chamber on him. The Qixing then held the Rite of Parting and took over all of Rex Lapis' duties together with the Eight Trades.

Zhongli later said that their seizure of power was the one thing he had not anticipated, and the best parting gift he could have received. Existing Mora remains valid, but the Golden House had to stop minting for a long time, because making Mora requires the Geo Archon's power, and Ningguang used the Fatui's sabotage at the Jade Chamber to pressure Snezhnaya's diplomats. Keqing spent months stuck rewriting land-infrastructure law. Over that time she gave up her old resentment of Rex Lapis and began to see his smile at her Rite speech as a sign of approval.

**Rebuilding (2.4).** Months later, Ningguang announced a contest to gather materials for a new Jade Chamber. She had secretly sped up the rebuilding to lure out Beisht, Osial's consort. This time the chamber survived, thanks to Shenhe.

Relations: - **Rex Lapis**: the Qixing served as his executors for millennia. Since his "death" they have ruled alone.
- **Adepti**: the adepti seem to have worked more closely with the Qixing in the past. Madame Ping says the Qixing stopped letting her and her friends into their counsel long ago. The two sides clashed after the god's "death", then fought Osial together. Ganyu bridges the two worlds.
- **Fatui**: mutual suspicion. After the Jade Chamber incident the Qixing nullified their Chasm agreement with Snezhnaya and pressed the Fatui's diplomats hard.
- **The Crux**: an independent ally. Beidou is the only person in Liyue Harbor who dares to bet against Ningguang.
- **Eight Trades and the Ministry of Civil Affairs**: both work under the Qixing. The known Eight Trades offices include Yinyuan Hall (salt), Shenglu Hall (glazed ceramics), Huishan Hall and the Communications Office.
- **Neighbouring nations**: the Tianquan handles foreign relations. During a limited-time event in 4.7, the Yuheng invited the armed services of neighbouring nations to a joint wargame in Liyue.

Reputation: Most citizens regard the Qixing as the cream of Liyue and the pillars of its prosperity. Their staff consider it an honour to serve them. Others think of the Qixing mostly as mortals living in the god's shadow: before the god's "death", the merchant Linlang remarked that the Qixing were mere mortals while Rex Lapis was a god. Locals warn foreigners that "Ningguang knows everything". Rumours about her contradict each other but all agree she is extraordinary.

Secrets: The Tianshu's identity is kept from the public. Wangshu Inn's role as a Qixing front and support base for Xiao is not public knowledge. Yelan's true role is hidden behind her Ministry cover. The Qixing know that Rex Lapis did not really die, but publicly claim he fell in a divine trial.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Qixing still govern Liyue. Ningguang and Keqing remain in office, and the rebuilt Jade Chamber floats above Liyue Harbor again.

During the 6.3 Lantern Rite, Ningguang and Keqing looked into a strange moon phenomenon and artifacts excavated near the Chasm, while Ganyu consulted the adepti. No further Qixing story developments were found for 6.4-7.1. The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

392.comment: Liyue Qixing: Qixing titles and seats
392.content: Each seat of the Qixing is named after a star of the Big Dipper, in Chinese reading. Five titles appear in official material. The Tianshu (Dubhe) is Uncle Tian, who plans policy behind the scenes. The Tianxuan (Merak) is mentioned in Ganyu's stories but no current holder is named. The Tianquan (Megrez) is Ningguang, who keeps the laws and runs foreign relations. The Yuheng (Alioth) is Keqing, who oversees land, livelihood and construction. The Kaiyang (Mizar) is an unnamed current member who is addressed as "Lord Kaiyang". The two remaining stars' names are fan extrapolations that have never appeared in canon. Members are addressed as "Lady Tianquan", "Lady Yuheng" and so on, and are of equal rank.

393.content: Yuehai Pavilion on Yujing Terrace is where the Qixing meet, discuss official business and rule on matters affecting all of Liyue. Their day-to-day operations and staff are based there, though some days all seven members are away on private business. Ganyu works there as General Secretary, alongside junior secretaries such as Huixin. Those with civil matters are sent on to the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Bu'yun at the pavilion controls access to the Jade Chamber. In the Liyue Archon Quest the password to go up was "Excuse me, do you sell the moon here?"

394.comment: Liyue Qixing: The Qixing and Wangshu Inn
394.content: Wangshu Inn in Dihua Marsh was built by the Qixing and is secretly run by them; it already stood about 500 years ago, when Yelan's ancestor Rongzhao passed by it. It gives the yaksha Xiao a place to rest and covert support in his fight against evil spirits. It also collects intelligence on notable people entering Liyue. All its staff are Qixing agents, including the boss Verr Goldet and the innkeeper Huai'an.

395.comment: Liyue Qixing: The Qixing take power
395.content: After Rex Lapis was apparently killed at the Rite of Descension, the Qixing at first hunted the culprit. Then a secret message told them the god was not dead, and they abruptly ended the investigation. They announced that he had died failing a divine trial and moved to take sole control of Liyue. This set them against the adepti until the Fatui unleashed Osial, when Qixing, adepti, Millelith and the Traveler joined forces. Ningguang sacrificed the Jade Chamber to defeat him. At the Rite of Parting she told the people that the contract with Rex Lapis had ended and that Liyue must build a new age of prosperity. Keqing told the Traveler that the Qixing always repay their debts. Zhongli, watching in mortal guise, called their seizure of power the best parting gift he could have wished for.

396.content: In Yelan's story quest (2.7), Uncle Tian felt his energy failing and decided to name a successor as Tianshu. Because the Tianshu works behind the scenes and must be shielded from outside influence, the outgoing Tianshu nominates a candidate in private, and the other Qixing approve the choice. Tian asked Yelan to assess three of his own students. Qianwei was a wealthy entrepreneur, Mingbo worked at the Ministry of Civil Affairs, and Zhiyi studied and travelled. Whoever was appointed would be bound to carry out the manifesto they had submitted. Zhiyi seemed ideal, but his background had been suspiciously cleaned up. Yelan and the Traveler traced him to a meeting with a Fatui contact and found he had been slowly poisoning Tian with fish soup. Baizhu made an antidote in time. Shaken, Tian chose to hand over his duties gradually while mentoring new candidates. Yelan had half-jokingly offered herself for the seat, and Tian said Ningguang would not let her go easily.

397.comment: Liyue Qixing: The Chasm and the Seven-Star Array
397.content: A little over two years before the Traveler arrived, the Qixing closed the Chasm despite its mineral wealth, after mysterious accidents, strange quakes and a harmful "wish-granting" find by the miners. They sealed the underground mines with the Seven-Star Array, whose anchor points were Bedrock Keys around the seal, while a few professional miners stayed on. Shortly after the closure, Signora negotiated trade agreements that let a Fatui advance team investigate inside. After the Jade Chamber incident, a Qixing order cancelled the agreement with Snezhnaya, handed the exploration back to the Qixing and banned the Millelith from contact with the Fatui. The Traveler later broke the weakened seal to enter the mines in "The Chasm Delvers".

398.comment: Liyue Qixing: Rebuilding the Jade Chamber
398.content: Several months after Osial's defeat, Ningguang publicly offered to answer one question each, honestly, from the first three people to bring her materials for a new Jade Chamber: Sunset Vermillionite, Wonder Cores and Adepti Sigils. The Traveler, Shenhe, Yun Jin and Beidou took part. Ningguang revealed that she had sped up the rebuilding to lure out Beisht, Osial's consort, and was ready to sacrifice the chamber again. This time it survived the battle, thanks to Shenhe. Huixin later sighed with relief that the reconstruction was finally finished, and Uncle Tian was glad to see the chamber "back up where it belongs".

399.content:
Lochknight (also: Lochknights, Lochknight order, Knights of the Lakelight): The Lochknights were the knights of Fontaine's legends: sworn, in silver armour, to protect the Oceanids (spirits born of pure water), the unpolluted springs and one another, and to resist the golden empire of Remuria. Their leader was Erinnyes. They are remembered less as a documented order than as a tale retold in plays, poems and films, and the Fontinalia Festival commemorates them.

Canon itself says their history is "heavily shrouded in legend". Remurians dismissed them as barbarians who worshipped a false god, so most of what survives comes from later romance.

Read them as a layered subject: a real rebellion against Remuria in its final years, and the many-versioned legend that grew on top of it.

Structure: The Lochknights were a band of sworn knights around a leader, not a state office. The books name a court of followers: Agricane, Blancandrin, Drest, Guillaume of Gellone (whose sword is Narbonnais), Marsile, Naimes, Otkerus of Rhenanie and Tulpin, with Kudenin of Dunnaer named in NPC dialogue. In the Chanson the knights come from many regions and unite behind Erinnyes. There is no recorded rank system, headquarters or founder.

In the Chanson, Erinnyes is addressed as "Knight Erinnyes of the Lakelight" and is the beloved leader of the knights. Her sword Hauteclaire is described there as a gift from the maiden Daeira. The knights meet in council: Drest and his companion Adsiltia, Guillaume, Naimes and Tulpin each speak or pledge their swords before Erinnyes answers the envoy of Remus.

Members: Erinnyes is the one figure tied firmly to the order: High King of Aremorica, a singer who claimed to hear the voice of Egeria, and the unifier of Fontaine's tribes against Remuria. She has her own entry. The other named knights appear only in legend-style sources.

- Guillaume of Gellone: quick to draw Narbonnais when Remus' envoy threatens Erinnyes, but obeys her order to spare him.
- Drest, Prince of Lyonnais, and Adsiltia: Drest is a bowman who counsels against trusting Remus' promised harmony. Their farewell is regarded in Fontainian culture as a classic romance.
- Otkerus of Rhenanie: praised in the Chanson for his battle with a venom-breathing dragon.
- Others named: Agricane, Blancandrin, Marsile, Naimes, Tulpin and Fierabras (who prepares gifts for the envoy).

Goals: By the oath, Lochknights protect the Oceanids and the pure springs until "the pure spring flows as before", protect their fellow believers in Egeria, and drive the Remurian "golden usurper" out of Fontaine. Two vows run through every version of the pledge: never draw a sword against those who pledge faith in Egeria, and never compromise in the face of evil. The legends also give the knights a quest for the Pure Grail, a vessel said to grant any wish and wash away sin, and to welcome Egeria back.

The historical motive behind the quest is the prophecy that all Fontainians would be dissolved by the Primordial Sea for their original sin. Erinnyes sought the Grail to save her people and to free Egeria from her prison. According to her sword's lore, she did not find it.

Methods: War and oath. Erinnyes united warring tribes by force of arms, then required them to pledge themselves to Egeria, and her army struck at Remurian holdings. Remurian sources call these acts atrocities and call her mad. The legend's version is gentler: courtly councils, tournaments and a quest.

The order's imagery matters as much as its tactics: silver armour against Remuria's gold, and a feathered helm that opera composers later copied in their hats (Poetry of Days Past).

History: The Lochknights are placed in the last years of the Remurian Empire, when Remus' rule over Fontaine was being resisted from the northern border, Aremorica. Erinnyes united the tribes and made her stand. When Remuria sank, Egeria was freed and became the new Hydro Archon, and the knights laid down their armour not long afterwards. A few decades after the fall, the idea of the Lochknight died out. An old legend says Egeria gave a Lakelight Lily to the last Lochknight as a farewell present.

In the Chanson, the envoy of Remus demands water and earth as tribute and threatens war, hunger and plague. Erinnyes refuses to bend the knee to any ruler but Egeria, and the knights back her. Later, Erinnyes bids Egeria farewell and throws her sword into a lake three times; the third time it sinks, and she departs with a spirit. The wiki notes this romanticises her exile. According to her weapon lore, she met Egeria after Remuria's fall, learned that Egeria herself had created humans from the Oceanids (the "original sin"), threw down her sword and was never seen again.

Relations: - **Oceanids and Egeria**: the order's reason for being. The knights serve the "Mistress of Many Waters", and the Oceanids are the spirits born of pure water.
- **Remuria**: the enemy. Remurians, such as the musician Goldoni speaking for Boethius' regime, called Lochknight tales ridiculous ravings.
- **Marechaussee Hunters**: later monster-hunters; some of their members descend from Lochknights.

- **Fontinalia Festival**: established to commemorate the Lochknights' quest (see the entry below).
- **Song of Days Past artifacts**: the set's flavour text is the main in-game portrayal of the vows and the helm.
- **Weapon materials**: the Silver Goblet of the Pristine Sea text carries the oath of silver armour and the later shedding of armour.

Reputation: In modern Fontaine the Lochknights are beloved literary heroes. Their adventures are told in plays, poetry and films, such as the historical film "Lochknight of the Lance" (seen in a limited-time event) and a play about a mounted python and the Pure Grail. Remurian-era views were hostile: the Empire called them barbarians, and their tales fictions told by slaves.

The ballads and the real woman are not the same thing. An artifact text insists the hero of the ballads has nothing to do with the real Erinnyes, and the modern stories are "dreams of the present".

Status as of 7.1: Defunct for centuries, existing now only as legend and festival.

No Lochknight story development was found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1. The name still appears in item text, the Fontinalia Festival and Remuria-related lore.

400.content: The Fontinalia Festival commemorates the Lochknights' search for the Oceanids and the return of Egeria. Traditionally, people dress as the knights, raise golden cups and go from door to door asking for pure water. In recent years Furina turned it into something closer to a carnival, trading the pure-water custom for candy, and children now call "Trial or treat!" at each house. A Fontinalia Film Festival, part of the limited-time event Roses and Muskets, was added by the Fontaine Film Association.

401.content: The Lakelight Lily is a pale-blue flower that grows where Water Veins meet, notably in Erinnyes Forest. Its meaning in the language of flowers is "waiting" and "everlasting promise". The legend that Egeria gave a lily of this kind to the last Lochknight as a farewell is the origin of a living custom: Fontainians pick a lily for those starting a long journey, wishing them a road as calm as pure water and a safe return.

402.content: Versions of the pledge differ across poems and plays. The artifact text gives two constants. First, never draw a sword on those who pledge faith in Egeria. Second, never compromise in the face of evil (also rendered as tolerating not even a trace of filth). One recorded wording swears by the ever-blooming silver flower to drive the golden usurper from the high sea and to protect the spirits born of pure water until the spring flows again. The Pure Grail, the object of the quest, is a vessel in the legends that can grant any wish and wash away any sin.

403.content: This three-volume in-game book is a verse romance about Erinnyes. Volume 1 shows Remus' emissary demanding the gifts of Aremori Castle's water and earth, while Volume 2 shows the knights of every region uniting behind Erinnyes. In Volume 3 she bids farewell to Egeria and casts her sword Hauteclaire into the lake three times. It is a romantic retelling, and the wiki points out that its picture of her exile differs from what her weapon lore says really happened.

404.content:
Maison Cardinalice (also: Cardinal House): The Maison Cardinalice is one of the government offices of Fontaine, based in the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine. It oversees financial approvals and related administration, which in practice means reviewing and signing off on expense reports and salary payments from other offices.

It is a separate body from the Maison Gestion, which handles documents and general administration, and from the Maison Ordalie, which runs the courts under Chief Justice Neuvillette. Ordinary Fontainians rarely deal with it directly. Most of what is known comes from office workers who must submit paperwork to it.

It is seen mostly from outside. Clerks in other offices speak of it as the last gate before money is released, and its dealings stay in the background of the Palais Mermonia's everyday routine.

Structure: No internal ranks, departments or staff names are given in canon. The Maison Cardinalice is one of the offices that share the Palais Mermonia with the Maison Gestion, the Maison Ordalie, the Maison Gardiennage and the Marechaussee Phantom. It receives batched summaries from other offices rather than individual claims.

Cornelia of the Maison Gestion describes the chain: a Gestionnaire files a claim, the Gestion compiles all receipts and documents monthly into summary reports, and these go to the Maison Cardinalice at month's end. Whether the Cardinalice has staff divisions of its own is not stated.

Leadership: No head of the Maison Cardinalice is named in game text. The wiki infobox lists Chief Justice Neuvillette as leader, but the quests show something narrower: when a sum is large enough, the Maison Cardinalice sends the matter up to Neuvillette for approval, and its requests for written explanations are said to come from him. Treat his leadership as unconfirmed.

The Gestion staff are not sure those requests really come from Neuvillette, so the office has an air of using the Chief Justice's name as cover. This is the opinion of Iaune, a Gestionnaire, not a confirmed fact, and nobody dares to test it.

Goals: Its role is to control spending and to make sure that salaries and expense payments are reviewed and signed before money leaves the public purse. Workers who deal with it describe a system built around audit trails, including end-of-year checks on where funds came from.

Methods: Approval is slow, written and cumulative. Claims are batched monthly, reviewed, signed and only then paid. If an expense raises questions, the person who made it must submit a written report. For large totals, the Maison Cardinalice submits the matter to Neuvillette himself.

In A Certain Stamp, a missing typewriter keycap leads to a demand for a separate report to the Chief Justice, because keycaps are not on the list of eligible items. Cornelia says the Maison Cardinalice relayed this as Neuvillette's own request. A cheaper route exists: the claimant buys the item and holds an acknowledgment of debt, which is paid from the public purse once the process finishes.

Relations: Its closest working partner in the quests is the Maison Gestion, whose staff depend on it for payment approval. Because Neuvillette signs off on large sums, the Chief Justice sits at the top of its approval chain in practice. It shares the Palais Mermonia with the other Fontainian governing offices.

Reputation: Among those who deal with it, the Maison Cardinalice is seen as slow and exacting. Palais Mermonia bureaucracy is a running joke, and this office is the last obstacle in the payment chain. The Strict Adherence to Office Codes furnishing set, which includes items named after the Maison Cardinalice, recreates the regimented, always-busy look of the Palais.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 it is still an active office in Fontaine. Nothing about it was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content, and no scandal, reform or change of leadership has been shown.

405.content:
In A Certain Trifle, Cornelia of the Maison Gestion explains how an office expense is paid. The claimant signs a request; receipts are compiled into monthly reports; everything goes to the Maison Cardinalice at month's end; payment follows once the review and signatures are done. The same approval covers salaries across the Maison Gestion, and the Maison Cardinalice may pass a large sum to Neuvillette. A queried expense needs a written report. Iaune, the Gestionnaire in the quest, decides to buy a keycap himself rather than risk needing the Chief Justice's signature.

In the next quest, A Certain Stamp, the Maison Cardinalice is blamed for the demand for a separate report on one keycap. Roialte tells Iaune that nobody tests whether such orders truly come from Neuvillette, because for a Gestionnaire an order from the Chief Justice carries the full weight of the administration.

406.content:
Maison Gardiennage (also: Maison Gardiennage of Fontaine, Fontaine law enforcement service, Fontainian law enforcement): The Maison Gardiennage is Fontaine's law enforcement service. Its main force is the Gardes, the uniformed officers, together with the Gardemeks, the clockwork meka that patrol with them. Two special branches sit beside them: the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, which arrests violent criminals, and the Marechaussee Phantom, a detective force that answers directly to Chief Justice Neuvillette. The service is based in the Court of Fontaine.

It keeps public order, guards the courts, and feeds the machinery of Fontaine's famously theatrical justice: its officers investigate, arrest and escort suspects, and carry out sentences once the court has ruled. Fontainians generally trust it, though the Special Patrol's fearsome reputation is a running joke.

Structure: The wiki lists five groups under the Maison Gardiennage: the Gardes, the Gardemeks, the Guard Poodle, the Marechaussee Phantom and the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.
- **Gardes**: the uniformed officers, whose captain is Grosrochard. They respond to disputes, patrol, and are the officers most citizens meet.
- **Gardemeks**: Clockwork Meka built for security work, maintained and operated by the Maison.
- **Special Security and Surveillance Patrol** (the Special Patrol): a department led by Chevreuse.
- **Marechaussee Phantom**: the investigative branch, mostly Melusines, led by Neuvillette.

The branches differ in how they work. The Gardes and Gardemeks handle everyday security. The Special Patrol is for particularly difficult cases and violent offenders, and it does less investigation than arrest. The Phantom investigates. The service is based in the Court of Fontaine, and the Palais Mermonia, which also holds Neuvillette's office, houses both the Maison Gardiennage and the Marechaussee Phantom.

Leadership: No single head of the whole service is named. Grosrochard is Captain of the Gardes and is known from Chevreuse's profile, where he is shown sending her pleading letters about the Special Patrol's recruiting standards. Chevreuse leads the Special Patrol. Neuvillette leads the Marechaussee Phantom and is its direct superior as Chief Justice.

Grosrochard and Chevreuse get on well enough to share praise: Turenna said in the 4.7 limited event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation that a rating from "Captain Chevreuse and Captain Grosrochard" was the highest acknowledgement of both the Special Patrol and the Gardes. Chevreuse is lax with her own people, hires former criminals as "special consultants" on her personal cases, and defends them when challenged, which her Maison colleagues dislike.

Members: Named current members include Captain Grosrochard of the Gardes, Captain Chevreuse of the Special Patrol, Special Patrol officer Turenna, and Gardes such as Edler. Many Gardes appear as ordinary NPCs. Former members include the retired Garde Nolette; Thurel, who served in both the Gardes and the Special Patrol; Riqueti, who left the Special Patrol for Maison Gestion; and Enghiene, a Special Patrol veteran who retired in 2026 events. Vaughn, a Garde, was killed.

Melusines are common in the service, especially in the Phantom. Enghiene, a Melusine Special Patrol member and Turenna's former drillmaster, retired after 150 years in the Maison because age had impaired her firearm skills; this was shown in the 6.7 limited-time events Final Long-Range Sightlines and Dance Dance Easy-Breezy Disco. Historically, Vautrin was the Special Patrol's captain about 400 years ago, with Grizzetti as vice captain; both are dead.

Goals: The Maison's job is to keep Fontaine safe and orderly and to bring wrongdoers before the court in a form that the courts can try. It also keeps the records of various civil cases. The Special Patrol's own stated aim, in Chevreuse's words, is to leave criminals no hope of escape, so that no one need be dragged away for real.

Methods: Officers patrol, answer calls, investigate and arrest. Fontaine has many odd ordinances, and Fontainians judge how serious a breach is by who arrives: a Maison Gardiennage officer means the parties will not get off scot-free and may be fined, while the Special Patrol's arrival means a violent case is under way. Gardemeks aid patrols: citizens say that shouting for help is enough to summon a nearby one, and every Gardemek carries a serial number for accountability. Privately owned Gardemeks exist but only the wealthiest can afford them. Maison-owned Gardemeks are pre-programmed for assigned tasks, so a human Garde cannot fully control one.

The Special Patrol works differently. Its members need not wear uniform outside formal occasions or use standard weapons, though most carry muskets and are trained in unarmed combat to Chevreuse's standards. They are the least mechanised section, because Gardemeks block their line of fire and could be turned against them by criminals. They will recruit descendants of criminals if the recruit can prove the ability to enforce justice. Members start the day with a six-mile jog, and the Patrol keeps a Melusine cafeteria that serves buttered Tidalga.

The Maison also transports and punishes prisoners. Suspects sentenced by the court are sent to the Fortress of Meropide: a notice at the Opera Epiclese records that the Maison carried out the sentence that sent Tartaglia there. It polices the Opera Epiclese too, expelling rule-breakers and prosecuting serious offenders. The Steambird's editor-in-chief Euphrasie uses Maison intelligence to publish bounties on dangerous monsters, meka and bandits.

History: **The Siege of Poisson.** More than 500 years ago, before the cataclysm, Eduardo Baker, an outlaw leader of Fleuve Cendre, was arrested during the purge of Fleuve Cendre and was being taken to exile when his followers rescued him. They joined allies and occupied Poisson, seizing the Maison Gardiennage personnel who were transporting them and making demands. When talks failed, the Marechaussee Hunters entered through secret paths and ended the siege by force, and the town was burned. Emanuel Guillotin, a Hunter who directed the operation, left the Hunters afterwards. The Maison's role was that of the escorting officers taken hostage.

**Carole and the emblem.** About 400 years ago, after Neuvillette brought the Melusines into Fontaine's society, a Melusine of the new Marechaussee Phantom named Carole was framed for murder by hardliners from the old order. When the Gardes failed to hold back the angry mob, she sacrificed herself to end the fight. Vautrin, the Special Patrol's captain, killed her accusers. The service later redesigned the Garde hat emblem, which at first showed only the scales of law, to add Melusines in her memory.

Relations: - **Marechaussee Phantom**: the investigative branch, led by Neuvillette, who is also the Chief Justice to whom it answers.
- **Neuvillette and the courts**: the Maison investigates and arrests; the Trial Court and the Iudex try. The Iudex retains the right to prosecute and enforce the law in person, a legacy that is now mostly symbolic.
- **The Steambird**: Euphrasie uses Maison intelligence for her bounty listings.
- **Fortress of Meropide**: the Maison transports prisoners there and serves as the link between court and prison.

- **Champion Duelists**: Clorinde and the other duelists act for the court, not the Maison. Clorinde is Marechaussee-Hunter trained but is not stated to belong to the Phantom.
- **Chevreuse and Chiori**: Chevreuse overlooks Chiori's rough treatment of people in her boutique in return for information, according to a voice-over.
- **The old regime**: hardliners opposed to Neuvillette and the Melusines appear in the Carole story as the Maison's main internal tension.

Reputation: Fontainians generally rely on the Maison, and say that its public security is "top-notch". Parents threaten naughty children with the Special Patrol, and adults still straighten up when Chevreuse approaches. Special Patrol officers resent being a bogeyman, but Chevreuse wants the reputation to remain. In the Carole story, hardliners accused Neuvillette's "reformed" police force of being corrupt, and the Gardes were unable to protect a Melusine from a mob.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Maison Gardiennage continues to operate in the Court of Fontaine, with Chevreuse leading the Special Patrol and Neuvillette leading the Phantom.

Its main story appearances are the 4.x Fontaine quests. Later appearances are limited-time events: Operation Downpour Simulation (5.6), in which Special Patrol members Turenna and Enghiene ran a tabletop wargame; Moonlit Patrol Exercise (6.3), in which the Garde Edler brought a Maison wargame to Nod-Krai; and Final Long-Range Sightlines (6.7), Enghiene's last assignment before retiring. No Archon Quest development for the service was found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

407.comment: Maison Gardiennage: Special Security and Surveillance Patrol
407.content:
The Special Patrol is a department of the Maison Gardiennage, currently led by Captain Chevreuse. Its members arrest violent criminals and handle cases that ordinary Gardes would struggle with. Most use muskets and are skilled in unarmed combat. Outside formal events they need not wear uniform or use standard weapons, and they are the least mechanised section of the Gardes. They may recruit descendants of criminals who can prove they will enforce justice. Chevreuse has a standing habit of hiring convicted criminals as "special consultants" for her own cases. Its fearsome reputation is the basis of the parental warning "behave, or the Special Patrol will get you".

There is an unwritten rule that when a member falls in the line of duty, the others hold on to their caps, and that the cap is passed to the fallen member's child should the child join. Chevreuse's namecard refers to a standard-issue "Type II Standard Musket" for the Patrol. Its Melusine cafeteria is known for buttered Tidalga. Grosrochard has written to Chevreuse nine times asking her to tighten recruiting, after he learned that her ranks included petty thieves, street brawlers and a would-be bank robber.

408.content: Gardes are the Maison Gardiennage's uniformed officers, in charge of public security alongside the Gardemeks. Their captain is Grosrochard. Their arrival at an ordinance breach usually means fines for those involved. In the Carole episode the Gardes were stopped by an enraged mob and could not save her, and the service later changed its hat emblem in her memory. Retired members include Nolette and Thurel; Vaughn was killed.

409.content: Gardemeks are specialist Clockwork Meka that serve the Court of Fontaine and help Gardes patrol. They are maintained and operated by the Maison Gardiennage and are pre-programmed for tasks, so a human Garde cannot fully control one. The public sees them as reliable helpers, and a shout for help will bring a nearby Gardemek. Each carries a serial number for accountability, and privately owned units exist but are expensive. The Special Patrol dislikes them because their size and rigid movement block musket fire, and criminals might turn them against their allies. Miss Gardemetiquette and Mademoiselle Belleville are known individual Gardemeks.

410.comment: Maison Gardiennage: Carole, Vautrin and the Garde emblem
410.content: About 400 years ago Carole, one of the first Melusines in the Marechaussee Phantom, and Vautrin, the Special Patrol's captain, worked together to win the trust of humans. After five years Neuvillette gave both a Medal of Peace. Hardliners of the old regime then framed Carole for murder, and the Gardes could not stop the mob that formed. She sacrificed herself to prove her innocence. Vautrin killed the culprits, was tried by Neuvillette and sent to the Fortress of Meropide. The Garde emblem was redesigned to add Melusines in her honour. Her Medal of Peace was later destroyed in a fire, and Kiara, a Melusine who came to the Court with her, remembers her in a dream during the quest In a New Light.

411.content: More than 500 years ago, before the cataclysm, Eduardo Baker, the outlaw leader of Fleuve Cendre, was arrested in the purge of that district and was being taken to exile in the desert. His followers rescued him, joined allies and occupied Poisson, taking the Maison Gardiennage escorts hostage and making unreasonable demands. After talks broke down, the Marechaussee Hunters entered through secret paths and resolved the matter by force. The town was burned and many of its people died. Emanuel Guillotin, the Hunter who directed the operation, quit the Hunters afterwards. Eduardo is presumed to have died there. The source is mainly artifact and weapon text, so details are sparse.

412.content:
Maison Gestion (also: Management House, Gestionnaires): The Maison Gestion is Fontaine's governmental body for document management and administrative tasks, based in the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine. Its employees are called Gestionnaires. It is known for paperwork, official stamps, endless approvals and an overcomplicated bureaucracy.

Where the Maison Ordalie runs the courts, the Gardiennage keeps order and the Maison Cardinalice approves money, the Gestion keeps Fontaine's paper moving. Its workers are not villains. They are tired, quarrelsome, often witty clerks who care, in different ways, whether their work means anything.

The Maison Gestion is also Fontaine's face abroad in small ways: two of its Gestionnaires are sent to Natlan on a preliminary mission to look for cooperation opportunities. Several former colleagues have left to do other things, such as the café owner Arouet.

Structure: The Maison Gestion is divided into offices, for example one responsible for confidential items and one for staff matters. No office is directly in charge of Kameras, which shows how rigid the division is. Staff carry thick notepads to remember who handles what. It has its own official seal, and documents get a series of stamps from different people before they count.

Named offices in A Certain Notice: Gattineo's handles secrecy and the security classification of documents, and Difor's handles staff. Cornelia fields enquiries and expense claims and sits nearest the entrance. Roialte acts as a senior coordinator who guides younger colleagues, and Semaine is a former courts assistant secretary who was transferred back. Some of them are mentioned in other places: Jacquetta says she chases signatures from two leaders whose desks stand side by side and who rarely agree, and Eunomia moved over from external publicity to a job about measurement standards. The Maison Gestion also has members in the Fountain of Lucine and Vasari Passage areas.

Leadership: No overall head is named. Individual office heads appear, and Chief Justice Neuvillette's orders are treated as binding by Gestionnaires. Carsix, who has his own office and a backup official stamp and, according to Difor and Gattineo, relies on others to draft his speeches, is a senior figure whose exact title is not given.

Difor says that if his office must take charge of something unwelcome, someone named Maneval should come and tell him in person, which suggests a higher authority but gives no title. Neuvillette appears more as a distant superior whose signature the Gestionnaires fear to need than as someone who manages the office day to day.

Members: Gestionnaires seen in the Palais Mermonia include Roialte, Iaune, Semaine, Cornelia, Gattineo and Difor. Iaune is a newer, idealistic and sleep-deprived junior. Roialte is easy-going and experienced and explains the unwritten rules. Cornelia is polite and procedural. Gattineo is described as affable and as an exemplary Gestionnaire who avoids risk, while Difor is quick to anger but clever. Gravier is a shy newcomer and Chatelet is an old colleague of Arouet.

Thales operates the stamping machine in A Certain Stamp. Clapiers and Monthois work in the office that stamps payments to outside parties, and Monthois is said to be waiting to retire without working. Arouet used to be a Gestionnaire and now manages Cafe Lutece in Vasari Passage. Fleicher is another Gestionnaire, met in Erinnyes, who says he cannot put work down once he has picked it up.

Goals: The Gestion's stated work is to manage documents and handle administrative tasks, and in practice it tries to follow correct procedure: proper signatures, reports and classifications. Its staff also try to avoid taking sole responsibility, preferring shared accountability. Roialte teaches that in a large organisation everyone must take some responsibility.

Methods: Work runs on stamps, forms, written proposals and reports. A policy needs signatures from the offices concerned, and each office tends to push the matter toward another. The Autostamper 3000 and the key that activates it are meant to preserve confidentiality, though the machine only works after a hard knock. Office notices are drafted by juniors and signed by those above them.

In A Certain Notice, Gattineo and Difor both sign as 'co-organizer', which Difor defines as 'at least I'm not responsible for this', until Roialte reframes the task: Gattineo handles enforcement as before and Difor merely posts a large proposal. Gestionnaires also use a staff rule that no Kameras may be brought in except for work, to prevent leaks. Small expenses must pass through the Maison Cardinalice, so even a missing typewriter keycap generates multiple rounds of paperwork.

History: No founding or earlier history is given. The Gestion first becomes visible in 4.0, when the Traveler meets Iaune and Roialte in the Palais Mermonia.

Relations: The Maison Gestion shares the Palais Mermonia with the Maison Ordalie, Maison Gardiennage, Maison Cardinalice and the Marechaussee Phantom. It depends on the Maison Cardinalice for payment approval, and Gestionnaires treat Neuvillette's orders as imperatives. It is also tied to the press: The Steambird often reports the office's internal matters before its own memos spread, a point Gattineo notes with bitterness.

Outside suppliers also feel its weight. In the commission Tales From the Court, Livre, a maker of Clockwork Meka, has had to return to the Palais Mermonia three times for payment on an order. Each time a different formality blocks him, such as an end-of-month audit, empty stamp pad ink or an updated form, and a police officer helps him. Caron says problems like this occur often.

Reputation: Fontainians do not think much of the Maison Gestion. Gattineo says the people of the Court of Fontaine take every chance to mock and deride it. Its bureaucracy is a joke, and quests treat the office's slowness and overcomplication as typical. At the same time it is a source of employment and sometimes sympathy: its staff feel overworked, and colleagues care for one another.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the Maison Gestion is still in operation. Its latest appearance found is the 5.0 Natlan daily commission. No later change in leadership, structure or role was found.

413.content:
Gestionnaire is the title of an employee of the Maison Gestion. Staff are seen at their desks inside the Palais Mermonia and sometimes elsewhere in Fontaine, such as Vasari Passage and the Fountain of Lucine. They speak formally, quibble over procedure, and often talk about the purpose of their work.

Newer Gestionnaires are expected to learn by doing. Roialte refuses to write Iaune's document for him because 'he will not remember this lesson', and says that fantasies about the job are for the young, not for Gestionnaires.

414.comment: Maison Gestion: A Certain Notice, Stamp and Trifle
414.content:
These three linked Fontaine world quests follow Iaune in the Palais Mermonia. First, a ban on Kameras bounces between Gattineo and Difor until Roialte resolves it. Second, a missing typewriter keycap grows into a reimbursement problem that could reach Neuvillette. Third, the notice gets stamped by the Autostamper 3000, a colleague finds the keycap and Iaune collapses from overwork, ending with the question of what his work is for.

The Traveler's role in each is mostly observation, nudging debates and even tapping the stamping machine to start it. Gattineo explains that Carsix leaked his own minutes to reporters, and that the meetings behind such minutes exist to decide what must not appear in a speech.

415.comment: Maison Gestion: Kamera policy and leaks
415.content: Staff may not bring Kameras into the Maison Gestion or take photos except for work, to prevent leaks of secret information. The rule follows a case in which a staff member showed his desk to a Kamera Club and a reporter spotted an internal memo in the photo, which appeared in The Steambird.

416.content: A slow, temperamental stamping machine that Thales brought in for confidentiality. It needs a key and a correctly aligned document, and users must sign in and be photographed with a Kamera, per an instruction attributed to Carsix. In A Certain Stamp it only works after the Traveler hits it hard. A backup stamp is kept in a box in Carsix's office, which Thales has a key to.

417.content: In the Tales From the Court daily commission, Livre cannot get payment for Clockwork Meka that the Palais Mermonia ordered. Cornelia says only Clapiers, who holds the stamp key, can process the case. Livre is turned away over an audit, a lack of ink and a form update. Officer Rhemia helps him obtain the form so he can try again, and Caron says that this happens often.

418.content: The daily commission An Official Mission shows Roialte and Iaune in Natlan on behalf of the Maison Gestion, sent to make preliminary contact and find areas for cooperation in trade or travel, though they say trade specialists would handle the real talks. They are puzzled by the lack of an administrative structure and the Traveler suggests they speak to the tribes directly.

419.content:
Maison Ordalie (also: Ordalie, the Maison Ordalie): The Maison Ordalie is the part of Fontaine's government that runs the judicial system. It is led by the Chief Justice of Fontaine, called the Iudex, who is Neuvillette. It works from the Palais Mermonia in the Court of Fontaine, and its most public work is the trials held in the Opera Epiclese.

The name is French and the wiki glosses it as "Ordeal House". Fontaine's other main government bodies sit in the same palace: the Maison Gardiennage (law enforcement), the Maison Gestion (document and administrative work) and the Maison Cardinalice (financial approvals and other administration). The Palais Mermonia is, as far as Fontainians are concerned, the highest authority in the land.

Structure: At the top is the Chief Justice, or Iudex. Besides Neuvillette, other judges working from the Palais Mermonia can be assigned to preside over trials, so he does not hear every case himself. The Maison Ordalie judges. It does not police or investigate by itself. Arrest, transport and punishment of offenders belong to the Maison Gardiennage, which also keeps civil case records, and archiving and paperwork are handled by the Maison Gestion. The detective force known as the Marechaussee Phantom belongs to the Maison Gardiennage but answers directly to the Chief Justice.

Trials are staged in the Opera Epiclese, an opera house on the island of Erinnyes that doubles as Fontaine's main courthouse. The Fortress of Meropide, reached by a lift from behind the opera house, receives people sentenced there, but it is autonomous and sits outside the Court of Fontaine's jurisdiction. Its administrator is Wriothesley.

Leadership: The Iudex is Neuvillette, a figure of strict impartiality. He has been the only Iudex for a very long time, so long that people assume divine favour gave him an unusually long life.

The Iudex has duties beyond judging trials. Under historical and traditional legacies, the Iudex may also prosecute and enforce the law in person. This was once meant to keep order in chaotic times and is now mostly symbolic. If the Iudex investigates or prosecutes a case, he must step down as judge and have someone else take the seat, and Neuvillette is said to have followed that rule in the few cases he handled personally.

Members: Neuvillette is the only person the wiki lists as a member. Other judges exist, but none are named in the sources checked. Charlotte, a reporter for The Steambird, relays in a quest that one trial was assigned to another judge from the start. Champion Duelists are a separate group of fighters who stand in for an accused person's honour, and the strongest of them is Clorinde.

Neuvillette describes Clorinde as his nation's most powerful Champion Duelist and a successor to the old Marechaussee Hunters, playing a vital part in keeping the courtroom fair and impartial. The Special Security and Surveillance Patrol of the Maison Gardiennage is currently led by Chevreuse.

Goals: The Maison exists to maintain order through law and trial. A map description of the Court of Fontaine says law serves a stable order, which is the foundation for equity and justice. Neuvillette's own voice-overs are more guarded: he says society's ideas of justice, fairness, equality and the rule of law are not equivalent and never can be.

Methods: Cases begin with an accusation, usually from the Maison Gardiennage, and go to a public trial in the Opera Epiclese. Before the trial the accused may choose to face a Champion Duelist instead in order to keep their honour. If the accused wins the duel they are acquitted. If they lose, they stand trial, and a duel can end in death if the accused refuses to yield. Public trials were put on like performances, with bulletins announcing the charge and the verdict. Convicted people are sent to the Fortress of Meropide.

Fontaine's legal code is famously complex and full of odd old articles. Neuvillette's own examples include a rule about pets and Furina's name, one about tomato ketchup being only a condiment, and the requirement that Melusines be addressed as "she".

Until 4.2 a verdict was formally handed down by the Iudex together with the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a large mechanical scale in the Opera Epiclese. The Oratrice could reach a verdict that differed from the Iudex's own view, and its result had to be honoured whatever he believed. After the Oratrice stopped working at the end of Masquerade of the Guilty, the wiki records that Neuvillette decided to hear every case and pass verdicts himself.

History: The Court of Fontaine is said to have been the court of Focalors, God of Justice, for at least a thousand years. Neuvillette's Iudex-led judiciary continues that court under his charge, and the sources found do not date the Maison Ordalie more exactly.

Roughly 400 years ago, shortly after Neuvillette was appointed Iudex, he brought the Melusines into Fontainian society. Many people feared them. The Melusine Carole, one of the first to join the Marechaussee Phantom, was framed by hardliners opposed to him and died proving her innocence. Her partner Vautrin, then captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, took revenge and was sentenced by Neuvillette to the Fortress of Meropide. The emblem of Fontaine's law enforcement now shows two Melusines beneath the scales of law to honour Carole.

Relations: - **Maison Gardiennage**: arrests, investigates, transports and punishes, and supplies the cases that the courts hear. Its Marechaussee Phantom answers directly to the Chief Justice.
- **Maison Gestion and Maison Cardinalice**: administrative and financial sister bodies in the same palace.
- **Fortress of Meropide**: where sentences are served. It is independent of the court's jurisdiction.
- **Champion Duelists**: a separate group offering the accused a duel in place of a trial.

- **Furina**: the former Hydro Archon, who treated trials as theatre in her public role. In 4.2 she abdicated the post of Hydro Archon and left its affairs to Neuvillette, who now runs the nation and helps take care of her needs.
- **The Steambird**: Fontaine's newspaper reports on trials and on the Iudex. Neuvillette has had run-ins with it, such as its story claiming he called his post a springboard.
- **Melusines**: Neuvillette secured their rights and the rule that they be called "she".

Reputation: Fontainians see the Palais Mermonia as the top authority and the Iudex as unassailably impartial. To children, the person in the judge's seat just wears a wig, keeps order and acts as the Oratrice's messenger. The Fortress of Meropide has a notorious reputation among law-abiding people.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Maison Ordalie still runs Fontaine's judicial system under Chief Justice Neuvillette, who has also effectively taken over the running of Fontaine from the Palais Mermonia.

The Oratrice has not worked since 4.2, so verdicts no longer come from it. The Archon Quests of 6.x (Nod-Krai) and 7.0-7.1 did not touch this body in the sources checked.

420.content: "Iudex" is the title of Fontaine's Chief Justice, held by Neuvillette. The Iudex presides over trials, may prosecute and enforce the law in person under an old tradition, and must step down as judge when doing so. The title heads the Maison Ordalie. The Marechaussee Phantom answers to the Iudex directly.

421.comment: Maison Ordalie: Trials at the Opera Epiclese
421.content:
Fontaine's trials are held in the Opera Epiclese, which is also a theatre. The public can watch, and under Furina they were treated as entertainment. The Iudex sits in the seat above where the Oratrice stands at the back of the stage, though other judges can preside too. Before 4.2, verdicts were issued by the Iudex together with the Oratrice. Convicts go to the Fortress of Meropide.

Notice boards at the opera house showed public trials of burglars, an impostor who pretended to be the Maison Gardiennage, and the serial-disappearances case. The announcements state the charge, the investigation's findings and the verdict in a fixed style.

422.comment: Maison Ordalie: Duel instead of trial
422.content: Anyone accused may ask an official Champion Duelist to fight instead of standing trial, as a way to defend their honour. If the accused wins, they are acquitted. If they lose, they go to trial, and death in the duel is possible if they refuse to yield. Duelists are chosen from Fontaine's best fighters, and the strongest today is Clorinde.

423.comment: Maison Ordalie: Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale
423.content: The Oratrice is a large mechanical scale in the Opera Epiclese, made by Focalors. It turns belief in justice into Indemnitium, which supplies power to the Court of Fontaine and Erinnyes, and it delivered verdicts that the court had to accept. In 4.2 it condemned "the Hydro Archon" to death, which let Focalors destroy the divine throne. It has not functioned since. The wiki says Neuvillette's restored authority now substitutes for its power supply and he hears cases himself.

424.comment: Maison Ordalie: Carole and the Melusines' place in the law
424.content: Carole was a Melusine who joined the Marechaussee Phantom alongside Vautrin to build goodwill with humans. Hardliners opposed to Neuvillette framed her, and she died proving her innocence. Neuvillette sentenced Vautrin for his revenge and, in the years after, defended the Melusines' standing. The rule that they be addressed as "she" is part of that legacy.

425.comment: Maison Ordalie: Sister Maisons of the Palais Mermonia
425.content: Beyond the Maison Ordalie, the Palais Mermonia houses the Maison Gardiennage, the Maison Gestion and the Maison Cardinalice. Gestion handles documents and administrative work, divided into offices. Its employees are called Gestionnaires, and it is known for heavy bureaucracy and overworked staff. Cardinalice oversees financial approvals and other administration. Gardiennage polices the nation.

426.content:
Marechaussee Phantom (also: Marechaussee Hunters, Maréchaussée Phantom): The Marechaussee Phantom is Fontaine's elite detective force, led by Chief Justice Neuvillette and made up largely of Melusines, whose sharp eyesight lets them notice more than most humans. It is a special branch of the Maison Gardiennage, based at the Palais Mermonia, and answers directly to Neuvillette. Its name comes from the Marechaussee Hunters, who once hunted monsters across Fontaine with special sword techniques.

Today the Phantom spends its time on criminal investigation, not battle. The Hunters survive only as a tradition passed down through families and chosen successors, and none of them are known to serve in the Phantom now.

Structure: Canon gives little formal structure. The Phantom is one of two special branches of the Maison Gardiennage, alongside the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, and it is chiefly responsible for investigation. It is led by Neuvillette, and its uniform is typically blue. Aquabus operators belong to the same service with slightly different, custom-coloured outfits: Aeval of the Clementine Line wears light blue and Elphane of the Navia Line wears red.

No ranks, headcount or captains are given for the Phantom itself. The Special Patrol, by contrast, has a captain (Chevreuse), and about 400 years ago Vautrin, its captain, worked beside the Melusine Carole when the first Melusines joined the Phantom.

Leadership: Neuvillette leads the Phantom, and it answers directly to the Chief Justice. The Iudex of Fontaine has the historical right to prosecute and enforce the law in person, a power now exercised mostly in symbol, and the Phantom serves as his investigative arm. The Hunters, the Phantom's predecessors, were founded by Cassiodor, called the Golden Hunter.

The wiki lists no other current leaders. Melusines revere Neuvillette as a father figure, and he calls them his dependents and successors, which colours how the Phantom's Melusine staff relate to him.

Members: Most of the Phantom's staff are Melusines. Confirmed members include Sedene, who works at the Palais Mermonia, and Kiara, who helped solve a smuggling case. Historical members include Carole. Emanuel Guillotin, a Hunter, and the Narzissenkreuz Institute survivors Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin are linked to the force in artifact text. The Marechaussee Hunters are Cassiodor, Este, Walter, Petronilla, Emanuel Guillotin, Florian and his father, and Clorinde.

The wiki's count of current members is a category list rather than a roster. Clorinde is the best-known heir of the Hunters. She was trained by Petronilla in their marksmanship, but she serves the Trial Court as Champion Duelist, not the Phantom. Florian, a descendant of Hunters, appears in Clorinde's story quest.

Goals: The Phantom investigates crime in the Court of Fontaine and brings its findings to the Chief Justice. The older Hunters sought to hunt down monsters, and the founding motto credited to Cassiodor was to pursue the phantoms in the dark and drive them out. Neuvillette also hoped Melusines in the force would help them win the trust of humans.

Methods: Melusines' powerful eyesight and ability to perceive more than ordinary people make them well suited to detective work, which is why Neuvillette recruited them. The Hunters' techniques were different. A Hunter's weapons were traditionally a musket or pistolet to drive prey and a sword for the kill, with training in close combat, tracking, camouflage, footwork and marksmanship. The Hunters enchanted weapons to glow near monsters.

Hunters carried keys passed down generation to generation, and quickly revealed their identity to fellow Hunters to avoid accidental injury. On a new member's first birthday as a Hunter, their mentor makes them a short-sword necklace engraved with their name, symbolising interrogating one's own heart at swordpoint. These customs are known mainly through Clorinde, whose voice-overs and profile describe them.

History: **The Hunters.** After Remuria fell, Cassiodor, a former Remurian warrior later known as the Golden Hunter, founded the Marechaussee Hunters to hunt down the monsters the dynasty left behind. Remurian survivors such as Este and Walter followed him, and the group is said to have included heirs of the Lochknights. The Hunters thinned the monster population and returned to ordinary lives; their special methods faded and their names were forgotten. Cassiodor himself disliked the name "Marechaussee Hunter", seeing it as a humiliation, according to artifact text.

**The Siege of Poisson.** More than 500 years ago, outlaws under Eduardo Baker occupied Poisson and held Maison Gardiennage escorts hostage. The Hunter Emanuel Guillotin directed the operation, and the Hunters entered through secret paths to end it by force. The town was razed and many of its inhabitants burned to death. Disillusioned, Emanuel left the Hunters.

**The cataclysm and after.** After the Narzissenkreuz Institute's Director and Vice Director vanished in the cataclysm, some members, including Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin, were taken in by the Marechaussee Phantom or the Special Patrol to protect Fontaine. Years later, the Court of Fontaine noticed the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, and the Phantom was told to investigate. Knowing this, the Ordo invited the Marechaussee Hunters to guard construction of the Tower of Ipsissimus and so allay suspicion. The conflict ended in a fierce battle at Elynas with many casualties on both sides.

Relations: - **Maison Gardiennage**: the Phantom is a special branch and shares the Palais Mermonia with it.
- **Special Security and Surveillance Patrol**: sister branch, led by Chevreuse. The Patrol makes arrests; the Phantom investigates.
- **Champion Duelists**: Clorinde is both the Trial Court's strongest duelist and the Hunters' heir, which gives the old tradition a living link to the courts.
- **Melusines**: the Phantom's main workforce. Neuvillette treats them as dependents and successors.

- **Narzissenkreuz Ordo**: investigated by the Phantom, which led to the battle at Elynas.
- **Clorinde and Navia**: Petronilla introduced the young Clorinde to Navia, and in Silent Night's finale Navia calls Petronilla "the Hunter I respect the most".

Reputation: Most Fontainians know the Hunters only as a legend, usually through the "Hunter's Oath" they have met in plays and novels. The Phantom itself is less known, but hardliners once complained that Neuvillette had given Melusines official posts and investigation powers. Neuvillette, for his part, praises Clorinde as a successor to the Hunters who ensures the courtroom's fairness.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Phantom is a detective force under Neuvillette, staffed mostly by Melusines. The Hunters exist as a tradition, with Clorinde as their best-known heir.

No new Marechaussee Phantom story developments were found for 5.x, 6.x or 7.0-7.1; those versions are set elsewhere or concern other characters.

427.content:
The Marechaussee Hunters were founded by Cassiodor, the Golden Hunter, to hunt the monsters and phantoms that threatened Fontaine. They used special sword techniques, musket marksmanship, tracking and camouflage, and enchanted weapons that glow near monsters. Over time the monsters were thinned out, the Hunters returned to ordinary work, and their names were forgotten. Today the Hunters are a family tradition: Clorinde inherited the training from Petronilla, and Florian descends from Hunters. The best-known surviving custom is the Hunter's Oath, which most Fontainians know only from stories.

Cassiodor's motto was to pursue the phantoms in the dark, expel them all and hunt them down. The Hunter's Brooch was an emblem awarded for feats of arms in Fontaine's defence, though some recipients hid or drowned theirs. Hunters whose names are called in Silent Night's finale include Este, whom the tablet records as having inherited the Golden Hunter's responsibilities ("inheritor of Cassiodor's will"), Walter and Petronilla.

428.comment: Marechaussee Phantom: Cassiodor, the Golden Hunter
428.content: Cassiodor founded the Marechaussee Hunters. He was a warrior of Remuria's age, and the Hunters gathered Remurian survivors and heirs of the Lochknights around him. His epithet "Golden Hunter" is credited to him as a hero, though the artifact text says he saw the Marechaussee Hunter name as a humiliation. Accounts disagree on when he founded the Hunters, and the wiki says he guided later generations over a very long time.

429.comment: Marechaussee Phantom: Siege of Poisson (Phantom view)
429.content: More than 500 years ago the Marechaussee Hunter Emanuel Guillotin led the operation that ended the siege of Poisson, entering the occupied town through secret paths. The town was burned and many residents died. He left the Hunters disillusioned and later became cold and detached, until an old friend asked him to live among people again, and he raised Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin. He is recorded as a member of the Narzissenkreuz Institute and the Phantom.

430.comment: Marechaussee Phantom: Melusines in the Phantom
430.content: Neuvillette brought Melusines from Merusea Village into the Phantom because their special sight suits detective work. Carole, one of the first, believed Melusines would find meaning in work and live in peace with humans. Distrust remained, and she died after being framed. The tragedy led to Vautrin's imprisonment and to the Garde hat emblem being redesigned to include Melusines. Kiara, who came to the Court with Carole, later joined the Phantom and was threatened after a smuggling case, which Neuvillette personally investigated.

431.comment: Marechaussee Phantom: Silent Night and the Hunters' vault
431.content: In Clorinde's story quest Silent Night, an apparent Tabletop Troupe script cast Navia, Lyney, Furina and the Traveler as Marechaussee Hunters, with Clorinde as game master. It was actually Florian's script, written under the influence of a monster called the Devorator. He led the group to the Hunters' vault, which held a tablet of names and the broken weapons of past Hunters. When the Devorator took over Florian's body, the group recited the names and the weapons glowed. Clorinde struck the final blow, the group accepted Florian's help in making amends, and Clorinde left the vault untouched.

432.content:
Masters of the Night-Wind (also: Mictlan, Mictlan tribe, Night-Wind tribe): The Masters of the Night-Wind, also called Mictlan, are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live in a settlement perched on a foothill of the Tezcatepetonco Range. Of all the tribes they have the deepest bond with the Night Kingdom: their shamans commune with the Wayob, read fortunes, heal, bless weapons and keep watch over Natlan's Ley Lines and Phlogiston. Their chief is Biram, and their most famous member is the great shaman Citlali ("Granny Itztli").

Outsiders find them mysterious, reclusive and fond of cryptic speech. Most Mictlan folk met outside the settlement are travelling doctors or diviners on a commission. The tribe also records Natlan's history in woven scrolls, and it is known for graffiti.

Structure: The tribe is led by a chief, who keeps its relics and oversees its rites. Below and beside the chief stand its spiritual specialists: high priests and priestesses, shamans of varying skill, and, rarely, a "great shaman", a title reached only at the very peak of the mystic arts. Citlali is the only great shaman alive. Shamanic knowledge passes from master to student, and some shaman families keep whole schools of technique. The tribe also has guards, trainers, Phlogiston inscribers, artisans and a Graffiti Alliance. Its bonded Saurians are the Iktomisaurs, and an ancient one, Elder Tlapo, is treated as an elder of the tribe.

Like every Natlanese tribe, it has its own Wayob, which protects it and makes its will known through the chief's dreams. The Mictlan Wayob is the soul of the tribe's last Holy Sovereign, Maghan's master. A chief's duties include granting (on the Wayob's behalf) permission to leave Natlan. Special scrolls for events that affect all of Natlan are woven by someone Tlapo appoints.

Leadership: Biram, the current chief, is an enormous man (more than twice the Traveler's height) who wears an Iktomisaurus-like mask. He is progressive but unwilling to let change destroy tradition.

Biram speaks in omens and likes to let questioners "stew" before answering. He keeps the ceremonial sword Calamity of Eshu between ceremonies, and for certain rites he wears the Soul-Shielding Cloak, a relic handed down through generations of chiefs. He treats Citlali with open respect, calling himself a humble junior beside the tribe's eldest priestess, where other elder shamans are frankly afraid of her.
