Citlali, for her part, says her duties include advising the chief and speaking with the Wayob.

Past leaders include Maghan, the founding priest-king; his successor, the priest Wagadu; the fourth high priest, Hanga; and Ayizu, chief 500 years ago, who died during the cataclysm-era fighting after telling the man later known as Capitano the secret of the Gnosis.

Goals: The tribe's role is spiritual stewardship: keeping the bond between the living, the Wayob and the Night Kingdom, monitoring the health of Natlan's Ley Lines and Phlogiston, guiding lost souls home, and preserving memory. Its founding charge, given by the Holy Sovereign to Maghan, was to spread the stories of heroes among the tribes and weave memories into scrolls, to "anchor" humanity's home in Natlan.

Methods: Mictlan shamans see Phlogiston energy and even souls. Their arts include divination, potion-making, healing, astral projection (clairvoyance), telekinesis, concealment, memory extraction, border spells that blur the line between the Night Kingdom and the waking world, and Phlogiston Engraving. A shaman's repertoire depends on training and talent. Citlali has mastered many rare spells and invented her own. Shamans can also sense their own link to the Wayob and tell when they are about to travel too far from home to keep it.

Every spell and every "problem-solving method" of the tribe works through spirits, so a degree of spiritual sensitivity is required. A tribesperson born with none at all is called a "spirit-duffer". A spirit-duffer can be forced into clairvoyance, but if their spirit gets lost or harmed it is very hard to recover, and even the tribe's healing does not work on them. Shamans teach through rivalry: a master often engineers clashes between students and a formidable peer to push them to improve.

Members: - **Citlali**: great shaman and high priestess, a Cryo Vision holder who has lived for more than two centuries. She lives in seclusion away from the settlement.
- **Ororon**: a young man abandoned in the mountains as an infant and raised by the whole tribe, with Citlali as his "Granny". He has a fragmented soul and lives alone in the wilds, farming.
- **Biram**: chief.
- **Tlapo**: the Iktomisaurus Elder, "He of the Sharp Mist-Shaded Claws", once Huitzilin's companion "Claw".

Other named members include the high priest Caholom; the Phlogiston inscriber Ixim; the witch doctor Matla; the trainer Bitsin; the ley-line inspector Toltec; Leyla, a spirit-duffer whose spirit got lost during clairvoyance; and Huitzilin's living school of shamans (Aywastin, Besuci, Caholom and Chogan). Historical members include Maghan, the Holy Sovereign, Sanhaj Kompore, Ayizu, Huitzilin, and Aroni, Bennett's biological mother.

History: **Before the tribe.** Near the end of Xiuhcoatl's reign, the tribe's forerunners lived in a valley ruled by the Dragonlord Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox, the "Weaver of Secrets". She guarded them with a labyrinth of mirrors and a fortress of mist, and in return they appointed a "Holy Sovereign", a child with a "star-bright soul" who was blinded and maimed so as to guide the dragons into dreams. The last Holy Sovereign was served by a silent attendant, Dinga.

**Founding.** Prophesying the future, the Holy Sovereign sent Dinga to follow Xbalanque and asked him to stab her in the heart when they next met. After Xiuhcoatl fell and Cinder City was founded, Och-Kan declared the valley's people traitors. Dinga, now the dragon slayer Maghan, led the attack and killed his master as she had asked, and she became the tribe's Wayob. Maghan then refused Och-Kan's favour, retired and built the Mictlan tribe, around 2,000 years ago. His successor Wagadu renewed the pact with the Weaver of Secrets, giving rise to the first Iktomisaurus.

**Cataclysm.** Five hundred years ago, Chief Ayizu fought the Abyss beside the Khaenri'ahn later known as Capitano. The tribe's Border Master Sanhaj Kompore, one of the six heroes, is said to have exploded a miniature Night Kingdom at the Battle of the Mare Jivari, dying with Tenoch.

**Recent past.** About two centuries ago Citlali and Huitzilin became great shamans on the same day. Later, with the Ley Lines failing, a chief tried to use the newborn Ororon as a vessel to carry lost souls into the Night Kingdom. The ceremony failed and he survived.

Relations: - **Pyro Archon**: Mavuika values Citlali's help and has said she thought Citlali was chief material. The tribe fought under her in the Abyss war.
- **Other tribes**: the six tribes have coexisted since Och-Kan's era. Members of other tribes travel to Mictlan for divination, healing and weapon blessings.
- **Fatui**: tense. Ororon briefly worked with Capitano. In the "Memories Flowing With Color" Tribal Chronicles, Montluson, a Fontainian printing-company owner backed by Pantalone's Fatui, tried to destroy Huitzilin's legendary dye so he could market his own; Tlapo's Iktomisaurs caught him.
- **Abyss Order**: the Abyss Lector Enjou (under the alias Kokuchuu) manipulated Leyla into "hypersensitivity training" to learn about the Mare Jivari during a limited-time event.

Reputation: Other Natlanese regard the Masters as profound, eccentric and a little alarming. Shamans are trusted as both doctors and prophets, and people believe that items crafted by the tribe have special effects. Within the tribe, "Granny Itztli" is a bogeyman parents invoke to quiet crying children.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is intact under Chief Biram, after the Abyss war ended in 5.3. Citlali remains its great shaman, and Ororon still lives in the wild.

No tribe story was found in the 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quests. A few members appear abroad in Nod-Krai: Kofitse sells Natlanese hornshrooms in Piramida, saying the Wayob sent him to guide the outlanders there.

433.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: Shamans and great shamans
433.content: "Shaman" is the respected Mictlan profession of mystic practitioners who serve as doctors and prophets for all of Natlan. A "great shaman" is a title earned only at the very peak of the art, and there have been few in Natlan's history. Citlali and her rival Huitzilin both became great shamans on the same day, and Citlali is the only one alive now. Shamans cast spells through spirits: divination, clairvoyance, healing, telekinesis, concealment, memory extraction and border spells.

434.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: Woven scrolls
434.content:
The tribe records stories, legends and histories in woven scrolls instead of writing. Thread patterns are abstract and carry the weaver's feelings. For an event that affects all of Natlan, a special scroll is woven by someone Elder Tlapo appoints, and Huitzilin's art of using "color" as a medium for memory lets these scrolls hold memories. A huge graffiti mural above the settlement has been with the tribe since its founding, which is one reason Biram refuses to abandon weaving. By an old rule Maghan set, weavers once worked blindfolded; Hanga, the fourth high priest, ended it because the results were a mess.

In "Memories Flowing With Color" (5.2), Tlapo chose the Traveler as the first outsider ever to weave a special scroll. It emerged that the "gift from the spirits" that had helped earlier appointees was really Citlali's secret help, and that Tlapo's appointments were meant to bring her new friends.

435.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: Maghan and the Holy Sovereign
435.content: Maghan (born Dinga) was the silent attendant of the tribe's last Holy Sovereign, a blinded young mystic. She foresaw her own end, sent him to follow Xbalanque and spread heroes' stories, and told him to stab her in the heart when they met again. When Och-Kan branded her valley traitors, Maghan led the assault and killed her. She became the Mictlan Wayob, and he founded the tribe as its priest-king. The tribe keeps her statuette, Starcaller's Watch, as a sacred relic. Grainfruit lore says Maghan, guided by night spirits, grew the first Grainfruit from animal teeth watered with his own blood, so its stalk must never be casually thrown away.

436.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: Sanhaj Kompore, the Border Master
436.content: Sanhaj Kompore was a high priest, storyteller and legendary Border Master, and one of the six heroes who fought the Abyss under Tenoch 500 years ago with his Iktomisaurus Mahamba. Born silent, he travelled to the Night Kingdom in search of half his soul and returned able to see past and future. He forged the ceremonial sword Calamity of Eshu, which chiefs still keep. At the Battle of the Mare Jivari he is said to have summoned and exploded a miniature Night Kingdom, dying with Tenoch. His Ancient Name, Bidii, has passed to Ororon.

437.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: The graffiti challenge
437.content: Huitzilin, a great shaman and scroll weaver, challenged Citlali for twenty years before their first draw and became her closest friend. In old age she had her students paint provocative graffiti on Citlali's house as a challenge, believing only those brave enough to face Citlali deserved her legacy. Her disciples kept the custom after her death, calling it her dying wish. Challengers always lose, and Citlali erases their graffiti, but many go on to high posts in the tribe. Huitzilin's school still survives, split among several disciples.

438.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: Ororon's ceremony
438.content: The Masters view a fragmented soul as a bad omen. When the infant Ororon was found with one, the chief of that time planned to make him a vessel: lost souls would gather in him, and he would be sent into the Night Kingdom to return them and strengthen the Ley Lines, dying in the process. Citlali neither approved nor objected. The ceremony failed and he lived. The plan was never a secret, and Ororon never said he resented it, but some elders still carry an unspoken guilt. Ororon has asked whether Natlan would have been saved had it succeeded; Citlali says he knows the Ley Lines' state is not his fault but still feels guilty.

439.comment: Masters of the Night-Wind: Spirit-duffers and clairvoyance
439.content: During the limited-time event "Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls" (5.2), the tribesman Leyla, a spirit-duffer with no spiritual sensitivity, was talked by the Abyss Lector Enjou, posing as "Kokuchuu", into forced clairvoyance to learn about the Mare Jivari, and his spirit was lost. Citlali drew a gateway to the Night Kingdom around his body, and with Ororon and the Traveler gathered roaming spirits until he could be drawn back. The rite briefly touched the lingering spirit of Sanhaj Kompore.

440.content:
Matra (also: the Matra, Matras, Akademiya disciplinary officers): The Matra are the disciplinary officers of the Sumeru Akademiya, its executive arm for academic integrity. They hunt down and sentence researchers guilty of serious offences such as plagiarism, fraud, bribery, misappropriation of funds and forbidden research. Their leader is the General Mahamatra, Cyno. Researchers fear them: a visit from the Matra almost never goes well.

The Matra also police the trade in Knowledge Capsules and smuggled books, and apply a special seal to goods that have passed their inspection.

Structure: Matra answer to the General Mahamatra, currently Cyno, who is formally under the sages of the Akademiya. They are separate from the Mahamata, the Akademiya's civil administrative officials. The Matra have an office in the Akademiya, a canteen and a reputation for being stretched thin. A message-board post calls them short-staffed.

A Matra's usual path: the offence reaches them, a Matra visits the offender in person, and the case ends in a disciplinary action or trial. A personal visit from the General Mahamatra signals a serious offence; Tighnari remarks that most research is nowhere near significant enough to warrant a talk with a Matra. Matra are often posted away from the Akademiya: Nayab is in Sumeru City, Shohre in the House of Daena library, and Nabil at the Akademiya.

Leadership: General Mahamatra Cyno commands the Matra. He is a young man of the desert who is stern, tireless and fond of jokes that nobody finds funny.

Cyno's profile says he will judge every lawbreaker by the sages' six cardinal sins, and that even sages shall not be exempt. He once says that, as a Matra, one of his duties is to help people "remember" their mistakes. He pursues escapees across the Great Red Sand but will rescue them from danger first so that only the law may judge them. He sees the Matra as guardians of those who seek knowledge, and he accepts a researcher's nickname for the Matra, "the Akademiya's Sumpter Beasts", as an apt description of carrying the weight of the rules.

Members: Known Matra: Cyno (General Mahamatra), Nabil (a Matra who first meets the Traveler in the Akademiya in Cyno's story quest), Taj Radkani (Cyno's former senior partner, died in 3.1), Usem, Shohre, Nayab ("Relaxed Matra") and Aarav. The Matra office has a custom: after Cyno tells a joke, everyone in the room forces a laugh so that he won't start explaining it. A Matra who tries to imitate his style is punished by having their canteen meal tickets confiscated.

Shohre, in the House of Daena, dreads Cyno's jokes and, during the limited-time event A Parade of Providence, wondered whether to use his vacation as a chance to visit the office. Nayab is found at Puspa Café, fretting over a card-game deck. Taj taught Cyno polearm training and is the Matra's most important recent loss.

Goals: Keep the Akademiya's research within its laws. Cyno's profile says the sages laid down six cardinal sins, among them interfering with human evolution, tampering with life and death, and delving beyond the universe. The Matra judge breaches of these laws and the laws that evolved from them. Their purpose, as Cyno explains it, is to stop uncontrolled "wisdom" from becoming calamity.

Cyno cites Cyrus, a scholar who tutored him, who told him that without the Akademiya's laws, wisdom would turn to calamity. In Character Story 5, he is resolved to judge all lawbreakers by the six sins, "even sages".

Methods: Investigation, arrest, trial and seizure. Matra inspect and seal goods, check Knowledge Capsule transactions, and halt banned research. Files from halted projects are mostly destroyed, but some are kept as a warning in the Restricted Repository, a heavily guarded vault of the Akademiya accessible only to the General Mahamatra and trusted associates. Bribes and force are treated as aggravating, so offenders who try them are punished more severely. Cyno is described as patient with excuses. Researchers have claimed reasons including cut funding, favouritism and stolen results.

In the Sands of Solitude quest, Cyno and the Traveler investigate a Canned Knowledge smuggling ring. The Matra also use bulletin boards, posting public notices through the Akademiya message boards. Typical notices remind readers to observe protocol, warn that spreading rumours will be referred to the Matra, and announce investigations of Canned Knowledge smuggling.

History: **Before 3.0.** The Matra are the Akademiya's law enforcement. They are not described as founded at a particular time. They enforce the Akademiya's modern regulations, which Cyno says grew from six cardinal sins laid down by the sages after early researchers' experiments went too far.

**Sands of Solitude (3.1).** Nabil, a Matra, asked the Traveler for help with a Canned Knowledge smuggling case while Cyno was absent. Cyno was already investigating. The trail led to a ring seeking information on the Court of Desolation, a ruin whose study the Akademiya had banned. In the last part, All Returns to Silence, Cyno's former senior partner Taj Radkani was found to have joined the ring on purpose, leaving a trail for Cyno. Taj had lost his son Murtada, whom he had himself arrested for entering the Court of Desolation. He died in the quicksand he caused to bury the Court. Over the next four days Cyno cleared his name, the Matra arrested the traitors in the Akademiya from Taj's list of some 300 names, and some who escaped were caught by Cyno.

**Archon Quest (Chapter III).** The Matra's exact role is not covered in the pages checked. In Ever So Close, they arrived to arrest Mizri after Alhaitham defeated him.

Relations: **Researchers and the Darshans.** The Matra are feared by researchers across the Darshans, who call them demolishers or paper shredders. A Haravatat researcher coined the "Sumpter Beasts" nickname. Cyno's character stories mention cases from Amurta, Spantamad and Vahumana.
**Sages.** Cyno treats even the sages as subject to law. The sages create the rules the Matra enforce.
**The Eremites.** Cyno hails from the desert, and the proudest mercenaries are said to dare not defy him after a group was destroyed for sheltering wanted researchers. The Matra arrived to arrest Mizri of Ayn Al-Ahmar in Port Ormos.
**Cyno's friends.** Tighnari, a friend of Cyno's, warns that if Cyno chases you for work you should prepare for a nightmare. Cyno visits Collei in Gandharva Ville when he can.

Tighnari says he told the Matra that Karkata is his research assistant so that nobody touches it.

Reputation: Feared in the Akademiya, resented by researchers who say they obstruct knowledge, and quietly respected elsewhere. Researchers say the Matra "cut off the path to knowledge". Cyno does not mind: Tighnari remarks that most research is nowhere near significant enough to need a Matra.

Status as of 7.1: Active under General Mahamatra Cyno as of 7.1.

After the Sumeru Archon Quest the Akademiya was reformed under Lesser Lord Kusanali. No source found shows the Matra changing in structure or leadership.

441.content: Cyno leads the Matra. His Electro Vision, and his profile titles "Judicator of Secrets" and "General Mahamatra", are covered in his own entry. As leader he is feared by researchers, and his profile says even sages shall not be exempt from his judgement. Colleagues find his jokes dry and long to explain, and the Matra office has agreed to force a laugh after each one so he will not explain it.

442.content: Taj was a Matra and Cyno's senior partner, who taught him polearm combat and retired from field work a year before the Sands of Solitude quest, taking an administrative post. He arrested his own son Murtada for entering the banned Court of Desolation, and Murtada took his own life in prison. Taj later pretended to join the ring that had lured Murtada, left a trail for Cyno, and collapsed the Court under quicksand at the cost of his life.

443.content: Canned Knowledge, the Akademiya's knowledge capsules, is banned for private circulation: taking too much also affects health. The Matra check Knowledge Capsule transactions. When they halt dangerous research, most project files are destroyed, but some are kept in the Restricted Repository as warnings for later researchers.

444.content: The Mahamata are civil administrative officials of the Akademiya, explicitly alumni, dispatched around Sumeru. The Chinese names suggest they are a different group from the Matra.

445.content:
Mighty Mythical Beasts (also: Mighty Mythical Beasts troupe, Gaming's Wushou troupe): The Mighty Mythical Beasts is a small Wushou dance troupe in Liyue. Gaming founded and leads it, and his aim is to make the beast dance a regular sight in Liyue Harbor. He promotes it by busking and by recommending it to the clients of the transport agency where he works as a guard. It has not yet had much professional success.

The Chinese name uses a Cantonese word meaning "amazing", which gives the troupe a cheerful, big-talking character.

Members: Gaming is the founder, head and lead dancer. Dip Yeuk, a new guard at the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency, is the troupe's drummer. Gaming has taught him the basics and Dip Yeuk practises them daily. Gaming's suanni companion, Man Chai, is closely tied to the troupe's origin, but the wiki does not list it as a member.

Goals: The troupe exists to make Wushou Dance a regular fixture in Liyue Harbor. Gaming's character story says the dream still has a long road ahead.

Methods: Gaming performs in the street with drums and gongs, and announces the troupe when he is thanked for escort work. He recommends it to the transport agency's clients as a booking. The troupe trains by the same discipline as the guards: horse stance, stamina and core strength. Dip Yeuk repeats Gaming's saying that one second on stage takes ten years of training off stage.

History: Gaming loved Wushou Dance from childhood and left his family's tea business in Qiaoying Village to make a career of it in Yilong Wharf. His first attempt burned through his savings, and he took a job at the transport agency during a Lantern Rite. He later founded the Mighty Mythical Beasts formally, soon after meeting Man Chai.

In the Lantern Rite of version 4.4 (the event Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze) the troupe was featured, and its performance at Liyue's Lantern Rite was very well received. This is limited-event material: most Liyue residents saw it only as a festival act.

Relations: - **Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency**: the troupe's members are the agency's guards. A bulletin-board exchange has someone ask whether Liyue's hired muscle also moonlights as dancers, and the agency replies that one need not be surprised to find its people performing.
- **Liyue Harbor audiences**: crowds cheer, but the troupe more often gets applause than paid bookings.

Status as of 7.1: As of the pages read, the troupe remains a two-named-member amateur outfit led by Gaming, with the Lantern Rite performance its high point. No later developments were found.

446.content: Dip Yeuk is a newer guard-for-hire at the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency in Yilong Wharf, and the drummer of the Mighty Mythical Beasts. By his own account his kung fu is not yet up to standard, so he drills horse stance for hours and tries to follow Gaming's advice on training.

447.content: Wushou Dance is a Liyue performance art in which a dancer wears a beast mask and moves like a waking beast, shaking the head and blinking. Gaming's version is suanni-themed. The art needs precise movement and core strength, and the Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency's bulletin board mentions that its guards sometimes take part in it.

448.content:
Millelith (also: the Millelith, Millelith Brigade, Millelith soldiers, Millelith General Staff): The Millelith are Liyue's army and guard. They patrol the land, defend settlements against monsters and bandits, and answer to the Liyue Qixing. Their soldiers are famous for their skill with polearms, and their motto promises that evil will not prevail while they stand guard.

Their name combines Latin and Greek words for "thousand stone"; in Chinese the force is the Qianyan-jun, the Thousand Rock Army. The modern force is the successor of the Millelith Brigade that served the Geo Archon, Morax, in the Archon War.

Structure: According to Phonia of the Knights of Favonius, the Millelith concentrate on formations and the disposition of their troops, a style that demands a very high degree of awareness and discipline from every soldier. Squads are led by sergeants and unit leaders, and each unit has both offensive and defensive abilities and can split into smaller formations to suit difficult terrain. After the battle against Beisht, the Qixing reorganised the chain of command and created the General Staff, a department that gathers military advisers so they can share intelligence and divide work, rather than each strategist working alone.

The Yuheng (Keqing) introduced "scenario-based training", a way of testing a soldier's ability to raise, deploy and command forces from many angles. The assessment is stricter than the tabletop wargames made from it. All of the force's equipment comes from Blackcliff Forge.

Leadership: The Millelith report to the Liyue Qixing. Keqing, as Yuheng, drove the post-Beisht reform of the chain of command. The sources checked name no single commander-in-chief. Named personnel are mostly low-ranking: Fengyan and Lin (sergeants), Yijian (a unit leader) and Yanbo (a squad leader).

Members: Ordinary soldiers carry the White Tassel, the standard-issue polearm. Some front-line officers use the heavier halberd, and soldiers have also been seen with other weapons such as the Dark Iron Sword. Fengyan, for example, earned his sergeant's rank through skill at unarmed combat and now teaches martial arts to recruits.

Su Ding spoke for the General Staff during the 4.7 wargame event, and Turenna and Phonia, two characters in that event, comment on the force's armour and tactics. The Millelith of the distant past favoured the Lithic Spear and Lithic Blade, which modern people find too heavy to lift.

Goals: Their job is to protect Liyue's people and roads, keep order, and be ready for the day a true threat appears. Fengyan says the present Millelith rarely face the evil forces they are sworn against, but serve with the same rock-solid commitment as their predecessors. He admits that discipline in daily life can look lax.

Methods: In battle the Millelith lean on the size of their formations to overwhelm an enemy, with offence and defence built into each unit. According to Phonia, studying their tactics and formations still leaves little weakness to exploit. They also work undercover, infiltrating criminal groups to weaken or arrest them.

The force is developing a new armour of ceramic blocks wedged between layers of hardened fabric, meant to spread the force of projectiles and reduce penetration. Turenna describes this. During the Rite of Descension the Millelith also keep Liyue Harbor safe, with sergeants such as Fengyan patrolling around Yiyan Temple.

History: The Millelith began as the Millelith Brigade, raised during the Archon War to protect the people and fight monsters. Item lore says local elders swore oaths to Morax and chose soldiers. Once the war ended the force reported to the Qixing. Many Millelith soldiers died in the Chasm, fighting beside the yaksha Bosacius against the Abyss and the monsters of Khaenri'ah during the cataclysm 500 years ago.

**The Chasm.** Monsters poured out of the Chasm after an iron meteorite struck it. Morax sent the Millelith to defend the miners and help them flee. The Millelith vanguard, the thaumaturge Boyang and the maddened Bosacius used a spatial catalyst to seal the monsters in with themselves, and few survived. Boyang's brother Rongzhao, an exorcist who helped seal the space from outside, returned home but went insane, which Xiao and Yelan attribute to the yaksha's karma. In the world quest The Millennial Mountains, a stone tablet left by a Millelith soldier who lost the use of his four limbs at the Chasm leaves his armour and equipment for someone fated to claim them, and the miner Wang relates the tale that he became a famed self-taught doctor and set up the memorial to his comrades after obtaining a Vision.

**Modern reforms.** After Beisht was driven off, the Qixing moved to strengthen Liyue's military and created the General Staff.

Relations: - **Liyue Qixing**: the Millelith's masters, who set policy and reorganised the command.
- **Yaksha**: the Millelith fought beside Bosacius at the Chasm, and the yakshas were once Morax's guardians.
- **Criminal groups**: the force infiltrates and arrests them.

- **Knights of Favonius**: present at the wargame event, which also drew forces from other nations.
- **Xiao and Wangshu Inn**: the Qixing's own agents, not the Millelith, run Wangshu Inn to support the last yaksha.

Reputation: Sergeant Fengyan recalls how childhood visits to the Rite of Descension shaped his life, and the force's ancient predecessors are remembered for the sacrifice at the Chasm. The achievement for completing the world quest The Millennial Mountains is titled "The Millelith Shall Never Be Moved".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Millelith are active and still answer to the Liyue Qixing, with a General Staff and scenario-based training.

No Millelith-specific story developments after the 4.7 wargame event were found in the 5.x to 7.1 material checked. The Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya content does not feature them.

449.content: The motto, as Fengyan gives it, runs: "While rock stays hard, the mountain shall never fail; while the Millelith stands guard, evil shall never prevail." He recites it when asked about the force's history.

450.content: Five hundred years ago the Abyss pushed monsters through the Chasm. The Millelith vanguard fought beside the thaumaturge Boyang and the yaksha Bosacius, who no longer remembered his own name and was later called the Nameless Yaksha. They used the Fantastic Compass to trap the monsters in a sealed space. It needed an adeptus and a mortal to power it, so Bosacius, Boyang and the vanguard stayed inside and died. Survivors outside, such as Boyang's brother Rongzhao, carried the memory.

451.comment: Millelith: General Staff and scenario training
451.content: The General Staff is a department set up after the battle against Beisht. It brings advisers together to pool intelligence and streamline planning. Su Ding explained this during the limited-time event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation. Scenario-based training tests soldiers on organising, deploying and commanding forces. In 4.7 Su Ding told the Traveler it was a concept Yuheng promoted.

452.content:
Minghua Company (also: Minghua Bank, Minghua Trading Company): The Minghua Company, with its Minghua Bank, was the business of Gentry De'an in Liyue Harbor. A decade ago it was among the proudest firms on its street. Today the Bank is sold and the Company is languishing.

Gentry De'an blames Snezhnayan bankers, backed by the Fatui, for undercutting his businesses and forcing their way into Liyue's market. In daytime he can be found near the Adventurers' Guild, looking at his old bank.

Leadership: Gentry De'an owned and managed both the Company and the Bank. No other officer is named.

Goals: The Company has no stated goals now. De'an says that were he a young man he would fight to make a comeback, but there is little an old man can do.

History: A decade ago, everyone from Feiyun Slope to the Dockyard knew De'an's name. The Fatui's growing involvement in Liyue's economy, through the Northland Bank's foothold in the Harbor, cut into the Minghua Bank's trade. After his daughter Huachu's supposed death, he sold the bank to pay for her funeral, and a notice on the Feiyun Slope bulletin board advertises the former building.

The death was staged. The "corpse" found in a Feiyun Slope well, which fouled the water supply, was another person's, dressed as Huachu, while she and the arithmetic teacher Jianqiu eloped. De'an believes his refusal to accept the match drove her to suicide. The pair are met later at Stone Gate. In the Lantern Rite Tales event (1.3, limited-time), Huachu was homesick and the pair stopped at the Emerald Maple Inn, where Jianqiu again claimed to work for the Minghua Bank. Mr. Zhu knew of both the death and the bank's closure, grew suspicious, and chose not to pry.

Relations: - **Fatui and Northland Bank**: De'an treats them as the force that ruined him.
- **Huachu**: his second daughter, whom he calls "Chu".
- **Jianqiu**: the teacher Huachu loves, whom De'an would not accept for his daughter.

Reputation: The firm was once known across the Harbor. De'an's bitterness shows how far it has fallen: the street remembers it, but its business has dwindled.

Secrets: Huachu is alive. Only those who met the couple, such as Mr. Zhu, know it, and he does not tell. De'an still believes she died.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Company still exists with failing business and De'an remains in Liyue Harbor. No newer developments were found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

453.content:
Ministry of Civil Affairs (also: Liyue Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, General Affairs Bureau): The Ministry of Civil Affairs is the working civil administration of Liyue, a body under the Liyue Qixing headquartered at Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor. It is made up of various departments and deals with the paperwork of a trading nation: permits, ports, taxes, festivals, information and public order. It can call on the Millelith when safety is at stake. Its staff are known for being overworked and curt.

The Ministry's own explanation of its trade is "resource management": goods, information and people, exchanged and combined to solve problems. In Liyue, where commerce comes first, that makes it central to daily life. It also employs outside help. After the Traveler has finished the Archon Quest chapter that ends with Rex Lapis's departure, Ms. Yu offers paid Ministry work that feeds Liyue's reputation system.

Structure: The Ministry is not a single office but several departments, for example a Maritime Authority that administers the harbor and ships, and staff who handle commerce, labor and festivals. Named staff are modest in rank: Clerk Zhao and Yanbei are clerks, Ms. Yu is a resource manager, Nervous An administers the Maritime Authority, Muning is a specialist sent to the Chasm, and Woliu is a hydrologist. Its records are said to cover every employee in Liyue, from ordinary members of the Eight Trades to officials of Yujing Terrace. It answers to the Qixing, who set policy; the Ministry carries it out.

Nervous An supervises Linling in the Maritime Authority, and clerks like Zhao staff the counters near Feiyun Slope. Mail forwarding is also among its tasks. A library is housed in the Ministry building, and Yanfei has used it. The Ministry also hires temporary groups: the Chasm Exploration Team was assembled to investigate anomalies in the Chasm, and Muning later made it part of Huishan Hall.

Leadership: No head of the Ministry is named in the sources checked, so do not give it one. Policy comes from the Qixing, and the Ministry is the executor. Yelan claims to be a Ministry employee, but see the secrets section for why that is doubtful.

Goals: The Ministry keeps Liyue running smoothly and safely, which in Liyue means protecting trade and order. Its documented concerns are the safety of the harbor, roads, villages and festivals, honest trade and tax declarations, and early warning of anything that could harm Liyue. Yelan's profile adds a deeper aim behind the watch lists: that Liyue should never again be caught unprepared by a disaster as it was 500 years ago.

Methods: It governs by permits and paperwork: business permits, exit permits, proficiency tests, tax and customs checks, port rent, bounties and watch lists.

Typical examples. Sedan chair bearers need a permit and must pass written and road tests. Sailors need nine certifications (four major, five minor) and a two-year training and apprenticeship before sailing the sea. Business and exit permits are issued here, and transactions are checked for contraband and correct tax declarations. Outsiders register with it: Kliment cites his Ministry registration for an archaeological survey. The Ministry handles customs for imports and exports and mediates disputes; in a quest, Ganyu tells a Fatui Skirmisher to file a complaint with the Ministry. Its notice board offers temporary unemployment, medical and food stipends and reviews tax exemption and deduction applications. It also issues bounties for wanted criminals.

Intelligence is part of the job. Ganyu says she hears from the Ministry about big-time Treasure Hoarders planning a joint operation across Liyue and Mondstadt. Yelan's profile says the Ministry keeps two watch lists compiled by her: a fairly short Special Attention List of people with the power or means to cause Liyue great harm (Beidou, the Traveler and some reclusive adepti are named), and a higher-level Secret Intelligence List. Beidou knows the second exists but cannot see it.

Members: Clerk Zhao (clerk, near Feiyun Slope by day and the Xinyue Kiosk at night), Ms. Yu (resource manager who runs Ministry Missions), Nervous An (overworked administrator of the Maritime Authority), Muning (specialist posted to the Chasm), Yanbei (clerk), Woliu (hydrologist), and Mingbo, Qi Nan and Weijin, about whom little is recorded. Many staff and Millelith sent by them complain of too much work and too few people, and Zhao and An are blunt with visitors.

Yelan is listed by the wiki as a self-proclaimed member and a "non-entity" on its rosters. Ganyu says she does not know what the Ministry does, yet in her voice line about Yaoyao says someone she knows in the Ministry asked her to keep an eye on the girl.

History: The Ministry has been part of Liyue's government since the earliest content, and its founding date is not given. Documented episodes:

**The Chasm.** After an accident in the Chasm mines, the Ministry sealed the area, ordered work stopped and made its approval necessary for work to resume. In the Chasm Delvers quests, the Adventurers' Guild notes that nobody can enter without the Qixing's agreement, and the Ministry sends its specialist Muning along with a hired Chasm Exploration Team to investigate.

**Public-safety crises.** During the meteorite incident of the Unreconciled Stars event (limited-time), it sent nearly every available Millelith to guard main roads and key villages. During the Siege of Qingce it sent Millelith to protect the movement of supplies. During The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes (limited-time) it sent Millelith against Treasure Hoarders near Qingce Village. After the battle with Osial, the Traveler helped it clear flotsam from the harbor.

Relations: It stands under the Qixing, which makes policy, and gives orders to the Millelith when public safety needs them. It works with Huishan Hall and the Feiyun Commerce Guild on Chasm and commercial matters. The Adventurers' Guild depends on others' passes for restricted places. It is wary of outsiders with power: its Special Attention List includes Beidou and the Traveler. Fatui and foreign visitors are dealt with through ordinary regulation and complaint procedures.

Reputation: Liyue's people see it as essential and overstretched: there is always a queue, a form or a clerk who wants the Traveler to be quick. Yelan's profile calls it an organisation marked by transparency, because everyone's basic information is on its lists, which is exactly why her own absence from them is notable.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Ministry is still Liyue's active administration. No major Ministry-led story event after the 2026 Lantern Rite was found in the checked sources.

Secrets: The existence of the watch lists is established. What is not established is who is on the Secret Intelligence List, or what Yelan's real relationship to the Ministry is. Her own profile says she is absent from its rosters, though she compiles its lists.

454.comment: Ministry of Civil Affairs: Ministry of Civil Affairs headquarters
454.content: The Ministry is based at Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor. Nearby are Clerk Zhao and a notice board carrying Ministry announcements and sedan-chair rules. A shishi (lion-dog) statue stands outside. The building also contains a library. The Qixing's own offices are elsewhere, at Yujing Terrace.

455.comment: Ministry of Civil Affairs: Ministry watch lists
455.content: Two lists compiled by Yelan. The Special Attention List is short and names people with the power or means to cause great harm to Liyue: Beidou, the Traveler and certain reclusive adepti. The Secret Intelligence List is more classified and is understood to cover individuals and organisations the Qixing are extremely wary of; Beidou cannot see it. Yelan's stated reason is that Liyue should not be surprised by disaster again as it was 500 years ago.

456.comment: Ministry of Civil Affairs: Chasm seal
456.content: After an accident in the Chasm mines, the Ministry closed the area. Work stopped and could resume only with its approval. The Adventurers' Guild cannot enter without the Qixing's say-so, so groups like the Chasm Exploration Team were hired through the Ministry. See the Chasm Delvers quests for the investigation.

457.comment: Ministry of Civil Affairs: Ministry Missions
457.content: Ms. Yu, a resource manager, offers the Traveler paid work for the Ministry once the Traveler has finished the Liyue Archon Quest chapter that ends with Rex Lapis's departure. She says in effect that the Traveler helps the Ministry and the Ministry pays, and the available jobs depend on the Traveler's reputation.

458.content:
Mondstadt Aristocracy (also: Mondstadt's aristocracy, the Mondstadt aristocracy, Mondstadt nobility, Mondstadt nobles, Aristocratic Period, the aristocrats of Mondstadt): The Mondstadt Aristocracy was the class of noble clans who ruled Mondstadt after the fall of Decarabian's old city. They began as protectors of the people and, over centuries, became tyrants who enslaved commoners and staged gladiatorial games. The foremost clan, the Lawrences, ruled the city until Vennessa, an enslaved gladiator, led a rebellion with the help of Barbatos about a thousand years ago. Most nobles were exiled. The Knights of Favonius were founded so that nobles could never rule again.

The era still shapes Mondstadt. Its festivals partly come from noble customs, its freedom is defined against nobility, and its old families still carry reputations: the Gunnhildrs are respected as the clan that stayed honourable, while the Lawrences are widely resented.

Structure: The aristocracy was made up of clans, each claiming descent from heroes of the early days of Barbatos' Mondstadt. Named clans are the Lawrence, Gunnhildr and Imunlaukr, and the Ragnvindrs are presumably of noble standing. Other nobles belonged to no named clan, such as the family of Landrich.

The Gotini, Hlaewringi, Bructeri and Sitones clans are named in the Windborne Flower's Spruchdichtung. The late aristocracy was served by the order of "starlit knights", royal mages and a divided Church. Landrich's family produced the brothers Parsifal, Ingbert and Eberhart. Luther and Priscilla are further named aristocrats outside any clan. The Gunnhildrs held Dornman Port as a hereditary fief. After the rebellion the Gunnhildrs led a push to abolish hereditary fiefdoms and likely gave up their own.

Leadership: No single ruler stood over the whole class. In the early period Venerare led the Lawrence Clan when the new city was founded, and the leader of all the clans inscribed the clans' oath of protection beneath Barbatos' statue. By the end the Lawrences were effectively the rulers of the city. The manga calls the ruler at the time of Vennessa's rebellion Lord Lawrence, and names his son Barca Lawrence as heir.

Goals: The early aristocracy's role was to defend Mondstadt and keep Barbatos' freedom, an oath written beneath a statue of the god. In the late period the nobles instead protected their own power, with the Lawrences seeing themselves as overlords and kings.

Methods: By the late period the nobles kept the people ignorant: knowledge of the past was suppressed, and anyone seen as a threat could be enslaved for labour or entertainment. The knight order of the time served them and the Church justified their rule.

In the early period, nobles hunted to show strength and shared the spoils with the people, and the royal mages taught virtue and kept the history. Later the nobles tore down the statue of Barbatos to erase their oath and the mages stopped speaking of history. The gladiatorial games, once religious ceremonies, were turned into bloodsport for noble enjoyment. Nobles came to consider swords the only proper weapon, and looked down on bows and spears as tools for commoners and gladiators. The Lawrences' own sense of identity moved, in the words of weapon lore, from conquerors to overlords to kings.

History: After Barbatos freed the people from Decarabian, the Gunnhildr, Imunlaukr and Lawrence clans were prominent in founding the new city. Barbatos left so he would never become a tyrant, and the clans took over. The Lawrences rose to be the foremost clan and drifted into tyranny, while the Gunnhildrs refused to follow. Vennessa, a Muratan enslaved with her people after fleeing Ursa the Drake, became the gladiator known as the Lionfang Knight. In the manga's account, the Lawrences pitted her whole clan against Ursa for their freedom, and with Barbatos' help she drove the drake off. The rebellion that followed was broader than that one battle. Most nobles were exiled, uncorrupted houses such as the Gunnhildrs stayed, and Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius and restored the Church.

**Early period.** Nobles set up festivals such as Ludi Harpastum, Windblume and Weinlesefest for the people's benefit. The Church split in the late period between clergy backing the nobility and those opposed. In the manga's account Vennessa and Venti met on Ludi Harpastum, which angered Barca Lawrence.

**Failed earlier revolt.** Before Vennessa, the Wanderer's Troupe, a travelling band of musicians and fighters, tried and failed to overthrow the aristocracy in Mondstadt. Most of its members died, were enslaved or fled. The Dawnlight Swordswoman was turned into a gladiator but kept singing of freedom, and her example inspired Ragnvindr to rise against the nobles. Kreuzlied, a Lawrence who had abandoned his clan, survived because of his lineage and founded an underground society that later helped Vennessa.

**The wider rebellion.** According to Venti's Character Story, Barbatos forged a secret treaty in which the aristocrats sold all of Mondstadt, soldiers included, to Morax. The nobles' own soldiers, fearing enslavement, turned to Vennessa's side, leaving the clan with few loyal troops. Ragnvindr and the Gunnhildrs, who had refused to follow the other nobles, also supported the rebellion.

**Aftermath.** Ragnvindr converted a noble bathhouse into the first Mondstadt library, according to the wiki timeline. Vennessa ended her life ascending to Celestia at Windrise, where the great oak now stands.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: founded by Vennessa to replace the aristocracy. The order of "starlit knights" that served the nobles was a different, earlier body.
- **Church of Favonius**: the Church split during the late period, and the higher clergy backed the nobility. Vennessa restored it afterwards.
- **Lawrence Clan**: the main ruling house. See its own entry.
- **Gunnhildr Clan**: maintained its honour, broke with the Imunlaukrs, and was allowed to stay; it still supplies many of Mondstadt's knights and clergy.
- **Barbatos**: left Mondstadt so as not to become a tyrant, and returned when the land cried out for freedom.

- **Ragnvindr Clan**: Ragnvindr, a squire, joined the rebellion and his family later became one of Mondstadt's most prominent.
- **Fatui**: in the present day Eula's uncle Schubert conspired with the Fatui to restore Lawrence rule, and the Traveler and Eula foiled the plot.

Reputation: The aristocracy is remembered as a cautionary tale. The Lawrence Clan especially carries a poor reputation, and some citizens grow hostile at the mere mention of the name.

Before she joined the Knights, Eula reports that almost every shop refused to take her money. Eula says one aristocratic tradition is to dance for loved ones on one's birthday, which grants the blessing of ancestors to both. The Lawrences kept up a strict regimen of combat, dance, cooking and etiquette, stressing appearances.

Status as of 7.1: The aristocracy no longer exists as a ruling class. Descendants of its clans, especially the Lawrences, live in Mondstadt as ordinary citizens under suspicion.

Eula, a Lawrence, serves as a captain in the Knights of Favonius. Her relatives denounced her as a traitor. Another Lawrence, Lessig, left for Sumeru hoping to restore the clan's honour, and found that nobody cared. As of 7.1 no new aristocracy-related story was found in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content checked.

459.content:
The Lawrence Clan was the foremost clan of the aristocracy and its last ruling house. In Decarabian's time they were said to have lived outside the city and survived in the frozen wilderness, which made them see themselves as conquerors. Their emblem is the Glacial Seal. They were disgraced and exiled after Vennessa's rebellion. Eula carries the seal today. Other living members include her uncle Schubert and Lessig.

Many Lawrence traditions survive. The curriculum covers combat, dance, cooking and etiquette, and Eula's character stories describe the Dance of Sacrifice, whose third act, Flickering Candlelight, is passed down the family. Members cook for themselves rather than rely on commoners. The clan has strict phrasings for addressing others, which outsiders are not supposed to learn.

460.content: The rebellion that ended aristocratic rule began, in the manga's account, when an enslaved Muratan gladiator named Vennessa was made to fight Ursa the Drake in the arena in return for her people's freedom. Barbatos, travelling as the bard Venti, helped her win. A wider uprising followed; a forged treaty selling Mondstadt to Morax turned the nobles' soldiers against them, and most nobles were exiled. Afterwards Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius. See the Knights of Favonius entry for the later history.

461.comment: Mondstadt Aristocracy: The Wanderer's Troupe's revolt
461.content: The Wanderer's Troupe was a band of travelling musicians and fighters that made its last stand in Mondstadt, where it tried and failed to overthrow the nobles. Its Conductor was killed in the fighting. The Sojourner died protecting his allies. The Dawnlight Swordswoman was enslaved as a gladiator and kept singing of freedom, influencing Ragnvindr. Kreuzlied survived and went on to build an underground society against the aristocracy.

462.content:
Mondstadt Wine Guild (also: Mondstadt Wine Appreciation Guild, the Wine Guild): The Mondstadt Wine Guild, also called the Mondstadt Wine Appreciation Guild, is the trade body of Mondstadt's wine industry. Its Executive Chairman is Elzer, who also manages affairs at Dawn Winery for Diluc. It is allied with the winery.

Canon says very little about the guild itself. Almost everything known comes from Elzer's open-world dialogue at Dawn Winery.

Leadership: Elzer is the guild's Executive Chairman, called Chief Executive in his own dialogue.

Elzer served at Dawn Winery while Crepus was alive and says Crepus was like a father to him. After Crepus died and Diluc left Mondstadt in grief and anger, Elzer took on much of the winery's business and, some time later, became chairman. He says he does not hide the role or do it for show.

Elzer explains that, given Dawn Winery's standing in Mondstadt, there is barely any difference between running the winery and running the whole industry. In his words, anyone who wants to talk business at the winery should talk to him directly, because Diluc does not trouble himself much with such matters.

Members: Elzer is the only named member. No other members are named in canon.

Goals: The guild's purpose is never stated outright. From Elzer's dialogue, it looks after the commercial side of Mondstadt's wine trade, including partnerships with merchants and festival organisers.

During the Weinlesefest event "Of Ballads and Brews" (3.1, limited-time), Elzer greeted visitors as potential Weinlesefest partners and said he had Diluc's permission to help. That event material is not a permanent feature of the guild.

Relations: - **Dawn Winery**: the guild's ally, and Elzer's other post. The winery belongs to Diluc, and the Ragnvindr family founded it.
- **Diluc**: Elzer's master. Elzer is one of the few people who know Diluc is the rumoured "Darknight Hero".

- **Angel's Share and Cat's Tail**: Elzer once tried to headhunt Diona for Angel's Share after her drink-mixing made Cat's Tail popular. He did not know she hates alcohol, and she bit him.

Status as of 7.1: No change to the guild was found in any version from 1.0 to 7.1. Elzer remains at Dawn Winery in the open world.

463.content: Elzer is a formal, businesslike open-world NPC at Dawn Winery. He handles the winery's major affairs when Diluc is away and is Executive Chairman of the Mondstadt Wine Guild. He grew up in Crepus's service, took on part of the winery's burden after Crepus's death, and says he did so partly because he thought Crepus would have wanted it. He knows Diluc is the "Darknight Hero".

464.content:
Muratans (also: Muratan, the Muratans, the lost seventh tribe, the lost tribe): The Muratans were Natlanese exiles from the seventh tribe of the old Grand Alliance. After the civil war that ended Och-Kan's rule, one group of the defeated tribe accepted exile and wandered the land for generations before settling in Mondstadt. There they eventually forgot their heritage and the name Muratan. The best-known Muratan is Vennessa, the gladiator who led the rebellion against Mondstadt's aristocracy.

Their sister group, who refused to leave Natlan, became the Tenochtzitoc.

Structure: No Muratan government or leadership is described. They were a wandering people, and Vennessa's story shows them as a clan led by elders and families. Their knowledge passed down through the generations was mostly combat and survival technique rather than history.

Members: Historical figures tied to the Muratans:
- Vennessa: a "flame-touched Muratan", slave warrior, and later first Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.
- Lind: Vennessa's younger sister (named in the manga; relation per the wiki).
- Tenoch: a warrior of the Muratan tribe who was exiled from it before the Cataclysm and who later gathered heroes against the Abyss.

Vennessa inherited the Muratan "fiery-red" vermilion hair, according to the wiki's description of her.

Goals: The Mondstadt Muratans wanted food, safety and freedom. Vennessa fought in the Colosseum to win her people's freedom. The Tenochtzitoc branch refused to abandon their homeland.

History: Before the civil war, the Muratans were the seventh Natlanese tribe in the Grand Alliance. After the Alliance's collapse, the tribe split. One group accepted exile and wandered for generations before settling in Mondstadt. The other refused to leave and was eventually allowed to settle far from the other tribes, at Tenochtzitoc, now the Easybreeze Holiday Resort.

**Mondstadt.** By Vennessa's time, around a thousand years ago, the Muratans were enslaved by Mondstadt's nobles. According to the manga, Ursa the Drake hounded her clan for four days, starving them, and they fled into the city only to be enslaved. Vennessa fought in the Colosseum, and with Barbatos, Ragnvindr and others overthrew the aristocracy. The descendants of the Muratans had by then forgotten the word.

**Tenochtzitoc.** The Tenochtzitoc were Anemo warriors, who lived in neglect for millennia. When the Cataclysm came, the Bakunawa killed all of them except Tenoch, who had been exiled from his tribe earlier. Tenoch died as a sacrifice in Sanhaj's border spell against the Bakunawa in the Mare Jivari.

Relations: - **Grand Alliance**: the Muratans belonged to its seventh tribe.
- **Och-Kan**: the wiki places the tribe on his side in the civil war.
- **Mondstadt aristocracy**: enslaved them, and was overthrown by Vennessa.
- **Knights of Favonius**: founded by Vennessa, a Muratan.
- **Tenochtzitoc**: the sister group who stayed in Natlan.

Reputation: Natlan's Easybreeze Holiday Resort stages actors playing Tenochtzitoc tribe members as part of its themed attractions, according to Pucli in the quest. Mondstadt remembers Vennessa as a hero of freedom, not as a Muratan.

Status as of 7.1: No Muratan community is known to survive under that name as of 7.1. Their legacy lives on in Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius and its ideal of freedom.

465.content: Tenochtzitoc was the settlement of the Muratans who refused to leave Natlan, set in a remote, barren part of the nation where the Easybreeze Holiday Resort now stands. Its people were warriors who wielded Anemo and were neglected for millennia. When the Cataclysm arrived, they were the first to fight and fell one by one. Only Tenoch, who had been exiled earlier, survived. Enjou calls the place where their bones were buried the Windless Land.

466.content: Vennessa is called a "flame-touched Muratan", a gladiator enslaved by Mondstadt's nobles. The wiki notes that by her time the Muratans in Mondstadt had forgotten their heritage and the term Muratan. Her own entry holds her story as the first Grand Master and Dandelion Knight.

467.content:
Mutual Aid Network (also: Mutual Aid Society, the Mutual Aid Network): The Mutual Aid Network is a small society of prisoners in the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's underwater prison. Vautrin, a former Garde captain exiled there, founded it about 400 years ago. Its members are mostly minor offenders who band together so that stronger inmates cannot push them around. Their badge is based on Vautrin's Medal of Peace.

Membership is free and has no compulsory events. The Network sees itself as a way of getting through a sentence with dignity, not as a gang, and it is not the same group as the dissolved Beret Society.

Structure: The Network is informal. Vautrin was its first president, and it has kept a badge, a pamphlet and a short list of principles ever since. Canon names no current president or ranks. Joining costs nothing and no event is compulsory. Members the Traveler meets are Millereau, who hands out the pamphlet in the Dormitory Block, Gordes, and Auriol.

Gordes stresses that the Network has never had many members and has little reputation, but that its members treat each other like family. Millereau mentions that a new member had joined the previous month, so recruitment is slow and steady.

Goals: Members help one another, work for justice and accept lawful judgment. They try to do something useful with their time inside and to face up to the crimes they committed.

The pamphlet gives three principles: help each other, do all you can to further justice, and do not detest just judgment. It encourages cleaning, exercising, tutoring and studying, and hopes members will support one another as they face their crimes and welcome the future together.

Members: - **Vautrin**: founder and first president, deceased. His own file carries his full story.
- **Millereau**: the Network's advertiser in the Dormitory Block. He greets passers-by with the phrase "Help each other".
- **Gordes**: a member who explains the Network's history to the Traveler and helped put down Domenico's rebellion.
- **Auriol**: a member who says the Network turned a miserable sentence into one with friends and shared purpose.

Auriol describes the first president as powerful but never using that strength against anyone, and says every member respects him. Members are chiefly people with minor offences. Gordes insists none of them has committed a serious crime and that they are not especially strong, which is why they are at a natural disadvantage inside the Fortress.

Methods: The Network's main weapon is solidarity: weaker prisoners stick together so that others will not pick on them. Members tutor, study, clean and exercise, and keep to the Fortress's rules. They are willing to act when order is threatened. During the failed rebellion of Domenico against Neuvillette, Network members stepped in and, in Gordes's words, taught him a lesson. Domenico complained that nobody would team up with him, the Network in particular.

History: **Founding.** Vautrin was the captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol when Neuvillette brought the Melusines into Fontainian society. His friend, the Melusine Carole, died after hardliners opposed to Neuvillette framed her, and in revenge Vautrin killed those hardliners. Neuvillette sentenced him for abuse of authority. He was exiled to the Fortress of Meropide, where he never showed physical or verbal aggression, urged weaker criminals to stick together, and founded the Network about 400 years ago.

**The badge.** Vautrin designed the Network's badge from the Medal of Peace that Neuvillette had made for him. Neuvillette says he crafted two such medals, for Carole and Vautrin. Carole's was lost in a fire, so the surviving one should be Vautrin's. Members today know the badge only as a symbol, and Auriol has never seen the medal itself.

**The Traveler's investigation (4.1, In a New Light).** While visiting the Fortress with Neuvillette during the Diluvies Chapter, the Traveler and Paimon notice inmates wearing the familiar badge. Questions to Auriol, Millereau and Gordes reveal the Network's history. Wriothesley, the Fortress's Duke, later says he had noticed the small group when he took over. He studied its founder and reasoned that Vautrin's courtroom anger had been staged to prove Neuvillette's fairness to the undecided. Neuvillette reflects with regret on that trial.

Relations: Wriothesley, who runs the Fortress, regards the Network as small but principled. Neuvillette has a personal link to its founder and the badge. Among inmates, the Network opposes bullying and rebellion, and has no recorded link to any group outside the Fortress.

Reputation: Gordes admits the Network has little reputation. Wriothesley sees it as a group that always stood up for what was right.

Status as of 7.1: As of the 4.1 Diluvies Chapter, the Network is active in the Fortress of Meropide and canon records no later change.

It is not mentioned in the 6.x Nod-Krai or the 7.0 to 7.1 Snezhnaya content. A similarly named group, the Mutual Aid Advancement Network, appears in a Version 7.0 limited event but is a separate organisation.

468.comment: Mutual Aid Network: Mutual Aid Network Badge and Pamphlet
468.content: Members of the Network wear a badge on their chests, designed by Vautrin from the Medal of Peace he received from Neuvillette. The pamphlet lists three principles: help each other, do all you can to further justice, and do not detest just judgment. It states that membership is free, that there are no compulsory events, and that members should do what they are able: cleaning, exercising, tutoring, studying. Its closing wish is for members to face their crimes in the Fortress, encourage and support one another, and welcome the future together.

469.comment: Mutual Aid Network: Vautrin's Founding and Trial
469.content: Vautrin killed the hardliners who had framed his friend Carole, and was sentenced by Neuvillette and exiled to Meropide. In court he showed fury, but in prison he was disciplined and non-violent. Wriothesley suggests the court display was a deliberate act to prove Neuvillette's impartiality, which Vautrin trusted him to show. Treat that as an inference, not stated fact. Use Vautrin's own file for more.

470.comment: Mutual Aid Network: Mutual Aid Advancement Network (Snezhnaya event)
470.content: In the limited-time 7.0 event Mutual Aid in Bloom: Into the Frostlands, the Traveler joins a group called the Mutual Aid Advancement Network, managed by an enthusiastic young Snezhnayan girl named Chichikova. Its stated aim is to pool diverse talents to help more people with a wider range of challenges, and its camp has a storage device for sharing spare equipment. It is a separate group from the Fontainian prison society, and canon shows no connection.

471.content:
Narzissenkreuz Institute (also: Narzissenkreuz orphanage, the Institute (orphanage), Narcissus Cross Institute): The Narzissenkreuz Institute was an orphanage and school in Fontaine that raised orphans and the children of criminals. An Oceanid, Lyris, was its Director, and the retired admiral Basil Elton was its Vice Director. It scattered during the cataclysm 500 years ago, but its alumni, among them Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin, Rene and Jakob, went on to shape Fontaine for good and ill.

The building stood over the ruins of an older civilisation. Life there was gentle, with make-believe adventures and afternoon tea. Its legacy is bittersweet: its children founded both the Fontaine Research Institute and, separately, the secret Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

Treat the Institute as a lost home: almost every later character connected to it is defined by what they did after it was gone.

Structure: The Director was always an Oceanid, because the post was created in honour of the first Hydro Archon, Egeria. Lyris was a gentle Oceanid who played with the children but, per the Court of Fontaine's register of Oceanids, was not good with cause and effect or counting. The Vice Director, chosen for "exceptional moral quality and ability", was the practical manager: Basil Elton, who took the post on retiring as Admiral of the Fontaine Navy. The institute was part of a public welfare system and, being built over ruins, was described as a home that would see neither sun nor moon.

Children were raised together across generations. The "second-to-last" generation included Basil herself, Emanuel Guillotin, Karl Ingold and Dwight Lasker, who stayed friends for life. Carter Scherbius also belonged. The last generation included Rene de Petrichor, Jakob, Alain Guillotin and Mary-Ann Guillotin.

Leadership: Lyris (Director) and Basil Elton (Vice Director). Lyris regarded Basil as her assistant, but Basil actually ran the orphanage's affairs. Basil was an easygoing woman, beloved by the children, who baked and made refreshments that the children thought were the best part of the day.

Basil's old ship, the Sponsian, had been the pride of the Fontaine Navy. When the Armada was disbanded after an incident she retired, and was picked for the Vice Director's post, which an unnamed person in the records joked about. She learned baking over a few years at the Institute, although her cooking was poor in her youth. A dark-green feather on her hat fascinated the children.

Members: Known members from 500 years ago: Lyris, Basil Elton, Emanuel Guillotin, Karl Ingold, Dwight Lasker, Carter Scherbius, Alain Guillotin, Jakob, Mary-Ann Guillotin and Rene de Petrichor. The children are minors in the Institute-era accounts; they are described here only factually, by what they did and what happened to them.

- Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin: siblings. Alain played a champion in the children's games; he later enrolled in the Institute of Natural Philosophy and eventually founded the Fontaine Research Institute. Mary-Ann joined the Marechaussee Phantom.
- Rene and Jakob: Rene cast as the "fell dragon" in the games, Jakob as a knight (per the artifact text). Rene's notes show they went to the Girdle of the Sands with Karl to research energy sources, and both later founded the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.
- Dwight Lasker went on to direct the Institute of Natural Philosophy. He visits Basil's grave in the present.

Goals: To house, feed and raise orphans and the children of criminals. Beyond that the Institute had no known political aim.

Play was part of the routine. Children acted out Narzissen champions, wicked mages, evil dragons and heroes, with the Vice Director's tea breaks pausing every adventure. The story of the hero Narzissenkreuz that Alain had them play became the allegory Mary-Ann later told Lyris.

History: The founding date is unknown, but the Institute kept an Oceanid Director from the start. When the cataclysm came, both Lyris and Basil were called away to deal with it, and expected not to return. Basil placed the children with trusted friends, and the Institute flooded and was lost. Basil died at sea in the last battle against the beast Elynas. The Director and the "sisters" she left with never came back to the children. The members scattered: some were taken in by the Marechaussee Phantom or the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, others by explorers who took them abroad.

Before leaving, the Vice Director gave Jakob the dark-green feather from her hat for safekeeping and entrusted Rene with another child's care, according to artifact text in which the children's names are blanked. Rene and Jakob later went to the Girdle of the Sands with Karl Ingold. Alain enrolled in the Institute of Natural Philosophy, Mary-Ann joined the Marechaussee Phantom, and Rene and Jakob joined the Institute of Natural Philosophy on Alain's recommendation.

Relations: - **Marechaussee Phantom**: took some of the orphans in, and later hunted the Ordo.
- **Institute of Natural Philosophy**: where Alain, Rene and Jakob studied; Dwight Lasker directed it.
- **Fontaine Research Institute**: founded later by Alain Guillotin.
- **Narzissenkreuz Ordo**: the secret society of Rene and Jakob; unrelated to the orphanage as an organisation, but made up of its former children.

- **Annapausis**: the Institute's location now. A character, Seymour, confirms the orphanage ruins' coordinates match Annapausis.
- **Egeria**: the Director's post honours her as the first Hydro Archon.

Reputation: Little is known of its public standing. The only official views come from records that treat it as a branch of the public welfare system, and from the Court of Fontaine's Oceanid register, which labels Lyris as affectionate and caring.

Status as of 7.1: Gone for 500 years. Its ruins are submerged beneath Annapausis.

No new Institute developments were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

472.content: Lyris was the Oceanid Director. She was tall and gentle, played with the children, and relied on her Vice Director. She returned to the flooded Institute after the cataclysm, saddened, and swam around its ruins. Mary-Ann once told her a fairy tale in which Lyris was a princess. Rene and Jakob persuaded her to join the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, where she was called the Red Empress; her Oceanid essence was used in the Ordo's experiment, and she later absorbed Mary-Ann's personality in the clash at Elynas.

473.comment: Narzissenkreuz Institute: Basil Elton, the Vice Director
473.content: Basil Elton was a former admiral of the Fontaine Navy and a childhood alumna of the Institute. She became its Vice Director after retiring and was the one who really ran it. When the cataclysm came she sent the children to trusted friends and sailed on the repaired Sponsian against Elynas. The ship broke in two and she died. People still visit her grave, including Dwight Lasker.

474.comment: Narzissenkreuz Institute: Annapausis and the Institute ruins
474.content: The Institute's coordinates are the same as those of the submerged Annapausis, according to Seymour in Search in the Algae Sea. The place reappears in the Ann of the Narzissenkreuz quests as a dreamlike castle realm built by an Oceanid out of memories of the Institute. Ann says the assembly hall is where the children studied, always lively though never sunlit.

475.content: The Nymph's Dream artifact set holds most of what the game says about the Institute's daily life and its end: the tea breaks, the feather on Basil's hat, the children's role-play, and the scattering after the cataclysm. Its text is poetic and sometimes blanks out names, so the wiki's identifications (for example of who took in which child) are partly inferences.

476.content:
Narzissenkreuz Ordo (also: the Ordo, Ordo of Narzissenkreuz, Narcissus Cross Society): The Narzissenkreuz Ordo was a Fontainian secret society founded by Rene de Petrichor and his adoptive brother Jakob Ingold. Convinced a second flood would end the world, it sought to fuse countless wills into one being able to survive it. Its base was the Tower of Ipsissimus. It is defunct as of 4.2.

The name means "Narcissus Cross" and is shared with the Narzissenkreuz Institute where the founders grew up. Its style mixed scholarship, ritual and showmanship. The Ordo appears only through the past: the Enigmatic Pages and the Fontaine world quests.

Structure: The Master, Narzissenkreuz, led; Jakob Ingold served as his right hand. Members held clearance levels 1 to 4.

Clearance came with exams and a reading list of the Ordo's ideals. Those who could not pass but gave much, such as sponsors, received honorary levels. The Ordo hid among, and recruited from, the Institute of Natural Philosophy. The tower itself expresses its creed. Its plaque calls Ipsissimus an old Remurian idea of a will able to rule, sustain and destroy the world, and presents spiritual evolution through four ages: Hyperborea, Natlantea, Remuria and the present Khraun-Arya (the Ordo's own names, not a rival to Akademiya findings).

Leadership: Narzissenkreuz, the Master, is Rene after he dissolved himself and was reborn in a body drawn from the Oceanid Lyris, Carter Scherbius and Alain's watch. Jakob built him.

Rene was the planner and Jakob the performer who designed rituals and won people over. After the Master's creation Jakob ran the society day to day and hid that the first ritual had failed.

Jakob's grip hardened after Rene's near-loss: he grew used to deception and was ready to use defecting members as test subjects. The Master believed his plan should leave a place for Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin. He is also said to have created Caterpillar, the hilichurl with human speech.

Members: Rene and Jakob (founders), the Master, the Oceanid Lyris ("Red Empress"), Caterpillar, and scholars and patrons of lower levels.

Certificates in the tower name Madam M. Laveaux (Level 4), Ms. E. Lenormand and Ms. Giuffria (Level 3), Erich (Level 2) and Eichi Karasawa, an Inazuman scholar and novelist (Level 1).

Mr. Griffin L. Randolph and Susannah held honorary Level 1; the wiki also lists Mr. Eliphas, Mr. Forsamiro and Ms. Zenaida, with little canon detail. Lenormand was promoted by exception for spreading the teachings, Giuffria's injured leg was healed by the Master, and Erich, a historian from the Institute of Natural Philosophy, joined the Ordo at Jakob's invitation after the Institute disbanded. The Master dissolved and absorbed three agents sent against the society, among them Emanuel Guillotin and the Champion Duelist Marfisa. Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin refused to join. Dwight Lasker, the Institute's director, received a report about strange activity and asked Emanuel to look into it.

Goals: To outlive the end of the world. Rene's "world-formula" predicted a flood, and the Ordo meant to merge many wills into a Descender-like being.

The method was to use the Primordial Sea and an Oceanid to gather the egos of all Fontainians into one consciousness, freed from bodies and separation. According to Caterpillar, Narzissenkreuz taught that one's own will is an obstacle and that receiving a Vision is a "guaranteed path to destruction".

Later, Jakob's final version was to reverse the Seal of Chymical Marriage, which he described as an ancient ritual that sealed off the source of life, reforge the Holy Blade, free the Primordial Sea and bring Rene back so all souls were preserved as one. The Ordo also drew on Golden Troupe techniques, whose symbols Rene linked to the Institute's archives.

Methods: Research and ritual. The Ordo gathered knowledge from Remuria and Khaenri'ah ruins and from archives, and ran initiations, reading lists and ceremonies with the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz. It also experimented on people: Carter Scherbius, Alain's sick assistant, was treated with materials from Elynas, which failed and ended Alain's friendship with the founders. Rene had earlier saved Jakob with the Abyss's power, making him a "neohuman".

Later experiments targeted defecting members. The founders rebuilt a Circle of Four Orthants and a Tree of Emanation from ancient records and posted members to candidate sites to find the nodes. Rene's notes call the ritual behind the sword "extremely effective witchcraft" that exploits the situation. Caterpillar says the Master led ceremonies with the Holy Blade "in accordance with ancient dictates".

History: **Roots.** Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold grew up in the Narzissenkreuz Institute, an orphanage run by the Oceanid Lyris and her Vice Director Basil Elton, after the Siege of Poisson. During the cataclysm the Director and Vice Director left and never came back, and the Institute disbanded. Rene and Jakob went to the Girdle of the Sands with Karl Ingold, studied Khaenri'ahn technology and derived the world-formula.

**Founding.** Back in Fontaine they joined the Institute of Natural Philosophy through Alain Guillotin. Alain would not believe their results. After the failed attempt on Carter, Rene turned the scholars who had become believers into a society. They built a headquarters in the Morte Region, the Tower of Ipsissimus.

**Rebirth.** Rene found Lyris, still haunting the sunken Institute, and brought her into the project. Rene obtained the Holy Blade at great cost and made himself the first subject. The ritual failed, but Jakob built Narzissenkreuz from Lyris's essence, Carter's remains and Alain's pocket watch and placed Rene's mind in him. The Master later calculated the Doomsday Clock from the world-formula.

**Downfall.** The Court of Fontaine declared the Ordo an illegal extremist group and sealed the tower. The Master absorbed agents and failed to win over Alain. He sent Jakob, Lyris and many members to Elynas, where they were used as bait, and the Marechaussee Hunters, led by Alain and Mary-Ann, defeated them. Lyris absorbed Mary-Ann's personality and Mary-Ann was listed as missing in action, while Narzissenkreuz fell into "the chasm that dissolves all things", the Primordial Sea beneath the tower. Caterpillar was jailed in the Fortress of Meropide about 400 years before the main story.

Relations: - **Narzissenkreuz Institute**: the founders' childhood home and the source of the Ordo's name. The Ordo was built partly on the Institute's archives.
- **Institute of Natural Philosophy**: the Ordo's recruiting ground. It was hidden within the Institute, and some staff left with it.
- **Guillotin family**: Alain and Mary-Ann were old friends and refused to join. Emanuel was absorbed by the Master. They were the main force against the society.
- **Court of Fontaine and the Marechaussee Phantom**: declared the Ordo illegal. The tower's sealing notice carries Alain Guillotin's and Neuvillette's signatures.
- **Golden Troupe and Remuria**: sources of the techniques the Ordo tried to reverse.

Reputation: To the law the Ordo was a criminal extremist organisation. Caterpillar remembers most members as kind, yet calls the Ordo the chief culprit of a great sin.

Status as of 7.1: Defunct as of 7.1. The Master lies at rest in Annapausis, Jakob was lost in the Doomsday Clock's collapse and the tower has sunk.

The Traveler resealed the Primordial Sea. Caterpillar, Ann and Seymour live on; other survivors are unnamed. Nothing new about the Ordo appeared in 5.x to 7.1 in the sources checked.

477.content: The Tower of Ipsissimus, also called the Tower of Gestalt, is the Ordo's headquarters in the Morte Region. Its top is a hidden meeting chamber with the Doomsday Clock, reachable through a book in the Institute of Natural Philosophy. The tower was sealed by court order and, once the 4.2 quest Savior's Wake is complete, sinks permanently to the sea floor. Mek guardians left behind when it was sealed protect the lowest level and the seal over the Primordial Sea. Inside, floor certificates list members and their clearance levels.

478.content: The Doomsday Clock is mounted in the Ordo's meeting chamber, where it was set by Narzissenkreuz using the world-formula to count down the apocalypse. When it strikes midnight, the apocalypse is meant to come. Caterpillar notes that when he was there, the Ordo thought the end was far off and the point was to stop it for later generations, but that if the clock is accurate it is now "not far off". In Search in the Algae Sea it strikes its final hour as Jakob declares the appointed time has come, and a giant hand falls.
