479.comment: Narzissenkreuz Ordo: Clearance levels of the Ordo
479.content: Members of the Ordo held clearance levels from one to four, depending on their work and conduct. Honorary levels went to people who could not complete the tests but had contributed significantly, such as patrons. Level 1 required finishing the Ordo's reading list and understanding its ideals. The wealthy sponsor Mr. Randolph failed the tests because he could not remember the keywords, and Susannah, whose scones and cookies brought Jakob and the Master "lucky" rewards, never finished the list; both were made honorary Level 1 members. Madam Laveaux, the highest listed, held Level 4.

480.comment: Narzissenkreuz Ordo: Enigmatic Pages and the Book of Revealing
480.content: Rene's notes, called the Enigmatic Pages, were hidden in Elynas and found by the Melusine Canotila, who studied them in the Book of Revealing. They cover his reading of an ancient order's texts, his world-formula, Jakob's transformation and Carter's failed treatment, the founding of the society, visiting the Director, the sword as a "key", Lyris's persuasion and his final decision to dissolve himself. Later pages in the Master's voice describe his rebirth, the mission sent to Elynas and Alain's refusal.

481.comment: Narzissenkreuz Ordo: Jakob Ingold in the Ordo
481.content: Jakob was born to a Fleuve Cendre family and was raised with Rene in the Narzissenkreuz Institute. Rene saved him with the Abyss's power and made him the first neohuman, able to turn into an Iniquitous Baptist. In the Ordo he became Rene's right hand, a ritual designer and showman who cried easily in his youth. After Rene's failed rebirth he led the Ordo, deceived members and experimented on defectors in order to bring Rene back. Centuries later he reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage in the hope of freeing the Primordial Sea, then was lost when the Doomsday Clock's hand fell. See his own entry for more.

key: Incomplete Order of the New Cosmos
482.content: Narzissenkreuz is what Rene de Petrichor became when he dissolved himself and was placed in a Hydro Tulpa body that drew on Lyris, Carter and Alain's watch. His memories of the failed rebirth were erased. He absorbed enemy agents' minds, taught the Ordo that a personal Vision is a path to ruin and created Caterpillar. In the Primordial Sea in 4.2 he fought the Traveler and Ann, convinced that he could free everyone from the disaster. After his defeat, he accepted Mary-Ann's forgiveness and faded away to rest.

483.comment: Narzissenkreuz Ordo: Lyris, the Red Empress
483.content: Lyris, the former Director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute and an Oceanid, was persuaded by Rene and Jakob to join the Ordo although she was reluctant. In the society she held the title Red Empress, and her essence was used to extract egos for merging. Her health declined as the project went on. During the Elynas clash, her mind merged with Mary-Ann's, which led to the Oceanid Mary-Ann in Annapausis and later Ann. In the sources, Lyris herself is said to have longed to return to the days when the Institute's children played.

484.comment: Narzissenkreuz Ordo: Caterpillar and the Ordo
484.content: Caterpillar is a hilichurl that the Master gave human speech, memory and a name in the Ordo, Chrysalis of the Phantasmic Moth, in the hope he would one day become human. After a task for his master failed, he was jailed in the Fortress of Meropide around 400 years before the main story. He regards the Ordo with mixed feelings, remembers most members as kind and does not call himself human. He helped the Traveler in Fontaine and in 4.2 helped reach the sunken tower. His own origin is still partly lost to him.

485.content:
Northern Intelligence Network (also: the intelligence network, the black market of intel): The Northern Intelligence Network is an underground organisation in Nod-Krai that works as a forum, or in Varka's words a black market, for intelligence. Well-connected people trade what they know for payment, with no real rules or regulations. It is run by Nefer, its current representative, and sells to clients of any faction across the world, though it has no foothold in Liyue.

Its main point of sale is the Curatorium of Secrets, Nefer's ordinary-looking agency in Nasha Town, which serves as its front. Anyone may enter the Curatorium, but only people with a "key" are admitted to the inner sanctum that is the Network. The Network is not a conventional spy service or a state body: members are volunteers, and its customers include a Liyue intelligence agent and the Knights of Favonius.

Structure: Loosely structured, with no rules or regulations to speak of. It is made of volunteers, informants and paying clients who deal with one another through Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets.

- **Representative**: Nefer, who also owns the Curatorium. She is the person clients deal with.
- **Employees**: Jahoda, the Curatorium's only official employee, and the black cat Ashru. Jahoda acts as a public face that covers for Nefer's informants and for the Network's real activity.
- **Contacts and members**: Diluc is a contact under the codename "Owl". The wiki also lists Nefer herself as the member holding the representative's seat.
- **Informants**: Cairuo and Lestocq, who run the Nasha Town shop Nuts 'N' Nuts, plus Iratxa, Sarin, Sieciech and Tarno, are listed on the wiki as informants. Their ties vary. Sieciech, for instance, is one of Nefer's contacts inside the Lightkeepers, while Lestocq is secretly with the Marechaussee Phantom.
- **Clients**: Yelan and Varka.
Members join voluntarily. Diluc's character story says many have willingly given up their former positions and reputations, and a few have even abandoned their names, which fits the culture of codenames. Nefer explicitly enforces this: she will not use a contact's real name at work.

Leadership: Nefer, the owner of the Curatorium of Secrets, is the Network's current head and representative.

Nefer's character story describes her as the unseen hand that keeps Nod-Krai's waters "just the right degree of murky". The same story shows an emissary of the Network bringing her a request, and an aging, influential representative who had long been looking for a successor and had approved the deal. It hints that the talks might change who leads the Network. In the main story she is introduced by Varka as the current head of the Network. When Varka first brings the heroes to the Secret Base, he says that if they want intel, she is the one to see.
Nefer's own account of the Network is businesslike: the Curatorium's doors are open to all, but only those with a "key" reach the inner sanctum, and whether a visitor leaves with fool's gold or the real thing depends on their own abilities. The Curatorium abides by a policy of strict neutrality towards Nod-Krai's other factions. In 6.1 she at first declined to join the alliance against Rerir, saying she does not work for free, and agreed to help "just this once" only after Jahoda pleaded with her.

Members: Nefer is the head. Jahoda is the only official employee. Diluc is a contact with the codename "Owl". Yelan and Varka are customers.

- **Nefer**: representative and owner of the Curatorium.
- **Jahoda**: a former Seahook Gang member whom Nefer took in. She serves as the Curatorium's sole front-line employee, covering for the informants. According to the wiki's account of her story, Nefer and she agreed that Jahoda would take over the Curatorium if Nefer could no longer run it.
- **Diluc Ragnvindr**: a key Mondstadt informant. After resigning from the Knights, he travelled across Teyvat hunting the source of the Delusion that killed his father. A third-party observer from the north saved him from the Harbingers and said that he approved of his methods. Later he joined the Network, and rose to the upper echelons.
- **Yelan**: a valued customer but not a member of the Network in the usual sense. She buys information for her own purposes, not for the Ministry of Civil Affairs.
- **Varka**: a customer on behalf of the Knights of Favonius' expedition.
- **Ashru**: Nefer's black cat, the Curatorium's receptionist.
- **Cairuo and Lestocq**: run Nuts 'N' Nuts in Nasha Town. Cairuo is a Liyue-born merchant who works with Yelan; she appears in Yelan: Motives and Means, where she packs up samples to send back to the Ministry of Civil Affairs.
- **Sieciech**: an informant inside the Lightkeepers, whom Nefer calls "my old friend". In One There Was, Who Hunted the Moon (6.0) he briefs her at the scene of a Lightkeeper Sergeant Major's murder, reporting that Flins was seen entering and leaving around the time of the crime.
- **Iratxa**: a Marechaussee Phantom agent hunting someone called Thianges in Nasha Town; Nefer's intel notes read her as having a fruitless day.
- **Sarin and Tarno**: Sarin is the Adventurers' Guild branch master in Nasha Town; Tarno manages the Voynich Guild's souvenir outlet and has since represented the Guild in the League. The wiki counts both as informants.

Goals: The Network's aim is trade: to move information from those who have it to those who will pay, and to protect its own members and interests in the process. Nefer does not do favours for free. Beyond commerce, the Network's other purpose is shaped by the people it serves, as in Varka's use of it to gather intelligence on the Abyss and the Wild Hunt.

Methods: Information is bought and sold at the Curatorium of Secrets. Nefer reads clients carefully and prices by risk ("the riskier the job, the more it'll cost"), and she prizes clients who pay up front. Members use codenames or other aliases. The Network also takes on discreet jobs: the wiki's Lohen profile shows it asking the Knights' expedition to deal with an underground auction house in Nod-Krai that traded in smuggled and dangerous goods, a confidential request from its current head.

Nefer's playable kit reflects the same style: the Curatorium lets her and Jahoda gather intel on certain Nod-Krai NPCs by approaching them, as an in-game mechanic, and Nefer's secret room opens after A Nation That Doesn't Exist. In the story, intelligence is often exchanged in person or through letters sent to the Curatorium. Nefer treats favours warily, telling Jahoda never to accept them because "they're the hardest debts to repay".

History: The Network was first hinted at in Diluc's fourth Character Story as a vast underground intelligence network in the north. It was named in 6.1 and became central to the Song of the Welkin Moon story, in which Varka brought the heroes to a Network contact hub.

**Before Nefer.** The Network had an aging representative who wanted a successor. Nefer came to Nod-Krai and set up the Curatorium; by 6.1 she is the Network's head, though the handover is never shown. Her character story describes how Nod-Krai's so-called "leaders" once carved the land into private spheres of influence, and implies that she has personally destroyed a gang, led a certain boss to ruin and sparked conflict between rival factions.

**Diluc.** After his encounter with the Harbingers, Diluc joined, and he rose through the ranks. Nefer refers to him by the codename "Owl". She declines to say how they met, saying only that he pays promptly.

**Liyue.** Efforts to put the Network down in Liyue failed. Yelan and her associates turned back every approach, whether it came from official representatives or smuggled spies, with a polite but firm rejection. She says Liyue is one of the very few unknown spots on the Network's map.
**Song of the Welkin Moon (6.1).** When Rerir returned and Varka rescued the Traveler's group from the Wild Hunt, he took them to the Secret Base, the Knights' meeting place in Nod-Krai and a contact hub for the Network. He described it as the black market of intel, with headquarters in Nod-Krai and contacts in every nation, and said that working with it was the best way for a foreign expeditionary force to get reliable local information. He then introduced Nefer as its current head. She first refused to help, saying she did not work for free; Lauma offered a formal commission, which Nefer said she could not afford, and Nefer finally agreed "just this once" after Jahoda offered to cover the difference from her own pay and begged her. During the final planning in Echoes of Fate, Nefer refused to let Varka name Diluc and referred to him only as "Owl".

**Favonius Keep (6.3).** In the world quest On This Intoxicating Night, Varka told the Honorary Knight that the expeditionary force intended to form a long-term partnership with the Network and turn the temporary camp into an intelligence station, to share findings on the Abyss and keep collecting information about it.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: customers and partners. Varka's expeditionary force used the Network for local intelligence, and its camp, the Favonius Keep, was planned as an intelligence station.
- **Yelan**: a major client, and also an opponent in the sense that she and her colleagues have kept the Network out of Liyue.
- **Diluc**: a contact and informant in Mondstadt.
- **Curatorium of Secrets**: the Network's front and primary point of sale.
- **Lightkeepers and Voynich Guild**: some of their members double as informants; the Curatorium itself stays neutral between Nod-Krai's factions.
- **Dori**: Lord Sangemah Bay, a regular business partner of Nefer's who brings her news from Sumeru, and who is in Nod-Krai during Echoes of Fate. Nefer drained the kuuvahki charge from a pendant Alice had made for Dori, and promised to make it up.
- **Marechaussee Phantom and Spina di Rosula**: listed as allies on the wiki, but based only on NPC listings; see the uncertainty notes.
- **Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Qixing**: Yelan's side. She says her dealings with the Network are personal and not the Ministry's business.

Reputation: To outsiders it looks like a mysterious secret society. In-game dialogue disagrees: when Paimon calls it a secret society pulling the strings, the Traveler remarks that "secret society" seems like a stretch, since they know a whole bunch of the people involved. Within Nod-Krai, Nefer's skill with information is widely respected; Aino calls her "the intel queen of Nod-Krai", and the shut-doored Curatorium is a wellspring of urban legends in Nasha Town. The Network is regarded as the place to buy and sell intelligence whatever faction a person belongs to.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Network is active under Nefer, based in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai.

The Knights of Favonius remain its clients; in 6.3 Varka said the expeditionary force planned a long-term partnership with it and would turn the Favonius Keep into an intelligence station. Nothing in 7.0 or 7.1, whose Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya, was found that changes the Network's position.

486.comment: Northern Intelligence Network: Curatorium of Secrets
486.content: The Curatorium of Secrets is the intelligence agency that fronts the Network in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. Nefer owns and runs it, and Jahoda is its only official employee. Ashru the cat works as receptionist. In public it takes small commissions from anyone. Its second floor has a reception area and Nefer's office. Her secret room opens after A Nation That Doesn't Exist, and letters sent to the Curatorium appear there after Echoes of Fate. It abides by a policy of strict neutrality in relation to Nod-Krai's other factions.

487.content: The Secret Base is a well-hidden underground meeting point that Varka calls the Knights of Favonius's meeting place in Nod-Krai and a contact hub for the Network. Nefer says she helped the Knights settle in Nod-Krai and, as the one running the Network, knows where it is. Varka brought the Traveler's group here in 6.1 after rescuing them from the Wild Hunt, and it was where Nefer met them at his request.

488.content: "Owl" is Diluc Ragnvindr's codename in the Network. Nefer calls him a key informant in Mondstadt who pays promptly, and she will not discuss how they met. During Echoes of Fate she stopped Varka from saying his name, telling him that real names are not used at work. In the Traveler's own voice-over, Paimon jokes about what Varka's codename might be, and the Traveler suggests the Knights delegate spy work to Kaeya and Rosaria.

489.comment: Northern Intelligence Network: Yelan and the Network
489.content: Yelan and her colleagues have kept the Network out of Liyue, turning away every approach, both official representatives and smuggled spies. Even so, she buys intel from Nefer for large sums, and Nefer in turn says she is one of the Network's most valued clients, one who pays up front, in cash and in full, often at two or three times the asking price. Yelan says her purchases are personal, not on behalf of the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

490.comment: Northern Intelligence Network: Diluc's path to the Network
490.content: After resigning from the Knights, Diluc left Mondstadt and travelled all seven nations tracing the source of the Delusion that had killed his father. He destroyed many Fatui strongholds, which drew the Harbingers' attention. A third-party observer from the north, part of a vast underground intelligence network, saved him from them, said that they had been watching him for some time, and approved of his methods. He later joined the network and rose to the upper levels. The character story does not name the Network, but the wiki connects it to the Northern Intelligence Network and the observer to the Curatorium of Secrets.

491.content:
Northland Bank (also: Banque du Nord, Northland Bank branch, Regrator's bank): The Northland Bank is a Snezhnayan bank with branches across Teyvat. Its president is Pantalone, "Regrator", the Ninth Fatui Harbinger. The Fatui use funds from the Bank when operating outside Snezhnaya and sometimes use its branches as bases. Its main branch and the underground vaults beneath it are in Snezhnograd. Visible branches stand in Liyue Harbor, Nasha Town in Nod-Krai and the Court of Fontaine, and a branch was being opened in Sumeru City.

The Bank describes itself as no ordinary bank. It embodies what Snezhnaya values, loyalty and promises, and it is generous with loans but expects them repaid in full and on time.

Structure: Pantalone is president and runs the Bank's operations as a whole. Each branch has its own manager and staff; Andrei manages the Liyue branch, with Ekaterina as receptionist and Javert as debt collector. The Fatui have a debt-collection division staffed mostly by Fatui Pyro Agents. New branches may be set up by other Harbingers: Pulcinella handled the Sumeru opening, assisted by Viktor and Vsevolod.

The Snezhnograd branch has named staff including the account manager Strinov, receptionist Kamenov, banker Avaz, several other employees, and guards. The Nod-Krai branch in Nasha Town is run by Jarosznski, with Kudratov as a debt-collection agent. Fontaine's branch building stands in the Court of Fontaine between two clockwork workshops, with its interior inaccessible.

Leadership: Pantalone founded the Bank shortly after becoming a Harbinger and has been president since. He also oversees Snezhnaya's finances.

He is said to have merged human rules with fae customs when designing its system, and given his great age the Bank has grown exponentially and survived numerous crises. A map description credits him as the master of a "web" of exchanges across Teyvat.

Goals: Pantalone saw that Snezhnaya's private banks served only themselves and that no money reached the leadership, so he created the nation's first state-run bank. The Bank's purpose is to channel the flow of Mora and wealth, and Pantalone aims to take the continent's economy out of the gods' hands. According to Vesna, he once told the Tsaritsa that the Bank would become the beating heart of finance for the whole world.

Methods: The Bank lends generously. If a borrower defaults, an agent from the Fatui's debt-collection division is usually sent, using as much force as needed, though other options are tried too. In Nod-Krai the branch gave a loan to Zhuoxin; instead of collecting, it made him a spy for ten years, which he accepted to protect his family. Branches also exchange funds for the Fatui. In Liyue the Bank marks its bags with elemental energy, to identify what belongs to it.

In Liyue Tartaglia occasionally helps the Bank collect debts. After he and Javert confronted the former owner of the Yanshang Teahouse, he uncovered the owner's fraud and reported it to the Millelith, which let Yelan take the teahouse over. The episode contributed to the Bank's notorious reputation among borrowers.

History: **Origins.** Pantalone founded the Bank soon after he became a Harbinger.

**Liyue.** The Liyue branch was set up before the Traveler arrived. In the first Archon Quest chapter it served as a rendezvous for the Traveler and Tartaglia. After Tartaglia's attack on the authorities during the Osial incident, Ningguang made the Bank pay a large sum in reparations, which left its staff resentful. In Endless Smoke she confronted them over spying on her.

**Sumeru and Fontaine.** A Sumeru City branch was being opened when the Traveler arrived, and a branch building also stands in the Court of Fontaine.

**Natlan and Nod-Krai.** Zhuoxin, a Nod-Krai borrower working as the branch's spy, was offered a waiver of his debt in connection with the elite Fatui squad that Sandrone sent to Natlan under Velimiru after Ineffa. In the Archon Quest The Journey Home the squad was killed, and Zhuoxin, fearing Fatui reprisal, stayed with his family under the protection of the Flower-Feather Clan.

Relations: The Bank is tied to the Fatui but is not identical to them, and the exact tie differs by account. Harbingers use its funds, and Liyue's Qixing are wary of it. Tartaglia helps in Liyue. Pulcinella oversees some branch openings. Dottore's research was funded by Pantalone, who in turn received an immortality elixir.

In Snezhnaya the Bank is a state institution; Pantalone sits on the Snezhnograd Veche and voted to continue Project Stuzha. Together with Pulcinella he gave the House of the Hearth money and a key role in Project Stuzha.

Reputation: Liyue customers know the Bank for generous loans but also for hard methods; rivals such as Gentry De'an claim it used underhanded means to establish itself. Staff stress client service and security. In Snezhnaya it is spoken of as extremely secure.

Secrets: The Seals of Life were donated by the public and kept in its deepest vaults. When seals went missing, the banker Avaz, who had noticed the discrepancy and was scouting buyers to sell seals himself, pointed the blame at Pantalone as the only person with unrestricted access; the Tsaritsa dismissed this, saying Pantalone was too prideful to involve himself. The losses turned out to be the work of a creature tied to Rhinedottir, and Avaz was to be handed to Fatui Internal Affairs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bank operates normally with Pantalone as president. The Seals of Life it stored in Snezhnograd were returned to their donors at the end of the 7.1 Archon Quest, and the Bank is negotiating compensation for damaged or missing seals.

Branches continue in Liyue, Sumeru City, Fontaine and Nod-Krai; nothing in 7.1 shows any branch closing.

492.content: The main branch in Snezhnograd has a huge underground complex reached by a short train ride. The most valuable items are stored there. Oprichniki guard it with radios and access cards, monitoring devices and lasers cover it, and the deepest vault is protected by four turrets that Pantalone can control.

493.content: The only non-local bank in Liyue, in Feiyun Slope. It exchanges leftover funds from Tartaglia into Mora. Manager Andrei, receptionist Ekaterina and guards Vlad and Nadia work there; Ekaterina refuses to confirm direct Fatui ties.

494.content: A regional branch in Nasha Town run by Jarosznski. It looks unremarkable outside but is a fortress of defences and alarms inside. It made Zhuoxin into a spy in exchange for his debt.

495.content:
Order of Skeptics (also: Shamaniyya, Nagarjunites, the Skeptics, Vijnanapati, Nasuraia): The Order of Skeptics, which the Akademiya calls the Nagarjunites, is a small group of scholars living in the Girdle of the Sands in southern Sumeru. They descend from an Akademiya Darshan that came to the desert 500 years ago, during the cataclysm, and helped the Pari purify the Harvisptokhm. They have long since cut ties with the Akademiya and are rarely acknowledged. Their creed is the "transmission of knowledge at all costs" and that "conflict is the natural order of Teyvat". In 3.6 their leader Nasejuna turned on the Pari and tried to take the Great Songs of Khvarena for the Abyss Order.

Outsiders also know them by the name Shamaniyya. Their leaders hold the title Nasuraia, also read as Vijnanapati, which the game glosses as "one who has epiphanies". Many people in the rainforest treat them as a myth.

Structure: The order is led by a single Vijnanapati, the equivalent of a sage. Ranks below that are not described, and canon names only a handful of members. The order keeps a camp near the Temir Mountains in the desert. Its old archives burned, so much of its structure and ritual knowledge has been lost.

Five ritual Kory Drums were made to mark the bond between the Skeptics and the Pari, and loading-screen text says they were meant to symbolise that union. The order has since lost the tradition. The Skeptics also used to perform the Rite of Chinvat at the Harvisptokhm, but they neglected the duty after their records were destroyed.

Leadership: Leaders are called Nasuraia or Vijnanapati. Nagarjuna, a one-armed sage, is counted as the first. The last, Nasejuna, fled in 3.6, and the order is currently leaderless.

Before his betrayal Nasejuna was stationed in the Girdle of the Sands to study the Abyssal phenomenon there. Pyrrho, who calls himself one of the order's oldest qualified members and a desert native, praised him as more knowledgeable than anyone he had met and said he was helping the order recover its traditions.

Nasejuna told the Traveler that the order's old traditions had been lost with the Kory Drums, and that he depended on Aryadeva, an elder who had gone to Sumeru City. When the Traveler told Pyrrho and Sosi of his betrayal, both were shocked. Afterwards Sosi calls him by his name alone, "Nasejuna", rather than by his title.

Members: - **Nagarjuna**: the first Nasuraia, a one-armed sage who led the founding scholars.
- **Nasejuna**: the last known Vijnanapati, now a defector.
- **Pyrrho**: a desert-born member who is suspicious of outsiders.
- **Sosi**: a member who studies the order's documents and keeps looking for the truth despite finding discrepancies between records and reality.
- **Aryadeva**: a former elder who left to write light novels in Sumeru City but is still best versed in the order's traditions.
- **Nagahvaya**: a Herbad who calls himself a Skeptic and a follower of Nagarjuna; he is in the Desert Pavilion.
- **Klingsor**: a former ranger who became an Abyss Herald.

Klingsor is described as a descendant of Hadura, a Khaenri'ahn of the Schwanenritter. Hundreds of years ago the then-Vijnanapati sent him to accompany an Akademiya investigation team into Khaenri'ahn ruins, and he came back as an Abyss Herald.

Goals: Under its founders the order's duty was to keep the Harvisptokhm purified and remember the heroes who fought the Abyss. Its stated ideals are the transmission of knowledge at all costs and the belief that conflict is the natural order of Teyvat. Pyrrho says the surviving members want to recover the order's lost traditions and glory. Nasejuna's real aim was different: to use the Great Songs of Khvarena to destroy the Harvisptokhm so that the Abyss would flood Teyvat, which he called bringing truth without mercy to an unjust world.

Methods: The order works through the study of old documents and ruins and its bond with the Pari. It takes no part in Akademiya politics. In the 3.6 events Nasejuna used deception, sending the Pari Sorush to collect the Great Songs under the belief that she must sacrifice herself, and he misled the Traveler until the last song was found.

History: **Founding.** About 500 years ago, as the cataclysm struck, scholars from an Akademiya Darshan led by the one-armed sage Nagarjuna met the Schwanenritter fighting the Abyss in the Dharma Forest. They took the knights for the "heroes of Dahri" and followed their trail to the Girdle of the Sands, where the Pari Zurvan and Dainsleif were defending the Vourukasha Oasis. With documents and machines left by Khaenri'ah's survivors, Nagarjuna found the way into the Harvisptokhm. Together they performed the first Rite of Ab-Zohr, which purified the sky and the land and gave rise to more Pari. Dainsleif left with a golden-haired traveller, Nagarjuna disappeared into the ruins, and the other scholars stayed, bonded with the Pari and became the Order of Skeptics.

**The fall of the archives.** Centuries ago an Akademiya investigation team came to study Khaenri'ahn ruins. The Skeptics warned against it and then sent Klingsor along. He returned as an Abyss Herald, and the team was never found. Abyssal monsters came to the Vourukasha Oasis hunting for the Great Songs, and Zurvan sealed the Oasis and many ruins. The Skeptics lost their archives to fire in the conflict, and over time they neglected their duty to maintain the seal.

Relations: - **Pari**: the order's oldest bond, symbolised by the Kory Drums. Zurvan sealed the Oasis after Klingsor's attack, and the Pari still guard the Harvisptokhm.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: the order was once one of its Darshans, but the Akademiya calls it the Nagarjunites and the two have long been separate. The Akademiya's investigation team led to Klingsor's fall.
- **Abyss Order**: Klingsor, a former member, is now one of its Heralds, and he and Nasejuna worked together.

- **The Traveler**: Pyrrho and Sosi were wary of outsiders until Sorush spoke for the Traveler. After the betrayal the Traveler told them the truth about Nasejuna.
- **Nagahvaya**: he apologises for the modern Skeptics' deeds, saying his Darshan's methods have become their purpose and its philosophy has been simplified and distorted over time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the order has no leader, and its few members remain in the Girdle of the Sands. No newer Skeptics content was found after the 3.6 Khvarena of Good and Evil chapter.

The Harvisptokhm has been purified and the Sign of Apaosha is gone. Nasejuna and Klingsor are at large, and Pyrrho and Sosi remain in the desert.

496.content: Nasejuna was the last Vijnanapati of the Order of Skeptics, stationed in the Girdle of the Sands to study the Abyssal phenomenon there. He learned that his ancestors, who resisted the land's impurities, were heroes in Khaenri'ah's eyes but were smeared and forgotten by the Akademiya, and he plotted with the Abyss Order. In Khvarena of Good and Evil he guided Sorush and the Traveler to the Great Songs of Khvarena while secretly planning to use them to destroy the Harvisptokhm. When the plot was revealed he showed contempt for the Pari, attacked and fled. He is currently at large.

497.content: Klingsor was once a ranger of the Order of Skeptics and a descendant of Hadura of the Schwanenritter. Resentful of how Khaenri'ahns were remembered, he doubted the order's origin story. Hundreds of years ago he was sent to accompany an Akademiya investigation team into Khaenri'ahn ruins. He found material that confirmed his doubts, heard a "gospel" and became an Abyss Herald, and later led an attack on the Vourukasha Oasis. In 3.6 he gave Nasejuna the documents that won him over and fought beside him. His fate after that battle is unknown.

498.content: The Kory Drums are five ritual drums made in honour of Barsom's familiar, which liked music. According to Nasejuna, on the day the Skeptics and Pari made their bond formal, the drums were played together to a score. With the drums lost, the Skeptics lost the ceremony, and Barsom's familiar stopped answering them. In the 3.6 quest chain a map in a cave shows the drums' locations. Loading-screen text says the drums were meant to symbolise the union, and also hints that the order "might have gotten something wrong".

499.content: Aryadeva is a former elder of the Order of Skeptics living in Sumeru City near the Kalimi Exchange. He left the desert to write light novels and is planning a Light Novel Society, though Yae Publishing House keeps rejecting his manuscripts. Nasejuna calls him a ridiculous old geezer but relies on him, since Aryadeva is the best versed in the order's traditions. After the plot failed, Aryadeva said he had kept one Kory Drum away from Nasejuna on purpose.

500.comment: Order of Skeptics: Rite of Ab-Zohr and the Sign of Apaosha
500.content: The Rite of Ab-Zohr is the ceremony that purifies the Harvisptokhm of Abyssal defilement. The Order of Skeptics used to perform the Rite of Chinvat for the same purpose, and the first Ab-Zohr was performed 500 years ago by Zurvan, Dainsleif and Nagarjuna. The Sign of Apaosha, a rift-like mark in the sky above the Harvisptokhm, appears as defilement builds up. Zurvan says that if defilement erodes the tree, the Tunigi Hollow's rift might reopen. In 3.6 the Traveler, Paimon and Sorush performed the rite and the sign disappeared.

501.content:
Pale Star Court (also: Pale Star's royal court, Pale Star Royal Court): The Pale Star Court was the empire and royal court of the Belyi Tsar (White Tsar), whose personal name was Monomakh Snezhnyi. He united the rival Snowland Fae kingdoms of the far north under one crown, and his realm is the direct ancestor of the nation of Snezhnaya. Later texts also use the name for his regime as the first Cryo Archon. It ended when he fell in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago, and Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, took his place.

Fae chroniclers call the Tsar "Emperor" and "lord of all fae". The court's memory survives in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya through books, a palace-tomb, and fae nobles who remember it. It is history rather than a living institution.

Structure: The court was a fae empire built on clan loyalty. The Tsar sat at the top, with fae Grand Dukes ruling territories under him. The Grand Dukes were clan rulers of peoples such as the Domovoy, and the court had ministers who handled matters like finance. A personal guard, the Druzhna, answered to the Tsar and was mustered in wartime; the Tsaritsa later kept it as her own guard.

The Snegovik had their own Grand Duchess, who lived at the House of Hesperides, a mountain manor that a receptionist there says was built by the first Snegovik Grand Duchess after the Tsar unified the north. The seat of the Grand Duchy has changed hands several times since, but the house is still kept as it was. The Tsar also set up an institute, Hvergelmir, under his foster daughter Aksinya, which was separate from the fae clans.

Leadership: The Belyi Tsar, Monomakh Snezhnyi, founded and ruled the court. He claimed a "sacred bloodline" that set him above other fae, though the fae chronicle suggests the claim was a way to appear legitimate. He later became the first Cryo Archon and God of Love.

As a youth he was taken into the House of Hesperides by Yalyane Morevna, who taught him the spear, and he fought with a polearm named Frostbreath during his campaign. In the book's account, the Emperor's reasoning was practical: giving in to Miscislav would only invite worse wars for the next generation. He is shown as merciful too, returning the bodies of fallen enemy dukes to their clans.

Palace notes written in his own hand show a private man who was torn about Hyperborea, the ancient civilisation he sought on expedition. At first he resented the Hyperboreans and Anacharsis as heretical usurpers and blamed the Voyager for inviting Hyperborea's destruction, while respecting the Heavenly Principles as the world's Great Judge. Later notes show him revising these views once he learned the truth about his own origin. He raised an infant girl, Aksinya, whom he found in a time capsule in the Shadow Realm, and he favoured the Khaenri'ahn exile who called himself Professor Rotwang. These details come from palace notes and artifact texts, not from the fae chronicles.

Members: The court's people were the Snowland Fae: Domovoy, Snegovik and Snegurochka, Vila, Jack Frost and others, plus beings such as Volkodlak and water imps (the Dalegrad clan) who were once rivals. Humans were later admitted by the Tsar. His closest figures include Aksinya (his foster daughter), Zver (a Chimeric Winged Lion he named), Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis. The Lantern Fae Flins, who claims to be six or seven hundred years old, is listed as formerly of the Pale Star Court.

Anastasya was a herald of the Pale Star Court before she became the Tsaritsa. The Tsar once incited her and her lover Saarelainen, the Third Descender, to open a gate in Pohjola, which led to the Heavenly Principles erasing her. In the wiki's account he later explained what had happened to the revived Anastasya, whose memories of the incident had been removed, so the story no longer felt real to her.

Goals: At first the court's aim was to unite all fae under one banner and secure the frozen north. After the Tsar learned the truth about Hyperborea and his own nature, his private aim became to complete his ascension as a Primordial Human. He established the Hvergelmir institute to build a "Proto Man" and seek the vacant seat in the court of the stars. This purpose was the Tsar's own, not the court's public programme.

Methods: The Tsar waged unification by war, such as the three battles at Kitezh, and tempered it with mercy. After victory he honoured defeated nobles (Seriviiki received the ceremonial tap of a sword). He later "pardoned humanity" and gave humans membership in his realm. In the "pioneering age" he had the borderland of Nod-Krai explored and industrialised. His expeditions into the Shadow Realm and Hyperborea's ruins were a major project: his notes count at least 446 forays.

History: **Unification.** The Tsar raised Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya, on frozen ground and made it the imperial capital. Seventy-six years later (in the fae calendar), he told the Vila to stop paying tribute to King Miscislav of the Volkodlak. Miscislav accused the court of breaking a standing peace, demanded thirty times the tribute the Vila had paid, and the Emperor refused. Miscislav then attacked Kitezh. In three battles (at Kitezh, in the foothills, at the frozen lake and on the plains) the Tsar killed Miscislav and Grand Dukes Skoldyryt and Vodyanoy with his thrown spear. All remaining fae clans then swore loyalty to him and he took the title Belyi Tsar.

**The long reign.** Kitezh remained the capital for around a thousand years. Then the Tsar welcomed humans into his realm, moved the seat to Snezhnograd and renamed the nation Snezhnaya. About 2,000 years ago he accepted Celestia's offer to become the Cryo Archon. After the Archon War he attended the first gatherings of the original Seven in Liyue.

**The end.** About 500 years ago, in the Cataclysm, the Tsar led an expedition to Khaenri'ah with Zver, fae and many chimeric monsters. They fought forces serving Chernobog for a week and were routed, and the Tsar was killed. Zver dragged his body home. Anastasya was crowned Tsaritsa of all Snezhnaya.

Relations: - **Tsaritsa and Snezhnaya**: the Pale Star Court is the direct predecessor. Anastasya ended the fae princes' rule and broke up the clan system. Her state keeps the Druzhna as a guard, but the Fatui became its main arm.
- **Volkodlak and Miscislavli**: the main rivals, defeated at Kitezh.
- **Fae today**: the Snowland Fae lost most of their old glory but still influence the nation.
- **Celestia and the Heavenly Principles**: the Tsar accepted their offer to become Archon but later pursued the Hyperboreans' goal of overthrowing them.
- **Hyperborea**: the Tsar sent research expeditions to its ruins in the Shadow Realm.

Status as of 7.1: The court no longer exists as a state. It ended with the Belyi Tsar's death roughly 500 years ago.

As of 7.1 its ruins and relics remain: the Pale Crown Palace (the Tsar's mausoleum in the White Birch Snowgrave), the House of Hesperides, and the Tsaritsa's Snezhnaya built on its foundations. Long-lived fae such as Flins, listed as formerly of the court, still carry its memory. No further story about the court itself was found for 7.1.

502.comment: Pale Star Court: Battle of Kitezh and King Miscislav
502.content: King Miscislav, the Blood-Devourer, ruled the Volkodlak and led the Miscislavli alliance. The Vila paid tribute to him until the Tsar's envoys told them to stop. Miscislav then demanded a huge tribute from the Pale Star Court, and the Emperor refused. His host included the Nyholmgarthir (bovine Volkodlak), the Dalegrad (water imps) and the wolf-like Cirnareka. The Tsar threw his spear like an arrow and killed Miscislav, Grand Duke Skoldyryt of the Nyholmgarthir and Grand Duke Vodyanoy of the Dalegrad. Seriviiki of the Cirnareka escaped. Miscislav's skull is said to be kept in the Zapolyarny Palace treasury. A sudden icy fog that misled the Schpekin Legion is recorded by historians, but its cause is unknown.

503.content: Kitezh was the first city of Snezhnaya and the Pale Star Court's imperial capital, built in the fae style on frozen ground. It remained the seat of power until the Tsar moved to Snezhnograd. The Abyss later destroyed Kitezhgrad, and Novokitezhgrad was built to replace it under the supervision of Alvis.

504.comment: Pale Star Court: House of Hesperides
504.content: A mountain manor in Fellfrost Peak and home of the Snegovik and their Grand Duchess. The receptionist Raduzhnaya says it was built by the first Snegovik Grand Duchess after the Belyi Tsar unified the north and founded the Pale Star Court. It has changed leaders but still looks as it did originally. According to a book on Snezhnayan history, the young Monomakh was taken in here by Yalyane Morevna.

505.content: Hvergelmir was a research institute for bio-alchemy and Shadow Realm study, founded by the Belyi Tsar and entrusted to Aksinya. Its goal was to find the stairway to the vacant seat in the court of the stars, using a "Proto Man" as the key to let the Tsar become the Primordial Human. It modified Hyperborean devices into firearms, and Koshchei's work there led to the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters.

506.content: The Druzhna were the personal guard that the Tsar mustered in wartime. They are mostly Vila. Filipov, a fae spy and infiltrator who foiled Skoldyryt's plan in the second battle, later commanded them. After her coronation the Tsaritsa chose not to call the Druzhna against rebels and founded the Fatui instead. Today they answer only to her and are also responsible for containing Shadow Realm breaches, under Vesna.

507.content: Anastasya Feodorovna was crowned Tsaritsa of all Snezhnaya in the fourth month of the first year of the 799th Cycle. The fae princes were not all present. In the following years her troops moved against the self-government declared by the humans of Port Belovodye, which accepted her offer of amnesty in return for its instigators, ended hereditary rule in the Drevogorye, Volkhovan and Cirnareka lands, and created the Fatui. The edict and the Veche shifted power from the princes to appointed officials and the Veche, whose first chair, Ioanna Ivanovna, was human.

508.comment: Pale Star Court: Pale Crown Palace and the Tsar's remains
508.content: The Pale Crown Palace is the Belyi Tsar's mausoleum, once one of his palaces. His preserved corpse grew into the Tsar's White Birch. Notes by a Certain Noble Individual, written in his own voice, were left there describing his visits to Hyperborea's ruins and his ascension. In the quest An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, Aksinya transferred the Primordial Human's power into the corpse, and the Traveler defeated it using the Eye of Graeae.

509.content:
People of the Springs (also: Meztli, Meztli tribe, the People of the Springs): The People of the Springs (Meztli) are one of Natlan's six tribes. They live by the hot springs and coast of Toyac Springs, in a settlement also called "People of the Springs". Their Saurian partners are the swimming Koholasaurs. They are famous as guides, mapmakers, surfers and hosts, and their land is the tribe most popular with visitors. Their current chief is Amina. Mualani, a guide and surf-shop owner, bears the tribe's hero Ancient Name, Umoja ("unity").

The tribe is easygoing and fond of music, fishing, watersports and long soaks. Its chief jokes that seriousness is a rare virtue among her people. It has still produced some of Natlan's most respected warriors, and it suffered heavily in the Abyss's attacks on Natlan.

Structure: Like the other tribes, the Meztli are led by a chief, with the tribe's elders behind them. When Amina's grandfather died, the elders voted her in because of her many new ideas. The tribe shares in Natlan's tribal institutions: its members take part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, and its Wayob, the ancestral spirit in the Night Kingdom, grants Ancient Names to worthy members. Hero names are tied to their tribe, and the Meztli's is Umoja. In the wiki's comparison of the tribes, they are paired with the Hydro element and the Flow-Inverted Wayob Manifestation.

Daily life rests on trades rather than ranks. There are guides (Nuu is a famous one and Koolau is called the top guide), hot-spring administrators, lifeguards, guards, musicians, shopkeepers and inn staff. Guide-craft is taught by apprenticeship. Nuu told the young Mualani to spend about three years learning wilderness survival, the land, the tides and the timing of eruptions before she could start, and she paid him a large tuition fee.

Leadership: Chief Amina leads the tribe. She is young, full of ideas and determined to take her job seriously. She took over after her grandfather died, and the late warrior Atea was her mentor.

Amina's grandfather taught her that "positivity should be our guiding star", and she quotes him. As chief she has designed a new stage, strengthened patrols, run the defence of the tribe during the Abyss invasion and dealt with scammers who used the tribe's legends. She believes the Natlanese dead are reunited in the Night Kingdom. She says that idea is also how Ancient Names carry heroes' memories forward.

Members: - **Mualani**: playable Hydro guide who runs the Leisurely Puffer watersports shop. She bears Umoja and fought in three Night Warden Wars without ever needing resurrection.
- **Amina**: chief.
- **Atea**: an elder warrior with a Pyro Vision, titled Candlekeeper. She died of long-term Abyssal corrosion during the Chapter V story.
- **Kaiulani**: an Ancient Name bearer and veteran warrior.
- **Nuu**: a famous guide who taught Mualani.

In the settlement, the Traveler can meet Kupo Nui (owner of the Golden Dusk), Mahina Nui (Golden Dusk reception), Mataoho and Pele Nui (hot-spring administrators), Yelafath (owner of Atlahua's Net), Pakaa Nui (owner of Xochicuicatl Records), Anchieta (owner of Djembe Studios), Milu Nui (freelance musician), Wakea Nui (guide), Umi (lifeguard), and Ipora and Tairona (guards). Hinaeia Nui, a sailor who calls herself the "Gourmet Hunter", trades the tribe's goods in Nod-Krai. Kaulu is a tribesman Amina caught swindling tourists.

Goals: The tribe wants to live well and share that with others. It keeps its springs clean and welcoming, guides travellers safely through Natlan, defends its home against the Abyss, and keeps its heroes' memories alive through Ancient Names. Its founding legend sets its central value: companions matter more than the prize.

Methods: **Guiding.** The Meztli have a long tradition as guides and cartographers. Their ancestors "measured the world with their feet" and turned dangerous paths into maps. Guides are expected to bring clients to their destination safely. As Nuu put it, guides are not treasure hunters.

**Hot springs.** The tribe has both natural and artificial springs. The natural springs are hotter and are for locals and vetted visitors. After some travellers were scalded, an unwritten rule now says outlanders must first acclimatise in the cooler artificial springs. Atea spent years digging new artificial springs so that more visitors could enjoy them.

**Livelihood.** Tourism is the tribe's main income, and its hot springs are famous across Teyvat. The tribe's leisure is fishing, music, surfing and relaxing alongside the Koholasaurs.

The Meztli make record discs for portable players, which also work on Fontainian record players, and they build string and percussion instruments. A trader in Nod-Krai said the instruments sell well there even though most of the tribe's other goods suit the cold poorly. Their rooftops often have wavy canopies meant to evoke "sailing through waves". In the hot-spring culture the Traveler sees, visitors swim, surf, dive and play water polo, and hosts recommend lucky colours and the best spring for each guest.

History: **Founding.** According to the tribe's legend, the first chief was the best guide in Natlan but began as a treasure hunter who was never satisfied. He set out for a legendary mysterious island. His companions helped and trusted him, and at the end he gave up the glowing prize, an ore that also warned of an eruption, to bring them all home safely. Realising that they were the treasure, he settled down with them and founded the People of the Springs. Elders say the tribe began on a small island that later joined the coast.

**Heroes.** Uenuku, the first bearer of Umoja, fought the dragon order alongside an Oceanid. Five hundred years ago his descendant Tupac joined Tenoch's band against the Abyss, survived the final battle long enough to carry Mavuika to the Sacred Flame, and then died. Legend credits Tupac with thrusting rocks into the earth so that the hot springs of the southwest bubbled up.

**Present day (Chapter V, 5.0-5.3).** After the Pilgrimage ended Mualani's bid for the Night Warden Wars, she brought the Traveler home. An Abyss attack on the tribe was driven back without deaths. Atea destroyed an Abyssal pylon at the abandoned spring, and the Traveler briefly purified her, but she died soon after. During the invasion (5.1), the Abyss fouled the tribe's springs and weakened its defences. The tribespeople, with Mualani and Amina, worked to purify the waters. Many people died. Before the Traveler and Mavuika went into the Night Kingdom, Amina organised a sending-off feast, and Atea's spirit later helped in the fight there.

Relations: - **Pyro Archon**: Mavuika was one of Atea's "hot spring buddies" and was with her when she died. At Amina's feast, Mavuika arranged for the Speaker's Chamber to buy any leftovers for redistribution. Tupac's last deed was carrying Mavuika to the Sacred Flame.
- **Other tribes**: the six tribes have coexisted since Och-Kan's era. At the end of the war, Amina and the other chiefs went to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to give their blessings to the Traveler and Mavuika. Mualani is a close friend of Kachina of the Children of Echoes, and she pesters Citlali of the Masters of the Night-Wind for fortunes before trips.
- **Koholasaurs**: the tribe's Saurian partners. Legend says they descend from the great sea dragon of old.
- **Visitors**: travellers are welcome and well looked after, but they must respect the spring rules.

Reputation: Across Natlan the tribe is known as the place to relax. An official description calls it the tribe most popular with visitors from afar. Its guides are said to know Natlan better than the birds do.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and rebuilding after the Abyss war, with Amina as chief.

Mualani is active and travels. In 6.0 she helped throw the Traveler's farewell party before the trip to Nod-Krai. In Linnea's story quest (6.5) she entered the Spirit Envoy Championship in Nod-Krai with her Koholasaur partner Mamala. Meztli traders such as Hinaeia Nui sell the tribe's goods in Nod-Krai. No tribe-specific story developments were found for 7.0-7.1.

key: first chief of the People of the Springs
510.comment: People of the Springs: The first chief and the mysterious island
510.content:
For as long as the Meztli have existed, they have told of a mysterious island in a rarely visited Domain that promises wealth and glory. Few have ever reached it, and even top guides cannot guarantee passage. In Mualani's Tribal Chronicle (5.0), she guided the Traveler and two Sumeru scholars there. Statue text left by the first chief tells his story: a restless treasure hunter whose companions trusted him to the end. He gave up the glowing prize, which was also the warning sign of an eruption, to bring everyone home alive. Then he founded the tribe. Nuu explained that the chief left the legend and map on purpose, to lure young guides into the challenge and teach them what he had learned.

The legend draws tourists, and some tribesfolk exploited it. Kaulu and others charged visitors for fake trips to the island. Amina could not prosecute them because the scammers claimed the money covered travel costs, so she gave the Traveler marked coins as bait and caught Kaulu with them.

511.comment: People of the Springs: Umoja and the heroes of the Springs
511.content: Umoja ("unity") is the Ancient Name of the People of the Springs' hero line. Its known bearers are Uenuku, Tupac and Mualani. Uenuku, the Treader of the Rainbow, travelled with Xbalanque, served in the Grand Alliance and later left. Tupac, Uenuku's descendant, was a giant of a man whom no Saurian could carry. In songs he breaks mountains, makes hot springs, fights a two-tailed whale, and spars with the young Tenoch over a drinking horn. Five hundred years ago he was one of the six warriors who joined Tenoch against the Abyss. Gravely wounded, he lived long enough to carry Mavuika to the Sacred Flame. In Into Eternal Night (5.0), Tupac's projection appeared to Mualani in the Night Kingdom. He passed his memories to her and told her she would unite the tribes.

512.comment: People of the Springs: Hineila and the rainbow legend
512.content: Many versions exist of Uenuku's meeting with an Oceanid, Hineila (or Ianeira), who came from Fontaine. In one, she blesses his spear in exchange for "the spring where vicious beasts prowl", because she meant to purge Phlogiston from Natlan's waters. Each of them knows the other is a means to an end, yet they fall in love, and she dies shielding him from the dragonlord Xiuhcoatl's flames, leaving a rainbow behind. The Meztli's own scrolls tell a happier tale. Uenuku drove her away in a moment of suspicion and searched for her for decades, until a rainbow guided him to "the sea's other side" and they were reunited. Canon does not settle which version is true.

513.comment: People of the Springs: Atea, the Candlekeeper
513.content: Atea was an Ancient Name bearer with a Pyro Vision, a famous Night Warden Wars veteran, and a neighbour and friend of Mualani. She loved the hot springs and threw parties for her "hot spring buddies", including Kaiulani, Liliuo, Vichama and Mavuika. Years earlier an Abyssal monster had impaled her. She survived, but the corruption stayed in her organs, so she could no longer fight on the front line or bathe in hot water. She turned instead to digging cooler artificial springs for visitors. In Home of the Hot Springs (5.0), she destroyed an Abyssal pylon at an abandoned spring, and the Traveler purified the fresh contamination. She told Mualani she had only days left, gave the Traveler her talisman to deliver to Mavuika, and died soon afterwards with Mavuika at her side. Amina, whom she had mentored, called her an elder she deeply respected. Her spirit later helped the Traveler in the Night Kingdom (5.3).

514.comment: People of the Springs: Hot-spring etiquette of the Meztli
514.content: The People of the Springs keep two kinds of springs. The natural springs are hotter, and locals and vetted visitors use them. The artificial springs are deliberately cooler. After some travellers were scalded, an unwritten rule took hold that outlanders must first get used to the artificial springs, a "trial" in Atea's words, before using the natural ones. In scenes, locals greet guests by asking whether they have had a bath today, and an ailing person may be forbidden hot water altogether.

515.comment: People of the Springs: Cochanina and the Volcano Lord
515.content: Told as a lively children's tale in the lore of Surf's Up: the Volcano Lord, a huge black salamander-like monster that had squatted in the Great Volcano of Tollan, dumped his filth into the Meztli's springs. The tribe's elder ran to the ancient Pyro Archon Cochanina. She was remembered as the tribe's surfing champion. Leaving her famous blade behind, she brought only a surfboard. She lured him into a surfing race to find the "Iridescent Chalice", a supposed treasure of Uenuku, and drove him off by throwing a Drifting Pufferfish at him. He never troubled the tribe again.

516.comment: People of the Springs: The Abyss and the Springs
516.content: The tribe has long been a target of the Abyss. Atea's wound and an attack seven years before the Traveler's arrival are earlier examples. In 5.0, an attack on the night before Atea's party was repulsed without deaths. During the full invasion in The Rainbow Destined to Burn (5.1), the Abyss rained a dangerous substance on Meztli territory and defiled the hot springs. The tribe's defences were badly weakened, and Mualani and Amina joined the effort to purify the waters. Afterwards Amina mourned how many people had died.

517.comment: People of the Springs: Settlement of the People of the Springs
517.content: The settlement called "People of the Springs" lies in Toyac Springs, and its viewpoint calls it the "home of hot springs and flowing waters". It has the Golden Dusk inn (Kupo Nui), Atlahua's Net shop (Yelafath), Xochicuicatl Records (Pakaa Nui), Djembe Studios (Anchieta), Mualani's Leisurely Puffer, a market street, guards, lifeguards and spring administrators. Bulletin boards serve tribe notices and visitors' messages. Nearby Ameyalco Waters is the setting for part of the mysterious-island story. Out of universe, many Meztli names come from Polynesian languages, which is a helpful guide when naming new tribesfolk in roleplay.

518.content:
Ragnvindr Clan (also: Ragnvindr Family, House Ragnvindr, the Ragnvindr Clan): The Ragnvindr Clan is a rich and respected Mondstadt family who own the Dawn Winery, the city's premier winery. It takes its name from Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight, who sided with Vennessa against the aristocracy about 1,000 years ago. It is one of the two known noble houses that were not exiled when the aristocracy fell. Its present head is Diluc.

The winery dominates Mondstadt's drinks trade, and Diluc's profile calls him in effect the uncrowned king of the city because of the money and gossip network that comes with it. The family's recent history is shaped by the death of Crepus Ragnvindr and the break between the family and the Knights of Favonius that followed.

Structure: Diluc is head of the family and owner of the winery. His adopted brother Kaeya belongs to it by adoption.

The household is small. Crepus, the previous head, is dead. Staff are close to the family: Adelinde is head housemaid and ran the winery for a time when Diluc left, and Elzer is a long-serving employee who also minds the winery when Diluc is away. Other named winery staff include the winemaker Connor and warehouse manager Ernest. The staff mourned Crepus and treat Kaeya as part of the household.

History: The family's namesake Ragnvindr was a young nobleman and knight's squire in the aristocratic age who joined Vennessa's rebellion. Later generations ran the winery. Four years before the main story Crepus died, Diluc left the Knights of Favonius, and he returned to take over the winery.

**Ragnvindr.** Ragnvindr was moved by the enslaved Dawnlight Swordswoman of the Wanderer's Troupe, who kept singing of freedom as a gladiator. After she died in the arena he buried her with her sword and took the title Dawn Knight in her honour. He sided with Vennessa. Afterwards, he turned the aristocrats' public baths into the Mondstadt Library. The Ballads of the Squire are said to be his songs.

**Crepus.** Crepus dreamed of becoming a knight when he was young, but he was not accepted. He became a talented winemaker and wished his son to become the most esteemed knight. He took in Kaeya, a boy who was found at the winery about ten years before the main story, and raised him as a son.

**Diluc and the break with the Knights.** Diluc trained hard, passed the Knights' trials and became the youngest Cavalry Captain in the order's history. On the night of his coming-of-age celebration at Angel's Share, Ursa the Drake attacked the convoy that Crepus and Diluc were travelling with. Crepus used a Delusion to defeat the drake, but it mortally wounded him. Back at headquarters, Inspector Eroch ordered Diluc to conceal the truth to protect the Knights' reputation, and Diluc resigned that day, left his Vision behind and left Mondstadt. Kaeya's stories record his own version of that night: Diluc ended his father's suffering and Kaeya arrived too late. Their paths diverged from then on.

**Return.** Diluc handed the winery to Adelinde and spent about three years travelling Teyvat to learn where the Delusion came from. He traced it to the Fatui. After a near-fatal clash with Harbingers he was spared by a watcher from a northern intelligence network. He then returned to take over the winery, and by night became the "Darknight Hero" while publicly appearing to despise the hero.

Members: Diluc Ragnvindr is the head. Kaeya, adopted by Crepus, is Diluc's estranged brother and is Cavalry Captain of the Knights. Crepus is dead. The founder-figure is Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight.

Diluc and Kaeya were once close and now keep their distance. Staff in Taste of Home (3.8) say Kaeya is always welcome at the winery, and Adelinde says she has never considered him an outsider. Kaeya's profile calls him an adopted son of the Ragnvindr family and says he has not called Diluc "brother" for a long time.

Goals: Diluc's profile gives him a simple creed behind the winery's motto "Shine True": evil must not go unpunished, he must never settle for mediocrity, and the dawn will one day come. The family's wider role is to supply Mondstadt with wine and cider, and to support the city, as the old mutual support between winery and Knights recalls.

Methods: Business is run from the manor, with Diluc as owner. At his request the winery has developed alcohol-free drinks, including apple cider, which sells as well as dandelion wine. Diluc himself does not drink alcohol, and gives work as the reason. By night he hunts monsters and criminals alone.

Relations: - **Knights of Favonius**: a long history of mutual support; Crepus and Diluc both served the city this way. Since Crepus's death Diluc has distrusted the order, though he still cooperates with it in a crisis.
- **Gunnhildr Clan**: the other house known to have escaped exile.
- **Lawrence Clan**: the former rulers, exiled after the rebellion.
- **Fatui**: Diluc tracked them as the source of the Delusion that killed his father.
- **Dawn Winery**: the family's seat and business; see the Dawn Winery location entry.

Reputation: The Ragnvindrs are among Mondstadt's best-known and most affluent houses. At winery festivities, fathers present their daughters to the unmarried winery master, and onlookers joke that Diluc should stay married to the winery. Diluc is known as the Dawn Winery's owner; few link him to the Darknight Hero.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Diluc runs the winery, remains outside the Knights and keeps up his night patrols. Kaeya remains a Knights captain. No new family developments were found for 6.7 to 7.1.

519.comment: Ragnvindr Clan: Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight
519.content: Ragnvindr was born into Mondstadt's upper class during the aristocratic age, became a knight's squire and grew sick of the nobles' indifference to the common people. He befriended the enslaved Dawnlight Swordswoman and, after she died fighting in the arena, buried her together with her sword, The Flute. He chose "Dawn Knight" as his title in her memory and took Vennessa's side. After the rebellion he converted the aristocracy's baths into a library. The Ballads of the Squire are said to be his own songs. It is unknown whether he joined the Knights of Favonius or whether the winery began with him.

520.content: Crepus was the head of the family and of the Dawn Winery until his death. He wished for his son Diluc to become the most esteemed knight, and he told him, "Sometimes, life can change in an instant." He raised Kaeya as a second son. When Ursa the Drake attacked the winery's convoy, he used a Delusion, and the power that defeated the drake also mortally wounded him. Winery staff such as Elzer and Connor remember him as a talented winemaker and a father figure. In Taste of Home (3.8), Adelinde says Crepus mixed and named a nearly alcohol-free drink to comfort the young Kaeya after a punishment.

521.content: Kaeya was taken in as a boy and grew up beside Diluc. The night Crepus died, Kaeya arrived too late and hung back behind Diluc. That night also saw him receive his Vision. Diluc became the head of the family and Kaeya joined the Knights as Cavalry Captain, and the two grew apart. In Taste of Home (3.8) Kaeya visits the winery and the staff welcome him warmly. Kaeya's secret as a Khaenri'ahn agent is told in his own stories.

522.comment: Ragnvindr Clan: Dawn Winery household staff
522.content: Adelinde is the head housemaid who kept the winery running while Diluc was away and still says Kaeya is part of the winery family. Elzer is a long-time employee who regarded Crepus as a father figure and manages the winery whenever Diluc is absent. Connor is the winemaker and Ernest the warehouse manager. All are devoted to the family.

523.content:
Rokot (also: the Rokot, Рокот): The Rokot is a covert popular movement in Snezhnaya that serves "the common people" and works against Project Stuzha, the Tsaritsa's grand scheme that has strained the country's supply of Kresnik Kristall. Members use codenames and mostly do not know who one another are. The movement avoids violence and tries to help the public by quieter means. The Fatui keep watch on it and count it as an opponent. Alyosha, Vodyanitsa and Odette are members, and the Traveler joins in the Archon Quest.

The name is the Russian word for a rumble. The Traveler and Paimon joke about whether it means a howl or a gust of wind. The movement acts as an outlet for people who disagree with how the country is run but have no easy way to be heard. Alyosha describes it as giving the disaffected false identities and an outlet for their frustrations.

Structure: The Rokot is deliberately loose. Members get a codename on joining, usually do not meet in person and often do not know each other's real identities, which keeps each one independent and means nobody else is exposed if something goes wrong. Members choose their own methods, so long as the result does not break the group's principles, and they may also choose not to act at all, since many members have never done anything. A president approves new recruits by letter and sends notices to all members.

A written code of conduct exists, though Vodyanitsa admits she has never finished reading it. Technicians check equipment for members' projects, and some members act as sources of intelligence. New members fill in an application form with a name, race, codename and a stated reason for joining. In the Archon Quest the choices are mostly jokes (a Primogem as a "race", for example), and Vodyanitsa accepts the Traveler's form regardless. Recruitment goes by recommendation: Alyosha wrote to the president about the Traveler after working beside them, and the reply came back almost at once. Because members hide even from one another, a member can hold a second life, as a Fatuus for example, or work beside another member without either knowing the other's affiliation.

Leadership: No leader is named. The only authority shown is a "president" who answers recruitment requests, and the leadership's notice to members ends with a motto: "We act only for the greater glory and solidarity of our nation. May the aurora shine ever on and the tundra always stand firm." Nothing identifies the president or where he works.

Members: Alyosha (a hunter from Sretomorozsk), Vodyanitsa (Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe) and Odette (Prima Ballerina of the troupe and a Fatuus), plus the Traveler. Trapeznikov, a research-minded NPC, also belongs.

- **Alyosha** (Electro Vision): a young hunter with a strong sense of justice. He recommends the Traveler. He sets money aside partly for the Rokot's medicine and plays Genius Invokation TCG against fellow members, who often beat him. When Polonsky hints that the Rokot recruits people with his talents, Alyosha claims never to have heard of it.
- **Vodyanitsa** (Hydro Vision): the Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe. Alyosha calls her a vital source of intelligence for the Rokot.
- **Odette** (Cryo Vision): Prima Ballerina and a Fatuus. Under the codename Lelek she was the movement's best-known and most controversial member. She says Project Stuzha has emptied the theatre while corrupt people prey on a struggling public, and she refuses to turn a blind eye. Her codename is now withdrawn and she is suspended.
- **Trapeznikov**: a bookish man obsessed with Shadow Realm technology. He says the Rokot helped him after he spent his Kristall funds on research data, and that he might otherwise have frozen.
- **The Traveler**: invited by Alyosha and Vodyanitsa in Silence Alone is Disfavored. Players choose a codename from a list of jokes such as Wayfarer, Chest Mimic or King Jabberfries!.

Goals: The Rokot wants to improve ordinary people's lives and to see Project Stuzha ended, which is why it opposes the plan's backers and, on occasion, the Tsaritsa herself.

Members focus on practical help: medicine, repairs to freezing stations, exposing waste, and getting scarce Kristall to where it is most needed. Alyosha says ordinary people have no easy way of being heard in Snezhnograd, and the Rokot gives them one. He also hopes that Snezhnaya will one day change and that "the Rokot won't need to exist forever". Odette says Project Stuzha has driven audiences away from her theatre while corrupt people prey on a struggling public, and that she refuses to turn a blind eye.

Methods: The Rokot works by gathering information, steering evidence toward people with authority and doing small acts of service, such as recon, repairs and distributing Kristall.

In practice the work means recon at factories, steering information toward people the authorities take seriously, repairing shelters and stations, and distributing Kristall. Alyosha says quiet work fits his creed: he can stand up for what the Rokot believes in without reaching for his gun. He also practises low-profile discretion as a matter of principle, for example keeping secret that he built a shelter for refugees. The movement is non-violent by principle, but each member decides how to act, and one went well beyond the others. As Lelek, Odette became notorious. Vodyanitsa says the more decent members disapprove: Lelek believed votes in the Veche were all that mattered, and used threats, coercion or bribery to change them. Lelek worked alone, and Valeriy has read the case files at the Armory Palace.

History: Nothing in the sources checked says how the Rokot began. It first appears in the 7.0 Archon Quest after the Traveler reaches Snezhnaya. In Gunfire in the Silent Lands the Fatui officer Polonsky mentions the group to Alyosha, who then explains it to the Traveler. In Silence Alone is Disfavored the Traveler joins. The Chapter VII story then turns on the exposure of Lelek.

**Svetloledovka to recruitment.** After the incident at Svetloledovka, Alyosha arranges tickets to the Korolevskiy Theater and a Rokot contact. Odette has spoken highly of the Traveler, and in the greenroom, once Odette has left, Alyosha shows Vodyanitsa the president's approval and both reveal their membership. They recruit the Traveler.

**Lelek.** In the Veche's Project Stuzha debate, the finance scholar Arapov alludes to "extremist activists", and the commentator Mironova raises the Rokot and the notorious Lelek by name. Childe and Sandrone come to suspect Odette. In Lelek's Confession, while the theatre's audience is trapped by Ronova's Curse of Death, two merchants are found dead and Chugunov, who had been threatened by Lelek, blames Lelek. The Traveler passes Childe's intel to Vodyanitsa and "Alyosha", and Odette publicly admits to being Lelek while denying the murders. The killer was Ronova, who had taken Alyosha's form after he died; once the disguise was destroyed everyone in the theatre woke up alive.

**Aftermath.** In Mistilteinn, after Project Stuzha is suspended, the Rokot's leadership writes to Alyosha and Vodyanitsa. It permanently withdraws the codename over the effect of Lelek's radical actions on the group's reputation and social stability, says Lelek acted for the people's benefit, and notes that the Rokot negotiated with the authorities to waive all penalties. Lelek is suspended and might return under a new codename depending on future conduct. The letter reminds members that motives and methods matter equally, and mentions Project Stuzha's suspension as an "interim operational victory" that must not breed complacency.

Relations: - **Fatui**: officially an opponent. Polonsky says the Rokot is non-violent but opposes Project Stuzha, so the Fatui keep tabs on it. Yet one of its stars, Odette, is a Fatuus, and Alyosha admits he never expected a Fatui member to share the group's principles.
- **Snezhnograd Veche**: the Rokot is a topic of debate there. Vodyanitsa explains that the commentator Mironova is rephrasing Pantalone's remark that critics take no responsibility for their actions, and the critics he means are the Rokot.
- **Tsaritsa**: the Rokot opposes Project Stuzha and, occasionally, the Tsaritsa herself. Alyosha stresses that members still believe in her, and that they differ only over how best to tackle the country's problems.
- **Korolevskiy Troupe**: two of its stars are members, and Vodyanitsa's greenroom doubles as a meeting place.

Reputation: Polonsky calls it non-violent with the goal of improving the lives of common folk, Pantalone's side treats its critics as irresponsible, and Alyosha says it is in a grey area. Lelek's methods damaged the group's reputation, as Odette's story shows and the organisation's own letter admits.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Rokot is active. Its president remains unnamed, the codename Lelek is retired, and its members continue everyday good works in Snezhnaya.

Odette is suspended and may rejoin later under a new codename. The Traveler remains a member with a codename of their own choosing. Nothing in 7.0 or 7.1 resolves the long-term fate of the movement.

524.content: Lelek was the Rokot's most famous and most infamous member, an anonymous figure who made ending Project Stuzha an obsession. Vodyanitsa says Lelek used threats, coercion or bribery to change votes in the Veche, unlike the more decent members. Valeriy knows the codename from Armory Palace files as a lone operator. In Lelek's Confession Chugunov blames Lelek for the deaths of two merchants, but Vodyanitsa objects that such a roundabout method is not Lelek's style; the killer was in fact Ronova, disguised as Alyosha. The holder is Odette, who joined while serving the Fatui. Citing the effect of Lelek's radical actions on its reputation and on social stability, the Rokot withdrew the codename for good and suspended her.

525.content: The form asks for a name, a race, a codename and a reason for joining. The options are playful: names such as Monpai, races such as Primogem or Dodoco, codenames such as Wayfarer, Chest Mimic, Seamount Abyss, The 12th, King Jabberfries! or Lord of the Seven Calamities, and reasons that range from "I oppose Project Stuzha" to "I need a part-time job". Vodyanitsa tweaks any answer she considers unacceptable and says the form will be kept. Filling it in earns an achievement called The Howling Gale.

526.content: When the Traveler joins, the Rokot's current target is Chugunov, owner of the Iskra Manufacturing Plant. Recon suggests its energy consumption is far above the legal limit. The Rokot wants proof for the Veche so that the plant is shut down and the Kristall goes where it is needed most. Vodyanitsa had hoped Chugunov would let something slip in conversation, but he stays tight-lipped, so she plans to let the issue slip to Mitya, a renowned energy expert whom the authorities would take seriously. Later, in Mistilteinn, Chugunov tells his staff he is closing the plant.

527.content:
Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya (also: Energy Commission, Snezhnaya Energy Commission, Royal Energy Commission): The Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya, often just the Energy Commission, is the state organisation responsible for Snezhnaya's energy upkeep. It maintains the Kresnik's Torches, the furnaces that make Snezhnayan cities habitable, and manages the transport and use of Kresnik Kristall, the ore the torches burn. It answers to Zapolyarny Palace.

Its staff are mostly administrators, inspectors and technicians who travel between torches. A few are scientists: Mitya, an expert in energy technology, also works on Pierro's Project Mistilteinn at the Armory Palace.

Structure: The Commission has a President, a Vice President and rank-and-file administrators, technicians and prospectors who work in the field. The post of President fell vacant on Izmaylov's death and has been covered by an Acting Chair assigned from Zapolyarny Palace, with Zaretsky as Vice President. Its people are constantly on the move, because the torches they tend are spread across the whole nation. Staff such as Rakitina inspect local torches, while others, such as Yelagina and Zaretsky, work in the central Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd. Zavyalov and others report that outdoor teams sometimes cross paths with Shadow Realms.

Field teams appear in the open world as Energy Commission Prospectors and logistics or contract staff at facilities, ice quarries, ruins and maintenance centres. Rakitina, at the Morepesok torch, describes herself as an administrator for the Commission, so the work is not only manual. Staff also work from Nasha Town, where Manez says he was working on kinetic mechanisms for the Commission before his father pulled him back to run a port. The Commission is not the same body as the Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, which runs the trains that carry the ore.

Leadership: The Commission has been led by an Acting Chair, Zarechnaya, since its long-time President Izmaylov, an old Domovoy, died. She was sent from Zapolyarny Palace to keep the Commission running until a permanent chair is found.

Zarechnaya says the post could not be left empty, since the Commission is vital to people's livelihoods across Snezhnaya, and hopes to return to the Palace soon. She finds the handover paperwork in perfect order yet suspects things have been carefully hidden, and then shrugs it off as long as the Commission keeps functioning.
