Zaretsky, the Vice President, grumbles about the High Table and the gangs and says some matters left by the former Chairperson now fall to people lower down. Staff such as Zybina still call Izmaylov "the President" out of habit.

Izmaylov was long-lived and held the presidency for a very long time. He had hoped to join the Commission as a young man, but Grand Duke Alvis placed him at Hvergelmir to spy on Aksinya. Her kindness converted him, and after she vanished in the Cataclysm he took the presidency from under Alvis' nose after making an undisclosed deal with the new Tsaritsa. Later he also became Speaker of the High Table, the council of the fae gangs. Late in life he handed that post to Zmei and moved the Commission away from Shadow Realm commissions.

Members: Named staff, all met as NPCs in 7.0, include Zarechnaya (Acting Chair), Zaretsky (Vice President), Yelagina (keeps the central torch's log), Rakitina (inspects a local torch), Zavyalov, Zybina (who has to handle technical problems alone), and Mitya. Izmaylov is the deceased President. Manez is a former member who left for family reasons.

Mitya is the Commission's most prominent scientist, an energy expert known for being talkative, sociable and fond of the Korolevskiy Theater. His sentient scarf sometimes chokes him to stop him leaking secrets. He is escorted by Commander Valeriy of the Special Assignments Battalion, and in Pierro's Project Mistilteinn he extracted energy from Stellar Linchpins and reverse-engineered it into Anti-Celestia Energy. Zybina says the Commission once had a "technical expert" who made troubleshooting much faster and has since been sent elsewhere; the text does not name him, so do not assume it is Mitya.

Goals: The Commission exists to keep Snezhnayans warm and alive. Its work is to keep the Kresnik's Torches running, supply them with Kresnik Kristall, and ensure that ore and heat reach every settlement. Rakitina describes the network design: instead of one mega-torch for the entire permafrost, which proved a pipe dream, Snezhnaya maps habitable zones with torches as local nodes joined by railways, cutting the heat lost in long-distance transport. The Eye of Graeae says that before the torches existed the land consisted only of Frigid and Subzero zones, utterly unsuited to human habitation.

Methods: Routine work is inspection and logging: staff listen to a torch, check its exhaust pipes and record its state, then clear faults. Ore is mined mainly in Novokitezhgrad and shipped by rail to every torch. A village such as Alatyr, which has no train station, can lose its deliveries and risk freezing, as a Druzhna soldier fears in the quest Gunfire in the Silent Lands. When teams find a Shadow Realm while travelling, protocol is to leave safely and report it to the Druzhna.

The Druzhna in turn say they handle every Shadow Realm report the Commission sends, by forming search groups that neutralise the energy core if they can find it or else seal the Realm off. Most Shadow Realms vanish on their own, so the real danger is entering one by accident. Yarovaya, a Druzhna officer, finds the Commission oddly well informed about Shadow Realms and calls it good enough that they detect them in time.

History: **Origins.** The Commission is tied to the Belyi Tsar's era. According to the loading-screen text, the Belyi Tsar created the Kresnik's Torch to help humans survive. In Yelagina's words, construction of the central torch began almost immediately after his experiments in the Pale Crown Palace were finished, and the prototype torches remain there. The wiki's history section for the Commission itself is blank, so no founding date is known.

**Izmaylov's presidency.** Izmaylov took the chair after the Cataclysm destroyed Kitezhgrad and the new Tsaritsa showed little regard for the old guard. Alvis went off to build Novokitezhgrad to win her favour, and Izmaylov instead struck his own bargain with the Tsaritsa. Their rivalry later played out over who would direct the Transport Bureau, until the heroes of Luchkin, whom Izmaylov backed, put down a rebellion and credited him with the win. He and the survivors founded the High Table.

**The Shadow Realm commissions.** For about five centuries the Commission took on Shadow Realm work, in part so that Izmaylov could search for Aksinya. It cost him his health. Aksinya was eventually rescued, visited the aged Izmaylov, and he returned the pen she had given him. Satisfied, he steered the Commission away from deep involvement in Shadow Realm matters.

Relations: - **Zapolyarny Palace and the Tsaritsa**: the Commission is affiliated with the Palace, which sent its Acting Chair.
- **Druzhna**: they take over Shadow Realm reports that Commission teams pass on.
- **High Table and the Izmaylov gangs**: Izmaylov led both the Commission and the High Table, so their histories are linked. Gang members say the Commission and Druzhna leave them the thankless jobs.
- **Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau**: carries the ore the Commission oversees.

- **Armory Palace and Pierro**: Mitya carries out energy research for Project Mistilteinn there, and Pierro treats his eccentricity as the price of results.
- **Hvergelmir and Aksinya**: Izmaylov's loyalty to Aksinya shaped the Commission's Shadow Realm work.
- **Alvis**: Izmaylov's lifelong rival, from the contest over the presidency.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Commission still operates under an Acting Chair, Zarechnaya. Its president Izmaylov is dead.

Content checked for 7.1 gives no Commission-specific story; Mitya's fix note in the 7.1 patch notes only concerns an Elemental Type icon.

528.comment: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya: Kresnik's Torch
528.content: A Kresnik's Torch is a furnace that burns Kresnik Kristall and keeps a temperature-controlled zone alive around a city or settlement. Every Snezhnayan city is built around one, the loading-screen text credits the Belyi Tsar with creating it, and smaller civilian models stand across the land. The most important one is the central torch in Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd, built soon after the Belyi Tsar's work at the Pale Crown Palace ended, where prototype torches still stand. The Commission is the organisation responsible for overseeing and maintaining them. In gameplay, small torches dispense Kresnik Energy for the Eye of Graeae.

529.comment: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya: Kresnik Kristall
529.content: Kresnik Kristall is the crystalline ore that Snezhnaya burns for warmth. Quest text describes it as power refined from the authority released when the Cryo Dragon lost control in Snezhnaya about 6,000 years ago, and Aksinya says the outpouring turned ley lines into veins of pure crystal. Early settlers are said to have found the veins by following Kristall Bugs. It burns very efficiently, and it is mined mostly in Novokitezhgrad and sent out by rail, with the Commission overseeing transport and use.

530.comment: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya: Izmaylov
530.content: Izmaylov, the Old Sire, was a Domovoy of Kitezhgrad who served first at Hvergelmir under Aksinya and later served as President of the Royal Energy Commission and Speaker of the High Table. He was devoted to Aksinya, spent centuries seeking her, and saw her rescued. His son Vasiliy killed him. For the full account see his own file.

531.content:
Rtawahist (also: Rtawahist Darshan, School of Illuminationism, the Rtawahist school): Rtawahist is one of the six Darshans, the great schools of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is illuminationism, the study of the stars, including astronomy and astrology. Its members believe the sky reflects truth and that the stars write people's destinies. Its school colour is blue, and its crest shows an elephant-like mascot.

The Darshan's name comes from the Zoroastrian concept of Asha Vahista, "best truth". In Sumeru only academics may study astrology, although other forms of fortune-telling are allowed. Shakir is the current sage. Azar was its sage until Chapter III, when he fell as Grand Sage of the Akademiya.

Structure: Rtawahist is led by a sage, one of the Six Great Sages who sit on the Akademiya's advisory councils. Below the sage come professors, researchers and students. Students may take elective courses in Darshans other than their own, although how often that happens is not stated. Its disciplines include astronomy and astrology. Students work on star charts, dissertations and papers, and scholars keep regular long hours.

A Rtawahist student can specialise further. Layla, for example, studies Theoretical Astrology. Voice-overs also mention a chief editor of Rtawahist who keeps Starlogs showing the fates of all living beings, and Mona's astrology column in The Steambird is well known among Rtawahist scholars.

Leadership: Shakir is the current Rtawahist sage. Azar was the Darshan's sage and the Akademiya's Grand Sage before he was removed.

Shakir looks stern but is soft-spoken. He is devoted to his work and tracks his tasks on a whiteboard. He once taught Layla and, in the Chapter III quest As All Falls to Emptiness, helped the Traveler with his expertise on dreams and foresight.

Azar rose to Grand Sage. After the death of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, he and other sages wanted a proper god to replace her successor Lesser Lord Kusanali, whom they judged a disappointment. As Grand Sage he barred desert-born students from the entrance exam that decides which Darshan a new student may join. When the Archon's authority was restored in Chapter III, Azar was removed. He was a Rtawahist sage, and the sages who supported him were replaced with new ones.

Members: - **Shakir**: sage and the Akademiya's expert on dreams and foresight.
- **Layla**: a student of Theoretical Astrology, chronically sleep-deprived, who sleepwalks and finds her work finished in the morning.
- **Azar**: former sage and Grand Sage, now exiled.
- **Haypasia**: a researcher the Akademiya considers a genius for linking to the Irminsul with Spirit Borneol after three years of training.
- **Ashk, Qushji and Farghani**: scholars met in the open world, who watch the sky or calculate star courses.
- **Kaveh's father**: a Rtawahist scholar who entered the Interdarshan Championship 20 years ago and later died helping a caravan stuck in quicksand.

Faruzan says most Rtawahist students, like Layla, are geniuses. Layla's own profile says her first year ended with her listing good observation and estimation skills, and that she often worries about whether her papers are good enough.

Goals: Rtawahist holds that the stars show the truth about the world and that studying them will lead to it. Ashk says the untouchable sky conceals the truth, and that the stars "show" a destiny rather than decide it, because a decided destiny could be changed. Ashk adds that mortal sight is limited and asks who can guarantee they see all the celestial signs clearly.

Methods: Rtawahist scholars watch the sky, draw and recalculate star charts and write theses on the movements of the heavens. Calculation takes as much time as stargazing, which is why Sitt jokes that if they are not watching the sky they are calculating. Haypasia's research took a different route, linking her mind to the Irminsul using Spirit Borneol.

History: The Akademiya's Six Great Schools were set up with the Akademiya itself under Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, each representing a type of wisdom, and Rtawahist is one of the six that endured. In the wiki's account, the Darshan's later history is mostly recorded through its people.

**Twenty years ago.** Kaveh's father, a Rtawahist scholar working for the Akademiya, entered the Interdarshan Championship to win the Diadem of Knowledge for his son Kaveh. After meeting Sachin he told his family he was going to Aaru Village in the desert, where he supported the villagers financially and medically. He died saving a caravan stuck in quicksand.

**Azar's rule.** Under Azar the Akademiya shut desert-born students out of the entrance exam. When Dottore, a scholar expelled long ago and now a Fatui Harbinger, offered to make a new god, Azar and three other sages accepted at once. Naphis and Baladhuri, who opposed it, were locked up on his orders. Azar oversaw the preparations, which included a dream samsara that harvested the energy of the city's inhabitants. He threatened Nilou during the Sabzeruz Festival and banned public art performances. When Cyno noticed anomalies in the data he submitted to the Akasha System and asked to investigate, Azar refused and told him he had no right to judge, and Cyno resigned as General Mahamatra.

Relations: - **Other Darshans**: Rtawahist is one of six schools and the others (Amurta, Spantamad, Haravatat, Vahumana and Kshahrewar) each have a different specialty and colour. Sitt's service-desk line sums up Rtawahist as watching the sky or calculating.
- **The Steambird**: a magazine whose astrology column by Mona is popular among Rtawahist scholars.
- **Cyno**: he is a former General Mahamatra rather than a member, but he arrested Azar in Chapter III.

- **Spantamad**: a sister school; Lisa and Cyno both studied there. Rtawahist and Spantamad both had sages replaced after Azar's fall.
- **The Archon**: Azar's group wanted a replacement for Lesser Lord Kusanali. Her return and the restoration of the Irminsul ended that plan.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Rtawahist is led by Shakir. Azar remains in exile in the Avidya Forest, and no new Rtawahist story was found after Chapter III.

Layla, Shakir and other scholars appear in the open world and in events. The Darshan continues its research on the sky.

532.content: Azar was the Rtawahist sage and the Grand Sage of the Sumeru Akademiya. After Greater Lord Rukkhadevata died, he and other sages wanted a new god, and he accepted Dottore's offer to build one. He locked up Naphis and Baladhuri for opposing it, harvested the city's energy through a dream samsara, and threatened Nilou to shut down her performance. In Chapter III Cyno arrested him; after the Irminsul was restored he and his accomplices supposedly repented and were exiled to the Avidya Forest.

533.content: Shakir is the current sage of Rtawahist. He is tall, with long brown hair, a full beard and round golden glasses, and wears a deep blue sherwani. He is stern in manner and soft-spoken in practice. He was once Layla's master and helped the Traveler during As All Falls to Emptiness by contributing his expertise on dreams and foresight.

534.content: Layla is a Cryo character and a student of Theoretical Astrology in the Rtawahist Darshan. She is prone to sleepwalking and loses sleep over academic stress, and believes "the Stars' Blessing" is why she wakes to find her papers completed. Her own character story says she is slower to finish papers than her peers, but has good observation and estimation skills. Her full entry is a separate character entry.

535.content: Haypasia is a Rtawahist researcher and considered a genius for connecting to the Irminsul with Spirit Borneol after only three years of training. In A Forest of Change she ignored the Traveler's request for directions to focus on her work, which caused the Traveler to faint and see a vision of the Irminsul. Later she believed she had made contact with a divine being and began acting strangely, so Tighnari had her taken to Pardis Dhyai for evaluation rather than see her labelled a Village Keeper and exiled to Aaru Village.

536.comment: Rtawahist: Kaveh's father and the Interdarshan Championship
536.content: The Interdarshan Championship is a competition between the Darshans. Twenty years ago Kaveh's father, a Rtawahist scholar, entered to win the Diadem of Knowledge for Kaveh. Sachin of Vahumana, who sponsored the event, influenced him, and he left for Aaru Village, where he died saving a caravan. Spantamad has produced the highest percentage of champions, and the competition later dropped its fight-to-the-death events.

537.content:
Saurian Relics Association (also: Saurian Relics Association (Faction), the Saurian Relics Association): The Saurian Relics Association is a Natlan organisation that gathers, appraises and studies relics left by the ancient saurians. It was founded by Copan, a scholar of the Collective of Plenty. It is poorly funded and of uneven reputation. Its branch at the Chuwen Fair in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame has become a souvenir counter, a notice board and, in the manager's words, a giant flea market.

Its name promises dragon scholarship, but the Chuwen Fair counter's own map description notes that its interests also include many topics unrelated to saurians.

Structure: The Association employs researchers and excavators, accepts donations from the public, and manages excavation sites across Natlan that visitors enter for a fee. At one long-running site, the guard Quipia charges 300 Mora to dig. The Chuwen Fair branch is managed by Siyah, a Child of Echoes. Relics are appraised at an unnamed "headquarters". No present leader is named.

Known present-day staff are the researchers Akeor (also a part-time archaeologist), Chuno, Hoa (also a part-time courier), Manqu and Mtwa; the investigator Zompaynco; the member Peyotli; the guard Quipia; and the manager Siyah. Members come from several tribes: Chuno, Siyah and Manqu are Children of Echoes, and Zompaynco is from the Collective of Plenty.

Goals: The Association's stated aim is to study the treasures of the age of the ancient dragons and keep them in Natlan. Its notices say relics must not be sold to foreign merchants or research institutions. Surveying and analysis inside Natlan are allowed once the relevant access fees are paid.

It also wants income and reputation. Its notice board advertises "unlimited potential" in place of a base salary, promises diggers fame in both adventuring and archaeology, and presents its finds as contributions to Natlan's technology.

Methods: It appraises and exhibits finds, charges entry fees at dig sites and access fees to foreigners who wish to study relics, and posts "research bounties" with money rewards. Chuno, for example, took a bounty to decipher Iridescent Inscriptions to make up an overspent monthly budget. Its announcements give each find a use, such as a mount saddle or a back-muscle trainer, dated with instruments.

Announcements and replies appear on the Chuwen Fair message board, which also serves for commissions. Appraisals are sometimes contested in public. When Hoa suggested her find might simply be a saddle lost by a recent Qucusaur Rider, the Association asked how badly the Rider would have had to fall to bury it that deep, and Hoa answered by asking about compensation for work injuries.

Reputation: Mixed. Siyah admits the collection has "essentially turned into a giant flea market". Researcher Hoa has doubted one of its conclusions. On the other hand, the Speaker's Chamber has publicly thanked the Association for its excavations and said an object related to early Phlogiston Engraving will be used for research at the Temple of Pax.

The Association has also been dragged into local rumour. A board thread claimed that Citlali's divination tools had been dug up and that her curse might spread. The Association replied that the objects were just liquor bottles and that someone had been sent to return them. This is a joking exchange on a message board, not a verified event.

History: Copan is the earliest known figure. Artifact text describes a scholar of the Collective of Plenty who called himself President of the Association, carried woven scrolls and tinkered with mysterious mechanisms. When the Cataclysm destroyed his scrolls, he put his research aside and helped adapt machines of the secret source from ancient ruins to aid warriors. He later joined the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team and died on the way to the Tonatiuh. At some later point a group of Association members was commissioned to investigate Ochkanatlan and disappeared, so the Association has avoided anything to do with the place.

In the present the Association is a modest outfit whose dig sites have been open for years, and Quipia says her site is the cheapest because it has been open the longest. In Version Luna I (6.0), Zompaynco appears in Nod-Krai's Nasha Town, supposedly there to look into saurian ruins but mostly warming himself by a furnace.

Relations: It has close ties to the Collective of Plenty (its founder and an investigator) and the Children of Echoes (its shopkeeper and several researchers). The Speaker's Chamber has expressed appreciation for its work. It serves Natlan's public and visitors but refuses relic exports. During Nefer's Research Spillover quest, her private thought is a guess that Zompaynco's arrival might worry the Guild about rivals.

Its notices attribute finds to the territories of the Flower-Feather Clan, the Collective of Plenty and the Masters of the Night-Wind.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Association is an ordinary part of Natlan life. Its Chuwen Fair counter becomes available to the Traveler once Tona's Flame's Restitution reaches level 50, and it sells goods for Pyro Sigils. Before then Siyah explains that stock has arrived in a random state and is not yet sorted.

538.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Siyah and the Chuwen Fair counter
538.content:
Siyah manages the Association's branch at the Chuwen Fair. He is a Child of Echoes, who he says are reputed to have a knack for business, which is why he was made shopkeeper, though he says the shop really needs a storage specialist. He says the Association's official purpose is to collect and sort relics, but in truth it has become a giant flea market. For Pyro Sigils the counter sells weapon ascension materials, Mora and furnishing blueprints. It sits beside the Association's message board.

Siyah's idle line is a complaint that sorting is hard. When the Traveler jokes that their backpack is just as cluttered, he briefly believes them, then laughs and asks for organising tricks.

539.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Association message board
539.content: The Chuwen Fair board posts commissions, hiring notices and announcements, cycling through different messages. Posts include a recruitment drive for analysts, provenance experts and excavators, and finds credited to Hoa, to Akeor with the traveling scholar Tahmures, and to Tizoc of the Collective of Plenty. The Speaker's Chamber answers one post, and a joking thread about Citlali's supposed divination tools also appears.

540.content: Copan was the Association's founder and self-styled president, a scholar of the Collective of Plenty. He died in the Cataclysm era as a member of the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team. Liriwu refers to him as "Uncle Copan" in a note. Little more is stated.

541.content: Members of the Association once took a commission to investigate Ochkanatlan, the ruined city north of the Flower-Feather Clan's territory, and vanished. Manqu, a Child of Echoes who also works with the Association, tells the Traveler that both his tribe and the Association forbid him from going there.

542.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Research bounties and Chuno
542.content: Chuno, a researcher, takes Association research bounties to cover his bills. His current project is deciphering Iridescent Inscriptions, a task he says has never been completed. He is angry at a seller who once sold him fake "Remnants of the Secret Source" and wants only genuine fragments.

543.comment: Saurian Relics Association: Zompaynco in Nod-Krai
543.content: Zompaynco, an investigator from the Collective of Plenty, came to Nasha Town because he heard Nod-Krai had ruins related to saurian relics. He hates the cold, warms himself by a furnace and is more taken with Nod-Krai's machines than with his research. He wants to meet the Frostmoon Scions, and Nefer's quest has him asking for an introduction through Lyylikki. He says the funds he requested are for research, and admits he cannot keep buying "funny little machines".

544.content:
Schwanenritter (also: Schwanenritters, Swan Knights, heroes of Dahri): The Schwanenritter ("Swan Knights" in German) were an order of Khaenri'ahn knights who fought the Abyssal monsters when the cataclysm struck Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago. Led by Knight Marshal Anfortas, they escorted able-bodied survivors up into Sumeru and held the line with machines called Ruin Golems. Their known members all fell, one by one, in a foreign land. Nagarjuna's scholars, the future Order of Skeptics, honoured them as the "heroes of Dahri".

Almost everything known about them comes from texts left in Sumeru's ruins, not from living witnesses. Their story is told through logs, letters and epitaphs.

Structure: Canon gives only fragments of the order's organisation. Its head was the Knight Marshal, and below him were ranks such as Knight Commander and Garrison Commander, whose relative order is unknown. Members carried epithets, such as "Sentinel of the Golden Hall", "Beard-Father" and "Damsel of the Dale". The order's machines were called Mechanical Wardens. Its size, founding and place in the Khaenri'ahn state are not stated.

Leadership: Knight Marshal Anfortas led the order and, when King Irmin was left "indisposed" by the crisis, proclaimed himself Marshal Regent and led the Regnum Concilium Ultimum, the Final Kingdom Council.

Under Anfortas, Hadura served as a Garrison Commander and later as a Knight Commander, and received the epithet "Sentinel of the Golden Hall" for a successful operation that stalled the beasts. Anfortas lost his left eye in the fight that ended with Hadura's execution. A coded message left on Ruin Guards in Dharma Forest, attributed to him, says the Schwanenritters "fought to the last one".

Members: Four named members are known:
- **Anfortas**: Knight Marshal and Marshal Regent, the last of them standing.
- **Hadura**: "Sentinel of the Golden Hall", a Knight Commander. Later called a traitor, executed and given a knight's funeral anyway. Klingsor of the Order of Skeptics later called Hadura his ancestor.
- **Hildric**: "Beard-Father". Died of multiple-organ failure in a foreign land.
- **Ynghildr**: "Damsel of the Dale". Went missing in battle against the dark beasts, leaving only her signet ring and a second personal item.

Ynghildr is also titled "Sword of a Lost Homeland" in the quest text of Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter, where she is the Shadowy Husk guarding the control module of the fallen Valley of Dahri golem. This later reading of her fate is not something the order's records know: they list her only as missing.

Goals: First, to hold back the dark beasts that overran Khaenri'ah, and second, to get the survivors who could still fight or work out of the dying kingdom and onto the surface. In Sumeru the aim narrowed to fighting the cataclysm to the end. The Order of Skeptics later took up that purpose.

Methods: The knights fought with Mechanical Wardens, huge Ruin Golems of an earlier design than the common Ruin Guards. Hadura also ordered a proving-ground workshop to activate all its self-defence systems before the evacuation went on, because the workshop was unsuitable for the Wardens' large-scale attacks. In Sumeru the order salvaged parts from broken golems to keep weapons working, for want of spares.

One golem was lost in the Desert of Hadramaveth. A second, at the Valley of Dahri, suffered a design defect that made it unstable, and its smart-boot system finally failed. The knights stripped it for parts and left it to await retrieval. Those parts kept the last golem running at Devantaka Mountain. The work log that records these decisions reads like an engineer's logbook, matter-of-fact about shortages and trade-offs.

History: **Cataclysm.** Khaenri'ah's use of knowledge from beyond the skies, understood to be forbidden knowledge, ended in an onslaught of dark beasts. While Irmin was unfit to rule, Anfortas took the regency, and the order chose to leave the kingdom.

**Evacuation.** The knights led able-bodied survivors through the Girdle of the Sands and east to the Dharma Forest, using the Ruin Golems against the monsters. Once on the surface, some refugees were afflicted by a strange disease that turned them into monsters, and some of those not yet affected chose to go back underground.

**Last stand.** In Dharma Forest the knights fought beside Nagarjuna's Akademiya darshan, who acknowledged them as the "heroes of Dahri" despite the bad name Khaenri'ahns had earned for the cataclysm.

**Order of events at the golems.** The Desert of Hadramaveth golem was lost first, where an unnamed Schwanenritter died of what was probably disease. The Valley of Dahri golem was abandoned next, and the Devantaka Mountain golem was the last. Hildric died of organ failure. Ynghildr vanished in battle. That left Hadura and Anfortas.

**The betrayal.** Hadura then betrayed the order and wrecked a machine beyond repair. Anfortas killed them in the ensuing fight and lost an eye, but still granted a knight's funeral because they were the last of his comrades. He carried on alone until his presumed death.

Relations: - **Khaenri'ah's crown**: the order served a kingdom whose king, Irmin, was incapacitated at the crisis. Anfortas replaced him at the council.
- **Order of Skeptics**: Nagarjuna's darshan fought beside the knights and later continued their cause. Hadura's relatives presumably followed Nagarjuna and joined them.
- **Abyss**: the enemy throughout. The later Abyss Order is a separate story.

- **Alberich Clan**: Anfortas is presumed to belong to the clan of non-royal regents.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: an Akademiya investigation team's interim report, left at the Zandik's Legacy site, records the golems' salvaged parts. Zandik's own note says the golem parts have a unique, ingenious style unlike anything made under the Archons, and that he meant to keep the secret from his team.

Reputation: Among Nagarjuna's followers the knights were remembered as heroes. Khaenri'ahns in general were blamed for the cataclysm, and Klingsor's grievance shows how that stigma could harden into doubt about the Order of Skeptics' own history.

Status as of 7.1: The order no longer exists. Its last known member, Anfortas, is presumed dead.

Nothing about the Schwanenritter was found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content. Their ruins and logs in Sumeru remain the only places their story is told.

545.content: Anfortas was the Knight Marshal of the Schwanenritter. When King Irmin became "indisposed" in the cataclysm, he declared himself Marshal Regent and led the Final Kingdom Council. He led the survivors into Sumeru and fought to the end, losing his left eye to Hadura. Like Irmin, he is one-eyed. See his own entry for his biography.

546.comment: Schwanenritter: Hadura, Sentinel of the Golden Hall
546.content: Hadura began as a Garrison Commander who ordered defensive systems armed so the evacuation could go on. As a Knight Commander they were given the epithet "Sentinel of the Golden Hall" after leading a successful operation against the beasts. Later they betrayed the order and destroyed a machine, and Anfortas executed them, losing an eye. Hadura was the last of Anfortas' comrades, so a proper knight's funeral was granted. Klingsor, much later, called Hadura his ancestor. Canon does not say why they betrayed the order. Their gender is not stated here; the wiki uses "they".

547.content: Hildric, "Beard-Father", died of multiple-organ failure in a foreign land, and the Schwanenritter chronicle asks that he rest in peace there. Ynghildr, "Damsel of the Dale", went missing in a battle with the dark beasts. Only her signet ring and one other item were recovered, and a knight's funeral was arranged. Later quest text reveals she was not simply lost: she became a Shadowy Husk and kept guard over the control module of the Valley of Dahri golem until the Traveler defeated her in Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter.

548.comment: Schwanenritter: Ruin Golems and Mechanical Wardens
548.content: Three huge Ruin Golems stand in Sumeru: in the Desert of Hadramaveth, the Valley of Dahri and on Devantaka Mountain. The wiki identifies them as the Schwanenritter's Mechanical Wardens. In Vimana Agama, Jazari notes that the golem's Amiti device carries Khaenri'ahn patterns of an earlier type than those on common Ruin Guards. The golems' work logs are the main source for the order's last days.

key: We Schwanenritters have fought to the last one
549.comment: Schwanenritter: Final days of the Schwanenritter
549.content: Fragments of a coded message can be found on Ruin Guards around Dharma Forest. When all five parts are deciphered, they read: "We Schwanenritters have fought to the last one." It is the clearest statement of the order's end. Reading all five parts earns the achievement In the Name of Anfortas, whose description sends the player to the place where the heroes met their end.

550.content:
Scions of the Canopy (also: Huitztlan, Huitztlan tribe, the Scions of the Canopy, Scion of the Canopy): The Scions of the Canopy, also called the Huitztlan, are one of the six tribes of Natlan. They live in a village of huge trees and platforms hung by ropes off the cliffs of Coatepec Mountain, alongside their saurian partners, the Dendro Yumkasaurs. They are known as couriers, hunters and explorers, and they love extreme sports. Their chief is Wayna. The tribe's best-known member today is the Saurian Hunter Kinich, and the Pyro Archon Mavuika was born among them about 500 years ago.

The tribe's hero lineage is the Ancient Name "Malipo", tied to the legendary Turnfire: the ancestor Yupanqui, the cataclysm hero Burkina, and now Kinich have carried it.

Structure: The tribe is led by a chief, currently Wayna, together with a council of elders. Its village, also named "Scions of the Canopy", is a sub-area of Coatepec Mountain. According to the official site, the ancestors hung giant trees on the cliff with ropes and grappling hooks, which gave the tribe its name. Within the tribe operates the Courier's Longhouse, a courier agency led by Michica, which delivers goods that are not too valuable, fragile or dangerous. The tribe also runs a Learning Lodge where elders teach the children for free.

Like every Natlan tribe, the Scions have an ancestral Wayob spirit that selects worthy members for Ancient Names. Their bonded saurian is the Yumkasaurus, whose grappling tongue suits life on the cliffs, and their tribal warriors are known in-game as the "Swiftstep" fighters. The tribal emblem marks them as specialists in communications and in tracking saurians.

Leadership: Wayna is the chief. He insists he is not as old as the nickname "Uncle Wayna" suggests: in his view, leading the tribe simply means he has the most adventuring experience of anyone in it. He is easygoing and fond of risk, but he still warns people not to be reckless. He borrowed a Spiritspeaker Stone from Citlali of the Masters of the Night-Wind, and he gave it to the Traveler's group when they set out to rescue Kachina.

Elders share major decisions. Elder Trinidad cared deeply about the Turnfire Night ritual. When Kinich showed no interest in it, he sought outside help, which brought in the Traveler. Elder Leik taught at the Learning Lodge and raised the young Kinich for years after his father died.

Members: - **Kinich**: Saurian Hunter, former courier, current bearer of "Malipo" and one of Natlan's six modern heroes. He is bound by contract to the self-proclaimed dragonlord Ajaw.
- **Mavuika**: the Pyro Archon, born to an ordinary Scions of the Canopy family before the cataclysm.
- **Wayna**: the chief.
- **Michica**: manager of the Courier's Longhouse.
- **Vichama**: a famed scout and Ancient Name bearer who helped the Traveler's group find Kachina's Ancient Name. He died defending the village in the Abyss invasion.

Other named villagers include Aclla (the village "doctor"), Hakau ("Wayfinder"), Roca (a rock-climbing instructor), Sinchi (a hunter), Tundama (a courier), the guards Illapa and Yawar, and the children Toba and Huni, who call Kinich "Malipo" Kinich. Poca and Tisoc guard the Mother Flamegranate Tree. Historical members include Yupanqui, Burkina, Mallko (Vichama's friend, who died five years before the Archon Quest when his whole Night Warden War team fell), and Mavuika's mother Haumia and younger sister Hine.

Goals: The Scions want to honour their ancestors, keep their bonds with the Yumkasaurs, and serve Natlan as its messengers and pathfinders. For generations they have also cared for Kongamato, the ancient Yumkasaur called the Mountain King, and kept his Abyssal corruption in check.

Methods: The tribe earns its living from delivery and hunting commissions. Its people climb, rappel and grapple across terrain other Natlanese avoid, and they track and hunt dangerous saurians. Visitors come for extreme sports: rock climbing, rappelling, bungee jumping and "volcano parkour". Natlan's local Adventurers' Guild is said to be made up mostly of Huitztlan.

A courier's work, as one tribal furnishing describes it, needs more than an adventurous spirit: travel over varied ground, long survival in the wild, and precise navigation. In wartime these skills become intelligence work. During the 5.1 Abyss invasion Wayna sent many tribesmen out as messengers to carry real-time news across Natlan, and Kinich's tribe delivered battle reports between fronts. Kinich's own habit of setting a price for every job, which troubled some elders, is a personal trait, not tribal law.

History: **Yupanqui and the Turnfire.** About 2,000 years ago the tyrant Och-Kan used a terrible fire, the Turnfire, to oppress Natlan. Anyone it touched felt burning pain behind them and was burned to ash if they looked back. The tribe's ancestor Yupanqui, an old companion of Och-Kan who turned against him, stole the Turnfire and hurled it at the tyrant's army. Then, thinking he heard Och-Kan's voice, he looked back. He burned for a hundred days until he pierced the ley lines and fell into the Night Kingdom, where the Turnfire is said to burn still. The tribe remembers him as the "Firethief", and his Ancient Name Malipo is bound to the Turnfire.

**The cataclysm.** Five hundred years ago, Burkina and his Yumkasaur Kongamato fought the Abyss alongside the hero Tenoch and the Pyro Archon Mavuika. Kongamato was corrupted by the Abyss and killed Burkina, who passed his blood and power to the saurian as he died. Kongamato survived for centuries and became the Mountain King, a living symbol of the tribe's glory. After the war, Mavuika's younger sister Hine became an architect and helped rebuild the tribe, though none of her buildings survive.

**The present (5.0-5.1).** Wayna gave Citlali's Spiritspeaker Stone to the group rescuing Kachina, and Vichama helped them. In Kinich's story quest the tribe held what became its last Turnfire Night (see the entry below). In the 5.1 Abyss invasion the village fell and was evacuated. Many Scions died, among them Vichama. They returned after Mavuika ended the invasion.

Relations: - **Pyro Archon**: Mavuika is a daughter of the tribe. Her father was one of three warriors killed in a three-day battle in her youth. When she visited the site of her family's old home 500 years later, a descendant of a Huitztlan family Hine had helped gave her Hine's architecture manual.
- **Masters of the Night-Wind**: Wayna borrowed a Spiritspeaker Stone from Citlali, and the Traveler's group destroyed it during Kachina's rescue. Wayna dreaded her scolding but agreed that a life mattered more.
- **Other tribes**: the six tribes share the Pilgrimage, the Ancient Name system and the war against the Abyss. Kinich is close to Mualani of the People of the Springs and Kachina of the Children of Echoes.
- **Abyss**: the tribe's old enemy. It corrupted Kongamato and overran the village in 5.1. The Abyss Lector Enjou has been studying the Turnfire, and he gave Kinich the Beastly Rift used in the last Turnfire Night.

Reputation: Other Natlanese see the Scions as fearless climbers and reliable messengers, and the village is a destination for thrill-seekers. Wayna treats even war like an extreme sport: whichever way a jump ends, he says, every outcome has value and deserves to be remembered. Kinich's cold, price-first manner is famous, and Mavuika defends it. In her view, "Malipo" also means "cost" or "price" and teaches people to stay calm and ask the questions others do not want to hear.

Secrets: The tribe's stories say Burkina fell fighting the Abyss. Kinich, the current Malipo, revealed in his story quest that the Mountain King killed Burkina in a fit of Abyss-driven madness. Burkina chose not to fight back and gave his blood and power to the saurian. Kongamato carried that shame for five centuries and even asked to be put out of his misery.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is back in its cliff village under Chief Wayna, rebuilding after the 5.1 Abyss invasion killed many of its people.

Kongamato's corruption is now sealed by a protective shell, so the yearly Turnfire Night is no longer needed, and the Mountain King has offered to train future heroes. No new tribe story developments were found for 6.0-7.1; the 6.x Archon Quests take place in Nod-Krai and 7.0-7.1 in Snezhnaya.

551.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Turnfire and the Malipo name
551.content: The Turnfire was Och-Kan's weapon of oppression. It burned anyone who looked back at it. Yupanqui stole it, used it on the tyrant's army, then looked back and burned for a hundred days before falling into the Night Kingdom. The Ancient Name "Malipo" comes from it. Its bearers are Yupanqui, Burkina and, today, Kinich, whose profile title is "Turnfire Hunt". Malipo is one of the six heroic Ancient Names, and a bearer who truly connects with it can receive memories of earlier holders. Mavuika notes that Malipo also means "cost" or "price".

552.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Kongamato, the Mountain King
552.content:
Kongamato is a gigantic Yumkasaurus, Burkina's partner from the cataclysm, who joined the great heroes against the Abyss. Abyssal corruption both stretched his lifespan and threatened his sanity. The tribe kept him asleep in a cave and fed him Mountain King Flamegranates grown from the Mother Flamegranate Tree. Some tribesfolk think he is huge because of a special build, but the Archive says he has just lived a long time and eaten far too much. After the last Turnfire Night a shell formed around him that stops him from absorbing or leaking Abyssal energy. He now trains the tribe's warriors.

Before the Traveler descended into the Night Kingdom, Kongamato appeared with Kinich as a projection. He said Burkina had come to him in a dream and urged him to support the hero of the present age.

553.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Turnfire Night
553.content: Turnfire Night was the tribe's ceremony, usually held every year, to commemorate their ancestors and drain the Mountain King's Abyssal corruption. A flame bearer, traditionally the current Malipo, led a delegation that lit braziers with kindling from the Sacred Flame and carried the fire into Kongamato's cave. In Kinich's story quest the corruption was building up faster than usual. Kinich planned to put Kongamato into a Beastly Rift provided by Enjou, and Wayna reluctantly agreed. Elder Trinidad, believing they meant to kill the Mountain King, smashed the device. Kongamato woke and badly burned him. Kinich and the Traveler subdued the saurian, and Kinich refused his plea to die, telling him to live with his shame. The shell that formed afterwards made this the last Turnfire Night.

554.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Courier's Longhouse
554.content: The Courier's Longhouse is the courier agency based in the Scions' village and managed by Michica. It handles ordinary deliveries, not extremely valuable, fragile or dangerous goods. Michica regularly loses patience with couriers who lose packages. Kinich and his late father once worked for it.

555.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Mother Flamegranate Tree
555.content: The tribe guards the Mother Flamegranate Tree, whose root cave is taboo ground. Its Mountain King Flamegranates are picked and offered to Kongamato, and some say Yumkasaurs secretly bring him Flamegranates too. In the world quest Ripe For Trouble the guards Poca and Tisoc look into why the fruit will not ripen.

556.comment: Scions of the Canopy: Learning Lodge
556.content: The Learning Lodge is where the tribe's elders teach children, free of charge. Elder Leik let the young, impoverished Kinich attend in exchange for running errands. When Leik asked the class to name heroes, the children answered with "Malipo" Burkina and Master Yupanqui. Leik later took Kinich in and trained him for years. Kinich's methods sometimes stirred controversy among the elders, and Leik defended him.

557.content:
Seahook Gang (also: the Seahooks, the original Seahook crew): The Seahook Gang was a gang of thieves and bandits that once held real sway in Nod-Krai, centred on Nasha Town. It no longer exists in its original form: its boss was killed by his own men and the rest scattered. Today the name is used by impostors who want its intimidating reputation. The best-known former member is Jahoda, now an employee of Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets.

Almost everything the world knows of the gang comes from Jahoda's memories, since she joined when it was already established. She describes it as a hard place where making friends was foolish, though some members looked after one another in their own way.

Structure: The gang had a boss, an unnamed man spoken of with a mixture of respect and exasperation, and mid-level leaders such as Zinaida, who brought Jahoda in. Members included skilled earners like Ihanti, who relied on persuasion rather than brute force. Most of the rank and file were thieves who drank, feasted and fought together. The base was a house in Nasha Town where Jahoda had her own room as a child.

The Heizou anecdote relays a rumour that the gang took in exiled criminals from across Teyvat, which fits a hideout where nobody asked about the past. No ranks, headcount or formal organisation are given beyond "boss" and "mid-level leader".

Leadership: The original boss is never named. He is shown as shrewd but fond of his youngest member: he coached Jahoda on how to quiet a rowdy crowd, took her stray apple in the middle of a negotiation, and docked her share when she secretly returned a necklace. One of his sayings was "Grant rest to those who seek it", a code Jahoda and Ihanti both remember. Zinaida, who once protected him, later calls him a blood-soaked bandit chief.

Members: - **Jahoda**: recruited as a child by Zinaida; now an employee of Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets and a playable character. Her own entry carries her story.
- **Zinaida**: a former mid-level leader who brought Jahoda into the gang. According to the intel Nefer holds, she now works for the Voynich Guild as a treasure hunter and covert bodyguard of the port supervisor Manez.
- **Ihanti**: a skilled earner and smooth talker who treated Jahoda as a sidekick. In the Intel Quest "They Who Abandoned the Past" (6.2) he is dying, and he is dead by the end of it.
- **Ratfan**: the wiki lists him as formerly of the gang, but canon presents him as a rich merchant who bribed members to kill their boss. Jahoda killed him.

Other former members are unnamed. Some died, some left Nod-Krai for other nations, and some stayed in Nasha Town and quietly put the past behind them.

Goals: The gang lived by theft and banditry, according to Jahoda. Ihanti stood out from "dumb scams and petty robberies" by getting victims to hand money over willingly. Beyond profit, no ideology is stated.

Methods: Theft, robbery and swindling, plus rough "business deals" with rich targets. In the one job shown in detail (Jahoda's Character Story 2), the gang captured a merchant known as a black-hearted swindler, made him repay his victims and then split the rest among themselves at an all-night feast.

In that story the merchant begged for a pendant, saying it held the only picture of his wife and daughter. The veteran thieves took it for the usual ploy, since prisoners often plead for an item that hides a clue to treasure. Jahoda secretly returned it anyway and lost her share as the price.

History: **Rise.** Nothing is known of the founding. By the time Jahoda arrived the gang was powerful enough to be called a hidden force that once controlled Nasha Town.

**Fall.** Jahoda's Character Story 3 says the rich merchant Ratfan bribed members to assassinate their boss, then burned the evidence with oil. The gang fell into chaos and scattered. In a looser account in the Heizou anecdote, Jahoda says the old leader ended up thrown overboard while underlings fought over the scraps.

**Aftermath.** Jahoda stalked Ratfan over many nights, was badly wounded, and eventually killed him. Nefer then took her on as an employee. By Jahoda's story, Nefer had told her where to find Ratfan and saw her as a pawn who might remove a troublesome man.

**Impostors.** Some time after the breakup, others began using the Seahook name to scam and rob people. In the anecdote "The Crimes of Others", Shikanoin Heizou came to Nod-Krai tracking a fugitive from Inazuma who had joined these self-styled Seahooks. Hired through the Curatorium of Secrets, Jahoda told him they were not the original crew.

Relations: - **Nefer and the Curatorium of Secrets**: Nefer employs Jahoda and, in Jahoda's story, pointed her at Ratfan. Nefer keeps watch on what remains of the gang.
- **Voynich Guild**: employs Zinaida as a treasure hunter and bodyguard.
- **Treasure Hoarders**: Nefer once offered Jahoda introductions to more reliable Treasure Hoarders as a career option, and Jahoda refused.

- **Marechaussee Phantom**: in a Nefer dialogue, Nefer asks Lestocq to track down former gang members said to have reached Fontaine.
- **Shikanoin Heizou**: the Inazuman detective who learned from Jahoda that the Seahook Gang now active are impostors.

Reputation: The name once carried weight and still frightens people, which is why impostors borrow it. Heizou was relieved to learn his targets were only impostors, since he did not fancy facing the real gang and its international cohort. Jahoda treats the gang as a past to leave behind and says Ihanti was no friend.

Status as of 7.1: The original gang is gone. Impostors still use the name in Nod-Krai, and a few ex-members are said to have crossed to Fontaine.

Zinaida works for the Voynich Guild, while Ihanti and Ratfan are dead. Jahoda works for Nefer. No new Seahook Gang story was found for 6.3-7.1.

558.content: Zinaida is an open-world NPC in Nasha Town, titled Treasure Hunter. She was a mid-level leader in the Seahook Gang and recruited Jahoda. As a child Jahoda would slip out to wake her in the night to talk through bad days, and Zinaida would carry her back to bed. She now guards Manez, the port supervisor, for the Voynich Guild, and says that beats protecting a blood-soaked bandit chief. Nefer invites her to visit Jahoda at the Curatorium; Zinaida says it is best left as it is.

559.content: Ihanti was a Seahook Gang member skilled at persuading people to hand over money, and he took Jahoda along as a sidekick. In 6.2 he posts a bounty at the Adventurers' Guild with a stolen pendant as collateral. When Jahoda finds him he is terminally ill, nearly blind and has been robbed. He says his wife and daughter are gone. He asks to be left to die in peace, reminds Jahoda of the boss's code, and gives her a doll he made himself. He is dead the next day and leaves a short letter.

560.content: Ratfan was a wealthy Nod-Krai merchant. According to Jahoda's Character Story 3, he used money to have gang members kill their boss, burned the evidence, and bought intelligence from a mysterious businesswoman. Jahoda hunted him over many nights, then killed him in revenge. He is dead before the Traveler reaches Nod-Krai.

561.content:
Seven Pillars (also: Seven Sages, seven monk-kings, King Deshret's Seven Pillars, Seven Pillars of King Deshret, Seven Pillars of Al-Ahmar): The Seven Pillars, also called the Seven Sages or seven monk-kings, were the chief retainers of King Deshret (Al-Ahmar), the desert god-king of ancient Sumeru. He gave them his power, and they served as his "pyramid of authority". Three were gods he had defeated: Heryshaf the Goat King, Sobek the Crocodile King and Thoth the Ibis King. Bennu and Shesepankh were intelligent constructs he built, and Hermanubis was a human sage raised to be his familiar. The seventh, the Dendro Dragon Apep, was named a Pillar by Deshret but never accepted it.

Almost all of them are gone. Hermanubis died long ago. In 6.6 the three Kings, who had been shut in Aaru for thousands of years, were freed, and Bennu and Shesepankh were woken. Together they voted to open Aaru to the people of Sumeru.

Structure: Heryshaf stood at the head, as deputy-king and Minister of Ministers. Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth were the highest-ranking and are called the Three Retainers. Each Pillar had a style of office. Heryshaf was Minister of Ministers, Sobek Captain of Captains, Thoth Scribe of Scribes, Hermanubis the Greatest of Sages, Bennu the Most-Radiant and Shesepankh the Most-Holy. Apep carried the title Dragon King, the Supreme Spirit, which Deshret and the other six devised and which Apep herself dismissed.

- **Heryshaf, the Goat King**: embodied Deshret's rulership. He executed the king's authority and kept his own counsel.
- **Sobek, the Crocodile King**: embodied Deshret's strength, as foremost general. Statues of him stand at oases and water temples.
- **Thoth, the Ibis King**: embodied Deshret's wisdom as a counsellor. Texts also record him as a flatterer and a god of deceit.
- **Hermanubis, the Greatest of Sages**: the only Pillar who rose from humanity, born among the Tighnar people.
- **Bennu, the Most-Radiant**: Deshret's "soul". A construct who guarded the gates of Aaru.
- **Shesepankh, the Most-Holy**: Deshret's "will". A construct who oversaw all the Jinn of the world.
- **Apep, the Dragon King**: the Dendro Dragon Sovereign, counted by Deshret but not by herself.

Bennu is likened to a great bird winging toward the sun and Shesepankh to a lioness with a human head. In art, Heryshaf wears blue-violet, Thoth red, Sobek blue and Hermanubis purple with a jackal head. Sumeru's scholars say the three Kings were once on the level of the gods. Hermanubis was counted a priest, sage and warrior and was the guide of all priests.

Leadership: Heryshaf was chief of the Pillars and the "right hand" of King Deshret. Above him stood only the king, who raised the Pillars to run his realm. Hermanubis led the priestly class. A Pillar's rank came from the king, and as Thoth puts it, a retainer's fate, including any chance to walk away, was the king's to decide.

Members: The seven Pillars and where they stand as of 7.1:
- **Heryshaf** (Goat King): alive, freed from Aaru in 6.6, and has asked to stay in the Temple of Silence.
- **Sobek** (Crocodile King): alive and freed. Sobek Oasis in the Hypostyle Desert bears his name.
- **Thoth** (Ibis King): alive and freed, and speaks with Nefer as his chosen disciple. He formerly served as a Moon Envoy.
- **Bennu** and **Shesepankh**: constructs that were dormant after Deshret's death. They were woken in 6.6 and can appear on the shield of Aaru Village's Guardians (Bennu) and Dehya's gauntlet (Shesepankh).
- **Hermanubis**: dead. His power lives on in the Temple of Silence, and Heryshaf calls Cyno his representative.
- **Apep**: alive. She helped heal the Dendro Archon Nahida and made her choice about Aaru ahead of time.

Goals: The Pillars existed to serve Deshret's rule and his dream of protecting his people. In the Lay of Al-Ahmar, the three Kings urged him to seek a way past the Heavenly Principles by taking control of the past and defeating death. In 6.6 Heryshaf says Deshret's greatest wish was to protect his people, which is the standard he asks the Pillars to apply when deciding what to do with Aaru.

Methods: Deshret divided his power among his sages across the desert, and the Pillars governed, fought and recorded on his behalf. Sobek led campaigns across many lands, and Thoth is credited with inventing the desert script and its arcane arts. Thoth keeps a chess set tied to Safhe Shatranj, the great chessboard laid out in the desert by Deshret and the Pillars. In 6.6 Thoth shows Nefer that the set can be connected to Safhe Shatranj, and by moving pieces on it allies can be transferred across the material plane in battle. Bennu and Shesepankh needed the three Kings to call them awake with their voices, and Aaru's gate required the unanimous consent of the Seven Pillars to open.

History: **Origin.** Several thousand years ago Deshret split his power among sages across the desert. Among the Pillars, Sobek, Thoth and Heryshaf had been gods defeated in the Archon War. The Lay of Al-Ahmar says the three urged Deshret to defy the Heavenly Principles after he mourned his losses. Heryshaf and then Thoth were rebuked, but Sobek talked Deshret round to seeking forbidden knowledge and immortality. In that legend Deshret then built a huge labyrinth and shut himself inside, and his kingdom was buried by the sand in a single night.

**Banishment.** Deshret imprisoned the three Kings in Aaru for what Sobek calls iniquity. Thoth was told he could be released if humans could answer three questions put to Deshret by Nabu Malikata. They are what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood.

**Hermanubis and the Temple of Silence.** After Deshret's death, Hermanubis led his followers to Tulaytullah and founded the Temple of Silence. When the king of Gurabad besieged the city, Hermanubis shattered himself so his followers could use his power.

**The three questions.** Goudarz answered the first with conspiracy and betrayal, and was granted the power to deceive. Makhaira answered the second with vengeance, and was granted the power to be loved. Both gifts later helped bring them down, though Thoth is unsure whether the gift or the answer was at fault. Around five hundred years ago, the researcher Zandik also visited Thoth and refused a gift. Thoth then gave Nefer the third question, and she gave an answer meant for herself, which did not free him. He rewarded her anyway.

**Apep.** Apep agreed that Deshret could build his civilization in her domain in exchange for his knowledge and power after death. When he died, she took his body and was contaminated by forbidden knowledge. Deshret counted her as a Pillar, but she rejected the idea and never met with the others.

Relations: - **King Deshret (Al-Ahmar)**: their master. The Kings were loyal and also called his most treacherous advisers. His death left Bennu and Shesepankh dormant, and Hermanubis led his own followers away.
- **Apep**: Deshret's pact partner. The Pillars regard her as absent from their number. Sobek calls her vicious and cruel, and Heryshaf says she holds contempt for gods.
- **Nefer**: Thoth's chosen disciple. She freed the three Kings and holds the chess set.
- **Temple of Silence**: founded by Hermanubis. Sethos, its present leader, hosts Heryshaf and Thoth, and Cyno is Hermanubis's representative.
- **Nahida (Dendro Archon)**: Heryshaf and Thoth support her, and Heryshaf warns that her softer style of rule has both advantages and dangers.

Reputation: Scholars of the Akademiya know the Pillars as the sages of King Deshret and honour Hermanubis as a foundational figure of desert civilisation. The desert's legends are less kind to the three Kings: the Lay of Al-Ahmar curses them as the retainers who led the king astray. Sobek is secretly worshipped by some mercenaries, and the Temple of Silence praises Hermanubis. In 6.6 Heryshaf remarks that to today's people the Ibis King seems a kind and passionate god.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pillars no longer act as an order. Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth are free, and Bennu and Shesepankh are awake. Hermanubis is gone, and Apep keeps her distance.

Heryshaf and Thoth have settled, for the time being, in the Temple of Silence, subject to Sethos's agreement. They declined to move their statues there, as Thoth refuses to leave his statue in Hermanubis's home. Aaru is open and the people of Sumeru may modify it. No new content about the Pillars was found for 6.7 to 7.1.

562.content:
Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth were the highest-ranking Pillars. The Lay of Al-Ahmar curses them as the three retainers who flattered Deshret into seeking forbidden knowledge. Heryshaf is enigmatic and neutral and gives few opinions, but he is dry and sharp in 6.6. Sobek was once hot-tempered and competitive but has grown easygoing after thousands of years of tabletop games. Thoth is clever, quick-witted and fond of chess. His nickname for the others, "Goatie" and "Croco", appears in 6.6. Their long confinement softened them, and Thoth says prison can teach a person to cherish what they have.

Thoth says Heryshaf and Sobek could not sit still for chess and played badly, yet the three remained good friends. Heryshaf concedes that the three of them spent their past on misguided ventures that wasted time.

563.content: Bennu and Shesepankh were intelligent constructs made by Deshret, not gods. Bennu guarded the gates of Aaru and the Golden Slumber within, and is serious, earnest and stern with careless colleagues. Shesepankh oversaw all the Jinn, whose mother was Nabu Malikata, and is leisurely, curious and fond of questions. They stood still after Deshret's death. In 6.6, Heryshaf woke them by invoking the right of the Three Kings, and they responded "Saint Bennu" and "Saint Shesepankh" with their will awakening. Bennu has said he admires Hermanubis most among the Pillars, while Shesepankh misses Hermanubis's willingness to take responsibility.

564.comment: Seven Pillars: Hermanubis and the Temple of Silence
564.content: Hermanubis was a Tighnar sage and warrior picked by Deshret to be his familiar, the only Pillar to rise from humanity. He was sincere, steadfast and kind, and he guided the priests. After Deshret's fall he took his followers to Tulaytullah and founded the Temple of Silence to guard Deshret's knowledge and technology. When the king of Gurabad attacked, he shattered himself and left his power to his followers. The wiki says two Ba fragments of his power were later held by the Temple, and that they were fused within Cyno. Heryshaf called Cyno "Hermanubis's representative" in 6.6.

565.comment: Seven Pillars: Apep and the seventh seat
565.content: Deshret named the Dendro Dragon Apep a Pillar in his pact with her, but she never accepted it, and the other six never met her in council. Thoth jokes that she is like a card one never draws. Her relations with Deshret were a bargain for forbidden knowledge. In 6.6 Heryshaf says Apep and Hermanubis's representative had both voted ahead of time to open Aaru.

566.comment: Seven Pillars: Aaru and the three questions
566.content: Deshret locked the three Kings in Aaru and said they could be freed if humans answered the three questions that Nabu Malikata had put to him. They were what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood. Goudarz, Makhaira and Nefer each gave an answer, but only one more answer counted. Thoth spoke through the cats near his ruins, including one called Ashru, which Nefer later took with her. In 6.6 Nefer gave "time", and the seal broke.

567.comment: Seven Pillars: The Pillars at Aaru's Shut (6.6)
567.content: The council that opened Aaru took place after the Traveler's party reached Aaru's Shut in the Mausoleum of King Deshret. Heryshaf, Thoth and Sobek awakened Bennu and Shesepankh, and the five present voted. Shesepankh asked what a unanimous vote means when Apep never answers. Heryshaf made Thoth accountable for the claim that Apep was healing Nahida, as Thoth's disciples had told them. Both constructs approved. Bennu said the Golden Slumber would end. By Heryshaf's final words, the gates of Aaru were reopened.

568.content:
Shenglu Hall (also: Shenglu Chamber): Shenglu Hall governs Liyue's glazed ceramics industry. It is one of the Eight Trades, the commerce sectors that answer to the Liyue Qixing. Its members are said to descend from tribes that lived near the Chasm long before Rex Lapis arrived, and the trade depends on materials from the Chasm.

The Hall is one of only four of the Eight Trades named in canon. In English its name is a "Hall", which follows the Chinese word for a government office.

The Hall appears mostly in the background: on a bulletin board at Feiyun Slope, in the speech of Chasm workers, and through a scholar met in Zhongli's story quest.

Structure: Shenglu Hall is a trade body, not a military or religious order. Canon names an industry representative, Miss Ruoyu, who speaks for the glazed ceramics trade, and a research department, Human Culture and Civilization Research, headed by Wanyu. Ordinary members are ceramics merchants and craftspeople, who are told to follow the Qixing's guidance.

The Hall's notices are posted publicly, such as on the Feiyun Slope board, so merchants in the trade can follow developments.

Leadership: Miss Ruoyu is the Hall's industry representative.

She has been discussing the reopening of the Chasm mine with the Tianquan, Ningguang. The notice says she may go to inspect the situation herself because of the continued incidents there. Nothing more is known about her.

Members: - Miss Ruoyu: industry representative.
- Wanyu: Head of Human Culture and Civilization Research. A scholar who was on her way to a conference when two Geovishap Hatchlings and three Pyro Slimes attacked her near Lingju Pass. Zhongli and the Traveler saved her. She had seen four miners and a child heading toward Nantianmen and said so.
- Muning: not an official of the Hall but a specialist of the Ministry of Civil Affairs posted at the Chasm. Canon says his family plays a significant role in the Hall and the porcelain trade.

Muning's father paid off his son's heavy debts and then told him that he now owed his father. Muning accepted the second chance and now works seriously at the Chasm, though he sometimes finds it pointless. He also likes to spend leisure time at the Yanshang Teahouse and is said to gamble there.

Goals: Keep the glazed ceramics trade supplied and calm. The Hall's main concern in canon is getting the Chasm mine open again, because its ceramics rely on resources from that area.

Methods: The Hall works through the Qixing. Its representative talks to the Tianquan, merchants are asked not to panic, and the trade follows official guidance. Its research department, headed by Wanyu, studies human culture and civilization, which shows an interest in Liyue's early peoples, though canon does not detail that work.

History: According to the Chasm safety technician Jinwu, tribes already lived near the Chasm before Rex Lapis arrived. They gathered Glazed Sand Crystal and traded finished porcelain. After he came they made blood pacts with his yaksha and became his allies, fighting Azhdaha and the monsters of the cataclysm. Most later moved to Liyue Harbor and formed Shenglu Hall, whose glazed ceramics were an art handed down through the generations.

Jinwu is relaying a story ("they say"), and she jokes that the nitpicky members of the Hall had ancestors who fought beside Rex Lapis himself. She adds that the claim stirred up the Hall.

Relations: Under the Liyue Qixing, with Ningguang as the Tianquan dealing with its representative. A sister Hall in the Eight Trades. The Ministry of Civil Affairs runs the Chasm and posted Muning there. Its trade need links it to the Chasm Exploration Team's work.

Yinyuan Hall (salt) is another Hall, with an entirely different founding story.

Reputation: Jinwu calls its members nitpickers. Beyond that, canon does not describe how the Hall is regarded.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Hall remains an active part of the Eight Trades. Nothing about it was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content. Its most recent canon appearance is its notice about the Chasm mine.

569.content: The Feiyun Slope bulletin board carries a Shenglu Hall announcement. Industry representative Miss Ruoyu and the Tianquan have discussed restarting the Chasm mine and made progress. Ningguang, speaking for the Qixing, expressed deep concern about the closure's effect on the glazed ceramics trade and promised to organise the reopening quickly. Because of continuing incidents, Miss Ruoyu says she may investigate personally. Ceramics merchants are told not to panic and to follow the Qixing's guidance.

570.content: Wanyu is a scholar of Shenglu Hall and head of its Human Culture and Civilization Research. In the Historia Antiqua story quest she appears in the third part of No Mere Stone, attacked by monsters near Lingju Pass on her way to a conference. She is rescued, tells Zhongli and the Traveler that she saw four miners with a child, and leaves for her conference.

571.content:
Shogun's Army (also: Shogunate Army, Bakufu Army, Shogunate forces, Inazuma Shogunate army, Army of the Shogun): The Shogun's Army is the military of the Raiden Shogun, Ei, and of the Inazuma Shogunate. It keeps peace and order across Inazuma and is divided among the three bodies of the Tri-Commission. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, provides the main fighting force. The Kanjou Commission handles border security, and the Yashiro Commission handles protection of shrines, festivals and public events. Some members serve the Shogun directly. Its soldiers are also called Shogunate Samurai, and their ranks are modelled on those of the historical Tokugawa shogunate.

Players first meet the army enforcing the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree in Chapter II, and fighting the Watatsumi Army around the Kujou Encampment in Kannazuka. After the Traveler and their allies brought the Vision Hunt Decree to an end, the army stopped seizing Visions, and a ceasefire now stands between it and the Watatsumi Army.

Structure: Soldiers are assigned to a commission, and each commission gives them a different job.
- **Tenryou Commission**: the executive arm of the Shogun and the army's main fighting force. It handles security and military matters and is led by the Kujou Clan.
- **Kanjou Commission**: guards Inazuma's borders, finances and customs. Its soldiers, under the Hiiragi Clan based in Ritou, are the ones who stop travellers at the port.
- **Yashiro Commission**: protects shrines, festivals and public events. It is led by the Kamisato Clan.

A few serve the Shogun directly, outside any commission: Hatamoto and the Okuzumeshuu.

The wiki lists these ranks, which it says mirror the Tokugawa shogunate's military:
- **Ashigaru** are foot soldiers. Kanjou Ashigaru block the way out of Ritou.
- **Doushin** are patrol officers who do police and general-affairs work. Many patrol Inazuma City.
- **Yoriki** are middle-ranking officers who command them. They patrol the city and appear on the battlefield at the Kujou Encampment.
- **Hatamoto** are high-ranking samurai in direct service to the Shogun. The wiki names two, Naoe Hisamasa and Shima Masaoki, both stationed at Inazuma City to guard Tenshukaku.
- **Okuzumeshuu** are the bodyguards of the Almighty Shogun and take orders only from her. The wiki lists Takeshi and Saizou.
- **General** is the highest rank shown. Only Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito hold it.

Generic terms also occur: "Shogunate Officer" for an officer of any rank (Masahito is one, as is Toranosuke) and "Shogunate Samurai" for a soldier.

Leadership: The Raiden Shogun, Ei, is the army's head, and the Kujou Clan commands it in her name through the Tenryou Commission. Kujou Sara, an adopted tengu, and Kujou Masahito are its two Generals.

Sara is described as the pride of the army. She is the Vision Hunt Decree's main enforcer, she surveys battle lines and plans training herself rather than commanding from the rear, and she is said to hold herself to a regimen over ten times as tough as ordinary troops. Her profile says she gave clear orders forbidding harm or exploitation of civilians while carrying out the decree. Masahito, the eldest son of Kujou Takayuki, commands at the Kujou Encampment.

The Kujou Clan's own leadership shifted after Omnipresence Over Mortals. Kujou Takayuki, the Tenryou Commissioner, was found to have colluded with the Fatui and is under house arrest. Masahito, as eldest son, had the right to take over as clan head, but he stood aside for his younger brother Kujou Kamaji, whom he judged better suited, and promised to support him as a warrior of the clan. Kamaji, who manages the Tenryou Commission's government business in Inazuma City, is Proxy Clan Head. After the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, Ei challenged Takatsukasa Susumu, head of the Kujou branch Takatsukasa Clan, to a duel for the Tenryou Commissioner post. Susumu refused. Kamaji accepted, knowing he was outmatched. Afterward Ei said he was not a great descendant of the clan but that his honour was admirable, and she gave the Kujou Clan more time.

Goals: The army exists to keep order and defend the Shogun's realm. Under the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou Commission's job was to seize Visions across Inazuma, which were to be set into the Statue of the Omnipresent God in service of Ei's pursuit of Eternity. The Tenryou Commission also had the stated aim of putting down the Sangonomiya rebellion, and the Kujou Encampment was set up to guard against revolt from Watatsumi Island. Sara in particular believed that Visions in the hands of people with "incorrectly aligned" minds would unsettle the foundations of Inazuma.

Since the repeal, the army's role has moved toward security and keeping the truce. Ei has relaxed the Shogun's functions and let the country open to foreigners, and the army no longer seizes Visions. A Tenryou notice had ordered families with a draft order to send at least one adult. It is not stated whether that draft was ended.

Methods: The army fights as disciplined formations of infantry led by yoriki and officers. Most Shogunate Samurai behave much like Millelith, according to the wiki. Its leaders favour ordered procedure: Vision Hunt Ceremonies, formal duels, and orders against harming civilians. At the Kujou Encampment, the Shogunate has stationed a larger, better-trained and better-equipped force than the Sangonomiya rebels. The Traveler fights Shogunate infantry, infantry captains and yoriki in quests such as In the Name of the Resistance, but these are not enemies that can be met freely in the open world.

History: Most of the army's visible history is recent. About a year before the Traveler's arrival, the Shogun instituted the Sakoku Decree and the Vision Hunt Decree, with the Fatui manipulating the Tenryou and Kanjou commissions behind the scenes. The Tenryou Commission carried out the Vision Hunt. In response the Sangonomiya Resistance (the Watatsumi Army) formed, and the two armies fought a war that had stalled by the time the Traveler arrived. The Traveler and their allies helped end the Vision Hunt Decree, and the Shogun's Army agreed a ceasefire with the Watatsumi Army, signed by Kujou Sara and Sangonomiya Kokomi with the Traveler as witness.

After the ceasefire, Ei descended from the Plane of Euthymia, agreed a new idea of Eternity with the Shogun puppet and lifted the Sakoku Decree. The Tenryou Commission's leaders were then reorganised as described above. The wiki also notes that Masahito had warned his father that the Tatarigami suppressed on Yashiori Island had intensified, and was scolded; the team Takayuki sent to look was lost to its energy. The Kanjou and Tenryou commissions lightened their treatment of foreigners after Omnipresence Over Mortals.

Relations: - **Watatsumi Army**: its opponent in the war, led by Sangonomiya Kokomi with Gorou as General. The Shogunate calls them "Sangonomiya rebels". The two sides now keep a ceasefire.
- **Fatui**: manipulated the Tenryou and Kanjou commissions into pushing the decrees and fed the war.
- **Kamisato Clan**: leads the Yashiro Commission and also controls the Shuumatsuban. Kamisato Ayato refused Fatui help.
- **Hiiragi Clan**: leads the Kanjou Commission and the border. Chisato is acting head.

Reputation: Inazumans' view of the army is mixed. The Kujou Clan is widely regarded as the most loyal and powerful of the families supporting the Shogun, and many ordinary people see Sara as an inaccessible, stone-cold soldier. During the Vision Hunt, the Tenryou Commission was resented. Yashiro soldiers have the best reputation: they are relaxed, care for the people, and are the least controversial of the three groups. Kanjou border guards were known to be abusive toward the foreigners living in Ritou.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the army remains Inazuma's military, but under a more open, post-decree Shogunate. The Vision Hunt and Sakoku decrees are gone and the ceasefire with the Watatsumi Army holds.

The Tenryou Commission has no confirmed new commissioner: Kamaji is acting clan head, Sara and Masahito remain Generals, and Takayuki is under house arrest. No Shogun's Army events were found in the 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

572.content: The Tenryou Commission is the Shogun's executive arm and the part of the Tri-Commission responsible for security and military matters. The Kujou Clan leads it, and its troops are the army's main fighting force. It enforced both the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree, which gave it the worst desertion problems of the three commissions. Its leadership is unsettled after Takayuki's collusion with the Fatui was revealed.

573.content: The Kujou Encampment in Kannazuka is the headquarters of the Shogun's Army under the Tenryou Commission and was built to guard against rebellion from Watatsumi Island. Its fortress is attributed to Kujou Shigeyori. Kujou Masahito, the Shogunate Officer Toranosuke and the yoriki Iwakura Mitsunari are among the NPCs there.

574.content: The Okuzumeshuu are the Almighty Shogun's guard and take orders only from Ei. Hatamoto serve the Shogun directly and are not part of any commission. Two Hatamoto, Naoe Hisamasa and Shima Masaoki, guard Tenshukaku in Inazuma City.

575.content: Masahito, the army's second named General, doubted the Vision Hunt Decree and thought it harmed rather than helped the people. He still fought the Watatsumi Army, and believed either side could win if the war dragged on. Kamaji, his younger brother and Proxy Clan Head, privately held doubts about the Shogun's new policy but kept them to himself. Takayuki, their father, was the Tenryou Commissioner and is now under house arrest. For Sara, see her own character entry.

576.content:
Shuumatsuban (also: Shiyuumatsu-Ban, Shuumatsu-ban, the Shuumatsuban): The Shuumatsuban is a secret unit of ninja in Inazuma, part of the Yashiro Commission's hidden side and answerable to the head of the Kamisato Clan, currently Kamisato Ayato. Most Inazumans do not know it exists. It takes on matters that are awkward for the higher-ups to handle openly. Its best-known member is Sayu, a sleepy young ninja who is far better at hiding from work than doing it.

The name is written 終末番 and glossed by the wiki as "End Squad". The wiki reports its informal slogan, taken from a fortune-slip series, as a promise to send in the Shuumatsu against traitors and criminals alike. Inazuma's safety is its stated concern, but it is neither public nor peaceful.
