Structure: There is no public structure. The unit reports to the Kamisato Clan head, who is also the Yashiro Commissioner. Beneath him are ninja and support staff, with most identities classified.

Ayato says the unit reports directly to the head of the Kamisato Clan, and it passed to him when his father died. Orders are carried by staff such as Ogawa, who delivers orders and receives reports on ambush missions. Kazuaki appears in Thoma's hangout looking after the unit's stored belongings, and Kano Nana is assigned to keep an eye on Sayu. Koharu, a Kamisato household servant, is a ninja in training. Members receive a monthly salary; Sayu's is 200,000 Mora.

Authority beyond Ayato is informal. Thoma says nobody else may normally inquire into the unit's business, but Ayato agreed to let him do so once. The unit may also answer to others in exceptional circumstances. Ayaka is shown giving direction regarding Sayu. Retired figures such as Nakanishi and the ninken Taroumaru are named by the wiki as former members. Sayu's own sensei left the unit after she grew capable, and their present status is not stated.

Members: Sayu is the best-known ninja. Other named ninja include Hisashi, Gaumaru and the ninken Inu Shoushou. Most members are orphans raised from a young age by the unit.

Ayato says the unit takes in orphans and raises them, which he considers the surest way of securing loyalty. Sayu was raised there since childhood and is very loyal despite her laziness. Dogs also serve: Inu Shoushou is a ninken in ninja attire, paired with a human partner. Identities are classified so thoroughly that members who die on top-secret missions are not publicly commemorated.

Named active staff and ninja, per the wiki: Hisashi, Gaumaru, Kazuaki, Kano Nana, Ogawa, Koharu and an inspector named Sumire. Named former members: Furuta (Koharu's teacher), Nakanishi, the ninken Taroumaru and Ayato's late father. Ayaka and Thoma are not members but have some say. Treat the roster as incomplete.

Methods: Ninjutsu and stealth, escape and concealment, and combat when needed. Sayu explains in her hangout that the unit deals with matters that are "inconvenient" to the higher-ups, and that this sometimes includes ambushing people. Ayato describes the unit as his means of resolving situations he cannot involve himself in directly. Ninken serve as partners.

The wiki also records some trade skills. Members can make an elemental powder that is slightly toxic and can permanently blind if it gets in eyes. They can also build artificial corpses to fake a death, using raw meat, white-iron composite bones and Sea Ganoderma, dressed in the subject's clothing and burned so that only the clothes identify the body. One body takes about a day. A text attributed to the unit holds that a competent ninja never overlooks a mechanism in play. Ayato also uses the unit to deliver oddly chosen food to Thoma.

Goals: Keep Inazuma safe and deal with threats, traitors and criminals without publicity, in service of the Kamisato Clan and the Yashiro Commission. Ayato describes his own work as being for all of Inazuma.

Relations: Its closest tie is to the Kamisato Clan and Ayato, who commands it. Ayaka cares about Sayu's wellbeing and has arranged for Kano Nana to watch over her. Thoma deals with the unit with Ayato's consent. In Sayu's hangout, Ogawa is aghast when a client asks the unit to move against the Tenryou Commission.

In Sayu's hangout, a forged Yashiro Commission order was used to send a ninja to ambush the Traveler. Ogawa delivered it to Sayu, who normally ignores orders, and she carried it out efficiently. The scheme was then traced back to its instigators and the Traveler and Sayu captured the man behind it.

Reputation: Almost no one in Inazuma knows it exists, and fewer know that Sayu belongs to it. Those who do, mostly Kamisato Clan insiders and the Traveler, see it as loyal and efficient, if grim.

Secrets: The unit's existence, its members' identities and the fates of ninja killed on missions are all deliberately concealed. Inu Shoushou's owner was sent on a dangerous mission at sea and did not return; Kazuaki told Thoma and the Traveler as much.

History: Before Ayato, his father led the unit. Players first met it in Version 2.0 with Sayu's release, and its inner workings were shown in Sayu's and Thoma's hangout events (both tagged 2.2 on the wiki).

Sayu's profile says she was trained by a sensei who left quietly once she could defend herself; she later earned a Vision. Ayaka thinks Sayu's laziness comes from that loss. Inu Shoushou waited by the shore near Konda Village for his owner until Thoma and the Traveler brought the owner's old training kunai in Thoma's hangout.

Status as of 7.1: Active and still secret as of 7.1. No later story has changed its status in the sources checked.

577.content: Sayu is the unit's "resident ninja" and is famous for avoiding work. She sleeps and hides to grow taller and has mastered escape and concealment techniques accordingly. When missions appear, she vanishes, and by the time she is found a more suitable ninja has been assigned. Her colleagues know that she will not betray the unit's principles or shirk truly important jobs. Ayaka has arranged for Kano Nana to keep an eye on her. Her own entry carries her full details.

578.content:
A red Shiba ninken in ninja attire, with scarring near the left eye. He and his owner went on missions together until the owner left on a top-secret mission and never returned. Shoushou waited by the shore near Konda Village. Thoma and the Traveler eventually calmed him with the owner's old training kunai, which Kazuaki found in the warehouse. The unit agreed to cover his expenses.

Thoma uses the episode to explain the unit's lot: its ninja face dangerous work, and those who die on top-secret missions are not commemorated. The story is told in Thoma's hangout event.

579.content: In his voice-overs Ayato says it is a secret unit reporting directly to the Kamisato Clan head, and it came to him after his father passed. It lets him act where he cannot appear himself. He adds that most members are orphans raised in the unit from childhood, which makes their loyalty close to guaranteed. In another line he hints that the unit is not his only resource.

580.content:
Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau (also: Transport Bureau, Railway Transport Bureau, Chicota, Snezhnaya Imperial Railway Transport Bureau, Transportation Bureau): The Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau, usually called the Transport Bureau and sometimes Chicota, is the organisation in charge of Snezhnaya's railway system. Its staff run Central Station in Snezhnograd and the trains that cross the snowfields. The wiki also notes an uncommon translation as the Snezhnaya Imperial Railway Transport Bureau.

Canon treats it as both a transport service and a guardian of order. Weapon lore makes the head of the Chicota the "guardian of law and order" and gives each head an oath. The wiki page on the organisation is only a stub, so most of what is known comes from NPC dialogue and item text.

Structure: Named job titles in the Bureau are Conductor, Safety Officer and Ticket Agent. Conductors work on the platforms and aboard trains, safety officers stand watch at the station concourse and platforms, and ticket agents sell passage. Staff listed at Central Station include the conductors Aryna, Bazhenov, Kholodnaya, Kira and Rudov, the safety officers Gurevikov, Iliana and Sochikov, and the ticket agent Voskresensky. Other conductors such as Lukova and Baryatinsky are found aboard trains that can be summoned at several stations.

Bureau staff are also found outside the capital. Nekrasov, listed with the Bureau on the wiki, works in the ice-mining town of Svetloledovka, though no job title is given for him. Donya, a quest NPC of the Forested Snowfield quest, is also affiliated with it.

Leadership: No present-day head is named. Weapon lore describes the leader of the Chicota as the keeper of law and order within Snezhnaya, who must judge by the law that binds all living beings even when he feels sorrow and compassion as a person.

The text describes an oath that every head swears on taking the seat. Its lines speak of conquering humanity's weaknesses, forsaking useless emotions while keeping a frozen heart beating, using authority with humility, and keeping conscience and distance from cowardice and arrogance.

Goals: The Bureau's duties, as seen in its staff, are safe and orderly travel and the security of the stations. Bazhenov describes Snezhnograd Central Station as the lifeline of the city and the city as the heart of Snezhnaya, so even a tiny error is unacceptable. The oath adds a larger aim of sanctioning acts of terror and preserving peace along the long borders.

Methods: Staff manage crowds, ask passengers to board and leave in an orderly way, and guard the exit gates. Kira says that, under new regulations, staff are authorised to carry out random checks on anyone seen as a potential risk, including luggage inspection and questions about the traveller. The official map text for Central Station confirms that visitors pass inspections by Bureau staff before taking the elevator up to the centre of Snezhnograd.

Baryatinsky says a conductor must keep the train comfortable and, in extreme circumstances, take immediate corrective action against anything that threatens the train's proper operation. Gurevikov notes that the platforms are always especially crowded during boarding and disembarking. Lukova warns passengers that the Bureau will not pay compensation for falls while the train is moving, and avoids saying when it does.

History: Canon gives only a legend. In the Covenant of Frost and Snow text, a young human who was not yet head of the Bureau shared ideals with a pale fae. Both lamented injustice, and they were close at a time when humans and fae seldom agreed. They then split: the human chose order and new laws, the fae chose destruction as a path to rebirth. The human went on to lead the Chicota, and the fae became "the wise one", inciting those who longed for destruction in the name of rebirth. The conflict ended on a train near white birches. The fae fled with brigands' help but could not escape the Chicota's chief, who raised the bow and loosed on his friend. The bow came with the words that it was not given to Eprokin but to the guardian of order. That promise became the oath of every later head. The text does not name the two or date the events.

Relations: - **Snezhnaya's capital and government**: the wiki lists the Zapolyarny Palace as its affiliation, but this is not confirmed in the in-game text read.
- **Passengers and visitors**: staff are courteous but firm, and treat inspection as routine.
- **Fae**: the weapon legend frames the Chicota as having stood against a fae rebel, but gives no general policy toward fae.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Bureau remains active, with staff at Central Station and on trains. No Bureau-centred story was found in the sources checked for 7.0 and 7.1.

The Bureau is mainly a world-building organisation with ambient NPCs and the Covenant of Frost and Snow weapon lore. This file is intentionally short because canon about it is thin.

581.comment: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau: Chicota
581.content: Chicota is the alternate name of the Bureau used in the Covenant of Frost and Snow text. Its head is the guardian of law and order in Snezhnaya, and each head swears the oath that descends from the legend. The weapon was said to be given to such a guardian, not to Eprokin, an unexplained name.

582.comment: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau: Central Station staff
582.content: Central Station is the largest station in Snezhnaya and the entry to Snezhnograd. Visitors who leave the platforms pass inspection by Bureau staff before riding the elevator into the city. Bazhenov watches the exit gates, Gurevikov and Iliana keep platforms orderly as safety officers, Kira greets arriving passengers, and Voskresensky acts as a ticket agent.

583.comment: Snezhnaya Royal Railway Transport Bureau: Train conductors
583.content: Lukova can be met aboard a summonable train at Central Station, Svetloledovka, Sretomorozsk and Rankova Zorya. Baryatinsky serves on a train reachable from Central Station, Morepesok and Rankova Zorya. He emphasises passenger safety and quick corrective action if the train is threatened.

584.content:
Snezhnograd Veche (also: the Veche, Veche, Snezhnogradskoye Veche): The Snezhnograd Veche (Snezhnogradskoye Veche, "the Veche") is Snezhnaya's legislative assembly. It sits in the Veche State Hall in Snezhnograd and decides matters by majority vote in sessions chaired by a Speaker. The Tsaritsa founded it to take over the administration once the fae princes' rule ended. The Speaker is the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella, and the Fatui steer most of its decisions.

The word "veche" belongs to medieval Russian tradition, where it names a public assembly that debated and decided key matters. In Snezhnaya the body has kept the name and the procedure, but its members are mostly the powerful: Harbingers, nobles, merchants and officials, each speaking for an interest group.

Structure: Sessions are chaired by a Speaker, who opens the floor, manages motions and calls the final vote. Business follows a pattern: officials present reports, representatives speak in turn, a proposal is drafted or amended, then the members vote and the Speaker announces the result by percentage. Policies are set for a Veche "period" and stay in force until the next one. A new proposal follows "the usual procedure" and is raised as a motion at a later session. Visitors may attend from the audience seats if arranged in advance, but they cannot speak.

Seats are tied to groups rather than to a single electorate. Sandrone describes a room where each person represents an interest: Pantalone the financial sector, Tartaglia the Fatui soldiers, Sandrone her engineers and researchers, and Pulcinella "politics" itself. Some seats are reserved by family or class: Vesna's profile says only a few are reserved for House Strivozha, fewer even than those allotted to the merchant class. Councillors can hold titles such as Privy Councillor, and the State Hall also has a Privy Advisor. Specialist bodies report into it, as when the Energy Commission supplies regional consumption statistics.

Leadership: The Speaker is Pulcinella, the Fifth Fatui Harbinger, "the Rooster", who is also Mayor of Snezhnograd and of Glupov. Members call him "Lord Rooster" at sessions.

The first Speaker, also the first Mayor of Snezhnograd, was the human Ioanna Ivanovna N., a former Hexenzirkel witch who was appointed by the Tsaritsa and later became Pulcinella's teacher. Sandrone calls Pulcinella the linchpin of the Veche, because everything involves him and he knows how to mediate any issue, which she says is what the Tsaritsa values most in him. Councillor Euphrosiniya complains that he finds excuses to dismiss her heating proposals, while Councillor Golitsyn says his house stands with the Rooster.

Members: Known members and speakers in the 7.0 and 7.1 story:
- **Pulcinella**: Speaker.
- **Pantalone** ("the Regrator"): finance and the Northland Bank.
- **Tartaglia**: speaks for the Fatui soldiers. He privately sympathises with Stuzha's critics and keeps raising concerns, but says he has held back from casting a dissenting vote because the Tsaritsa would never let him get away with it.
- **Sandrone** ("the Marionette"): speaks for engineers and researchers.
- **Euphrosiniya Ignatyevna Trubetskaya** ("Euphie"): Privy Councillor and head of House Trubetskoy. She has put forward at least five proposals for heating in the town of Zolnyy.
- **Eteri Vsevolodovna Strivozha**: Vila councillor, descendant of Saint Strivozha, and nostalgic for the Belyi Tsar's age.
- **Andrei Dmitrievich Golitsyn**: second-rank noble, Active Privy Councillor.

Other voices at the 7.0 session include the industrialist Chugunov, owner of the Iskra plant, the finance scholar Arapov, the Energy Commission's Sharova, and Akvilina, who spoke on behalf of the Druzhna commander Vesna. The wiki says Harbingers are commonly entitled to take part in sessions.

Goals: Officially the Veche exists to handle the administrative issues that arose when the fae princes lost their power. In practice its work under Pulcinella is steering national policy, above all the long Project Stuzha energy-rationing program. In the story, members argue over the fairness of distribution, the interests of factories and soldiers' families, and whether the Fatui's central planning is sustainable.

Methods: Debate and pressure. Alyosha says opposition has been growing, but detractors end up caving to political pressure from the Rooster. The Fatui hold the advantage of already running Kristall shipments, and at the 7.0 session Tartaglia proposed that the Fatui collect regional data on that basis, with the Druzhna supervising. The Speaker backed drafting a proposal but questioned whether basing quotas on local data was safe in the long term. Opponents win only by flipping votes: the Rokot's Lelek did so through threats, coercion and bribery.

History: **Founding.** About 500 years ago the Belyi Tsar died in the Cataclysm and Anastasya succeeded as the Cryo Archon. A Brief History of the Pale Starborn records that in the sixth year of the 799th Cycle she set up the Snezhnograd Veche to handle the administrative issues caused by the princes' absence, with the human Ioanna Ivanovna as its first chairperson. The next year she issued the Imperial Order Reformation Edict, after which many princely fae gave up their titles and left.

**Project Stuzha.** The Veche is the body that passes Project Stuzha, the energy reforms that limit public consumption so power can be redirected to the Armory Palace. The project was meant to last about six months but has been extended repeatedly, each time by majority vote.

Relations: - **The Tsaritsa**: founder and ultimate authority. Members speak of acting in her name.
- **The Fatui**: dominant. Harbingers sit in the Veche, and Tartaglia presses the case of Fatui soldiers and their families.
- **Rokot**: an anonymous civilian society that opposed Project Stuzha through evidence, leaks and, in Lelek's case, pressure on voters.
- **Druzhna**: the Tsaritsa's guard is represented in debates, as when Akvilina spoke for Commander Vesna.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Veche continues to meet under Speaker Pulcinella. Project Stuzha was kept going in 7.0, then paused.

After Ronova lost her Authority in 7.1 the wiki says Project Stuzha resumes, though no vote has been shown. No new Veche story was found in the 6.x Nod-Krai content or in 7.1 beyond this context, and no change of Speaker is known.

585.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: The Speaker and the Rooster
585.content: At Veche sessions the Fatui Harbinger Pulcinella is addressed as "The Rooster" or "Lord Rooster". As Speaker he reports statistics, calls "Order", opens and closes the floor, supports the drafting of proposals, and announces votes. He ends sessions with a standard line about debating "only for the greater glory and solidarity of our nation".

586.content: The Veche's first chairperson was a human named Ioanna Ivanovna N., codename "J". She was a member of the Hexenzirkel with no magic or combat training, left the witches after marrying, and was appointed by the Tsaritsa as the first Mayor of Snezhnograd and Speaker. She mentored Pulcinella, and Golitsyn credits her grace for his house's standing. She died centuries ago, and in the Hexenzirkel story her line of followers continues.

587.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: Project Stuzha and the Veche vote
587.content:
Project Stuzha is a set of energy reforms passed by the Veche that cut household and factory use of Kresnik Kristall so that energy can be sent to the Armory Palace. It was intended to last about six months but was extended repeatedly by majority vote, and the 7.0 vote kept it with 61%. Pierro later reveals it served Project Mistilteinn, the Tsaritsa's weapon against the Heavenly Principles using Stellar Linchpins.

Supporters call it a resource-distribution framework, not the cause of shortages. Critics point to cold towns, shortfalls for soldiers' families and the lack of visible benefit. The project was suspended when Ronova's Curse of Death stopped the research and, per the wiki, resumes after 7.1's revocation of her Authority.

588.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: Rokot and Lelek in the Veche
588.content: The Rokot is an anonymous society that works for ordinary people and opposed Project Stuzha. Its codenamed members use mostly peaceful methods, such as publishing evidence of corruption. The codename Lelek, held by Odette, used threats, coercion and bribery to flip Veche votes, turning Chugunov and narrowing the margin to 61%. In Mistilteinn the Rokot withdrew the codename and suspended its holder.

589.comment: Snezhnograd Veche: Snezhnograd Veche State Hall
589.content: The Snezhnograd Veche State Hall is where the Veche holds its regular meetings. Its map description says citizen representatives from various groups deliberate on newly issued laws, in a tradition kept from Snezhnaya's early days, and that it is presided over by "The Rooster". In the hall are the councillors Eteri and Euphrosiniya and the Privy Advisor Golitsyn.

590.content:
Spantamad (also: Spantamad Darshan, School of Elementalism, the Spantamad school): Spantamad is one of the six Darshans of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is elementalism, the study of the elements and the elemental reactions and changes that follow from them, with related work in Ley Line studies and alchemy. Its school colour is red. Because Ley Line research needs fieldwork, it has the most Driyosh, the Akademiya's traveling scholars. Lisa of the Knights of Favonius and Cyno both studied here.

Its crest shows a peacock with seven feathers above a tree, which the wiki reads as the seven elements and the Ley Lines of the Irminsul. The Darshan's name comes from the Zoroastrian goddess Spenta Armaiti, who is associated with the earth. Spantamad has also had the highest percentage of Interdarshan Championship winners.

Structure: Spantamad is led by a sage, one of the Six Great Sages, and staffed by professors, researchers and students. A large share of its scholars are Driyosh: they travel in the field to study Ley Lines. Its disciplines include alchemy, elemental science and Ley Line studies.

Elective courses in other Darshans are open to students in general. Spantamad had a stream of mechanical-life research until it was banned.

Leadership: Alkindi is the current Spantamad sage. Cyrus, a retired professor, is a former sage.

Alkindi was once Cyrus's classmate and rival. He threw himself into many research fields for years before becoming sage, and his receding hairline is blamed on academic stress. He is tall, with grey hair and round blue goggles, and wears a crimson sherwani. In As All Falls to Emptiness (Chapter III) he helped the Traveler by investigating Ley Line anomalies.

Cyrus was an eminent sage, and a line of his, "Change is the only constant", appears on Bimarstan's Proverb Column. His students included Lisa, Cyno and Gafoor. When Nefer arrived at the Akademiya as a young girl, Azar's policy barred her from the entrance exam as one of the desert-folk, and Cyrus complained that such students were not treated fairly. Later, as a sage, he wrote a formal letter of protest. That letter ended up among unclaimed mail in the House of Daena, where an older Nefer found it.

Members: - **Alkindi**: the current sage.
- **Cyrus**: a retired professor and former sage who raised Cyno as a foster son.
- **Lisa**: a former student who graduated in two years, got disillusioned with the Akademiya and joined the Knights of Favonius.
- **Cyno**: a former student of Cyrus who became General Mahamatra.
- **Hosseini**: a Driyosh from Vimara Village, a Spantamad researcher on Ley Lines who is under 30 but looks middle-aged from thesis stress. He appears in Version 2.2's event quests.
- **Abattouy**: a researcher who studied mechanical lifeforms and was expelled for continuing; he later built Karkata.

Gafoor is a professor who ran a Ley Line research project in the Second Blooming event (limited-time) and was Lisa's classmate under Cyrus. Hajanad is a student alchemist who appears in event content. Kimiya, Zinat and others are minor Spantamad scholars who appear in events and open-world commissions.

Goals: Spantamad researchers treat the Seven Great Elements as the essence of all matter and life. They aim to understand elemental reactions, how Ley Lines behave and what alchemy can produce, and to apply that knowledge. Hosseini's own goals show the school's practical side: he wants to use ancient devices such as the Energy Amplifier and Pursina's Spikes, and regrets that the Spikes lie unused in the Akademiya's warehouses.

Methods: Sitt sums up the school as conducting reaction experiments when not travelling in the field. Driyosh scholars go out to the Ley Lines, collect data and run commissions. Alchemists brew elixirs and test reactions in labs. In the Glittering Elixirs web event (limited-time), the potions and elixirs shown could be taught at Spantamad. Hosseini's thesis work is an example: he went to collect a perfectly preserved Irminsul Fruit, which burst into fragments in a monster ambush, and the Traveler helped recover them and take them to a Domain with an Energy Amplifier to gather data.

History: Spantamad is one of the Six Great Schools set up with the Akademiya under Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. It was prominent in mechanical-life research until overzealous researchers began to perform unregulated vivisections and other cruel experiments on animals, after which the Akademiya banned the field; students caught researching it risk expulsion. Abattouy is a case in point: he kept working on machines after his expulsion.

Relations: - **Other Darshans**: Spantamad is one of six, alongside Amurta, Rtawahist, Haravatat, Vahumana and Kshahrewar. Rtawahist, its sibling in astronomy, also had its sage replaced after Azar's fall.
- **The Knights of Favonius**: Lisa carries her Spantamad training to Mondstadt and works as the order's librarian.
- **The Fatui and Sumeru politics**: nothing in the sources read ties the Darshan as a whole to the Fatui plot, though Cyno, once its student, played a key role in Chapter III.

- **Cyrus and Cyno**: Cyno was raised as Cyrus's foster son and followed him into the Akademiya.
- **Nefer**: she was assigned to Vahumana after being barred from the entrance exam, and Cyrus protested the policy on behalf of such students.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Spantamad is led by Alkindi. No new Spantamad story was found for 6.x-7.1.

Ley Line studies and alchemy continue in the Akademiya. Scholars such as Hosseini and Gafoor remain minor figures in events.

591.content: Alkindi is the current sage of Spantamad and a former classmate and rival of Cyrus. He is tall, with medium-length grey hair that flares at the sides, round blue goggles and a crimson sherwani. His receding hairline is blamed on academic stress. In Chapter III's As All Falls to Emptiness he helped the Traveler by studying Ley Line anomalies.

592.content: Cyrus is a retired Akademiya professor and former Spantamad sage. Lisa and Cyno were his students, and he raised Cyno as his foster son. His line "Change is the only constant" is on Bimarstan's Proverb Column. He once nearly died exploring the Great Red Sand and was saved by the Temple of Silence. He also protested the rule that kept desert-born students out of the entrance exam, and his formal protest letter ended up unclaimed in the House of Daena.

593.content: Hosseini is a Driyosh in Spantamad from Vimara Village who appears in event quests such as Energy Amplifier. His hair has greyed from the stress of getting papers approved. For his thesis he went to collect a preserved Irminsul Fruit found by Liyue's Adventurers' Guild. Treasure Hoarders ambushed him and the fruit burst into fragments, so the Traveler helped recover them. He admires inventor-researchers such as Pursina, who made Pursina's Spikes, and Ayesha, who made a Chaos Prospector.

594.content: Abattouy is a former Spantamad researcher who enrolled to study mechanical lifeforms, which the Akademiya banned. After his expulsion he carried on in secret, building a machine called Karkata that resembled a Ruin Defender and had the mindset of a child. Roughly two years before the start of the game he built a laboratory in a secluded area. He was Tighnari's junior at the Akademiya and appears in flashbacks in The Unanswerable Problems. He is also credited with the eight Energy Extraction Devices of The Foolish Fatuus.

595.content: Driyosh are the Akademiya's traveling scholars. Spantamad has the most of them because Ley Line research needs fieldwork. Their commissions often reach the Adventurers' Guild, which is how the Traveler meets scholars such as Hosseini.

596.content: The Interdarshan Championship is a competition among the Darshans in which Spantamad has had the highest percentage of champions. Huvishka lists Cyrus, Ruzicka, Lisa and Cyno as examples of its talent. The championship later cut the events in which people fought to the death. Twenty years ago it was the setting for Kaveh's father's entry for the Diadem of Knowledge.

597.content:
Spina di Rosula (also: Spina, the Spina, Thorny Rose Association): The Spina di Rosula is a Fontainian organisation that helps ordinary people and takes on the problems the Gardes cannot or will not handle. Callas founded it, and his daughter Navia is now its President and "Boss". Its members work from Fleuve Cendre, the undercity beneath the Court of Fontaine, and from Poisson. Officially it describes itself as law-abiding and citizen-focused, and it cooperates with the authorities where needed. Navia's own description is "a business partner" that helps with any problem, using the velvet glove or the iron fist as the case demands.

The Spina also runs a quieter, harder side. It has enforcers for the dirty work, and it keeps order in Fleuve Cendre better than the Court of Fontaine ever tried to. Core businesses sustain the Spina, while much of Navia's problem-solving brings little profit, and its help can come with conditions. Navia's profile notes that people who adopt her own description of the Spina will find it easier to make friends with her.

Structure: The Spina has a single President. Navia lists her titles as president, leader, commander-in-chief, executive director and Boss, and members simply say "Boss". Below her are advisors and specialists rather than a rigid rank ladder. Florent is Senior Advisor and Yvette is Technical Advisor. Areta is the organisation's physician, Archenoul a diver on its payroll, and Tetreaux a bartender in Fleuve Cendre. Faustier, Rege and others do manual and construction labour, Hinterman is a fisherman, and Sonny and Luca are the enforcers.

The Spina deliberately recruits from people the surface world has given up on. Faustier was invited to join after serving time in the Fortress of Meropide for petty theft. Areta, who grew up poor, had her medical studies at the Akademiya paid for by the Spina on the condition that she come back and work as a salaried doctor in Fleuve Cendre, and she says she thought it a fair deal. Yvette quit the Fontaine Research Institute because she could not work with people at her short temper, and she now says it does not matter whether a Spina member is eight or eighty, so long as they have ability. A black bowler hat is commonly worn by members. In-game text says the hat sits between a luxury good and an accessory, and that since Callas led, an unwritten rule has held that a measured display of wealth can itself be a warning to rivals. The emblem of the Spina, which Navia says is shaped like a heart, was designed by her mother Clementine.

Leadership: Navia is the second President. She took the post from her father Callas, who founded the Spina, after his death. She is cheerful, tireless and theatrical, and her own people treat her as the one to bring problems to.

Navia says plainly that she will not become the same sort of person as her father, though some veterans think she is becoming more like him. She says the Spina has changed a lot since Callas's day and she intends to be "the president for the Spina of today". Unlike Callas, she says she is willing to hear opinions. In the Romeuf case she handed her former members over to the law instead of settling it privately.

Callas ran the Spina as a stubborn, closed-off man. He was a respected figure in Fontainian society, so well regarded that Neuvillette and Clorinde both spoke highly of him, yet he refused the honorary title the Palais Mermonia sought to grant him after the aquabus lines were completed (the Callas wiki page calls it the title of Baron). Navia's guess, which she never confirmed with him, is that he feared a title would set the Spina above the common folk it worked with. He taught her business, negotiation and weapons, took her to the negotiating table, and appeared to be grooming her as his successor, but he never spoke of his own feelings or of how her mother died.

Members: Current members named in canon include Florent (Senior Advisor), Yvette (Technical Advisor), Areta (physician), Archenoul (diver), Tetreaux (bartender), Faustier and Rege (manual and construction labour), Hinterman (fisherman) and Sonny and Luca (enforcers). Consigliere is the organisation's tortoise confidant, and Bizerte leads its Simulanka branch. Former members include the founder Callas and his wife Clementine, who are dead; Melus and Silver, who were dissolved in the flood; Colter, who was dismissed and detained; Romeuf, who left and is imprisoned; and Virgil, who was killed.

Sonny, called "White Glove", and Luca, called "The Fisherman", are the enforcers. Navia herself says that someone who is not in the mood to sit and talk will be handled by "White Glove". They are named after characters from a well-known crime film. The two meet the Traveler after Virgil, a rogue member who led the Traveler into a trap while hunting for treasure, is dealt with. Sonny's and Luca's later fish gift to the Traveler is a pointed reference to that scene.

Goals: The Spina exists to help the people of Fontaine, above all the poor and the forgotten, and to investigate matters that the Gardes would not or cannot. Its public statement is that it is a citizen-oriented society involving many walks of life, focused on hard problems among the common folk, and cooperative with the Fontainian authorities. Navia puts it more briefly: the work is "a little bit of everything", but the focus is always on solving other people's problems. Under Navia, the Spina also aims to rebuild Poisson, keep Fleuve Cendre safe and keep faith with the people who died for it.

Navia sees two kinds of trouble, the solvable and the unsolvable, and the Spina is aimed at the first kind. She takes on small, unprofitable cases such as separated lovers or a middle-aged breadwinner left unable to work by an accident, because she believes in "a stitch in time saving nine" and that dealing with them early saves someone from being hauled up onstage at the opera house.

Methods: The Spina prefers to settle matters peacefully, through mediation, negotiation and favours, but it does not rule out force. In Fleuve Cendre it mediates conflicts, manages relations with the Court of Fontaine and keeps the peace. Residents say that under the Spina it is much harder to find illegal funding and that anyone who starts an armed fight may be "sent away to start a new life in the ocean". It also supports its people with supplies, household help, jobs and sponsored study. Tetreaux says that, in theory, nothing exists that can only be solved by force, and that the Spina will resolve a problem with minimal harm.

Its aid is not pure charity. Areta's sponsorship came with a return-to-work condition, and Navia's profile contrasts her unprofitable problem-solving with the core businesses that sustain the Spina. For large jobs, such as building the aquabus or running the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland, it works with the Court of Fontaine, the Fontaine Research Institute and private partners. Navia uses a network of informants and agents, and she sometimes deploys Spina people as escorts, as she did for the courier Kirara when Kirara was harassed.

History: Callas founded the Spina and led it as first President. A dispute over funding the aquabus split the organisation, and after Callas died in a duel three years before the Fontaine Archon Quest, his daughter Navia took over.

**Founding and the aquabus dispute.** Callas founded the Spina and was its first President. His wife Clementine was its mediator in disputes between members. Callas decided to sponsor the aquabus system in partnership with the Court of Fontaine and the Fontaine Research Institute, hoping it would improve the relationship between the rest of Fontaine and Poisson and pay off in the long run. Romeuf, a senior member, thought the money should go into Poisson itself. When Clementine sided with Callas, Romeuf's faction decided that her pregnancy had made her an unfair mediator and left, with a large share of the membership, on extremely bad terms. They continued to despise the family, including Navia. After Clementine died, Callas went on with the construction to honour her wish, and the lines are named after Callas, Clementine and Navia.

**Callas's death.** Three years before the Fontaine Archon Quest, Callas banned Sinthe, the popular drink that Marcel secretly made from Primordial Seawater, and turned his informant Jacques against the producers. Jacques was killed and Callas was blamed. Rather than stand trial, Callas chose a duel against the Champion Duelist Clorinde and refused to yield. His benefactors withdrew and the public called him "Callas the Unfaithful". Navia, with Melus and Silver as bodyguards, took over as President, and the strain between her and Clorinde lasted for years.

Relations: - **Gardes and the Court of Fontaine**: the Spina handles what the Gardes cannot, and it manages relations with the Court on behalf of Fleuve Cendre. The Court has never governed the undercity and left it to the Spina. The Maison Gardiennage arrests Spina rebels when the Spina calls on them.
- **Clorinde**: Navia's childhood friend, whom she could not forgive after Callas's death. They are now close, and Clorinde often accompanies her.
- **Neuvillette**: respected Callas and later rescued Navia from the Primordial Seawater.
- **The Fatui**: Arlecchino's group helped in the 4.x flood. The Spina accepted the aid but did not lower its guard.
- **Confrerie of Cabriere**: Marcel's organisation was the source of Sinthe and later of the plot against Navia. It no longer exists.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Spina di Rosula is active under President Navia, with Florent as Senior Advisor and Poisson's reconstruction under way.

Navia remains President and has represented the Spina outside Fontaine, as at the Nasha Town trade expo. Colter has been dismissed, awaiting the end of his sentence and a welcome back. Romeuf and his followers are in prison. The Simulanka branch exists only in an event story. No Spina-specific story developments were found for 7.0-7.1.

598.comment: Spina di Rosula: Fleuve Cendre base
598.content: The Spina's seat is in Fleuve Cendre, the settlement in the sewers beneath the Court of Fontaine. For centuries it was a gray legal area where the Court had no jurisdiction, once ruled by gangs and then by a protection racket under the outlaw Eduardo Baker. Today the Spina is its de facto governing body, and many members also live there. Residents include ex-convicts, people who have served time in the Fortress of Meropide, the poor and orphans. The air is damp, there is little sunlight and children are often left to themselves, but the Spina supplies food, medicine and help with household affairs. Tetreaux tends the bar. During the Fontaine Archon Quests the Traveler stays at the base between cases.

599.comment: Spina di Rosula: Aquabus dispute and the split
599.content: The aquabus system was proposed by Callas as a joint venture with the Court of Fontaine and the Fontaine Research Institute. Romeuf, who thought the money should go into Poisson, left with a large number of Spina members when Clementine backed her husband. Clementine later died after Navia's birth, and Callas went on with the project. The three lines carry the names of Callas, Clementine and Navia. The Callas Line was later destroyed in an explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute, and after Romeuf's plot Navia decided to start rebuilding it.

600.comment: Spina di Rosula: Romeuf and the plot against Poisson
600.content: Romeuf was a Spina member who left over the aquabus funds and whose followers saw Navia as no different from her father. Short on Mora, he plotted to collapse the Clementine Line and let the rubble destroy Poisson. He recruited Colter, a former Spina member who had just finished a sentence in the Fortress of Meropide and who blamed Navia for the death of his old colleague Melus. Colter failed to kill her at first because the Traveler was with her, and he then warned Romeuf that Florent was going to check on the faction. The Traveler and Navia stopped most of the damage. The Maison Gardiennage arrested Romeuf and his followers, and Navia refused to treat them gently because they had endangered innocents. She dismissed Colter but promised to take him back when he is free.

601.comment: Spina di Rosula: Sonny and Luca
601.content: Sonny, called "White Glove", and Luca, called "The Fisherman", are the Spina's enforcers. Sonny does the talking in a courtly, theatrical manner and Luca speaks very little. Navia says anyone who is not in the mood to talk will be dealt with by White Glove. They help the Traveler during the Aqueous Tidemarks and A Fontainian Message quests, and they hunt down Virgil, a rogue member who dealt in Sinthe. They are later found beside Consigliere in Fleuve Cendre.

602.comment: Spina di Rosula: Melus and Silver
602.content: Melus, the elder, and Silver, the younger, were Navia's two attendants and bodyguards after Callas's death. Melus managed her supplies, memos and daily logistics. When Primordial Seawater flooded Poisson they were dissolved while trying to save others. Their consciousnesses were forged into Oceanids, which helped shield Navia from the other victims who wanted to absorb her, long enough for Neuvillette to rescue her. They are the reason Colter blamed Navia.

key: Spina di Rosula Uniform Gift Box
603.comment: Spina di Rosula: Spina di Rosula uniform and hat
603.content: Members wear a black bowler hat. In-game text says it sits between a luxury and an accessory, and that since Callas's time a careful display of wealth has acted as a quiet warning to rivals (item text from the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event, 6.7). During Lost and Inherited, Navia collected a Spina uniform from Ludivine's shop as a promise for Adele, a child who admired the organisation after her father's name was cleared. It was too large for her for now.

604.content:
Sumeru Akademiya (also: Akademiya of Sumeru, Six Darshans): The Sumeru Akademiya is both Sumeru's government and the most prestigious academy in Teyvat. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata founded it, and its main building, the Akademiya, sits on the Divine Tree above Sumeru City. Its scholars are divided into six Darshans (schools), each led by a Sage, and one Sage serves as Grand Sage. It runs Sumeru's day-to-day affairs, from trade and ports to hospitals and law. The old sages under Grand Sage Azar confined the Dendro Archon and plotted with the Fatui to make a new god. Since their fall, the Akademiya has served Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), and its current Grand Sage is Naphis.

It accepts students of any age and from any nation, provided they pass its hard entrance exams. Its scholars travel all over Teyvat to research, and in Mondstadt, Liyue or Inazuma a travelling Sumeru scholar fretting over a thesis is a familiar sight.

Structure: The six Darshans began as the Six Great Schools that Rukkhadevata founded with the Akademiya, and today the two names mean almost the same thing. Each has a specialty and a uniform colour:
- **Amurta**: biology, ecology and medicine (green). The oldest and largest Darshan.
- **Rtawahist**: illuminationism, meaning the stars, astronomy and astrology (blue).
- **Spantamad**: elementalism, ley lines and alchemy (red).
- **Haravatat**: semiotics, languages and ancient scripts (black).
- **Vahumana**: aetiology, history and the social sciences (yellow).
- **Kshahrewar**: technology and architecture (white).

Each Darshan is led by one of the Six Great Sages, and the central leader among them is the Grand Sage. The Grand Sage's office is above the House of Daena. Alongside the schools are administrative bodies: the **Mahamata** (civil officials, including the Scribe), the **Matra** (disciplinary officers under the General Mahamatra), the **Navbed** (trade and taxes), the **Vizier** (the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street) and an office called the **Temple of Silence**, which handles information unfit for the public.

Academic rank depends on progress, not age. Students address one another as seniors and juniors by who graduated first. That is why Tighnari is senior to the older Abattouy. A **Driyosh** is a travelling scholar on leave to gather material, and passing one thesis is enough to graduate. A **Dastur** has passed two theses and may stay and research at the Akademiya. A **Herbad** is a high-ranking researcher in a leadership role. Thesis defences are notoriously hard. Graduating after thirty is common, there seems to be a limit on how long a student may stay without graduating, and some students never leave the Akademiya until they finish. Students may take electives outside their own Darshan; there is even a swimming elective.

Leadership: Grand Sage Naphis, the Amurta Sage, is a man of integrity with a legendary temper. He was Tighnari's teacher. Lesser Lord Kusanali now guides the Akademiya directly.

The current sages were introduced together in 6.6: Naphis (Amurta, Grand Sage), Baladhuri (Vahumana), Shakir (Rtawahist), Alkindi (Spantamad), Rushd (Haravatat) and Firnas (Kshahrewar). Naphis and Baladhuri kept their seats because they had opposed Azar's conspiracy, and the other four replaced sages who were removed.

- **Baladhuri** is a kind, gentle historian who is proud of his beard. Tighnari calls him "Uncle Baladhuri".
- **Shakir** looks stern but is soft-spoken. He tracks his tasks on a whiteboard and was once Layla's master.
- **Alkindi** was Cyrus' classmate and rival, and he tried many fields before becoming Spantamad's Sage.
- **Rushd** is the youngest of the current sages. He was a junior of Khajeh, the disgraced former Haravatat Sage, and is still targeted inside his Darshan because of an old dispute with Khajeh.
- **Firnas** is the Kshahrewar Sage. Weapon lore about an older "great master Firnas" stresses that he was not the current lecturer.

Goals: In principle the Akademiya exists to pursue and spread wisdom and to help the God of Wisdom govern Sumeru. Its three virtues, Admonition, Ingenuity and Praxis, are the "branches", "leaf-veins" and "roots" of the nation of wisdom. Its six cardinal sins mark the knowledge it considers too dangerous to pursue. Under Azar, these ideals hardened into control: the sages wanted to monopolise knowledge, restore Irminsul and replace a god they found disappointing.

Methods: The Akademiya governs mainly through the **Akasha System**. Rukkhadevata created it and the Akademiya expanded it after her death. It delivered knowledge to anyone wearing an Akasha Terminal, filtered by clearance, and it carried decrees and announcements. New material entered it on Jnagarbha Day through the Grand Sage's console. Unknown to most people, it drew its computing power from users' dreams. After the cataclysm the sages slowly stigmatised dreaming so that no one would notice. Leaked Knowledge Capsules ("Canned Knowledge") are banned, and the Matra pursue smugglers. The Akasha was shut down after Chapter III.

Rules are built on the six sins, and the sages have kept adding and amending them over the centuries. Research touching those sins can mean expulsion or imprisonment. Research on mechanical life forms, once popular in Spantamad, was banned after researchers began cruel, unregulated experiments on animals. The Matra visit offenders in person and are widely feared. The Mahamata relay decrees and oversee trade, ports and public healthcare. Each year the Pir Kavikavus Prize goes to a promising scholar under forty. Peace in Sumeru City is kept not by an army but by the Corps of Thirty, an Eremite mercenary brigade on permanent contract to the sages.

History: **Founding.** With her followers, who later founded Amurta, Rukkhadevata grew the rainforest. She founded the Akademiya and its Six Great Schools, and its sages helped her govern. Other Darshans have come and gone, but only the six original schools lasted. One of the lost Darshans, Nagarjuna's school, left for the desert during the cataclysm and became the Order of Skeptics, whom the Akademiya called the "Nagarjunites".

**After the cataclysm.** About 500 years ago, forbidden knowledge contaminated Irminsul and Rukkhadevata, who vanished and left a newborn successor. The sages distrusted the child-like Lesser Lord Kusanali and kept her confined in the Sanctuary of Surasthana for 500 years. About 400 years ago, the real Temple of Silence left for the desert in disgust at the sages' corruption, and the sages set up an empty office of the same name to hide its departure. In the same era the student Zandik was expelled for unauthorised and unethical research. He later became the Harbinger Dottore.

**Chapter III (3.0-3.2).** Dottore returned and offered to build the sages a new God of Wisdom from Scaramouche. Azar and three other sages agreed, and they imprisoned Naphis and Baladhuri for objecting. The conspirators harvested divine knowledge from scholars driven mad, ran a dream samsara through the Akasha during the Sabzeruz Festival, spread rumours of King Deshret's revival, and banned public art. Cyno resigned as General Mahamatra after Azar refused to let him investigate. The Traveler, Nahida, Alhaitham, Cyno, Tighnari, Nilou, Dehya and their allies freed Nahida and stopped the plot. Nahida revoked the sages' access to the Akasha. Azar and his three accomplices were removed from office and sent to the Avidya Forest, supposedly repentant, to "cultivate wisdom" for the rest of their lives.

Members: Notable current and former members:
- **Alhaitham** (Haravatat): the Scribe, of the Mahamata, and briefly Acting Grand Sage.
- **Cyno**: General Mahamatra, head of the Matra.
- **Kaveh**: Kshahrewar alumnus and architect.
- **Tighnari** (Amurta): Naphis' former student, who left the city's politics to become a Forest Watcher.
- **Layla** (Rtawahist): an overworked student.
- **Faruzan** (Haravatat): a researcher who was trapped in ruins for a century.
- **Nefer** (Vahumana): one of the few desert-born students.
- **Lisa** (Spantamad): its best student in 200 years, who graduated in two years and then left in disillusionment.

Collei plans to enrol once her studies are done. The Wanderer works quietly for Nahida and the Akademiya.

Relations: - **Lesser Lord Kusanali**: once the sages' prisoner, now their acknowledged god. She chose mercy for Azar's faction.
- **Temple of Silence**: since Oathkeeper (4.6) the real Temple, led by Sethos, has begun working with the Akademiya again and will share its knowledge with those he and Kusanali deem worthy. In 6.6 the scholars searched its records.
- **Eremites and desertfolk**: the Corps of Thirty serves the sages, but relations with the desert have long been prickly. Desertfolk students were treated with prejudice under Azar, and Vahumana has grown more popular since his exile.
- **Fatui**: Dottore's partner in the Chapter III conspiracy. After 6.6, Pulcinella sent apologies and relief supplies, and the Akademiya remains wary.
- **Order of Skeptics**: a former Darshan that broke away long ago. Many in the rainforest think it a myth.

Reputation: The Akademiya's scorn for art spread through Sumeru. Plays had to be approved, books were not openly sold, and practicality came to be valued over beauty in everything from dance to architecture. Even after the sages fell, talking about art is still the quickest way to kill a conversation. People grumble that the Mahamata are inefficient and that students may be assigned to them against their will. Abroad, people respect its learning but also know how gruelling its degrees are. Lisa will not speak well of it, having seen scholars driven mad in the forests and sages sitting idle on councils.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Akademiya is led by Grand Sage Naphis and five other sages, under Nahida's guidance. After the 6.6 Irminsul crisis, people have returned to Sumeru City and are rebuilding.

Irminsul has burned and Aaru now stores the world's information. Cyno remains General Mahamatra and Alhaitham remains Scribe. No new Akademiya story developments were found for 6.7-7.1.

605.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Six cardinal sins and three virtues
605.content: In the Akademiya's early days, researchers reshaped terrain, controlled the weather and reached for the stars and for life and death. To protect them from their own knowledge, six sins were declared to be the root of all crimes: interfering with human evolution; tampering with life and death; delving beyond the universe; investigating the origin of words; revering gods without acts of devotion; and attempting the forbidden and fearing none. Every later rule builds on them, and Cyno judges by them, "even sages". Over time most people forgot them. In 3.4, Alhaitham noted that Siraj's Hive project counted as research on human evolution. The three virtues, Admonition, Ingenuity and Praxis, are the qualities the Akademiya praises, and the Sumeru talent books are named after them.

606.content: Driyosh are students on leave to gather research material; they apply through an eligibility review with interviews. Passing one thesis graduates a student. A Dastur has passed two and may research at the Akademiya instead of travelling. A Herbad is a senior researcher in a leadership role. Above them are the Six Great Sages and the Grand Sage. Seniority depends on progress, not age. Thesis review panels are feared, and some students pile up rejected manuscripts.

607.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Mahamata, Matra and the Scribe
607.content: The Mahamata are Akademiya alumni sent across Sumeru to oversee information, enforce decrees and run public services such as trade and the Bimarstan hospital. The Scribe, Alhaitham's post, belongs to the Mahamata. The Matra are disciplinary officers who punish serious academic offences such as plagiarism and misused funds, and who inspect for Canned Knowledge and smuggled books. They are led by General Mahamatra Cyno, whom some scholars snipe at for not being a renowned researcher. The Navbed manages trade, ports and taxes, and the Vizier oversees the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street.

608.content: Grand Sage Azar and three other sages accepted Dottore's offer to build a new God of Wisdom from Scaramouche. They locked up Naphis and Baladhuri, who objected, and forged letters in Naphis' name to recruit Tighnari. Khajeh, the Haravatat Sage, went to Gandharva Ville to press Tighnari in person. The sages harvested energy through an Akasha dream samsara, opened Akasha Terminals to visitors, threatened Nilou and banned public performances. They also refused Cyno's investigation, and he resigned. After Kusanali was freed, Cyno arrested Azar and made him repent before her. Azar and his accomplices were removed and sent to the Avidya Forest. Cyno thought the punishment too light, but he respected his god's decision.

609.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Acting Grand Sage Alhaitham
609.content: After Azar's fall, the officials choosing his replacement nominated Alhaitham to be Grand Sage and help Kusanali run the Akademiya. He refused, saying he did not want to lead or even be a sage, but he agreed to act as Grand Sage in the meantime. During that time he dealt with Siraj's collective-consciousness "Hive" (Pride and Prejudice, 3.4). He then resigned so the temporary post would not become permanent, and went back to being Scribe, reportedly on the same salary.

610.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: Corps of Thirty and the Akademiya
610.content: The Corps of Thirty is the oldest Eremite brigade and is named after the thirty mercenaries the sages first hired. It keeps the peace in Sumeru City under a permanent contract and coordinates the other mercenary brigades. Its Parchamdar is Rukh Shah, and Effendi is the Akademiya's liaison. In 6.6 a member, Qanafiya, was exposed as a Fatui mole paid in ancient gold coins and was caught by Cyno.

611.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: The Akademiya's Temple of Silence
611.content: Inside the Akademiya, the Temple of Silence is an office for keeping and disposing of information unfit for the public. Rumour holds that it detains people. About 400 years ago, however, the real Temple of Silence, keepers of King Deshret-era knowledge founded by Hermanubis' followers, left the rainforest because of the sages' corruption and settled near Thamud Oasis. The sages kept an empty office with the same name to hide this, and Alhaitham calls it obsolete. Since Oathkeeper (4.6), the real Temple under Sethos has started cooperating with the Akademiya again.

612.content: The House of Daena is the Akademiya's library at the heart of the main building. Some books are restricted to senior researchers, and borrowers may annotate books. A Grand Conservator runs it, and the Akademiya has been seeking a new one. The Bimarstan is a free public hospital staffed by Amurta researchers and students. Pardis Dhyai is Amurta's botanical research centre, and Tighnari keeps close ties with it.

613.comment: Sumeru Akademiya: The six sages of 6.6
613.content: When the Irminsul crisis began, Naphis brought the other five sages to Caravan Ribat and introduced them to the Traveler. Alkindi joined Cyrus and Cyno in dissecting the abnormal Ley Line Blossoms. Baladhuri and Firnas helped hold Aaru Village against the Jinn. The sages and scholars searched the Temple of Silence records for a substitute power source for the Akasha. Naphis also bargained with the Seven Pillars of Aaru, asking for their help in return for their freedom, and sent scholars to work on Aaru's mainframe. After the crisis, Naphis delivered Pulcinella's letter to Nahida and asked her to join the victory feasts.

key: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
614.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
614.content:
Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency (also: Secure Transport Agency, Sword and Strongbox Agency): The Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency is a guild of guards for hire based at Yilong Wharf in Liyue. Its guards escort valuable cargo and lone travellers so that bandits and wild beasts cannot rob them. It is a sub-organization of the Communications Office, which handles shipments and transport across Liyue. Its best-known guard is Gaming.

The agency advertises delivering goods safe and sound and giving clients peace of mind, and warns that customers bear every consequence of not honestly disclosing what is in the cargo.

Structure: The agency is a sub-organization of the Communications Office. Hanqian, a guard who calls himself one of the leaders and "half an owner", is a senior figure; an owner has stepped back after the leadership group thinned out. Staff are called guards for hire. The recruitment notice offers food and lodging and excellent pay, and asks for physically fit applicants who can endure hardship and heavy labour.

Hanqian says there were originally three leaders. After the agency began working with the Communications Office, the best of them lost his drive, and another was ambushed by bandits and took almost a year to recover, so Hanqian is the one left, waiting for newly recruited guards to improve things.

Members: Gaming is the agency's gold-standard guard, a young man praised for pleasing clients while beating off bandits, and who also leads the Mighty Mythical Beasts troupe. Dip Yeuk is a newer guard and drums for that troupe. Hanqian, an open-world NPC at Yilong Wharf, is a leading guard. Huang the Third is another guard Hanqian worries about.

Hanqian says a good guard needs to be agile, patient, good with directions, observant and quick-witted, and above all chivalrous, immune to bribery. He recalls a guard who colluded with bandits and stole a shipment, was chased down by other guards, handed to the Millelith, made to repay everything and imprisoned for life.

Goals: The agency's business is delivering goods and clients intact. Its guards also protect customers who are travelling alone through mountains and forests.

Methods: Guards focus on stamina, endurance and weight training rather than adventurers' skills. They train in horse stance, and Gaming has asked for plum blossom poles in the yard to firm up their fundamentals. Gaming's character story shows guards lifting cargo by hand to build strength.

The agency's public bulletin board carries its advert, recruitment notice and messages from the public: one client thanks Gaming for a rescue in the mountains, another asks for a sparring match (refused because the guards are busy), a lovelorn customer complains that a delivered confession got no reply, and Baizhu writes that his apprentice is delivering medicine for the guards. The agency also takes outside bookings, such as arrangements for visits to Wangshan Hall, the Guhua Clan's old stronghold.

History: Gaming joined as a temporary hand during a Lantern Rite when he led a Fontainian merchant there while a lead guard was short of staff, and was kept on as an official guard after that run. The agency is first documented in version 4.4.

Relations: - **Communications Office**: parent organization; per Hanqian the partnership changed the agency's rhythm.
- **Mighty Mythical Beasts**: Gaming's Wushou troupe, whose members are the agency's guards.
- **Millelith**: guards hand over criminals to them.

Reputation: Merchants favour its guards, and a thanks plaque to Gaming praises his hawk-like sight. Public notices show a mix of admiration, jokes and complaints.

Status as of 7.1: The agency is open at Yilong Wharf and recruiting. No later developments were found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

615.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency: Hanqian
615.content: Hanqian is an open-world NPC at Yilong Wharf, a guard and one of the agency's leaders. He trains hard, worries about his colleagues and says punches only get strength through real practice. He is blunt about hiring: chivalry matters more than anything.

616.comment: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency: Yilong Wharf agency bulletin board
616.content: A bulletin board beside Hanqian displays the agency's advert and notices from passers-by, including recruitment, sparring requests, complaints and invitations. The messages cycle at random when read.

617.content:
Tanit (also: Tanit tribe, Tanit Tribe, the Tanit, Tanit Eremites): The Tanit were a nomadic Eremite tribe of Sumeru's Desert of Hadramaveth, matrilineal and led by a Matriarch and Nine Elders. They worshipped the Goddess of Flowers, traded in crocodile goods, spices and oils, and raised stolen or lost children as Falcons. Their last camp, the Tanit Camps, lay on the desert's southern edge. The tribe was destroyed in the events of Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...

The Tanit were the oldest of the wandering desert tribes and had many branches. They valued words and knowledge but distrusted the Akasha. They had no unified law and no written rules, only what was "written in their blood and habits", and they hated traitors from within more than any outsider. The Traveler meets them through Jeht, who joined the tribe after her father Jebrael's death.

Structure: The tribe was matrilineal. A Matriarch led it, and Nine Elders held authority beside her. Babel had most of the other elders removed before the Traveler arrived, so by then power sat with her and her chosen lieutenants, notably Azariq, her "Left Hand". Warriors, guards and Falcons served under them. Jeht joined as a "half-outsider", since her father Jebrael had been born to the tribe and left it.

The tribe had many branches, so the Tanit Camps were the largest and most recent settlement of a wider people rather than the whole of it. Trade was a main source of income, and the tribe also hunted Wenut for spices. Falcons were a special class: children taken in or plundered and raised to be devoted to the elders, of whom only a handful were favoured.

Leadership: Babel Tanit was the Matriarch. She presented the tribe as a family and used that word to justify punishing anyone she called a traitor. She tasked Jeht with removing the remaining elders by accusing them of betrayal. In truth she was consolidating power for herself, with Azariq's help and with Snezhnayan supplies and technology obtained from the Fatui. Once she had what she wanted she turned on the Fatui, claiming she had never meant to share the Eternal Oasis with them.

Members: Named members at the time of the Traveler's visit include Babel; Azariq, her trusted "son" and Left Hand; Aderfi, who fled after trying to have the Traveler removed; the guards Hugeweh and Mendas; the farmer Yuften; and the Falcons Nayram and Rezki, two of Babel's best. Jeht was a member until the tribe fell. Her father Jebrael and his companion Samail had belonged to the tribe earlier and left it.

Others named in the wiki's member list include Masseira, who fled after The Fallen Falcon; Tadhla, the Bent-Winged Falcon; and elders such as Bleda, Gwaffah, Izder, Meddur, Tafreh, Teyya and Uzad, whom Jeht assassinated on Babel's orders. Tarafa was a mole Babel sent to kill her opponents, and Jebrael killed him before the story begins. Babel herself had a daughter whom she had lost to the sands before the Traveler arrived.

Goals: Publicly, the Tanit sought to prosper as a tribe and to find the Eternal Oasis, a legendary place in the desert. Babel's own goal was larger. She wanted the Eternal Oasis, and after the Traveler became the master of the Jinni Liloupar, she wanted the Orchard of Pairidaeza too, so she could be the sole prophetess of Nabu Malikata and rebuild the glory of the desert empire that existed before its destruction, overthrowing the Sumeru Akademiya.

Methods: The tribe fought with ordinary warriors and with Falcons, and it hired mercenaries when needed. Babel ruled by suspicion: accusations of treachery, assassination of rivals and elders, and sending groups of followers into dangerous places. The groups she sent to the Eternal Oasis died, and she made it taboo to follow them. She also sent scouts to other tribes to warn them of Jeht's "treachery" in advance, so the Eremites would see her as dangerous.

The tribe kept an uneasy business relationship with the Sumeru Akademiya. A contract in the camp shows Babel hiring warriors, among them Azariq, to escort a Kshahrewar Dastur across the desert for a fee, with part of the pay for secrecy. Several books in the camp bear Akademiya Library emblems and are described as smuggled. Their pages are well worn, and some are books the Akademiya had refused to enter into the Akasha.

History: **Earlier years.** The Tanit lived in the desert for an unknown time. A weapon's text suggests the Falcon custom began when "ascetics" left the priests of King Deshret and bent his archery ceremonies into training lost children. Babel herself was a Vahumana scholars' orphan taken in by an Eremite mercenary and raised as a Falcon of the tribe.

**Jebrael's exit.** Babel sent expeditions to Gurabad and toward the Eternal Oasis. Jebrael and Samail were in one of them, and Babel sent Tarafa to kill adherents of King Deshret. Jebrael saw through the plan, feigned death and killed Tarafa before he could kill Samail. The two left the tribe, and Babel came to regard Jebrael as a traitor.

**The Fatui and the elders.** The Fatui came seeking the Eternal Oasis. With Azariq's help, Babel had the other elders removed in exchange for Snezhnayan supplies and technology, then backstabbed her partners.

Relations: - **Eremites**: the Tanit are one of several desert tribes. Babel deliberately cast Jeht as a traitor to them, so the other tribes would turn on her.
- **Fatui**: Babel traded with them for supplies and technology, then double-crossed them. Azariq was secretly allied with them, and she later sold Jeht to their scientist Froderock Fronkonsteen.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: ties of convenience. The Tanit hire out as guides and escorts and read Akademiya books, but distrust the Akasha.

- **Vahumana**: after the tribe's fall, the Vahumana Dastur Tanjiyy came to give educational assistance to the Tanit under a deal Setaria had made, and found the camps empty. He worked out that the tribe had been wiped out but did not know the details.
- **Nabu Malikata**: the Tanit believe in the Goddess of Flowers. In The Dirge of Bilqis, the Traveler found that the goddess Babel worshipped was nowhere to be found.

Reputation: Among Sumeru's markets the Tanit were known for crocodile products, spices and essential oils. The Akademiya looked on the tribes mostly as desert folk to hire. Inside the tribe, Babel's reputation was one of strictness and family loyalty. Her private plans were different, and by the end she had spread word to other Eremites that Jeht was a traitor.

Status as of 7.1: The Tanit are gone. Babel is dead and the tribe was destroyed by Jeht and the Traveler, leaving only a few survivors. The Tanit Camps are now empty.

Jeht left the tribe's ruin to travel on her own and later led a mercenary group, and nothing in canon through 7.1 shows the tribe returning.

618.content: Babel Tanit was the Matriarch of the Tanit tribe, who raised herself to power by having elders removed and cheating the Fatui. She spoke warmly of the tribe as a family, and showed particular favour to Jeht, while planning to use or kill her. She died at Jeht's hand in Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... Her own character is described in her NPC entry.

619.content: Falcons were children taken in or plundered by some desert tribes and raised devoted to the elders. In the Tanit, only a few became favoured. Babel, Tadhla (the Bent-Winged Falcon), Nayram and Rezki were Falcons. A weapon's text suggests the custom grew from the training of King Deshret's priests, in a distorted form.

620.comment: Tanit: The fall of the Tanit
620.content: After the Traveler told Jeht of Babel's plot, the two returned to the Tanit Camps and fought Babel and the tribespeople loyal to her. Jeht killed Babel. Babel's final claim was that scouts had already told the Eremites that Jeht was a danger. Afterwards the camps were empty, and Tanjiyy of the Vahumana, who came to teach the tribe under Setaria's deal, assumed that the tribe had been annihilated.

621.content:
Tenryou Commission (also: Tenryou Commissioner, Tenryou-bugyou, Tenryou Bugyou): The Tenryou Commission is the Raiden Shogun's executive arm in Inazuma: it keeps public order, commands the military and police, and enforced the Vision Hunt Decree and the Sakoku Decree. It is one of the three bodies of the Tri-Commission and is led by the Kujou Clan. After the Fatui plot in Inazuma was exposed, its Commissioner Kujou Takayuki was removed, and his son Kujou Kamaji now leads it as acting head.

Its name refers to Tenryou, the part of Inazuma City directly governed by the Shogun, below Tenshukaku. Its headquarters stand in the Tenshukaku area above Inazuma City, and the Kujou estate is directly adjacent to Tenshukaku.

Structure: The Commission is led by the head of the Kujou Clan. Its military side is the Shogun's Army, whose generals include Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito; Masahito commands from the Kujou Encampment on Kannazuka. The wiki lists a chief samurai and security head (Okawara Goemon), a quartermaster (Yasutake) and a Shogunate officer (Toranosuke). Below these are Shogunate samurai (such as Inaba Kyuuzou and Ogura Yuu), yoriki (such as Takasaka Izumi and Iwakura Mitsunari), and doushin, the foot officers who patrol the city. Shikanoin Heizou is listed as a Tenryou "Detective" among the doushin.

The police station in Tenryou, the street below the castle, is staffed by a yoriki (Owada) and a doushin (Uesugi). The Kujou Clan also keeps retainers of its own, including Ikeda Soushirou and Ippei, who serves Kamaji.

Leadership: The Commission is led by Kujou Kamaji, an official who fills in as Proxy Clan Head. Generals Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito command its forces. Sara is a tengu adopted into the Kujou Clan.

Kamaji is the younger son of Takayuki and handles the Commission's government business in Inazuma City. Before the Fatui plot came out he was doubtful about the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees but kept his doubts private. He took over after his father's fall, and Masahito, who as the elder son had the right to the headship, passed it to him because he judged Kamaji the better fit. Kamaji's sweetheart is Hiiragi Chisato, who was left as figurehead of the rival Kanjou Commission after her father's fall.

Takayuki, the former head, is described as an old man who aged overnight after his exposure. He is under house arrest and was denied bail. He had taken Sara in as an adoptive daughter after she was found as a tengu child with a glowing Vision. Kamaji's relationship with his adoptive sister Sara is amicable.

Members: Named staff include Okawara Goemon (Chief Samurai and head of the Kujou Clan's security, who describes himself as the best swordsman in Inazuma), Toranosuke, Yasutake, Ishikawa, Matsudaira, Motosuke, Ono, Sue Yoshitaka, Inaba Kyuuzou, Takasaka Izumi, Iwakura Mitsunari, Mikoshi Genjirou, Owada, Yata Kouki, Kagami Gozen, and the doushin Andou, Amano, Asakawa, Asakura, Inoue, Sanada, Uesugi, Watanabe and Heizou. Not part of the Commission: Naoe Hisamasa, a hatamoto in charge of security at Tenshukaku, tells visitors that he and his men take orders only from the Shogun and directs requests to the Tri-Commission.

Goals: Officially the Commission preserves order and carries out the Shogun's will. Under Takayuki this meant keeping the Shogun's decrees running at any cost to preserve the Kujou Clan's influence. Under Kamaji it is trying to preserve the clan's honour and adjust to a country that no longer follows the decrees.

Methods: The Commission runs patrols and police, mans checkpoints, keeps wanted lists and posts notices on Inazuma's bulletin boards. During the Vision Hunt Decree it carried out the confiscation of Visions from ordinary people, setting up the Vision Hunt Ceremony at the Statue of the Omnipresent God. It enforced the Sakoku Decree against illegal entry and exit, while the Kanjou Commission handled legal travel. It was also the Shogun's field force against the Watatsumi Army in the civil war.

After Thoma escaped the Vision Hunt Ceremony with Paimon and the Traveler in Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow, the Tenryou Commission put the Traveler on a wanted list. Sara, the Commission's general, kept her own Electro Vision throughout, one of the exceptions the wiki says were made for those who serve the Shogun and remain useful.

History: **Before the decrees.** The Kujou Clan is described as the most loyal of the major families serving the Shogun. At some point in the past the clan recruited the swordsman Iwakura Michihiro as its sword instructor and gave him the title "Douin". The Commission had the Shogun's trust over public security in Tenryou and Inazuma.

**The decrees.** A year before the Traveler arrived, the Fatui promised Takayuki support and rewards if he enforced the Vision Hunt Decree. He believed the Fatui could never threaten Inazuma, and, to protect the clan's influence, agreed. He sent the Shogun deceitful, optimistic reports. When Masahito reported the destructive power of the Tatarigami on Yashiori Island and asked for help, Takayuki reacted with anger, suspected incompetence and sent an investigation team to the island.

Relations: - **Kanjou Commission and the Hiiragi Clan**: rivals who keep each other in check; both were drawn into the Fatui's scheme, and both now have acting heads. Kamaji and Chisato are close, but their relationship is limited by the clans' rivalry.
- **Yashiro Commission and the Kamisato Clan**: the Yashiro is the only commission that did not take part in the Fatui plot. Ayato sided with Chisato and Kamaji in 2.6.
- **Raiden Shogun**: the Commission is her executive arm and ultimately answers to her.
- **Fatui**: Signora's faction manipulated Takayuki through promises of rewards and chaos, creating a market for Delusions.
- **Watatsumi Army**: the opposing force in the civil war the Vision Hunt Decree caused.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Kamaji acts as head of the Kujou Clan and the Commission. Takayuki remains under house arrest.

The Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees are no longer in force. The Commission's forces are led by generals Sara and Masahito. No Inazuman story was released in 5.8 to 7.1, so nothing found changes this.

622.comment: Tenryou Commission: Kujou Takayuki and the Fatui plot
622.content: Kujou Takayuki was head of the Kujou Clan and Tenryou Commissioner until the end of Chapter II. A year before the Traveler arrived the Fatui promised him support and generous rewards if he pushed the Vision Hunt Decree, and he accepted, thinking the Fatui no real threat. He lied to the Shogun in letters. He also adopted Kujou Sara. After the Traveler exposed him in Omnipresence Over Mortals, the Shogun stripped him of his post and he was placed under house arrest, denied bail and awaiting punishment. His son Kamaji replaced him as acting head.

623.comment: Tenryou Commission: Kujou Kamaji and the Tenryou duel
623.content:
Kamaji is the younger son of Takayuki and acts as clan head. Before the scandal he was an official handling the Commission's government business in Inazuma City and privately questioned whether the decrees were really good for people. After the scandal he says he is trying to stem the chaos and trusts that the next generation can mend its forebears' mistakes. He loves Hiiragi Chisato, the daughter of the Kanjou Commissioner, and they exchange letters. In Reflections of Mortality he challenges the Raiden Shogun to a duel for the Commission, knowing he will lose, and impresses her with his honour.

Kamaji says he sometimes feels that the burden is too much for someone like him, but that because the Shogun recognised his resolve he cannot disappoint her. He regards his father's actions as wrong and says he does not fully understand them.

624.comment: Tenryou Commission: Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito
624.content: Both are generals of the Shogun's Army who serve the Kujou Clan. Masahito, the clan's eldest son, commands from the Kujou Encampment on Kannazuka. He disliked the Vision Hunt Decree and believed it harmed the people, but kept fighting the Watatsumi Army and warned his father about the Tatarigami on Yashiori Island.
