Sara is the Shogun's aide, an adopted tengu who keeps her Vision as an exception. In 2.1 she works with the Traveler to expose Takayuki. See their own entries for fuller detail.

625.comment: Tenryou Commission: Vision Hunt Ceremony enforcement
625.content: The Tenryou Commission carried out the Vision Hunt Decree: seizing Visions from Inazuma's people and inlaying them in the Statue of the Omnipresent God. By the time of Amidst Stormy Judgment, 99 Visions had been seized. During the ceremony in Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow, Thoma escaped with the Traveler, and the Commission listed the Traveler as wanted. Okawara Goemon and the samurai Kinoshita guarded Thoma. After the Traveler showed the Shogun the power of the seized Visions' wishes, the decree was repealed and the Visions were returned.

626.comment: Tenryou Commission: Duel for the office of Tenryou Commissioner
626.content: In To Hear Mortal Hearts, a quest of Reflections of Mortality, the Shogun and the Traveler find Kujou Kamaji held by Takatsukasa Susumu, head of a Kujou branch family, at a hidden Tenryou base guarded by ronin. Kamaji had gone to negotiate handing the Commission to the Takatsukasa, and Susumu claimed the ronin were for security while pressing him for a confession of the Kujou's crimes. Ei says the office goes to whoever can beat her in a duel, and Susumu backs down. Kamaji accepts the challenge on behalf of the Kujou, fights until he collapses and is cared for afterwards. Ei tells the Traveler that the Shogun puppet would have beheaded him without a second thought, that he is hardly a great heir but shows that the Kujou honour remains, and that she will give the clan a little more time.

627.content: The Commission's headquarters stand in the Tenshukaku area above Inazuma City (the wiki lists it as a point of interest of Tenshukaku). Yoriki Okawara Goemon, Mikoshi Genjirou and Yata Kouki and the doushin Watanabe work there, and the Kujou retainer Ikeda Soushirou appears there as well. The police station and day-to-day patrol offices are in Tenryou, the commercial street below the castle.

628.content:
The Black Serpents (also: Black Serpents, Shadowy Husks, Shadowy Husk, Royal Guard of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ahn Royal Guard): The Black Serpents are what is left of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard, the knights who served under Captain Dainsleif before the nation fell. The curse on Khaenri'ah wore away their minds and memories. The Adventurer Handbook says only a will to "fight for something, someone, and some matter" remains. Depending on how worn they are, they are called Shadowy Husks or Black Serpent Knights. Outside quests they appear as elite enemies in the Chasm's underground mines and in the Spiral Abyss.

Canon files them under the Abyss, but they are not the Abyss Order, and the two meet in the Chasm. Many of them still guard what they once swore to protect.

Structure: No ranks or chain of command survive among the cursed. In life they were the Royal Guard under the Eclipse Dynasty, with Dainsleif as captain and bearer of the title "Twilight Sword". The wiki dates his promotion to about the time Irmin made the Traveler's sibling a vessel for Abyssal power. Today the Handbook groups them into two kinds. Shadowy Husks come as archers (Defender), lancers (Line Breaker) and banner bearers (Standard Bearer). Black Serpent Knights come as dual-axe fighters (Rockbreaker Ax) and greatsword fighters (Windcutter). Individual enemies in the Chasm carry names and epithets, such as Skeld, Augur of the Mirrors, and Serkir, Scribe of Swords.

The wiki notes that most of these Chasm names borrow from the 1999 film The 13th Warrior, so they are labels, not recorded Khaenri'ahn identities.

Members: Few members have histories. Halfdan, an elite Royal Guard, led the Chasm band. Irizar and Zephaniah fought beside the Children of Echoes in Natlan. Ynghildr was a Schwanenritter lost in Sumeru, not a Royal Guard, and Irizar and Zephaniah are called only Khaenri'ahn soldiers. Their sub-entries carry the detail.

In the Chasm, knights wear the same silent armour yet speak in broken lines when they spot the Traveler. They call the Traveler an outlander, an envoy of the heavens or a companion of "fate", echoing Khaenri'ah's old grievance against the sky.

Goals: Their purpose survives only as fragments. Dainsleif's order to protect the people of Khaenri'ah at all costs still guides Halfdan's band, and those people are now hilichurls, whom the knights shelter. Elsewhere the cursed seem to defend a place or duty, such as the control module of the Ruin Golem in Devantaka Mountain.

Methods: In battle they are durable and use slow elemental attacks. When a player's shield fully absorbs one of their hits, they buff themselves or nearby allies at the cost of some of their own health. This is a gameplay note, not lore.

History: **Before the fall.** The Royal Guard served the Eclipse Dynasty. Dainsleif led them as the Abyssal power that destroyed Khaenri'ah rose.

**The cataclysm.** When Khaenri'ah fell about 500 years ago, its people were cursed, and the Guard's members faded into armoured shades that outlived their memories.

**The Chasm.** In the Archon Quest Requiem of the Echoing Depths (2.6), Dainsleif and the Traveler enter the Chasm's mines. Dainsleif is pursuing an Abyss Herald and the Traveler is investigating hilichurl movements. A band of knights attacks them without recognising Dainsleif, but Halfdan does and orders the others to withdraw. The Abyss Order's amplification device then torments the knights and hilichurls; Halfdan shields others from its light at the cost of his life while the Traveler destroys its charging devices. The wiki says Dainsleif comforts his spirit with the untrue claim that Khaenri'ah still stands.

**Natlan.** During the cataclysm, Irizar and Zephaniah helped the Children of Echoes funnel Abyssal forces into a cavern in the Sulfurous Veins. They held the line while Elder Traore sealed it with the Shadow Pins, and their souls were trapped in the fight. In the Natlan world quest Peace to the Slumbering the Traveler frees them.

**Sumeru.** Ynghildr of the Schwanenritter went missing fighting the "Onslaught of Dark Beasts" after the order's last Ruin Golem reached Devantaka Mountain. In Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter the Traveler finds her turned into a cursed knight guarding the Ruin Golem.

Relations: Dainsleif is their former captain and the one person who can still reach them. The Abyss Order's amplification device, meant to lift the curse, only caused them agony. Hilichurls, former Khaenri'ahn civilians, are the people they protect. The Children of Echoes remember Irizar and Zephaniah first as villains and then as heroes.

The Traveler fights them as hostile enemies, but the quests show them as victims. When Jazari hears the Traveler met Ynghildr, he dismisses the idea that a Khaenri'ahn could have lived so long, which shows how little ordinary people know of the curse.

Reputation: Most of Teyvat knows them only as monstrous armoured enemies. The Children of Echoes first told a tale of two evil Khaenri'ahn soldiers, which Irizar and Zephaniah had themselves requested so the tribe would stay wary of the Abyss. Titu reversed that after learning the truth.

Secrets: That these monsters were once loyal knights is known to Dainsleif, the Traveler and those who took part in the quests. Dainsleif's white lie to Halfdan is one of the few kindnesses the knights receive.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Black Serpents survive only as cursed enemies. The one organised band seen, in the Chasm, lost its leader Halfdan in the Archon Quest. Nothing new was found for 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

629.comment: The Black Serpents: Halfdan and the Chasm Knights
629.content: Halfdan was an elite of the Royal Guard who kept Dainsleif's final order to protect Khaenri'ah's people. Cursed and eroded, he still guarded dying hilichurls entering the Chasm, recognised Dainsleif and shielded others from the Abyss Order's device at the cost of his life. His spirit passed on after Dainsleif told him Khaenri'ah still stood.

630.comment: The Black Serpents: Irizar and Zephaniah
630.content: Two Khaenri'ahn soldiers who held the line for the Children of Echoes in the Sulfurous Veins during the cataclysm. Their souls were bound to an endless fight against the Abyss when the Shadow Pins sealed the cavern. They asked the tribe to remember them as villains, and the Traveler later set them free.

631.content: A Schwanenritter who went missing fighting the "Onslaught of Dark Beasts" in Sumeru. Only her signet ring and one other item were recovered, and Anfortas believed the order had fought to the last. In truth she became a cursed knight and guarded the Ruin Golem's control module until the Traveler defeated her.

632.content:
The Crux (also: Crux Fleet, the Crux Fleet, Crux): The Crux is an armed fleet based in Liyue Harbor and led by Captain Beidou. Its sailors carry cargo across seas no ordinary merchant would risk, fight sea monsters and pirates, and are famous throughout Liyue for daring voyages and rich bounties. Its flagship is the Alcor. Everything it does is approved by the Qixing, in the words of Beidou's profile, "more or less".

Its crew is fiercely loyal to Beidou, and she in turn risks her ship for strangers. The fleet is also known for its feasts, its hired chefs and its guests, which have included Xiangling and the Inazuman wanderer Kaedehara Kazuha.

Structure: The crew is split into two arms. The Spear of the Crux is trained for naval warfare and handling cargo deals. The Shield of the Crux is trained in survival and safe navigation: maritime rescue, cartography, weather reading and even counselling, and it also plans the crew's recreation. Beidou's hangout quests show both arms training an outsider, one with a boat-handling drill and one with seamanship lessons from the ship's surgeon, navigator and a sailor.

Known roles aboard the Alcor include Juza (Chief Mate), Huixing (navigator), Yinxing (surgeon at sea), Mora-Grubber (bookkeeper), Suling (ironworker) and Muzhen (chief technical officer), plus sailors such as Furong, Xu Liushi and Sea Drake. A young girl called Little Yue also lives among the crew. The fleet operates at least two ships of the Alcor class. The second, called "No. 2" because she was launched without a naming ceremony, carries upgraded Guizhong Ballistas that can remotely intercept incoming projectiles. Beidou says it is an older model that the Millelith have already moved beyond, approved for the civilian market.

Leadership: Captain Beidou, the Uncrowned Lord of the Ocean, established and leads the Crux. When she goes ashore for business, Chief Mate Juza minds the Alcor and the crew, as he tells visitors himself.

Beidou treats her crew with respect and in return they trust her to tame storms. Juza says he was a dockworker with no direction until she invited him aboard. His version of the legend is that Beidou stood at the wheel in a terrible storm and sang a fishermen's song until the waves died and dawn broke. He tells new sailors that story over drinks after their first safe return.

Members: Beidou is the only playable member. Kaedehara Kazuha is a temporary crew member, taken aboard at Ritou while wanted in Inazuma, and he stayed even after the Vision Hunt Decree ended. Xiangling is a regular guest rather than crew, sailing with them in search of new seafood ingredients.

Alcor crew in the open world include Juza, Yinxing, Huixing, Furong, Mora-Grubber, Suling, Sea Drake, Xu Liushi and Little Yue. Fengyun, Gongmiao, Huoxiang, Seahawk, Stone Stool and Zhiyao are further crew who appear at the expo. Muzhen appeared in a limited-time Inazuma event, where she was studying Ruin Sentinels for a client from Sumeru.

Goals: Profit and freedom, in that order, with a strong streak of justice. Beidou tells the Traveler that almost every confrontation the Crux faces is settled by negotiation, that weapons come out only when talks fail, and that the Alcor opens fire only in a fight to the death. In her words the ship is there to deter or to destroy, and the fleet is an armed crew with a sense of justice rather than war-hungry lunatics.

Methods: The Crux earns money in two ways. It acts as an armed carrier, delivering goods between places separated by sea, and it also deals in illegal trade. One hangout quest shows Beidou meeting trading partners and staging an after-hours handover on the beach at Guyun Stone Forest. It also trains navigators. In a Lantern Rite event quest (limited-time), the navigator Huixing explains that sailors need nine Ministry of Civil Affairs qualifications plus two years of maritime training and apprenticeship, and that the Crux and the Ministry have organised an intensive navigation training programme whose graduates receive a Deep Sea Navigation Qualification certificate. Its prices are very high, yet Beidou is known to tow a stranded boat to safety at risk to her own keel and to share the fleet's last food with the rescued.

History: **Early reputation.** The fleet earned its name over many years. Its landmark feat is the slaying of the sea monster Haishan, which Beidou had dreamed of since she was nine. Her Vision profile says the battle lasted four days, with cannons, harpoons and ropes pinning the beast while she fought it for ten hours, then finished it with one strike at dawn. A bolt of lightning struck the sea and she received her Electro Vision. Pier gossip adds that she has not sung a fishermen's shanty since. Tea Master Liu Su tells the story as "The Wrath of Haishan" in a Liyue storytelling quest.

**Kazuha comes aboard.** After Ei enacted the Vision Hunt Decree, Beidou befriended Kazuha at Ritou and took him on the Alcor as a sailor. She was wary of staying docked there longer than necessary. In the Inazuma Archon Quest she and the Alcor carry the Traveler from Liyue to Ritou.

Relations: Beidou and Ningguang, the Tianquan of the Liyue Qixing, are an odd pair. Beidou does not fear her as most of Liyue does and insists nobody is her boss. Ningguang says she hires Beidou, never the Crux. Ningguang's advisers call Beidou unpredictable, but Ningguang calls her the most reliable person in Liyue. Ningguang also lays hefty fines on the fleet's shipments, which Beidou simply pays, and the two play chess and bet against each other.

Beidou dislikes Treasure Hoarders but honours first-come, first-served in treasure hunts, and she offers hoarders a chance to leave that life. Rumour holds that Ningguang is the fleet's secret owner, a claim both women reject. The Qixing approve the expeditions "more or less". Abroad, the Crux deals with Inazuma through Yoimiya and Kokomi, and has met Fontaine's Navia and Clorinde at the Nod-Krai expo.

Reputation: Every merchant in Liyue Harbor knows Beidou and her crew. The harbour tells exaggerated tales of her feats, from cutting a sea monster in two to winning money from Ningguang at chess, and merchants gossip about the fines she pays on shipments. Children look up to her. Criminals such as Treasure Hoarders fear and avoid her. Her crew consider her capable of anything and the stories grow with every telling.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Crux is active and still led by Beidou. Juza keeps the Alcor, which is anchored off Guyun Stone Forest while Beidou is in the city.

It last featured prominently in the 6.5 expo event. No 6.x Nod-Krai Archon Quest or 7.0 and 7.1 Snezhnaya content was found that changes the fleet's status.

633.content:
The Alcor is the Crux's flagship, anchored off Guyun Stone Forest when at rest. The map text says it crosses oceans and can penetrate tempestuous storms. Juza calls it the fastest ship on Liyue's seas, armed to the teeth, and says pirates flee at the sight of it. A world quest, A Lone Ship in Guyun, has the Traveler help the crew with small chores after Juza first mistakes them for an intruder. The name comes from a star. Beidou says in a hangout quest that the Alcor is thought an omen of death.

The Alcor is the lead ship of its class. A second ship, No. 2, appeared at the 6.5 expo with upgraded Guizhong Ballistas, as the map description for that event notes.

634.comment: The Crux: Shield and Spear of the Crux
634.content: The Shield of the Crux covers survival: rescue at sea, charts, weather, counselling and crew recreation. The Spear covers naval warfare and cargo deals. In Life on the High Seas, Yinxing teaches the Traveler about health risks (underestimating danger is the answer to the greatest danger for new sailors), Huixing about navigation and Xu Liushi about reading storms, with Beidou setting a test afterward. In Beneath the Surface, the Spear's training uses older Skirmish Boats kept as backups on the Alcor.

635.content: Juza is the Chief Mate of the Alcor. He is loud, proud of the ship and devoted to Beidou, a former dockworker she invited aboard. When Beidou is ashore he treats unknown visitors suspiciously and threatens to have them fed to the fishes, until Yinxing steps in. His name is Inazuman in style, which fits the fleet's links to Inazuma.

636.comment: The Crux: Kazuha aboard the Alcor
636.content: Kazuha joined the Alcor at Ritou as a temporary sailor, hiding from those hunting him after the Vision Hunt Decree. Beidou did not realise at first that he was a trained swordsman and told her crew to take care of him. They welcomed him for his skill and for predicting weather, and overlooked his reticence about his past. After the Decree ended he stayed, and Kazuha's profile calls the Crux his new home. The crow's nest gives him space to think.

637.comment: The Crux: The Beidou and Ningguang arrangement
637.content: Ningguang is said to be the Crux's hidden owner. Neither woman accepts that. Ningguang hires Beidou, not the Crux; Beidou says they are equals. The Qixing's administrators see her as a lawbreaker who pays hefty fines without complaint, while the two women still keep each other company over chess and cooperate when Liyue's greater good is at stake.

638.content: Haishan was a leviathan-like sea monster that merchants were bound to meet sooner or later. Beidou had challenged it many times with the Crux. She struck it down after a four-day fight in which the fleet pinned it with ropes and harpoons. Her Electro Vision appeared afterwards. The crew sang a sea shanty during the battle, per her profile. Zhang Shun, a sailor injured then, retired and became a peddler.

639.comment: The Crux: Xiangling's feasts aboard the Crux
639.content: After a long voyage, the Crux held its customary three-day banquet and hired the then little-known Xiangling to save money. She objected to being asked for Yue-style seafood, but Beidou's offer of a fifty thousand Mora retainer won her over. Beidou told the crew to call her "Madam Xiangling" and predicted she would be famous. Xiangling has since joined voyages to find new ingredients, though she does not always heed Beidou's advice on what is edible.

640.comment: The Crux: Nod-Krai Trade Expo booth
640.content: During the limited-time event Where Waves Meet the Reef (6.5), the Crux took part in the expo in Nod-Krai with a new Alcor-class warship. The vessel was built for a special purpose, was launched quietly alongside a supply ship and had no naming ceremony, so she was just called No. 2. Beidou hoped to name her at the expo debut, and afterwards lets the Traveler choose between "Alkaid" and "Alioth" (the choice is the player's). Beidou met Navia and Clorinde there.

641.content:
The Steambird (also: Steambird, The Steambird newspaper, Steambird Newspaper): The Steambird is the main newspaper of the Court of Fontaine, read across Teyvat. Its office stands in Quartier Narbonnais, and its Chief Editor is Euphrasie. Its best-known reporter is Charlotte. Besides news it runs a reader-submission column, and it organises the La Verite Prize for journalism.

The paper covers everything from celebrity gossip and opera to politics, crime and science. Its pitch on the Newsstand Board is "your credible source of the unbelievable truth". Euphrasie says a good newspaper should be a lighthouse of truth. The paper also works as a community notice board through its "Tales of Humanity" column, which is the in-game explanation for Fontaine's Reputation system.

Citizens bring it both scoops and troubles: readers write in, reporters chase leads across Fontaine, and the Maison Gardiennage and Palais Mermonia use it to publicise wanted notices. Other publications compete for readers, such as La Gouttiere (also sold at the Newsstand Board), and, per Charlotte, "The Observer" for celebrity gossip and "Leisure Weekly".

Structure: The paper is led by Chief Editor Euphrasie. Beneath her is a staff of reporters who each cover an area, plus a photographer, a reviewer, a columnist and a trainee. Sir Arthur, apparently a mechanical newscaller, stands in Quartier Narbonnais shouting headlines and special issues. The office, called the main office in an item description, is in Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine.

Reporters have distinct beats. Chronie covers political affairs, Ethan covers real estate, Charlotte is a field and special correspondent, and Staelle writes a romance-novel column. Delerue is a reviewer, Antila a photographer, Gaston a trainee reporter, and Paban is listed as a "newsy". Galanopoulo, Herbier and Houallet are also listed as reporters. The wiki gives these roles from NPC profiles and map descriptions; most staff have no detailed profile.
The Serenitea Pot furnishing "Court of Justice's Authenticity" shares its model with the main office: a metal-and-glass structure with a circular centre divided into eight panels and a blue glass roof. Its description says sunlight is often likened to truth and justice, and that the paper may have chosen the design to remind people entering and leaving of their duty to be a credible source.

Leadership: Euphrasie is the Chief Editor. She runs the paper, assigns and recalls reporters such as Charlotte, and deals with the complaints and threats that follow. She speaks formally and with dry humour.

Euphrasie also posts the paper's commissions for locals' everyday troubles, helps the Palais Mermonia put up wanted posters for criminals and dangerous monsters issued by the Maison Gardiennage, and uses the paper's sources to find the right people for jobs. An earlier Chief Editor, Nellie Cochran, interviewed Alain Guillotin. In Charlotte's recruitment story, Euphrasie personally approached Charlotte to ask her to become a special correspondent.

Per Charlotte's profile, Euphrasie has repeatedly sent Charlotte on faraway field assignments to keep her away from the Court of Fontaine until the Maison Gardiennage or the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol have cleared up whatever she stirred up. Captain Chevreuse is quoted there trading exasperated words with her over a trip Charlotte made to Romaritime Harbor that nearly ended with her being thrown into the sea.

Members: Key people: Euphrasie (Chief Editor), Charlotte (reporter and special correspondent), Sir Arthur (newscaller), and columnists such as Mona. Nellie Cochran is a historical Chief Editor. Charlotte's father Galanopoulo, a veteran reporter and nature photographer, is listed among the staff, and the paper first published the photos he and Charlotte took.

Mona writes the astrology column "All Things Astrological". Her predecessor wished to retire and recommended her to the editor; her academic style drew readers interested in astrology's details. The Traveler is credited as the columnist "Ryuji-kun" for the real-world "Teyvat Food Notes" blog posts on the official Chinese site, a marketing tie-in outside the story. Chronie, a political reporter, appears in the Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles quest and can later be found at Cafe Lutece.

Goals: The paper's stated purpose is to keep information flowing so that everyone can understand what is happening around them, and then to let readers express themselves through "Tales of Humanity". Euphrasie calls it a lighthouse illuminating humanity. Practically, it also needs to be read: its pages mix serious reports with gossip because, as the Traveler puts it, trivial stories grab attention and sell copies.

Methods: Reporters pursue stories in person. Charlotte's creed is that nearer to the action is closer to the truth. The Traveler's account of the layout is that the front page leads with opera and actor news, early pages carry positive local news such as falling prices and aquabus progress, and bigger stories run later or as multi-day series. Sir Arthur advertises special editions in the street. When a reporter is threatened, Euphrasie says the paper has its own ways of dealing with it and would have gone bust long ago if it could not handle a tussle or two.

History: The paper is old. A past Chief Editor, Nellie Cochran, interviewed Alain Guillotin about his early years, which the wiki dates by inference to roughly 400-500 years ago. In the present day, the wiki, citing quests, says the paper covered the Traveler's fight with Dvalin (headlines for three weeks, with expert interviews and hand-drawn illustrations) and Kazuha blocking the Raiden Shogun's attack, a topic that held Fontaine's imagination for a while. The Traveler did not know about the first of these.
Charlotte became a Steambird reporter after her father sent in her photographs. The editors praised them, and Euphrasie then asked her to become a special correspondent. Charlotte's La Verite exposé and her long absence after investigating the diving employer Dollander are told in her character stories.

Relations: The Steambird works closely with law and order: the Maison Gardiennage once posted a guard detail at its entrance while Charlotte lived in the office, and the paper helps the Palais Mermonia advertise wanted people. It competes for readers with La Gouttiere and other papers. It is connected to Yae Publishing House through the Great Detective Hurlock series, which Paimon says the publishing house will print. The Traveler explains that the paper cannot easily publish it itself, because Yae has the best illustrators on its payroll.

Reputation: The Steambird is trusted enough that readers send it their problems, and Charlotte's profile records that it has also faced accusations of favouritism around its prize. Charlotte says in a voice-over that it has many outstanding journalists, an open-minded Chief Editor and, most importantly, pays its writers on time. Paimon treats it as the model of a gossip-filled paper.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 The Steambird is active in the Court of Fontaine with Euphrasie as Chief Editor. Sir Arthur, Charlotte and the columns continue as before.

Euphrasie's Reputation menu and the "Tales of Humanity" commissions remain available, and the La Verite Prize is still described in the Opera Epiclese bulletin. Nothing checked indicates that The Steambird changed in 6.x or in 7.0-7.1, and it plays no part in Snezhnaya content.

642.content: She is the one who repeatedly pulls Charlotte back from danger. When the Traveler asks about Charlotte, she first fears someone has come to make a threat, then says the paper has its own ways of dealing with that.

643.content: Sir Arthur is the Steambird's herald in Quartier Narbonnais. He cries "Extra, extra!" followed by headlines, and says "beep-boop". His content changes with story progress and ranges from opera and exhibition notices to crime news, rumours and special issues. He once announced that his regular maintenance had been completed and asked the public not to believe rumours that he had been stolen and split into three. The wiki lists his title as "The Steambird". He appears to be a machine, but canon does not say so outright.

644.content: Tales of Humanity is the Steambird's reader-submission column, begun so that people could express themselves and not only read. Euphrasie says it is "drowning in all manner of content" and that this is acceptable, because readers also want light reading and helping them is good for the paper's reputation. Many locals use it to post commissions, which Euphrasie coordinates; small jobs feel like splinters to those who write in. It is the in-game basis for Fontaine's Reputation system: finishing commissions raises the Traveler's standing, and Euphrasie later offers harder jobs.

645.content: Charlotte's profile says she won it several times in a row, which detractors blamed on collusion between the paper and the selection committee. She then published an exposé of the committee's long-running money dealings and unfair judgments, and also wrote about figures at the paper tied to the committee. The Maison Gardiennage investigated for three months and punished unjust judges, undeserving contestants and editors seeking favours. Charlotte stayed in the office meanwhile, Euphrasie turned visitors away, and a guard detail was posted at the entrance.

646.content: Nellie Cochran was a Chief Editor of The Steambird in the past. In Alain Guillotin's text she asks him about his early years, and the surrounding text describes him as a lonely, reclusive man. The wiki assumes she lived 400-500 years ago because she interviewed him; this is an inference. The unnamed Steambird editor who appears at a banquet in the same texts is not confirmed to be her.

647.content: "All Things Astrological" is the Steambird's astrology column. Its previous columnist wanted to retire and recommended Mona to the editor. Her writing was more academic and complicated, which attracted readers interested in the intricacies of astrology. In Owe Mora, Pay Mora she has written a manuscript for the paper on celestial shifts and their relation to a person's changing fates.

648.content: The Newsstand Board is a news board in Quartier Narbonnais, beside Angelique near Hubel's shop. It pitches the Steambird as "your credible source of the unbelievable truth" and notes that the stand also sells La Gouttiere and other magazines. Its messages rotate. Samples include the crowbar-wielding honored citizen detective, a reopened drowning case, the rising-water panic, and a verdict report by Charlotte on the trial after the serial disappearances case. La Gouttiere's pieces are gossip in tone, for example on Clorinde and on the Fontaine Research Institute explosion investigation.

649.comment: The Steambird: Great Detective Hurlock series
649.content: Great Detective Hurlock is a detective series connected to The Steambird. Paimon says Yae Publishing House will publish it and asks why the paper does not print it itself. The Traveler replies that a successful light novel depends on illustrations, and that Yae has the best illustrators under contract. Detective stories such as Hurlock and The Case Files of Miss Orith are popular in Fontaine. Authorship and other in-world details are not given in the pages checked.

650.content:
Treasure Hoarders (also: Treasure Hoarder, the Treasure Hoarders): The Treasure Hoarders are a gang of bandits who hunt treasure in ruins and domains all over Teyvat and get rough with bystanders who happen to be nearby. They are poorly organised because the groups are so far apart. The gang's official description credits a founder called Reed Miller, who called it "an organization of mutual cooperation." The group is said to have originated in Nod-Krai. Members join over crime or lack of steady income, and they tend to burn through loot fast and stay poor.

Members use a raven (Ravenwing) motif, and most wear a mask to hide their faces from the law. The few unmasked ones are either important or bait to draw victims into traps. Not all members get along, and some are looked down on more than others. The Nod-Krai content shows that the gang's roots were more idealistic than its present: a thief who wanted a world without borders.

The name Reed Miller turns out to have belonged to several different people, so the "founder" is both a legend and a succession of real, dead individuals. The modern gangs live off that name.

Structure: There is no known central command or fixed headquarters. Each region has its own groups, some led by a named boss such as Freckle Huang in Liyue. The wiki describes them as disorganised, mainly because of the distances between groups. Some members belong to sub-groups of the wider organisation, such as the Fruity Order in Fontaine. In Nod-Krai several groups follow in the footsteps of their founder.

Rank shows in who is unmasked and who holds an elite post. In the Traveler's fights the common types are scouts, marksmen, seamen, handymen, crushers, gravediggers, pugilists and four kinds of Potioneer (alchemists who throw Cryo, Electro, Hydro or Pyro concoctions). Named elites include Raptor, Carmen, Liuliu, Wallenstein and "Boss". Under Alia, Tolfin says in the 6.3 quest, the gang became "a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order," whose mantra was that people should not put their faith in gods.

Leadership: Today no overall leader is named. Regional bosses include Freckle Huang (Liyue, defeated in a Guizhong quest) and "Boss" or "Big Sis" in Liyue, who turns out to be Yan'er. The legendary leaders are the three holders of the Reed Miller name: Avrelian, Alia and Brahe, all long dead. See the entries on each. Hiljetta, the "Black-Barreled Hag," is a retired but renowned Hoarder in Nod-Krai who wants to restore the gang's old glory.

Others have taken the name since, and some only borrow it: in the 6.0 quest The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot, a thief named Netochka fancies herself the next Reed Miller. Jahoda named her chic badger companion Reed Miller XIII.

Members: The wiki lists many members by region. A few are worth knowing.
- **Mondstadt**: small-time thieves such as Tyler and Nimrod (an informant to Kaeya), plus the elite Raptor.
- **Liyue**: Freckle Huang (leader), Yan'er ("Boss"), Carmen, Liuliu and Wallenstein. Liyue is the gang's main haunt, including beneath the Chasm.
- **Inazuma**: Shun, Kojirou, Koichirou and others.
- **Sumeru**: Narzam, Pabag and others.
- **Fontaine**: the Grand Thief and several nicknamed members.
- **Natlan**: Coztic and Matthias.
- **Nod-Krai**: Hiljetta, Kaleva, Basu and Hoyka.

Former members include Jilliana, who left the gang secretly to raise a family with Rudolf and became a nun in Mondstadt's Church of Favonius, and Jahoda, whom the wiki lists as a former member (she is formerly of the Seahook Gang and now works with the Curatorium of Secrets and the Northern Intelligence Network). Tolfin, Hiljetta's grandson, is a travelling storyteller and merchant and is also on the former-members list.

Goals: Most members want treasure and a living. Their reasons for joining vary, but the wiki says they are usually crime or a lack of stable income. The idealistic founders had a bigger aim, an "Elysium" for the poor and hungry built on the wealth of the powerful. Hiljetta and others in Nod-Krai want to claim Reed Miller's hidden treasure and restore the gang's reputation.

Methods: Treasure Hoarders sack ruins, domains and chests, ambush travelers, and get rough with anyone who stumbles on them. In Liyue the leader called "Boss" leaves false trails and notes so that curious adventurers walk into ambushes. When beaten, they throw smoke bombs and vanish. Masks hide identity. Some groups in Fontaine use rogue or stolen Clockwork Meka, and some groups travel with a Sumpter Beast.

Regional partnerships are opportunistic. In Inazuma some work with the Nobushi, and one member colluded with the Fatui over the Electro Hypostasis in Kannazuka. In Sumeru they sometimes work with the Fatui and the Eremites. In Natlan they cooperate with tribal warriors in robbery and saurian trafficking. A sub-group introduced in 6.0 uses Fatui-style and Natlan-style weapons.

History: **Origin legend.** Nod-Krai folklore says the gang was founded by Reed Miller, an infamous master thief who buried a "great treasure" in the land that became Nod-Krai. The real story is told in quests of 6.3 and is covered in the entries below.

**Founding.** About 500 years ago, Avrelian, the son of a Snezhnayan officer and a Frostmoon Scion mother, graduated from the Snezhnayan military academy, "died in the line of duty" on paper shortly after becoming a non-commissioned officer, and turned to banditry. He raised the black raven emblem, gathered the forsaken and despised, and preached a world without borders. He was manipulated by Rotwang into stealing the Sampo Mill, then gave himself up in Snezhnograd hoping to speak to the Tsar. He was executed without ever meeting the Tsar.

**Alia and Brahe.** Alia took the mask and reorganised the gang. In a single night her force emptied the governor's palace of its ill-gotten wealth and shared it among the poor of Nasha Town. Brahe, the governor's adopted son, saw the deed and fell in love with her at first sight. Alia died stopping Rotwang's scheme during the Cataclysm, and Brahe became the third Reed Miller.

**Legend-making.** Seeing people commit cruelty in the name of Reed Miller's ideals, Brahe spread deliberately contradictory tales of Reed Miller, and set up the Great Treasure and the Proofs of the Cognoscenti, so that anyone abusing the name would look absurd.

Relations: - **Fatui**: sometimes allies of convenience in Inazuma and Sumeru. In Nod-Krai, Fatui agents accosted Hiljetta and she easily dealt with them. Netochka targeted a Fatui facility.
- **Crux / Beidou**: Liyue's Hoarders fear meeting Beidou and try to placate her.
- **Abyss Order**: a team of Hoarders tried to rob it and failed, as shown through the Grand Thief.
- **Eremites, Nobushi, tribal warriors**: occasional partners in the regions where they operate.
- **Frostmoon Scions and Snezhnaya**: Avrelian had Frostmoon blood, and Alia was a Scion by birth; both tangled with Rotwang and with the Snezhnayan state.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Treasure Hoarders remain active, scattered local gangs across every nation. No 7.0-7.1 story content about them was found. Their last major appearance is in the Nod-Krai content: the Reed Miller legend, Hiljetta and the Proofs of the Cognoscenti (6.3).

The 6.3 quest series revealed the truth about Reed Miller. Tolfin gave the Traveler a raven insignia (which he believes Avrelian left behind) as a keepsake, and Hiljetta wants the Traveler to visit for further sparring matches.

651.content: In Nod-Krai folklore, Reed Miller is the Treasure Hoarders' founder and an infamous master thief who buried a great treasure. In truth the name was worn by at least three people: Avrelian (first), Alia (second) and Brahe (third). Brahe wrote many conflicting legends under other names, such as "Brahe the Bard" and "Grand Duke Trubetskoy," so that nobody could use the name seriously. Popular tellings are collected in the book The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire. Others have adopted the name since; Jahoda named her chic badger partner Reed Miller XIII, and Netochka dreams of being the next Reed Miller.

652.content: Avrelian, nicknamed Relya, was the first Reed Miller and the Treasure Hoarders' founder. He was the son of a Frostmoon Scion Maiden and a Snezhnayan officer, and after his parents died he was adopted by an officer named Mikhnenko. He attended the Snezhnayan military academy and befriended Solovei, with whom he went treasure hunting; on one such hunt a young Brahe, the governor's adopted son, told them where the treasure was. Shortly after becoming a non-commissioned officer he faked his death. Avrelian dreamed of an Elysium for the poor and founded the gang under a raven emblem. Rotwang told him of his Frostmoon blood and a destiny as ruler of Elysium and got him to steal the Sampo Mill. Persuaded by Solovei to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar, he was arrested without meeting the Tsar and executed in public, in view of Solovei and Alia.

653.content: Alia was the second Reed Miller and Aila's older twin sister. Their adoptive grandmother Lovia, the Frostmoon Scions' Archpriestess, raised them in seclusion on Hiisi Island and had them kill other Scions and drink their blood. Alia escaped, apparently after Avrelian stole the Sampo Mill, and joined the Treasure Hoarders. After Avrelian's execution she took his mask and reorganised the gang, raiding the governor's palace for Nasha Town's poor. She and Solovei worked to stop Rauthvangi's plan to use the Pillar of Embla to pierce the false sky, and she gave her life by casting herself into the Sampo Mill and igniting it. Her last wish was that her sister live a life of happiness and freedom. Local legend made her a fae.

654.content: Brahe was the adoptive son of Prokhor Trubetskoy, governor of Nod-Krai, and later the last governor himself, and the third Reed Miller. He regarded Avrelian and Alia as true idealists and himself as a realist who understood human malice. After the Cataclysm he faked his death in the records and, over years, seeded contradictory legends about Reed Miller, including an invented companion named "Wagtail." He built the Great Treasure and later turned it into the Proof of the Cognoscenti trial, a test of wit rather than greed. A former academy instructor, Sukhotin, once found the vault, mistook him for a thief and stood down on recognising Avrelian's gauntlet.

655.content: Hiljetta is a very old woman living in an alcove in Wavechaser Plain and a retired Treasure Hoarder known as the Black-Barreled Hag for her fighting skill. She wants to bring back the gang's glory days under Reed Miller. She holds the last Proof of the Cognoscenti and gives it only to someone who will restore the legacy. She resents Brahe, her ancestor, for cheapening Reed Miller's legacy. After the Traveler beats her in a spar she hands it over. Her grandson Tolfin is a wandering storyteller and merchant who steered the Traveler to her, has a special bond with Weasel Thieves and travels with a weasel named Huginn. Hiljetta scolded him for not telling the Traveler that they were all linked to the gang.

656.content: Liyue is where the Treasure Hoarders are most visible. Freckle Huang leads the group in a Guizhong quest and is defeated there. Notes in several world quests refer to a female "Boss" who lays false treasure trails to lure adventurers into ambushes; she is later revealed to be Yan'er, also called "Big Sis." Yan'er is a childhood friend of Hiromi and Shun; after the Sakoku Decree she and Shun went treasure hunting in Liyue. She tried to plunder ruins south of Wuwang Hill during The Chi of Yore, and later teamed with Raptor on a raid on the Abyss Order. They hired the Grand Thief, who died. Beidou of the Crux frightens Liyue's Hoarders.

657.content: The Grand Thief is a popular Hoarder, said to come from Fontaine. After Osial was defeated, a group of Hoarders banded together to distract the Abyss Order while the Grand Thief slipped in to steal valuables. The Traveler and Paimon find the defiled statue and his kneeling corpse in Involuntary Sacrifice (Archon Quest Chapter I, Act IV, We Will Be Reunited). The cause of his death is unknown.

658.content: Fontaine's Hoarders roam the countryside in groups. Some use rogue or stolen Clockwork Meka for mining or guarding. Others belong to sub-groups such as the Fruity Order. Some members have crossed the sea to Chenyu Vale. According to the wiki their standing seems fairly high.

659.comment: Treasure Hoarders: Treasure Hoarders in other nations
659.content: In Mondstadt the Hoarders have little presence but cause trouble occasionally. In Inazuma some cooperate with the Nobushi, and one colluded with the Fatui over the slumbering hypostasis in Kannazuka. In Sumeru they sometimes work with the Fatui and the Eremites, and a few groups in Liyue travel with a Sumpter Beast. In Natlan they have far less influence than elsewhere, cooperating occasionally with tribal warriors in robbery and saurian trafficking.

660.content: Jilliana was a Treasure Hoarder until she met and married Rudolf and had a daughter, Lily. Having a family made her see where she was heading, so she left the gang in secret, joined the Church of Favonius and became a nun at the Favonius Cathedral. In A Surprise Gift the Traveler helps Rudolf pick a gift for her. According to the wiki, she is also the source of the remark that Hoarders burn through money quickly, leaving a cycle of wealth and poverty.

661.comment: Treasure Hoarders: Proofs of the Cognoscenti
661.content: The Great Treasure was Brahe's invention to keep the Reed Miller name harmless. It became the Proof of the Cognoscenti, a set of pieces and trials. The Traveler collects four pieces, and the last is held by Hiljetta, who tests the Traveler first. Netochka tried to steal one from the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, and Tolfin gave the Traveler the Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask after testing the Shesternin heirs. At the site the Traveler opens several doors, defeats a Radiant Lunapod guardian and finds a mysterious ship.

662.content:
Tri-Commission (also: Sanbugyou, San-bugyou, Three Commissions, Three Commissioners): The Tri-Commission (Sanbugyou, "Three Commissioners") is the collective name for the three organisations that run Inazuma's government under the Raiden Shogun. The Tenryou Commission, led by the Kujou Clan, handles security and the military. The Kanjou Commission, led by the Hiiragi Clan, handles finance, customs and the borders. The Yashiro Commission, led by the Kamisato Clan, handles shrines, festivals and ceremonies. An Inazuman in Liyue compares them to Liyue's Qixing and Eight Trades and to the Knights of Favonius.

The three commissions can check one another. The Hiiragi and Kujou are described as political rivals who keep each other in balance. The Yashiro is the only one of the three that stayed out of the Fatui's scheme.

Structure: Each commission has its own clan, its own commissioner and its own staff. The wiki lists them like this:
- **Tenryou Commission**: Kujou Clan; head of public security, military and police affairs, enforcer of the Vision Hunt Decree and of the Sakoku Decree against illegal entry or exit.
- **Kanjou Commission**: Hiiragi Clan; the financial arm, supervising the borders, trade and bureaucracy, and enforcing the Sakoku Decree for legal entry and exit.
- **Yashiro Commission**: Kamisato Clan; the cultural arm, handling ceremonies, celebratory events and public festivals, and managing shrines and temples. It is considered the commission closest to the Raiden Shogun.

Soldiers of the Shogun's Army are assigned to each commission.

The wiki says the Tri-Commission meets at Tenshukaku to decide government affairs. Kamisato Ayaka says that when the Yashiro Commission proposed repealing the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions vetoed it, which suggests that proposals pass through some council and that the Yashiro cannot approach the Shogun directly. Naoe Hisamasa, who guards the area around Tenshukaku and says he takes orders only from the Shogun, tells petitioners to see the officers of the Tri-Commission.

Leadership: The Raiden Shogun rules over the three. The Kujou, Hiiragi and Kamisato clans lead the Tenryou, Kanjou and Yashiro Commissions. Kamisato Ayato leads the Yashiro Commission, which was untouched by the Fatui scandal.

Kujou Kamaji (Tenryou) and Hiiragi Chisato (Kanjou) are acting heads of their clans, as their fathers Kujou Takayuki and Hiiragi Shinsuke fell after the Fatui plot came out. In the Cypressus Custos Chapter a wedding announcement refers to both as Proxy Clan Heads. Kamisato Ayato leads the Yashiro Commission as clan head, and the wiki lists his sister Kamisato Ayaka among its leaders and Thoma among its staff.

Generals Kujou Sara and Kujou Masahito serve under the Tenryou Commission. The Kanjou Commission's military chief is Katsuie.

Goals: The Tri-Commission carries out the Shogun's decrees and handles ordinary government. During the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees this meant seizing Visions and sealing the borders in the name of the Shogun's eternity. Since those decrees ended, its work is again security, trade, ceremony and the relations among the clans.

Methods: Each commission governs through its specialty. The Tenryou Commission uses soldiers, patrols and wanted lists. The Kanjou Commission uses financial control, permits and border assessments at Ritou. The Yashiro Commission works through festivals, shrines and the Kamisato Estate's retainers, and controls the Shuumatsuban, a clandestine ninja organisation used for gathering information.

The Fatui exploited this arrangement. The wiki says the Vision Hunt Decree began as a Fatui plot to create a market for Delusions, and that the Fatui won over the heads of the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions with promises of power and wealth. The Yashiro Commission took no part, because Ayato turned down the Fatui's offer of cooperation, according to the wiki's citation of his character demo.

History: **Long-standing houses.** The Hiiragi Clan has served the Shogun for at least 500 years, and the Kujou Clan, which takes its name from Kujou Shigeyori, is regarded as the most loyal of the Shogun's major families. The sources read do not say when the three commissions took their present form.

**The decrees (about a year before the Traveler arrived).** The Sakoku Decree and Vision Hunt Decree were imposed. The Tenryou Commission carried out the Vision Hunt and the Kanjou Commission ran the border approvals. Ayaka says proposals from the Yashiro Commission to repeal the Vision Hunt Decree were vetoed by the other two.

Relations: - **Raiden Shogun**: the sole authority above the Tri-Commission. Naoe Hisamasa says the Tenshukaku guards answer only to her.
- **Grand Narukami Shrine**: a separate institution under Guuji Yae Miko, with religious and informal political influence. It is not one of the three commissions.
- **Fatui**: manipulated two commissions and left the Yashiro alone.
- **Watatsumi Army**: the opponent of the Shogun's forces in the civil war the Vision Hunt Decree caused.
- **Liyue Qixing and Eight Trades; Knights of Favonius**: the comparison offered by Atsuko, an Inazuman who fled to Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tri-Commission stands, with Ayato leading the Yashiro Commission and acting heads Kamaji and Chisato leading the Tenryou and Kanjou.

The Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees are gone. Former commissioners Takayuki (under house arrest) and Shinsuke (imprisoned) are still awaiting the Shogun's punishment. The sources checked show no later story, up to 7.1, that changes this.

663.content: The Yashiro Commission manages shrines, festivals and cultural events and is led by the Kamisato Clan; its headquarters are at the Kamisato Estate. Kamisato Ayato is its Commissioner and clan head. Because its work is mostly civilian it has less influence than the Kanjou and Tenryou. The soldiers assigned to it are relaxed and caring toward the people. It runs the Shuumatsuban. It was untouched by the Fatui because Ayato declined their offer, and it gained some sympathy after Chapter II. Its members include Ayato, Ayaka and Thoma, and the Komore Teahouse, a Kamisato-linked business, is run by Taroumaru.

664.comment: Tri-Commission: Comparison with other nations' governments
664.content: In A Path Through the Storm, Atsuko explains Inazuma's government by comparing it to Liyue's Qixing and Eight Trades and to the Knights of Favonius. The comparison is loose: the Tri-Commission serves a Shogun, whom neither of the other bodies has. The English version of her line says the Eight Trades work "under" the Qixing, while the Chinese and Japanese versions list them side by side.

665.comment: Tri-Commission: Fatui collusion with the commissions
665.content: In Chapter II the Fatui, working through the Harbinger Signora, set out to create a market for Delusions by stirring conflict in Inazuma. They gained the cooperation of two of the three commissions. Kujou Takayuki, Tenryou Commissioner, agreed to push the Vision Hunt Decree and sent false reports to the Shogun. Hiiragi Shinsuke, Kanjou Commissioner, stockpiled Crystal Marrow for the Fatui and planned with Signora to keep the Traveler stranded in Ritou. After the Traveler unravelled the plot, both men were removed and held awaiting the Shogun's judgment. See the Tenryou and Kanjou entries for detail.

666.content:
Universitas Magistrorum (also: the Universitas, University of the Magisters): The Universitas Magistrorum was a Khaenri'ahn institute of learning whose members worked in astrology, alchemy and other arts. It was directly subordinate to the Vinster King Irmin and held real influence in the kingdom. Before the cataclysm it was led by President Hroptatyr, "The Wise", with Eftirvit, later called Pierro, as Vice-President. After Irmin became obsessed with the Abyss, it turned into a major centre of Abyssal research. What became of it after the kingdom fell 500 years ago is not stated.

The name is Latin, roughly "University of the Magisters". The institute is known only through memories, book text and story quests set in the last years of Khaenri'ah, never as a place the Traveler visits in the present day.

Structure: At the top were a President, who was also the Chief Royal Mage with the royal title "The Wise", and a Vice-President. Beneath them worked professors and researchers, among them Professor Mimameith (the teacher of both leaders) and the Moon Marrow researcher Tholindis. The Universitas also held a collection of literary works, and in at least one legend it had a champion fighter. It answered to the king directly and had no other known superior.

The only unit named is the Moon Marrow lab, which studied the Crimson Moon's remains as a possible energy source. President Hroptatyr's own field of research was the Crimson Moon. No source lists other departments, and the institute's size is not given.

Leadership: Hroptatyr was the President, a rising prodigy who had studied under Mimameith and was favoured by the king. Eftirvit, his friend and rival, was passed over for the presidency and served as Vice-President. Both were counted among the most promising scholars of their generation. Rhinedottir remarked to Hroptatyr that the Vice-President did not hide his envy, and Hroptatyr answered that missing the presidency spared Eftirvit a great deal of stress.

The two shared a respectful rivalry until their teacher fell ill. Hroptatyr's discovery about the Crimson Moon's authority over death, and his sudden refusal to use it to save Mimameith, left Eftirvit embittered. By the time the Traveler's sibling and Paimon each arrived in Khaenri'ah, the pair were at odds, and each tried to win the king's favour in his own way. See the entry on the two leaders below.

Members: Named members are Hroptatyr, Eftirvit (Pierro), their teacher Professor Mimameith, and Tholindis, a young Moon Marrow researcher. Alf is described in the legend Perinheri as the greatest warrior in the Universitas Magistrorum.

Tholindis was a distant descendant of the Crimson Moon Dynasty who hid her ancestry, and she was engaged to Rerir. Her story ends at the Universitas on the night of the raid (see below). Hroptatyr later became one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, and Eftirvit later became Pierro, the Director of the Fatui.

Goals: The Universitas served the crown by forecasting from the stars, working with alchemy and seeking sources of power for the kingdom. Under Irmin's growing fixation, its purpose narrowed to understanding and using the Abyss. Individual researchers had their own aims, such as a cure for Mimameith or an alternative energy source to the Abyss.

Methods: The Universitas offered the king predictions drawn from the stars. In the text of the Orbits achievement namecard, it tells Irmin that two stars captured by the world's gravity will, after a long orbit, cross paths again. The namecard does not name the stars; the wiki connects it to the twin Travelers. Its alchemy worked on principles Jakob, as the wiki reports, thought neglected the foundations of the art. It also produced devices and spells, from a party trick (see Chaos Permeation below) to the instruments Tholindis used to try to hold open a gate through the Moon Marrow.

History: **Before the cataclysm.** The institute was an established, esteemed body. In their youth Hroptatyr and Eftirvit studied under Professor Mimameith there and became its leading minds. Hroptatyr rose to the presidency.

**The Abyss turn.** Irmin's research into the Abyss drew in Mimameith, whose health declined. Hroptatyr found a way to take the Authority of Death from the Crimson Moon, which could make a person immune from death, but he realised that this "blessing" was a curse of endless suffering and did not use it on his teacher. She died, and the rift with Eftirvit began. The Universitas was by then redirected to Abyssal research.

**The night of the raid.** Dainsleif gathered Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir to rescue his imprisoned brother Vedrfolnir from the palace. As the raid released Abyssal energy, monsters appeared in the Universitas, which was a nest of Abyss research. Vedrfolnir told Rerir to go there. Barricaded in the lab and without weapons to defend herself, Tholindis opened a Moon Gate and leapt into the "moon's reflection". Rerir arrived in time to see it but could not stop her.

Relations: - **King Irmin**: the direct master of the institute, whose Abyss obsession redirected its work.
- **Eclipse Dynasty**: the royal house it served. Pierro is described as having served it as a royal mage.
- **Crimson Moon Dynasty**: the Universitas studied the Crimson Moon's remains, and Tholindis was a hidden descendant of the dynasty.
- **Fatui**: Pierro, its former Vice-President, later headed the Fatui. In 7.1 Arlecchino said that whatever methods the Universitas used on the Crimson Moon were centuries old and "history", and that she cared more about the future.

- **Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah**: Hroptatyr, its President, became one of them, and so did Rerir, the fiancé of its researcher Tholindis.
- **Skirk and Surtalogi**: Surtalogi mastered the Universitas' Chaos Permeation spell (see below) and taught it to his disciple Skirk.

Reputation: In the Khaenri'ah of the story, the Universitas is spoken of as influential and as flattering its leaders. Rhinedottir said it "won't stop fawning" over Hroptatyr. Skofnungr, recalling Surtalogi's childhood in Unbounded (5.7), said he faced more criticism than the literary works of the Universitas, which only shows that the institute produced written works. Rerir, hearing of monsters in the city, feared for anyone at the Universitas because of its Abyss research.

Status as of 7.1: The Universitas Magistrorum no longer exists as a known body. Its two leaders live on as the Fatui Director Pierro and as Hroptatyr, a Sinner of Khaenri'ah whose memory was glimpsed in 7.1. Canon does not say whether the institute itself survived the cataclysm.

667.content: Hroptatyr and Eftirvit studied side by side under Professor Mimameith at the Universitas and were its brightest scholars. Hroptatyr became President and the royal mage titled "The Wise"; Eftirvit became Vice-President. When Mimameith fell ill from her work on the Abyss, Hroptatyr found a way to extract the Authority of Death from the Crimson Moon, but realised it would curse her to endless suffering and refused to use it, without telling Eftirvit why. She died, and Eftirvit grew bitter. Around the time Eftirvit brought Paimon down from Celestia, Hroptatyr summoned the Traveler's sibling. Hroptatyr later took a share of the sibling's power, became a Sinner, and gave Eftirvit a notebook of his research and a prism holding his memories before leaving. Pierro told Paimon in 7.1 that, five hundred years on, he still felt unable to step out of Hroptatyr's shadow.

668.comment: Universitas Magistrorum: Moon Marrow lab and Tholindis
668.content: The Moon Marrow lab at the Universitas studied the remains of the Crimson Moon as a possible new power source for Khaenri'ah. After Irmin shifted resources to the Abyss, Tholindis, a young researcher from a hidden branch of the Crimson Moon Dynasty, was its only remaining staff member. She found that the Moon Marrow could open a spatial gateway to a place where time runs backwards, the "moon's reflection", but could not explore it for lack of funding and technology to keep the gate open. She was engaged to Rerir. On the night of the raid, trapped by monsters, she jumped through a Moon Gate into the reflection, and her loss pushed Rerir toward joining the Five Sinners. Her fiancé's earlier role as an executioner of the Crimson Moon's descendants is told in the quest A Nation That Doesn't Exist.

669.content: Chaos Permeation was a minor spell developed by the Universitas to mock Vision wielders. A user drew on Abyssal energy to create negative pressure in reality that called up the flow of an element, producing effects like an elemental power. In Khaenri'ah it was a party trick for performances and parades, and ordinary street performers needed months of practice to shift just one element. Surtalogi, who understood Abyssal power, mastered it almost at once, cycling through all seven elements on his first attempt. He renamed it the Seven-Shifting Serpent and taught it to his disciple Skirk, who uses it to hide her Abyssal powers on Teyvat.

670.content:
Vahumana (also: Vahumana Darshan, School of Aetiology, Darshan of Aetiology, Vahumana scholars): Vahumana is one of the six Darshans (schools) of the Sumeru Akademiya. Its field is aetiology, the study of the causes and origins of things, and it covers history, sociology and other social sciences. Its colour is yellow. It is led by Sage Baladhuri.

The name comes from the Avestan Vohu Manah, "Good Mind", as the other Darshan names are drawn from the Amesha Spenta. Its emblem's mascot resembles a horse.

The receptionist Sitt sums up the Darshan with a quip: if it is not memorising facts, it is refuting rumours. She says it began with the rejection and reflection of the theories King Deshret left behind, and then became the basis of the social sciences.

Structure: Vahumana is one of six Darshans, alongside Amurta, Haravatat, Kshahrewar, Rtawahist and Spantamad. Each has a Sage at its head, and the six Sages sit together in the Akademiya's leadership. Scholars carry ranks such as Herbad (Yarshater is a Vahumana Herbad) and Professor (Manetho is a Vahumana professor in the quest Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion). Students normally take an entrance exam that decides which Darshans they are eligible for.

The Akademiya's school colours mark each Darshan, and Vahumana's is yellow. A scholar's Darshan shapes their approach even in a casual argument. In an open-world exchange outside the House of Daena, the Vahumana researcher Khaldun and a Haravatat scholar, Yavanani, trade jibes about each other's methods, and Yavanani calls the sociological approach to history "putting the cart before the horse".

Leadership: Baladhuri is the current Vahumana Sage.

He is a kind, gentle scholar, tall, with an elaborate stone-grey beard he is proud of. He took office before Azar fell from power. He and Naphis of Amurta opposed the Akademiya's secret collaboration with the Fatui and were locked up by the other four Sages until the conspiracy collapsed. Tighnari calls him "Uncle Baladhuri", which shows a personal bond. Baladhuri has a wife and a young daughter and is devoted to them. He teaches students such as Khaldun and, in Where Flowers Awaken (6.6), stays with them through the city's crisis.

In A Divergence Leading to Oneself (6.6), Naphis introduces the six sitting Sages: Baladhuri and herself as the old guard, and four who took office after Azar's clique fell, among them Alkindi of Spantamad, Firnas of Kshahrewar and Shakir of Rtawahist. Baladhuri and Tighnari greet each other warmly there. In the As All Falls to Emptiness story, Baladhuri helps during the crisis with his historical knowledge.

Members: Known Vahumana scholars include the following.
- Baladhuri: the Sage.
- Khaldun: a researcher and Baladhuri's student.
- Yarshater: a Herbad who helped translate the Scroll of Streaming Song.
- Manetho: a professor named in a Sumeru quest.
- Nefer: assigned here as a student (see history), now listed as a former member.
- Vikram: mentioned by NPCs as one of the candidates for Grand Conservator.

Other named members are Ebert, a researcher who reviewed and rated the films in a book about Fontaine's cinema, and Siraj, a scholar with a thesis on a unified "collective consciousness" who was jailed under Azar's regime for activities the Akademiya deemed illegal. Raed was a Vahumana researcher who led an expedition into the Great Red Sand and was secretly selling relics on the black market.

Methods: Vahumana scholars study history and society. They mount expeditions to ruins and bring artefacts back for study. They also translate old documents, often with the Haravatat, who handle language and runes. Cooperation has its edges: in the Scroll of Streaming Song, a Haravatat Herbad (Tafazzoli) added footnotes correcting the Vahumana translators, and the Vahumana Herbad Yarshater replied in the margin that he had never been told. The wiki infers these remarks are annotations, since the House of Daena lets borrowers annotate books.

Applied work reaches the city. Furnishing descriptions say that Vahumana students favour the topic of time-sensitive commodities, and their advice has helped fruit and vegetable sellers at the Grand Bazaar waste less and save Mora. They also design products with Amurta scholars to address food preservation and overfishing.

History: Sitt places the roots of Vahumana in the reaction to King Deshret's remaining theories, and it later grew into the basis for the social sciences. Nothing more precise about its founding is stated.

Under Grand Sage Azar, desertfolk accepted into the Akademiya were assigned to Vahumana automatically and did not get the entrance exam that other students took. Nefer's first character story shows a scholar telling her this, with Professor Cyrus objecting and being warned that Azar's circle would make trouble for him. After Azar was exiled, the Darshan, which had been declining, became more popular, as Nefer says in a voice-over.

Relations: - **Haravatat**: the nearest neighbour in translation work. They collaborate and also criticise each other's methods.
- **Amurta**: Naphis and Baladhuri were allies against the Akademiya's secret plans, and the two Darshans co-design food-preservation products.
- **Sumeru Akademiya**: Vahumana is one of its six schools, and its Sage sits among the Sages.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Vahumana is active under Baladhuri.

No Vahumana-specific story developments were found in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content checked, apart from Baladhuri's appearances in the Sumeru section of the 6.6 Archon Quest (Where Flowers Awaken, A Divergence Leading to Oneself). The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests take place in Snezhnaya.

671.content: Baladhuri is the Sage of Vahumana, a kind man who opposed the Akademiya's deal with the Fatui and was imprisoned for it. He is a devoted husband and father with a prized beard, and Tighnari calls him Uncle. He is a teacher first, and stays with his students through the 6.6 crisis.

672.content: A three-volume book collection in the House of Daena. Vahumana researchers recovered torn pages from desert ruins and translated them. The Haravatat Herbad Tafazzoli and the Vahumana Herbad Yarshater trade footnotes about mistranslations and about what each knew while they worked together. It is a small example of scholarly rivalry between the two Darshans.

673.content: As a student from the desert, Nefer was assigned to Vahumana without sitting the entrance exam, a rule that held during Azar's time. Cyrus objected on principle that anyone admitted had a right to take the test. She says in a voice-over that Vahumana grew popular again after Azar's exile. Nefer is listed as a former member.

674.content:
Voynich Guild (also: the Voynich Guild, Voynich): The Voynich Guild is a commerce guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai, and one of the most powerful forces in the region. With no government in Nasha Town, it is the nearest thing to a regulator. It manages trade deals, imports and exports, business certificates and many disputes.

Nefer, owner of the Curatorium of Secrets, is a member, and the Curatorium's headquarters stands directly behind the Guild's. Its representative in the Nod-Krai League is Tarno.

Structure: No guildmaster, charter or rank structure is given in canon. Tarno is the manager of its Nasha Town souvenir outlet. According to Zinaida's intel text, the Guild also hired Zinaida, a former Seahook Gang member, as a covert bodyguard for Manez, the port supervisor. The Guild keeps a bulletin board in Nasha Town for business notices.

The bulletin board's welcome note says the Guild created the board so that public opinion could be heard in an authoritative and convenient way, with no restriction on the content or format of posts. A disclaimer says the Guild accepts no legal or financial liability for what is posted and offers no mediation of its own for disputes arising from the board.

Leadership: Leadership is unnamed. After the crisis in Nod-Krai, Tarno, the outlet manager, became the Guild's representative in the League. He hosted the League's opening ceremony and gave its welcome address in that role.

In his speech, Tarno spoke of the unity and cooperation learned from the crisis and of sailing toward prosperity, freedom and hope. The wiki lists Nefer as a Guild member, with no stated rank. The story never says who chose Tarno, and Illuga privately wonders whether Tarno was pushed onto the stage by bigger names.

Members: Known members and staff are Nefer, who is also the owner of the Curatorium of Secrets, and Tarno, listed as a "Voynich Guild" employee. The Guild issues certifications: Sarin says a bounty hunter lost his Guild certification over his old habits (limited-time event, Clink Clank Clash).

A man named Ashvapati joined the Guild during the 6.5 trade-expo event with a private agenda and later admitted that he had nearly ruined its reputation (limited-time event).

Goals: The Guild's stated aim, in its bulletin-board announcement, is to promote economic activity in Nasha Town. It hopes people will find endless business opportunities there.

Beyond trade, the Guild appears interested in technology. It developed a hovering daybed using artifacts from the pioneering age, though it has been unable to fully reverse-engineer the original and the daybed remains somewhat unstable.

Methods: The Guild issues business certificates, manages trade deals, handles imports and exports, and investigates and resolves disputes when its name is called in. A merchant who was robbed just before reaching the city was told to go to the Guild. They brought back his stolen goods and bought them all, in a story the merchant told as an example of the Guild's reach (limited web event, 2024).

The Guild also enforces order at its own events. At the annual Nod-Krai Trade Expo, which it hosts, violence is forbidden. Outside authorities cannot make arrests inside the venue without breaking the Guild's rule, so they act outside it (limited-time event, 6.5).

History: Canon gives no founding history. The Guild first appears in the Marvelous Merchandise web event (2024), where a traveling seller describes Nod-Krai as a wild place that plays by its own rules and the Guild as the strongest force in the area. Its own members first appear in 6.0 (Luna I).

In a mail dated 2025-08-26, sent before the Traveler's trip to Nod-Krai, Ningguang advised the Traveler that the Voynich Guild was a significant piece on Nod-Krai's chessboard and an accord with it might be worth considering. In 6.0 the Moonchanter Lauma sought a joint investigation with the Guild after the Moon Marrow was stolen. After the True Moon crisis (6.3), the Guild took a seat in the newly formed League.

Relations: **Curatorium of Secrets:** closely linked, since Nefer is a member and the two headquarters are back to back. **Frostmoon Scions:** Lauma approached the Guild for a joint investigation of the stolen Moon Marrow. **League:** Tarno represents the Guild. **Others:** the Guild is one of several factions in Nasha Town's power balance, alongside the Curatorium, Speranza and the Fatui.

The sources checked say nothing definite about how the Guild deals with the Fatui or the Adventurers' Guild. Tarno speaks warmly of the League's ideals of unity, suggesting the Guild supports it.

Reputation: Liben was told it is the strongest force in the area, and his experience bore that out. Ningguang considers it a significant player worth cultivating.

Its bulletin board carries a blunt liability disclaimer. In Clink Clank Clash a bounty hunter is said to have lost his certification, which suggests the Guild enforces its standards.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Voynich Guild remains Nasha Town's leading merchant body, with Tarno speaking for it in the League.

The sources checked show no Voynich Guild story content in 7.0 or 7.1.

675.content: Tarno is a manager at the Voynich Guild's Nasha Town outlet, which runs the souvenir shop. After the crisis in Nod-Krai he became the Guild's representative in the League and hosted its opening ceremony. He greets visitors in a friendly, helpful way and offers whatever help he can. His wiki profile has no further background.

676.content: The Nod-Krai Trade Expo is an annual event hosted by the Voynich Guild in Nasha Town. In the Where Waves Meet the Reef event (6.5, April to May 2026), Nefer asks the Traveler to help Jahoda handle VIP guests. Guests include Beidou, captain of the Crux fleet, and Navia, who leads an underworld organisation. The Guild forbids violence at the venue, so officials from Liyue and Fontaine had to wait before arresting an arms syndicate that had taken an interest in the expo. Nefer refuses to let customers be seized at the expo, so Chevreuse notes that only deals made through the expo are protected; Nefer agrees she cannot interfere outside it, on condition that the Traveler takes part in the operation.

677.content: During the Marvelous Merchandise web event (November 2024), a seller named Liben describes his trip to Nod-Krai. He was robbed by vagrants before even entering Nasha Town, where he found no courts of law or Knights of Favonius. Someone told him to visit the Voynich Guild, the strongest force in the area. The Guild recovered his goods and then bought everything from him. He was robbed again on the way out.

678.content:
Wanderer's Troupe (also: Swordsman's Troupe, the Wanderer's Troupe, Wanderers' Troupe): The Wanderer's Troupe, also called the Swordsman's Troupe, was a group of travelling musicians who were also skilled fighters. A thousand years ago they wandered across Teyvat, then ended their journey in Mondstadt, where they stormed the city to overthrow its tyrannical aristocracy. They failed, and the troupe broke up, but its memory lives on in artifact and weapon lore and in the people it inspired.

Its four known members were the Conductor, the Sojourner (a harpist), the Dawnlight Swordswoman and Kreuzlied. They owned no sheet music, played swords for flutes and bows for harps, and performed for friends and for foes alike. The troupe's story is told only through item text and a few related books, so details are sparse and its members are known by titles rather than names.

Members: - **The Conductor**: the leader. He kept a book of the troupe's journeys called The Widsith and died holding it.
- **The Sojourner (the harpist)**: a privileged man from Fontaine who left home to wander. A skilled archer, he wielded The Stringless, a harp that was also a bow.
- **The Dawnlight Swordswoman (the Sword Dancer)**: wielder of The Flute, a sword that sang as she swung it. Her origin is unknown.
- **Kreuzlied**: a disowned member of the Lawrence Clan and the last to join. He carried The Bell, a greatsword with a clock in it.

The meeting order was: the Conductor and the Sojourner first, then the Dawnlight Swordswoman, then Kreuzlied. It is unknown whether the troupe had other members. Chronologically it grew by chance meetings, and a tavern scene in the Goblet of the Sojourner lore has the harpist introducing a young woman he had met to his companions.

Goals: The troupe set out to perform and to see the world, and its members decided there was so much to sing about that they wrote their journey down in The Widsith. Once in Mondstadt, they learned how the aristocracy treated the people and decided to end its rule by force.

Methods: Music and combat were one skill. The Flute made a flute-like sound depending on its swing angle, The Stringless fired arrows that followed its tune, and The Bell's clockwork gave the troupe a combat rhythm. The harpist reportedly lured birds with his harp and shot them down, and never looked at the sky while playing, which one companion read as the hunter's mercy and others read as arrogance. Artifact lore says the troupe's performances had two audiences, friends and foes, and that they once entered Mare Jivari to perform for their enemies.

History: **Wandering.** The troupe travelled all over Teyvat and through harsh lands such as the desert and the burning Mare Jivari. Members came from many places. **Arrival in Mondstadt.** Their journey ended in Mondstadt around the time of Ludi Harpastum. The harpist fell in love with a woman who had been chosen as the Harpastum maiden, the one who would be claimed by a member of the tyrannical Lawrence Clan. **The uprising.** The troupe stormed Mondstadt's city to overthrow the aristocracy. It failed: the Conductor and the Sojourner died in the fighting, the Sojourner covering his friends' retreat and playing until he ran out of songs and arrows. The Dawnlight Swordswoman was enslaved as a gladiator. Kreuzlied was left alive because of his privileged birth, and what punishment he received was never made public.

**Aftermath.** The troupe broke up. In item lore, the Sojourner's harp was stripped of its strings, The Bell was soaked in acid, and The Flute was buried. The Dawnlight Swordswoman kept singing of freedom as a gladiator and eventually died in the arena. A young squire, later the Dawn Knight Ragnvindr, watched her final fight and was moved. He befriended her, buried her with her sword, and took the title Dawn Knight in homage to her name. Kreuzlied went on to found a secret society against the aristocracy and helped Vennessa when she rebelled. The Widsith's own text says the troupe is nearly forgotten but that the spirit of resistance still runs in Mondstadters.

Relations: - **Mondstadt Aristocracy and Lawrence Clan**: the troupe's enemies. Kreuzlied was himself born a Lawrence.
- **Ragnvindr**: inspired by the Dawnlight Swordswoman, he became the Dawn Knight and turned against the corrupt nobles.
- **Vennessa**: aided by Kreuzlied's society when she rebelled.

- **Fontaine**: the harpist's homeland. Item lore says the ladies of the Court of Fontaine mourned when he left without a farewell.

Reputation: The troupe is largely forgotten. The Widsith's lore says the memory of the rebellion faded, yet the spirit of resistance remains. Item lore treats it with fondness: the troupe's end is mourned, and the dying notes of its instruments are described as the last sound it made.
