Status as of 7.1: The troupe is long gone. Nothing in canon through 7.1 shows its members returning, though the Wanderer's Troupe weapons and artifacts survive in the world.

No story content about the troupe was found for 6.0 to 7.1.

679.comment: Wanderer's Troupe: The Sojourner's love story
679.content: The harpist, who came from Fontaine and was well loved by the ladies of its Court, left home to follow a wandering life and seek his destiny. In Mondstadt, by a lake, he met a stern, unsmiling maiden who was to be offered up as the Ludi Harpastum maiden of the Lawrence nobles. Item lore records his promise to break her chains and see her smile once. When the uprising came, he fired his last arrow for his comrades, for freedom and against the nobles who had taken her joy. He died unnamed in a foreign land, regretting only that he never sang another love song. Artifact lore (Feather of Homecoming) notes that the Mondstadt sky reminded him of his homeland. The wiki notes that "Sojourner" is an unofficial name.

680.content: She wielded the sword The Flute and moved to music, "beautiful as the light on water, elegant as the chirping lark". After the failed uprising she was made a gladiator but still sang of freedom. Ballads of the Squire quotes her challenging a young Ragnvindr about the lives he placed on a pedestal, asking whether he had not once known freedom. Ragnvindr watched her last fight, buried her with her sword and named himself the Dawn Knight after her title.

681.content: The Widsith is the troupe's travel journal. The members had no sheet music and turned the notes they played into words. The Conductor held it tightly even in death. The weapon of the same name is a catalyst. Its text says the troupe's song was an anthem of rebellion and that their last act was an attempt to storm the city and sentence its rulers.

682.comment: Wanderer's Troupe: The Bell and Kreuzlied
682.content: Kreuzlied, a Lawrence who became the troupe's outcast member, wielded a greatsword with a clock in it. Its ticking gave the troupe a combat rhythm, and its text calls its strike the toll of the bell of judgment. After the troupe's defeat the weapon was soaked in acid and rusted. Kreuzlied avoided harsh punishment because of his birth, and later founded a secret society to carry on his companions' work.

683.content:
Wangsheng Funeral Parlor (also: Wangsheng, Wangsheng Parlor, Hall of Rebirth, Wangsheng-tang): The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is the funeral house of Liyue Harbor, on Feiyun Slope. It arranges burials, cremations and memorial rites for the dead of every rank, and it also performs the rites that send off adepti. It is run by the Hu family, which has held the Directorship for 77 generations. The current Director is Hu Tao, and Zhongli works there as consultant. The parlour also keeps a duty most people never see: watching the border between life and death, and burning away the fetor that leaks across it.

In Liyue, people tend not to talk to Wangsheng staff or to dwell on what they do. The parlour treats that as part of the job, and its stated client philosophy is that everyone who departs, whatever their wealth or standing, deserves a ceremony that honours them.

The parlour began, by the wiki's account, as something closer to a doctor's office, and grew into a funeral house over time. Its Chinese name, 往生堂 (Wǎngshēng-táng), is rendered "Hall of Rebirth" in the wiki's translation.

Structure: The head is the Director, a title passed down the Hu family; Hu Tao is the 77th. Under her are undertakers who carry out ceremonies and prepare burials and cremations. The wiki lists the Ferrylady and Meng among them. Hu Tao also invites consultants from different trades to lecture the undertakers once the parlour closes each day, so that funeral practice is taught as a body of knowledge, not as habit. Zhongli is the most revered of these lecturers. Commissions are taken at a board outside the door, where clients write requests on blank wooden tiles and slide them under the door.

Hu Tao is said to know the parlour's rules by heart. Funerals follow strict steps (a wake, a burial, a memorial plaque), but she instructs her undertakers to follow clients' wishes: some want a quiet ceremony, some a lively one, and wealthy clients may want something grand. The Director personally leads the undertakers through lamp-lit alleys when a funeral procession goes out, and that is the one time her dignified side comes forward.

Leadership: Hu Tao is the 77th Director. She is a cheerful, eccentric young woman who treats the work seriously beneath the jokes. Zhongli is the parlour's consultant; Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned while trusting him more than anyone else.

Before her came Old Hu, the 75th Director and her grandfather, and Hu Tao's father, the 76th. Her great-uncle, Baizhu's master, was Old Hu's younger brother, according to the wiki. Zhongli handles ceremonies that rely on exact tradition. His profile says Hu Tao asks him to help with the rites for sending adepti away, because the tradition now exists only in texts and almost nobody alive has seen it performed.

Hu Tao took over the Directorship young, after the Wuwang Hill disaster killed her father and, soon afterwards, her grandfather. Her father was considered one of the family's finest ritualists. Zhongli's profile calls Hu Tao the current owner of the parlour and himself a friend in more or less the same business, and the wiki records that he became its consultant after the Rite of Descension.

Members: - **Hu Tao**: 77th Director.
- **Zhongli**: consultant who lectures the undertakers on rites and etiquette. In the Archon Quest Tartaglia introduces him to the Traveler as consultant to "an organization known as Wangsheng" and a trusted associate of the Fatui.
- **The Ferrylady**: an undertaker who stands outside the parlour at night. She prepares ashes silently while families stay shut in their rooms, and she does not speak to the bereaved, following old custom.
- **Meng**: a newer undertaker who joined, according to the story quest, so he could ask the Director to search for his dead childhood friend Big G.
- **Past Directors**: Old Hu (75th) and Hu Tao's father (76th), both dead.

The Ferrylady is unused to being addressed; if the Traveler hints they are "something else", she takes them for a lost soul and bids them go into the light. Her title evokes the ferryman who carries the dead across the water, a comparison the wiki notes. Meng is described in the story quest as a nervous newcomer who at first takes the Traveler and Paimon for ghosts; after Big G's farewell Hu Tao grants him unpaid time off to process his grief.

Goals: Two commitments are named. First, to give everyone who dies a ceremony that honours them, regardless of wealth or rank; this is described as the parlour's client service philosophy. Second, to keep the balance between life and death in Liyue: monitoring its "border", making sure death does not spill out, and burning off any fetor growths that appear. Hu Tao also wants the business to grow, and invents marketing schemes with that in mind, though they tend to backfire.

Methods: Funerals follow traditional steps: a wake, burial, a memorial plaque, cremation where requested. Hu Tao's own approach is flexible about style but strict about respect. The parlour's secret technique is the Art of Homa, which purifies the border between life and death and burns away fetor. Practitioners use Homa altars and the Staff of Homa. Hu Tao says doing it right takes great focus and no hesitation in the face of death; a faulty performance can shorten the caster's life or even kill them at once, depending on how much fetor they take in.

Hu Tao's repertoire includes showmanship as well as ritual. In the story quest she stages an "exorcism" for a worried client, using a Ley Line Monolith as a prop; hilichurls drawn to it prove real, and she later tells him it was a prank and that he was never cursed. She explains that frightened people have to be convinced with something tangible, by making a show of destroying the bogeyman they believe in. For adepti farewells, the parlour follows ancient protocols on costume, timing, place, items, weather, length of ceremony and the size and make-up of the audience.

History: **Origin.** By the parlour's own account, after the Archon War the Yaksha accumulated karma while fighting vengeful gods, and part of it became a plague that swept Liyue. Frightened people took it for a divine curse. A few realised the plague could be stopped by purifying the air and burning the infected dead; they became the parlour's founders, and after many years the plague ended. Since then their successors have preserved the balance between life and death.

**Recent generations.** Old Hu and Hu Tao's father were the 75th and 76th Directors. Ten years before the Traveler arrived, the two went to Wuwang Hill to burn away a runaway growth of fetor. Her father, unable to let go of his regrets, faltered at the last moment and died on the spot. Old Hu contained the damage, but the fetor he absorbed killed him soon afterwards, before he was sixty. The nearby village was abandoned and the hill changed permanently. Hu Tao succeeded them.

**Hu Tao's early life.** Hu Tao's profile says she began living at the parlour at eight and learned funeral etiquette there. After Old Hu's funeral she searched for his spirit at Wuwang Hill and found no trace; she concluded he had already passed on because he died without regrets, and was inspired by that to live fully. When she returned home she found she had received a Pyro Vision. In the story quest she says that on her many visits to the border she has never seen any former Director there, so she knows they all died without regrets.

**Zhongli joins.** After staging his own death at the Rite of Descension, Zhongli became the parlour's consultant. He had no funds of his own and, per the wiki, often relies on the parlour or Tartaglia to pay his way.

**Papilio Charontis (1.3).** In the story quest, the Traveler helps Hu Tao and Meng deal with Meng's lost friend Big G. The party goes into the border, Big G says farewell and moves on, and Meng is given leave. The quest is also where Hu Tao gives the short history of the plague.

Relations: - **Fatui**: Tartaglia says the Fatui are glad to do business with "friends who walk in the shadows", and that the parlour ostensibly does not take part in assassination. The relationship is never explained.
- **Liyue Qixing and the Ministry of Civil Affairs**: they work with Hu Tao when the border is threatened; in Springtime Charms Hu Tao informed the Ministry about the fetor leaks.
- **Adepti**: the parlour keeps the rites for sending adepti off, and the Art of Homa traces to the Eight Adepts.
- **Bubu Pharmacy**: Baizhu and Hu Tao disagree about prolonging life, and Hu Tao once tried repeatedly to cremate Qiqi, who is a zombie, until Baizhu stopped her.

Reputation: Liyue's people are polite but wary of the parlour. It is generally not customary to speak to its staff, who are associated with death. Since Hu Tao took over, her tactful ceremonies have changed some superstitious people's attitudes toward funerals. She herself is better known in Liyue Harbor as an eccentric and a poet than as Director.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the parlour is active. Hu Tao is Director and Zhongli remains consultant. Hu Tao appears in the 6.3 (Luna IV) Lantern Rite story with her friends, but no story about the parlour itself was found for 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya).

The most recent major Wangsheng story is the 5.3 Springtime Charms event, a limited-time event whose ritual Hu Tao survived. The Ferrylady, Meng and the other undertakers continue to serve.

684.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Hu Tao as Director
684.content: Hu Tao is the parlour's 77th Director. See her own entry for biography and personality. In the parlour she leads the undertakers through funeral processions and decides how each ceremony will go, and she is the one who takes parties into the border to speak with the dead. Her unusual approach, equal parts showmanship and solemnity, is described in the parlour's methods.

685.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Zhongli, Wangsheng consultant
685.content: Zhongli is the parlour's consultant. He teaches the undertakers and supplies the exact customs of rites, especially ceremonies for sending adepti off. Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned, yet trusts him most. He joined after staging his death as Rex Lapis. His own entry carries the full story.

686.content: The Ferrylady is an undertaker, found outside the parlour at night. She prepares burials and cremations and, by old custom, does not speak to the families of the dead. Strangers who speak to her surprise her, and she may take them for lost souls. During Springtime Charms she is the person people ask about Hu Tao's whereabouts. The wiki notes her name may refer to Charon.

687.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Meng and Big G
687.content: Meng is a newer undertaker who joined the parlour to ask Hu Tao to find his childhood friend Big G, who died in an accident. With the Traveler's help, Hu Tao takes Meng and Big G into the border, where Big G says goodbye and moves on. Meng takes unpaid leave afterwards. The story is part of Hu Tao's story quest.

688.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Art of Homa and fetor
688.content:
Fetor is the energy that leaks out when the border between life and death is disturbed. It ages the living, causes weakness and coma, and can kill; adepti can see it and humans generally cannot. The parlour's secret Art of Homa burns it away with altars and the Staff of Homa, and demands total focus. Minor leaks are routine for the parlour. A major leak may require purifying the whole border, which is what happened in Springtime Charms.

The first user of the technique was the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame, one of the Eight Adepts, who sacrificed herself in the Sanctification of Tao Dou. Wuwang Kid passed her arts to the founders of the parlour. Qiqi, being a zombie, is somewhat resistant to fetor.

689.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Border between life and death
689.content:
The "border" is a place most people never know exists, reached from Wuwang Hill. Ley Lines run wild there, and the dead who are unwilling or unable to leave linger. Hu Tao holds farewell ceremonies there and asks the dead questions. The parlour monitors it so that death does not spill out. Visitors must keep calm and follow Hu Tao's lead.

A disturbance at the border ten years before the Traveler's arrival led to the deaths of the 76th and 75th Directors. A larger one in Springtime Charms required a ritual across Liyue's Ley Lines.

690.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Wuwang Hill disaster
690.content: According to Springtime Charms, a limited-time event, ten years before the Traveler's arrival Old Hu and his son went to Wuwang Hill to burn away a runaway fetor growth. Hu Tao's father, unable to let go of his regrets, faltered and was killed instantly. Old Hu contained the damage but died soon afterwards. A nearby village was abandoned and the hill changed permanently. Hu Tao took over as Director.

691.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Springtime Charms ritual
691.content: In the limited-time event Springtime Charms (5.3), Hu Tao proposed purifying a damaged stretch of the border with the Art of Homa, using the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method to carry the rite across Liyue's Ley Lines. Eight gates had overseers: Keqing (Life), Hu Tao (Death), Qiqi and Baizhu (Repose), Ganyu (Concealment), Ningguang and Lan Yan (Initiation), Xiao (Terrain), Beidou and the Crux (Fright), and Yelan (Injury). Lan Yan made rattan dolls of Hu Tao to share the burden of the fetor. Hu Tao took the Gate of Death and was overcome, and the Traveler took her place.

692.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Wangsheng and the Fatui
692.content: In Archon Quest Chapter I Act II, Tartaglia introduces Zhongli as consultant to Wangsheng and as a trusted Fatui associate, saying the parlour understands discretion and that the Fatui are glad to do business with friends who walk in the shadows. He adds that the parlour ostensibly does not do assassinations and does not finish the thought. Nothing more is established; the wiki reports that the Millelith later suspected Hu Tao of collaboration and dropped the matter.

693.comment: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor: Commission board and special offers
693.content: Outside the parlour hangs a board of wooden tiles. Clients write their commission on a tile and slide it under the door. During Hu Tao's story quest, her advertising scheme appears on the back of each tile as a "buy one get one free" offer for whoever holds it.

694.content:
Watatsumi Army (also: Watatsumi Troops, the Resistance, Sangonomiya Rebels, Sangonomiya troops, Sangonomiya Samurai, Watatsumi forces): The Watatsumi Army, also called the Resistance, is the armed force of Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. It was raised against the Vision Hunt Decree and the Shogunate's Sakoku order and is led by Sangonomiya Kokomi, the island's Divine Priestess, with General Gorou commanding in the field. Its soldiers are called Sangonomiya samurai or troops, and the Shogunate calls them rebels. The decree is now abolished, so the army works as peacekeepers and rebuilders.

Its ranks include people who had lost their Visions, people who feared losing them, and people who simply opposed the decree, Visions or not. The Resistance also hid those unwilling to fight the Shogun's forces. Its bases are Watatsumi Island, where the Sangonomiya Shrine stands, and Fort Fujitou on Yashiori Island.

Structure: The army is organised into small numbered units named after fish: Herring, Stingray, Swordfish and Gorgasia. Each is divided into numbered squads (Herring I, Swordfish II, Gorgasia II and so on). Kokomi sits at the top, Gorou is general, and officers such as Kaida Ryouma hold camps like Fort Fujitou. Rank-and-file soldiers are Sangonomiya samurai in a standard uniform based on the ashigaru foot-soldier. It is red and white, with the Sangonomiya crest on the back and on the right shoulder guard, and soldiers such as Nathan carry a cross-bladed spear (juumonji yari). The Traveler was made captain of Swordfish II.

Named squads and officers: Teppei, the first captain of Herring I (until his death in Chapter II); Yabe of Stingray III; Ueno, a provisional squad leader of Swordfish I who appears during a limited-time event; Koutoku, Kaneda, Shikishima and Yoshihisa of Swordfish II; and Gorou, who rose from Gorgasia II member to its captain. Kokomi governs through detailed written directives, and soldiers are expected to follow them. She also issues temporary decrees for island affairs, such as one against price gouging. Support staff, workers and smiths are attached to the camps. One example is the blacksmith Miyazaki Saburou at Fort Fujitou.

Leadership: Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Divine Priestess, is the supreme leader. She is a brilliant strategist who plans for every scenario in advance. General Gorou, who is open-hearted and trusted by his troops, leads the soldiers on the battlefield.

Kokomi inherited the Priestess role through the Sangonomiya bloodline. It passes on the will of the dead god Orobashi in a mortal body, to defend Watatsumi Island. She has read military treatises since childhood, favours winning wars at the lowest cost by shaping the larger strategic situation, and in her story quest admits privately that she never wanted to be a leader, though her bloodline made it inevitable. The islanders say "Things will be alright as long as Her Excellency is here." Gorou came up through the ranks. In one crisis his unit's captain fell, and he led a feint that held the line for days until Kokomi's own relief force arrived. That earned him command of Gorgasia II and later the generalship. He is humble and straightforward. His troops call him the "ever-victorious pointy-eared general," and he has a short temper in the heat of battle.

Kokomi's directives are often long because she predicts so many scenarios. Gorou's task is to choose the right one in the moment, and he believes he will internalise her ideas in time. She once told him that materiel, supplies and wages are what an army depends on, so he began explaining weapon upkeep personally and watching the granaries to prevent illegal deductions. Gorou leads from the front and values his own life less than his soldiers', as his story puts it. Kokomi, by contrast, tires from social duties and uses a private "energy" measure to decide when to retreat into a book. She even leaves a directive for her own absences, so a guard at the shrine knows where to send visitors.

Members: Notable members: Kaida Ryouma, an officer at Fort Fujitou who once worked for the Kujou Clan on Narukami Island and who remembers the Kujou brothers as sympathetic to commoners; Teppei, a logistician turned front-line captain; and many named samurai, including Moriguchi, Takahashi, Denjirou, Arisawa and Koutoku. Kaedehara Kazuha was sheltered by the Resistance before leaving Inazuma to join the Crux. Beidou and Kazuha appeared at the battle of Nazuchi Beach as mercenary reinforcements that Kokomi brought.

Others include the blacksmith Miyazaki Saburou and the workers Yuuzou and Sumi at Fort Fujitou. Yoshihisa is a veteran of Swordfish II. Kouzen, Tsuneo and Uchimura appear in Kokomi's story quest. Nathan appeared to be a foreign volunteer from Mondstadt but was a Fatui infiltrator; he vanishes after the Delusion quest, and in the world quest Clean House the shrine maiden Shizuru says he tried to flee but was caught and thrown into a cell.

Goals: During the war the army's aim was to resist the Vision Hunt Decree and to protect Watatsumi Island and its people. It also opposed the Sakoku Decree, which was imposed at the same time. Kokomi had her own aim as well, which was to win in a way that kept costs low. After the war the army's aims are to keep the peace, rebuild the island's economy, and root out Fatui remnants.

Methods: The army was outnumbered and short of materiel, so it relied on Kokomi's planning, defensive lines, ambushes and morale. A "fight of honour," a ceremonial contest between each side's best fighter that Kujou Sara proposed, was accepted at Nazuchi Beach. Gorou explains that a win in such a contest can steady a weaker side's nerve. Kokomi also brought mercenary reinforcements to turn that battle. Kokomi's tactics, in the army's own account, rely on forcing the opponent to give up rather than on bloody victories.

History: **Before the war.** Watatsumi Island's people once lived in Enkanomiya under the sea, until their god Orobashi lifted them to the surface. The Electro Archon slew Orobashi in the Archon War, leaving a skeleton and resentment that gave rise to the Tatarigami. Relations between Watatsumi Island and Narukami Island have been poor since. The island's military tradition is carried by the Sangonomiya bloodline, whose heir is the Divine Priestess.

**The war.** The Vision Hunt Decree was issued about a year before the Traveler reaches Inazuma, with the Tenryou Commission enforcing it. The Watatsumi Army declared war on the Shogunate, which fought back with the Shogun's Army under Kujou Sara. The Fatui secretly fed the conflict in order to build a market for Delusions.

**Joining the Traveler.** In Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow, Thoma sends the Traveler to the Resistance after the Vision Hunt Ceremony. They rescue Teppei, meet Gorou at Fort Fujitou, join the defence against Sara, and are invited by Kokomi to Watatsumi Island. She makes them captain of Swordfish II.

Relations: - **Inazuma Shogunate and the Shogun's Army**: former enemies. The Shogunate called the army "Sangonomiya Rebels." Peace talks followed the decree's end, and relations are warming. Gorou now visits Narukami Island often.
- **Tenryou Commission**: enforced the decree and led the war. Kujou Sara represented it in the peace talks.
- **Kanjou Commission**: Crystal Marrow it collected was used to make the Delusions.
- **Fatui**: secretly armed the Resistance with Delusions and infiltrated it with Nathan. Fatui camps and ships remained on Watatsumi Island afterwards.
- **Yae Miko and the Grand Narukami Shrine**: Miko trained the Traveler and helped bring down the Shogun's puppet rule. She later enlisted Gorou to write an advice column for her publishing house.
- **Kamisato Clan and Yashiro Commission**: neutral, but Thoma pointed the Traveler to the Resistance and the clan arranged the venue for the peace talks.

Reputation: Among the islanders the army is deeply trusted, and Kokomi's name is a byword for reassurance. Gorou is beloved by his men, and even Shogunate warriors repeat his "ever-victorious" nickname. The Shogunate treated it as a rebel force during the war.

Status as of 7.1: The Vision Hunt Decree has been repealed and the Watatsumi Army no longer fights the Shogunate. It serves as peacekeepers and helps the island recover, while still clearing out Fatui remnants.

Peace talks with the Tenryou Commission followed, and Kokomi created a new corps for island defence. No new Watatsumi Army story was found in 6.0 to 7.1.

695.content: Swordfish II is a special operations unit that Kokomi gives the Traveler to captain in Sword, Fish, Resistance. Members named in canon are Koutoku (a former provisional squad leader), Kaneda, Shikishima and Yoshihisa. The unit investigates the disappearance of supplies near Fort Mumei while staying at Bourou Village. In the Reunion anecdote, the members still call the Traveler their captain and invite them to a bonfire party.

696.content: Fort Fujitou is the Resistance camp on Yashiori Island. Kaida Ryouma is its officer, and workers and a blacksmith live there. Teppei brings the Traveler there to meet Gorou, and the camp is the base from which the fight against Sara's troops is organised. After Kokomi's story quest the camp's background soldiers withdraw.

697.content: Teppei was a logistics officer who wanted to make a name for himself. He guides the Traveler to the Resistance and becomes captain of Herring I. Fatui supporters gave him a "secret weapon" that was really a Delusion. It drained his life, and he died rapidly aged. Kokomi ordered all use stopped afterwards.

698.comment: Watatsumi Army: Nathan the Fatui mole
698.content: Nathan claimed to be a Mondstadt volunteer sympathetic to the cause. A notice in the Delusion factory shows he was a Fatui infiltrator. His job was to sabotage the Resistance and prolong the war. He disappears from Fort Fujitou after the Delusion quest. In the world quest Clean House (2.2), Shizuru of Sangonomiya Shrine says he tried to escape but was punished and imprisoned, and the Traveler recovers a report he had written for the Fatui.

699.comment: Watatsumi Army: Battle of Nazuchi Beach
699.content: Kujou Sara arrives at Nazuchi Beach to take the Traveler, offering a fight of honour. The Traveler wins the contests and the two sides clash. The Shogun's Army starts to prevail until Kokomi arrives with mercenaries including Beidou and Kazuha, and Sara retreats.

700.content:
Yae Publishing House (also: Yae-dou): Yae Publishing House is a light-novel publisher and bookshop in Inazuma City. Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, founded it and is its editor-in-chief. She started it, by her own account, because she wanted more entertaining light novels to read. Its flagship event is the periodic "This Novel Is Amazing!" writing contest, and its books are read well beyond Inazuma.

The ground floor is a shop where the house sells its own titles. Editors, authors and illustrators work under Miko, who is feared and relied on in equal measure.

Structure: Miko is boss, founder and editor-in-chief. Under her are editors who each manage particular authors, such as Kuroda (executive editor and shopkeeper, who handles Chang the Ninth), Shigeru (Junkichi's editor), Aratani (organises the writing contest and runs author correspondence) and Onodera (organises release events). Authors write under pen names more often than not. The shop on the ground floor sells the house's books directly, including serialised volumes and early printings.

The wiki's staff list adds Hirayama (an event-only editor-in-chief), Hiratsuka (sales analyst, who appears in the Kamisato Estate), Murata and Fukumoto (festival stall editors), and a columnist signing as "Ms. Hina". The house is small enough that its editors personally deliver invitations and letters, and it often turns to the Traveler when it needs a courier.

Leadership: Yae Miko decides what gets published. She is known to be warm and bookish in the house and openly mercenary about profit, and she teases her authors about their deadline excuses.

Miko says she has never written a novel herself and that being an editor is its own entertainment. She told the Traveler that if they ever finish their journey and want it recorded, she might write it, if she has time. She is said to review the house's novels personally. She has also sent manuscripts back for being "not free enough", telling the author to ignore genre fashions and write the story well. In one character story, the author's very next manuscript worried her only because the pen name seemed too ordinary for its content.

Goals: The house exists to publish and sell light novels. Miko's own motives are entertainment and a taste for watching writers struggle with deadlines. Commercial success also matters: she is described as having an obsessive side about profit. The house wants to attract new talent, and the writing contest is its way of finding it.

When a rival hit threatened to spread dangerous spirit-summoning methods, Miko's solution in Friendship in Writing was to outcompete it with a better-selling novel, not to issue a warning that would only advertise the book. That fits the house's habit of solving problems through popularity.

Members: Named staff and authors from canon include:
- Yae Miko: boss, founder and editor-in-chief.
- Kuroda: executive editor who sells books at the shop and handles the Liyue author Chang the Ninth.
- Aratani, Shigeru, Onodera, Murata, Fukumoto and Hirayama: editors and event staff.
- Hiratsuka: sales analyst (wiki list).
- Junkichi: author of the Onibudou series, managed by Shigeru.
- Satomi: the house's "ace in the hole", who writes under many pen names.
- Souka: up-and-coming author who joined Miko at the beast-tamers tournament in Sumeru for inspiration (3.2).
- Chang the Ninth: Liyue author of "First Apprentice of Guhua", who won a contest.
- Xingqiu, writing as Zhenyu: author of "A Legend of Sword".
- Ms. Hina: advice columnist, in truth Gorou.

Methods: The house runs the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest, invites past winners to judge it, and holds writers' submission events. It publishes light novels in serial form, then collects them into volumes. Citlali notes that a serial takes about two weeks to reach Natlan and about a year before it is collected as a single volume. It also prints comics, guidebooks and military-strategy works such as the Teyvat Art of War, which Kokomi loves. It sells collectable first and deluxe editions and gives away early prints as gifts, as Miko did for the Legion of Soulblazers. It keeps in touch with authors by mail, even for those who never show up in person.

Editors give authors advice by letter, often as suggestions on future subjects. Aratani sent Chang the Ninth a pile of "creative suggestions" with his invitation. The Hina column is a running service in which readers write letters and receive replies.

History: The house is no more than 500 years old. Ei, who withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia about that long ago, says there was no Yae Publishing House at the time. By the time of the Traveler's first visit to Inazuma the house was a giant of the industry and a lively bookshop. During the Sakoku Decree (before Transient Dreams) it could not invite outlander authors or send them royalties. Afterwards its editors eagerly planned visits.

**This Novel Is Amazing! (1.0).** A Liyue commission has the Traveler carry Chang the Ninth's entry to the Feiyun Commerce Guild for shipping to Inazuma. Xu says he cannot imagine Chang winning against the Inazuman craze for "A Legend of Sword".

**Reborn as Raiden and the Ei visit (2.1).** Ei visits the shop in To Traverse the Mortal Plane and reads some of its recent winners to understand mortal fiction.

**Friendship in Writing (2.5).** Miko uses her editors, Junkichi and Satomi to write a new hit novel in a hurry, with the Traveler as a consultant.

**Hues of the Violet Garden (2.6).** The house co-runs the Irodori Festival with the Yashiro Commission and has booths, including a children's books stall.

Relations: The house is closely tied to its founder's other posts. The Grand Narukami Shrine is where Miko is Guuji, and readers see no clash between her two jobs. The Yashiro Commission, headed by the Kamisato Clan, co-runs the Irodori Festival with the house. The Shogun Ei is both Miko's friend and one of the house's unlikely readers. Outside Inazuma, the Feiyun Commerce Guild helps ship manuscripts from Liyue, and readers in Natlan, Fontaine and Liyue follow its serials.

Reputation: Inazuma's publishing giant: famed for light novels, bestsellers and the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest. Fans make pilgrimages to buy its books.

Kuroda says many light-novel readers from other islands travel to the shop, and calls it a "pilgrimage". Kokomi names the house's military-strategy publications as her favourites, and Citlali says she has read almost every novel it has published. Not every reader is impressed: Chang the Ninth's editor Aratani calls his themes slightly dated, though his book sells steadily.

Citlali also treasures an old house serial, "Mirage Warriors", which was started by Nakajima Jun and later continued by other authors up to 200 years ago.

Secrets: "Ms. Hina", the house's beloved advice columnist (the "That's Life" column), is Gorou. He agreed to write replies after an editor told him that only he could do it. Hina's fan club does not know. The Traveler hides the truth from him and from the fans.

Status as of 7.1: Active and thriving as of Version 7.1. Miko still runs it, the bookshop in Inazuma City still sells its books, and the contest is still held.

No canon shows any change in the house's standing in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content checked. Its latest appearances in canon are the 6.2 Witch's Homework quest with Onodera and the Soulblazers event gift.

701.content:
Kuroda is the executive editor of Yae Publishing House and runs its bookshop in his spare time. He edits Chang the Ninth, wishes he had gone to Liyue to chase him for manuscripts during the Sakoku Decree, and wanted the author to use a flashier pen name. He knows the collection value of the house's books. For the Traveler's friend Citlali he handed over a first edition of "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power" and the limited deluxe edition of "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?", which are no longer sold. He is nervous around Miko and, when Ei visited, worried she was there to inspect regulations or fire safety.

Kuroda is also the staff member who deals with the Hina column's business. When the Traveler asked for an endorsement, he said Ms. Hina rarely does them, but would make an exception for the Guuji. He also edits the "King of Invokations" novel, which is why he studies the card game.

702.comment: Yae Publishing House: This Novel Is Amazing contest
702.content:
The house's recurring writing contest is famous across Teyvat. Past winners are invited to serve as judges. Chang the Ninth entered and won with his martial-arts novel, "First Apprentice of Guhua". The title is a nod to a real-world light-novel guidebook. In Yae Publishing House's Invitation (2.0), Aratani sends gifts and letters to Chang the Ninth and Zhenyu to ask them to judge.

Xu notes in the first commission that Chang's entry would struggle, since another Liyue author's "A Legend of Sword" was the rage in Inazuma. That author is Xingqiu, who did not know.

703.comment: Yae Publishing House: A Legend of Sword
703.content:
"A Legend of Sword" is a six-volume space-opera adventure by Zhenyu, illustrated by Calx. Zhenyu is Xingqiu's pen name. Liyue publishers had rejected it, so Xingqiu printed a few copies privately and left them at Wanwen Bookhouse. A merchant carried one to Inazuma, where it was a smash hit and later reached Fontaine. It sits at the top of the bestseller list. Xingqiu is surprised to learn this. Kokomi is an enthusiastic reader.

Albedo's voice-over reveals the house asked him to switch authors for more royalties. The wiki credits "Calx" to Albedo, but his voice-over does not confirm it. Volume 5 is found at the Yashiro Commission headquarters rather than in the shop.

704.comment: Yae Publishing House: Ms. Hina and That's Life
704.content:
"That's Life" is a magazine whose advice column is answered by "Ms. Hina". Readers love her, and a fan club of three has formed in Inazuma City. Its club rules are not to pry into her identity, not to say controversial things and not to push the column on the uninterested. Gorou secretly writes the replies. He enjoys it, he says, because letters let readers treat him as a friend, unlike soldiers who are reserved around a general.

The house keeps Hina away from publicity and she declines most promotional requests. When the Traveler needs her endorsement in Friendship in Writing, Kuroda says that has to come through Miko's request.

705.comment: Yae Publishing House: Mr. Nine and Nod-Krai
705.content: In the Witch's Homework quest "Alan Smithee, Author of Fischl", Mr. Nine, in danger in Nod-Krai, writes to the house. Onodera travels to Mondstadt to commission the Traveler and Fischl, who adopted a persona from Mr. Nine's "Flowers for Princess Fischl". They first suspect Chang the Ninth, who is not Mr. Nine, and then use Oz to track her to Nod-Krai, where Nicole is revealed. Mr. Nine tells them she buried Chang's royalties in his yard.

706.comment: Yae Publishing House: Irodori Festival stall
706.content: During the limited-time event Hues of the Violet Garden, the house co-hosted Ritou's Irodori Festival with the Yashiro Commission. Murata ran its official stall, Fukumoto a children's book booth, and Onodera planned the release party of A Legend of Sword. Kuroda regretted that Chang the Ninth could not deliver a manuscript in time. Kokomi's pen-pal visit and Gorou's lucky draw appear in the same event.

707.content:
Yaksha (also: Yakshas, the Yakshas, Five Yakshas, Five Mighty Yakshas, Guardian Yakshas, Vigilant Yaksha, yaksha adepti): The yakshas were a fierce kind of illuminated beast-adepti. After the Archon War, Morax summoned them to wage an unending war on the monsters, plagues and curses born from the hatred of defeated gods. Five were the strongest and became known as the Five Yakshas. The work burdened them with karmic debt, and nearly all died, went mad or vanished. Only Alatus, now called Xiao, remains.

In Liyue the yakshas are now mostly forgotten, though statues and a few old books still keep their memory. The wiki spells "Yaksha" with a capital only for the five foremost, but the word is also used for the whole kind.

Structure: The yakshas were adepti, not a mortal organisation. Many served, but five stood above the rest: Bosacius, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus. Bosacius, the eldest, led them. The wiki lists Pervases as a lesser yaksha who was slain in the Archon War, and the book notes many other yakshas of unknown name who also died or fled.

Each of the Five Yakshas has a title: Alatus the Golden-Winged King (also the Conqueror of Demons and the Vigilant Yaksha), Bosacius Marshal Vritras, Indarias General Musatas, Bonanus General Chizapus and Menogias General Kapisas. Each also has an element: Alatus Anemo, Bosacius Electro, Indarias Pyro, Bonanus Hydro and Menogias Geo. In battle they wore masks based on Nuo opera masks, whose symbols resemble the Seven's elemental symbols but are cruder.

Leadership: The yakshas answered to Morax, the Geo Archon, who summoned them. The book says they followed him wherever battle took him. Bosacius, the eldest, was their leader.

Members: - **Alatus (Xiao)**: the last yaksha. Morax freed him from a cruel god who had enslaved him and gave him the name Xiao for his protection.
- **Bosacius**: leader of the Five, an Electro yaksha with four arms. He left his treasures at Minlin, later went mad and forgot his own name, and died in the Chasm as the "Nameless Yaksha".
- **Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias**: the other three of the Five, all dead.
- **Pervases**: a junior yaksha who died in the Archon War and whose spirit lingers in a crane statue at his run-down temple near Mt. Tianheng.

Sources checked do not say how Indarias, Bonanus and Menogias died. The book says some yakshas fell to rage, others to fear-driven madness, and many turned on each other.

Goals: Their duty was to defend Morax's rule and Liyue by purging the monsters and miasmas that grew from defeated gods' lingering hatred. The cinematic gives their oath as restoring order through slaughter and purging evil through battle, to which they gave their lives.

Methods: They fought without mercy, as the book puts it. They are adeptal arts users: Xiao performs Dream Trawler to cultivate himself and Mortal Lingering was used by Pervases. Xiao's Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering, a rite for purging demons and divine karma, is thought to have been practised by several yakshas, each in their own version.

Bosacius sealed his treasures with adeptal arts in the region of Minlin, and the puzzles of the quest The Yaksha's Wish reflect this.

History: Morax summoned the yakshas to purge the demons born from the bodies and hatred of the gods he had defeated. For about a thousand years they fought. The accumulating karmic debt wore at their souls: some raged, some went mad with fear, some turned on their own, and some were lost to illusion. Three of the five died, a fourth vanished and the rest of the many yakshas died or fled. Alatus alone survived.

**Bosacius.** Tired of an endless duty, and believing Liyue at peace with only himself and Alatus left, Bosacius sealed his treasures in Minlin and departed. His karmic debt took his sanity and his name. Five hundred years ago, drawn by the bloodshed of the cataclysm, he joined the Millelith and the thaumaturge Boyang at the Chasm and gave his life to seal the Abyssal monsters in. Before he died he became lucid enough to remember his comrades, his duty and his name.

**Xiao.** Xiao nearly succumbed himself, but according to the story teaser video he was saved by the music Venti played on a visit to Liyue. He later wondered whether the Nameless Yaksha was Bosacius, asked Zhongli's leave to investigate, and in the Chasm's depths confirmed it (End of the Line, Interlude Chapter Act II, 2.7).

Relations: - **Morax and Zhongli**: the yakshas shared a special bond with Morax, who named Xiao and Pervases himself. As Zhongli he prepares medicine for Xiao to ease his karmic pain.
- **Other adepti**: respect the yakshas' strength. Xiao holds high seniority and is called Conqueror of Demons; Ganyu has asked him for training, though Xiao thinks himself unfit to teach her.
- **Liyue Qixing**: its secret agents built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh to support Xiao's duty.

- **Millelith**: fought beside Bosacius at the Chasm.
- **Hu Tao and Chongyun**: through their lineages they know more of the yakshas than most, and have met Xiao.
- **Starsnatcher (Wang Ping'an)**: his grandfather, a folklorist, researched the yakshas and shared the tales with him.

Reputation: Long ago mortals revered the yakshas as Liyue's protectors, raising large statues (for example at Luhua Pool) and offering chants and food to ease their pain. Today the statues are battered and the features worn away. The surviving books, such as Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti and the "Ode to Windborne Wraith" chapter of a travel guide to Liyue, are dull and little read, and the Liyue edition omitted the latter. Hu Tao notes that talk of curses and miasmas would cause panic if people knew they were real, so the yakshas remain legend.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Xiao is the only living yaksha. The 5.x to 7.1 material checked adds nothing new about the yakshas.

Xiao still keeps watch over Liyue, living at Wangshu Inn. Version 7.0 added only a cosmetic Echo for him, and the Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya story content did not revisit the yakshas.

708.content: Bosacius (Electro, Marshal Vritras, eldest and leader), Indarias (Pyro, General Musatas), Bonanus (Hydro, General Chizapus), Menogias (Geo, General Kapisas) and Alatus (Anemo, the Golden-Winged King and Conqueror of Demons) were the strongest yakshas. Only Alatus, now Xiao, lives. The wiki gives the element for Indarias and Menogias from their Japanese voice actors; Bonanus is Hydro by elimination.

709.content: A volume from the "Hidden Wonders and Folklore of Liyue" series, written in archaic, wordy prose by a Sumeru scholar. It says Rex Lapis summoned the yakshas to purge demons, that the five strongest were Bosacius, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus, and that after a thousand years only Alatus survived. It adds that at the Lantern Rite people see a glow at Guyun Stone Forest and hear a flute among the marsh reeds of Dihua Marsh, which they take as the Vigilant Yaksha at work. Starsnatcher buys it during the Alatus Chapter and Paimon and the Traveler read it.

710.content: In this setting karma builds up in those who slay the lingering remnants of fallen gods. It wears away at the soul, causing rage, madness and pain, and it taints the surroundings: Xiao's karma can strengthen nearby monsters and stain mortals who stay near him. Xiao and Yelan attribute the madness of Rongzhao, who fought beside Bosacius without a Vision, to that karma, reasoning that without a Vision he could not resist it for long. Hu Tao says part of the yakshas' karma once became a plague in Liyue, which the founders of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor stopped by purifying the air and burning the dead.

711.comment: Yaksha: Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering
711.content: A rite for purging demons and divine karma. The wiki notes the English name was rewritten to match its use as a title. Liyue's rulers, who know Xiao's truth, call his millennia of work the "Bane of All Evil". It is not known how many other yakshas used the same technique.

712.comment: Yaksha: Wangshu Inn and the yakshas
712.content: The Liyue Qixing's secret agents built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh to give Xiao a place to rest and to help him purge plagues. Verr Goldet and Huai'an run it and cover for the damage his night work can cause. The wiki says it has stood at least since the years after the cataclysm, about 500 years ago.

713.comment: Yaksha: Xiao and the other yakshas
713.content: Xiao's character story and voice-overs describe a reserved warrior who avoids mortals for their sake and does not want sympathy, believing his fallen comrades would find tears a stain on their memory. He is fond of his fellow yakshas. When the Traveler met Pervases, he quickly grew nostalgic. Xiao's own entry carries his full history.

714.content:
Yashiro Commission (also: Yashiro Bugyo, Yashiro Bugyou, Sha-bugyou, Yashiro Commissioner): The Yashiro Commission (Sha-bugyou, "Commission of Shrines") is one of the three bodies of Inazuma's Tri-Commission, alongside the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions. It handles shrines, festivals, ceremonies and the cultural life of the people, and is run by the Kamisato Clan from the Kamisato Estate on Narukami Island. The Commissioner is Kamisato Ayato. His sister Ayaka is its warm public face. Behind the festivals it also commands the secret Shuumatsuban ninja.

It has less raw influence than the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions but is the best liked. Its soldiers are relaxed and care about ordinary people, and in the Inazuma Archon Quests it stayed clear of the Fatui's schemes. All three commissions hold the same authority and can keep one another in check.

Structure: Authority sits with the Kamisato Clan. Ayato, as Clan Head, is the Commissioner and handles governance, while Ayaka handles the clan's public image and dealings with ordinary people. The Commission is headquartered inside the main building of the Kamisato Estate. Representatives such as Hirano, Hirotatsu and Madarame Hyakubei work at the estate, and other listed staff include Furusawa, Kazumasa, Ogawa and Takami. Shogun's Army soldiers assigned to it are described as more relaxed than those under the other commissions. The clan also owns the members-only Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City and controls the Shuumatsuban.

The Kamisato Clan's household and the Commission overlap heavily. The clan's housekeeper and well-known fixer, Thoma, also appears on the Commission's staff list. The Traveler compares the headquarters to the Dawn Winery or the Jade Chamber, which are likewise seats of a powerful institution.

Leadership: Kamisato Ayato is the Yashiro Commissioner and head of the Kamisato Clan. He keeps a low public profile, works on government affairs and is known as clever, polite and hard to read. His sister Kamisato Ayaka, the Shirasagi Himegimi ("White Heron Princess"), is the clan's popular public face.

Ayaka says that after their parents died she and Ayato took responsibility for clan matters together, though she still relies on Ayato for every important decision. Ayato took the post young, after his father's early death, following his parents' wishes and to protect Ayaka. A character story says that at first nobody was impressed by the inexperienced young head, and that he stabilised the clan's position. Thoma, who came to Inazuma from Mondstadt, serves as housekeeper and is a trusted fixer.

Ayato and Ayaka divided the work deliberately. Ayato avoids public events and handles dealings with Shogunate officials, while Ayaka keeps up the clan's image, which her profile says matters in Inazuman noble politics. Ayato says the Tri-Commission looks calm but is turbulent beneath the surface, and claims he has never dishonoured the clan.

Goals: Officially the Commission arranges ritual matters, shrines and public festivals, so that both the gods and the people are pleased. Its quieter aim, shown through Ayato, is to protect Inazuma and the Kamisato Clan, deal with corrupt officials, and use the Shuumatsuban where the Commissioner cannot act openly. The Commission also proposed repealing the Vision Hunt Decree, according to Ayaka.

Methods: Public work includes festival planning, ceremonies and community outreach. Ayaka says the Commission and shrine maidens share festival affairs, and that safety concerns such as fire prevention are planned in advance rather than cancelling events like fireworks. Ayato prefers to deal with corrupt officials within legal bounds, though he uses a wide range of methods.

Information and discreet fixing are major tools. Thoma builds a large network of contacts, learning first-hand news and striking deals that help the Commission without personal gain. The Shuumatsuban handle espionage, intelligence gathering and covert operations. In Sayu's hangout quests they are shown making blinding powder and faked corpses.

Relations: Within the Tri-Commission, which divides the executive powers of what Ayaka's profile calls the Triarchal Council, the Yashiro are equal to the Kujou-led Tenryou Commission (security and military) and the Hiiragi-led Kanjou Commission (finance and borders). Ayaka says Yashiro proposals to repeal the Vision Hunt Decree were vetoed by both. Naoe Hisamasa calls the Yashiro the commission closest to the Raiden Shogun. The Grand Narukami Shrine's Guuji Yae Miko and Ayato work together because their duties overlap, though she dislikes his ways and calls him the "Yashiro rascal".

Ayato says the Kaedehara Clan was once a subordinate branch of the Kamisato Clan. He feels a duty to support Kazuha and says he could help him avoid arrest by the Tenryou Commission. Ayaka says she has had disputes with Kujou Sara of the Tenryou Commission, but that Sara is a loyal servant of Inazuma.

Reputation: Many Inazumans see it as the least controversial of the commissions, and as caring. After the Archon Quests, which left it mostly unaffected, it gained slightly more influence and goodwill. The public admires Ayaka warmly. Ayato is far less known, and rumours about him run from meticulous festivals to political tricks.

Secrets: The Shuumatsuban is a secret unit that reports directly to the head of the Kamisato Clan. Ayato inherited command from his father. Most members are orphans taken in young, which Ayato says guarantees loyalty. Members' identities are highly classified, and members who die on secret missions are not publicly honoured.

Ayato's profile says he risked his life to smuggle the Watatsumi Army into Tenshukaku as a small favour for Ayaka. In the Fatui plot, Ayato's character demo shows him rejecting a Fatui offer of cooperation.

History: The Commission's early history is not described. Its recent past is tied to the Kamisato Clan's decline: Ayaka says the clan once failed to protect a swordsmith of national significance. The Fatui harassed it, many clan people were lost, and the Shogunate's trust fell. This aged their father and badly damaged the clan's standing. Ayato rebuilt it, and Ayaka says the Commission is now unified again.

Thoma's profile places the Kamisato Clan's loss of power ten years before the present, when Ayato was caught in a dispute over succession rights after the death of both parents (Ayato's own story says his father died first, while his mother was also unwell). Several groups tried to exploit the clan's weakness, but Ayato's cunning let him overcome them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Yashiro Commission is active under Ayato and remains based at the Kamisato Estate.

The wiki shows no major role for it in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya storylines of 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

715.content:
The Shuumatsuban is a secret organisation of ninja under the Yashiro Commission. It is led by the head of the Kamisato Clan, currently Ayato, and its members report to him. Its work is espionage, intelligence gathering and covert action, and its slogan appears to be about sending the Shuumatsu to end traitors and criminals alike. Sayu is described as its resident ninja, and its headquarters is a ninja village. Members are paid monthly: Sayu's salary is 200,000 Mora. Most members are orphans raised from a young age, so loyalty runs deep. Known members include Inu Shoushou and Momoyo, plus staff such as Ogawa and Kano Nana. The retired Nakanishi and Taroumaru are former members.

The Shuumatsuban can make a toxic elemental powder that can blind, and can fake a death with an artificial cadaver built from meat, white iron and sea ganoderma, a day-long task. Members killed in secret missions are not publicly commemorated.

716.content: The Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City is owned by the Yashiro Commission. Entry is members-only, limited to people the Kamisato Clan approves, and the clan often uses it as a local base and private meeting place. Its boss is Taroumaru, a Shiba Inu and a former Shuumatsuban ninja dog, who was famous with dog lovers, even overseas, before the Sakoku Decree. Other staff include Kozue, Nobumori and the retired Nakanishi. Customers leave payment in a box after drinking tea.

717.content: The Kamisato Estate is the clan's residence. The Yashiro Commission Headquarters is inside its main building, and staff such as Furuta, Koharu, Hirano, Hirotatsu and Madarame Hyakubei work there. Its map text says the Commission's duties are so pervasive that even Shogunate officials cannot follow them, and that the Shirasagi Himegimi is more popular than the head of the household.

718.content:
Yinyuan Hall (also: Yinyuan Chamber): Yinyuan Hall governs Liyue's salt industry and is one of the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing. Its members descend from people who survived the fall of Sal Terrae, the last haven of the God of Salt, Havria. The Hall tells a story of her death that the truth contradicts.

The Hall's version blames the Geo Archon Morax, who they say killed Havria out of envy. Zhongli, Morax's current vessel, corrects this in the Sal Flore story quest.

Structure: Yinyuan Hall is a trade body for salt merchants and producers. The only named member is Wanyan. The Hall passes down its history among its own people by word of mouth.

Canon does not name a representative or any other office-holder.

Members: Wanyan is the only member named. In Sal Flore she first said she was an archaeologist but lacked even basic archaeological knowledge. She is in truth a devotee of Havria from the Hall, and she wanted proof that Morax was guilty. She joined Zhongli, the Fatui researcher Kliment and the Traveler in the sealed ruins of Sal Terrae.

Zhongli made her and Kliment agree to alternate claims on treasures found there, one object per claim. Kliment took the self-refilling salt chalice and Wanyan the salt ruler, which covers the ground in salt. When Kliment broke the contract out of greed, Zhongli and the Traveler made an example of him. Later Zhongli told Wanyan she could claim only part of a broken sword, and she chose to break the contract rather than leave it. Zhongli then punished her by telling her the truth.

Goals: Its trade is salt. Beyond that, the story shown in canon is Wanyan's personal aim to prove her god's death was Morax's crime.

Methods: Its heritage is oral. The Hall passes down Havria's story through generations, and the account that survives has drifted away from the facts.

History: The Hall's origins lie in the Archon War. Havria refused to fight, gave way to other gods and finally held a small plot at Sal Terrae. According to Zhongli, her people's king killed her with a sword as a mercy, because her kindness could not protect them. Her power spread out and turned most of her followers into salt. The survivors scattered across Liyue, and some reached Liyue Harbor, which Morax protected, and eventually formed Yinyuan Hall.

Over the millennia the survivors' story warped into one where Morax murdered Havria out of envy. Other descendants of Sal Terrae's survivors kept a truer account, which appears in the Diary of Roald the Adventurer. Descendants fearing a curse later returned, broke the sword and placed it on a pedestal with two of her relics, then resealed the ruin.

Relations: Under the Liyue Qixing, in the same Eight Trades as Shenglu Hall. Its tradition is hostile to Morax, Liyue's old archon, though the Hall sits in his harbour city.

Wanyan did not know Zhongli was the Geo Archon when she told him about her hatred of Morax.

Secrets: The Hall holds a mistaken belief rather than a secret. The truth was told only to Wanyan, within a sealed ruin, so other members should not be assumed to know it.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. The last event concerning the Hall in canon is the Sal Flore story quest from Version 1.1. No appearances were found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

719.comment: Yinyuan Hall: Havria and the Hall
719.content: Havria was a gentle, weak god of salt who fled the Archon War and was killed by her own king. The Hall's descendants believe Morax assassinated her. Zhongli says the sword found in Sal Terrae was the murder weapon, not her relic, and that her people acted from mercy. She left two relics: a chalice that refills itself with salt and a ruler that covers ground in salt.

720.content: Wanyan is a follower of Havria and a member of Yinyuan Hall. She posed as an archaeologist to seek proof against Morax, and she heard the truth from Zhongli in the ruins of Sal Terrae. She refused to believe it at first.

721.content:
Yun-Han Opera Troupe (also: Yun-Han Troupe, Yunhan Opera Troupe, Yun-Han Opera Company): The Yun-Han Opera Troupe is the best-known Liyue Opera company in Liyue Harbor. The house of Yun has run it for generations, and its current director is the opera singer and playwright Yun Jin. It performs regularly at Heyu Tea House.

Liyue Opera is a traditional art handed down over generations, and its performers usually work in troupes; canon calls this the most acclaimed of them. Beyond its star, it is a working organisation of veteran performers, a manager and backstage staff.

Structure: A director sits at the top and makes the big decisions. Managers handle daily work. Yunning is the manager seen in canon, and Yinggong looks after wardrobe and props. Many veteran performers belong to the troupe, and some joined under Yun Jin's grandfather. No other ranks or headcount are given.

Putting on a Liyue Opera needs many people on and off stage, as Yinggong puts it. His own work covers cannons, flags, costumes, accessories and other props. Some costumes and props are hand-me-downs from earlier years, and others were bought or made by him.

Leadership: Yun Jin is the director, the troupe's lead performer and the author of its new plays. Her manager Yunning handles bookings and press.

Yun Jin's grandfather directed the troupe before her, and long-time fans called him "Sir Yun". After she took over, those fans came to her shows too and began to use the same title for her. Business circles call her "Director Yun" because she makes the big decisions. Veterans follow her lead in rehearsal, but offstage they treat her like a granddaughter and nag her about diet and tastes. Yunning is protective and anxious about Yun Jin's safety and public image.

Members: - **Yun Jin**: director, singer, playwright and star. See her own entry.
- **Yunning**: manager. Panics when Yun Jin disappears to seek inspiration, screens interviews and had the Millelith pursue tabloid impersonators.
- **Yinggong**: wardrobe and props manager and stagehand. He also makes paper theatre plays for children as a hobby and appeared in the 3.4 Lantern Rite event.
- **Veteran elders**: unnamed senior performers, some from her grandfather's time, who stay devoted to traditional Liyue Opera.
- **Yun Jin's grandfather**: former director, unnamed.

Canon also mentions backstage helpers who have time off at festival time, but names none of them.

Goals: The troupe's work is to perform Liyue Opera well and keep the art alive. Under Yun Jin it also stages new plays beyond the classic repertoire. Yun Jin has privately wished to sing the stories of ordinary people's joys and sorrows rather than the adepti legends that dominate the genre. That is her own wish, and canon does not call it troupe policy.

Methods: The troupe performs for paying audiences at Heyu Tea House, where Yun Jin appears from time to time. Fans gather there hoping to catch her and ask about her schedule, which keeps the tea house busy. According to Yun Jin, troupe rules forbid accepting private gifts from patrons. Interview requests go through the manager and not directly to the star.

The repertoire includes old adeptal legends such as "The Divine Damsel of Devastation", written by Yun Jin's father, alongside the newer plays that canon credits to Yun Jin.

History: The Yun family were famous weaponsmiths about 500 years ago, and over time the family took up Liyue Opera. By the time of Yun Jin's grandfather the Yun-Han Opera Troupe existed.

Yun Jin's mother took up the mantle from her grandfather and was a famous opera singer in Liyue Harbor, and her father is a playwright. Yun Jin grew up around the troupe, and its veterans watched her grow into a rising star. She debuted young and later became director.

In 3.4 (limited-time Lantern Rite event) Yinggong said that no special troupe performance was planned that year, because the troupe had already performed at many Lantern Rites in a row and could finally rest.

Relations: - **Heyu Tea House**: the troupe's regular venue. Its owner, Fan Er'ye, earns a great deal from Yun Jin's shows.
- **Xinyan**: a close friend of Yun Jin. The elders look down on rock 'n' roll, so Yun Jin keeps her visits secret from them.
- **Adventurers' Guild**: Yunning commissioned it in 2.4 to find Yun Jin.
- **The Millelith**: Yunning had them pursue tabloid impersonators.

- **The Steambird**: a reputable publication. Two tabloid reporters falsely claimed to be from it, and the troupe now handles press through its manager.
- **Shenhe**: told Yun Jin a less heroic version of the divine damsel legend, which influenced how Yun Jin approaches the role.

Reputation: The troupe is regarded as the most famous opera company in Liyue Harbor. Yun Jin's character story says nine out of ten Heyu Tea House patrons are her fans. The elders are known for being devoted to traditional Liyue Opera and rather rigid about other kinds of music.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1. Yun Jin still directs the troupe and performs in Liyue Harbor.

No news of the troupe was found in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

722.content: Yunning is the manager of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe and appears in Yun Jin's Hangout Event. When Yun Jin vanished days before a big show, she commissioned the Adventurers' Guild and begged the Traveler to find her, afraid the audience would tear the place down and that Yun Jin might get hurt. She insists on handling interviews herself and had the Millelith pursue the fake Steambird reporters. In canon she is excitable, dramatic and fiercely protective of her star. Her full name, age and background are not given.

723.content: During the 3.4 Lantern Rite event "The Exquisite Night Chimes", Yinggong ran a paper theatre for children in Liyue Harbor, and the Traveler helped perform "Homeward, Bravebeard". He explained that he works for the Yun-Han Opera Troupe on wardrobe and props, that he can carry a tune after years with the troupe, and that backstage helpers had the festival off. He stayed in the city himself because his parents had died two years earlier. He says paper plays are simpler than Liyue Opera because one person can do everything.

724.comment: Yun-Han Opera Troupe: Yun Jin's Hangout Event, Act I
724.content: In Act I of Yun Jin's Hangout Event, Yunning asks the Traveler to find Yun Jin, who has gone to Lingju Pass to feel real danger for her acting. The Traveler brings her back. After a show, admirers invite Yun Jin to dinner and she uses the Traveler as an excuse. At Heyu Tea House two journalists claim to represent The Steambird but are really from a small tabloid, and one is bound by a strict contract to her editor. Yunning later reports the tabloid to the Millelith and tells the troupe to be careful. The act has several possible endings.

725.comment: Yun-Han Opera Troupe: The Yun family and the troupe
725.content: The Yun family were prominent Liyue weaponsmiths about 500 years ago and worked with the Han family on the Prototype series of weapons after the cataclysm. Over the centuries a family member tired of forging became interested in the performing arts, and by Yun Jin's generation few Yuns still forge. Yun Jin carries a lock-shaped copper pendant that was forged and handed down. The wiki notes that the "Han" in the troupe's name uses a different character from the Han weaponsmith family and is unrelated to it.
